rows.original: Evergreen greets you with a nod. "Ah, you're back. Did you have any luck getting my bag back from the foxes?" Why yes, you did. There were some circumstances that complicated matters in retrieving it, but you do have it on you. Which leads to some questions you'd like to ask before turning in the goods... "And those would be?" First of all, you definitely deserve some hazard pay for this. Her little errand turned out to be a lot more dangerous than she'd led you to expect. She could at least be a little more forthright about her jobs in the future. Sure, it's partly your own fault for not asking beforehand, but — "Hand it over, and let's see if the things inside are still intact. I'm sure those fuzzy good-for-nothings have their wet-fur stink all over my toys now." You do just that, and Evergreen pulls apart the strings, peering into the small brown bag. Standing, she crosses over to a nearby table and upends the linen pouch onto its surface, a veritable mountain of sex toys of various shapes and sizes spilling out into view. The tanuki witch picks up a few choice pieces, sniffs them, then nods. "Looks like all of my favorite pieces are still there, yes. Renegotiating price after the task is done is rather poor form, but I think I understand where you're coming from; at the same time, I'd rather not start a precedent by making an exception for you. Let's call it a bonus for a job well done, hmm?" You suppose that'll have to do — that, and being more careful while accepting jobs from her in the future. Evergreen smiles sweetly, then snaps her fingers. One of her daughters shuffles in to put away the mess on the table, and she turns her attention back to you. "Very well, then. Anything else?" You shake your head and stifle a sigh. Of course. Well, if she'd be so kind as to pay you for services rendered... "Ah, of course." Evergreen whistles sharply, and another daughter comes up with a tray, a bag of coin set on it. The tanuki witch takes it and shoves it into your hands; it feels appropriately heavy and clinks with a very satisfactory sound. So long as it doesn't disappear or turn into leaves in the morning, that'll do just fine. Evergreen chuckles. "I've long grown past simple glamours like that. Here, you wanted hazard pay? Take the bag as well. It'll be of more use in your hands than it is holding all my knick-knacks." You mean... after everything... well, you don't know what's been inside of it... "But you do. You saw it all come out, didn't you?" That was a rhetorical question. "Don't be such a prude, it's pretty clean inside. Extradimensional spaces don't come cheap, you know, and they don't get dirty." Would bad things happen if you turned it inside-out? "No, it just gets turned inside-out. Seriously, Estelore fixed that basic loophole a long time ago. Shame on you for not knowing your history, dear. Now that we've concluded business, perhaps we should have a little pleasure? My treat — if you're up for it, that is. Just ask."
rows.translation: 常青女士向你点头致意。啊，你回来了。有没有成功把我的包从那些狐狸手里夺回来呢？ 没错，你确实做到了。在取回它的过程中确实遇到了一些复杂的情况，但你现在确实把它带在身上了。因此，在上交这些物品之前，你有一些问题想要先问清楚…… 那么，这些是什么呢？ 首先，你确实应该因为这件事得到一些额外的补偿。她那个小小的差事，结果比她让你想象的要危险得多。以后她至少应该更坦诚地告诉你自己要去做什么。当然，你没有事先询问，这也是你自己的疏忽，但是—— 把东西交出来，让我们看看里面的东西还完好无损吗。我敢肯定，那些毛茸茸的家伙肯定把他们的湿漉漉的臭味弄得我的玩具到处都是。 你照做了，然后常青女士便拆开了那个小棕色袋子，将里面的东西都倒了出来。她站起身，走到附近的一张桌子旁，把那个亚麻布制成的袋子倒放在桌面上，顿时，各种各样形状和大小的成人玩具就像一座小山一样散落在桌上。这位狸猫女巫挑了几件她中意的玩具，闻了闻，然后点了点头。 看起来我所有喜欢的物品都还在那里，没错。在任务完成后才重新协商价格，这种做法确实不太妥当，但我大概能理解你的立场；不过，我也不想因为为你破例而开创一个先例。我们就把这看作是对你出色完成任务的奖励吧，嗯？ 你认为那样做就足够了——还有就是，以后在接受她安排的工作时，要更加谨慎一些。 常青女士微微一笑，然后打了个响指。她的一个女儿走过来，把桌子上弄乱的东西收拾好，她这才把注意力重新转向你。那好吧，还有其他事情吗？ 你摇了摇头，强忍住一声叹息。当然了。不过，如果她能好心地为你提供的服务付钱的话…… 啊，当然。常青女士发出清脆的哨声，另一个女儿拿来了一个托盘，上面放着一袋硬币。那只狸猫女巫接过袋子，塞到了你的手里；硬币的分量恰到好处，相互碰撞时发出的声音也非常令人满意。 只要这些硬币不会在早上消失，也不会变成树叶，那就没问题了。 常青轻笑了一声。“我早就不玩那种简单的幻术了。给，你不是想要危险津贴吗？这个袋子也拿去吧。放在你手里，总比留在这里装我那些小玩意儿有用。” 你是说……在经历了这一切之后……嗯，你根本不知道里面发生过什么…… 但你确实看到了。你亲眼看到了这一切发生，对吧？ 那只是一个反问句而已。 别这么古板嘛，里面其实挺干净的。你知道的，异维空间可不是便宜能买来的，而且它们也不会弄脏的。 如果把它翻个里朝外，会发生什么坏事吗？ “不，翻过来也只会被翻过来而已。说真的，Estelore 很久以前就补上了那个基本漏洞。亲爱的，连这点历史都不知道，真该羞愧。既然正事谈完了，也许我们该找点乐子？我请客——前提是你愿意的话。开口就行。”
rows.raw: " Evergreen greets you with a nod. "Ah, you're back. Did you have any luck getting my bag back from the foxes?" Why yes, you did. There were some circumstances that complicated matters in retrieving it, but you do have it on you. Which leads to some questions you'd like to ask before turning in the goods... "And those would be?" First of all, you definitely deserve some hazard pay for this. Her little errand turned out to be a lot more dangerous than she'd led you to expect. She could at least be a little more forthright about her jobs in the future. Sure, it's partly your own fault for not asking beforehand, but — "Hand it over, and let's see if the things inside are still intact. I'm sure those fuzzy good-for-nothings have their wet-fur stink all over my toys now." You do just that, and Evergreen pulls apart the strings, peering into the small brown bag. Standing, she crosses over to a nearby table and upends the linen pouch onto its surface, a veritable mountain of sex toys of various shapes and sizes spilling out into view. The tanuki witch picks up a few choice pieces, sniffs them, then nods. "Looks like all of my favorite pieces are still there, yes. Renegotiating price after the task is done is rather poor form, but I think I understand where you're coming from; at the same time, I'd rather not start a precedent by making an exception for you. Let's call it a bonus for a job well done, hmm?" You suppose that'll have to do — that, and being more careful while accepting jobs from her in the future. Evergreen smiles sweetly, then snaps her fingers. One of her daughters shuffles in to put away the mess on the table, and she turns her attention back to you. "Very well, then. Anything else?" You shake your head and stifle a sigh. Of course. Well, if she'd be so kind as to pay you for services rendered... "Ah, of course." Evergreen whistles sharply, and another daughter comes up with a tray, a bag of coin set on it. The tanuki witch takes it and shoves it into your hands; it feels appropriately heavy and clinks with a very satisfactory sound. So long as it doesn't disappear or turn into leaves in the morning, that'll do just fine. Evergreen chuckles. "I've long grown past simple glamours like that. Here, you wanted hazard pay? Take the bag as well. It'll be of more use in your hands than it is holding all my knick-knacks." You mean... after everything... well, you don't know what's been inside of it... "But you do. You saw it all come out, didn't you?" That was a rhetorical question. "Don't be such a prude, it's pretty clean inside. Extradimensional spaces don't come cheap, you know, and they don't get dirty." Would bad things happen if you turned it inside-out? "No, it just gets turned inside-out. Seriously, Estelore fixed that basic loophole a long time ago. Shame on you for not knowing your history, dear. Now that we've concluded business, perhaps we should have a little pleasure? My treat — if you're up for it, that is. Just ask." "

rows.original:
It is ironic, perhaps, that this entrance has been unearthed in a similar fashion by which it was sealed off. Freed from an eternity of darkness from the snowstorm, piles of rubble still lie strewn here and there about the main gates both inside and out, dirt and rock and bits of ancient masonry. A strange chill sensation divides the interior of Fort Marrok from the outside world, marking the beginnings of the haunts' territory.

    There are slots in the entry archway's ceiling, the portcullis raised and held in place by rusted metal latches. Several racks lie to the side of the entryway, but what's left of them and anything they might have held lies on the cracked ground, almost unrecognizable heaps of rusted decay moldering away as time gnaws on their bones.
    
    To the north, a hallway that stretches on; to the south, little River sits in a nook just outside the fort, mightily absorbed in what you presume is composing the tale of your exploits here. You could approach him if you wanted to back out, but you know that doing so means that you'll have to go back to Garth empty-handed.
rows.translation:
具有讽刺意味的是，这个入口被发现的方式，与它当初被封死的方式如出一辙。暴风雪带来的永恒黑暗被打破之后，成堆的碎石仍然散落在主城门内外各处——泥土、岩石，还有些古老的砖石碎块。一种诡异的寒意将马罗克要塞的内部与外部世界分隔开来，标志着幽灵领地的起点。

    入口拱门的天花板上有一些开口，栅门被生锈的金属锁扣抬起来并固定在那里。入口处旁边摆放着几排架子，但那些架子如今早已残破不堪，它们原本可能放着的物品也都散落在满是裂痕的地面上，那些锈迹斑斑、腐烂不堪的残骸早已难以辨认了，时间正在一点点侵蚀着它们的存在。
    
    北边是一条向前延伸的走廊；南边，小小的瑞弗坐在堡垒外的一个角落里，正全神贯注地——你猜——撰写你在这里的冒险事迹。如果你想掉头回去，可以去找他，但你知道那样一来，你就只能空着手回去见加斯了。

rows.original:
This room appears to be lodgings for a single person — being barely more than a glorified storeroom, there's just enough floor space for a cupboard, desk, a folding bed and a bookcase. All but the last have been consumed by dry rot — the dry and cold climate has preserved them as best as possible, but they still look like they could fall apart at a touch. A series of small rusted hooks have been hammered into the far wall, but it looks like nothing's been hung on them for ages. A small brass plaque is set beneath the hooks, dusty but still legible.

    The bookcase, though, is another matter altogether. There's clearly been some kind of preservation at work here — the rune-carved wood still appears solid enough, and the books are in readable condition, however yellowed and dusty they might be. You could take a moment to look through them, if you like, but there doesn't seem to be much left for you here otherwise.
    
    The only exit here is west and back out into the entrance hallway.
rows.translation:
这个房间似乎是供一个人居住的住处——充其量不过是个稍微像样点的储藏室，地上只够放一个橱柜、一张书桌、一张折叠床和一个书架。除了最后那件，其余都已被干腐侵蚀——干燥寒冷的气候尽力保存了它们，但它们看起来仍然一碰就会散架。远处的墙上钉着一排小小的锈钩，但看样子已经很久没在上面挂过东西了。钩子下方嵌着一块小铜牌，积满灰尘，但字迹仍然可辨。

    不过那个书架就完全是另一回事了。这里显然施加过某种保护手段——刻着符文的木头看上去依然结实，书本虽然发黄积灰，却仍然可以阅读。你如果愿意，可以花点时间翻一翻，但除此之外，这里似乎没剩下什么别的了。
    
    这里唯一的出口是向西，然后回到入口走廊。

This large room, you can only presume, served as the barracks for the garrisoned soldiers. Passing through a high archway decorated with numerous lupine runes, you emerge into a truly cavernous chamber, propped up by rows of pillars. The metal frames of various pieces of furniture lie in neat, orderly rows, their more organic components having succumbed to the ravages of time; you can make out the remains of beds and a footlocker or two, but that's about the long and short of it.

    The rest of the place is rather spartan. A number of long stone basins line one wall, but the slits in the wall which fed them have long since dried up. A number of empty pole holders and hooks suggest that portions of the barracks may have been curtained off to allow its inhabitants some measure of privacy, but beyond that the entire place appears to have been used communally.
    
    Near the back of the hall, you spy a large set of metal hooks.
    
    [pc.hasKeyItem RampartKey
    |Now that you've obtained the keys that hung here, there's nothing left on the hooks but emptiness.
    |Most of them are empty, but an old keyring hangs on one of them. It's heavily tarnished, but otherwise in serviceable condition — as is the single massive key that hangs off it. That certainly looks important, if nothing else.
    ]
    
    The only exit here is the same way you came in by — east out to the great hall.
rows.translation:
你只能推测，这个大房间曾是驻军士兵的营房。穿过一道装饰着许多狼族符文的高拱门，你进入一个真正像洞穴般空旷的厅堂，由一排排柱子支撑着。各种家具的金属框架整齐地排成行列，它们那些有机材质的部件早已在时间的摧残下腐朽；你能辨认出床的残骸和一两个储物箱，但也就仅此而已。

    这地方其余部分相当简陋。一面墙边排着一列长长的石槽，但为它们供水的墙缝早已干涸。许多空着的支架和挂钩表明，营房的一部分可能曾被帘子隔开，好让居住者有一点隐私，但除此之外，整个地方似乎都是共用的。
    
    在大厅的尽头，你看到了一组巨大的金属挂钩。
    
    [pc.hasKeyItem RampartKey
    |现在你已经取下了原本挂在这里的钥匙，钩子上只剩下空荡荡的痕迹。
    |其中大多数都是空的，但有一个上面挂着一个旧钥匙扣。钥匙扣已经严重生锈了，不过其他部分仍然可以使用——挂在那里的那把巨大的钥匙也是如此。单凭它的外观，就足以让人觉得它很重要了。
    ]
    
    这里唯一的出口就是你进来时走的那条路——从东边出去，就能到达大厅。

rows.original:
You're standing in the great hall of Fort Marrok, a chamber so vast your footsteps audibly echo in its eaves. The beginnings of the arched, vaulted roof are visible where they meet the high walls, but the rest of the ceiling is swathed in impenetrable darkness; tall pillars bear spikes from which banners, tapestries and other decorations might have been hung, but if any were there, they too have long since crumbled to dust.

    In the middle of the room, a stage or dais of sorts, comprised of a small pyramid of steps that eventually flatten out — a focal point for any gatherings which took place here. On the north and south sides of the hall, a huge hearth to provide heat and light for the entire chamber, now cold and abandoned.
    
    [flags.GARTH_QUEST_GREAT_HALL_STATE 1 2
    |Although the cauldron you set down is empty, the restless ghosts in the hall seem to be having the time of their unlife, jabbing spectral swords into the cauldron and coming out with... well, you can only assume the white goop coating the bread is whatever the cauldron used to hold a thousand years ago. They sure seem to enjoy it, that's for sure — those not currently busying themselves with helping themselves from the cauldron have started up a bawdy drinking song, slumped on the spectral longtables and swilling themselves silly from kegs, mugs and tankards alike.
    
    In their current distracted state, sneaking past them and into the archway in the hall's west end would be a trivial task.
    |With the revelers' defeat at your hands — no matter how impossible it seems that you managed to pull through such odds — you're left with an empty hall, as empty and dead as it should be. Something tugs at your mind, the fleeting thought that perhaps you could have handled this better, perhaps in a way that would have been easier on both the restless ghosts and you, but well, there's not much point in crying over spilt milk now, is there?
    
    |As you enter, you note rows upon rows of spectral longtables, each one easily able to seat a dozen people or more — and at each and every one of them are seated several lupines, knife and fork in hand, clearly agitated as they wait for something — a meal, most likely — that will never be served. They drum their utensils and mutter amongst themselves, casting the occasional glance at the entry archway.
    
    [pc.ra lupine
    |The specters give you a cursory glance but turn away after a moment, clearly too aggrieved at their lack of chow to pay you any serious attention once having registered you as a lupine. It's possible that they may have mistaken you for one of their own... in which case, it would probably be safe to cross the great hall just like that[party.som|| while [companion1.name] sneaks by as their attention is focused on you| while the others sneak by as their attention is focused on you].
    
    The question is: how sure are you of your guise?
    |They don't seem to have noticed you yet, but you get the feeling that walking straight into a giant room packed full of crotchety, hungry ghosts isn't the best of ideas.
    
    Well, what now?
    ]
    ]
    
    The only exits here are east out into the hallway, and west further into the garrison.
rows.translation:
你此刻站在马罗克要塞的宏伟大厅中，这个厅堂如此宽敞，以至于你的脚步声在拱顶下都能清晰地回响。拱形穹顶与高墙相接的地方还能隐约看到其起始部分，但天花板的其余部分却笼罩在一片无法穿透的黑暗之中；高高的柱子上装着尖刺，上面原本可能挂着旗帜、挂毯和其他装饰物，但倘若真有这些东西的话，它们也早已化为尘埃了。

    在房间的中央，有一个类似舞台或高台的设施，由一小段逐渐变平的阶梯组成——这里曾是任何在此举行的聚会的焦点。大厅的南北两侧各有一个巨大的壁炉，曾经为整个房间提供温暖与光线，如今却已冰冷废弃。
    
    [flags.GARTH_QUEST_GREAT_HALL_STATE 1 2
    |虽然你放下的大锅是空的，但大厅里那些不安分的幽灵似乎正享受着它们的死后时光——它们把幽灵之剑刺进大锅，捞出来的……嗯，你只能猜测，那些涂在面包上的白色黏糊物，就是这口大锅一千年前装过的东西。它们看上去确实很享受，这一点毫无疑问——那些暂时没忙着从大锅里取食的，已经开始唱起粗俗的饮酒歌，瘫在幽灵长桌旁，用酒桶、杯子和酒杯把自己灌得酩酊大醉。
    
    在它们目前这种心不在焉的状态下，悄悄从它们身边溜过去、进入大厅西端的拱门，简直轻而易举。
    |狂欢者已经败在你手上——尽管你似乎凭着难以置信的运气才挺过了那样的劣势——此刻留给你的是一座空荡荡的大厅，空寂而死寂，正如它本该有的样子。有个念头在你脑中萦绕不去：也许你本可以处理得更好，也许有办法让那些不安分的幽灵和你自己都好过一些；不过，现在为打翻的牛奶哭泣也没什么意义了，不是吗？
    
    |你一进门就注意到一排排幽灵长桌，每一张都能轻松坐下十几个人甚至更多——而每一张桌旁都坐着几名狼人，手里握着刀叉，显然焦躁不安地等着什么东西——多半是饭菜——而那永远也不会被端上来。它们敲着餐具，彼此低声抱怨，偶尔瞥一眼入口的拱门。
    
    [pc.ra lupine
    |那些幽灵只是漫不经心地瞥了你一眼，随即又转开了——显然它们因为没饭吃而太过恼火，在确认你是狼人之后，便懒得再认真关注你。说不定它们把你误认成了自己人……如果是这样，那么就这样穿过大厅大概也没什么危险[party.som||，而[companion1.name]则趁着它们的注意力集中在你身上时溜过去|，而其他人则趁着它们的注意力集中在你身上时溜过去]。
    
    问题在于：你对这身伪装有多大把握？
    |它们似乎还没注意到你，但你有种感觉：径直走进一个挤满了脾气暴躁、饥肠辘辘的鬼魂的巨大房间，可不是什么好主意。
    
    那么，现在怎么办？
    ]
    ]
    
    这里唯一的出口是往东通往走廊，以及往西深入驻军区。

They sure seem to enjoy it, that's for sure — those not currently busying themselves with helping themselves from the cauldron have started up a bawdy drinking song, slumped on the spectral longtables and swilling themselves silly from kegs, mugs and tankards alike.
    
    In their current distracted state, sneaking past them and into the archway in the hall's west end would be a trivial task.
    |With the revelers' defeat at your hands — no matter how impossible it seems that you managed to pull through such odds — you're left with an empty hall, as empty and dead as it should be. Something tugs at your mind, the fleeting thought that perhaps you could have handled this better, perhaps in a way that would have been easier on both the restless ghosts and you, but well, there's not much point in crying over spilt milk now, is there?
    
    |As you enter, you note rows upon rows of spectral longtables, each one easily able to seat a dozen people or more — and at each and every one of them are seated several lupines, knife and fork in hand, clearly agitated as they wait for something — a meal, most likely — that will never be served. They drum their utensils and mutter amongst themselves, casting the occasional glance at the entry archway.
    
    [pc.ra lupine
    |The specters give you a cursory glance but turn away after a moment, clearly too aggrieved at their lack of chow to pay you any serious attention once having registered you as a lupine. It's possible that they may have mistaken you for one of their own... in which case, it would probably be safe to cross the great hall just like that[party.som|| while [companion1.name] sneaks by as their attention is focused on you| while the others sneak by as their attention is focused on you].
    
    The question is: how sure are you of your guise?
    |They don't seem to have noticed you yet, but you get the feeling that walking straight into a giant room packed full of crotchety, hungry ghosts isn't the best of ideas.
    
    Well, what now?
    ]
    ]
    
    The only exits here are east out into the hallway, and west further into the garrison."

rows.original: The ghosts appear to be waiting for dinner...
rows.translation: 这些鬼魂似乎在等着吃晚餐……
rows.raw: "The ghosts appear to be waiting for dinner..."

rows.original: The ghosts appear to be waiting for dinner, but you don't have anything to serve the ethereal.
rows.translation: 那些鬼魂似乎在等着吃晚餐，但你并没有什么可以招待这些幽灵的东西。
rows.raw: "The ghosts appear to be waiting for dinner, but you don't have anything to serve the ethereal."

rows.original:
As you forge your way further down this hallway, you notice the ambient temperature drop perceptibly, enough to send you to shivering. You're not completely sure if it's a by-product of the ruins' haunting or the result of a draft which blows in through a number of cracks in the north wall, but it certainly adds to the atmosphere of this place. Winter is coming and all that.

    [flags.GARTH_QUEST_RAMPARTS_DOOR|
    Now that you've managed to get the door to the east open, nothing stands between you and the stairwell leading to the fortress' second floor. Onwards and upwards, as they say — onwards and upwards.
    |
    However, it would appear that the hallway ends here abruptly — stopped cold by a massive, metal-bound door that blocks the path to the east, still in surprisingly good condition despite how old it must be. Through a small rusted grille set in the door, you catch a peek of a stairwell on its other side.
    
    Of course, in order to get there, you'll have to deal with the door on this end first... various possibilities come to mind, some more palatable than others.
    ]
rows.translation:
当你继续沿着这条走廊前行时，你明显感觉到周围的温度在下降，低到让你不自觉地开始发抖。你并不完全确定这是这些废墟所散发出的阴森气息造成的，还是因为北墙上的许多裂缝让寒风钻了进来，但无论如何，这种温度变化确实为这个地方增添了一种阴郁的氛围。冬天即将来临，一切都在预示着这个。

    [flags.GARTH_QUEST_RAMPARTS_DOOR|
    现在你已经成功打开了通往东侧的门，那么，通往堡垒二楼的楼梯通道已经完全在你面前了。正如人们所说，继续前进吧——向上攀登吧。
    |
    然而，走廊似乎在这里突然结束了——一道巨大的金属门挡住了通往东方的道路，尽管这扇门肯定已经非常老旧了，但它依然保持着惊人的完好状态。透过门上那块生锈的小格栅，你可以隐约看到另一边有一段楼梯。
    
    当然，要想进入那里，你首先必须解决这扇门的问题……各种解决办法浮现在脑海中，有些似乎比其他的更可行。
    ]

"
    As you forge your way further down this hallway, you notice the ambient temperature drop perceptibly, enough to send you to shivering. You're not completely sure if it's a by-product of the ruins' haunting or the result of a draft which blows in through a number of cracks in the north wall, but it certainly adds to the atmosphere of this place. Winter is coming and all that.

    [flags.GARTH_QUEST_RAMPARTS_DOOR|
    Now that you've managed to get the door to the east open, nothing stands between you and the stairwell leading to the fortress' second floor. Onwards and upwards, as they say — onwards and upwards.
    |
    However, it would appear that the hallway ends here abruptly — stopped cold by a massive, metal-bound door that blocks the path to the east, still in surprisingly good condition despite how old it must be. Through a small rusted grille set in the door, you catch a peek of a stairwell on its other side.
    
    Of course, in order to get there, you'll have to deal with the door on this end first... various possibilities come to mind, some more palatable than others.
    ]"

rows.original: You'll have to do something about this if you want to get to the stairwell beyond.
rows.translation: 如果你想继续前往那边的楼梯间，就必须想办法解决这个问题。
rows.raw: "You'll have to do something about this if you want to get to the stairwell beyond."

rows.original:
This spiral stairwell leads around and up to the second level of Fort Marrok. The steps themselves don't look very trustworthy, but appearances can deceive and besides, it's not as if you've got any choice in the matter. Several of the stone flagstones are cracked, as is the central pillar; the flooring feels shaky as you put your weight on it, but at least it still holds.

    Your breathing echoes about in the tall, cylindrical stairwell, the sound bouncing off the walls over and over again until they finally fade into the oppressive darkness of this cold stone tomb.
    
    The darkness beckons.
rows.translation:
这段螺旋楼梯蜿蜒向上，通向马罗克要塞的二楼。这些台阶看起来并不十分可靠，但外表往往具有欺骗性，而且你也没有其他选择。几块石板已经出现了裂缝，中央的支柱也一样；当你踩在这些台阶上时，会感觉到地面有些摇晃，但至少它们还没有倒塌。

    你的呼吸声在高大的圆柱形楼梯间中回荡，那声音一次次地撞击着墙壁，最终消失在这座冰冷石墓的压抑黑暗之中。
    
    黑暗在召唤着你。
rows.raw:
"
    This spiral stairwell leads around and up to the second level of Fort Marrok. The steps themselves don't look very trustworthy, but appearances can deceive and besides, it's not as if you've got any choice in the matter. Several of the stone flagstones are cracked, as is the central pillar; the flooring feels shaky as you put your weight on it, but at least it still holds.

    Your breathing echoes about in the tall, cylindrical stairwell, the sound bouncing off the walls over and over again until they finally fade into the oppressive darkness of this cold stone tomb.
    
    The darkness beckons."

rows.original:
You give the assorted crockery and cookware lying over the dead hearths a look-over. They look hefty — enough that you could only carry one at a time, but if there were some reason you wanted to take one of them along with you, that would be possible — unlike the others tacked up against the walls, they're not so heavily corroded to be fused to the masonry.

    That being said, would you like to take one of them along with you? Who knows why you might want to do this, but the option remains.
rows.translation:
你仔细看了看那些堆放在废弃壁炉旁的各式各样的陶器与炊具。它们看起来相当笨重——一次只能携带一件，但如果你有特别的理由想要带走其中某件，也是完全可行的。与那些靠墙堆放的器具不同，这些器具并没有严重腐蚀到与墙壁粘连的程度。

    那么，你愿意带走其中某件吗？谁知道你为什么会想要这么做呢，但这个选择确实是存在的。
rows.raw:
"
    You give the assorted crockery and cookware lying over the dead hearths a look-over. They look hefty — enough that you could only carry one at a time, but if there were some reason you wanted to take one of them along with you, that would be possible — unlike the others tacked up against the walls, they're not so heavily corroded to be fused to the masonry.

    That being said, would you like to take one of them along with you? Who knows why you might want to do this, but the option remains."

rows.original: Might there be something of use here?
rows.translation: 这里会不会有什么有用的东西呢？
rows.raw: "Might there be something of use here?"

rows.original: You're standing in what's clearly a training hall of some sort. The room is mostly large and featureless, with windows set high in the northern wall; of course, considering the state of the fortress, none of them have seen daylight for a long, long time. Several alcoves in the walls harbor statues of lupines in various appropriately martial poses — some wielding spears, one with a longsword, another swinging a flail menacingly — all of which have survived the years in good shape. There's a lot of dust and a few extremities have crumbled, as expected, but the glory of the pack is laid out in full before you. There's a large, empty area in the back of the hall which might have once been used for storing training material, but there's nothing held there now but rot and old cobwebs. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_TOURNAMENT_DONE| Now that the tournament is over, the mats have been cleared away and some semblance of normalcy has settled upon the training hall. The ghosts continue their drills and bouts, preparing for an enemy that will never come — or if you will, an enemy that has already come and gone. It only highlights the cruelty of the circumstances of their imprisonment, but they just seem to be having so much fun going through the motions. Better that than them trying to kill you, one supposes. | The hall may be packed with spirits, but none of them appear aggressive towards you — in fact, most of them remain content to ignore your presence, instead focusing their attention on a circle of space that's formed in the middle of the training hall. A number of ghostly mats have been laid out on the hard stone floor, and it seems that the ghosts are having a competition or tournament of some sort — a simple one-on-one series of brawls with no holds barred. A cheer rises from the wolves as one of the two combatants in the circle throws the other to the ground, then quickly pounces on the poor bastard, pinning the latter down on the ground, fingers grasping his windpipe. "Desist! Desist! And the round is over! Five minutes until the next!" The victor lends the defeated a hand up, and the two leave the circle laughing as if nothing had ever happened. Two more enter, and it looks like the cycle is about to begin anew. ] The only exit from the training hall lies south, away from the merriment and fierce competition.
rows.translation: 你正站在一个显然是某种训练场的地方。房间很大，几乎没有什么装饰，窗户开在北墙高处；当然，考虑到这座堡垒的状况，它们已经很久没见过天日了。墙上的几个壁龛里立着狼族的雕像，摆出各种恰当的战斗姿态——有的手持长矛，一个握着长剑，另一个威胁性地挥舞着连枷——所有雕像都历经岁月而保存完好。灰尘积得很厚，有几处突出的部位已经崩落，这在所难免，但狼群的荣光完整地展现在你面前。 大厅的后面有一块很大的空地，那里可能曾经被用来存放训练用品，但现在那里只有腐烂的物品和陈旧的蜘蛛网。 [flags.GARTH_QUEST_TOURNAMENT_DONE| 既然比赛已经结束，垫子也被清理干净，训练场恢复了几分正常的模样。那些幽灵继续操练和对打，为一个永远不会到来的敌人做准备——或者说，为一个早已来过又离去的敌人做准备。这只会更凸显他们被囚禁的残酷，但它们似乎非常享受这种走过场的过程。总比它们想杀你好，大概吧。 | 大厅里可能充满了各种灵体，但它们并没有表现出任何攻击性——事实上，大多数灵体都选择忽略你的存在，而是将注意力集中在训练大厅中央那个特定的区域上。在坚硬的石地上铺着许多诡异的垫子，看来那些鬼魂们正在举行某种竞赛或比试——一场毫无规则、简单的一对一斗殴。 当圈中的其中一名战斗者将对手摔倒在地，然后迅速扑了上去，将对方压在地面，手指紧紧掐住对方的喉咙时，狼群中爆发出一阵欢呼声。 停止！停止！这一轮结束啦！距离下一轮还有五分钟！ 胜利者伸出手帮助失败者，两人笑着离开了那个圈子，仿佛什么都没有发生过。又有两个人走了进来，看来这个循环即将重新开始。 ] 训练厅唯一的出口位于南方，远离那些欢乐与激烈的竞争。

The room is mostly large and featureless, with windows set high in the northern wall; of course, considering the state of the fortress, none of them have seen daylight for a long, long time. Several alcoves in the walls harbor statues of lupines in various appropriately martial poses — some wielding spears, one with a longsword, another swinging a flail menacingly — all of which have survived the years in good shape. There's a lot of dust and a few extremities have crumbled, as expected, but the glory of the pack is laid out in full before you. There's a large, empty area in the back of the hall which might have once been used for storing training material, but there's nothing held there now but rot and old cobwebs. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_TOURNAMENT_DONE| Now that the tournament is over, the mats have been cleared away and some semblance of normalcy has settled upon the training hall. The ghosts continue their drills and bouts, preparing for an enemy that will never come — or if you will, an enemy that has already come and gone. It only highlights the cruelty of the circumstances of their imprisonment, but they just seem to be having so much fun going through the motions. Better that than them trying to kill you, one supposes. | The hall may be packed with spirits, but none of them appear aggressive towards you — in fact, most of them remain content to ignore your presence, instead focusing their attention on a circle of space that's formed in the middle of the training hall. A number of ghostly mats have been laid out on the hard stone floor, and it seems that the ghosts are having a competition or tournament of some sort — a simple one-on-one series of brawls with no holds barred. A cheer rises from the wolves as one of the two combatants in the circle throws the other to the ground, then quickly pounces on the poor bastard, pinning the latter down on the ground, fingers grasping his windpipe. "Desist! Desist! And the round is over! Five minutes until the next!" The victor lends the defeated a hand up, and the two leave the circle laughing as if nothing had ever happened. Two more enter, and it looks like the cycle is about to begin anew. ] The only exit from the training hall lies south, away from the merriment and fierce competition."

rows.original: Watch the tournament a little more closely.
rows.raw: "Watch the tournament a little more closely."

rows.original: You're standing in what looks to be a library or study of some sort. The frames of two ancient desks still stand, while their attendant seats have collapsed in heaps of dry rot and dusty residue. Instead of shelves, numerous rectangular recesses and cubbyholes have been cut into the walls, each one large enough to house a comfortable number of tomes. A small border of runes lines each nook, and judging by the reasonable condition of the books held within you figure they must be preservation wards or something similar. The jarl and his pack may have been a warlike people, but they certainly knew the value of a good book. At the foot of one of the cubbyholes, a tarnished brass chest rests. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_CHEST_OPENED |Now that the trap's deactivated and there's nothing left in there, it's of no further interest to you. ] Mounted high on the wall, above the collection of tomes, a single large plaque rests: No branches, but has leaves. No bones, but has a spine. Many overlook its import Yet 'tis more precious than wine. The only way out from here is east through the entry archway and back out to the ramparts corridor.
rows.translation: 你此刻站在一个看起来像是图书馆或书房的房间里。两张古老书桌的框架依然立在那里，而配套的座椅早已坍塌成一堆干腐的碎屑和灰尘。墙上没有书架，而是凿出了许多长方形的壁龛和小格子，每一个都大到足以容纳相当数量的书籍。每个格子边缘都有一圈细小的符文，从里面所藏书籍的状况来看，你认为这些符文应该是保存结界之类的东西。那位酋长和他的狼群也许是好战的民族，但他们显然懂得一本好书的珍贵。 在一个小隔间的底部，放着一个已经失去光泽的黄铜箱子。 [flags.GARTH_QUEST_CHEST_OPENED |现在陷阱已经失效，里面也没有任何东西了，所以它对你来说已经没有任何意义了。 ] 高悬在墙上，位于那些典籍之上，有一块巨大的牌匾静静地陈列着： 没有树枝，却有叶子； 没有骨头，却有脊柱。 许多人忽视了它的价值， 然而，它比葡萄酒还要珍贵。 从这里出去的唯一办法就是向东穿过入口拱门，然后回到城墙走廊。

The frames of two ancient desks still stand, while their attendant seats have collapsed in heaps of dry rot and dusty residue. Instead of shelves, numerous rectangular recesses and cubbyholes have been cut into the walls, each one large enough to house a comfortable number of tomes. A small border of runes lines each nook, and judging by the reasonable condition of the books held within you figure they must be preservation wards or something similar. The jarl and his pack may have been a warlike people, but they certainly knew the value of a good book. At the foot of one of the cubbyholes, a tarnished brass chest rests. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_CHEST_OPENED |Now that the trap's deactivated and there's nothing left in there, it's of no further interest to you. ] Mounted high on the wall, above the collection of tomes, a single large plaque rests: No branches, but has leaves. No bones, but has a spine. Many overlook its import Yet 'tis more precious than wine. The only way out from here is east through the entry archway and back out to the ramparts corridor."

rows.original: This looks like it could hold something interesting.
rows.translation: 这看起来似乎藏着一些有趣的东西。
rows.raw: "This looks like it could hold something interesting."

rows.original:
Like the corridor outside, this watchtower looks different in make and slightly newer than the rest of the fortress. The bricks are finer here, the walls and ground more carefully smoothed, and the entry doorway is more square than the arches which dominate the architecture of the rest of the fortress.

    The remnants of weapon racks lie along one wall, the halberds within advanced stages of decay with the handles long gone and their blades brown, formless lumps. Upon an ancient, worm-eaten table, tarnished silverware and a tankard, strewn about as if someone was interrupted in the middle of a meal. In a corner, a number of footlockers which have managed to weather the years.
    
    Arrow slits in the walls would have once looked out upon the advance to the fortress, perhaps, but buried as they are beneath so much cold soil and dirt, the only thing they now look out upon is a cold death.
    
    The only exit is out west to the corridor.
rows.translation:
就像外面的走廊一样，这座瞭望塔在建造工艺上与其他堡垒的部分有所不同，也显得稍微新一些。这里的砖块更加精致，墙壁和地面也经过更加精细的打磨，入口处的门框也是方形的，而堡垒其他部分的建筑风格则以拱门为主。

    残破的武器架沿着一条墙摆放，里面的戟已经腐朽到了后期阶段，握柄早已不见，刃部也变成了褐色、没有形状的团块。在一张被虫蛀的古老桌子上，失去光泽的银器和一个大酒杯散乱地放着，仿佛有人在用餐中途被打断了。角落里还有几个历经岁月而留存下来的储物箱。
    
    墙上的箭孔原本或许可以用来观察敌人向堡垒发起的进攻，但如今它们被厚厚的积土所掩盖，因此所能看到的，只有冰冷的死亡。
    
    唯一的出口是在西边，通往那条走廊。
rows.raw:
"
    Like the corridor outside, this watchtower looks different in make and slightly newer than the rest of the fortress. The bricks are finer here, the walls and ground more carefully smoothed, and the entry doorway is more square than the arches which dominate the architecture of the rest of the fortress.

    The remnants of weapon racks lie along one wall, the halberds within advanced stages of decay with the handles long gone and their blades brown, formless lumps. Upon an ancient, worm-eaten table, tarnished silverware and a tankard, strewn about as if someone was interrupted in the middle of a meal. In a corner, a number of footlockers which have managed to weather the years.
    
    Arrow slits in the walls would have once looked out upon the advance to the fortress, perhaps, but buried as they are beneath so much cold soil and dirt, the only thing they now look out upon is a cold death.
    
    The only exit is out west to the corridor."

rows.original: Grab the silverware off the tables.
See if there's anything worth salvaging in the footlockers.
rows.translation: 看看那些储物箱里有没有什么值得回收的东西。
rows.raw: "See if there's anything worth salvaging in the footlockers."

rows.original: The top of the stairs, at last. This tower — at least, it feels like a tower, with all the stone steps you've just climbed — makes up the third floor of Fort Marrok. This landing might have been carpeted once — a change from the bare stone that floors the entire fortress — but if not, there's one now. The air up here is especially stale — not surprising, considering all the dust on the floor — and the landing is quite featureless save for two stone fountains at the base of either wall. By some miracle, these fountains are still working; although the flow of water over so many years has eroded away at the basins, it nevertheless still gushes freely, adding a faint gurgle and rush to the sepulchral silence of these halls. Ahead of you to the south lies a large set of double doors, massive ironbound things with their wood more petrified than rotted. One of the duo has set in place thanks to its rusted hinges, but the other has given way some time over the years and has collapsed onto the floor, lending you a view into the darkness beyond, in which something — no, someone shifts and stirs. [party.has cait| "This is it," Cait murmurs behind you. "That presence..." ] You are now faced with a choice: south and ahead into the darkness, or retreat north down the stairs.
rows.translation: 终于来到了楼梯的顶端。这座塔——至少从你刚刚攀爬的那些石阶来看，它确实像一座塔——实际上是马罗克要塞的第三层。这个平台或许曾经铺过地毯，这与要塞其他地方光秃秃的石地面形成了对比；但如果没有的话，现在也已经铺上了地毯。 这里的空气格外浑浊——考虑到地板上积满了灰尘，这也并不奇怪。这个厅堂的设计相当简单，除了两座位于墙壁两侧的石制喷泉外，几乎没有其他装饰。奇迹般的是，这些喷泉至今仍在运转；尽管经过多年的水流侵蚀，喷泉基座已经严重损坏，但水依然源源不断地流淌出来，为这些阴森寂静的厅堂带来一丝轻微的潺潺声。 你前方的南面是一扇巨大的双开门，铁包边的庞然大物，木质与其说是腐朽，不如说是已经石化。两扇门中的一扇因生锈的铰链卡在原处，另一扇则在某一年月里脱了位，倒在地上，让你得以窥见门后的黑暗——那里有什么东西——不，是有人——在移动、在辗转。 [party.has cait| 就是这里了。凯特在你身后轻声说道。那种存在…… ] 你现在面临着一个选择：是向南前进，进入黑暗之中，还是退回北方，沿着楼梯下去。
rows.raw: ' The top of the stairs, at last. This tower — at least, it feels like a tower, with all the stone steps you've just climbed — makes up the third floor of Fort Marrok. This landing might have been carpeted once — a change from the bare stone that floors the entire fortress — but if not, there's one now. The air up here is especially stale — not surprising, considering all the dust on the floor — and the landing is quite featureless save for two stone fountains at the base of either wall. By some miracle, these fountains are still working; although the flow of water over so many years has eroded away at the basins, it nevertheless still gushes freely, adding a faint gurgle and rush to the sepulchral silence of these halls. Ahead of you to the south lies a large set of double doors, massive ironbound things with their wood more petrified than rotted. One of the duo has set in place thanks to its rusted hinges, but the other has given way some time over the years and has collapsed onto the floor, lending you a view into the darkness beyond, in which something — no, someone shifts and stirs. [party.has cait| "This is it," Cait murmurs behind you. "That presence..." ] You are now faced with a choice: south and ahead into the darkness, or retreat north down the stairs.'

rows.original: Take a sip from the fountains.
rows.translation: 从这些喷泉中喝上几口吧。

rows.original:
The closer you draw to the south end of the hall, the more the temperature plummets, until you're practically shivering in your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] as you make your way forward. Your footsteps ring hollow in the vastness of the cavernous chamber, and somewhere from above, water drips down in a steady drip-drip-drip, collecting on the old stone floor in shallow puddles. 

    At least the eerie glow in the air hasn't diminished any, allowing you to take in the scene as it draws into view. The stone throne is the only piece of furniture that's still physically present — everything else from the banners to the candlesticks to the carpet is ghostly and translucent, fading into view and solidifying before your very eyes as you forge your way forward.
    
    This is it.
    
    By and large, your footsteps aren't the only sounds in this chamber now. A faint panting, wheezing, the labored breathing of someone being smothered; the figure in the throne leans forward, doubled over in unending agony, hunched over with both hands on the pommel of a bastard sword. He leans his weight on it like an old man on his cane, the blade still in its scabbard, its point delicately balanced on the floor.
    
    This must be the jarl, then. The muzzle sticking out from above the heavy, fur-lined cloak, the broad-shouldered stature, and most of all, the medallion hanging from his neck by a heavy gold chain, gold untarnished by the years and sapphires glinting in the eldritch light.
    
    What do you do now? You're mere paces from the jarl at this very moment; if you're going to do something, you have the initiative. Calling yourself to arms and putting him out of his misery might be the obvious thing to do, but could there possibly be some way to break apart the false reality that's enshrouded his mind and by extent, this entire accursed fortress?
    
    [var0|
    It might be doable, if you had a silver mirror on you. You faintly remember hearing old old wives' tales about most undead not having reflections in normal mirrors, but silver ones are apparently an exception. If the jarl could see his dead self, it might help break whatever spell's ensnared his mind.
    
    [pc.hasKeyItem SilverMirror
        |And it just so happens you managed to acquire one, and in this place no less.
        |Unfortunately, you don't have one on you. Might you still want to try, though? It's not as if you have anything to lose by making the attempt.
    ]
    ]
rows.translation:
你越靠近大厅南端，气温就降得越低，等你一路往前走时，已经冷得让你的[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]都在发抖。你的脚步声在这洞穴般的巨大空间里回荡出空洞的响声，头顶某处有水滴稳定地滴答滴答落下，在古老的石地上积成浅浅的水洼。

    至少空中那种诡异的光芒丝毫没有减弱，让你能看清渐渐映入眼帘的景象。那座石制王座是唯一仍然实际存在的家具——从旗帜到烛台再到地毯，其他一切都呈现出幽灵般的半透明状态，随着你向前走，在你眼前逐渐浮现、凝实。
    
    就是现在。
    
    再说，现在这厅里响着的不只是你的脚步声。微弱的喘息、呼哧声，那是被人闷住的艰难呼吸；王座上的身影向前倾着，因无尽的痛苦而佝偻，双手撑在一把双手剑的剑柄上。他像老人拄拐那样把重心压在上面，剑仍插在鞘中，剑尖轻轻点着地面。
    
    那么，这一定就是那位酋长了。从那件厚重的毛皮衬里斗篷上方探出的口鼻部，那宽阔的肩膀，尤其是他脖子上用粗重金链挂着的那枚圆形徽章——黄金历经岁月而未失光泽，蓝宝石在诡异的光线中闪烁。
    
    你现在要做什么？此刻你距离那位酋长只有几步之遥；如果你想做点什么，主动权在你手上。拔剑上前、结束他的痛苦，也许是最显而易见的做法，但是否有办法打破笼罩他心智、并进而笼罩整座受诅咒堡垒的虚假现实呢？
    
    [var0|
    如果你身上有一面银镜，也许就能做到。你隐约记得听过一些老掉牙的无稽之谈，说大多数亡灵在普通镜子里没有倒影，但银镜似乎是个例外。如果那位酋长能看到自己死后的样子，也许就能打破束缚他心智的咒语。
    
    [pc.hasKeyItem SilverMirror
        |而巧的是，你竟然得到了这么一个，而且还是在这样的一个地方。
        |不幸的是，你身上并没有它。不过，你还是想试试看吗？尝试一下并不会让你有任何损失。
    ]
    ]

rows.original: Strike down the jarl. There is no other way.
rows.translation: 必须除掉那个酋长。没有其他办法了。
rows.raw: "Strike down the jarl. There is no other way."

rows.original: Attempt to tell Galon Gunvaldsen the ugly truth.
rows.translation: 试图告诉加隆·冈瓦尔德森这个残酷的真相。
rows.raw: "Attempt to tell Galon Gunvaldsen the ugly truth."

rows.original:
The top of the stairwell. Looking down at the huge stone steps spiraling down into the void below, you have to wonder how something didn't manage to fall out from under you, or alternatively, fall down onto you. Fort Marrok might be solidly built, but even so, time's fire is fierce and unrelenting.

    Now that you're standing here, you realize that the stairwell is designed in such a way that sounds at the bottom are amplified as they travel upwards, such that each scratch and echo from the lower landing comes cleanly to your hearing. It would be useful, considering that the stairwell would be a bottleneck for any invading army... 
    
    Hm...
    
    The only exits from here are north and out to the second floor, or back down to the first if you were so inclined.
rows.translation:
楼梯的顶端。俯瞰那些蜿蜒向下、通向下方虚空的巨大石阶，你不禁会想：究竟是什么力量让这些石阶始终稳稳地固定在原地，而没有从你脚下掉落下来，或者砸到你身上呢？虽然马罗克要塞的建筑结构十分坚固，但时间的侵蚀力依然是强大而无情的。

    现在你站在这里，才意识到这座楼梯的设计使得底部的声音向上传播时会被放大，因此从下方平台传来的每一声刮擦和回响都清晰地传进你耳中。考虑到楼梯井会成为任何入侵军队的瓶颈，这可真有用……
    
    嗯……
    
    从这里出发，唯一的出口要么是往北通往二楼，要么就是返回一楼。

rows.original:
The interior of the frozen tower was once a workshop, though if this was set up before or after the rest of the structure sunk into the ice... you can't say at a glance. There's a solid floor of cobbled stone, and racks of armorer's tools hang from pegs nailed into the walls. An anvil sits in the middle of the chamber, but there's no forge to speak of. 

    A pair of threadbare banners are draped besides the door. One displays a minotaur warrior gird in ice-blue armor, an axe held high. The other: a circle of white-scaled nagas surrounding an empty throne, high on a dias.
    
    [flags.FRZ_TOWER_CLEAR|It seems safe enough here, now that the spirit has been put to rest. Camping here would be a sweet reprieve from the howling winds of the Rift.|The pounding sound you heard from outside — clearly the work of that anvil — stops suddenly when you enter, and does not resume. Nevertheless, you feel like you're being watched... this is clearly an unsafe place to dawdle.]
rows.translation:
这座被冰封的塔内部曾经是一间工坊，不过很难确定这是在该建筑的其他部分沉入冰层之前还是之后建造的……一眼是看不出来的。地面铺着鹅卵石，墙上钉着钉子，架子上挂着各种打造盔甲的工具。房间中央摆着一个铁砧，但根本没有什么锻炉。

    门边悬挂着两面破旧的旗帜。其中一面上画着一位身穿冰蓝色铠甲、高举斧头的弥诺陶洛斯战士；另一面上则描绘着一圈白色鳞片的娜迦怪围着高台上的空王座。
    
    [flags.FRZ_TOWER_CLEAR|现在灵魂已经得到安息，这里看起来已经足够安全了。在这里露营，确实能够让人远离裂谷那呼啸的风声，享受到片刻的宁静。|当你走进去时，外面传来的那阵剧烈声响——显然就是那个铁砧发出的声音——突然停止了，再也没有继续下去。然而，你却感觉有人在注视着你……显然，这个地方可不是闲逛的好地方。]

rows.original: Take the Ring of Fate back to Khor'minos.
rows.translation: 将命运之环带回科尔米诺斯。
rows.raw: "Take the Ring of Fate back to Khor'minos."

rows.original: You haven't gotten the ring yet...
rows.translation: 你还没有得到那枚戒指……

rows.original:
There is a tremendous mausoleum at the end of the southern hall. Once it might have been secured by a pair of heavy bronze-faced doors, but they've been cracked open and left hanging in splinters off the hinges. A huge mural dominates all the walls within, displaying a primitive minotaur king in fur-lined hides and a golden belt, breastplate, and crown lifting up a tremendous labrys over his head. The king's face is obscured by a strange, bearded mask wrought in a perpetual grimace, with a mob of curly copper hair. 

    The tomb of the First King sits before you on a raised plinth, [flags.RING_GEMS
        |closed once more after your tomb-robbing but unsecured without its lock
        |still secured by a lock displaying a myriad of gemstones
    ].
rows.translation:
在南厅的尽头，有一座规模庞大的陵墓。它曾经被一对重型的青铜门所封闭，但现在那些门已经裂开，门扇只剩下碎片挂在门轴上。陵墓内部的墙壁上绘有巨大的壁画，画中描绘了一位身披毛皮、佩戴金色腰带、胸甲和王冠的原始弥诺陶洛斯国王，他正高举着一柄巨大的战斧。国王的面容被一个奇特的、布满胡须的面具遮住，那个面具永远保持着一种阴沉的表情，面具上还长着一簇卷曲的铜色头发。

    第一位国王的陵墓就坐落在你面前的高台上。 [flags.RING_GEMS
        |在你洗劫了它的墓穴之后，它又一次被关上了，但由于没有锁，它仍然处于不安全的状态。
        |仍然被一把镶嵌着无数宝石的锁锁住
    ].

    ]."

rows.original: Perhaps this ancient king of the minotaurs was buried with something that could help you on your quest.
rows.translation: 也许这位弥诺陶洛斯的古老国王被埋葬时，带了一些能够帮助你完成任务的物品。
rows.raw: "Perhaps this ancient king of the minotaurs was buried with something that could help you on your quest."

rows.original:
A lone grave sits in the final chamber on this long passage, humble in its own adornment but surrounded by a mural that depicts the goddesses Tira and Sorra, far larger than life, shaking hands in friendship. Beneath them, closer to human size, are a pair of cowgirls, one dressed in black robes and the other in a feather tunic that leaves little to the imagination. The two cows are locked in a loving embrace, holding each other tightly.

    [party.comp brint brienne|Brint scratches his chin, looking at the mural. "I think this was the first king's daughter. She was called to Sorra, came up to the mountains to learn with the harpies back before they were so... y'know."|Brienne smiles to herself, looking up at the mural. "I think this was the first king's daughter. She was called to Sorra, came up to the mountains to learn with the harpies back before they were so... y'know."]
rows.translation:
在这条长长通道的最后一间厅室里，有一座孤零零的坟墓。它的装饰很朴素，但四周的壁画描绘了蒂拉与索拉两位女神——身形远比真人巨大——友好地握着手。在她们下方，接近真人大小的是两个牛女：一个穿着黑色长袍，另一个穿着一件几乎遮不住什么的羽毛束腰衣。两个牛女紧紧相拥，深情地抱在一起。

    [party.comp brint brienne|布林特挠了挠下巴，看着壁画。“我想这应该是第一位国王的女儿。她受到索拉的召唤，来到群山中跟随那些鸟身女妖学习——那时候她们还没那么……你知道的。”|布蕾妮微微一笑，抬头看着壁画。“我想这应该是第一位国王的女儿。她受到索拉的召唤，来到群山中跟随那些鸟身女妖学习——那时候她们还没那么……你知道的。”]

rows.original: Perhaps this ancient priestess of Sorra was buried with something that could help you on your quest.
rows.translation: 也许这位古老的索拉女祭司被埋葬时，带了一些能够帮助你完成任务的物品。
rows.raw: "Perhaps this ancient priestess of Sorra was buried with something that could help you on your quest."

rows.original:
You pluck the gold token out of your pack and flash it at Rooh. The tall cow-lad blinks and takes the coin-sized trinket, scrutinizing it up and down. After a few seconds, he straightens up, looking more serious than before. "Haven't seen one of these since training. Right, you can go on in."
    
    The other guard with him takes a horn from his belt and gives it a [silly
        |doot
        |quick bellow
    ], and the gate begins to open. 
    
    Well, that was easy.
    
    [flags.ROOH_BJ_GUARD_M
        |The bull-stud gives [party.has cait
            |you and Cait both a rough ass-grab
            |your [pc.butt] an affectionate pat
        ] as you pass him by. [party.has cait
            |Cait blows him a kiss and gives him a wink.
        ]
    ]
rows.translation:
你从背包里掏出那枚金色信物，在鲁赫面前晃了晃。这个高大的牛小子眨了眨眼，接过这枚硬币大小的饰物，上上下下仔细端详。几秒钟后，他直起身，神情比先前严肃多了。“自打训练时起我就没见过这种东西。好了，你可以进去了。”
    
    和他一起的那名守卫从腰带上取下一只号角，吹了[silly
        |嘟嘟声
        |迅速咆哮
    ]，大门开始缓缓打开。
    
    嗯，这还挺简单的。
    
    [flags.ROOH_BJ_GUARD_M
        |这头公牛壮汉在你经过时，[party.has cait
            |狠狠地捏了你和凯特的屁股一把
            |在你那[pc.butt]上亲昵地拍了一下
        ]。 [party.has cait
            |凯特向他飞了个吻，还冲他眨了眨眼。
        ]
    ]

rows.original:
Once you're through the gates, you roll your shoulders and take a look around. The inside of the city's west quarter is much less grand than the main street you've mostly stuck to so far; a grid of narrow streets and alleys dividing up blocks of modest homes wherein the bulk of the city's population dwells. The thoroughfares have been hastily covered by repurposed fishing net and sharpened stakes, anything the locals can gather up to protect themselves from a potential swarm of imps flying over the city walls. 
        
        Despite the threat of war looming over the city, though, the people of Khor'minos are still trying to live. The streets are crowded with bouncy cowgirls and laughing children all in their colorful togas, and there are peddlers lining the streets hawking cheap clothes and jewelry. There are foodsellers, too, all with thick crowds around their carts — and the prices you hear being called for are exorbitant. 
        
        [party.has cait
            |Cait grimaces. "It's almost criminal what they're charging. But it's hard to blame them; they don't have much left to sell, I bet."
        ]
        
        [party.has brint
            |Brint gives one of the hawkers a dour look, clenching his fist around his axe.
        ]
        
        [party.has brienne
            |Brienne sighs, shaking her head. "Everything's so expensive now..."
        ]
        
        [party.has ryn
            |"Maybe Njorhaalt can help," Ryn murmurs. "We had a strong harvest this year... but there's so many people..."
        ]
        
        You move through the crowd, towards the small river that runs from the upper terraces of the city and down into the west quarter. A few small boats are moored along it, and one decently-sized cargo barge. You're just in time to see a pair of minotaurs in Royal Navy blue cloaks hefting up a crate emblazoned with a crimson labrys off it, hauling it into a wide structure by the waterfront. 
        
        "There's the goods," you say, hopping down onto one of the boats moored on your side of the river. A few curious cows watch you from the bank, but nobody lifts a hand to stop you save a single elderly fisherman waggling his rod at you. You pass him by quick enough. It's easy to hop from deck to deck, until you're clambering onto the cargo barge. There's sounds of hooves clattering on the stone from the other side of the warehouse, followed by the commotion of workers rushing around. 
        
        The princess has arrived, right on time. And she'll be a perfect distraction while you slip inside and do some counter-snooping.
rows.translation:
一穿过城门，你活动了一下肩膀，环顾四周。城市西区的内部远不如你此前主要行走的主街那样气派——一片由狭窄街道和小巷组成的网格，把一处处朴素的住宅区切割开来，城里的大部分人口就住在那里面。这些街巷被当地居民匆忙地用改造过的渔网和削尖的木桩遮了起来，凡是能收集到的东西都拿来用了，以防成群的小恶魔飞过城墙。
        
        然而，尽管战争的威胁笼罩着这座城市，科尔米诺斯的人们仍在努力继续生活。街道上挤满了穿着色彩鲜艳长袍、活泼好动的牛仔女孩和欢声笑语的孩子们，沿街还有小贩在兜售廉价的衣服和首饰。也有卖食物的小贩，他们的摊位周围总是围着密密麻麻的人群——而那些被叫出的价格实在高得离谱。 
        
        [party.has cait
            |凯特皱起脸。“他们收的价钱简直跟抢劫差不多。但也很难怪他们；我敢打赌，他们手里已经没剩多少东西可卖了。”
        ]
        
        [party.has brint
            |布林特狠狠地瞪了其中一个小贩一眼，同时将拳头紧紧握在斧头周围。
        ]
        
        [party.has brienne
            |布蕾妮叹了口气，摇了摇头。“现在什么都太贵了……”
        ]
        
        [party.has ryn
            |“也许尼约哈尔特能帮上忙，”瑞恩低声说。“今年我们的收成很好……可是人实在太多了……”
        ]
        
        你穿过人群，朝那条从城市上层平台流下、穿过西区的小河走去。河边系着几条小船，还有一艘体量不小的货驳船。你正好看见两个披着皇家海军蓝斗篷的弥诺陶洛斯从船上抬起一只印着深红色双刃斧的箱子，拖进河岸边一栋宽大的建筑里。
        
        “货在那儿，”你说着，跳上你这一侧河岸边系着的一条船。几头好奇的牛从岸上看着你，只有一个年迈的渔夫挥着鱼竿想拦你。你很快就从他身边过去了。从一条甲板跳到另一条甲板很容易，直到你爬上了那艘货驳船。仓库另一侧传来蹄子敲击石地的声音，接着是工人们四处奔忙的骚动。
        
        公主准时到了。你溜进去做些反侦察的时候，她会是个绝佳的掩护。

rows.original: You find somewhere concealed from view and wait, watching your chosen cargo with an eagle eye. Nobody's getting past you. And so you wait. And wait. Until you finally hear the warehouse door opening. Yes, this is it. Here comes the spy! Two spies! Right on time. A pair of minotaurs in heavy workman clothes march up to the cargo and start looking it over, checking its tags and comparing it to a tablet one of them is carrying. You leap from your concealment and draw your [pc.weapon], demanding the pair of them drop what they're holding and surrender in the name of the crown. There's a bellow of surprise from one, and the other drops his tablet. It shatters on the stone floor. "Fuck! Wh-what did we do? What's going on?" You just hold them there for a minute or two until Varena and her bodyguards finally arrive. The princess hurries over to you, dress hiked up in her hands, an eager look on her face. "You did it!" she beams, wrapping you in a fierce hug while the pair of Chargers trailing her slap manacles around the ne'er-do-wells. "Wow, you must've chased them all over the place, huh?" "Huh?" you echo. Varena points across the warehouse. "Well the stuff's over there, so..." "Ah, shit." "... You got the wrong cargo?" "I got the wrong cargo." The princess throws up her hands. "How hard is it to find a red labrys! Big axe, color of blood, royal sigil. I told you twice what it was!" You fidget awkwardly while Varena orders the release of the dock workers. The two men scamper off as quick as they can. "Some help you are," the princess sighs. "Do you know how expensive this was to set up? It'll be weeks before I can get more cargo in." One of the Chargers clears his throat. "Maybe you ought to listen to your father, princess. There's nobody following you, except the Champion here." Despite Varena's royal title, there's a commanding edge to the soldier's voice. The kind that brooks no debate. You doubt the Chargers are going to let Varena get away with this again, even if she wants to. The princess scrunches up her lips in a furious pout, and then storms off the way she came. The soldiers give you a reproachful look and follow her. Well, shit.
rows.translation: 你找到一个隐蔽的地方藏好，用鹰隼般的目光盯着你选定的那批货物。没人能溜过你。 于是你等着。 等着。 直到你终于听见仓库的门被打开。没错，就是现在。间谍来了！ 两个间谍！来得正是时候。两个穿着厚重工装的弥诺陶洛斯走到货物前，开始翻看起来，检查标签，并与其中一人手里拿着的石板作比对。 你从藏身处一跃而出，拔出你的[pc.weapon]，命令他们两个放下手里的东西，以王室之名投降。 其中一个发出一声惊吼，另一个则把手里的石板掉在地上，摔得粉碎。“操！我、我们做了什么？这是怎么回事？” 你就那样把他们按在那儿一两分钟，直到瓦蕾娜和她的保镖们终于赶到。公主快步跑到你身边，双手提着裙摆，脸上满是急切的神情。“你做到了！”她笑着说，紧紧抱住你，而她身后的两名冲锋者则把镣铐扣在了这两个歹人手上。“哇，你肯定把他们追得满城跑了吧，嗯？” “嗯？”你应了一声。 瓦蕾娜指向仓库另一边。“呃，那些东西在那边，所以……” “啊，糟了。” “……你搞错货了？” “我搞错货了。” 公主双手一摊。“找一批红色双刃斧图案的货有多难！大斧头，血一样的颜色，还有王室徽记。我都跟你说过两遍了！” 瓦蕾娜下令放走码头工人时，你尴尬地扭来扭去。那两个人飞快地跑掉了。 “你可真帮了大忙，”公主叹道。“你知道布置这些花了多少钱吗？我得等好几周才能再进一批货。” 一名冲锋者清了清嗓子。“公主，也许您该听听您父亲的话。除了这位冠军，根本没人跟着您。” 尽管瓦蕾娜顶着公主的头衔，那士兵的语气里却带着一种命令的意味——那种不容争辩的意味。你怀疑冲锋者们不会让瓦蕾娜再把这种事胡闹下去，哪怕她想。 公主气鼓鼓地撅起嘴，然后顺着原路冲了出去。士兵们责备地看了你一眼，跟了上去。 唉，真糟糕。

rows.original: Varena's righteously upset, but maybe you can make it up to her?
rows.translation: 瓦蕾娜感到非常委屈，不过也许你可以弥补她的损失吧？
rows.raw: "Varena's righteously upset, but maybe you can make it up to her?"

rows.original: You sigh and turn back the way you came as well.
rows.translation: 你叹了口气，也转身走回了来时的路。
rows.raw: "\n        You sigh and turn back the way you came as well.\n        "

rows.original: You should just leave before you upset her further.
rows.translation: 你最好现在就离开，免得让她更加难过。
rows.raw: "You should just leave before you upset her further."

rows.original: You find somewhere concealed from view and wait, watching the labrys-marked crates with an eagle eye. Nobody's getting past you. And so you wait. And you aren't left waiting long. Just a few moments after you've taken up overwatch, there's a flash of movement falling from the beams overhead, dropping cat-like onto a few sacks of salt laid out just beside the princess's goods. The figure's lithe and silent, dressed all in black. A shadow in the shape of a woman. You watch her search around the crates, then grab the crowbar from where it hangs from a support beam beside them. She wedges the lever in and starts to pry the top of one open, quiet as a mouse. Alright, that's far enough. You have your quarry. You leap out from your vantage and draw your weapon. "Hold it right there!" The spy spins around with a gasp. Her black hood falls back, letting a pair of bunny ears spring into view. The crowbar in her hand clatters to the floor. "Who are — oh, shit, you're the Champion!" "Why are you spying on Varena?" you demand. "Why are you helping a traitor?" the bunny snaps back. Her slim body tenses, but you're able to grab her before she can make a break for it, shoving her hard against one of the crates. "Let me go! [pc.mf |Bastard |Bitch ]!" Not likely. You just hold her there for a minute or two until Varena and her bodyguards finally arrive. The princess hurries over to you, dress hiked up in her hands, an eager look on her face. "You did it!" she beams, wrapping you in a fierce hug while the pair of Chargers trailing her slap manacles around the ne'er-do-well. Varena gives the two big bulls with her a devastatingly smug look. "See, what did I tell you?" One of the troopers grunts, wrenching the shadowy bunny down on her knees. The other pats her down, revealing a set of lockpicks and a small dagger hidden in her robes. The princess tenses when the knife is drawn out, but you put a reassuring hand on her shoulder. "She didn't pull it on me when she had the chance. I don't think she's an assassin." "Yeah! I'm not a killer!" the bunny squeaks, looking up at two massive minotaurs looming over her. "Take it easy." Varena squats down, getting onto her level. "So what are you, then? Who are you working for?" "I'm not telling you shit!" The spy squirms in her restraints. "Traitor!" You glance at Varena, but the expression on her face seems like genuine confusion to you. The princess pouts, bovine ears flicking up and down. "Explain yourself." No answer's forthcoming. Varena looks to you. How do you go about finding your answers?
rows.translation: 你找到一个隐蔽的地方藏好，用鹰隼般的目光盯着那些标有双刃斧印记的箱子。没人能溜过你。 于是你等着。 而你并没有等太久。 你刚开始警戒没多久，头顶的横梁上就闪过一道身影，像猫一样轻巧地落在一旁几袋盐上——就在公主那批货物旁边。那身影轻盈无声，一身黑衣。一个女人的形状的阴影。你看着她翻找那些箱子，然后从旁边的支撑梁上取下撬棍，把杠杆卡进箱盖，开始悄无声息地撬开其中一个，安静得像只老鼠。 好了，足够了。你的猎物到手了。 你从藏身处跳出来，拔出武器。“站住！” 那间谍惊呼一声转过身来。她的黑色兜帽滑落，一对兔耳弹了出来。她手里的撬棍当啷掉在地上。“你是谁——哦，糟了，你是那位冠军！” “你为什么要监视瓦蕾娜？”你质问道。 “那你又为什么要帮一个叛徒？”兔子反唇相讥。她纤细的身体绷紧了，但你在她试图逃跑前抓住了她，把她狠狠按在一个箱子上。“放开我！[pc.mf |混蛋 |贱人 ]！” 想得美。 你就那样把她按住一两分钟，直到瓦蕾娜和她的保镖们终于赶到。公主快步跑到你身边，双手提着裙摆，脸上满是急切的神情。“你做到了！”她笑着说，紧紧抱住你，而她身后的两名冲锋者则把镣铐扣在这个歹人手上。瓦蕾娜得意洋洋地瞥了那两个大块头一眼。“看吧，我怎么跟你们说的？” 一名士兵咕哝了一声，把那个阴影般的兔子按得跪在地上。另一名士兵搜了她的身，从她的袍子里找出一套开锁工具和一把小匕首。匕首被抽出来时，公主绷紧了身体，但你把手安抚地放在她肩上。“她有机会的时候并没有对我动手。我觉得她不是刺客。” “对！我不是杀手！”兔子尖声叫道，抬头看着两个居高临下盯着她的巨大弥诺陶洛斯。“别紧张。” 瓦蕾娜蹲下身，与她平视。“那么你究竟是什么人？你在为谁做事？” “我什么都不会告诉你们！”间谍在束缚中挣扎。“叛徒！” 你瞥了瓦蕾娜一眼，但她脸上的表情看起来是真正的困惑。公主撅起嘴，牛耳上下抖动。“你给我解释清楚。” 没有回应。瓦蕾娜看向你。 你打算怎么找出答案？

rows.original: You trot after Varena once she's had a few moments to calm herself down. Once you're out on the street, you find her speaking to a cowgirl in workman's clothes and a pair of heavy spectacles — the foreman of the place, you guess. Varena passes the woman a solid gold coin and gives her an apologetic smile, which prompts the smaller woman to bow and turn back to her place of business. She gives you a foul-tempered scowl as you walk past. "Varena..." The princess gives you a cross look and crosses her arms. All you can really do is say "I'm sorry." Her expression softens, just a bit. "It's... it's not fine, but I'm sure it was an honest mistake. Nobody attacked either of us, so it's not like whatever's going on is dangerous. At least immediately so." "So what was in that cargo?" you ask. "Oh! Right, let me show you. Hopefully nothing's missing." Nothing is, it turns out, though you can't help but notice a crowbar lying on the floor next to the stack of crates marked with the princess's labrys. Her bodyguards crank the boxes open, revealing several neat stacks of white bags inside. Varena picks one up and opens it, showing off the contents: apples. Bright red apples, hundreds and hundreds of them between all the sacks in just this one box. "It's... fruit?" you wonder, looking them all over. The princess grins. "Mmhm. As much as all my money could buy. It wasn't easy getting so much through the quarantine. I had to beg an ice mage I know from Sartanni to come with the shipment and keep them fresh. But look, they're still ripe and shiny!" [pc.isDK |"All this trouble for fruit? What's the big idea?" |"So all of this was over fruit? Why?" ] "Well it doesn't matter what was in the boxes, does it? I wanted to lure out somebody who wanted to find out what was in them in the first place. So I thought, I might as well bring in something nice for the people of the city! Many of them haven't seen fruit, or anything fresh, in weeks now." Varena sinches the sack closed and slings it over her shoulder. "So now that you know the dark and terrible truth of what I was sneaking into the city... what do you say to helping me get these into the hands of the needy?"
rows.translation: 等瓦蕾娜花了几分钟平复心情之后，你快步跟了上去。 一到街上，你就看到她正在和一位穿工装、戴着厚眼镜的牛仔姑娘说话——你猜那是这里的工头。瓦蕾娜递给那女人一枚足金硬币，并给了她一个歉意的微笑，那矮个女人便鞠了一躬，转身回到自己的店里。你从她身边走过时，她恶狠狠地瞪了你一眼。 “瓦蕾娜……” 公主不快地看了你一眼，抱起双臂。你能做的其实只有说一句“对不起”。 她的表情稍微缓和了一点。“这……这可不算没事，但我相信那是个无心的失误。没有人袭击我们中的任何一个，所以不管发生了什么，至少算不上危险。至少暂时不危险。” “那批货里到底装的是什么？”你问道。 “哦！对了，我让你看看。希望什么都没少。” 结果什么都没少，只是你忍不住注意到，在那堆标着公主双刃斧徽记的箱子旁的地上，躺着一根撬棍。她的保镖们把箱子撬开，里面整齐地码着好几摞白色袋子。瓦蕾娜拿起一个袋子打开，展示里面的东西：苹果。鲜红的苹果，仅这一只箱子里，那些袋子加起来就装了成百上千个。 “这是……水果？”你打量着它们，不禁疑惑。 公主咧嘴一笑。“嗯哼。我所有的钱都用来买这个了。要把这么多东西运过检疫可不容易。我不得不求一位我在萨塔尼认识的冰法师随货同行，让它们保持新鲜。不过你看，它们还是那么饱满鲜亮！” [pc.isDK |“为了水果费这么大劲？你到底图什么？” |“所以这一切都是为了水果？为什么？” ] “盒子里装的是什么并不重要，对吧？我只是想把那个一开始就好奇箱子里有什么的人引出来。所以我想，不如顺便给城里的百姓带点好东西！他们中有很多人已经好几周没见过水果，也没见过任何新鲜东西了。” 瓦蕾娜把袋口扎紧，甩到肩上。“既然现在你知道了偷偷运进城的东西那黑暗又可怕的真相……帮我把这些分给有需要的人，怎么样？”
rows.raw: ' You trot after Varena once she's had a few moments to calm herself down. Once you're out on the street, you find her speaking to a cowgirl in workman's clothes and a pair of heavy spectacles — the foreman of the place, you guess. Varena passes the woman a solid gold coin and gives her an apologetic smile, which prompts the smaller woman to bow and turn back to her place of business. She gives you a foul-tempered scowl as you walk past. "Varena..." The princess gives you a cross look and crosses her arms. All you can really do is say "I'm sorry." Her expression softens, just a bit. "It's... it's not fine, but I'm sure it was an honest mistake. Nobody attacked either of us, so it's not like whatever's going on is dangerous. At least immediately so." "So what was in that cargo?" you ask. "Oh! Right, let me show you. Hopefully nothing's missing." Nothing is, it turns out, though you can't help but notice a crowbar lying on the floor next to the stack of crates marked with the princess's labrys. Her bodyguards crank the boxes open, revealing several neat stacks of white bags inside. Varena picks one up and opens it, showing off the contents: apples. Bright red apples, hundreds and hundreds of them between all the sacks in just this one box. "It's... fruit?" you wonder, looking them all over. The princess grins. "Mmhm. As much as all my money could buy. It wasn't easy getting so much through the quarantine. I had to beg an ice mage I know from Sartanni to come with the shipment and keep them fresh. But look, they're still ripe and shiny!" [pc.isDK |"All this trouble for fruit? What's the big idea?" |"So all of this was over fruit? Why?" ] "Well it doesn't matter what was in the boxes, does it? I wanted to lure out somebody who wanted to find out what was in them in the first place. So I thought, I might as well bring in something nice for the people of the city! Many of them haven't seen fruit, or anything fresh, in weeks now." Varena sinches the sack closed and slings it over her shoulder. "So now that you know the dark and terrible truth of what I was sneaking into the city... what do you say to helping me get these into the hands of the needy?" '

rows.original:
You nod, earning an ear-to-ear smile from Varena. "Awesome! Grab a bag and follow me!"
    
    The princess leads the way from the warehouse and onto the streets of the city outside. Densely packed crowds of cowfolk move through the boulevards, following the gentle flow of the river. Varena chants a spell as you walk, and her formal dress shimmers against her skin, reweaving itself into the corset and cloak you remember from Ember's. She gives you a wink and adjusts her hood over her horns.
    
    Once the pair of you reach a promising street corner, Varena sets her sack down and draws forth a shiny red apple. Your royal companion turns heads just with her looks, but pulling out something so rare and precious in these times in the middle of a crowded street. Several children break from their mothers and come running, eyes wide beneath the fluffy fur of their bovine faces. 
    
    "Here," you say, handing one of the apples from your bag to the first of the calves.
    
    "Really? Wow! Th-thank [silly
        |moo
        |you
    ]!" he gasps. The tiny bull takes a huge bite out of it, and his eyes light up. "Mmmfh!" 
    
    His mother trots over with a look of dismay, though. "I'm sorry, [pc.mf
        |sir
        |ma'am
    ]. We... we really can't afford something like that. [silly
        |Timmy
        |Tima
    ], you need to give it back."
    
    Varena gives her a reassuring smile. "It's fine. We're not asking for anything. Here, for you." 
    
    You watch the woman's expression go from sorrow to shock and then to delight and gratitude all in the span of a second. She takes a bite from the second apple, and tears well in her eyes. "Oh, bless you both!"
    
    The mother and son are soon replaced by a growing crowd of Khor'minoans. You and Varena hand out the fresh fruit to the grateful herd, paid in childrens' smiles and the grateful embrace of young mothers. It only takes a couple of minutes for the two of you to empty out those sacks, but by then the Charger that stayed behind has brought another pair slung over her shoulders. 
    
    And so it goes. The crowd ebbs and flows around you, hungrily taking the sweet, fresh treats as fast as you and Varena can hand them out. You lose track of how many times you're given hugs, handshakes, and cheek kisses from adoring cowgirls. Over the span of half an hour, you're able to empty out the entire shipment into the hands of Varena's subjects. Varena just smiles the whole time, picking up little kids and hugging them to her chest before sending them off with apples until she's got none left to give. 
    
    "We'll try and get more!" she assures the crowd, handing the last empty sack to a young cowgirl in badly-worn clothing. "Just try and hold out a little while longer, everyone. This war can't last forever!" 
    
    "Khor Aterna!" someone shouts. 
    
    The slogan is taken up by every man and many of the women in the crowd around you. Even some of the kids get in on it, between messy bites of juicy fruit. There's a proud swell in Varena's chest, and she thumps a fist against her chest — quite the jiggly affair — before waving goodbye to the crowd. She takes your hand, and the pair of you make your getaway to the sounds of patriotic cheers. Her Charger bodyguard is waiting around the corner with her carriage.
    
    Varena pauses short of climbing in, and throws her arms around you for a big, tight hug. "Thanks for your help, [pc.name]. [pc.isDK
        |You gotta admit, it was nice to see so many people so happy, right?
        |It was so good to see so many people so happy!
    ]"
    
    She squeezes hard enough to make your ribs ache before finally clambering up into the carriage. "I've got to go and [var0
        |talk to Dad about our spy
        |apologize to Captain Fenraus for this spy stuff, I guess
    ], but I'll see you around Ember's again, okay?"
    
    "See you," you say, [var1
        |helping her up with a two-handed push on that enormous caramel ass. She gasps, and slaps your face with her tail
        |helping her up into the seat
    ].
    
    The Charger closes the door, clambers up into the driver's seat, and takes her away.
    
    For your part, you head back to the gate.
rows.translation:
你点了点头，换来瓦蕾娜一个咧到耳根的笑容。“太棒了！拿上一个袋子，跟我来！”
    
    公主领路，从仓库走到外面的城市街道上。挤得密密麻麻的牛人沿着河流的缓流方向在宽阔大道上移动。走路时瓦蕾娜念了个咒语，她身上那件正式礼服贴着肌肤闪烁起来，重新编织成你记忆中在艾姆伯酒馆见过的那身束腰和外袍。她冲你眨了眨眼，把兜帽拉好盖住自己的角。
    
    等你们俩找到一个合适的街角，瓦蕾娜把袋子放下，掏出一个鲜红的苹果。你这位王室同伴光凭长相就能引来目光，而在这种时候、在拥挤的街道中央掏出如此稀有珍贵的东西，效果更甚。几个孩子从母亲身边跑开，跑了过来，毛茸茸的牛脸上瞪大眼睛。
    
    “来，”你说着，从袋子里拿出一个苹果递给第一头小牛。
    
    “真的吗？哇！谢[silly
        |哞
        |你
    ]！”他喘着气说。那头小公牛大咬了一口，眼睛顿时亮了起来。“嗯呣！”
    
    不过他的母亲一脸惊惶地小跑过来。“对不起，[pc.mf
        |先生
        |女士
    ]。我们……我们真的买不起那样的东西。[silly
        |蒂米
        |蒂玛
    ]，你得把它还回去。”
    
    瓦蕾娜给了她一个安抚的微笑。“没关系。我们什么都不要。来，这是给你的。”
    
    你看着那女人的表情在一秒之内从悲伤变成震惊，再变成喜悦与感激。她咬了第二只苹果一口，眼泪涌上眼眶。“哦，愿神明保佑你们俩！”
    
    母子俩很快就被越来越多聚拢过来的科尔米诺斯人取代。你和瓦蕾娜把新鲜水果分发给感激的牛群，换来的是孩子们的笑脸和年轻母亲们感激的拥抱。你们俩只用了几分钟就清空了那些袋子，而这时留在一旁的那名冲锋者又扛来了两袋。
    
    就这样继续着。人群在你周围涨落，贪婪地接过那些甘甜新鲜的恩物，你们俩递多快，他们就拿多快。你记不清自己被那些崇拜的女牛仔拥抱、握手、亲脸颊了多少次。半个小时里，你们把整批货物都分到了瓦蕾娜的子民手中。瓦蕾娜全程都在微笑，她把小孩子抱起来贴在胸前，再塞个苹果打发他们走，直到自己手里一个也不剩。
    
    “我们会想办法再弄一些来！”她向人群保证，把最后一个空袋子递给一个衣衫破旧的年轻女牛仔。“大家再撑一会儿。这场战争不可能永远打下去！”
    
    “科尔·阿特纳！”有人喊道。
    
    这句口号被你周围人群中的每个男人和许多女人接了过去。就连一些孩子也一边咬着多汁的水果一边跟着喊。瓦蕾娜胸中涌起一股自豪，她握拳敲了敲自己的胸口——胸前晃得厉害——然后向人群挥手告别。她拉住你的手，你们俩在爱国的欢呼声中脱身离去。她的冲锋者保镖在街角等着，身边就是她的马车。
    
    瓦蕾娜在爬上车前停了一下，张开双臂把你紧紧抱住。“谢谢你的帮助，[pc.name]。[pc.isDK
        |你得承认，看到这么多人这么开心，感觉真好，对吧？
        |看到这么多人这么开心，真是太好了！
    ]”
    
    她抱得你肋骨生疼，才终于爬进马车。“我得走了，去[var0
        |跟爸爸谈谈我们抓到的间谍
        |为这些间谍的事向芬劳斯队长道个歉，大概吧
    ]，不过我们还会在艾姆伯酒馆再见的，好吗？”
    
    “再见，”你说，[var1
        |两手托着那硕大的焦糖色屁股把她推了上去。她倒吸一口气，用尾巴抽了你的脸。
        |扶她坐进座位
    ]。
    
    冲锋者关上车门，爬上驾驶座，把她带走了。
    
    而你呢，则回到了城门那里。

rows.original:
You start with a visual examination of your captive.
    
    She's a taeleer, with short blonde hair and dark makeup, wearing a loose black cape over what appears to be just a simple chest wrap and loincloth. None of her clothes have crests or other markings on them, and they're made of cheap materials. You can't see any jewelry on her, and the pat down didn't reveal a coin purse. She's not well to do, then. 
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |Maybe even a slave? 
        
        There's a thought. You squat down with Varena and yank the criminal's cloak aside, examining her mostly-bare body beneath it. The spy squirms, but she can't exactly hide herself from you with the Chargers' hands locked on her shoulders. You push up the hem of her loincloth, exposing a buttock. It's been tattooed with a water jug surrounded by a laurel, all in off-green ink. 
        
        [party.has arona
            |"Weak-ass tatt," Arona says, rubbing a hand over her own banner wolf sleeve.
        ]
        
        "Look at that," Varena muses. "An owner's mark."
        
        "Do you recognize it?"
        
        The princess peers at it a moment, furrows her brow, then nods. "It's the mark of House Iavari."
        
        The bunny spy struggles against her bonds, but she can't wiggle her way out of the truth. The mark's on her flesh, and it isn't fresh. She's served that house for many years, you'd guess. Maybe since she was a child. And she doesn't like that you know it.
        
        You aren't familiar enough to Khor'minoan politics for the name Iavari to mean anything, but it clearly does to Varena. 
        
        "That's enough," the princess says. She looks to her bodyguards. "Take her to Lord Ignafaerus. He can hold onto her for now."
        
        "Aye, ma'am," one of the soldiers says, unceremoniously hefting the bunny onto his shoulder. The guards stomp back out the front door, dragging the squirming spy with them.
        
        Varena pushes up to her feet and gives you a smile. "Well done, [pc.name]. I would never have suspected a spy of her skill to be a slave! I'm going to go tell the warehouse workers everything's okay, and then we can figure out the next step, okay?"
        
        Sounds good to you.
        |Unfortunately, she's not carrying anything that identifies her, much less who might have sent her. You take the dagger she was carrying and give that a look over, but on examination it's crudely made and lacking any maker's mark; it's a cheap tool, not a fighting implement. Even its sheathe is loose, thin leather that's been worn raw with time. 
        
        Out on the streets, she'd look like any other underclass refuse. Indistinct and unremarkable in every way. 
        
        You doubt you'll learn anything just by looking at her.
    ]
rows.translation:
你首先对这名被俘虏的人进行了外观检查。
    
    她是个泰利尔人，金色短发，化着浓妆，身上罩着一件宽松的黑色斗篷，里面似乎只穿着简单的裹胸和缠腰布。她的衣服上没有任何纹章或标记，料子也很廉价。你看不到她戴任何首饰，搜身也没搜出钱袋。那么她并不富裕。
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |也许甚至是个奴隶？
        
        有个念头。你和瓦蕾娜一起蹲下身，把那罪犯的斗篷拉开，查看斗篷下几乎赤裸的身体。间谍扭动着，但冲锋者的手牢牢按在她肩上，她没法把自己藏起来。你掀起她缠腰布的下摆，露出一侧臀部——上面用暗绿色的墨水纹着一只水罐，周围环绕着月桂。
        
        [party.has arona
            |“烂透了的纹身，”阿罗娜说着，一只手摩挲着自己袖子上那面狼旗纹身。
        ]
        
        “看那个，”瓦蕾娜若有所思地说。“主人的标记。”
        
        “你认得它吗？”
        
        公主端详了一会儿，皱起眉头，然后点了点头。“那是贾瓦里家族的标记。”
        
        那个兔子间谍在束缚中挣扎，但她无法从真相中挣脱。标记就在她的皮肉上，而且并不新。你猜她为那个家族效力了很多年，也许从孩提时就开始了。而她不喜欢你知道这件事。
        
        你对科尔米诺斯的政治还不够熟悉，贾瓦里这个名字对你毫无意义，但对瓦蕾娜显然不是。
        
        “够了，”公主说。她看向自己的保镖。“把她带到伊格纳法鲁斯大人那里。先让他看管着她。”
        
        “遵命，夫人，”其中一名士兵应道，然后毫不客气地将那只兔子扛在了肩上。卫兵们重重地走回前门，同时还拖着那个拼命挣扎的间谍。
        
        瓦蕾娜站起身，对你笑了笑。“干得不错，[pc.name]。我绝不会想到一个有她这种本事的间谍竟是奴隶！我去告诉仓库的工人们一切都好，然后我们再商量下一步，好吗？”
        
        你觉得可以。
        |不幸的是，她身上没有任何能表明身份的东西，更不用说能指出是谁派她来的。你拿起她带着的那把匕首看了看，但仔细一看，它做工粗糙，也没有任何工匠标记；那是件廉价工具，不是搏斗用的兵器。连它的鞘都是松散、薄薄的皮子，早已磨得发白。
        
        在街头，她看起来和其他底层社会的流浪者没什么两样——毫不起眼，没有任何特别之处。
        
        你觉得光靠打量她，是查不出什么来的。
    ]
rows.raw:
"
    You start with a visual examination of your captive.
    
    She's a taeleer, with short blonde hair and dark makeup, wearing a loose black cape over what appears to be just a simple chest wrap and loincloth. None of her clothes have crests or other markings on them, and they're made of cheap materials. You can't see any jewelry on her, and the pat down didn't reveal a coin purse. She's not well to do, then. 
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |Maybe even a slave? 
        
        There's a thought. You squat down with Varena and yank the criminal's cloak aside, examining her mostly-bare body beneath it. The spy squirms, but she can't exactly hide herself from you with the Chargers' hands locked on her shoulders. You push up the hem of her loincloth, exposing a buttock. It's been tattooed with a water jug surrounded by a laurel, all in off-green ink. 
        
        [party.has arona
            |"Weak-ass tatt," Arona says, rubbing a hand over her own banner wolf sleeve.
        ]
        
        "Look at that," Varena muses. "An owner's mark."
        
        "Do you recognize it?"
        
        The princess peers at it a moment, furrows her brow, then nods. "It's the mark of House Iavari."
        
        The bunny spy struggles against her bonds, but she can't wiggle her way out of the truth. The mark's on her flesh, and it isn't fresh. She's served that house for many years, you'd guess. Maybe since she was a child. And she doesn't like that you know it.
        
        You aren't familiar enough to Khor'minoan politics for the name Iavari to mean anything, but it clearly does to Varena. 
        
        "That's enough," the princess says. She looks to her bodyguards. "Take her to Lord Ignafaerus. He can hold onto her for now."
        
        "Aye, ma'am," one of the soldiers says, unceremoniously hefting the bunny onto his shoulder. The guards stomp back out the front door, dragging the squirming spy with them.
        
        Varena pushes up to her feet and gives you a smile. "Well done, [pc.name]. I would never have suspected a spy of her skill to be a slave! I'm going to go tell the warehouse workers everything's okay, and then we can figure out the next step, okay?"
        
        Sounds good to you.
        |Unfortunately, she's not carrying anything that identifies her, much less who might have sent her. You take the dagger she was carrying and give that a look over, but on examination it's crudely made and lacking any maker's mark; it's a cheap tool, not a fighting implement. Even its sheathe is loose, thin leather that's been worn raw with time. 
        
        Out on the streets, she'd look like any other underclass refuse. Indistinct and unremarkable in every way. 
        
        You doubt you'll learn anything just by looking at her.
    ]
    "
