rows.original: With a sharp intake of breath, Kiyoko levers herself out of the rocking chair, planting both hands on the armrests and shaking away the last vestiges of sleep. [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|Despite her baby bump, the kitsune mother has no problems getting to her feet. That slight frame of hers is deceptive — she has so much energy, it's practically pouring off her. |The sheer size and weight of her full, rounded belly makes the process a little awkward, but you lend a helping hand, and she's up and about in no time at all. ] She takes a few moments to smooth out her hair and fix the worst of her bedhead, then turns and gives you a small, formal bow. "Forgive my appearance, [pc.name]. I wouldn't have let myself go like this if I'd known you were coming to visit today." That's just fine. This slightly wild look suits her just as well as the carefully groomed one does, either way. She is a fox, one way or the other. Kiyoko tilts her head, as if not quite fully believing your words, then dismisses her worries with a nonchalant shrug and resuming her usual cheerful demeanor. "Well, let's not keep standing around here all day. The sun is nice, but I'd like to get inside — especially if you want to play." [kiyoko.pregStage 4|Oh? Does she want to play? "Oh yes." You don't think Kiyoko's aware of it, but the kitsune mother-to-be is biting her lower lip as her eyes dart around. I wasn't feeling it that badly when I dozed off, but since you were so kind to wake me up, I'm feeling positively frisky. I wouldn't mind it if we could have a little fun... maybe enjoy a game together..." You'll think about it. "Be careful, now." Kiyoko's lips part to show just the barest hint of pearly white, slightly pointed teeth. "Work me up too much, and I just might not be able to control myself. Who knows what I might do, then? Hee hee..." |Oh? Is she feeling frisky? Does she have — well, you can't exactly quite call it morning wood, but she knows what you mean. "Ma-aybe?" Kiyoko replies in a little sing-song voice. "You're free to do as you wish, of course, but I would really appreciate it if you could play some with me before you leave, [pc.name]. It's been a while; I want to play rough." ] Leaving her words hanging in the air, Kiyoko leads you on through the front door, down the hallway, and into the sitting room. You take a seat, then watch as the kitsune goes through the by now familiar motions of preparing the tea set and a small plate of candies. "Ah," Kiyoko murmurs with no small satisfaction as she pours herself a small cup of tea. Her large fox ears perk up as she raises the steaming liquid to her nose and takes a deep breath. "There's nothing quite like the bitter scent of tea after a long, warm nap. Now, [pc.name], shall we get started? How about I do something good to you today? Would you like that?"
rows.translation: 清子猛地吸了一口气，从摇椅中坐起来，双手撑在扶手上，努力驱散残余的睡意。 [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|尽管腹部已经隆起，这位狐狸妈妈依然能够轻松地站立起来。她那娇小的身躯其实具有很强的欺骗性——她身上蕴含着如此巨大的能量，简直让人感觉这些能量都在向外溢出。 |她那圆滚滚的肚子既大又重，因此起身这个动作显得有些笨拙，但只要你伸出一只手帮忙，她就能很快地站起来活动了。 ] 她花了几分钟整理头发，把最糟的睡乱发丝弄平，然后转身向你行了一个简短而正式的鞠躬。 请原谅我这副样子，[pc.name]。要是知道你今天会来看我，我就不会这么不修边幅了。 那样也完全没问题。这种略带野性的造型，和她精心打理过的形象一样，都非常适合她。不管怎么说，她确实是只狐狸。 清子歪了歪头，似乎并不完全相信你的话，然后漫不经心地耸了耸肩，把心中的担忧抛到了一边，又恢复了她一贯开朗的神情。好吧，我们不要在这里站一整天了。阳光确实很明媚，但我还是想进屋去——尤其是如果你想玩的话。 [kiyoko.pregStage 4|哦？她想玩游戏吗？ 哦，是的。你觉得清子自己可能没意识到，但这位准妈妈正咬着下唇，目光四处游移。我打瞌睡的时候还没那么想要，但既然你这么好心地把我叫醒了，我现在反而觉得心痒难耐。如果我们能一起玩点什么有趣的东西……比如一起玩游戏，我当然不介意…… 你仔细考虑一下吧。 现在要小心了。清子的嘴唇微微张开，露出一点点珍珠般洁白、略带尖利的牙齿。如果你再这样激我，我可能就控制不住自己了。谁知道到时候我会做出什么来呢？呵呵…… |哦？她是不是变得有些活跃了？她是不是……嗯，虽然不能确切地称之为“晨勃”，但你应该明白我的意思。 也——许吧？清子用略带吟唱般的声调回答道。当然，你可以随心所欲地做任何你想做的事，但在你离开之前，如果你能陪我玩一会儿，我会非常感激的，[pc.name]。好久没玩了，我想玩得粗野一点。 ] 清子把那些话留在空气中，然后领着你穿过前门，沿着走廊走进客厅。你坐下来，看着那只狐妖开始进行那些已经变得熟悉的动作——准备茶具和一小盘糖果。 啊，清子一边满足地低声说着，一边给自己倒了一小杯茶。当她把热气腾腾的茶水送到鼻子前深吸一口气时，她那大大的狐妖耳朵立刻竖了起来。在睡了一个漫长而温暖的午觉之后，没有什么比茶的苦涩香气更让人感到惬意的了。现在， [pc.name]我们开始吧？今天我就为你做点好事怎么样？你愿意吗？
rows.raw: ' With a sharp intake of breath, Kiyoko levers herself out of the rocking chair, planting both hands on the armrests and shaking away the last vestiges of sleep. [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|Despite her baby bump, the kitsune mother has no problems getting to her feet. That slight frame of hers is deceptive — she has so much energy, it's practically pouring off her. |The sheer size and weight of her full, rounded belly makes the process a little awkward, but you lend a helping hand, and she's up and about in no time at all. ] She takes a few moments to smooth out her hair and fix the worst of her bedhead, then turns and gives you a small, formal bow. "Forgive my appearance, [pc.name]. I wouldn't have let myself go like this if I'd known you were coming to visit today." That's just fine. This slightly wild look suits her just as well as the carefully groomed one does, either way. She is a fox, one way or the other. Kiyoko tilts her head, as if not quite fully believing your words, then dismisses her worries with a nonchalant shrug and resuming her usual cheerful demeanor. "Well, let's not keep standing around here all day. The sun is nice, but I'd like to get inside — especially if you want to play." [kiyoko.pregStage 4|Oh? Does she want to play? "Oh yes." You don't think Kiyoko's aware of it, but the kitsune mother-to-be is biting her lower lip as her eyes dart around. I wasn't feeling it that badly when I dozed off, but since you were so kind to wake me up, I'm feeling positively frisky. I wouldn't mind it if we could have a little fun... maybe enjoy a game together..." You'll think about it. "Be careful, now." Kiyoko's lips part to show just the barest hint of pearly white, slightly pointed teeth. "Work me up too much, and I just might not be able to control myself. Who knows what I might do, then? Hee hee..." |Oh? Is she feeling frisky? Does she have — well, you can't exactly quite call it morning wood, but she knows what you mean. "Ma-aybe?" Kiyoko replies in a little sing-song voice. "You're free to do as you wish, of course, but I would really appreciate it if you could play some with me before you leave, [pc.name]. It's been a while; I want to play rough." ] Leaving her words hanging in the air, Kiyoko leads you on through the front door, down the hallway, and into the sitting room. You take a seat, then watch as the kitsune goes through the by now familiar motions of preparing the tea set and a small plate of candies. rows.original:
It's a nice day, isn't it? Birds are singing, the sun is shining... days like these are just perfect, which is probably why Kiyoko tries to have such weather as much as possible. A perfect day for a visit, too... which is why you're here, isn't it? Stepping up onto the raised porch, you approach the cabin door and rap on it with your knuckles. However, there's no response, and you're about to give it another go when a soft snore from around the corner draws your attention.

    That sounds familiar... 
    
    Crossing over to investigate the source of the snoring, you don't have long to go before you find Kiyoko slumped in a rocking chair, smack in the middle of a large pool of sunlight. The kitsune mother is sound asleep, nestled securely in the chair's soft cushioning and her own many tails; the sunlight illuminates her soft features and the faint smile on her lips. The poor thing clearly hasn't brushed her hair or fur in a bit, and snuggling up in the rocking chair has only mussed up the lot even more.
    
    Come to think of it, it must be nice to nap in the warm sun on a cool day... 
    
    Back and forth, back and forth, the gentle creaking of the rocking chair on the floorboards as Kiyoko dozes away, her hands [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4
    |folded across her chest, her head bent to one side.
    |in front of her, cradling the growing swell of her pregnant tummy, hugging it to herself as if to make the fox kit — and herself — a little more secure while she snoozes.
    |resting atop the massive mound of her pregnancy. The front of Kiyoko's yukata is undone, allowing her bare belly to spill out of her clothes and onto her lap where it soaks up the warm sunshine; the open halves are loosely draped over the kitsune mother's milk-swollen breasts, barely covering her nipples — the outline of which are clearly still visible against the sinfully thin fabric.
    ] Every now and then, Kiyoko murmurs something in her sleep, and her large, fluffy ears twitch ever so slightly. There's a book lying on the floor beside her — she must have read herself to sleep, dropping the book to the ground when she finally nodded off.
    
    She seems so content to nap like this... but you wanted to visit, didn't you? How do you want to wake up this fluffy mommy?
rows.translation:
今天真是美好的一天，不是吗？鸟儿在歌唱，阳光明媚……这样的日子简直完美无缺，也许正因如此，清子才会尽量让这样的天气多出现一些。今天也是适合出门游玩的完美日子……所以你才会来到这里，对吧？走上那抬高的门廊，你走到小屋门前，用指节敲了敲门。然而，没有回应。就在你准备再敲一次的时候，拐角处传来的一声轻鼾吸引了你的注意。

    这听起来有点耳熟……
    
    你走过去查看鼾声的来源，没走多远就发现清子瘫坐在一把摇椅里，正好坐在一大片阳光正中央。这位狐妖母亲正沉沉地睡着，安稳地窝在椅子柔软的靠垫和她自己那许多条尾巴之间；阳光照亮了她柔和的面容和唇边那抹淡淡的微笑。这可怜的家伙显然有一阵子没梳理过头发和毛发了，而蜷在摇椅里只会让它们更加凌乱。
    
    仔细想想，在凉爽的日子里躺在暖阳下打个盹，肯定很惬意……
    
    来来回回，来来回回，摇椅在地板上发出轻柔的吱嘎声，清子打着盹，她的双手 [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4
    |交叠放在胸前，头偏向一侧。
    |放在身前，抱着日渐隆起的孕肚，把它搂向自己，仿佛这样就能让腹中的狐宝宝——以及她自己——在打盹时更有安全感一些。
    |搁在那庞大的孕肚上。清子的和服前襟敞开着，让裸露的腹部从衣物中露出来、摊在膝上晒着暖阳；敞开的两片衣襟松松地搭在这位狐妖母亲因哺乳而肿胀的乳房上，几乎遮不住乳头——那轮廓在薄得离谱的布料下依然清晰可见。
    ] 时不时地，清子会在睡梦中呢喃些什么，她那又大又蓬松的耳朵也会轻轻抽动一下。她身旁的地板上放着一本书——她一定是读到睡着，终于点头睡过去时把书掉在了地上。
    
    她这样打盹似乎很满足……可你本来是来拜访她的，对吧？你想怎么叫醒这位蓬松的妈妈呢？

rows.original: Smiling, you reach for Kiyoko's shoulder and take a firm grip before gently nudging her a few times. She really is a deep sleeper — your first few attempts only get you soft murmurs and ear twitches, but you work at it. She must be used to being prodded from both inside and out by now, after all, and the pool of sunlight is starting to make even you slightly drowsy... At length, though, Kiyoko heaves a deep breath, her bosom visibly rising with the effort, and her eyes flutter open. Their deep, jade-green depths drink you in for a second or two, and then her smile widens.

rows.original: A good, relaxing petting would be a perfect thing for waking up a foxy creature like Kiyoko, wouldn't it? Smiling at the sleeping mother rocking away in her chair, you lay the flat of a palm against the back of one of Kiyoko's ears, stroking it in a steady back-to-front motion. The fine fuzz on the behinds of Kiyoko's large, fluffy ears evokes feelings of warm happiness in the pit of your stomach, and they only grow deeper as you slide your free hand along to the other side of her head and start toying with her long, amber-orange locks of hair. Kiyoko sighs happily, drawing in a deep breath and letting it out again. You see her bosom heave with effort, her [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4|little mouth turning upwards at the corners |rounded baby bump rising and falling gently |immensely pregnant, life-swollen womb heaving outwards and slowly shrinking back in, the fox kit inside stirring along with their mother ] as she nuzzles her head against your touch, aggressively tousling her hair and ears in your hand. You're only too happy to oblige her, chasing Kiyoko's ears about her head as they take on a life of their own, darting away from your touch even as your fingers chase them down. They twitch and wriggle, fold and swivel, and just when you think you've got them cornered to apply vigorous pets, they slip away to lead you on yet another merry chase, just as naughty as the fox mother they're attached to. On her part, while Kiyoko is quite the heavy sleeper — she has to be, to not wake up from all that's going on — she's practically squirming in her chair now, giggling softly to herself as you continue to scratch and pet and play with her. A hum of satisfied contentment leaves the kitsune's throat as she finally opens her eyes, drinking in the sunlight — and you. "Ah, so that's why I was having such good dreams... oh, my hair and fur's a mess." Of course they're a mess, you made them that way. And let's face it; she can't deny that it was worth it, yes? Kiyoko sighs, smiles, and pushes her head into your hands hungrily, rapidly turning her head to and fro until the skin of your palms feels all fuzzy and tingly from the furry rubbing. When she finally stops, Kiyoko has a big smile on her face, looking distinctly perky — if a little woozy in the bargain.
rows.translation: 轻轻抚摸她，让她放松下来，这样才最适合唤醒像清子这样的可爱生物，不是吗？你微笑着看着正在椅子上轻轻摇晃着入睡的清子，然后将手掌平放在她的一只耳朵后面，开始有节奏地来回轻抚。清子那双又大又蓬松的耳朵后面覆盖着细软的绒毛，当你用另一只手轻轻抚摸她头部的另一侧，开始玩弄她那缕缕琥珀色卷发时，这种温暖而愉悦的感觉会在你心中愈发强烈。 清子开心地叹了口气，深吸一口气后又缓缓呼出。你可以看到她的胸脯因为用力而上下起伏 [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4|嘴角微微上扬 |圆润的孕肚轻轻地上下起伏 |那只狐狸幼崽在母亲体内，随着母亲日益庞大的腹部不断膨胀又慢慢收缩，也在一起蠕动着。 ] 当她把头依在你的手上，任由你随意拨弄她的头发和耳朵时，你当然会非常乐意满足她的这个请求。你追着清子的耳朵玩闹，那些耳朵仿佛有了自己的生命，总是在你的手指触碰到它们之前迅速躲开。它们扭动身体、翻滚弯曲，就在你以为已经把它们逼入绝境、可以好好抚摸它们的时候，它们又会溜走，继续引诱你进行一场又一场有趣的追逐——就像它们所依附的那些狡猾的母狐妖一样顽皮。 就她而言，虽然清子睡得很沉——她必须这样，才能不被周围发生的一切吵醒——但此刻她却在椅子上坐得坐立不安，当你继续挠她、抚摸她、和她玩耍时，她还会轻声地咯咯笑起来。当那只狐妖终于睁开眼睛，沐浴在阳光下，同时也将你的身影尽收眼底时，她喉咙里发出了满足而愉悦的低鸣声。 啊，原来如此，难怪我会做那么美好的梦……哦，我的头发和毛发都乱成了一团。 它们当然是一团糟，都是你弄的。而且说实话，她也不能否认这一切都是值得的，对吧？ 清子叹了口气，然后笑了起来，急切地把头埋进你的手中，不停地转动着头，直到你的手掌因为她的摩擦而感到一阵阵刺痛和痒意。当她终于停下来时，清子的脸上露出了灿烂的笑容，看起来精神焕发——不过也有点晕乎乎的。

rows.original: You look down at Kiyoko's chest. [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4|Size isn't the only thing that matters — the gentle rise of the kitsune mother's bosom promises a firm, if not full groping. And given that she's the mother of your kits, it really would be a nice surprise to wake in a most pleasurable way, wouldn't it? All it would take is just the slightest touch to free her clothes from where they've snagged on her dark dugs... But where would be the fun in that? ] Time to play, then! She's wearing no bra at the moment, so all you have to do is dig your fingers in ever so gently and start moving them in lazy circles. The effects are immediate. Yet she doesn't wake up, not even when you start rubbing your palms all over her nipples, feeling them swell and stiffen at your touch. A soft blush creeps into the kitsune mother's cheeks, and it's only when you start rolling your fingers into her boobflesh, delighting in the sheer tactile sensation of such lush and maternal ripeness that her eyes finally crack open, and you see a tiny sliver of green peeping out at you. "Oh." Kiyoko gives you a mischievous smile. "I've have prepared a better greeting for you if I knew you were coming to visit today, [pc.name]." You don't know about that. The added weight's forced her to start walking with a pronounced waddle and her womb is hanging low in front of her; whenever her hands aren't occupied, they're cradled under her immense pregnancy for what support they can give. Her tummy button has popped out even further to the point where you can see it under her clothing, a marker of how obscenely — and pleasurably — gravid she is. There's no doubt that the kit is rapidly running out of space in an increasingly overstuffed womb, pushing against its mother's hips as it waits to be born. Kiyoko's had to make a few adjustments to her yukata to turn it into appropriate maternity wear, and you have to say it fits her very well — there's a good contrast with her amazingly glossy hair and fur. The big belly coupled with her sometimes playful, sometimes distant gaze, does make her look extremely attractive in a picture of maternal glory. "I have to admit, being like this can be quite distressing at times. I'll just look up from the laundry or wake up from a nap and want to play, but there's no one to play with... it sounds silly, but being so heavy makes me so frisky to boot." Ha! [kiyoko.numKits 8|To wrap it all up, the rosy patch on Kiyoko's pregnant belly has grown to encompass most of it, deepening to a bright red in the process to stand out in stark contrast with her pale skin. If there's any proof that your kitsune slut-wife is the best fox-factory around, this is it. ] ] Your examination of the kitsune complete, you set down your tea and give Kiyoko a satisfied nod. In return, she dips her head ever so slightly at you, large, fluffy ears twitching, and gives you a small grin. "If we're done admiring each other, let's move on." Gladly. Although you might want to ask — exactly what's it about you that she was admiring? Kiyoko smirks and shakes her head. "Wouldn't be fun if I just up and told you, would it? I'll leave that one for you to figure out on your own.""

rows.original: Having nothing better to do, you sit down with Kiyoko for a little bit and chat with the kitsune about anything and everything that comes to mind over tea and candies. Kiyoko is more than willing to entertain you, clearly glad to have someone to talk to. No topic is too banal for her impeccably polite countenance, and she's quite the conversationalist to boot.
rows.translation: 由于没有别的事情可做，你便坐下来和清子聊了一会儿，边喝茶边吃糖果，随意谈论着各种话题。清子非常乐意陪着你聊天，显然也很高兴有人可以和她倾诉。对她那无可挑剔的礼貌态度来说，没有任何话题是过于琐碎或无聊的；而且她本身也是一个非常健谈的人。

rows.original: So... "Yes, what is it?" Kiyoko's usually very genteel and soft-spoken, especially with that accent of hers, but does she know...? "Do I know what? It's not like you to be coy with your words." Does she know that when she's being fucked, her voice goes up by one octave, if not two? "What?!" The effect's instantaneous as the fox mother's face colors a deep shade of lovely red, her ears flattening against her head. Oh hey, just like that, actually. Kiyoko opens her dainty little mouth, but no words emerge. Her face goes through several shades of red before she finally closes her trap and sulks in her seat. "That's mean..." Perhaps you went a little too far there, but she's so cute when angry.
rows.translation: 那么…… “是的，有什么事吗？” 清子平时总是表现得非常文雅、说话也很轻声细语，尤其是带着她那独特的口音……不过，她自己知道吗……？ “我该知道什么？你可不是说话含糊的人。” 她知道吗？当她被人操的时候，她的声音会提高一个八度，甚至两个八度呢？ “什么？！”这一效果发生得极其迅速——狐狸母亲的脸瞬间变成了深红色的色调，她的耳朵也贴在了脑袋上。 哦，嘿，还真就是这样。 清子张开了她那小巧的嘴巴，但却没有说出任何话来。她的脸色经历了好几种不同的红色变化，最后她终于闭上了嘴，闷闷不乐地坐在那里。 “好过分……” 也许你有点做得太过火了，但她生气的时候其实挺可爱的。

rows.original: [rand|You spend a little time filling in the kitsune on what you've been doing out in the world, and she listens attentively and quietly until you're done. Then she asks you a few questions on what you just said, and is content with the answers you give. While you're not sure how long all of this takes — perhaps an hour or two, or at least it feels that way — the pleasant chat has gotten some of the weight off your chest. "Thank you for telling me about what's going on in the material world," Kiyoko says as the conversation winds down to a close. "My perception is limited to the orb's immediate surroundings, after all." Oh, it was your pleasure. |You spend a few moments making small talk with Kiyoko, a simple exchange of pleasantries that's more your mouths running on automatic than anything else. The kitsune is a pleasant companion as always, and even has the grace to laugh at your bad jokes — or at least, you think they're probably bad jokes... |You inquire about Kiyoko's well-being and ask if she's doing okay in between your visits. "Tolerably so. Before I ended up being stuck in this Astral Plane, I never quite completely understood the meaning of being coddled to death. Now, well, let's say that my knowledge of such is quite thorough." There can be too much of a good thing, as they say. Would it have been any different if she'd been stuck in here with someone else, or a whole group of people for that matter? She considers that a moment. "I suppose it'd have been better on the companionship front, but that'd have brought with it a whole host of problems on its own. It's one of those things you can't really tell without having gone through it yourself, I think — and I have no desire to be stuck in here any longer than I need to be. We are not made to endure true paradise; suffering has a purpose." |There's a question you've been meaning to ask — it's regarding her auguries as a diviner. "Yes?" She doesn't so much tell that something will happen, but rather the odds of an event happening, right? "That's correct. Of course, sometimes the odds of an occurrence are almost certain, while others are almost certainly guaranteed to fail." And if something is almost certain to happen, could it be called fate? "Perhaps. Fate is a very loaded word, you know; it conveys a certain gravitas about the event being foretold. And even if you're fated to do something, then how you go about meeting that fate can still vary wildly. You can take the road to the city, or you can cross the mountains. There is an easy path, or you can be dragged to your destination kicking and screaming." Then it doesn't sound too useful... at least not in the practical sense. A shrug, a smile. "Why do you think I tried to focus my efforts towards so-called proper magic?" Heh. Still, you'll have to get her to read your fortune sometime. "That shouldn't be too hard, so long as you give me enough time to prepare." You'll be looking forward to it. ]
rows.translation: [rand|你花了一些时间向这位狐妖讲述自己在外面经历的事情，她安静而专注地听着，直到你讲完。随后她针对你刚才说的内容问了几个问题，而她对你的回答很是满意。 虽然你不确定整个过程需要多长时间——也许一两个小时，至少给你的感觉是这样——但这次愉快的交谈确实让你心中的负担减轻了一些。 “谢谢你告诉我物质世界中正在发生的事情。”随着谈话逐渐接近尾声，清子说道。“毕竟，我的感知范围仅限于这光球周围的近处而已。” 哦，能为你效劳是我的荣幸。 |你花了几分钟时间和清子闲聊，只是一些简单的客套话，其实更多是出于习惯而脱口而出的。这只狐妖像往常一样是个令人愉快的伙伴，甚至还好脾气地对你那些蹩脚的笑话报以笑声——或者至少，你觉得那些大概算是蹩脚的笑话…… |你询问了清子的近况，想知道在你们见面之间的时间里，她是否一切都好。 “还算可以吧。在被困在这个星界之前，我其实从未真正理解过‘被宠溺致死’这个概念的含义。现在嘛，可以说，我对这个道理已经有了相当深入的了解。” 俗话说，好事也可能过犹不及。如果她当时是和别人，或者是一群人一起被困在这里，情况会有什么不同呢？ 她思索了片刻。“我想，在有人作伴这方面确实会好一些，但那本身也会带来一大堆麻烦。我觉得这种事不亲身经历是说不清的——而我一刻也不想在这里多待。我们并非生来就能忍受真正的天堂；苦难自有其意义。” |有个问题你一直想问——那就是关于她作为占卜师所做出的那些预言。 “是吗？” 与其说她是在说某件事会发生，不如说她给出的是某件事发生的概率，对吧？ “没错。当然，有时候某件事发生的概率几乎可以说是必然的，而有时候则几乎可以肯定一定会落空。” 如果某件事几乎肯定会发生，那么我们能否将其称为命运呢？ “也许吧。‘命运’这个词本身就带有很重的分量；它让人觉得被预言的事情背后蕴含着某种不可抗拒的力量。不过，即使你注定要去做某件事，你实现这个命运的方式仍然可以有天壤之别。你可以走通往城市的大道，也可以翻越群山。可以挑一条轻松的路，也可能一路挣扎尖叫着被拖向目的地。” 那么它听起来就不是那么有用了……至少在实际应用中并不是如此。 耸耸肩，笑了笑。“你为什么认为我会把精力集中在所谓的‘正规魔法’上呢？” 呵呵。不过，你总得找个机会让她给你算算命。 “只要给我足够的时间准备，这件事应该不会太难。” 你会对此感到非常期待的。 ]

rows.original: Talk a bit about this and that.
rows.translation: 闲聊几句，聊聊这个那个的。
rows.raw: "Talk a bit about this and that."

rows.original: [rand|So, what did Kiyoko do when she was — um — out there? What role did she play in service of Keros? She thinks a moment, dredging up old memories. "My talents didn't lend themselves well to the kind of spying and sneaking about some of the other kitsune did — the usual rejoinder whenever that was brought up was that I was too nice for such work. Besides, my natural aptitudes quickly shoehorned me into the role of diviner. I was quite good at it, I daresay." A diviner, huh? Was her job to read the future? "Not exactly. While I did do some augury, it consisted more of telling probabilities rather than certainties. The future is always in a state of flux, and making sense out of that chaos is no small task. I'd tell someone there'd be a seven out of ten chance of it raining that day, and they'd decide where to hedge their bets. That sort of thing. People get offended when you tell bad fortunes — no one likes being told there's a nine out of ten chance lightning will strike you when you're out in town today — but I did what I could while remaining honest." "No, my main task as a diviner — one of a few handfuls — was to work Keros' particular brand of magic as and when need be in his service. Actually, wait here a moment." With that, Kiyoko stands, crosses the room to one of the cabinets, and opens a drawer. She takes out a scroll, paper tightly wound between two wooden rods and tied shut with string, then returns to the table and sets it out on the empty space by the tea set. As she unfurls the paper, you notice the beautiful, flowing calligraphy upon it, as well as the fact that each end of the two rods is capped with an emerald. [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|Drawing on your magical learning, you quickly discern the scroll's function — while rather different in form, the principles of its functioning are familiar to you. The gemstones capping each rod no doubt serve as focuses, while the calligraphy, although not intrinsically magical, serves to remind the spellcaster of the spell being cast and direct one's mind. Some things never change.] "Many spellcasters on this continent prefer staves or wands, but those who work magic in my homeland have these as their preferred tools of the trade," Kiyoko explains. "One scroll for each spell works best, but where one cannot carry very many of them, a single one can be made for multiple purposes. This trades power for adaptability, allowing the diviner to practice his or her craft while traveling light." Oh? And what does this particular spell do? The language on the scroll is quite foreign to you. To your surprise, Kiyoko blushes but manages to look indignant. "Now, a magician can't reveal all her tricks, can she?" No, maybe she can't, but you'd still like to find out. "Well, if you're so insistent..." Kiyoko's lips turn upwards in a foxy, man-eating grin. "Why don't you play with me some, and I'll demonstrate to you firsthand?" |Her captivity in the Astral Plane can't have been easy on her. You know she told you something about it when you first met, but perhaps she could go into a little more detail? At this Kiyoko sighs, staring into her cup of tea. "More than you will ever imagine, [pc.name]. Perhaps it would have been better for me to be stranded in the wilderness or on an island — at the very least, the task of keeping body and soul together would have occupied me to the fullest, and if I'd failed, at least I'd be able to die and end my torment." "Here in the Astral Plane, where I don't even need to eat and food is readily available when I feel like eating... let's say it wears down one's sanity very, very quickly if you don't take measures to keep your will to live together." She did mention hobbies. Agriculture, for example. "I did try my hand at that, yes. Then there was calligraphy, poetry, folding paper cranes, spellcraft, cooking, flower arrangement, aesthetics... essentially, if you could learn it out of a book, I gave it a go. I won't say it was easy — some avenues of learning are terribly hard without instruction or feedback, and all I had to go on was the books and my own judgement, but it stopped me from sinking into lunacy until you came along." And she's not stopping, is she? You'd hate to be the cause of any kind of break in her self-improvement routine. "Not in the least," Kiyoko replies with a weary smile. "I do need things to do in between your visits, after all. [kiyoko.numKits 2|The children may keep me busy when they're awake, but there's still plenty of time for myself. ]" |"You know, I used to love thin-fried tofu. Back home, I'd fight with my siblings over the good stuff, there was so little of it... and here in the Astral Plane, I suddenly had all the tofu could eat. No prizes for guessing what happened next." "After about a week of stuffing myself — or at least, I think it was a week — I didn't want to touch any more of it for the rest of my life. These days, I enjoy it in moderation." |You have to wonder — what was her childhood like as a kitsune? Given the cultural differences, you'd expect it to be rather different from your own. Kiyoko stops and thinks for a moment, chewing on one of the candies as the gears turn in her head. "I'm not sure if you would call it good or bad, to be honest. Materially, I certainly lacked for nothing. Several families would live in a den, and we children would gather to play every day. Most chores could be made into a game — pulling up veggies, picking fruit, catching wild birds for the pot — and that made them far more fun." It sounds like a relatively carefree childhood. "It was. Any formal instruction we kits received was from the priestess and den mother — my mother — shrine maiden, and a couple of monks who'd drop by every now and then. For living space, several families would share a large house and a communal kitchen in the central courtyard, with each family to a set of rooms. Kitsune being what they are — and with my mother being the den mother to boot — I ended up with a good number of younger brothers and sisters in short order." "I suppose I was rather lucky. While all kitsune are dedicated to Keros, those who serve him in the most direct fashion are often related by blood, the positions and ownership of the shrines being largely hereditary. My mother was distantly related through her father's side to one of the caretakers, and they just happened to need a bit more fresh blood to replace casualties from the Godswar. With yet another kit in her belly, my mother was quick to take advantage of the opportunity, and as the eldest and most talented of the litter soon I was out the door and headed to one of the grand lakeside shrines. The adventure of a lifetime, as some might say." You nod. Kiyoko pauses a moment and looks around, her tails swishing on the ground behind her. She tilts her head, downs her bitter tea in one gulp, and daintily pours herself another cup. "I'd been there for a couple of years before the Godswar began, Keros himself manifested in our world to aid in our fight, and... well, the rest is history. You probably know more about that than I do." She doesn't regret leaving her den, then. "Oh, of course not. If not for the training I received as a diviner, I'm not sure how long I would've lasted once the Godswar spread to our lands — and it did, from the reports I read. There were good memories, of course. The taste of peaches and figs off the bough, and fighting with my brothers and sisters for the best of the fruit. Swimming in the lake. Standing on the road that ran through the rice paddies, feeling the warm morning sun on my skin and fur. My mother brushing out my fur until it was all nice and fluffy, and hearing everyone else compliment me on how pretty and glossy I looked." A wistful sigh. "Those were the days — they seem so long ago. They probably are so long ago, aren't they?" Given that the Godswar ended about two hundred and fifty years ago, that probably constitutes %"long" for her. Kiyoko closes her eyes and draws a deep breath. "Then... I suppose I no longer know anyone in the outside world." Hate to be a wet blanket, but unless she knew anyone with the potential to be that long-lived... well, it's unlikely. "Yes." You wait a little longer, but it looks like Kiyoko isn't about to volunteer any more on the subject. |One wonders... Kiyoko was around during the Godswar, right? She was born during the fighting, but had some experience on the front lines, didn't she? "That's correct, yes." She might not have actually witnessed it firsthand, but some amongst her parents' generations must have — what was it like when Keros himself decided to manifest on Savarra, when the Living Gods chose to give direct aid to the world's inhabitants? How did people react? "I... I don't know, to be perfectly honest. History wasn't a subject that I delved into very deeply during my studies, and no one really wanted to talk about it very much, not with the Godswar going on and all." That's rather odd. You'd have imagined that people would be rather enamored with the gods themselves arriving on Savarra itself to help fight for its survival; wouldn't such a monumentous event be better recorded? "I'm... not sure. During my training as a diviner, I'd run across one or two people who'd actually witnessed Keros' first arrival. No doubt there was some upheaval as would be expected when one's faced with one's patron deity, but no one seemed to want to discuss it very much." Hmm. Now that's interesting. "I know that if I'd been there, I'd be more than willing to share my thoughts and feelings on the matter. But I wasn't." A shake of her head, a shrug of her shoulders. "Sorry I couldn't be of more help." Oh no, she's not to blame. |Thinking back to the foxy orgy mural you saw back in the chamber where you found Kiyoko's orb, you have to wonder — did she, um, ever participate in any of those? Kiyoko laughs. "I might have, had things been a little different. But I'm not exactly the temptress type who's usually favored at such events — oh no, the little boys are usually all over those svelte glossy-furred ladies." "Me? I'm not so well-blessed, I suppose. Then there's the matter of me finding my divination and augury studies more pressing with the war and all..." Huh. So she never went to one of those breeding orgies? "Nope, although I'll be upfront about not being a virgin by any measure of the word. It's just that every time one of those events happened, I either didn't feel like attending, had something else going on, or wasn't invited in the first place. Besides, there's no fun in tromping over weak-willed sissies who just lie there and take it without even trying to put up a fight. Too easy." Too easy, she says. "Yes." ]
rows.translation: [rand|那么，清子当年在那里——嗯——都做了些什么呢？她在为凯罗斯效力时又扮演了什么样的角色？ 她沉思片刻，试图回忆起那些往事。“我的天赋不太适合像其他一些狐妖那样搞间谍和潜行——每当有人提起这事，得到的回应总是说我干这种活儿实在太善良了。再说，我的天资很快就让我坐稳了占卜者这个位置。我敢说，我在这方面相当在行。” 一个占卜师，哈？她的职责就是预测未来吗？ “不完全是。虽然我确实做些占卜，但更多是给出概率，而非确定的结论。未来始终处于变化之中，要从那片混沌里理出头绪绝非易事。我会告诉别人，那天下雨的概率是十分之七，他们就能据此决定该往哪儿下注。诸如此类。要是你告诉别人坏消息，人们往往会觉得被冒犯——没人喜欢听人说你今天出门有十分之九的概率会被闪电劈中——但我还是在保持诚实的前提下，做了自己能做的事。” “不，作为一名占卜师——像我这样的只有寥寥几个——我的主要职责就是在需要时为他效力，施展凯罗斯特有的那类魔法。其实，你在这里稍等一下。” 说完，清子站起身，穿过房间走向其中一个柜子，拉开抽屉取出一卷卷轴。纸被紧紧卷在两根木棒之间，用绳子捆扎着。她回到桌边，把卷轴摊在茶具旁边的空位上。当她展开纸张时，你可以看到上面那些优美流畅的书法字迹，同时也会注意到，那两根木棒的两端都镶嵌着翡翠。 [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|凭借你所学的魔法知识，你很快便看出这份卷轴的用途——虽然形态颇为不同，但其运作原理对你来说并不陌生。棒子两端镶嵌的宝石无疑是用来聚焦的，而那些书法文字虽然本身并不具备魔力，却能提醒施法者正在施展的法术，并引导自己的心神。 有些东西，永远都不会改变。] “这片大陆上的许多施法者更喜欢法杖或魔杖，但在我的故乡，那些施展魔法的人更偏爱把这种卷轴当作吃饭的家伙。”清子解释道。“一个法术配一卷卷轴效果最佳，但如果一个人没法携带太多卷轴，也可以把单独一卷做成多种用途。这是以威力换取适应性，让占卜者能够轻装出行，同时施展自己的技艺。” 哦？那么这个特定的法术到底有什么作用呢？卷轴上的文字对你来说确实很陌生。 令你惊讶的是，清子竟然脸红了，但仍然努力装出一副愤慨的样子。“当然，一位魔术师不可能把自己所有的魔术手法都暴露出来，对吧？” 不，也许她做不到，但你还是想知道答案。 “好吧，既然你这么坚持……”清子的嘴角上扬，露出狐狸般勾人的笑容。“你为什么不陪我玩一会儿呢？这样我就可以亲自给你演示一下了。” |她在星界中的囚禁生活肯定非常艰难。你知道，初次见面时她确实跟你说过一些关于这件事的事情，但或许她可以讲得更详细一些？ 此时，清子叹了口气，低头凝视着杯中的茶。“远远超乎你的想象，[pc.name]。或许，我要是被困在荒野或孤岛上反而更好——至少，光是维持自己的生存就能让我全神贯注；而如果我失败了，至少我还能死去，结束这份折磨。” “而在星界这里，我甚至不需要进食，只要想吃，食物就唾手可得……这么说吧，如果不设法维系自己的求生意志，它侵蚀一个人的理智的速度会非常非常快。” 她确实提到过自己的爱好，比如农业。 “我确实试过那个，没错。还有书法、诗歌、折纸鹤、法术、烹饪、插花、审美……基本上，只要能从书中学习到的东西，我都会尝试一下。我不会说这些事情很容易——有些学习领域如果没有老师的指导或反馈，确实会非常困难，而我所能依靠的只有书籍和自己的判断力。不过，在你出现之前，这些尝试至少让我没有陷入疯狂。” 她并不打算停下来，对吧？你可不想成为她自我提升计划中断的原因。 “一点也不。”清子疲惫地笑了笑作为回应。“毕竟，在你两次来访之间，我总得有些事情做。 [kiyoko.numKits 2|孩子们醒着的时候可能会让我忙得团团转，但我还是有很多属于自己的时间。 ]” |“你知道吗，我以前很喜欢煎豆腐。在家里，我会和兄弟姐妹们为了一点好豆腐争抢，因为那东西实在太少……而到了星界，我突然有了吃不完的豆腐。接下来发生了什么，不用我说你也猜得到。” “在连续大吃了大约一周之后——至少我觉得是这样——我这辈子都不想再碰它了。如今我只会适量享用。” |你不禁会想——作为一个狐妖，她的童年是怎样的呢？考虑到文化上的差异，她的童年肯定与你的童年有着很大的不同。 清子停下来想了一会儿，一边嚼着一颗糖，一边在脑子里转着这些念头。“说实话，我不确定你会把这种生活称为好事还是坏事。从物质条件来看，我们确实什么都不缺。几户人家会住在一个巢穴里，我们这些孩子每天都会聚在一起玩耍。大多数家务活都能变成游戏——拔菜、摘果子、抓野鸟下锅——这样它们就有趣多了。” 听起来那是一段相当无忧无虑的童年时光。 “确实是这样。我们这些幼狐所受的一切正式教导，都来自女祭司兼巢母——也就是我的母亲，一位神社巫女——以及偶尔会来访的几位僧侣。至于居住环境，几户家庭会共同使用中央庭院里的一栋大房子和一间公共厨房，每户家庭则拥有自己的一组房间。狐妖本就如此，再加上我的母亲本身就是巢母，不久之后我就有了一大群弟弟妹妹。” “我想我确实运气不错。虽然所有的狐妖都效忠于凯罗斯，但那些以最直接的方式为他服务的人往往有着血缘关系，因为那些神社的职位和所有权大多是世袭的。我的母亲通过父系与其中一位神社看护者是远亲，而他们正好需要一些新鲜血液，来填补神战中损失的人手。母亲肚子里又怀上了一只幼狐，于是她立刻抓住了这个机会；作为那一胎里最年长、天赋最高的孩子，我很快就被送出门，前往湖边一座宏伟的神社。有些人会说，那是一生一次的冒险。” 你点了点头。 清子停顿了一下，环顾四周，她的尾巴在身后地上甩来甩去。她歪了歪头，一口喝光了那杯苦茶，然后又优雅地给自己倒了一杯。“在神战爆发之前，我已经在那里待了好几年。凯罗斯本人降临到我们的世界，帮助我们进行抗争，而……嗯，接下来的事，你大概比我更清楚。” 那么，她并不后悔离开自己的巢穴。 “哦，当然不会。要不是因为我接受了占卜者的训练，我真不确定当神战蔓延到我们的土地上时，我还能坚持多久——从我读到的报道来看，神战确实发生了。当然，其中也有一些美好的回忆。枝头摘下的桃子和无花果的滋味，和兄弟姐妹们争抢最好吃的水果。在湖里游泳，站在穿过稻田的小路上，感受着清晨温暖的阳光洒在皮肤和毛发上。我的母亲仔细地梳理我的毛发，直到它变得柔软蓬松，然后听到其他人都夸我看起来多么漂亮、多么有光泽。” 一声怅然的叹息。“那些日子啊——仿佛已经过去很久了。它们或许确实已经是很久以前的事了，不是吗？” 鉴于神战大约在两百五十年前结束，对她来说，那大概也算得上是%"“漫长”了。 清子闭上眼睛，深吸了一口气。“那么……我想，我在外面的世界里已经不再认识任何人了。” 虽然不想泼冷水，但除非她认识某个有可能活那么久的人……嗯，那不太可能。 “是的。” 你又等了一会儿，但看起来清子无意再主动谈起这个话题。 |人们不禁会想……在神战期间，清子应该也在场吧？她虽然是在战争期间出生的，但应该也有一些在前线作战的经验吧？ “没错，就是这样。” 她本人可能并未亲历这一幕，但她父母那一代里肯定有人见过——当凯罗斯亲自决定在萨瓦拉现身，当那些活神决定直接帮助这个世界上的生灵时，人们又是如何反应的呢？ “我……说实话，我也不知道。在我的学习期间，历史并不是我钻研得很深的科目，再加上当时神战正打得不可开交，也没人愿意多谈这个话题。” 这确实有点奇怪。你本以为，神明亲临萨瓦拉、为它的存亡而战，人们应该会对此津津乐道才对；如此重大的事件，难道不该被更好地记录下来吗？ “我……不太确定。在我接受占卜师训练的过程中，确实遇到过一两个人，他们亲眼目睹了凯罗斯第一次降临。毫无疑问，当人们面对自己的守护神时，肯定会发生一些动荡，但似乎没有人愿意过多地谈论这件事。” 嗯，这可真有意思。 “我知道，如果我在场的话，一定会非常乐意分享自己对此事的看法和感受。但我当时并不在场。”她摇了摇头，耸了耸肩。“很抱歉，我实在无能为力。” 哦不，这不能怪她。 |回想一下你在找到清子的宝珠的那个房间里看到的那幅描绘狐妖群交的壁画，你不禁会想——她，嗯，有没有参与过其中任何一场呢？ 清子笑了。“要是情况稍有不同，我也许会去。不过，我并不是那种在这类场合通常受青睐的狐媚女子——哦不，那些身材苗条、毛发油亮的女士才会让小伙子们趋之若鹜。” “我吗？我想我没那么好的福气吧。再加上当时还在打仗，我觉得钻研占卜和预兆这些事更要紧……” 哈，这么说她从来没参加过那种交配狂欢吗？ “没有，不过我得直说，无论从哪个意义上讲，我都算不上处女。只是每次有这种活动的时候，我要么没兴趣参加，要么当时有别的安排，要么根本就没被邀请。再说，欺负那些软弱无力、连反抗都不会尝试的人，根本没什么意思——太容易了。” 太简单了，她说。 “是的。” ]
rows.raw: " [rand|So, what did Kiyoko do when she was — um — out there? What role did she play in service of Keros? She thinks a moment, dredging up old memories. "My talents didn't lend themselves well to the kind of spying and sneaking about some of the other kitsune did — the usual rejoinder whenever that was brought up was that I was too nice for such work. Besides, my natural aptitudes quickly shoehorned me into the role of diviner. I was quite good at it, I daresay." A diviner, huh? Was her job to read the future? "Not exactly. While I did do some augury, it consisted more of telling probabilities rather than certainties. The future is always in a state of flux, and making sense out of that chaos is no small task. I'd tell someone there'd be a seven out of ten chance of it raining that day, and they'd decide where to hedge their bets. That sort of thing. People get offended when you tell bad fortunes — no one likes being told there's a nine out of ten chance lightning will strike you when you're out in town today — but I did what I could while remaining honest." "No, my main task as a diviner — one of a few handfuls — was to work Keros' particular brand of magic as and when need be in his service. Actually, wait here a moment." With that, Kiyoko stands, crosses the room to one of the cabinets, and opens a drawer. She takes out a scroll, paper tightly wound between two wooden rods and tied shut with string, then returns to the table and sets it out on the empty space by the tea set. As she unfurls the paper, you notice the beautiful, flowing calligraphy upon it, as well as the fact that each end of the two rods is capped with an emerald. [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|Drawing on your magical learning, you quickly discern the scroll's function — while rather different in form, the principles of its functioning are familiar to you. The gemstones capping each rod no doubt serve as focuses, while the calligraphy, although not intrinsically magical, serves to remind the spellcaster of the spell being cast and direct one's mind. Some things never change.] "Many spellcasters on this continent prefer staves or wands, but those who work magic in my homeland have these as their preferred tools of the trade," Kiyoko explains. "One scroll for each spell works best, but where one cannot carry very many of them, a single one can be made for multiple purposes. This trades power for adaptability, allowing the diviner to practice his or her craft while traveling light." Oh? And what does this particular spell do? The language on the scroll is quite foreign to you. To your surprise, Kiyoko blushes but manages to look indignant. "Now, a magician can't reveal all her tricks, can she?" No, maybe she can't, but you'd still like to find out. "Well, if you're so insistent..." Kiyoko's lips turn upwards in a foxy, man-eating grin. "Why don't you play with me some, and I'll demonstrate to you firsthand?" |Her captivity in the Astral Plane can't have been easy on her. You know she told you something about it when you first met, but perhaps she could go into a little more detail? At this Kiyoko sighs, staring into her cup of tea. "More than you will ever imagine, [pc.name]. Perhaps it would have been better for me to be stranded in the wilderness or on an island — at the very least, the task of keeping body and soul together would have occupied me to the fullest, and if I'd failed, at least I'd be able to die and end my torment." "Here in the Astral Plane, where I don't even need to eat and food is readily available when I feel like eating... let's say it wears down one's sanity very, very quickly if you don't take measures to keep your will to live together." She did mention hobbies. Agriculture, for example. "I did try my hand at that, yes. Then there was calligraphy, poetry, folding paper cranes, spellcraft, cooking, flower arrangement, aesthetics... essentially, if you could learn it out of a book, I gave it a go. I won't say it was easy — some avenues of learning are terribly hard without instruction or feedback, and all I had to go on was the books and my own judgement, but it stopped me from sinking into lunacy until you came along." And she's not stopping, is she? You'd hate to be the cause of any kind of break in her self-improvement routine. "Not in the least," Kiyoko replies with a weary smile. "I do need things to do in between your visits, after all. [kiyoko.numKits 2|The children may keep me busy when they're awake, but there's still plenty of time for myself. ]" |"You know, I used to love thin-fried tofu. Back home, I'd fight with my siblings over the good stuff, there was so little of it... and here in the Astral Plane, I suddenly had all the tofu could eat. No prizes for guessing what happened next." "After about a week of stuffing myself — or at least, I think it was a week — I didn't want to touch any more of it for the rest of my life. These days, I enjoy it in moderation." |You have to wonder — what was her childhood like as a kitsune? Given the cultural differences, you'd expect it to be rather different from your own. Kiyoko stops and thinks for a moment, chewing on one of the candies as the gears turn in her head. "I'm not sure if you would call it good or bad, to be honest. Materially, I certainly lacked for nothing. Several families would live in a den, and we children would gather to play every day. Most chores could be made into a game — pulling up veggies, picking fruit, catching wild birds for the pot — and that made them far more fun." It sounds like a relatively carefree childhood. "It was. Any formal instruction we kits received was from the priestess and den mother — my mother — shrine maiden, and a couple of monks who'd drop by every now and then. For living space, several families would share a large house and a communal kitchen in the central courtyard, with each family to a set of rooms. Kitsune being what they are — and with my mother being the den mother to boot — I ended up with a good number of younger brothers and sisters in short order." "I suppose I was rather lucky. While all kitsune are dedicated to Keros, those who serve him in the most direct fashion are often related by blood, the positions and ownership of the shrines being largely hereditary. My mother was distantly related through her father's side to one of the caretakers, and they just happened to need a bit more fresh blood to replace casualties from the Godswar. With yet another kit in her belly, my mother was quick to take advantage of the opportunity, and as the eldest and most talented of the litter soon I was out the door and headed to one of the grand lakeside shrines. The adventure of a lifetime, as some might say." You nod. Kiyoko pauses a moment and looks around, her tails swishing on the ground behind her. She tilts her head, downs her bitter tea in one gulp, and daintily pours herself another cup. "I'd been there for a couple of years before the Godswar began, Keros himself manifested in our world to aid in our fight, and... well, the rest is history. You probably know more about that than I do." She doesn't regret leaving her den, then. "Oh, of course not. If not for the training I received as a diviner, I'm not sure how long I would've lasted once the Godswar spread to our lands — and it did, from the reports I read. There were good memories, of course. The taste of peaches and figs off the bough, and fighting with my brothers and sisters for the best of the fruit. Swimming in the lake. Standing on the road that ran through the rice paddies, feeling the warm morning sun on my skin and fur. My mother brushing out my fur until it was all nice and fluffy, and hearing everyone else compliment me on how pretty and glossy I looked." A wistful sigh. "Those were the days — they seem so long ago. They probably are so long ago, aren't they?" Given that the Godswar ended about two hundred and fifty years ago, that probably constitutes %"long" for her. Kiyoko closes her eyes and draws a deep breath. "Then... I suppose I no longer know anyone in the outside world." Hate to be a wet blanket, but unless she knew anyone with the potential to be that long-lived... well, it's unlikely. "Yes." You wait a little longer, but it looks like Kiyoko isn't about to volunteer any more on the subject. |One wonders... Kiyoko was around during the Godswar, right? She was born during the fighting, but had some experience on the front lines, didn't she? "That's correct, yes." She might not have actually witnessed it firsthand, but some amongst her parents' generations must have — what was it like when Keros himself decided to manifest on Savarra, when the Living Gods chose to give direct aid to the world's inhabitants? How did people react? "I... I don't know, to be perfectly honest. History wasn't a subject that I delved into very deeply during my studies, and no one really wanted to talk about it very much, not with the Godswar going on and all." That's rather odd. You'd have imagined that people would be rather enamored with the gods themselves arriving on Savarra itself to help fight for its survival; wouldn't such a monumentous event be better recorded? "I'm... not sure. During my training as a diviner, I'd run across one or two people who'd actually witnessed Keros' first arrival. No doubt there was some upheaval as would be expected when one's faced with one's patron deity, but no one seemed to want to discuss it very much." Hmm. Now that's interesting. "I know that if I'd been there, I'd be more than willing to share my thoughts and feelings on the matter. But I wasn't." A shake of her head, a shrug of her shoulders. "Sorry I couldn't be of more help." Oh no, she's not to blame. |Thinking back to the foxy orgy mural you saw back in the chamber where you found Kiyoko's orb, you have to wonder — did she, um, ever participate in any of those? Kiyoko laughs. "I might have, had things been a little different. But I'm not exactly the temptress type who's usually favored at such events — oh no, the little boys are usually all over those svelte glossy-furred ladies." "Me? I'm not so well-blessed, I suppose. Then there's the matter of me finding my divination and augury studies more pressing with the war and all..." Huh. So she never went to one of those breeding orgies? "Nope, although I'll be upfront about not being a virgin by any measure of the word. It's just that every time one of those events happened, I either didn't feel like attending, had something else going on, or wasn't invited in the first place. Besides, there's no fun in tromping over weak-willed sissies who just lie there and take it without even trying to put up a fight. Too easy." Too easy, she says. "Yes." ]"

rows.translation: 去问问清子关于她自己的事情吧。

rows.original: You lean over the table and ask Kiyoko if she can divine what the future holds for you. Kiyoko looks a little unsure. "Do you really want to do this, [pc.name]? Knowing one's future isn't always necessarily for the best. There are things which are better left unknown, and worrying about bad fortune can easily compound it." She is a diviner, isn't she? "Well, yes. But if I learned anything from being one, it's that I shouldn't flaunt such power willy-nilly." Kiyoko tenses a little while longer, then sighs and sags her shoulders. "Although if you insist, I suppose I will do it for you. I owe you as much for visiting me so often." Will you insist on having Kiyoko tell your fortune?
rows.translation: 你俯身在桌子上，询问清子是否能够预知你的未来会怎样。 清子看起来有些不确定。“你真的想这么做吗，[pc.name]？知道自己的未来并不总是好事。有些事最好还是留作未知，而担心厄运只会让厄运更重。” 她应该是个占卜师吧？ “嗯，是的。但身为占卜师让我学到了一点：我不该随随便便炫耀这种力量。”清子又绷紧了一会儿，然后叹了口气，肩膀垮了下来。“不过如果你坚持，我想我还是会为你做的。你常来看我，我欠你这份人情。” 你非要让清子为你算命吗？
