It's just that you were wondering what it was for, since there's nothing in it to make it ring. "It's not supposed to be functional. The anklet grows along with her, you see, so it's never too tight — although our daughter could take it off any time at this point, she doesn't want to. By now, I suppose you could say it's a part of her." That's one way to put it. "I wouldn't put too much thought into it, really," Kiyoko assures you. "It's just an accessory she likes to wear, that's all." |"I... won't deny that there are some days where I get a little jealous of Kinu," Kiyoko admits with a sigh. "I don't think it's natural for mothers to resent their daughters for the knowledge that they will surpass her someday..." You won't condone it, but neither is the feeling wrong in and of itself. She's still a kitsune, after all. It would be abnormal if even someone as sunny and genial as Kiyoko didn't feel jealous every now and then. "Do you feel jealous of our daughter, I wonder? It's as if she took the best of what we had to offer and combined them into one person." Now, is she sure that isn't some hyperbole right there? "No, really. She just picks things up so effortlessly, it's scary. Her siblings look up to, if not respect her. Some days when I look at her, I'm reminded of how I was when I was her age... I just ate and played a lot, or at least more than I should have." Well, your daughter might be intelligent, but she still lacks the wisdom to make truly good decisions on her own, right? She'll have to serve as Kinu's font of wisdom until her daughter can make her own way in life. Kiyoko sighs and sets down her tea. "I don't know. I just..." You reach across the table and give the kitsune mother a good petting between her big, fluffy ears. Kiyoko instinctively cranes her head forward to receive the affection, her jade-green eyes closing as she purrs gently. Now, then. It's understandable that she feels a little sad to see her daughter grow up, especially at such a young age and given the circumstances of the Astral Plane. But ultimately, the duty of a mother is to prepare her children for the day when they will no longer need her. Kinu may grow into someone greater than the two of you combined, but it's up to you and her — especially her, since you can't be around so often — to mold your daughter correctly and set her on the right path in life. Kiyoko looks away as you finish the petting, but doesn't say anything. There, there. |"Ehehe. Our daughter has really taken a shine to children. She seems to love her brothers and sisters more than I did when I was her age." Perhaps it's got something to do with the fact that unlike her mother, she doesn't have to deal with wailing fox kits and mountains of dirty diapers? "It's more than that, I think. She's just naturally good with her brothers and sisters and actually likes being put in charge of them; it's gotten to the point where I feel comfortable delegating important sibling-related responsibilities to her and know she'll carry them out with enthusiasm." A model big sister, then. Or maybe she just likes bossing around her siblings... while it's good that she's learning to wield authority at such a young age, even in a limited fashion, she needs to understand that this authority is to be wielded for the benefit of others, not massaging her own ego. Kiyoko looks thoughtful at that. "Come to think of it... hm. That explains a few things." Pardon? "Oh, it's nothing. But you're right — I should probably stress that bit of her education in responsibility a little more." ]
rows.translation: 一提到小娟的名字，清子就会抿起嘴唇微微一笑。 “哦，她啊。有时候我真的很喜欢她 [kiyoko.numKits 3|最年长的 ]女儿……有时候她真的会让我感到无比恼火，甚至让我希望能把她重新塞回她来的地方去。” 就等着她长大吧。母女之间总有些东西会让她们彼此对立，哪怕是在最和睦的家庭里，不是吗？ 一声叹息。“如今我处在当年我母亲的位置上，不禁会想，那些年的我是不是也这么爱哭爱闹、让人头疼。当然，从我自己的角度看好像并非如此，但话说回来，我在评价自己的行为时也没法保证客观公正……” 嗯，尽管小娟很聪明，但她是一个孩子，而且还是只狐妖；她自然会有一些特定的冲动和癖好。智慧这种东西，只有靠时间才能获得。 清子没有回答这个问题，只是拼命地喝着茶。 [rand|“我知道，想要溺爱我们的女儿是很自然的，尤其是考虑到你不可能一直待在星界中。”狐狸母亲终于开口说道。“但请不要送她太多礼物。” 你并没有—— “我并不是在指责你什么， [pc.name]但是，如果我们的女儿一次性吃了太多甜食，她就会变得非常闹腾——简直就像是在墙上蹦来蹦去，甚至在天花板上奔跑，根本不愿意安静下来学习或让别人给她梳头发。事实上，在她把自己累得精疲力尽、先小睡一会儿之前，她根本无法完成任何日常家务活。” 天哪。 “而这还只是她稍微多吃了一点的时候。如果我不加以约束，她肯定会跑到桃树林里去，吃个够而生病。我已经在一定程度上让她改掉了这个习惯，但你们送给她的礼物，她仍然会认为是可以吃的。” 好吧，你明白她的意思了。 “我不是说你们不能给我们的女儿送礼物，但请尽量适可而止。我只求这一点。我可不想看到她躺在山坡上，疼得抱着肚子，然后发现她居然试图一口气吃下两个整只甜瓜。一个没那么聪明的孩子说不定还能从这种经历里学到点东西，但她特别擅长为自己的错误找借口。聪明并不一定意味着你会更有理智——真要说的话，那只意味着替自己找借口会变得更容易。” |那么，她的学习进展如何呢？ “我们的女儿想成为像我这样的巢母。”清子回答道。“我真应该感到荣幸才对，不是吗？” 嗯，有了这样一个如此优秀的榜样可以效仿…… “哼，现在你也不要开始说这种话了。不过，我的确打算这样培养她。按照传统，这个头衔应该是从母亲传给长女，但我感觉等我们离开这里后，还有很多事情需要去处理——所以她获得这个头衔的时间会比预期来得更早。” 究竟有哪些东西会从一位巢母传给下一代呢？ “目前我正在努力培养我们女儿的良好性格。毕竟，外貌会随时间而消逝，智力也会随着年龄的增长而减退，但热情的性格和愉悦的心情却会伴随人的一生。” 这确实是一项相当艰巨的任务，而且可能需要花费相当长的时间才能完成；听起来这不是一夜之间就能解决的事情，而且你也不认为小娟惊人的学习速度能在这方面起到什么帮助。那么，她究竟是如何着手进行这项工作的呢？ “让她做家务。” 就这些吗？ 一丝淡淡的微笑。“你低估了这里可能会冒出来的家务活的数量，[pc.name]。而且当我没法让星界自己把弄乱的东西重新整理好时，这个数量还要翻倍。相信我，狐妖的孩子们特别擅长制造一大堆烂摊子。” 啊…… “再加上狐妖的孩子们活力旺盛，总是惹上各种各样的麻烦，人很快就会学会在面对足以让别人抓狂的逆境时保持积极的心态。身为巢母，她需要这种心态。”清子放下茶杯，拿了一颗糖果放进嘴里，若有所思地咀嚼着。“你该不会以为我一生下来就一直这么冷静、和善吧？” 嗯……说实话，你确实可以看到这种情况发生。至少，她小时候并没有哭闹太多，对吧？ 清子翻了个白眼，但还是笑了起来。“我小时候的确是只安静的幼崽，但天生的性情也需要悉心培养才能达到最佳状态。我正在这样培养我们的女儿——你只管放心，把她的教育交给我吧。” |“昨天真是累人啊。” 哦？发生了什么事？ “我不想细谈这些细节；过一段时间后，所有这些事情似乎都会混在了一起。总之，我们的女儿是个非常善于操纵他人的家伙，如果我不是一只狐妖的话，她肯定能把我玩得团团转。” 嗯，她是一只毛茸茸的狐妖……狐妖侍奉欺诈者可不是没有理由的，这一点她应该很清楚。 叹了口气。“哦，她可爱、讨人喜欢、毛茸茸的、摸起来很舒服，等等等等。而且她知道那样做能大大增加她得到想要东西的机会，哪怕对象是我，所以她总是那样做。就算在不高兴的时候，我们的女儿只要那么一撅嘴，看起来还是那么惹人怜爱……当一位母亲不得不管教一个任性的孩子时，她又能怎么办呢？” 她把小娟形容得好像是个狡猾的小狐妖一样…… “哦，我相当确定她并不是一直在装模作样，但很难分辨她什么时候是真心表现得可爱，什么时候只是在表演。而且问题还不止这些——昨天， [ kiyoko.numKits 4 |我发现她哄骗其中一个年幼的兄弟姐妹帮她摘桃子……” 哦不。 “哦，对了。‘妈妈说我不能摘任何水果，但她并没有提到你就这么做了……你可以想象接下来发生了什么。我不得不狠狠地打他们俩一顿。” |晚餐时，她试图把我绕得团团转，想让我用更多的肯钦汤来代替她的甜点。而我呢，还费了那么大劲才做出那些美味的大福…… 你肯定听说过孩子们总是想用蔬菜来换甜点，而从不会反过来想用甜点来换蔬菜。 “不管有没有甜点，只吃自己喜欢的东西而忽略其他食物，甚至更糟糕的是把不喜欢的食物强加给别人，这种行为都是不妥当的。我不得不把她拉到一边，反复跟她强调这一点。” ] 一个令人遗憾但不得不做出的决定。 清子点了点头。“听着，我不是想贬低我们这个天才女儿，但是……别上她的当，好吗？我知道你们很想宠小娟，因为你们没法像自己希望的那样经常陪在她身边，但别让她一直骗得你们顺着她的意思来。我宁愿她长大后不要变成人们对我们狐妖的那些负面刻板印象的样子；如果她想当一名巢母，孩子气地耍手段可不会给她加分。” 好的，你明白我的意思了。 “好的。”清子深吸一口气，然后缓缓呼出。“并不是说我对孩子们的爱不如刚开始的时候那么深了，但有时候，在一天结束之后，能和一位成年人进行一些有意义的对话，确实是一件很愉快的事情。因此，我真的很期待你的到访。” |你确实有一个问题想要问…… “是吗？” 小娟的铃铛脚链是从哪里来的？ “哦，这是她在出生几天后我制作的。这算是一种幸运符——它的作用就是让佩戴者与生命紧紧相连，你懂的。至于那个铃铛，我只是觉得它为这个原本很普通的脚链增添了一些趣味。” 你瞧，你之前一直在疑惑这个东西是用来做什么的，因为里面什么都没有，根本不可能发出声音来。 “这个脚链本来就不是为了实用而设计的。你看，这个脚链会随着她的成长而一起变化，所以它从来都不会太紧——虽然我们的女儿现在随时都可以把它摘下来，但她并不想这么做。我想，现在这个脚链已经成为了她身体的一部分了。” 也可以这么说。 “其实，我并不觉得这件事需要花太多心思去考虑。”清子向你保证。“那只是她喜欢佩戴的一个配饰而已，没什么特别的。” |“我……不得不承认，有时候我确实会有点嫉妒小娟。”清子叹了口气，承认道。“我认为，母亲们因为担心自己的女儿有朝一日会超越自己而心生怨恨，这种情绪其实并不符合常理……” 你不会认同这种情绪，但这种情绪本身也谈不上错。毕竟，她终究是只狐妖。如果连清子这样开朗和善的人都不偶尔嫉妒一下，那才不正常。 “我倒是很好奇，你会不会嫉妒我们的女儿呢？她仿佛把我们俩能拿出的最好的东西都取走，揉合成了一个人。” 现在，她真的确定那不是在夸张吗？ “不，是真的。她学什么都毫不费力，简直吓人。她的弟弟妹妹们就算谈不上敬重她，至少也很仰慕她。有时候我看着她，就会想起自己在她这个年纪时的样子……我那时整天只知道吃和玩，至少玩得比该玩的要多。” 嗯，你的女儿也许很聪明，但她仍然缺乏独自做出真正明智决定的智慧，对吧？在小娟能够自己闯出一条路之前，她还得继续充当女儿的智慧之源。 清子叹了口气，然后放下了茶杯。“我不知道。我只是……” 你伸手穿过桌子，轻轻抚摸那只狐妈妈那双蓬松的大耳朵。清子本能地把头凑过来接受这份关爱，她那翡翠般绿色的眼睛闭上了，轻轻发出呜呜声。 现在嘛，她看到自己的女儿长大，尤其是在她这么小的年纪、又身处星界这样的环境中，会感到有些难过也是可以理解的。但归根结底，母亲的职责就是为孩子们准备好那一天——他们不再需要她的那一天。小娟也许会成长成比你们两个人加起来还要出色的人，但是否能让她成为那样的人，取决于你和她——尤其是她，因为你没法经常陪在她身边——是否能够正确地引导她，让她走上正确的人生道路。 当你结束抚摸她的动作时，清子将视线移开了，但什么也没说。 好了，好了。 |“嘿嘿，我们的女儿真的很喜欢小孩子。她对待自己的弟弟妹妹们，似乎比我在她这个年纪时对他们的感情还要深啊。” 也许这与一个事实有关：与她的母亲不同，她不必应付那些哭闹的狐妖幼崽，也不必清理堆积如山的脏尿布吧？ “我觉得，事情并不只是这样。她天生就善于与兄弟姐妹相处，事实上喜欢现在由她来负责这些事情；我已经到了这样一个阶段：我可以放心地将一些与兄弟姐妹相关的重要职责委托给她，而且我相信她会满怀热情地去完成这些任务。” 那么，她应该是一个模范姐姐吧。或者，也许她只是喜欢指挥自己的弟弟妹妹们……虽然她在这么小的年纪就开始学习如何行使权力，哪怕这种权力只是有限的，但她需要明白，这种权力应该是为了帮助别人，而不是用来满足自己的虚荣心。 清子若有所思地听着这些话。“仔细想来……嗯，这就解释了一些事情了。” 什么？ “哦，没什么。不过你说得对——我确实应该再着重强调一下她关于责任感的教育。” ]
rows.raw: " At the mention of Kinu's name, Kiyoko gives you a thin-lipped smile. "Oh, her. Some days I love my [kiyoko.numKits 3|eldest ]daughter... and some days she exasperates me to the point where I wish I could stuff her back into where she came from." Just wait till she gets older. There's something about mothers and daughters that sets them to odds even in the most harmonious of families, isn't there? A sigh. "Now that I'm in my mother's position, I can't help but wonder if I was as much of a screaming handful all those years ago. Sure, it doesn't seem that way from my perspective, but then again I can't rely on myself to be honest when assessing my own behavior..." Well, for all her intelligence, Kinu is a child, and a kitsune at that; she'll have certain impulses and proclivities. Wisdom is something that's only gained with time. Kiyoko doesn't answer that, but sips furiously at her tea. [rand|"I know it's tempting to want to spoil our daughter, especially since you can't be here in the Astral Plane all the time," the kitsune mother says at last. "But please don't give her too many gifts." Now, you didn't — "I'm not accusing you of anything, [pc.name]. But our daughter is a terror when she'd had too many sweet things at once — she's practically bouncing off the walls and running across the ceiling, and won't sit still to study or be brushed. In fact, she becomes absolutely useless for any of her daily chores until she's exhausted herself and had a nap first." Goodness. "And that's only when she's had a bit too much. If I don't rein her in, she'll get into the peach grove and eat herself sick. I've somewhat managed to discipline that out of her, but your gifts to her are still considered fair game." All right, you get her point. "I'm not saying that you can't give our daughter gifts, but please try to keep it in moderation. That's all I ask. I don't want to find her lying on the hillside holding her tummy in pain, and discover that she tried to eat two whole sweet melons in one go. A less intelligent child might actually learn something from the experience, but she's great at rationalizing away her mistakes. Being smart doesn't necessarily mean that you behave more sensibly — if anything, it means making excuses for yourself all the easier." |So, how is her education proceeding? "Our daughter wants to be a den mother like me," Kiyoko replies. "I really should be flattered, shouldn't I?" Well, with such a great example to follow... "Hmph. Now don't you start as well. But yes, that's the way I'm taking her education in. Traditionally, the title is handed from mother to eldest daughter, but I get the feeling that there's a lot of empty land to be settled once we get out of here — and hence she'll get to be one sooner than expected." What sorts of things are passed down from one den mother to the next, anyway? "Right now I'm trying to improve our daughter's temperament. After all, beauty fades and the mind dulls with age, but a warm personality and pleasant temperament last till your dying day." A rather impressive undertaking, and one that probably is going to take some time; it doesn't sound like the thing that can be done overnight, and you don't think Kinu's astronomical rate of learning will help in this case. How is she going about it, though? "Having her do housework." That's all? A thin smile. "You underestimate the amount of housework than can potentially crop up here, [pc.name]. That goes double when I don't get the Astral Plane to re-order itself when messes crop up. And trust me, kitsune children tend to make a lot of messes." Ah... "Add that to the fact the kitsune children are boisterous and tend to get into all sorts of trouble, and one quickly learns to cultivate a positive temperament in the face of adversity that would have others screaming in exasperation. She will need it as a den mother." Kiyoko sets down her tea and pops a candy into her mouth, chewing thoughtfully. "You didn't think I came out of the womb this calm and genial all the time, did you?" Well... to be honest, you can see that happening. At the very least, she didn't cry much as a baby, did she? Kiyoko rolls her eyes, but smiles. "It's true I was a calm kit, but natural inclinations must still be carefully cultivated to reach their zenith. I'm doing that with our daughter — just relax and leave her education to me." |"Yesterday was rather tiring." Oh? What happened? "I don't want to go into the details; after a while, each and every incident seems to blend into each other. Suffice to say that our daughter is a master manipulator, and that if I weren't a kitsune myself she'd have me wrapped about her little finger." Well, she is a fluffy kitsune... and they don't serve the Trickster for no reason. She should know as much. A sigh. "Oh, she's cute, and adorable, and fluffy, and nice to pet, and so on. And she knows that acting that way will considerably improve her chances of getting what she wants, even from me, so she does it all the time. Even when she's upset, our daughter can pout just so and still appear endearing... what's a mother to do when she has to instil some discipline in a wayward child?" She's starting to make Kinu sound like some kind of devious little vixen... "Oh, I'm pretty sure that she isn't acting all the time, but it's hard to tell when she's truly being endearing, and when she's just putting on an act. That's not the end of it, either — yesterday, [ kiyoko.numKits 4 |I caught her tricking one of her younger siblings into picking peaches for her..." Oh no. "Oh yes. 'Mama said I couldn't pick any of the fruit, but she didn't say anything about you doing it...' You can imagine what happened next. I had to spank the both of them quite soundly." |she tried to talk circles around me over dinner, trying to get me to replace her dessert with more kenchin soup. And I went to all that trouble to make such good daifuku, too..." You've heard of children wanting to swap their vegetables for dessert, not the other way around. "Dessert or not, it's improper to eat only things you like and leave out the rest or even worse, foist them onto others; I had to take her aside and drill that into her head." ] A regrettable but necessary decision. Kiyoko nods. "Look, I'm not trying to put down our prodigy of a daughter, but... don't get tricked, okay? I know the temptation is there to spoil Kinu as you don't get to be with her as often as you'd like, but don't let her fool you into doing what she wants all the time. I'd rather her not grow up to conform to every negative stereotype about us kitsune, and if she wants to be a den mother being childishly manipulative is not going to be a point in her favor." Okay, you understand. "Good." Kiyoko heaves in a deep breath, and exhales. "It's not that I don't love our children any less than when we started, but sometimes it's nice to have an adult to hold an intelligent conversation with at the end of the day. It makes me look forward to your visits." |You did have a question you wanted to ask... "Yes?" Where did Kinu's bell anklet come from? "Oh, I made it a couple of days after she was born. It's a sort of good-luck charm — it's meant to keep the wearer tightly locked to life, you see. As for the bell, I just thought it was a nice touch to what was otherwise a plain anklet." You see. It's just that you were wondering what it was for, since there's nothing in it to make it ring. "It's not supposed to be functional. The anklet grows along with her, you see, so it's never too tight — although our daughter could take it off any time at this point, she doesn't want to. By now, I suppose you could say it's a part of her." That's one way to put it. "I wouldn't put too much thought into it, really," Kiyoko assures you. "It's just an accessory she likes to wear, that's all." |"I... won't deny that there are some days where I get a little jealous of Kinu," Kiyoko admits with a sigh. "I don't think it's natural for mothers to resent their daughters for the knowledge that they will surpass her someday..." You won't condone it, but neither is the feeling wrong in and of itself. She's still a kitsune, after all. It would be abnormal if even someone as sunny and genial as Kiyoko didn't feel jealous every now and then. "Do you feel jealous of our daughter, I wonder? It's as if she took the best of what we had to offer and combined them into one person." Now, is she sure that isn't some hyperbole right there? "No, really. She just picks things up so effortlessly, it's scary. Her siblings look up to, if not respect her. Some days when I look at her, I'm reminded of how I was when I was her age... I just ate and played a lot, or at least more than I should have." Well, your daughter might be intelligent, but she still lacks the wisdom to make truly good decisions on her own, right? She'll have to serve as Kinu's font of wisdom until her daughter can make her own way in life. Kiyoko sighs and sets down her tea. "I don't know. I just..." You reach across the table and give the kitsune mother a good petting between her big, fluffy ears. Kiyoko instinctively cranes her head forward to receive the affection, her jade-green eyes closing as she purrs gently. Now, then. It's understandable that she feels a little sad to see her daughter grow up, especially at such a young age and given the circumstances of the Astral Plane. But ultimately, the duty of a mother is to prepare her children for the day when they will no longer need her. Kinu may grow into someone greater than the two of you combined, but it's up to you and her — especially her, since you can't be around so often — to mold your daughter correctly and set her on the right path in life. Kiyoko looks away as you finish the petting, but doesn't say anything. There, there. |"Ehehe. Our daughter has really taken a shine to children. She seems to love her brothers and sisters more than I did when I was her age." Perhaps it's got something to do with the fact that unlike her mother, she doesn't have to deal with wailing fox kits and mountains of dirty diapers? "It's more than that, I think. She's just naturally good with her brothers and sisters and actually likes being put in charge of them; it's gotten to the point where I feel comfortable delegating important sibling-related responsibilities to her and know she'll carry them out with enthusiasm." A model big sister, then. Or maybe she just likes bossing around her siblings... while it's good that she's learning to wield authority at such a young age, even in a limited fashion, she needs to understand that this authority is to be wielded for the benefit of others, not massaging her own ego. Kiyoko looks thoughtful at that. "Come to think of it... hm. That explains a few things." Pardon? "Oh, it's nothing. But you're right — I should probably stress that bit of her education in responsibility a little more." ]"

rows.translation: 询问一下你的大女儿的情况。

rows.original: [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 4 8 16 24 32|[rand|"I'd be lying if I said I wasn't at least a little worried about the whole thing," Kiyoko admits. "I mean, for my tummy to swell up so quickly and my baby to grow into a child almost instantly... it's just not what I'm used to seeing. What does this place do to children? To me? Is it somewhere where I'd want to raise sons and daughters?" You pat Kiyoko on the shoulder and tell her that it's going to be all right. "I appreciate the sentiment, [pc.name], but the fact is that neither of us are sure of that." The kitsune flattens her fox ears against her head and rubs her temples. "Yes, I understand that there's little I can really do about the situation save do my best to raise Kinu well, but I'm not completely rational about this, you know?" Saying nothing, you continue to pat Kiyoko on the shoulder, slowly moving up to her head. It's all you can do to fight the melancholy creeping up on the usually peppy kitsune. "I mean, how much time have I lost without spending those years that I would've with our child as an infant? Sure, on the good side it means I don't have to deal with whole baskets of dirty diapers like I did for my brothers and sisters when they were young, but... well, babies have their moments. I really did like my siblings when they were babies; they were all so cute and fuzzy. "But listen to me go on like this, worrying about what I can't change. My situation's improved so much already, and all I can think about is how it might get worse. "I'd like to think I'm not one to scare easily, [pc.name]. But I do remember at least two times when I've been shaken to my core: first, when I realized I was trapped here in the Astral Plane, and secondly, when it hit home that I'm now responsible for more than just myself." |"I can't really decide whether Kinu takes more after me or you," Kiyoko says after some thought. "Little tyke's a kitsune all right, with the playfulness to match, but there's more to someone than their exterior, after all." Is kitsune blood that strong? Kiyoko shrugs. "I don't know. Never seen anyone breed with someone who wasn't a kitsune as well. And to be honest, even if I did, it's not as we did things the... um, conventional way, or at least in terms of what really happened." There's no need for undue worry, now. By all appearances, the daughter you and her made together is a perfectly normal and happy youngster. "I hope..." |"I suppose I'd better get to remembering all the things I used to do when Mother made me babysit my siblings. That knowledge is going to get put to use in good time." A gleam creeps into your eye. Oh? Kiyoko smiles, a warm, indeterminate smile that could turn naughty any moment. "Somehow, [pc.name], I get the distinct feeling that I'm not going to have the one and only kit to my name, thank you very much." Why, is that a divination she just made? A prediction of the future? And what are the odds on that, if she doesn't mind you asking? "Well, we diviners never say to be completely certain, but the chances of that are about as close to perfect as one can get." [kiyoko.pregStage 1|She rubs the rounded swell of her womb for emphasis. ] ] |[rand|So, how are the kids treating her? "You know how they say that two children aren't that much more work than one?" Not really, but it's an interesting saying. "Or how three aren't that much more work than two? Or how four aren't that much more work than three?" Yeah, you can see where this is going. "They have their good and bad days, and I have mine," Kiyoko continues with a sigh of resignation, then nods at you. "Like my own mother before me, I have to learn to take it all in stride. At least I've done this before, so I'm no stranger to juggling the care of several children." |"I've been drawing up a proper education for the children," Kiyoko tells you. "It's been hard to decide on an exact curriculum, but I hope to get things down soon enough." She's got to be a good teacher, isn't she? After all, she taught herself so many things while stuck on the Astral Plane. "Learning something yourself is one thing, imparting knowledge to another is something else altogether, although I won't say that there isn't overlap between the two. Thankfully, the children seem studious enough and willing to learn." They certainly take after their mother, then. "My main concern is practical real-life experience they'll need once you get us out of here," Kiyoko adds. "The forest beyond the hilltop might be endless, but in terms of variety it's actually very limited. I'd rather my sons and daughters not grow up stunted in that regard." |"To be completely honest, I'm quite thankful for the Astral Plane providing us with what we need," Kiyoko tells you after pausing to sip her tea. "Having so many of those needling little daily tasks done for you does make caring for a great number of children all the more possible." Yeah, you can see how leaving a dirty heap of clothes and finding fresh laundry in the cabinet would help. A nod. "Of course, I still assign chores; it took some working out, but I've got a good schedule going. Working the orchards, dusting and cleaning, cooking, making small repairs. I actually have to ask the plane itself to not fix those bits so the children can get to them, but I think it's a vitally important part of their education to realize that one day, not everything is going to fall into their lap when they want it." Living in a place which is pretty much as close as one can get to paradise... "Yes," Kiyoko says, finishing the thought for you. "It's a slow, painful death — if not of the body, then of the spirit. They won't suffer from crushing loneliness like I did, but it'll be an uphill battle to keep them from ending up utterly spoilt." Like how the Belharan Empire was just before its fall? Kiyoko wrinkles her nose daintily. "Something like that." ] |[rand|Her family's starting to get bigger these days, isn't it? Kiyoko wiggles her ears and smiles demurely at you. "Yes, it is. And I suppose I should thank you for that. I wasn't planning on this when I first made that proposal, and even for some time after I thought of the children as... by-products of your energy transferral. "Now, of course, I'm properly shamed for even entertaining such thoughts. Being a big sister is similar to being a mother in some aspects, but very different in others; I shouldn't have brought all of my expectations to the fold." From what you've seen of her, she's been the doing her utmost to be the best mother that she possibly can be. "I don't know about that, and even if it were true — well, is my best enough? But what I'm getting at, though, is that even though it has its ups and downs, this family that you've given me has been a source of constant joy in what ought to be this prison of mine. I can be grateful for as much." |"Not too long ago, I finished drawing up a system for putting some of the older children in charge of their younger brothers and sisters." Much like the one her own mother instituted, right? Kiyoko nods. "More or less. It worked rather well for me — after all, delegation is key everywhere, and a large family like this is no exemption. I only have so many hands and tails, after all!" And has it worked out well? "So far. At least this has been tried and tested, and I only need to step in when actual emergencies arise, instead of personally taking care of every single little chore and hiccup. How do you think I still get time to fold origami, do calligraphy and play the koto?" |"If you haven't noticed already, the cabin's begun to change." You think you have, but it's more and interior than an exterior thing, is it? Kiyoko shakes her head. "Remember, orbs of transference were created as weapons with which armies of kitsune were to be smuggled. The Astral Plane is perfectly capable of housing, feeding and otherwise providing for the needs of a literal army — and it changes itself to suit that fact." Right... "Whatever happens, we'll always be adequately provided for, so you don't have to worry about us. Focus on your efforts beyond this little realm." You will. ] |[rand|"You know how some women say they're turning into their mothers?" Yes, but they usually mean it in a derogatory sense, don't they? "Oh? And how do you know I don't mean it as such?" Aw, come on. You've been around her for long enough, known her in much more than one sense of the word... she didn't think that you wouldn't be able to read her, did she? That, and the fact that she's smiling in her oh-so-demure way. "I am?" She was. For being a servant of a trickster deity, she's not very tricksy. Nor very self-aware, either, which probably precludes the first. "No, I suppose not. But back to the point — to put it in a better light, at least I'm turning into the bits of my mother which I admired, and not the bits that I didn't, which is a small mercy. Perhaps it'd be better to say that I'm turning into an idealized version of my mother." Well, then. If that's what Kiyoko wants, you're not going to stop her. In fact, you hope that she surpasses her mother — something which you think she's well on the way to doing. "The compliment's appreciated." |You know... "Yes, [pc.name]?" Kiyoko sips at her tea. "A coin for your thoughts?" It's rather interesting as to how her figure hasn't deteriorated, but rather, improved with keeping. Having this many children would wreck most other womens' bodies. Kiyoko just shrugs and smiles ineffably, her ears twitching. "Most other women don't have their newborns grow into children at the breast, either. Or have their pregnancies progress this quickly. Or... well, you get the idea. The Astral Plane was never quite meant for long-term living on the scale of years, so strange things happen. I'm only grateful for this small mercy, you know?" Oh, definitely. Has she looked into the origins of this? She is a diviner, after all. "I think I did mention trying, but after losing all my leads I'm just content to take what's been given to me and not worry too much about what I can't change. I suppose if I'm going to have to look the part of a mother, I might as well be pleasing to the eye instead of the other way around, right?" No doubt about that! Kiyoko laughs. "Besides — and let's be honest here — can you visualize a fat kitsune? I don't think I can; Keros would never stand for it." |How goes the kits' education? Kiyoko practically beams at the question. "They're very talented, I swear; they seem to be able to pick up any skill or learning with much less effort than anyone else I'd know. Even with a century or two's worth of headstart on them, I'm sure it'd only take decades for them to catch up with me." That's marvelous! "I don't think this ability came from me, [pc.name], this affinity for learning. You seem to be able to pick up new knowledge and activities with relative ease compared to other people... almost as drastically as our children do. This is an ability the kitsune as a people would be very glad to have. "But I digress. I'm trying to do what I did for my younger siblings all that time ago — a well-rounded education, moreso now that I've the tools to do so. Mathematics, music, natural lore... although I will say that without a reference, history has been a bit of a bother. I try to frame it as a set of stories, rather than just dates and facts to be memorized — works better with the kits that way." You nod and gesture for her to go on. "A few of our children show some magical promise, so I'll see about that when they get older. When I eventually get out of here... when we do, that is, I want them to be useful to kitsune society. That's the ultimate goal of all this." As always, you're thankful for all her efforts in caring for your issue while you're away. "I'm just doing what a mother does, [pc.name]. Well, any respectable mother. There's no need to thank me at all — I'm just glad that all the things I learned to stave off boredom, to keep myself sane in this prison have actually turned out to have some use in the end." ] |[rand|"You know," Kiyoko says with a smile, "if I were out for good from this gilded cage of mine, I could very well be in the running for being a proper den matron." The name does suggest the qualifications, you suppose. Are you right? Kiyoko thinks a moment. "In a way. It's not strictly true that a den matron has to be the most prolific mother in the community — there's no rule stating as such — but once she gets the position she's pretty much propositioned by most of the males the den has to offer, and plenty others from other dens to boot. The mixing of blood is supposed to prevent excessive inbreeding, you see." Hrm. "Either way, if a den matron isn't one by the time she's named one, she'll be so in short order. As for me... well, I've enough children of my own that I could set up my own den all by myself." Better give her a few more, then. Can't have too many hands around to start striking the earth once she gets out of here. Kiyoko smiles sweetly at you and wiggles her large, fluffy ears, but says nothing. |"I'm glad all this has happened. Now, I'm still not very happy about being stuck in here for as long as I've been, and if I could I would have avoided it, but since it meant I got the opportunity to meet you and be a mother to so many children... it may just have been worth it." You're glad she thinks that way. All that's in the past now; there's a bright future ahead of her. Kiyoko nods. "To be able to see anything other than a perfect world... it's a relief. Perfection, especially when one has not earned it, is anything but. For the longest duration of my imprisonment here, I wanted for nothing, yet I had no reason to keep on existing as I was. I forced myself to pull through each day, each moment; I pretended to be excited that the highlight of my day was sitting down for hours on end and doing scroll painting... "But now, instead of living for nothing or even for myself, I've been given the opportunity to live for others. Instead of teaching myself to scroll paint for its own sake, I now teach the kits, and I learn as they do... to be given a meaning to exist, that's one of the greatest gifts both you and the children have bestowed upon me." You really didn't have such lofty goals in mind when you started making gifts of your chi to her. All you wanted was to - "Does it really matter why you did it? All that matters is that you did, and for that I'm grateful." Kiyoko closes her eyes and sips at her tea, and you see her lip tremble. "Please, continue doing what you're doing... and I'll work hard to support you from the rear." All right, you'll do just that. |"I think my mother would've been proud of me," Kiyoko says after some thought. "While I didn't quite become the famed diviner which she'd hoped for me to become by sending me off, I've nevertheless made something of myself." That can't be denied, yes. The Astral Plane sure has changed a lot ever since you first entered the place. "I think she'd have liked you too, [pc.name]. Then again, she liked anyone who was plenty virile, and I don't think you're lacking in proof of that." Kiyoko laughs and waves a hand dismissively. "At least you won't have to deal with any pesky in-laws in my case — chances are they're all dead by now." The world's changed since the Godswar by leaps and bounds. Even if she returned to her homeland once she's free, it's almost certain that it won't be as she remember it. "I don't know about that. Going back, I mean. It's far more likely that I'd ask the Trickster himself for permission to find someplace to settle and form a den in this locale. I think I've warmed up to the place some, and I'm sure he wouldn't mind having a presence around, no matter how small." ] |[rand|"I'd like to think I've gotten everything under control now," Kiyoko informs you, giving you a sagely nod as she picks a piece of candy off the plate. "At this point, most matters resolve themselves without my intervention, I've delegated most of the tasks to the eldest of our children, and I've raised them well enough to function without need for my constant oversight. I like to think I've succeeded as a mother in raising obedient, useful, and productive children, for what it's worth." She really is gearing up to be a den mother, isn't she? Kiyoko doesn't reply immediately, but stares out of the window for a second or two before finishing the last of her tea and licking her lips very, very slowly. "I suppose it's not too far off from actuality, is it? All that really remains is for Keros to give me his seal of approval; that's the only thing which is lacking. "But of course, it also means that I've more free time to do the things I truly enjoy, instead of dealing with endless squabbles and petty complaints. Things such as making more kits. Oh, there's no rush... but neither should one pause to rest on one's laurels, yes? There's always room for improvement." |How are the children treating her these days? By the looks of it, she's surpassed her mother several times over in terms of quantity. "Quantity, yes. Quality... well, I hesitate to make that judgement. My mother did produce me, after all — that's quite a hard achievement to top." Was that just a backhanded compliment she made there? Kiyoko just smiles. "But yes, to answer your question, [pc.name], the children are treating me just fine. By and large, they are respectful and obedient, with much potential for power... I don't want to venture guesses as to what came from which side of the family, but suffice to say that your seed and my womb work very, very well together." That's a polite way of putting it... but you are glad things have worked out well in the end. "Please, I do urge to continue. You and I... we're both doing very good work. It'd be a shame if either of us decided enough was enough." The kitsune dips her head ever so slightly and gives you a wink. |"Save for finally getting out of here on a permanent basis, I don't think there's anything else I could possibly ask for, [pc.name]. Ever since you arrived in my little world, the boons that have been granted to me are manifold — family, memories... and plenty of fun times. I know there're those who disdain the company of others, but when you've been to one extreme, it's hard to want to go back — I lost all my appetite for solitude after an eternity of it stuck in this gilded cage. "And speaking of cages... while I suppose I'm still imprisoned here, at least I don't mind it that much any more. Oh, I'd still like to get both myself and the orb fixed for the sake of the kits, but if it were up to me and me only... I don't think I care any more. Most people live bound in chains of their own making; even as I am, I think I'm considerably freer than most people are." It's a comfortable, idyllic life with the children, isn't it? Kiyoko nods. "Even afterwards... after my release... I still think I'd like to join you in your adventures, to project myself from the orb or even be with you in the flesh and offer you succor when you lay yourself down to rest. Even if physical distance separates us, there's no reason we can't meet in our dreams, there's no reason why you and I can't keep this arrangement going. I do find fighting alongside you rather... invigorating, plus I do get to test out the spells and abilities I devise. Plus, by this point, I'm not going to deny that I absolutely delight in receiving your chi and nurturing it within me, [pc.name]. Wouldn't have done it so many times if I didn't enjoy it, right? "So yes, don't worry about the kits and I; we're fine as we are. Focus your energies on the tasks which lie ahead of you... although if you have some left over for a faithful fox like me, I wouldn't be against taking some of that load off you."] |[rand|Kiyoko considers the question for a moment before setting down her tea and giving you a stupid, playful grin. "Even after all that we've been through, it still gladdens my heart every time you ask about the children. It's just — well — I just like hearing you pose the question." How many are there at this point, anyway? Sure, you've caught sight of some of the kits on the way in, but you'd never be able to count them all! Seventy-five? More? Who knows? "That's for me to know and for you to count." Well, if they could all assemble and stay in one place without zipping around all the time... "Trust me, these children don't have any setting besides off and full speed. I think they get that from their mother." |"The children and I are handling things very well. You know, when all of this started, I made a decision to try and recreate the system that my own mother used to have for managing me and my siblings, and it's worked out well. The children are cared for, fed, and given adequate love and attention. It's probably a little different from what you're used to, but the way I see things, there's no need to reinvent the wheel. If anything, I've made it even better." Oh? Kiyoko nods. "When a prospective den mother strikes out on her own, she doesn't do it alone; usually, several of her brothers and sisters come along for the ride. They help her take care of things and make the place suitable for little fox kits to grow up in. Of course, they add to their number, too, but most kitsune don't have the sheer —" you see Kiyoko run her tongue across her lips- "reproductive capacity a den mother does. I won't deny that the Astral Plane has been an immense help in this regard — it's nice to have a house that grows along with your family, not to mention the self-doing laundry. It gives me more time to tend to the children." And it also gives her more time to put towards adding to their number. "Ehehe..." Kiyoko tilts her head slightly and folds her ears forward. "I won't say no to playing with you, if that's what you want." |"The children and I couldn't be any better, thank you for asking. I haven't felt better in a long, long time, if ever, and the kits are all happy smiles all day. When I was new at this, I worried a bit as to whether I'd be able to give the kits all the attention they needed like my mother used to be able to do, but things just seem to have worked themselves out. I don't even need to think about things now, everything just falls into place of its own accord." Inasmuch the same way as she keeps on finding herself pregnant, right? "Exactly. You know what I'm talking about. Not that it doesn't require any effort on my part, but it's so enjoyable that it may as well not." Ah, to be able to do something you love for a living. Familiarity is supposed to breed contempt, but clearly that doesn't apply to your kitsune slut-wife and her enormous brood of children. "Sometimes they're quiet and calm, and sometimes they're running all over the place. At least their older brothers and sisters are well on the way to learning responsibility. They'll need it when we finally get out of here." Yes... "Like I said, I'm happy, and so are the children. Don't worry about us, and do what you need to do."] ]
rows.translation: [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 4 8 16 24 32|[rand|“如果我说自己对这件事一点也不担心，那肯定是在撒谎。”清子承认了。“我的意思是，我的肚子会这么快就胀起来，而我的宝宝几乎瞬间就从一个婴儿长成了一个孩子……这种景象真的超出了我的想象。这个地方对孩子来说到底有什么影响？对我来说又是什么影响？这里真的是我想养育儿子女儿的地方吗？” 你轻拍着清子的肩膀，告诉她一切都会好起来的。 “我很感激这种心意，[pc.name]，但事实上，我们两人都不确定这一点。”那只狐妖将她的耳朵贴在头上，然后揉了揉太阳穴。“是的，我知道对于这种状况，我其实能做的并不多，只能尽自己最大的努力把小娟抚养好。但你知道，我对此并不是完全理智的。” 你什么也没说，只是继续轻拍着清子的肩膀，手慢慢向上移，最终抚到了她的头。对于这个平时总是充满活力的狐妖来说，你能做的，就是尽自己最大的努力来抵抗那逐渐蔓延而来的忧郁情绪。 “我的意思是，如果我没有把那些本该陪伴在孩子婴儿时期的时间花在别的地方，那我究竟错过了多少时光呢？当然，从好的方面来看，这也意味着我不用像照顾弟弟妹妹们小时候那样，每天都要处理一大堆脏尿布了，但是……嗯，不过婴儿也有他们惹人喜爱的时候。我真的很喜欢我的弟弟妹妹们小时候的样子，他们一个个都那么可爱、那么惹人喜欢。 但是，你听听我这样不停地担心那些我无法改变的事情。我的情况其实已经改善了很多，可我满脑子想的却还是它可能会变得更糟。 我愿意认为自己不是那种容易受到惊吓的人，[pc.name]，但我确实记得有两次经历让我深受震撼：第一次是当我意识到自己被困在了这个星界之中；第二次则是当我真正意识到，现在我不仅要为自己负责，还要为更多的人负责。” |“我实在无法确定，小娟更像我还是更像你。”经过一番思考后，清子说道。“这个小孩子确实是一只狐妖，也确实有着与之相匹配的顽皮性格，但毕竟，一个人的本质并不仅仅取决于他们的外表。” 狐妖之血真的有那么强大吗？ 清子耸了耸肩。“我不知道。我从没见过有人和不是狐妖的人交配。说实话，就算有人这么做过，他们的方式也不像我们……嗯，不是传统意义上的方式，至少就实际发生的事情而言是这样。” 所以，别担心那些小狐狸和我，我们现在的状态挺好的。把你的精力集中在眼前的任务上吧……不过，如果你还有多余的精力可以分给我这个忠实的狐妖，我当然不介意帮你分担一些负担。”] |[rand|清子思考了片刻，然后放下茶杯，朝你露出了一个天真又顽皮的笑容。“尽管我们经历了那么多，但每次你提到孩子们，我的心里还是会感到无比欣慰。只是……嗯，我就喜欢听到你问这个问题。” 那到现在到底有多少个呢？当然，你进来的时候已经看到了一些小狐狸，但你绝对不可能把它们全数清！七十五个？还是更多？谁知道呢？ “这个嘛，我知道就好，你自己去数吧。” 嗯，如果他们都能聚在一起，待在一个地方，而不用到处跑来跑去的话…… “相信我，这些孩子身上只有两个档位：要么关着，要么全速。我想这种习惯是他们从他们妈妈那里学来的。” |“我和孩子们把一切都处理得很好。你知道，当这一切开始的时候，我决定尝试重现我母亲曾经用来照顾我和我的兄弟姐妹的那种方式，结果效果非常好。孩子们得到了照顾、饮食也得到了保障，同时还得到了足够的关爱和关注。虽然这种方式可能与你习惯的有所不同，但在我看来，没有必要重新发明轮子——事实上，我甚至让这种方式变得更好了。” 哦？ 清子点了点头。“当一位有意成为巢穴主母的狐妖自立门户时，她并不是孤身一人；通常，她的几个兄弟姐妹会跟着她一起走。他们会帮她操持事务，把那个地方变得适合小狐狸幼崽成长。当然，他们的数量也会随之增加，但大多数狐妖并没有巢穴主母那样惊人的——”你看到清子用舌头舔了舔嘴唇——“生育能力。我必须承认，星界在这方面确实提供了巨大的帮助——拥有一个能够随着家庭规模扩大而自动扩展的‘家’，实在是非常方便，更不用说那些自动完成的洗衣任务了。这些功能让我有更多的时间来照顾孩子们。” 这也让她有更多时间来增加他们的人数。 “嘿嘿……”清子微微歪着头，把耳朵向前折叠。“如果那是你想要的，我当然不会拒绝和你一起玩。” |“我和孩子们现在过得非常开心，真的非常感谢你的关心。我已经很久很久没有这种感觉了，孩子们整天都洋溢着幸福的笑容。刚开始做这份工作的时候，我还有点担心自己是否能够像我母亲那样给予孩子们他们所需要的关爱，但后来一切似乎都变得顺其自然了。现在我甚至都不用去思考这些事情，一切都会自然而然地得到解决。” 就像她总是意外怀孕一样，对吧？ “正是这样。你明白我的意思吧。虽然这确实需要我付出一些努力，但过程实在太有趣了，以至于这些努力简直都不算什么。” 啊，能够将自己热爱的事情作为职业来从事，真是太棒了。一般来说，熟悉某事物反而会让人对其产生厌倦感，但显然，这对你那个狐妖老婆和她那一大群孩子来说并不适用。 “有时候他们会很安静、很平静，而有时候则会到处乱跑。不过至少他们的哥哥姐姐们正在逐渐学会承担责任——等我们终于离开这里的时候，他们肯定会需要这些能力的。” 是的…… “就像我说的，我很开心，孩子们也很开心。你不必担心我们，去做你该做的事情吧。”] ]
rows.raw: " [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 4 8 16 24 32|[rand|"I'd be lying if I said I wasn't at least a little worried about the whole thing," Kiyoko admits. "I mean, for my tummy to swell up so quickly and my baby to grow into a child almost instantly... it's just not what I'm used to seeing. What does this place do to children? To me? Is it somewhere where I'd want to raise sons and daughters?" You pat Kiyoko on the shoulder and tell her that it's going to be all right. "I appreciate the sentiment, [pc.name], but the fact is that neither of us are sure of that." The kitsune flattens her fox ears against her head and rubs her temples. "Yes, I understand that there's little I can really do about the situation save do my best to raise Kinu well, but I'm not completely rational about this, you know?" Saying nothing, you continue to pat Kiyoko on the shoulder, slowly moving up to her head. It's all you can do to fight the melancholy creeping up on the usually peppy kitsune. "I mean, how much time have I lost without spending those years that I would've with our child as an infant? Sure, on the good side it means I don't have to deal with whole baskets of dirty diapers like I did for my brothers and sisters when they were young, but... well, babies have their moments. I really did like my siblings when they were babies; they were all so cute and fuzzy. "But listen to me go on like this, worrying about what I can't change. My situation's improved so much already, and all I can think about is how it might get worse. "I'd like to think I'm not one to scare easily, [pc.name]. But I do remember at least two times when I've been shaken to my core: first, when I realized I was trapped here in the Astral Plane, and secondly, when it hit home that I'm now responsible for more than just myself." |"I can't really decide whether Kinu takes more after me or you," Kiyoko says after some thought. "Little tyke's a kitsune all right, with the playfulness to match, but there's more to someone than their exterior, after all." Is kitsune blood that strong? Kiyoko shrugs. "I don't know. Never seen anyone breed with someone who wasn't a kitsune as well. And to be honest, even if I did, it's not as we did things the... um, conventional way, or at least in terms of what really happened." There's no need for undue worry, now. By all appearances, the daughter you and her made together is a perfectly normal and happy youngster. "I hope..." |"I suppose I'd better get to remembering all the things I used to do when Mother made me babysit my siblings. That knowledge is going to get put to use in good time." A gleam creeps into your eye. Oh? Kiyoko smiles, a warm, indeterminate smile that could turn naughty any moment. "Somehow, [pc.name], I get the distinct feeling that I'm not going to have the one and only kit to my name, thank you very much." Why, is that a divination she just made? A prediction of the future? And what are the odds on that, if she doesn't mind you asking? "Well, we diviners never say to be completely certain, but the chances of that are about as close to perfect as one can get." [kiyoko.pregStage 1|She rubs the rounded swell of her womb for emphasis. ] ] |[rand|So, how are the kids treating her? "You know how they say that two children aren't that much more work than one?" Not really, but it's an interesting saying. "Or how three aren't that much more work than two? Or how four aren't that much more work than three?" Yeah, you can see where this is going. "They have their good and bad days, and I have mine," Kiyoko continues with a sigh of resignation, then nods at you. "Like my own mother before me, I have to learn to take it all in stride. At least I've done this before, so I'm no stranger to juggling the care of several children." |"I've been drawing up a proper education for the children," Kiyoko tells you. "It's been hard to decide on an exact curriculum, but I hope to get things down soon enough." She's got to be a good teacher, isn't she? After all, she taught herself so many things while stuck on the Astral Plane. "Learning something yourself is one thing, imparting knowledge to another is something else altogether, although I won't say that there isn't overlap between the two. Thankfully, the children seem studious enough and willing to learn." They certainly take after their mother, then. "My main concern is practical real-life experience they'll need once you get us out of here," Kiyoko adds. "The forest beyond the hilltop might be endless, but in terms of variety it's actually very limited. I'd rather my sons and daughters not grow up stunted in that regard." |"To be completely honest, I'm quite thankful for the Astral Plane providing us with what we need," Kiyoko tells you after pausing to sip her tea. "Having so many of those needling little daily tasks done for you does make caring for a great number of children all the more possible." Yeah, you can see how leaving a dirty heap of clothes and finding fresh laundry in the cabinet would help. A nod. "Of course, I still assign chores; it took some working out, but I've got a good schedule going. Working the orchards, dusting and cleaning, cooking, making small repairs. I actually have to ask the plane itself to not fix those bits so the children can get to them, but I think it's a vitally important part of their education to realize that one day, not everything is going to fall into their lap when they want it." Living in a place which is pretty much as close as one can get to paradise... "Yes," Kiyoko says, finishing the thought for you. "It's a slow, painful death — if not of the body, then of the spirit. They won't suffer from crushing loneliness like I did, but it'll be an uphill battle to keep them from ending up utterly spoilt." Like how the Belharan Empire was just before its fall? Kiyoko wrinkles her nose daintily. "Something like that." ] |[rand|Her family's starting to get bigger these days, isn't it? Kiyoko wiggles her ears and smiles demurely at you. "Yes, it is. And I suppose I should thank you for that. I wasn't planning on this when I first made that proposal, and even for some time after I thought of the children as... by-products of your energy transferral. "Now, of course, I'm properly shamed for even entertaining such thoughts. Being a big sister is similar to being a mother in some aspects, but very different in others; I shouldn't have brought all of my expectations to the fold." From what you've seen of her, she's been the doing her utmost to be the best mother that she possibly can be. "I don't know about that, and even if it were true — well, is my best enough? But what I'm getting at, though, is that even though it has its ups and downs, this family that you've given me has been a source of constant joy in what ought to be this prison of mine. I can be grateful for as much." |"Not too long ago, I finished drawing up a system for putting some of the older children in charge of their younger brothers and sisters." Much like the one her own mother instituted, right? Kiyoko nods. "More or less. It worked rather well for me — after all, delegation is key everywhere, and a large family like this is no exemption. I only have so many hands and tails, after all!" And has it worked out well? "So far. At least this has been tried and tested, and I only need to step in when actual emergencies arise, instead of personally taking care of every single little chore and hiccup. How do you think I still get time to fold origami, do calligraphy and play the koto?" |"If you haven't noticed already, the cabin's begun to change." You think you have, but it's more and interior than an exterior thing, is it? Kiyoko shakes her head. "Remember, orbs of transference were created as weapons with which armies of kitsune were to be smuggled. The Astral Plane is perfectly capable of housing, feeding and otherwise providing for the needs of a literal army — and it changes itself to suit that fact." Right... "Whatever happens, we'll always be adequately provided for, so you don't have to worry about us. Focus on your efforts beyond this little realm." You will. ] |[rand|"You know how some women say they're turning into their mothers?" Yes, but they usually mean it in a derogatory sense, don't they? "Oh? And how do you know I don't mean it as such?" Aw, come on. You've been around her for long enough, known her in much more than one sense of the word... she didn't think that you wouldn't be able to read her, did she? That, and the fact that she's smiling in her oh-so-demure way. "I am?" She was. For being a servant of a trickster deity, she's not very tricksy. Nor very self-aware, either, which probably precludes the first. "No, I suppose not. But back to the point — to put it in a better light, at least I'm turning into the bits of my mother which I admired, and not the bits that I didn't, which is a small mercy. Perhaps it'd be better to say that I'm turning into an idealized version of my mother." Well, then. If that's what Kiyoko wants, you're not going to stop her. In fact, you hope that she surpasses her mother — something which you think she's well on the way to doing. "The compliment's appreciated." |You know... "Yes, [pc.name]?" Kiyoko sips at her tea. "A coin for your thoughts?" It's rather interesting as to how her figure hasn't deteriorated, but rather, improved with keeping. Having this many children would wreck most other womens' bodies. Kiyoko just shrugs and smiles ineffably, her ears twitching. "Most other women don't have their newborns grow into children at the breast, either. Or have their pregnancies progress this quickly. Or... well, you get the idea. The Astral Plane was never quite meant for long-term living on the scale of years, so strange things happen. I'm only grateful for this small mercy, you know?" Oh, definitely. Has she looked into the origins of this? She is a diviner, after all. "I think I did mention trying, but after losing all my leads I'm just content to take what's been given to me and not worry too much about what I can't change. I suppose if I'm going to have to look the part of a mother, I might as well be pleasing to the eye instead of the other way around, right?" No doubt about that! Kiyoko laughs. "Besides — and let's be honest here — can you visualize a fat kitsune? I don't think I can; Keros would never stand for it." |How goes the kits' education? Kiyoko practically beams at the question. "They're very talented, I swear; they seem to be able to pick up any skill or learning with much less effort than anyone else I'd know. Even with a century or two's worth of headstart on them, I'm sure it'd only take decades for them to catch up with me." That's marvelous! "I don't think this ability came from me, [pc.name], this affinity for learning. You seem to be able to pick up new knowledge and activities with relative ease compared to other people... almost as drastically as our children do. This is an ability the kitsune as a people would be very glad to have. "But I digress. I'm trying to do what I did for my younger siblings all that time ago — a well-rounded education, moreso now that I've the tools to do so. Mathematics, music, natural lore... although I will say that without a reference, history has been a bit of a bother. I try to frame it as a set of stories, rather than just dates and facts to be memorized — works better with the kits that way." You nod and gesture for her to go on. "A few of our children show some magical promise, so I'll see about that when they get older. When I eventually get out of here... when we do, that is, I want them to be useful to kitsune society. That's the ultimate goal of all this." As always, you're thankful for all her efforts in caring for your issue while you're away. "I'm just doing what a mother does, [pc.name]. Well, any respectable mother. There's no need to thank me at all — I'm just glad that all the things I learned to stave off boredom, to keep myself sane in this prison have actually turned out to have some use in the end." ] |[rand|"You know," Kiyoko says with a smile, "if I were out for good from this gilded cage of mine, I could very well be in the running for being a proper den matron." The name does suggest the qualifications, you suppose. Are you right? Kiyoko thinks a moment. "In a way. It's not strictly true that a den matron has to be the most prolific mother in the community — there's no rule stating as such — but once she gets the position she's pretty much propositioned by most of the males the den has to offer, and plenty others from other dens to boot. The mixing of blood is supposed to prevent excessive inbreeding, you see." Hrm. "Either way, if a den matron isn't one by the time she's named one, she'll be so in short order. As for me... well, I've enough children of my own that I could set up my own den all by myself." Better give her a few more, then. Can't have too many hands around to start striking the earth once she gets out of here. Kiyoko smiles sweetly at you and wiggles her large, fluffy ears, but says nothing. |"I'm glad all this has happened. Now, I'm still not very happy about being stuck in here for as long as I've been, and if I could I would have avoided it, but since it meant I got the opportunity to meet you and be a mother to so many children... it may just have been worth it." You're glad she thinks that way. All that's in the past now; there's a bright future ahead of her. Kiyoko nods. "To be able to see anything other than a perfect world... it's a relief. Perfection, especially when one has not earned it, is anything but. For the longest duration of my imprisonment here, I wanted for nothing, yet I had no reason to keep on existing as I was. I forced myself to pull through each day, each moment; I pretended to be excited that the highlight of my day was sitting down for hours on end and doing scroll painting... "But now, instead of living for nothing or even for myself, I've been given the opportunity to live for others. Instead of teaching myself to scroll paint for its own sake, I now teach the kits, and I learn as they do... to be given a meaning to exist, that's one of the greatest gifts both you and the children have bestowed upon me." You really didn't have such lofty goals in mind when you started making gifts of your chi to her. All you wanted was to - "Does it really matter why you did it? All that matters is that you did, and for that I'm grateful." Kiyoko closes her eyes and sips at her tea, and you see her lip tremble. "Please, continue doing what you're doing... and I'll work hard to support you from the rear." All right, you'll do just that. |"I think my mother would've been proud of me," Kiyoko says after some thought. "While I didn't quite become the famed diviner which she'd hoped for me to become by sending me off, I've nevertheless made something of myself." That can't be denied, yes. The Astral Plane sure has changed a lot ever since you first entered the place. "I think she'd have liked you too, [pc.name]. Then again, she liked anyone who was plenty virile, and I don't think you're lacking in proof of that." Kiyoko laughs and waves a hand dismissively. "At least you won't have to deal with any pesky in-laws in my case — chances are they're all dead by now." The world's changed since the Godswar by leaps and bounds. Even if she returned to her homeland once she's free, it's almost certain that it won't be as she remember it. "I don't know about that. Going back, I mean. It's far more likely that I'd ask the Trickster himself for permission to find someplace to settle and form a den in this locale. I think I've warmed up to the place some, and I'm sure he wouldn't mind having a presence around, no matter how small." ] |[rand|"I'd like to think I've gotten everything under control now," Kiyoko informs you, giving you a sagely nod as she picks a piece of candy off the plate. "At this point, most matters resolve themselves without my intervention, I've delegated most of the tasks to the eldest of our children, and I've raised them well enough to function without need for my constant oversight. I like to think I've succeeded as a mother in raising obedient, useful, and productive children, for what it's worth." She really is gearing up to be a den mother, isn't she? Kiyoko doesn't reply immediately, but stares out of the window for a second or two before finishing the last of her tea and licking her lips very, very slowly. "I suppose it's not too far off from actuality, is it? All that really remains is for Keros to give me his seal of approval; that's the only thing which is lacking. "But of course, it also means that I've more free time to do the things I truly enjoy, instead of dealing with endless squabbles and petty complaints. Things such as making more kits. Oh, there's no rush... but neither should one pause to rest on one's laurels, yes? There's always room for improvement." |How are the children treating her these days? By the looks of it, she's surpassed her mother several times over in terms of quantity. "Quantity, yes. Quality... well, I hesitate to make that judgement. My mother did produce me, after all — that's quite a hard achievement to top." Was that just a backhanded compliment she made there? Kiyoko just smiles. "But yes, to answer your question, [pc.name], the children are treating me just fine. By and large, they are respectful and obedient, with much potential for power... I don't want to venture guesses as to what came from which side of the family, but suffice to say that your seed and my womb work very, very well together." That's a polite way of putting it... but you are glad things have worked out well in the end. "Please, I do urge to continue. You and I... we're both doing very good work. It'd be a shame if either of us decided enough was enough." The kitsune dips her head ever so slightly and gives you a wink. |"Save for finally getting out of here on a permanent basis, I don't think there's anything else I could possibly ask for, [pc.name]. Ever since you arrived in my little world, the boons that have been granted to me are manifold — family, memories... and plenty of fun times. I know there're those who disdain the company of others, but when you've been to one extreme, it's hard to want to go back — I lost all my appetite for solitude after an eternity of it stuck in this gilded cage. "And speaking of cages... while I suppose I'm still imprisoned here, at least I don't mind it that much any more. Oh, I'd still like to get both myself and the orb fixed for the sake of the kits, but if it were up to me and me only... I don't think I care any more. Most people live bound in chains of their own making; even as I am, I think I'm considerably freer than most people are." It's a comfortable, idyllic life with the children, isn't it? Kiyoko nods. "Even afterwards... after my release... I still think I'd like to join you in your adventures, to project myself from the orb or even be with you in the flesh and offer you succor when you lay yourself down to rest. Even if physical distance separates us, there's no reason we can't meet in our dreams, there's no reason why you and I can't keep this arrangement going. I do find fighting alongside you rather... invigorating, plus I do get to test out the spells and abilities I devise. Plus, by this point, I'm not going to deny that I absolutely delight in receiving your chi and nurturing it within me, [pc.name]. Wouldn't have done it so many times if I didn't enjoy it, right? "So yes, don't worry about the kits and I; we're fine as we are. Focus your energies on the tasks which lie ahead of you... although if you have some left over for a faithful fox like me, I wouldn't be against taking some of that load off you."] |[rand|Kiyoko considers the question for a moment before setting down her tea and giving you a stupid, playful grin. "Even after all that we've been through, it still gladdens my heart every time you ask about the children. It's just — well — I just like hearing you pose the question." How many are there at this point, anyway? Sure, you've caught sight of some of the kits on the way in, but you'd never be able to count them all! Seventy-five? More? Who knows? "That's for me to know and for you to count." Well, if they could all assemble and stay in one place without zipping around all the time... "Trust me, these children don't have any setting besides off and full speed. I think they get that from their mother." |"The children and I are handling things very well. You know, when all of this started, I made a decision to try and recreate the system that my own mother used to have for managing me and my siblings, and it's worked out well. The children are cared for, fed, and given adequate love and attention. It's probably a little different from what you're used to, but the way I see things, there's no need to reinvent the wheel. If anything, I've made it even better." Oh? Kiyoko nods. "When a prospective den mother strikes out on her own, she doesn't do it alone; usually, several of her brothers and sisters come along for the ride. They help her take care of things and make the place suitable for little fox kits to grow up in. Of course, they add to their number, too, but most kitsune don't have the sheer —" you see Kiyoko run her tongue across her lips- "reproductive capacity a den mother does. I won't deny that the Astral Plane has been an immense help in this regard — it's nice to have a house that grows along with your family, not to mention the self-doing laundry. It gives me more time to tend to the children." And it also gives her more time to put towards adding to their number. "Ehehe..." Kiyoko tilts her head slightly and folds her ears forward. "I won't say no to playing with you, if that's what you want." |"The children and I couldn't be any better, thank you for asking. I haven't felt better in a long, long time, if ever, and the kits are all happy smiles all day. When I was new at this, I worried a bit as to whether I'd be able to give the kits all the attention they needed like my mother used to be able to do, but things just seem to have worked themselves out. I don't even need to think about things now, everything just falls into place of its own accord." Inasmuch the same way as she keeps on finding herself pregnant, right? "Exactly. You know what I'm talking about. Not that it doesn't require any effort on my part, but it's so enjoyable that it may as well not." Ah, to be able to do something you love for a living. Familiarity is supposed to breed contempt, but clearly that doesn't apply to your kitsune slut-wife and her enormous brood of children. "Sometimes they're quiet and calm, and sometimes they're running all over the place. At least their older brothers and sisters are well on the way to learning responsibility. They'll need it when we finally get out of here." Yes... "Like I said, I'm happy, and so are the children. Don't worry about us, and do what you need to do."] ]"

rows.original: Ask about the kits in general.
rows.translation: 笼统地问问那些小狐狸们的情况。

rows.original: So... "Yes, [pc.name]?" The second time you met Kiyoko — that time when you caught her having a soak in the spring — she mentioned something about freeing her from her prison. When you questioned her about it, she mentioned needing to check her notes, and that's when you woke up... "Right. It was so long ago that I did that work, and I had to go look it up again; thanks for reminding me about the matter. While stuck here, I did manage to come up with the beginnings of an idea which might let me temporarily manifest outside the orb for short durations, but it required someone else's aid. And since there was no one else in here with me and I'd long given up hope of anyone else coming along..." her voice trails off, and she looks straight at you. You nod and motion for Kiyoko to go on. "Remember what I was telling you, that my body, my physicality was ripped from me? Where I come from, magical theory holds that there are two forms of energy everyone possesses in varying amounts: chi, the energy of the body, and ki, the energy of the spirit. When I attempted to escape into the Astral Plane with the dark magic on my heels, the former was ripped from me, although the latter escaped unharmed. That's why I'm essentially what might amount to be a spirit right now, and it's why I can't leave the orb, even though you can pass freely back and forth. It's all conjecture, of course, but it's the best explanation I have." [pc.cl whitemage blackmage|Now, now. You'd like to consider yourself fairly well-read, and when it comes to the subject of magics you don't remember ever coming across any mention of %"bodily energy" or the like. "I'm not surprised. Like I said, it's not a concept that's found parlance amongst your scholars, or at least, it wasn't when I was still out and about. I think they have something similar in Jassira, but not so far north..." ] So that means you can't smash the orb and be done with it. Kiyoko sighs and crosses her arms under her breasts. "Oh, if it were only that simple. If I thought smashing the orb would have worked; I'd have asked you to do just that a long time ago. No, it's a gate, not a vessel, and even if it were, who knows what might happen to me? "Short of Keros himself fixing both the orb and me, the only solution I saw was for someone else to share their chi with me. It's not a light thing to ask of someone, and I didn't want to scare you off with that kind of talk." You nod warily. All this talk of essence and energy sharing... it does make her sound like some kind of succubus or vampire. Another sigh, deeper than the first. "Perhaps; it is rather close. There's one crucial difference, though: the word share, instead of steal. I'm no thief, I won't take anything you don't give of your own free will. Like I said, it's not a light thing to ask someone to give away their chi — while it'll regenerate on its own over time with proper care, lose too much of it at once and you'll weaken, even die. I'd be disappointed, but understand perfectly if you refused. "That's why I had to check my notes. Considering how weighty this subject is, I had to be sure of what I was speaking of before I discussed this with you. I... don't know if I can offer you anything in return, but if this does work — and it should, according to what I've been able to figure — then I'd be indebted to you. A kitsune always repays owed favors." It should work, she says. Kiyoko looks pensive and bites her lip. "That's right. As is obvious, I've never actually had the chance to try it, so... well, unforeseen circumstances are always possible, even for a diviner." So, let's say you wanted to lend her a hand. How would you go about transferring some of your, uh, chi, was it? Bodily essence? At first, Kiyoko doesn't respond, color slowly creeping into the kitsune's cheeks. You wonder if you've made some kind of unintentional gaffe at first, but she raises her head and sniffs at the air with her dainty little nose. "You'd need to fuck me," comes the blunt reply. [pc.hasCock|"Or if you'd rather, I can fuck you and milk you for what you're worth." [pc.dcb|Heh. You'd like to see her try.|Uh...|Ooh, sounds sexy!] "Come to think of it, that was one of my mother's favorite sayings," Kiyoko continues with a weak half-grin on her face. "Really. 'I'll suck out all your semen!' It sounds better in its original language, I assure you. The translation doesn't do it justice." Look, this is getting quite awkward. Kiyoko waves a hand dismissively. "Oh, please. It was going to be awkward no matter what." [pc.mf||Question, though. Um. how did she know? About what you have, if she gets your drift. "I sniffed for it. We kitsune can smell these things if we put our minds to it. Which, frankly, doesn't hurt one bit — with my kind being as pretty as we are, there're a fair number of traps and hopelessly ladylike fox-boys hanging around." Kiyoko gets a faraway look in her eyes, and smacks her lips. "Ah, those were good times. But my point stands. Don't worry, I won't be able to tell anyone even if I wanted to."] |"Although you don't quite have the equipment for what I had in mind. At least, I can't smell it on you. A lot of our fox boys are rather... ladylike by conventional standards, if you know what I mean. Having a good nose helps." And while you might regret asking the question, what did she have in mind, anyway? Kiyoko looks straight at you, this gentle and apparently unassuming little kitsune, and smiles. "Well, if it were up to me, as a starter I'd bind you up all nice and tight in my tails, then wring out and suck up every last drop of your semen." Uncomfortable silence. Did she really have to say that? "It's like telling a bad fortune. Honesty is the beast — I mean, best — policy here, because if you lie, chances are you'll be making more trouble for yourself down the road." ] And there's no other way to go about this, is there? "There are other ways to go about transferring one's chi to a recipient. However, they'd require that I already have some kind of physical form, which I don't have right now. The act of copulation — no, breeding is perhaps one of the most primal and forceful ways in which one gives of one's own life-force to another to be nurtured. "Like I mentioned back then, I'm not going to fault you if you find this distasteful. It's not likely that you share kitsune mores on these matters, after all. "If my spellcrafting isn't wrong, I should be able to materialize outside the orb for limited periods of time," Kiyoko replies. "Not on a permanent basis, like I said, but the more chi you give me, the longer I'll be able to do it. The rest... well, I'll say it again: theory is one thing, and practice is another. rows.translation: 那么…… “是的，[pc.name]？” 你第二次遇见清子的时候——也就是你发现她正在泉水中沐浴的那一刻——她提到了要让自己摆脱囚禁。当你追问她的意思时，她说需要查看自己的笔记，而就在那时，你失去了意识…… “没错，那已经是很久以前的事了，我当时做了那些工作，现在得重新去查阅一下资料；多亏你提醒了我这件事。虽然被困在这里，但我还是想出了一个初步的方案——或许可以让我暂时离开这个光球，出去短时间活动一下，不过这需要别人的帮助。而这里除了我之外没有其他人，而且我也早就放弃了还会有人来救我的希望……”她的声音渐渐低了下去，然后她直视着你的眼睛。 你点了点头，示意清子继续说下去。 “还记得我告诉过你吗？我的身体，我的肉体，其实是被强行从我身上夺走的。在我出生的地方，有一种魔法理论认为，每个人体内都存在着两种形式的能量，只不过每个人拥有的数量各不相同：气，即身体的能量；以及ki，即精神的能量。当我试图带着那些暗影魔法逃往星界时，前者被从我身上夺走了，而后者却毫发无损地逃走了。因此，现在我本质上已经变成了一种类似于‘精神’的存在，也正是这个原因，我无法离开那个光球，尽管你可以自由地进出它。当然，这一切都只是猜测，但这是我目前能想到的最佳解释。” [pc.cl whitemage blackmage|现在，现在。你自认为是个见多识广的人，但说到魔法这个话题，你却想不起来自己曾经读到过任何关于%"身体能量"之类的说法。 “我并不感到惊讶。正如我所说，这个概念在你们的学者中并不常见，至少在我还在外面的时候，还没有听说过。我想在贾西拉地区可能有类似的东西，但在这个更北边的地方……应该还没有吧。” ] 这意味着你不能仅仅砸碎那个球就完成任务了。 清子叹了口气，双臂交叉在胸前。“哦，要是真的那么简单该多好。如果我认为砸碎那个球体就能解决问题，我早就让你这么做了。不，那其实是一个通道，而不是一个容器；而且就算它是容器，谁又能知道这样做会对我带来什么后果呢？ 除非凯罗斯亲自修复那个球体以及我自身的问题，否则我所能想到的唯一办法，就是让其他人把他的气分享给我。这样的请求对任何人来说都不是一件容易的事，我本来也不想用那种话把你吓跑的。” 你小心翼翼地点了点头。所有这些关于精华与能量共享的谈论……确实让她听起来像某种魅魔或吸血鬼。 又一声叹息，比第一次更加深沉。“也许吧；确实挺接近的。不过有一点关键的区别：那就是那个词分享而不是偷窃。我不是小偷，我不会拿走任何你没有自愿给予的东西。就像我说的，要求别人把自己的气送出去，可不是一件小事——虽然只要悉心调养，它自己会随着时间慢慢恢复，但一次失去太多，你就会变得虚弱，甚至可能死掉。如果你拒绝，我会失望，但完全能够理解。 这就是为什么我需要查看我的笔记。考虑到这个话题的重要性，我在和你讨论之前必须确保自己了解得非常清楚。我……不知道能否以什么方式回报你，但如果这种方法真的有效的话——根据我目前的了解，应该是有效的——那么我就会欠你一个人情。毕竟，狐妖总是会报答别人对自己的帮助的。” 她说，这应该会有效吧。 清子显得若有所思，咬着嘴唇。“没错。显而易见，我其实从来没有机会尝试过，所以……嗯，总有可能出现一些意想不到的情况，就连占卜师也不例外。” 那么，假设你想帮她一把。你该怎么把自己的一部分……呃，气，是这么叫的吧？身体精华？ 起初，清子没有回应，她的脸颊上慢慢浮现出红晕。你一开始还在想自己是否无意中说错了什么，但她最终抬起头，用她那小巧的鼻子嗅了嗅空气。 “你得先跟我上床才行。”随之而来的是直截了当的回答。 [pc.hasCock|“或者，如果你更愿意的话，我可以上你，把你榨得一滴不剩。” [pc.dcb|呵呵，你倒想看看她是怎么做的吧。|呃……|哦，听起来真诱人！] “仔细想来，那确实是我母亲最常说的一句话。”清子脸上带着一丝勉强的微笑，继续说着。“真的。‘我会把你所有的精液都吸干！’这句话用原语言说出来效果要好得多，我向你保证。翻译版本完全无法传达这种效果。” 看，这种情况变得有点尴尬了。 清子随意地挥了挥手，表示不介意。“哦，拜托。不管怎样，这事都会很尴尬的。” [pc.mf||不过，有个问题……她是怎么知道的？我是说，她是怎么知道你拥有那些东西的？如果你明白我的意思的话。 “我仔细嗅了嗅。我们狐狸一族只要集中注意力，就能闻到这类东西。说实话，这也没什么坏处——像我们这样漂亮的种族，周围确实有不少‘伪娘’，还有一堆无可救药地淑女兮兮的狐族男孩。”清子的眼神变得恍惚起来，她轻轻舔了舔嘴唇。“啊，那些真是美好的时光。但我的观点依然不变。别担心，就算我想告诉别人，我也根本没办法说出来。”] 令人尴尬的沉默……她真的非得那么说吗？ “这就好比给人卜出个坏卦。在这儿，诚实才是那头‘野兽’——我是说，最好的——策略，因为如果你撒谎，将来很可能会给自己惹来更多麻烦。” ] 没有其他办法可以做到这一点，对吧？ “确实还有别的办法能把一个人的气转移给接受者。不过，那些办法都要求我先拥有某种实体形态，而我现在没有。交配这个行为——不，繁殖——或许是把自身生命力交给他人去培育的最原始、最有力的一种方式。 正如我当时所说，如果你觉得这种做法令人反感，我也不会责怪你。毕竟，你在这些事情上的观念很可能与我们不同。虽然鹰身女妖在这些方面比我们开放得多，但其他人并非如此。因此，我们不得不调整自己的行事方式。” 那么，让我们把事情弄清楚。为了让她暂时摆脱囚禁，她需要那种她所说的身体能量——而你正是这种能量的唯一来源。那么，当你最终给她足够的这种能量时，会发生什么呢？到底需要多少量才算足够呢？ “如果我的法术运用没有错误的话，我应该能够在那个光球之外短暂地现身。”清子回答道。“就像我说的，不是永久性的。但你给我的气越多，我能维持的时间就越长。至于其他方面……嗯，我还是要再说一遍：理论是一回事，实践又是另一回事。为了我们双方的好，我只希望最终的结果能够如愿以偿。” 你点了点头。 “再次强调，[pc.name]，我知道，这是我向你提出的一个很大的请求；将你的信任寄托在一个凯罗斯的仆人身上，确实是一件不轻的事。如果你觉得可以的话……随时跟我提这个事情吧。我绝不会强迫你做任何你不愿意做的事情——仅仅是因为你愿意来看我，允许我与你共度时光，你就已经为我做了很多。在经历了这么长时间的孤独之后，这对我的意义，远远超出了你的想象。 现在……我们是不是该谈谈一些更愉快的话题呢？将来我们还是会回到这个话题上，但现在——大概还不是时候吧。”
