rows.original: You step over to the maps and star charts hung up by the desk and take a closer look at them. While the writing looks vaguely similar to modern Belharan, a lot of the wording is archaic and largely illegible to you. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Even for someone who's been blessed enough to have received a formal education like you, old Belharan isn't one of the subjects you could go into deeply enough for lack of learning material, so |Someone with the likes of your background would never have warranted any kind of formal education, let alone the kind that would've been required for reading the scrawl on this ancient parchment. Either way, ] all you're reduced to is guessing the meaning of every other word, and even that is tenuous at best. Still, it's clear as day that these navigational aids are ancient, old enough to be from the Godswar or even before it — by all rights, the constant exposure to the salt air and moist should have caused them to fall apart long ago. Even if they do crinkle, they don't fall apart at your cautious prodding, and with the way the seat has an impression in it it's implied that these have been used recently and often. The question is, of course, why would anyone still plot a course by ancient maps? Sure, much of the continent may have been devastated centuries ago, but certainly the art of cartography wasn't lost. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |You've seen your share of maps in your time given your previous profession, that's for sure, so it's not as if anyone with even a smidgen of learning doesn't know what the world looks like |You may not have seen many with your own eyes, but everyone knows that you can freely buy a map of the world in any Jassiran port city; catfolk were — and still are — sold all over the place, after all ]. There're locations marked here that don't exist any more, one or two you've only heard about in legend, and the boundaries of the nations are all wrong... or at least, you think. [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |"Oh," Atugia says, coming up beside you to take in the maps on the wall. "Oh." Why, does she know something about these? "Carmen and I used to travel a bit just after... well, she wanted to get out of the castle for a few years after things settled down. Wanted to put the bad memories aside, you see. The maps are accurate... for their time. Teiglache's right there, you see." She jabs the map with a finger, causing it to bend and crinkle, but not tear. "And Jassira, and Tronarii... but a whole lot of these other places don't exist any more, or at least, they're not called by the same names. Especially the semi-independent city-states down by the continental coast, those got completely wiped out." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yeah. The coastlines and all are still the same, too — except for that one where the Idejima peninsula was torn off by an earthquake from one of the bigger battles and wound up floating about in the sea until it washed up down south. Look. Just cut this bit off — " she moves her finger on the map — "and add this bit just north of Tronarii. Not much, but when you consider it moved at all..." An entire peninsula... just torn away? How is that possible? Isn't land attached to the seafloor? Wouldn't it sink? Atugia sighs. "I don't know. Those days were crazy, I'm just glad Carmen and I only saw a little bit of the chaos, being as remote as we were. But back to the point — I can tell you that these maps are real. Carmen was always a passenger aboard the ships we took, but she was always treated nice and sometimes I'd see these around when the captains invited her to dine in their cabins." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "Well, many places like these were destroyed during the Godswar. My guess? They're looking for more and more of the old cities so they can loot them, bring the treasure and all to their mistress. It's the only explanation that I can see which also makes sense." |"Ah." Before you know it, your fox-wife has silently inserted herself at your side, peering at the old map. "I thought I would never see one of these again." Why, does she know something about these? "A little, beloved. Before there were torii gates, we had to come over the ocean by ship... some still do. The first ones were part of the advance fleet sent to conduct gunboat diplomacy upon our nation and annex us... we took their ships and the sailors who were brave enough to guide us back to their now torn homeland, and crossed the ocean." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yes. I saw several of these during the month-long trip, maps and star charts, other navigational tools." Gently, Kiyoko raises a finger to the ancient, yellowed paper, and gathers a bit of dust on her fingertip before smudging it away. "Fragile, yet immensely sturdy to have survived this long. That alone would have confirmed the authenticity of this relic, if not the information on it." And she saw these personally? "The Belharan sailors used these to navigate seas unknown to us. I would imagine them quite accurate." Your fox-wife closes her eyes, clearly dredging up deep memories. "Yes. The coastlines and landmarks are identical to the ones I saw, I am sure of this. Major ports, cities, and nominally independent city-states that nevertheless paid quiet tribute to Belhar. A month on a ship is a long time to absorb information and learn, when the alternative is boredom." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "My guess would be the same reason we do: to find old sites and try and excavate their treasures; no doubt this demoness of yours is highly interested in them, for all the wrong reasons. I am sure that we will find more information pertaining to this if we search a little more, that is to be sure." Kiyoko looks thoughtful a moment and taps her chin. "Komari tells me that many of the old maps the original Belharans brought along with them have been quite useful in searching for the ruins of the old empire. As far as I understand these things, the coastlines and their landmarks have not changed much since then as opposed to the interiors of the continents where much of the fighting occurred, so it would make sense to search by ship." |"Hmp." While you've been engrossed in trying to make sense of the maps and charts, Gweyr's padded over to you and started reading over your shoulder. "Don't know much about these. Do you?" [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Some, but none this old. |Nope. ] "Still, these look pretty old. Wonder why anyone would be sailing by them... unless they're trying to find stuff that isn't on the maps of the world you can buy out of Jassira. Look at all these... well, whatever they are." The old wolfess makes to jab at the ancient, yellowed parchment, then thinks better of it. "If they were places of interest to the Belharans of old, they'd be of interest to treasure hunters like some of the folks I knew when I was younger. Wouldn't be a week going by where the earth wouldn't move and reveal yet another damned ruin or the other. Many good kids would go in and wound up never coming out..." She thinks the cult might be digging up relics of old Belhar? Gweyr blinks. "I... I wasn't thinking of that, but now that you speak of it, that's almost certainly what the damn bastards were doing. Tollus was crowing about wanting the treasures in the baroness's vaults twenty years ago... I wouldn't be surprised if he's still looking for more of the same ever since." ] That... well, that makes sense. This very ship itself is a relic that the cult's been putting to their own nefarious purposes. No doubt Kas and Tollus wouldn't be stopping at one, would they? While you've no evidence of this, it nevertheless is a conjecture that would be worth investigating. Turning away from the maps, you pause to consider this theory, what it might mean, and most importantly, how it all ties in with what's going on in the rift and Kasyrra's larger plans... assuming she and Tollus are still on the same page, that is.
rows.translation: 你走到桌边，仔细观察那些挂在那里的地图和星图。虽然上面的文字看起来与现代贝尔哈兰的语言有些相似，但很多表达方式都非常古老，几乎无法辨认。 [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |就算像你这样有幸受过正规教育的人，古贝尔哈兰语也算不上你能深入钻研的科目，因为缺乏学习资料，所以 |像你这种出身的人，本来根本轮不到接受什么正规教育，更别提读懂这张古老羊皮纸上潦草字迹所需的那种教育了。无论如何， ]你只能靠猜来推断隔一个词的意思，而且连猜都猜得很不牢靠。 不过，很明显，这些导航辅助工具已经非常古老了，它们的历史可能可以追溯到“神战”时期，甚至更早——按照常理来说，长期暴露在盐雾和潮气里，它们早就该散架了才对。它们虽然会起皱，但你小心翼翼地拨弄时却没有碎掉；而且座位上有一处凹陷的印痕，说明这些东西最近还常被人使用。 当然，问题在于：为什么还有人会依靠古老的地图来规划路线呢？当然，虽然几个世纪前这片大陆的大部分地区可能已经遭受了严重的破坏，但制图技术肯定没有因此而失传。 [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |凭你以前的职业，你见过的地图也不少，这一点可以肯定，所以倒不是说稍微有点学问的人会不知道这世界长什么样。 |你或许没亲眼见过多少张，但谁都知道，在贾西拉的任何港口城市都能随便买到世界地图；毕竟猫人过去——如今也一样——到处都有人贩卖。 ]这里标出的一些地点已经不存在了，有一两个地方你只是从传说中听说过而已，而各个国家的边界也全都错了……至少你是这么认为的。 [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |“哦，”阿图吉娅走到你身边，看着墙上的那些地图说道，“哦。” 难道她对这些了解些什么吗？ “在……嗯，事情平息之后，卡门和我曾经一起出去旅行过一段时间。她想在局势安定下来后离开城堡住上几年，好把那些糟糕的回忆抛到一边，你知道的。这些地图在它们那个时代是准确的……泰格拉赫就在那儿，你看。”她用手指戳了戳地图，地图因此弯曲了一些，出现了一些褶皱，但并没有被撕破。“还有贾西拉，还有特罗纳里。但是，很多其他的地方已经不复存在了，或者至少，它们的名字已经变了。尤其是那些位于大陆海岸边的半独立城邦，它们已经被彻底消灭了。” 那么这些地图在它们制作的时候是相当精确的，对吧？ “是的。海岸线之类的也都没有变化——除了那片地区：在某场大规模战役中，伊德吉马半岛被地震从大陆上撕了下来，在海上漂来漂去，最后被冲到了南边。看，只要把这一块切掉——”她在地图上用手指指了指那个区域——“再把它添到特罗纳里以北就行了。变化不大，可你想想它居然整个挪了位置……” 整整一个半岛……就这样被撕裂掉了？这怎么可能呢？陆地不应该是固定在海底的吗？这样的情况下，半岛不应该会沉入海底吗？ 阿图吉娅叹了口气：“我不知道。那些日子真是太疯狂了……幸好我们住在那么偏远的地方，所以只目睹了那一部分混乱景象。不过，这些地图确实是真实的。卡门搭乘我们坐的船时总是以乘客的身份，但大家待她都很好；有时候船长请她到舱房里用餐，我就会看到这些地图。” 那么，为什么这艘船会用几百年前的地图来导航呢？ “嗯，像这样的地方很多都在神战期间被毁掉了。我的猜测是：他们正在寻找那些古老的城市，以便劫掠其中的财宝，然后将所有战利品带回给他们的主子。这是我能想到的唯一合理的解释。” |“啊。”还没等你反应过来，你的狐狸妻子就已经悄无声息地站到你身边，盯着那张古老的地图。“我以为再也见不到这种东西了。” 难道她对这些东西了解些什么吗？ “知道一点而已，亲爱的。在还没有鸟居之前，我们只能乘船渡海而来……现在仍然有人这样做。最初那些船只，其实是作为先遣队被派来对我国实施炮舰外交、企图将我们吞并的……我们夺下了他们的船，也让那些敢于为我们引路、驶回他们如今已支离破碎的故土的水手上了船，就这样渡过了大洋。” 那么这些地图在它们所处的时代来说，确实是准确的吗？ “是的。在为期一个月的旅行中，我看到了很多这样的地图、星图以及其他导航工具。”清子轻轻地将手指放在那张古老而泛黄的纸上，指尖沾上了一些灰尘，随后又将它们拂去。“这些物品虽然脆弱，但却异常坚固，才能保存至今。单是这一点就足以证明这件遗物的真实性，更何况它上面记载的信息。” 她这些都是亲眼所见吗？ “贝尔哈兰的水手就用这些来航行于我们陌生的海域。我想它们应该相当准确。”你的狐狸妻子闭上了眼睛，显然是在回忆那些往事。“是的，那些海岸线以及地标，和我当时看到的完全一样，我敢肯定。那些重要的港口、城市，以及那些名义上独立、却暗中向贝尔哈兰纳贡的城邦……在船上待一个月是很长的时间，既然别无消遣，正好够用来吸收信息、学点东西。” 那你觉得，为什么这艘船会用几百年前的地图来导航呢？ “我猜原因和我们一样：为了寻找古老的遗址，试着挖出里面的宝藏；毫无疑问，你这位女恶魔对那些东西非常感兴趣，只是动机全都不正当。我相信，如果我们再继续搜索一下，肯定能找到更多与此相关的信息。”清子若有所思地沉吟了一会儿，然后轻敲着下巴说道：“麻里告诉我，最初的贝尔哈兰人带来的那些古老地图，在寻找旧帝国遗迹时相当有用。据我所知，从那以后海岸线和地标的变化不大，反倒是那些发生过许多战事的大陆内陆变化很大，所以乘船搜索才说得通。” |“哼。”当你还在专心研究那些地图和图表、试图弄清它们的含义时，格维尔走了过来，从你肩后看那些东西。“这些我不太懂，你呢？ [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |有些，但没有这么古老的。 |不知道。 ] 不过，这些东西看起来确实很古老。真不知道怎么会有人靠它们航行……除非他们是在找那些在贾西拉买来的世界地图上没有的东西。看看这些……嗯，不管它们到底是什么吧。”那只老女狼伸手想戳那张古老发黄的羊皮纸，想了想又作罢。“要是这些地方对当年的贝尔哈兰人有价值，那对我年轻时认识的那些寻宝人来说也一样有价值。那时候几乎每个星期都会地动山摇，又冒出一处该死的废墟。许多好孩子进去之后就再也没出来……” 她觉得这个邪教可能在挖旧贝尔哈的遗物？ 格维尔眨了眨眼。“我倒没想到这一层，不过你这么一说，那些该死的混蛋八成就是在干这种事。二十年前托勒斯就嚷嚷着想要女男爵金库里的财宝……要是他从那以后一直在找更多同类的东西，我一点都不会意外。” ] 这……好吧，这确实说得通。这艘船本身就是一件遗物，被这个邪教用来干他们的邪恶勾当。毫无疑问，卡斯和托勒斯不会只用一件就罢手，对吧？虽然你并没有证据，但这仍然是个值得追查的猜测。 将注意力从这些地图上移开，你停下来仔细思考这个理论：它可能意味着什么，更重要的是，它与裂谷里正在发生的事，以及卡希拉更大的计划之间究竟有什么关系……前提是她和托勒斯还在同一条船上。
rows.raw: ' You step over to the maps and star charts hung up by the desk and take a closer look at them. While the writing looks vaguely similar to modern Belharan, a lot of the wording is archaic and largely illegible to you. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Even for someone who's been blessed enough to have received a formal education like you, old Belharan isn't one of the subjects you could go into deeply enough for lack of learning material, so |Someone with the likes of your background would never have warranted any kind of formal education, let alone the kind that would've been required for reading the scrawl on this ancient parchment. Either way, ] all you're reduced to is guessing the meaning of every other word, and even that is tenuous at best. Still, it's clear as day that these navigational aids are ancient, old enough to be from the Godswar or even before it — by all rights, the constant exposure to the salt air and moist should have caused them to fall apart long ago. Even if they do crinkle, they don't fall apart at your cautious prodding, and with the way the seat has an impression in it it's implied that these have been used recently and often. The question is, of course, why would anyone still plot a course by ancient maps? Sure, much of the continent may have been devastated centuries ago, but certainly the art of cartography wasn't lost. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |You've seen your share of maps in your time given your previous profession, that's for sure, so it's not as if anyone with even a smidgen of learning doesn't know what the world looks like |You may not have seen many with your own eyes, but everyone knows that you can freely buy a map of the world in any Jassiran port city; catfolk were — and still are — sold all over the place, after all ]. There're locations marked here that don't exist any more, one or two you've only heard about in legend, and the boundaries of the nations are all wrong... or at least, you think. [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |"Oh," Atugia says, coming up beside you to take in the maps on the wall. "Oh." Why, does she know something about these? "Carmen and I used to travel a bit just after... well, she wanted to get out of the castle for a few years after things settled down. Wanted to put the bad memories aside, you see. The maps are accurate... for their time. Teiglache's right there, you see." She jabs the map with a finger, causing it to bend and crinkle, but not tear. "And Jassira, and Tronarii... but a whole lot of these other places don't exist any more, or at least, they're not called by the same names. Especially the semi-independent city-states down by the continental coast, those got completely wiped out." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yeah. The coastlines and all are still the same, too — except for that one where the Idejima peninsula was torn off by an earthquake from one of the bigger battles and wound up floating about in the sea until it washed up down south. Look. Just cut this bit off — " she moves her finger on the map — "and add this bit just north of Tronarii. Not much, but when you consider it moved at all..." An entire peninsula... just torn away? How is that possible? Isn't land attached to the seafloor? Wouldn't it sink? Atugia sighs. "I don't know. Those days were crazy, I'm just glad Carmen and I only saw a little bit of the chaos, being as remote as we were. But back to the point — I can tell you that these maps are real. Carmen was always a passenger aboard the ships we took, but she was always treated nice and sometimes I'd see these around when the captains invited her to dine in their cabins." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "Well, many places like these were destroyed during the Godswar. My guess? They're looking for more and more of the old cities so they can loot them, bring the treasure and all to their mistress. It's the only explanation that I can see which also makes sense." |"Ah." Before you know it, your fox-wife has silently inserted herself at your side, peering at the old map. "I thought I would never see one of these again." Why, does she know something about these? "A little, beloved. Before there were torii gates, we had to come over the ocean by ship... some still do. The first ones were part of the advance fleet sent to conduct gunboat diplomacy upon our nation and annex us... we took their ships and the sailors who were brave enough to guide us back to their now torn homeland, and crossed the ocean." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yes. I saw several of these during the month-long trip, maps and star charts, other navigational tools." Gently, Kiyoko raises a finger to the ancient, yellowed paper, and gathers a bit of dust on her fingertip before smudging it away. "Fragile, yet immensely sturdy to have survived this long. That alone would have confirmed the authenticity of this relic, if not the information on it." And she saw these personally? "The Belharan sailors used these to navigate seas unknown to us. I would imagine them quite accurate." Your fox-wife closes her eyes, clearly dredging up deep memories. "Yes. The coastlines and landmarks are identical to the ones I saw, I am sure of this. Major ports, cities, and nominally independent city-states that nevertheless paid quiet tribute to Belhar. A month on a ship is a long time to absorb information and learn, when the alternative is boredom." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "My guess would be the same reason we do: to find old sites and try and excavate their treasures; no doubt this demoness of yours is highly interested in them, for all the wrong reasons. I am sure that we will find more information pertaining to this if we search a little more, that is to be sure." Kiyoko looks thoughtful a moment and taps her chin. "Komari tells me that many of the old maps the original Belharans brought along with them have been quite useful in searching for the ruins of the old empire. As far as I understand these things, the coastlines and their landmarks have not changed much since then as opposed to the interiors of the continents where much of the fighting occurred, so it would make sense to search by ship." |"Hmp." While you've been engrossed in trying to make sense of the maps and charts, Gweyr's padded over to you and started reading over your shoulder. "Don't know much about these. Do you?" [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Some, but none this old. |Nope. ] "Still, these look pretty old. Wonder why anyone would be sailing by them... unless they're trying to find stuff that isn't on the maps of the world you can buy out of Jassira. Look at all these... well, whatever they are." The old wolfess makes to jab at the ancient, yellowed parchment, then thinks better of it. "If they were places of interest to the Belharans of old, they'd be of interest to treasure hunters like some of the folks I knew when I was younger. Wouldn't be a week going by where the earth wouldn't move and reveal yet another damned ruin or the other. Many good kids would go in and wound up never coming out..." She thinks the cult might be digging up relics of old Belhar? Gweyr blinks. "I... I wasn't thinking of that, but now that you speak of it, that's almost certainly what the damn bastards were doing. Tollus was crowing about wanting the treasures in the baroness's vaults twenty years ago... I wouldn't be surprised if he's still looking for more of the same ever since." ] That... well, that makes sense. This very ship itself is a relic that the cult's been putting to their own nefarious purposes. No doubt Kas and Tollus wouldn't be stopping at one, would they? While you've no evidence of this, it nevertheless is a conjecture that would be worth investigating. Turning away from the maps, you pause to consider this theory, what it might mean, and most importantly, how it all ties in with what's going on in the rift and Kasyrra's larger plans... assuming she and Tollus are still on the same page, that is.'

rows.original: It's not too hard to find the ship's log — it sits on one of the stands by the desk, thick, heavy and well-thumbed. You open it to find dozens upon dozens of entries, each one meticulously written in neat handwriting; whoever penned this must have some kind of education to pay such attention to detail. How nice of the ship's captain to be so thorough for your benefit: the log is replete with everything from weather conditions, landfall, cargo taken on and offloaded, even minor altercations amongst the crew... While you only have a few minutes to flip through what entries you can, several things immediately jump out at you: Firstly, the ship moves fast; it has to, for the logs to state that landfall was made in a Jassiran port one day and then barrels were taken on in Tronarii the other. Even if the nations are neighbouring ones, that's far too fast for any reasonable ship you know... but this isn't one, is it? Secondly, it has far fewer crew than you might imagine for a vessel this size — only seven, just to get it to move. It's true that this ship doesn't have oars or sails, and without any weapons all the bunks you saw back in the crew quarters would have been defunct, but it's still hard to believe. With a ship like this, though, it wouldn't need any means of protecting itself if it can just outpace any pursuer... that, or it's got means of defense that aren't immediately obvious. Thirdly, you note that the ship's been weighing anchor at all kinds of places all over this region, funnelling... things back to — well, some of the cargo has ended up here in the rift, to be sure. But the lion's share of goods, special orders, building materials, and whatever the cult has been collecting from sites all over the world to somewhere on the Marches' east coast. While the log is quite vague about what things are being gathered, as would be natural for someone writing for themselves as opposed for someone else's elucidation, it's not hard to infer that either the cult or Kasyrra herself considers them pretty valuable, if not important. She did say she was a scientist of sorts back in the Winter City, didn't she? Amongst the most recent entries, there's one that catches your eye, though: The Master's hunch was right; we found the information we needed off the coast of the continental heartland, not too far from Willowpast where the river opens up into the sea. No one was hurt during the excavation, but it wasn't for lack of trying on the part of the things we found inside. Praise be to the Dark Lady for her blessings, that we are just as much monster now as the things that lie beneath the earth; our strength outmatched theirs. We had one casualty with a huge gash across the chest, but the wound was already half-healed by the time we returned to the boat via the dinghy. It was very clearly attempting to fester in an unnatural way, but our Dark Lady's powers outmatch those of our foes'. The total retrievable items amounted to: seven relics, sixteen manuscripts and eleven miscellaneous artifacts; I have had to stop Whelker from lifting any small items for "personal use", the bastard. Then again, she used to be one of those mouse people, same as Berach, so it only makes sense, I suppose. All are to be deliverable to Estelore, but not before allowing the Master to examine them first. We also found the inscriptions the Master instructed us to find, and I've made a rubbing of them to be delivered to him. The password is "Issal Saal Craa Gas Iskar". At least, that's how Whelker assures me they're pronounced, she's the historian here, and ever since accepting the Dark Lady's gifts her obsession with the subject has only intensified, as has her penchant for claiming bits of it for her own. Either way, the words are strange for a minotaur tongue, but it would appear that it was devised by worshippers of Nareva, so the serpentine nature of the words makes sense. At the very least, it's not something a northern minotaur would ever guess on their own; as far as I know, it's complete gibberish in any language they speak, or used to speak for that matter. But hopefully the Master will be content with this find; I've never seen him this sullen in all the years we've been together. I don't know why — the Dark Lady is everything we've hoped for and more, but it's not my place to question him. Future me, I'm writing down the password because every single one of my crew has the attention span of a gnat and the organizational habits of a — a gnat as well. If you forget, no one's going to remember this. Now hurry up to the Master and get this to him so he can finally open up the treasury. I'd have blown apart the doors myself, or tried to dig around the walls, but he said it would destabilize everything since the entire place is so deep under the ocean. I don't like it, but I guess all the other stuff we collected on the trip makes up for the bother, so fine. You thumb through the log another time, but there aren't any events recorded within the entries that jump out at you. By all appearances, this vessel is dedicated to doing milk runs for Kasyrra and her cult, even if the milk itself is pretty valuable. Kind of a shame you don't see anything of value down here in the belly of the beast, but in that case it might not be as deserted as it is... [party.has quintillus |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Quintillus sneers, looking very smug with himself. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "Not news to me," your bunny-boy companion replies. "Like I said, he was crazy about the stuff even before all this shit started going down. He wanted the power that they represented, to deny it from others even if he couldn't figure out how to use them himself. And boy did he try, the dumbass. Ever wonder why he's bald?" You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does Quin know anything about that? He shrugs. "Sorry, can't help you there. Must've been developments that happened after I booked it. He must've gotten a lot of help if he's got some kind of undersea fort or something, because that is not the kind of thing the Tollus I remember would've been capable of." Help like Kas, maybe? "Dunno. He doesn't seem to like her a lot, and I'm sure the feeling's mutual." |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Gweyr muses. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless. Not that it isn't a profitable trade, knew some myself." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "That he was. Remember, he was crowing about wanting to take the baroness's castle and everything that was in her vaults. I don't think she actually has any vaults, but he was certainly enamored with the idea." You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does that ring any bells for her? She rubs her chin. "Sorry, can't help you there. But it sounds like he got a pretty big boost to be capable of all this... the Tollus I knew twenty years ago wouldn't have been capable of that." ] Well, that's enough for now. Maybe the rest of the ship will provide further insight into just what's going on in Tollus's mind...
rows.translation: 找到这艘船的航海日志并不太难——它就放在书桌旁的架子上，厚厚的、重型，上面还有很多人翻阅过的痕迹。当你打开它时，会看到成百上千条记录，每一条都用整洁工整的笔迹仔细记录下来；撰写这些记录的人肯定受过一定的教育，否则不可能如此注重细节。船长真是考虑周到，为你的方便做了这么多记录：航海日志里详细记载了各种信息，从天气状况、到船只靠岸的地点、船上货物的装卸情况，甚至还包括船员之间发生的些小争执…… 虽然你只有几分钟的时间来浏览这些记录，但有几件事立刻吸引了你的注意： 首先，这艘船跑得很快；不得不快，因为日志上写着某天在贾西拉的港口靠岸，第二天就在特罗纳里装上了木桶。就算这两个国家是邻邦，这样的速度也远超你知道的任何一艘正常船只……可这艘船本来就不正常，对吧？ 其次，对于一艘这么大的船来说，它的船员数量其实比你想象的要少得多——只有七个人，仅仅够让船移动而已。的确，这艘船没有桨也没有帆，而且由于没有任何武器，你在船员区看到的那些铺位本来也应该是无法使用的，但这一切还是让人难以相信。不过，这样一艘船只要能甩开任何追赶者，它就不需要任何自卫手段……又或者，它有着不那么显眼的防御手段。 第三，你注意到这艘船在这一带的各处下锚，把……东西汇集运回——嗯，有一部分货物确实最终到了裂谷这里。但绝大部分货物、特殊订单、建筑材料，以及这个邪教从世界各地搜刮来的各种东西，都被运往霜冻边境东海岸的某处。日志对汇集来的究竟是些什么东西写得相当含糊——一个人为自己记事、而不是写给别人看时，自然会是这种写法——但不难推断，无论是这个邪教还是卡希拉本人，都认为这些东西就算算不上重要，也相当值钱。 她之前不是说过自己在冬城是一名科学家吗？ 在最近收集到的这些资料中，有一份确实特别引人注目。 大师的直觉是正确的；我们在大陆腹地的海岸附近找到了我们需要的信息，那里距离柳树镇并不远，也就是那条河流汇入大海的地方。在挖掘过程中没有人受伤，但这并不是因为我们发现的那些东西没有拼命尝试。感谢暗影女士的赐福，如今我们和埋藏在地下的那些东西一样都是怪物；而我们的力量压过了它们。我们中有一人受了伤，胸前被划开一道巨大的伤口，但等我们乘小艇回到船上时，那伤口已经愈合了一半。它显然正以一种不自然的方式试图化脓溃烂，但我们暗影女士的力量胜过我们敌人的力量。 最终被找到的物品总数为：七件遗物、十六份手稿以及十一件其他杂物；我不得不阻止惠尔克把那些小物件“据为己有”，那个混蛋。话说回来，她以前也是那种鼠人，跟贝拉赫一样，所以我想这也说得通。这些东西最后都要送到埃斯特洛尔去，但在那之前，得先让大师过目。 我们还找到了大师让我们寻找的那些铭文，我已经把它们拓印下来，准备交给他。密码是“伊萨尔·萨尔·克拉·加斯·伊斯卡”。至少，惠尔克是这么向我保证这些词该这么发音的。她可是这里的史学家，自从接受了那位暗影女士赠送的礼物之后，她对这一主题的兴趣就越发浓厚了，而且她还总喜欢把其中的一些内容据为己有。无论如何，这些词语对于弥诺陶洛斯来说确实显得很奇怪，但看来它们是娜瑞瓦的信徒们创造出来的，因此这些词语所具有的“蛇一般的蜿蜒特性”也在情理之中。至少，北方弥诺陶洛斯绝对不可能自己想出这样的词语；据我所知，用他们现在使用的任何语言来说，这些词语都完全是无意义的废话。 但希望大师对这个发现满意；我们一起这么多年，我从没见过他这么闷闷不乐。我不知道为什么——暗影女士正是我们所期望的，甚至超出期望，但轮不到我去质疑他。写给未来的我：我把密码记下来，是因为我这帮船员每个的注意力都短得像蚊子，整理东西的习惯也——也像蚊子。你要是忘了，就没人记得住这个了。 现在赶紧到大师那儿去，把这个交给他，好让他终于能打开宝库。我本来想亲自把门拆开，或者试着在墙壁里挖找，但他说那样会破坏整个结构的稳定性，因为这个地方位于海洋深处。虽然我不喜欢这样，但想想我们在旅途中收集到的其他东西，也算是弥补了这个麻烦，所以也就算了。 你再次翻阅了那些记录，但其中并没有任何特别引人注目的事件。从各方面看，这艘船就是专门替卡希拉和她的邪教跑常规运输的，哪怕运的货本身相当值钱。有点遗憾的是，在这头巨兽的肚子里什么都没找到，不过那样的话，这里或许也不像看上去那么空无一人…… [party.has quintillus |“所以，他们干的是盗墓的勾当。”昆蒂卢斯冷笑道，一脸得意。“说得体面些是盗墓，可说白了还是盗墓。” 这意味着托勒斯、卡斯，或者两人都，对旧贝尔哈的文物感兴趣。 “这我早就不意外了，”你的兔子男孩伙伴答道。“就像我说的，早在这一切开始之前，他就痴迷这些东西了。他想要它们代表的力量，就算自己弄不明白怎么用，也不肯让别人得到。而且那笨蛋还真的拼命试过。你想过他为什么是秃头吗？” 你一直只当那是他浑蛋的一部分。但那些关于某个地方在海洋下面，或者密码是用某种其他语言写成的说法——昆因到底知道些什么呢？ 他耸了耸肩。“抱歉，这个我帮不上忙。那肯定是我跑路之后发生的事。他要是真弄出了什么海底要塞之类的东西，那肯定得到了不少帮助，因为我记得的那个托勒斯绝不是能干出这种事的人。” 也许是像卡斯那样的帮助？ “不知道。他好像并不怎么喜欢她，我敢肯定她也是同样的感觉。” |“所以，他们干的是盗墓的勾当。”格维尔若有所思地说。“说得体面些是盗墓，可说白了还是盗墓。不过这行当倒确实赚钱，我自己也认识几个干这行的。” 这意味着托勒斯、卡斯，或者两人都，会对旧贝尔哈的文物感兴趣。 “他确实动过这念头。记得吗，他当年就嚷嚷着要拿下女男爵的城堡和她地窖里的所有东西。我倒不觉得她真的有什么地窖，但他确实对那个念头着迷得很。” 你一直只当这是他本性里的坏毛病。但那些关于某个地方位于海洋之下，或者密码是用某种其他语言写成的说法——这些会不会让她想起什么来呢？ 她摸了摸下巴。“抱歉，这个我帮不上忙。不过听上去他得到了相当大的助力才做得到这些……二十年前我认识的那个托勒斯可做不到。” ] 好了，目前就到这里吧。也许船上其他地方能让我们更清楚地了解托勒斯脑子里在盘算什么……
rows.raw: " It's not too hard to find the ship's log — it sits on one of the stands by the desk, thick, heavy and well-thumbed. You open it to find dozens upon dozens of entries, each one meticulously written in neat handwriting; whoever penned this must have some kind of education to pay such attention to detail. How nice of the ship's captain to be so thorough for your benefit: the log is replete with everything from weather conditions, landfall, cargo taken on and offloaded, even minor altercations amongst the crew... While you only have a few minutes to flip through what entries you can, several things immediately jump out at you: Firstly, the ship moves fast; it has to, for the logs to state that landfall was made in a Jassiran port one day and then barrels were taken on in Tronarii the other. Even if the nations are neighbouring ones, that's far too fast for any reasonable ship you know... but this isn't one, is it? Secondly, it has far fewer crew than you might imagine for a vessel this size — only seven, just to get it to move. It's true that this ship doesn't have oars or sails, and without any weapons all the bunks you saw back in the crew quarters would have been defunct, but it's still hard to believe. With a ship like this, though, it wouldn't need any means of protecting itself if it can just outpace any pursuer... that, or it's got means of defense that aren't immediately obvious. Thirdly, you note that the ship's been weighing anchor at all kinds of places all over this region, funnelling... things back to — well, some of the cargo has ended up here in the rift, to be sure. But the lion's share of goods, special orders, building materials, and whatever the cult has been collecting from sites all over the world to somewhere on the Marches' east coast. While the log is quite vague about what things are being gathered, as would be natural for someone writing for themselves as opposed for someone else's elucidation, it's not hard to infer that either the cult or Kasyrra herself considers them pretty valuable, if not important. She did say she was a scientist of sorts back in the Winter City, didn't she? Amongst the most recent entries, there's one that catches your eye, though: The Master's hunch was right; we found the information we needed off the coast of the continental heartland, not too far from Willowpast where the river opens up into the sea. No one was hurt during the excavation, but it wasn't for lack of trying on the part of the things we found inside. Praise be to the Dark Lady for her blessings, that we are just as much monster now as the things that lie beneath the earth; our strength outmatched theirs. We had one casualty with a huge gash across the chest, but the wound was already half-healed by the time we returned to the boat via the dinghy. It was very clearly attempting to fester in an unnatural way, but our Dark Lady's powers outmatch those of our foes'. The total retrievable items amounted to: seven relics, sixteen manuscripts and eleven miscellaneous artifacts; I have had to stop Whelker from lifting any small items for "personal use", the bastard. Then again, she used to be one of those mouse people, same as Berach, so it only makes sense, I suppose. All are to be deliverable to Estelore, but not before allowing the Master to examine them first. We also found the inscriptions the Master instructed us to find, and I've made a rubbing of them to be delivered to him. The password is "Issal Saal Craa Gas Iskar". At least, that's how Whelker assures me they're pronounced, she's the historian here, and ever since accepting the Dark Lady's gifts her obsession with the subject has only intensified, as has her penchant for claiming bits of it for her own. Either way, the words are strange for a minotaur tongue, but it would appear that it was devised by worshippers of Nareva, so the serpentine nature of the words makes sense. At the very least, it's not something a northern minotaur would ever guess on their own; as far as I know, it's complete gibberish in any language they speak, or used to speak for that matter. But hopefully the Master will be content with this find; I've never seen him this sullen in all the years we've been together. I don't know why — the Dark Lady is everything we've hoped for and more, but it's not my place to question him. Future me, I'm writing down the password because every single one of my crew has the attention span of a gnat and the organizational habits of a — a gnat as well. If you forget, no one's going to remember this. Now hurry up to the Master and get this to him so he can finally open up the treasury. I'd have blown apart the doors myself, or tried to dig around the walls, but he said it would destabilize everything since the entire place is so deep under the ocean. I don't like it, but I guess all the other stuff we collected on the trip makes up for the bother, so fine. You thumb through the log another time, but there aren't any events recorded within the entries that jump out at you. By all appearances, this vessel is dedicated to doing milk runs for Kasyrra and her cult, even if the milk itself is pretty valuable. Kind of a shame you don't see anything of value down here in the belly of the beast, but in that case it might not be as deserted as it is... [party.has quintillus |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Quintillus sneers, looking very smug with himself. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "Not news to me," your bunny-boy companion replies. "Like I said, he was crazy about the stuff even before all this shit started going down. He wanted the power that they represented, to deny it from others even if he couldn't figure out how to use them himself. And boy did he try, the dumbass. Ever wonder why he's bald?" You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does Quin know anything about that? He shrugs. "Sorry, can't help you there. Must've been developments that happened after I booked it. He must've gotten a lot of help if he's got some kind of undersea fort or something, because that is not the kind of thing the Tollus I remember would've been capable of." Help like Kas, maybe? "Dunno. He doesn't seem to like her a lot, and I'm sure the feeling's mutual." |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Gweyr muses. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless. Not that it isn't a profitable trade, knew some myself." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "That he was. Remember, he was crowing about wanting to take the baroness's castle and everything that was in her vaults. I don't think she actually has any vaults, but he was certainly enamored with the idea." You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does that ring any bells for her? She rubs her chin. "Sorry, can't help you there. But it sounds like he got a pretty big boost to be capable of all this... the Tollus I knew twenty years ago wouldn't have been capable of that." ] Well, that's enough for now. Maybe the rest of the ship will provide further insight into just what's going on in Tollus's mind... "

rows.original: Breath catching in your throat, you leave the walkway that lines the edge of the circular chamber and step onto the metal bridge that connects it to the orb's little plinth. [pc.isMage |Even if you weren't magically inclined, you'd have no problem feeling the sheer intensity of the power surging within the beam of light, and the fact that you are trained in these things only serves to set your teeth on edge all the more |While you aren't magically inclined, you don't need to be to feel the sheer intensity of the power surging through the beam of light. It makes your skin crawl — not necessarily in fear or as a danger response, but from the sheer potential that's present here. Potential for what? That's a question for someone who's more magically inclined to answer. ]. [party.has atugia |"Hey, careful there!" Tui's voice is barely audible over the thrumming. "Those runes about the base — they're clearly not good news!" She knows what they mean? "Y-yeah! They're pretty close to those we used to use in Teiglache! Look!" Atugia gestures to herself and the patterns on her skin, and now that she points it out, there's a passing similarity there — the patterns aren't exactly the same, but they're conceivably related. She is the runic expert here, though... if you do decide to get closer to investigate, she might be able to make something out of them. |"Careful, kid," Gweyr growls from behind you. "I don't know if this'll turn you into a smoking pile of dust, but... just know when to back off, okay? I've never trusted old Belharan shit since my days in the heartlands, and neither should you." Yeah, got it. ] That does bear the question, though. Do you want to get closer to the ship's engine and see what you can figure out about it? It's obviously not safe, but the insight might be worth it. You won't have time to come back to this given the fact that you're on short notice for being down here at all, so you'll have to make this decision now.
rows.translation: 你的呼吸变得急促起来，你离开了环绕着圆形大厅边缘的通道，踏上了那座将大厅与那个小球体底座连接起来的金属桥。 [pc.isMage |即使你并不通魔法，也不难感受到那道光束中奔涌的力量有多么强烈；而你确实受过这方面的训练，这只会让你更加牙根发酸、坐立不安。 |虽然你不通魔法，但要感受到穿过光束奔涌的力量有多强烈，也用不着通魔法。它让你头皮发麻——未必是出于恐惧或危险反应，而纯粹是因为这里蕴含的那种潜力。什么潜力？这个问题得由更懂魔法的人来回答。 ]. [party.has atugia |“嘿，小心点！”在嗡嗡的震响中，崔的声音几乎听不见。“底座周围的那些符文……显然不是什么好兆头！” 她知道那些符文代表什么吗？ “嗯……是的！它们和我们以前在泰格拉赫使用的那些符文很相似！看！” 阿图吉娅指了指自己以及自己皮肤上的那些图案。现在她这么一指，确实能看出它们之间有些相似之处——这些图案虽然并不完全一样，但显然存在某种关联。毕竟，她才是这里的符文专家……如果你决定靠近些查看，她或许能看出点门道。 |“小心点，孩子，”格维尔在你身后低吼道，“我不知道这会不会把你变成一堆灰烬，但……至少要知道什么时候该退开，明白吗？自从我待在内陆那会儿起，我就从不信旧贝尔哈的那些鬼东西，你也不该信。” “知道了。” ] 不过，这确实引出了一个问题：你是否想靠近那艘船的引擎，看看能从中发现什么线索呢？显然这样做并不安全，但这样的尝试或许值得一试。考虑到你被紧急派到这里来，根本没有时间再回来，所以你必须现在就做出这个决定。

rows.original:
Gritting your teeth, you back away slowly from the ship's engine, the black orb still thrumming and crackling with power. You know when you're out of your league, and this is it. [pc.isMage
        |Your magical senses are all telling you to back off, and — well, who are you going to believe, your curiosity or your own lying eyes?
        |You may not be as magically attuned to this kind of stuff as an actual wizard would, but every one of your senses are screaming at you to back off.
        ] It's only when you feel your shoulders hit the wooden paneling of the engine room's walls and press yourself up against it that you feel marginally safer than you did a moment ago.
        
        "You all right?" Gweyr asks, grabbing you by under the arm and steadying you on your feet. "Looking a little pale there, [pc.mf|kid|girl]."
        
        Yeah. It was... it felt as if the magical setup was drawing you in, like a moth to a flame, but you're all right now. Best to stay in this chamber as little as possible.
rows.translation:
你咬紧牙关，慢慢从这艘船的引擎旁退开，那颗黑色球体仍在嗡鸣着、噼啪地散发着力量。你知道自己什么时候是力不能及，而这一次就是。 [pc.isMage
        |你的魔法感官都在叫你别靠近——那么，你该信谁呢？信你的好奇心，还是信你自己这双会骗人的眼睛？
        |你或许不像真正的巫师那样对这类事物有魔法感知，但你的每一种感官都在尖叫着让你退开。
        ] 直到你感觉肩膀撞上引擎室墙壁的木板、把自己贴在上面时，才觉得比刚才稍微安全了一点。
        
        “你没事吧？”格维尔问道，一把扶住你的腋下，让你站稳。“你脸色有点苍白，[pc.mf|小子|姑娘]。”
        
        嗯。刚才……感觉那套魔法装置像是在把你往里拉，就像飞蛾扑火，不过你现在没事了。最好尽量少待在这个房间里。

rows.original: This is too dangerous and you don't know if there's anything concrete you can get out of this. It's time to back away before you wind up doing something you'll regret.
rows.translation: 这太危险了，而且你也不清楚能否从中获得什么实质性的东西。现在正是该退缩的时候了，否则你可能会做出让自己后悔的事情。
rows.raw: "This is too dangerous and you don't know if there's anything concrete you can get out of this. It's time to back away before you wind up doing something you'll regret."

rows.original:
Gritting your teeth, you force yourself to ignore your screaming senses and approach the black orb in its pillar of light. Nothing ventured, nothing gained — this whole quest has been dangerous enough as it is already, what's putting your life on the line one more time?

        "Careful there," Gweyr's voice comes from somewhere behind you, barely audible above the crackling and thrumming. "Would hate to see you turn into a pile of dust or something."
        
        Kneeling down, you take a good look at the runes inscribed at the base of the orb's pedestal, [pc.isMage
        |comparing them to those you've seen before in your magical training. There are several which seem familiar, but not exactly the same; you might be able to guess at their meanings if they're what you think they are and perhaps find someone to bounce your ideas off of
        |committing them to memory. While you don't have the training required to 
        ]. Either way, once you've got the runic inscriptions as thoroughly memorized as you can, you turn to
rows.translation:
你咬紧牙关，强迫自己无视尖叫不止的感官，朝那根光柱中的黑色球体走去。不入虎穴，焉得虎子——这整趟任务本来就已经够危险了，再拿命赌一次又何妨？

        “小心点，”格维尔的声音从你身后某处传来，在噼啪声和嗡鸣声中几乎听不见。“我可不想看到你变成一堆灰尘什么的。”
        
        你跪下身，仔细端详那颗球体基座上刻着的符文。 [pc.isMage
        |把它们与你在魔法训练中见过的那些作比较。有几样看起来很眼熟，却又并不完全一样；如果它们真如你所想，你或许能猜出它们的含义，也许还能找个人帮你验证一下这些想法。
        |把它们牢牢记下来。虽然你并不具备所需的训练，但…… 
        ]无论如何，等把那些符文铭文尽可能记熟之后，你转向

rows.original: find Atugia kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "Can't just let you stick your neck out and take all the risks when I'm the one who knows things about runes, can I? That, and you need someone to shield you if somethin' goes wrong." Well, when she puts it that way... you're glad she came up of her own volition to help out here. Now, she said earlier that the runes appeared familiar from a distance — does anything spring to mind now that she's able to have a closer look? "Give me a moment." Atugia traces the closest of the runes with her finger, and a spark of bluish-white power leaps from the light surrounding the pedestal to her — where it's absorbed into the runes on her body and dissipated harmlessly. "Yeah. It'd take a lot of explaining, but these are runes representing storm, sea and wind, almost identical to what we used in Teiglache." So she's saying that this pedestal is of Teiglachan make? "No. The runes we used didn't drive the ship like this thing is doin', they were for ensuring good weather, stayin' righted in rough seas, that kind of thing. A little country like mine didn't have this kind of power. But — " she clears her throat — "I will say that whoever made this drew a lot of inspiration from our runic system." Since the ship is of Belharan make, you'd assume that it was them who did it. "As good a guess as anyone's. The good thing about runes — " Tui points to her own body — "is that you can just draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while. They're usually not very good focuses, though. Wonder why they used them here." Yeah, wonder why. The black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "No, but it makes my skin crawl. Like, actually tremble, my runes are going crazy just being close to it. Don't do anything too stupid, would you?" ...You'll just get a closer look. "..." The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... [pc.isMage |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |There's something about this black crystal orb that against all logic is emitting and absorbing the magical light all at once, a sense of dread and wonder that sets in just by being close to it. ] ] "Look out!" With those words, Atugia grabs you by the collar of your [pc.armor] and hauls you backwards just in time for a crackling bolt of wayward radiance to narrowly miss you. It doesn't actually cause any damage to the wooden walkway that bridges the nest of pipes or the spot where you were standing, but the scorched, chemical smell it leaves lingering in the air strongly suggests that you wouldn't want to have been hit by that. Phew, that was close. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from where you are, is there? "None of the runes looked to be related to that kind of thing, and I'm not sure that'd be a good idea anyway; the demons would notice and come runnin' down." Atugia looks you up and down, then starts leading you back to Gweyr. "I think we'd better get back before anything else like that happens."
rows.translation: 发现阿图吉娅跪在你身旁，和你一样专注地研究着那些符文刻文。 她在这儿做什么？ “总不能让你一个人去冒险、把风险全担了吧？毕竟懂符文的人是我呀。再说，要是出了什么岔子，你也需要有人替你挡着。” 嗯，她这么一说……你很高兴她是自己主动来帮忙的。刚才她说那些符文从远处看似乎很眼熟——现在能凑近看了，她有没有想起什么？ “让我看看。”阿图吉娅用手指描过最近的一枚符文，一道蓝白色的能量火花从基座周围的光芒中跃向她——随即被她身上的符文吸收，无害地消散了。“嗯。解释起来很费口舌，但这些是代表风暴、海洋和风的符文，几乎和我们当年在泰格拉赫用的一模一样。” 那么她是说，这个基座是泰格拉赫人做的？ “不是。我们用的符文并不能像这东西一样驱动船只，它们是用来保佑好天气、在风浪中保持船身平稳之类的。像我国这样的小地方可没有这种力量。不过——”她清了清嗓子——“我倒是要说，做这东西的人从我们的符文体系里借鉴了很多。” 既然这艘船是贝尔哈兰人造的，你自然会认为动手的是他们。 “这猜测跟谁猜的都差不多。符文的好处是——”崔指了指自己的身体——“你只要把它们画上去或涂上去，然后很长一段时间都不用再管。不过它们通常不是很好的法术焦点。真不知道他们为什么在这里用符文。” 是啊，为什么呢。中间那颗黑色水晶球……她知道那是什么吗？ “不知道，但它让我浑身发麻。是真的会发抖，光靠近它，我身上的符文就乱成一团。你可别干太蠢的事。” ……你只是想凑近看看。 “……” 紧贴着光束时，那光刺眼得让人什么都看不清；可水晶本身却清晰可见——它悬在基座表面上方一两英寸处，缓缓上下浮动，把耀眼的光华尽数吸进体内。又或者，光本来就是它放出来的？不，不可能，要是那样的话，光就该朝四面八方散去，而不是形成一道轮廓分明的光束环绕着它，对吧？可偏偏…… [pc.isMage |你只在书里读到过这种东西，但描述完全对得上：实心的莱晶，表面打磨得光可鉴人，提纯过程中褪去了原本的红色，其余部分则与天然形成的一模一样，连瑕疵都在。 而贝尔哈兰人的每一艘战舰上都有一块？哇。 |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |你只在书里读到过这种东西，但描述完全对得上：实心的莱晶，表面打磨得光可鉴人，提纯过程中褪去了原本的红色，其余部分则与天然形成的一模一样，连瑕疵都在。 而贝尔哈兰人的每一艘战舰上都有一块？哇。 |这颗黑色水晶球有种说不清的地方——它违背一切常理，同时既放出又吸收那些魔法光芒；光是靠近它，就会让人心生既恐惧又惊叹的感觉。 ] ] “小心！”话音未落，阿图吉娅抓住你[pc.armor]的衣领，把你往后一拽，恰好让一道噼啪乱窜的光芒与你擦身而过。它其实并没有损坏架在管道堆上的木制通道，也没伤到你刚才站的地方，但它在空气里留下的那股焦糊的化学气味足以说明：要是被它打中，绝不会好受。 呼，好险。从你所在的位置，没办法把这一切关掉，对吧？ “那些符文看起来都跟这种事无关，而且我觉得那样做也不是什么好主意；恶魔们会察觉，然后跑下来。”阿图吉娅上下打量了你一番，然后领着你往回走向格维尔。“我觉得我们最好在再出什么类似状况之前回去。”

rows.original: find Kiyoko kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "Ah. Well, I can hardly allow you to walk into danger all by yourself, can I, beloved? Now then, there is no need to get too close to the engine core. The light is there to contain the energies present, but you would not want to be hit by a stray discharge." Well, when she puts it that way... you'll take a step or two back with her, then. Now, she knows about these things? "Some. I observed from a distance while one of the sailors explained it to me, although in not quite technical terms. The one or two war-wizards who came with the advanced fleet weren't so willing to talk... but sailors do." Kiyoko sighs, looking lost in thought. "This is the engine core of the ship, and is what provides the motive force to propel it through the water. Inscribed upon the base or the core holder are runes representing storm, sea and wind, based on those which the Belharans observed in Teiglache." You see. Why runes, though? "It is the same reason why both the Macahnese and we are accustomed to using paper charms for several purposes. Although they are far weaker than gems as foci, the good thing about spells based on symbology is that you can draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while — good for places which are too dangerous to approach on a regular or extended basis, such as the engine core of a ship such as this." Right. And the black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "Refined ley-crystal, such that the natural impurities that make it red or green have been excised from the structure, turning it black." ...You'll just get a closer look. "..." The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... "Mmm. Please refrain from venturing too far, beloved. There is nothing to be gained from getting too close that I cannot tell you outright." Right. You... you were just drawn to it. Like a moth to a flame, really... but you're glad she was here to pull you back from the brink. Phew, that was close. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from here, is there? "That would be up on the ship's bridge, and I do not believe that would accomplish anything substantial towards our goal here." Kiyoko looks you up and down, her expression completely placid. "We should return to Gweyr before something worse happens."
rows.translation: 发现清子跪在你身旁，和你一样专注地研究着那些符文刻文。 她在这儿做什么？ “啊。亲爱的，我总不能让你一个人走进危险里吧？好了，没必要靠引擎核心太近。那道光是为了约束这里蕴含的能量，可你总不会想被一道乱窜的放电打中吧。” 嗯，她这么一说……那你就跟着她往后退一两步吧。那么，她懂这些东西？ “懂一些。当时有一名水手给我讲解，我在远处观察过，虽然他用词并不算专业。随先遣舰队来的那一两位战法师并不怎么肯开口……不过水手肯说。”清子叹了口气，像是陷入了沉思。“这是这艘船的引擎核心，正是它为船在水中的前进提供动力。底座或核心托架上刻着代表风暴、海洋和风的符文，是依照贝尔哈兰人在泰格拉赫观察到的东西制成的。” 原来如此。不过为什么用符文？ “这和马卡人以及我们都习惯用纸符来做各种事情是同样的道理。虽然作为法术焦点，它们远比宝石弱，但以符号为基础的法术有个好处：你只要把它们画上或涂上，就能很长一段时间不再理会——对于太危险、无法经常或长时间接近的地方正合适，比如像这样一艘船的引擎核心。” 明白。那中间那颗黑色水晶球……她知道那是什么吗？ “提纯过的莱晶——天然杂质中让它显红或显绿的部分已经从结构中剔除，于是它就变成了黑色。” ……你只是想凑近看看。 “……” 紧贴着光束时，那光刺眼得让人什么都看不清；可水晶本身却清晰可见——它悬在基座表面上方一两英寸处，缓缓上下浮动，把耀眼的光华尽数吸进体内。又或者，光本来就是它放出来的？不，不可能，要是那样的话，光就该朝四面八方散去，而不是形成一道轮廓分明的光束环绕着它，对吧？可偏偏…… “嗯。亲爱的，请别走得太远。靠得太近，除了我直接告诉你的这些，什么也得不到。” 明白。你……你只是被它吸引住了。就像飞蛾扑火一样……不过幸好有她在，把你从边缘拉了回来。呼，好险。从这里没办法把这一切关掉，对吧？ “那得去船桥上才行，而且我也不认为那样做对我们此行的目标有什么实质帮助。”清子上下打量了你一番，神情十分平静。“我们该回到格维尔那儿去了，免得发生更糟的事。”

"This stuff's clearly magical, and I'm pretty sure I saw something like these in Dad's notebooks once," Cait replies with a small huff. "That, and you need someone to shield you if something goes wrong." Well, when she puts it that way... you're glad she came up of her own volition to help out here. Now, she said something about seeing these kinds of things in her father's notes? "Yeah!" Perking up, Cait makes to trace the closest of the runes with her finger, then thinks better of it. "They're not exactly the same, but on the trip across the ocean to here I had plenty of time to do some reading on Dad's stuff on a place called Teiglache. These are runes representing storm, sea and wind, almost identical to what was used by the shipwrights there." So she's saying that this pedestal is of Teiglachan make? "Nah, Dad noted that those ships had their runes painted on the prow and sails. Certainly a little podunk place like that doesn't have the knowledge or power necessary to make something like this... although like I said, it's clearly inspired from their runic system as Dad recorded it." Since the ship is of Belharan make, in that case you'd assume that it was them who did it. They did have a big empire and could afford to borrow ideas from all over the world. They're usually not very good focuses compared to the alternatives, though." Cait points up at the gem in her staff. "None of the runes looked to be related to that kind of thing, and I'm not sure that'd be a good idea anyway; the demons would notice and come running down." Without hesitation, Cait grabs you by under her arm and starts leading you back to Gweyr. "I think we'd better get back before anything else like that happens."
rows.translation: 发现凯特跪在你身旁，和你一样专注地研究着那些符文刻文。 她在这儿做什么？ “这东西明显是魔法造物，而且我挺确定我在爸爸的笔记本里见过类似的东西，”凯特轻哼了一声回答。“再说，要是出了什么岔子，你也需要有人替你挡一下。” 嗯，她这么一说……你很高兴她是自己主动来帮忙的。那么，她刚才说在她父亲的笔记里见过这类东西？ “对！”凯特来了精神，伸手想用指头描最近的符文，随即又打消了念头。“它们并不完全一样，但在渡海来这里的路上，我有大把时间读爸爸那些关于一个叫泰格拉赫的地方的资料。这些是代表风暴、海洋和风的符文，几乎和当地造船匠用的一模一样。” 那么她是说，这个基座是泰格拉赫人做的？ “不是啦，爸爸记过，那些船的符文是画在船首和船帆上的。像那样一个不起眼的小地方，肯定没有造出这种东西所需的知识和力量……不过就像我说的，这东西显然是受了他们那套符文体系的启发，爸爸也记录下来了。” 既然这艘船是贝尔哈兰人造的，那你就该认为是他们干的。他们确实有过一个大帝国，有能力从世界各地借鉴点子。 “是啊，这么说也说得通。符文的好处是你只要画上或涂上，就能很久都不去管它。不过跟别的选择相比，它们通常算不上好的法术焦点。”凯特抬手指了指她法杖上的宝石。“但在这种地方用它们也很自然；就算站这么远，那些噼啪声都让我浑身的毛竖起来了。” 是啊，为什么呢。中间那颗黑色水晶球……她知道那是什么吗？ “[pc.name]……别干太蠢的事，好吗？” ……你只是想凑近看看。 “……我说了，别干太蠢的事，听到没有？” 紧贴着光束时，那光刺眼得让人什么都看不清；可水晶本身却清晰可见——它悬在基座表面上方一两英寸处，缓缓上下浮动，把耀眼的光华尽数吸进体内。又或者，光本来就是它放出来的？不，不可能，要是那样的话，光就该朝四面八方散去，而不是形成一道轮廓分明的光束环绕着它，对吧？可偏偏…… [pc.isMage |你只在书里读到过这种东西，但描述完全对得上：实心的莱晶，表面打磨得光可鉴人，提纯过程中褪去了原本的红色，其余部分则与天然形成的一模一样，连瑕疵都在。 而贝尔哈兰人的每一艘战舰上都有一块？哇。 |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |你只在书里读到过这种东西，但描述完全对得上：实心的莱晶，表面打磨得光可鉴人，提纯过程中褪去了原本的红色，其余部分则与天然形成的一模一样，连瑕疵都在。 而贝尔哈兰人的每一艘战舰上都有一块？哇。 |这颗黑色水晶球有种说不清的地方——它违背一切常理，同时既放出又吸收那些魔法光芒；光是靠近它，就会让人心生既恐惧又惊叹的感觉。 ] ] “小心！” 冷不丁地，凯特用她的法杖勾住你[pc.armor]的衣领，把你往后一拽，恰好让一道噼啪乱窜的光芒与你擦身而过。它其实并没有损坏架在管道堆上的木制通道，也没伤到你刚才站的地方，但它在空气里留下的那股焦糊的化学气味足以说明：要是被它打中，绝不会好受。 “唔。”凯特撅起嘴。“我不是跟你说了别干太蠢的事吗？” 是啊，抱歉。它就是把你吸引过去了，你当时也不太清楚自己在干什么—— “是啊，我也感觉到了。所以才叫你要小心。” 明白了。从这里没办法把这一切关掉，对吧？ “那些符文看起来都跟这种事无关，而且我也不确定那样做是否明智；恶魔们会察觉，然后跑下来。”凯特毫不犹豫地抓住你的手臂，领着你往回走向格维尔。“我觉得我们最好在再出什么类似状况之前回去。”
rows.raw: " find Cait kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "This stuff's clearly magical, and I'm pretty sure I saw something like these in Dad's notebooks once," Cait replies with a small huff. "That, and you need someone to shield you if something goes wrong." Well, when she puts it that way... you're glad she came up of her own volition to help out here. Now, she said something about seeing these kinds of things in her father's notes? "Yeah!" Perking up, Cait makes to trace the closest of the runes with her finger, then thinks better of it. "They're not exactly the same, but on the trip across the ocean to here I had plenty of time to do some reading on Dad's stuff on a place called Teiglache. These are runes representing storm, sea and wind, almost identical to what was used by the shipwrights there." So she's saying that this pedestal is of Teiglachan make? "Nah, Dad noted that those ships had their runes painted on the prow and sails. Certainly a little podunk place like that doesn't have the knowledge or power necessary to make something like this... although like I said, it's clearly inspired from their runic system as Dad recorded it." Since the ship is of Belharan make, in that case you'd assume that it was them who did it. They did have a big empire and could afford to borrow ideas from all over the world. "Yeah, that'd make sense. The good thing about runes is that you can just draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while. They're usually not very good focuses compared to the alternatives, though." Cait points up at the gem in her staff. "But it's only natural that they'd want to use them in a place like this; even standing at this distance, all that crackling is making my fur stand on end." Yeah, wonder why. The black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "[pc.name]... don't do anything too stupid, would you?" ...You'll just get a closer look. "...I said, don't do anything too stupid, okay?" The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... [pc.isMage |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |There's something about this black crystal orb that against all logic is emitting and absorbing the magical light all at once, a sense of dread and wonder that sets in just by being close to it. ] ] "Look out!" Out of the blue, Cait hooks you by the collar of your [pc.armor] with her staff and hauls you backwards just in time for a crackling bolt of wayward radiance to narrowly miss you. It doesn't actually cause any damage to the wooden walkway that bridges the nest of pipes or the spot where you were standing, but the scorched, chemical smell it leaves lingering in the air strongly suggests that you wouldn't want to have been struck by that. "Mmh." Cait pouts. "I told you not to do anything too stupid, didn't I?" Yeah, sorry about that. It just drew you in, and you didn't quite know what you were doing — "Yeah, I felt it, too. That's why I told you to be careful." Point taken. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from here, is there? "None of the runes looked to be related to that kind of thing, and I'm not sure that'd be a good idea anyway; the demons would notice and come running down." Without hesitation, Cait grabs you by under her arm and starts leading you back to Gweyr. "I think we'd better get back before anything else like that happens." "

rows.original:
the black crystal orb, floating a few inches above the rune-lined pedestal. The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... 

            [pc.isMage
            |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all.
            
            And this is what makes the ship go? Wow.
            |[pc.bg scholar acolyte
            |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all.
            
            And this is what makes the ship go? Wow.
            |There's something about this black crystal orb that against all logic is emitting and absorbing the magical light all at once, a sense of dread and wonder that sets in just by being close to it.
            ]
            ]
            
            "Hey, watch it, [pc.mf|kid|girl]!"
            
            No sooner has Gweyr's gruff voice sounded out that a big hand grabs you by the collar of your [pc.armor] and yanks you back. Moments later, a sparkling tendril of energy lances out from the beam of incandescence and strikes the spot where you were just standing; while it doesn't actually cause any damage to the wooden walkway that bridges the nest of pipes, the scorched, chemical smell it leaves lingering in the air strongly suggests that you wouldn't want to have been struck by that.
            
            "Careful there. What did I just say?"
            
            Phew, that was close. Thanks.
            
            "Don't mention it, [pc.mf|kid|girl]."
            
            There isn't any way to shut all of this down from where you are, is there?
            
            "Doesn't look like it, I'd imagine that sort of thing would be up on the bridge. Besides, why would we want to, anyway? That'd just send them coming down to see what's up. Come on, let's move."

rows.original: Getting closer to the ship's engine while it's running might be dangerous, but it might reveal something about what Tollus and his goons are capable of, if you have the knowledge to glean some insight from it.
rows.translation: 在这艘船的引擎运转时靠近它可能会很危险，但如果你有相应的知识从中看出些门道，或许能弄清托勒斯和他那些手下到底有多大能耐。
rows.raw: "Getting closer to the ship's engine while it's running might be dangerous, but it might reveal something about what Tollus and his goons are capable of, if you have the knowledge to glean some insight from it."

rows.original: Something catches your eye as you pass by the bed — there's a trunk lying at its feet, bolted to the ground, no doubt in an attempt to keep it from sliding around from the rocking motion of the waves. The one bit of true luxury in this otherwise modest cabin, the glint of gold leaf upon wood is oh-so-alluring... Yes, definitely worth a closer look. Getting down on a knee by the bed, you dust off the lid and examine it in detail; there's a lock, but no readily obvious keyhole. And what's that on the side? Ah... [party.has quin |You glance at Quin and ask him if he knows anything about this kind of lock. Another of Tollus's interests in all things Belharan? Quin takes all of three seconds to study the box before shaking his head. "No, not Belharan — it's a jadelock chest. I've heard about these, they're supposed to be antiques by some place called Macah on the other side of the world. They're more toys than anything, curiosities as opposed to actual security — solve the puzzle and it pops open. Tollus wouldn't have any interest in this kind of stuff, which implies that he isn't personally captaining this ship. Unsurprising, since he's not a nautical man." And can he? The lock, you mean. "Well, that's your job. I'm just here to sneak around and look all dashing." Hmm, he could have just said no; it's not as if he needs to concern himself with saving face in front of you. Jadelocks, eh? Shouldn't be too hard to figure out — this looks like a child's toy more than an actual strongbox. |[party.has cait |"Father used to tell Calla and I about these," Cait pipes up as she studies the chest. "They're jadelock chests, a novelty from Macah in the far east. The lock uses gem shards and sockets to work the mechanism, for a time, they were sold as children's toys. Wouldn't think one would actually be used as a, well, lock." Well, demons aren't usually the smartest thinkers, a few notable exceptions excluded. So if you solved this thing, the lock would just pop open and you could just help yourself to anything inside. "Yep!" |[pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte |You've heard rumors of these whispered in higher circles — jadelock chests, an invention from Macah in the far east. More novelty than anything, they could still be used to secure goods by use of a combination lock of sorts consisting of gem shards and sockets, and a helpful hint or two to remind one of the solution. |Hmm, what can this all mean? It certainly seems like a thoroughly roundabout way to secure a container, but at least it isn't likely to be trapped in the bargain. The gems and sockets must be central to getting it open, though. ] ] ] Attempting to get this thing open might take some time if you're not quick about it, but on the other hand, it's practically certain that there's going to be something inside of here. Like everything else, you won't have the time to come back to this whether you choose to bother with it or not, so will you give it a try?
rows.translation: 你经过床边时，有样东西吸引了你的注意——床脚放着一只箱子，用螺栓固定在地上，显然是为了防止它随海浪摇晃而滑动。在这间原本朴素的船舱里，这算得上是唯一一处真正的奢华：木头上金箔的反光实在诱人得很…… 是的，绝对值得仔细看看。你单膝跪在床边，擦掉箱盖上的灰尘，仔细打量起来；上面有一把锁，却看不到明显的钥匙孔。侧面那是什么？啊…… [party.has quin |你瞥了昆因一眼，问他懂不懂这种锁。这又是托勒斯痴迷贝尔哈兰玩意儿的例子之一？ 昆因花了整整三秒钟端详那只箱子，然后摇了摇头。“不，不是贝尔哈兰的——这是翡翠锁箱。我听说过这东西，据说是世界另一边一个叫马卡的地方的古董。它们更像玩具，是稀罕玩意儿，而不是真正的保险装置——解开谜题它就会自己弹开。托勒斯对这种东西不会有兴趣，也就是说，亲自指挥这艘船的不是他。不奇怪，他本来就不是吃航海这碗饭的。” 那他会开吗？你是指那把锁。 “呃，那是你的活儿。我只是来这儿偷偷摸摸、顺便耍帅的。” 哼，他大可以直接说不会；他又不必在你面前顾及面子。翡翠锁，嗯？应该不难弄明白——这东西看起来更像小孩的玩具，而不是什么真正的保险箱。 |[party.has cait |“父亲以前常跟我和卡拉讲这些，”凯特一边端详着箱子一边插话道。“这叫翡翠锁箱，是远东马卡传来的新奇玩意儿。锁的机关靠宝石碎片和插槽来运作；有一段时间，它们还被当作儿童玩具出售。真想不到居然有人真会拿它当……嗯，锁用。” 好吧，恶魔通常都不是最聪明的思考者，少数几个例外除外。所以只要你解开这东西，锁就会弹开，里面的东西你就能随便拿。 “没错！” |[pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte |你在上层圈子里听过关于这种东西的传闻——翡翠锁箱，远东马卡的一项发明。它与其说是实用之物，不如说是新奇玩意儿，但仍可以用一套由宝石碎片和插槽组成的密码锁来保管财物，还会附上一两条提示帮人记住开法。 |嗯，这到底意味着什么？用这种办法锁一只箱子确实绕得离谱，但至少它不至于还带什么陷阱。不过，宝石和插槽一定是打开它的关键。 ] ] ] 如果你手脚不够快，想打开这东西可能会花上一些时间，但另一方面，这里面几乎肯定有东西。和别的选择一样，不管你决定管还是不管，都不会有时间再回来一趟，那么，你要试试吗？

The gems and sockets must be central to getting it open, though. ] ] ] Attempting to get this thing open might take some time if you're not quick about it, but on the other hand, it's practically certain that there's going to be something inside of here. Like everything else, you won't have the time to come back to this whether you choose to bother with it or not, so will you give it a try? "

rows.original: You shake your head and draw away from the chest. As tempting as it might be, the fiddly locking mechanism looks like it'll eat up far too much of your precious time to figure out, and given how far you're into the belly of the beast it can't be too much longer before the demons up top are all over you. No, you have more important matters to get to.
rows.translation: 你摇了摇头，远离了那个箱子。尽管它看起来非常诱人，但那复杂的锁闭机制似乎会耗费你太多宝贵的时间去研究，而既然你已经深入到了这个“怪物”的内部，上面那些恶魔应该很快就会找到你。不，你还有更重要的事情要处理。
rows.raw: "\n        You shake your head and draw away from the chest. As tempting as it might be, the fiddly locking mechanism looks like it'll eat up far too much of your precious time to figure out, and given how far you're into the belly of the beast it can't be too much longer before the demons up top are all over you. No, you have more important matters to get to."

rows.original: Right. Kneeling down by the chest, you brush the dust off gem chits and sockets alike, and try to make sense of this all...
rows.translation: 没错。你跪在箱子旁边，仔细清理那些宝石碎片和插槽上的灰尘，试图弄清楚这一切……
rows.raw: "\n    Right. Kneeling down by the chest, you brush the dust off gem chits and sockets alike, and try to make sense of this all..."

rows.translation: 珍珠在我东方（Pearl is east of me）。
紫水晶在我东北方（Amethyst is northeast of me）。
琥珀与我相邻（Amber is adjacent to me）。
翡翠与我相邻（Jade is adjacent to me）。
琥珀在我西方（Amber is west of me）。

rows.original: Something clicks within the chest as you slide the last gem into its socket, followed by a loud thump as the mechanisms within disengage. Instinctively, you step back, fearing a trap, but your fears are soon allayed as the spring-loaded lid pops open, revealing the chest's contents. A long knife carved out of bone — the bone of what kind of creature, you have no idea, but it's got to be a pretty special kind of bone to be trusted to hold an edge. In addition to this, there's a small amount of money in ancient coinage — certainly belharan hawks, although heavily tarnished and not quite of the kind you've seen in circulation of late. Still, cash is cash. [party.has einin |"Oh, early payday!" Einin chimes, the little mouse-girl whistling appreciatively as she picks up one of the electrum coins and bites it. "Yeah, these are good. Finders keepers, losers weepers. It's not stealing when you do it from bad guys, right?" She sure is picking up on this adventuring stuff really quickly. "Hey, it's kind of like what I used to do, if only a little bit more socially acceptable. A little bit." ] Without further ado, you pocket the small stash of coins and turn your attention to the long knife. The blade and hilt are slightly yellowed from age, but testing the edge and point with your finger confirms that it's still sharp enough despite how ancient it has to be. Another treasure of the kind Tollus and his ilk are pilfering? Has to be... the blade's kind of long for a knife, yet short for an actual sword; it's in that awkward place where it can't really decide what it wants to be and hence ends up being nothing at all. Kind of like the shortswords that were said to be standard-issue in old Belhar, which were used more for cutting bread than people. [party.has arona |"Oh hey, a seax," Arona says, clomping forward and peering over your shoulder at the thing. "Haven't seen one of those for a while." She knows what they are? "Oh, of course. Not an orc weapon, though — too small for us to be anything but table knives. They're more a shark thing back in the Sailgraves, if you know what I mean. [pc.heightRange 66 78 |These are more their size, if an proper orc actually tried to swing something as piddling as this it'd break off in our hands. |I'd say they're too small for someone your size, but hey, if you want to look silly waving that thing around, be my guest |But then given how tiny you are, I guess it's a good match ]." It doesn't look like an actual offensive thing, anyway. Look at the runes carved into its side. Does she think it's a magician's tool? Arona shrugs. "We've got runes painted on our shields, too. Doesn't make us shamans or wizards or anything." |"Oh hey, a seax," Gweyr says, clomping forward and peering over your shoulder at the thing. "The siorcs out and about the rift sometimes have these." Ah, so it's a local weapon and not something looted from a distant Belharan ruin? "Plenty of ruins about these parts from when the Jotuns and the dragons were at each other, and even more when Belhar was assing about. Totally possible — a whole bunch of peoples in this region used similar designs. Very practical when you can use the same tool for cutting bread or people." It doesn't look like an actual offensive thing, anyway. Look at the runes carved into its side. Does she think it's a magician's tool? "They're not lupine runes or anything, and we make ours of metal, not bone. Maybe a shark would know something about it, but I wouldn't hold my breath; this looks like it's been underwater for ages before being dredged up. Sharks and their ilk don't use metal much because seawater corrodes it really fast, so that's who I'd put my money on." ] You see. Well, you can deal with this later — slamming the chest shut, you prepare to be on your way.
rows.translation: 当最后一颗宝石滑入插槽时，箱子里咔嗒一响，紧接着内部机件脱扣，发出一声闷响。你本能地后退一步，怕是什么陷阱，但弹簧驱动的箱盖很快弹开，露出里面的东西，你的担心也随之消散。一把用骨头雕成的长刀——你完全不知道那是什么生物的骨头，但能被用来做刀刃，想必是相当特别的骨头。除此之外，还有一小笔古币——肯定是贝尔哈兰鹰币，虽然锈蚀得很厉害，也和你近来见过的流通币种不太一样。不过，钱就是钱。 [party.has einin |“哦，提前发工钱啦！”艾宁欢快地说，这个小老鼠女孩赞许地吹了声口哨，拿起一枚琥珀金币咬了一下。“嗯，这些成色不错。谁捡到算谁的，丢了的人哭去吧。从坏人手里拿的不算偷，对吧？” 她学起这套冒险行当来还真是快。 “嘿，这有点像我以前干的活儿，只不过稍微更被社会接受一点。就一点。” ] 不再多说，你把那一小堆金币揣进口袋，然后把注意力转向那把长刀。刀身和刀柄因年深日久微微发黄，但用手指试了试刃口和刀尖，可以确认它尽管古老，却依然足够锋利。又是一件托勒斯之流正在偷运的宝物？肯定是……这刀身作为刀来说有点长，作为真正的剑又太短；正处在那种尴尬的尺寸上，说不清自己到底是什么，结果什么也不是。有点像据说在旧贝尔哈作为制式装备的短剑——那些剑更多是用来切面包，而不是砍人的。 [party.has arona |“哦嘿，一把短刀，”阿罗娜说着，咚咚地走上前，从你肩后探头看那东西。“好久没见过这种玩意儿了。” 她知道那是什么？ “哦，当然知道。不过那不是兽人的武器——对我们来说太小了，顶多算餐刀。在赛尔格雷夫斯那边，这更多是鲨鱼人的东西，你懂我的意思吧。[pc.heightRange 66 78 |这些更合它们的尺寸；要是真有个像样的兽人抡起这么细气的东西，它在我们手里就得折断。 |我会说以你的个头用这个太小了，不过嘛，你要是想拿着那玩意儿挥来挥去显得滑稽，随你便。 |不过话说回来，你这么小个子，我看倒也般配。 ]。” 反正它看着也不像真正的攻击性武器。看看侧面刻的符文。她觉得这是法师的工具吗？ 阿罗娜耸了耸肩。“我们的盾牌上也画着符文。这并不代表我们是萨满或巫师什么的。” |“哦嘿，一把短刀，”格维尔说着，咚咚地走上前，从你肩后探头看那东西。“裂谷附近出没的鲨人有时会带这种刀。” 哦，那么这是本地武器，而不是从遥远的贝尔哈兰废墟里抢来的？ “这一带遗迹多得是，都是当年约顿人和巨龙互相厮杀时留下的，贝尔哈瞎折腾那会儿留下的更多。完全有可能——这个地区一大堆民族都用过类似的设计。既能切面包又能砍人，一把工具两用，实用得很。” 反正它看着也不像真正的攻击性武器。看看侧面刻的符文。她觉得这是法师的工具吗？ “那不是什么狼族的符文之类的东西，而且我们的东西是金属做的，不是骨头。也许鲨人会知道点什么，不过我可不抱希望；这东西看着像是在水底待了不知多少年才被捞上来的。鲨鱼那一类不太用金属，因为海水腐蚀金属特别快，所以我赌是它们。” ] 原来如此。好吧，这事可以以后再说——你啪地把箱子关上，准备继续上路。

rows.original: You rub your temples and sigh. The chest and gems are right there in front of you, but the clues just make no sense to you whatsoever. Time's short, and you've wasted enough of it trying to figure this thing out — best to cut your losses before you dig yourself even deeper into this hole.
rows.translation: 你揉了揉太阳穴，叹了口气。那些宝箱和宝石就摆在眼前，但这些线索却完全让你摸不着头脑。时间不多了，你已经浪费了太多时间试图弄清楚这些事情——最好及时止损，免得让自己陷入更深的困境。
rows.raw: "You rub your temples and sigh. The chest and gems are right there in front of you, but the clues just make no sense to you whatsoever. Time's short, and you've wasted enough of it trying to figure this thing out — best to cut your losses before you dig yourself even deeper into this hole."

rows.original: As you eye the well-stocked liquor cabinet on one side of the cabin, Gweyr raises an eyebrow at you as if to say, "really?"
rows.translation: 当你打量着船舱一侧那只储备充足的酒柜时，格维尔朝你挑了挑眉毛，仿佛在说：“真的吗？”
rows.raw: 'As you eye the well-stocked liquor cabinet on one side of the cabin, Gweyr raises an eyebrow at you as if to say, "really?"'

rows.original: Before you can reply, though, Quin's already gotten one step ahead of you and is right up against the wooden cabinet, gazing longingly at the displayed bottles through the glass with his face pressed up straight against the panes. It's only with considerable force of will that the bunny-man pulls himself away, takes out his thieves' tools and gets to work. "Don't you worry," he says with a dry, almost bitter laugh. "Stuff like this is art, and art deserves to be free. I'll have this open in no time." Itchy fingers again, huh? Well, it's not going to cost you anything, since he's the one acting on his own initiative... It takes only a blink of an eye for Quin to have the liquor cabinet open, and the scent of stale air, wood, and finely aged alcohol hits your nose like a hammer. "Phew," Quin says, taking an appreciative whiff as he puts his tools away. "It's a pity that all these pretty bottles should be cooped up in here — I'm sure they want to be shared." Oh, of course they do... Quin isn't listening to you, though, and is already grabbing bottles out of the cabinet and stowing them away amongst his possessions. With nothing for it, you do the same, grabbing as much as you can — the cabinet is so full that even if you took all you can carry, there'll be more than enough left over to avoid drawing suspicion, right? Gweyr sighs and chuckles as she watches the both of you go at it. "Oh, you kids. You really remind me of Garth when he was younger." Why, was he a kleptomaniac too? "I took him in knowing he was a thief who'd stolen from his own people and gotten kicked out for it. While I winnowed the worst tendencies out of him, his instincts nevertheless helped in some situations, and so I let him use them then." The old wolfess gives Quin a sidelong glance. "I'm just saying, you need to train that bunny of yours better, because he's still got a couple of vices in him."
rows.translation: 然而，还没等你回答，昆因就已经抢先一步，整个人贴在那只木柜上，脸紧贴着玻璃，痴痴地望着里面陈列的酒瓶。这位兔子人费了好大劲才凭意志力把自己拉回来，掏出他的盗贼工具开始干活。 “别担心，”他带着一声干涩、近乎苦涩的笑说道。“这种东西就是艺术，而艺术理应自由。我马上就能打开它。” 老毛病又犯了，是吧？好吧，反正你也不用付出什么代价，毕竟是他自己主动动手的…… 只一眨眼的工夫，昆因就把酒柜打开了，陈腐的空气、木头和醇香老酒的气味像一记重锤砸在你鼻子上。 “呼，”昆因一边嗅了嗅，一脸享受地把工具收起来，一边说道。“可惜了，这些漂亮的瓶子全被关在这儿——我敢说它们肯定想被人分享。” 哦，它们当然想……不过昆因根本没在听你说话，他已经开始从柜子里往外掏瓶子，往自己的东西里塞。你也没别的办法，只好跟着照做，能拿多少拿多少——柜子里东西太多了，就算你把能带的全都带走，剩下的也足够多，不至于惹人起疑，对吧？ 格维尔看着你们俩忙活，叹着气笑了。“哦，你们这些孩子。你们真让我想起加斯年轻的时候。” 怎么，他也有偷东西的毛病？ “我收留他的时候就知道他是个贼，偷了自己族人的东西，还因此被赶了出来。我把他身上最坏的毛病磨掉了不少，但有些时候他的本能还是派得上用场，所以那些时候我就让他用。”老女狼斜眼看了昆因一眼。“我只是想说，你那只兔子得好好调教调教，因为他身上还有几样恶习。”

rows.original:
Yes, really, and you're pretty sure you can do it, too, what with your background as a thief.

        "Hmph. Let's see if you're as good as Garth was."
        
        Well, you'll take that as a challenge, then. Inspecting the cabinet further, you tap on the glass with a finger — when you look closer at the panels, you see little bronze wires crisscrossed within them; was this made in Tychris? Either way, given how the glass has been reinforced, cutting it isn't going to work, or at least not without creating enough of a commotion that would bring the demons down on you. Time to see to the lock, then.
        
        It's not as bad as it could have been — the mechanism is simple enough, and with a bit of fiddling the bar holding the cabinet closed lifts and the scent of stale air, wood, and finely aged alcohol hits your nose like a hammer. You cough, fan the air in front of your face, and turn to Gweyr with a triumphant [pc.isDK|smirk|smile] on your face.
        
        "Not bad. You did it in about half the time Garth would've."
        
        You just chuckle at that, turning to the now-open cabinet and starting to pilfer its contents. Hey, she's the one who married a thief knowing full well what he was. Here's a perfectly good bottle of mirrorwine, why doesn't she have one? Courtesy of you and the ship's captain, whoever they may be.
        
        "Haven't drank very much since I was banished, and not because I can't get my hands on any. Pass."
        
        Hey, more for you. You scour the liquor cabinet quickly, picking out the bottles that stand out the most to you at a glance, then turn your attention back to the rest of the room. It's cold outside, and you'll need to warm up...
rows.translation:
是的，真的，而且你很确定自己也做得到，毕竟你有当过小偷的底子。

        “哼。让我们看看你有没有加斯那么厉害。”
        
        好吧，那你就把这当成挑战。你进一步检查柜子，用手指敲了敲玻璃——凑近看面板，你会发现里面交错着细细的青铜丝；这是提克里斯造的吗？不管怎样，玻璃既然加固过，割开是行不通的，至少免不了弄出足够大的动静，把恶魔们引下来。那就来看锁吧。
        
        情况还不算太糟——机关相当简单，摆弄了几下，卡住柜门的横杆就抬了起来，陈腐的空气、木头和醇香老酒的气味像一记重锤砸在你鼻子上。你咳了一声，扇了扇面前的空气，带着一脸胜利的[pc.isDK|坏笑|笑容]转向格维尔。
        
        “不赖。你用的时间差不多只有加斯的一半。”
        
        你只是笑了笑，转向已经打开的柜子，开始翻里面的东西。嘿，毕竟她当年明知那男人是个贼还嫁给了他。这儿有一瓶上好的镜酒，她怎么不来一瓶？算你和这艘船船长请客——不管船长是谁。
        
        “自从被流放以后我就没怎么喝过酒，倒不是弄不到酒。不了。”
        
        嘿，那你就多喝点。你快速翻遍酒柜，一眼挑出那些最显眼的瓶子，然后把注意力转回房间的其他地方。外面很冷，你需要暖和一下……
