"There'll be ghosts, I tell you, there can't not be. Get ready!" |Quintillus sniffs in disdain as he surveys the bodies and the pestilent mold growing on the old bones. "Foul. Might have been something Tollus himself came up with, were he around then. It's certainly similar to ideas he's had and merely didn't have the strength to put into action back then. Now... who can say?" |"This is the work of Wraiths, or at least those who followed them," Atugia mumbles as she surveys the dead. "They always liked their victims to die in great pain... or great arousal. They craved emotion...fed upon it." You don't ask how she knows. |"I heard of this happening to other hives sometimes. Fungal infections that spoiled honey and ate away at wax, caused walls to fall..." Azyrran shakes her head slowly. "Such diseases are harder on ant-people — I forget their proper name — but it affecting people other than insect-folk is a first for me." It doesn't. Or at least, usually doesn't... you think. Right now, you're reconsidering your stance, even if Hethia says that you and your companions should be impervious to a weapon that was very specifically keyed to destroy a singular subset of people. ] As you step over the bodies and press on, you come to a fork in the path, dominated by a fountain that takes up most of the junction. Stepping forward, perhaps driven by morbid curiosity, Ryn peers over the rim into the fountain's bowl, and swallows hard. Bones upon bones upon bones are piled up within, mixed in with bits of decaying plant matter and thickly carpeted with more of that spongy, scabby fungal growth. Ryn hurriedly covers her mouth at the sight and stench coming up from the mess — while all the flesh has rotted away long ago, the mold raises an overpoweringly putrid stink — and turns away. "Oh no..." Within the fountain lies a single skeleton, exquisitely adorned with ornaments of gold and silver, adorned with a headdress fashioned from what looks to be petrified wood — it's hard to be sure in the gloom. The orange mold and pinhead fungus have been unable to consume the metal or tarnish the gold, and it's clear that this was someone who was fairly prominent in life. The man — at least, you think it's a man based on the bone structure — lies on his side, having succumbed to this virulence inside the fountain. Was he trying to hide? Fell in and was unable to get out? Who knows? "Looks like it's a dead end, [pc.name]," Ryn says as Elthara swings her conjured light this way and that to search the ruined section of hallway. "Both junctions are blocked with rubble. Maybe we should investigate the walls closer, see if there's a collapsed passageway we missed — " '

rows.original: Her words are cut short by a gust of frigid wind, strong enough to buffet you all and send Ryn's cloak billowing. Clearly unnatural this far beneath the earth, it has you with your [pc.weapon] out and at the ready as Elthara's conjured light reveals a specter that wasn't there a moment ago. In life, he would've been a tall boreal elf, perhaps seven feet if he were standing at full height; his white linen shift rests loosely upon him in tatters, gold and silver adorning his wrists and ankles while a crown of leaves and twigs rests upon his brow, complete with carved wooden antlers. But there's little of him that remains pale to merit the name of pale elf. Clods of orange fungus infest the specter's skin like scabs from multiple wounds, spreading threads upon what parts of his body remain uncovered. The seething mass bursts with vileness and has claimed much of his twisted body; upon forcing yourself to gaze upon the specter directly, you realize that it's more than that. The druid's body is misshapen, giving the impression of so much flesh caught between forms; rampant growth unable to decide between the traditionally robust masculine or feminine figures of the boreal elves, or even the slighter figures of the half-sexed, resulting in something caught between all three. Then, of course, there's the massive, oversized dick that hangs between his legs and tents his tattered shift, and beneath that and a pair of oversized testicles, just a glimpse of a fat, gushing pussy that constantly dribbles pustulent fluids of arousal between his thighs. [etheryn.highConfidence |Ryn's eyes widen for a moment, and then her gaze hardens and she squares her shoulders. Still, she backs away warily from the revenant, holding up her hands with palms turned out. "We mean you no harm, whoever you are. Can you speak?" A terrible, hacking cough sounds from the druidic specter, spores spewing from his lips with each pained wheeze. "Pilgrims? You should not be here! Hurry, flee, flee before — " something snaps behind the spirit's gaze, a moment of cold, bitter realization before he refocuses his empty eyes on Ryn. "Synneva? No, it can't be. Synneva's... dead." "I'm not Synneva," Ryn says, continuing to back away from the ghostly druid's advance. "She rests peacefully now." "Peace? No. There was no peace for her up till the moment of her death. We know... we know what happens to those who are locked up in that... that place." The specter shudders, be it in agony of the body or the pain of remembrance. "If you can't be Synneva, then... that blood. That... that presence...!" It's not quite the banshee wail that you remember Synneva was capable of from below the palace of ice, but this is far more primal. Seeing things take a turn for the worse, Ryn raises her hands to make one final plea to the apparition, but he's already upon her. Ghostly, bark-encased fists dripping with corruptive fungus reach for Ryn's throat as the wight who can only be Archdruid Vaeril Xadaron seeks to throttle her out of existence. "You dare come here, Atheldred?" the druidic haunt roars, his voice howling over with the rage and sorrow of a winter storm. "You dare come here after what you did to Synneva! What you did to us all!" This is insane. Ryn's resemblance to her grandmother isn't that obvious... well, on the other hand, it's clear that the archdruid's specter is relying on senses other than mere sight and touch alone. As you rush to help her, Etheryn has already drawn her bow and nocked an arrow, aiming straight for the druid's scabbed-over chest. The icy arrow whistles along its path, entering Vaeril from the front and leaving through the back in a wet splotch of stinking ectoplasm. As the archdruid moves to close his bark-encrusted fists about Ryn's throat, you run him through with your [pc.weapon] — an act that takes a chunk of ectoplasm out of the haunt and leaves speckles of frost on your weapon. While it doesn't seem to have damaged him terribly much, it's enough of a distraction for Ryn to disengage and nock another arrow. "Looks like talking isn't going to calm him down, and I don't think beating him down inasmuch as you can do that to a ghost will, either." "Time for a quick exorcism, then." Elthara backs you up with a brilliant bolt of whitefire that strikes the archdruid's flank, and the twisted specter lets out another bloodcurdling scream; he raises his bark-encrusted arms to shield himself, staggering back under the impact while Elthara moves to interpose herself between Ryn and the archdruid. "Step back, [etheryn.crowned |my queen |lady regent ]!" Etheryn is already moving, taking aim while [var0 |Elthara, [comp2.name] |Elthara ] and you defend her from Vaeril's clawing, dripping grasp. |Ryn claps her hands over her mouth to stifle the gasp she knows is coming, but that doesn't matter to the wight, who has noticed her. "Synneva? No, it can't be. Synneva's... dead." The specter shudders, be it in agony of the body or the pain of remembrance. "Then... that blood. That... that presence...!" It's not quite the banshee wail that you remember Synneva was capable of from below the palace of ice, but this is far more primal. Ryn screams and scrambles away, raising her hands to ward off the apparition, but he's already upon her; ghostly, bark-encased fists dripping with corruptive fungus reach for Ryn's throat as the wight who can only be Archdruid Vaeril Xadaron seeks to throttle her out of existence. "You dare come here, Atheldred?" the druidic haunt roars, his voice howling over with the rage and sorrow of a winter storm. "You dare come here after what you did to Synneva! What you did to us all!" This is insane. Ryn's resemblance to her grandmother isn't that obvious... well, on the other hand, it's clear that the archdruid's specter is relying on senses other than mere sight and touch alone. As you rush to help her, Etheryn valiantly pulls at the fingers clawing at her throat, her eyes wide in terror and teeth gritted in desperation. Vaeril's words are cut short by you running him through with your [pc.weapon] — an act that takes a chunk of ectoplasm out of the haunt and leaves speckles of frost on your weapon. While it doesn't seem to have damaged him terribly much, it's enough of a distraction for Ryn to claw her way out of his grasp. Elthara backs you up with a brilliant bolt of whitefire that strikes the archdruid's flank, and the twisted specter lets out another bloodcurdling scream; he raises his bark-encrusted arms to shield himself, staggering back under the impact. "Get away, [etheryn.crowned |my queen |lady regent ]!" Etheryn is already moving, scrambling to her feet with [etheryn.weapon] in one hand, forcing her fear down and dodging out of the way as the ghost lunges for her throat again. ] "This is your fault! Your fault! You and your human goddess created this... this thing to wipe us out, us who would not bend the knee! Did you come to see us die? Is that — " The sting of failure, the resentment over seeing one martyred, the hatred directed at a tyrant — and of course, the bodily agony of Vaeril's dying moments as the fungal infestation consumed the druids and twisted their bodies with uncontrolled, cancerous growth. All this and more form the pain and rage that animates this haunt, the tip of a spear aimed at the heart of the var Ridell line. "Treachery! Murder! I always knew that getting too intimate with those Belharans would be our undoing, Atheldred var Ridell. Now you've begun worshipping their gods as well, and bring one of their priestesses here? Treachery by the queen against her own people and the Old Wyld! I... I may have failed, but I was never traitorous!" Having composed herself, Ryn nocks an arrow and aims it at the misshapen, hermaphroditic specter charging for her. "Oh, grandmother... please let this be the last piece you've left for me to pick up." It's a fight!
rows.translation: 她的话语被一阵刺骨的寒风打断了——那股风力之大，足以让所有人都感到不适，也让瑞恩的斗篷剧烈地飘动起来。在地下这么深的地方，这样的自然现象显然很不寻常 [pc.weapon] 就在这时，艾尔萨拉召唤出的光芒揭示出了一个方才还不存在的幽灵。在现实生活中，他应该会是一个高大的极北精灵——如果他完全站直的话，身高或许会有七英尺；他穿着一件破烂的白色亚麻长袍，手腕和足部踝上佩戴着金银饰品，额头上还戴着一顶由树叶和细枝编成的冠冕，上面甚至还有雕刻好的木制鹿角。 但是，他身上几乎没有任何地方还能被称为“苍白精灵”了。橙色的真菌团块像多处伤口结成的痂一样覆盖在他的皮肤上，那些未被遮盖的身体部位上也布满了这些菌丝。这些充满恶意的菌团已经侵蚀了他那扭曲的身体的大部分；当你强迫自己直视这个幽灵时，你会发现，实际情况比这还要糟糕。这位德鲁伊的身体形态很不规则，看起来仿佛有大量的肉体被强行塞进了不同的身体结构中；这种异常的生长使得他的身体既无法呈现出极北精灵传统上那种强壮的男性化或女性化特征，也无法形成半性别的那种更为纤细的身形，最终形成了介于三者之间的某种奇怪形态。 当然，还有那根巨大得离谱的阴茎，它悬挂在他的两腿之间，将他那破烂的内裤撑得变形；而在它的下方，是一对巨大的睾丸……偶尔还能隐约看到那片肥厚的阴部，那里不断有脓状的液体渗出，这些液体代表着他的性兴奋状态。 [etheryn.highConfidence |瑞恩的眼睛瞬间睁得大大的，但很快她的目光就变得坚定起来，双肩也挺得笔直。尽管如此，她还是小心翼翼地后退着，远离那个亡魂，同时将双手举起来，手掌朝外。“无论你是谁，我们都没有恶意。你能说话吗？”那个德鲁伊幽灵发出了一声可怕的、剧烈的咳嗽，每次痛苦地喘息时，都有孢子从他的嘴唇中喷出。“朝圣者们？你们不应该在这里！快逃吧，赶紧离开这里……”就在幽灵说话的瞬间，背后发生了什么，他瞬间意识到了什么，随后又将那空洞的目光重新投向了瑞恩。辛妮瓦？不，不可能。辛妮瓦的…… 死亡我不是辛妮瓦，”瑞恩边说边继续后退，躲避着那个幽灵般的女德鲁伊的逼近。“她现在已经安息了。”“安息？不。在她死去的那一刻之前，她从未得到过安宁。我们知道……我们知道那些被关在那个……那个地方的人会遭遇什么。地点那个幽灵在颤抖，无论是身体上的痛苦，还是回忆带来的伤痛。‘如果你无法成为辛妮瓦，那么……那鲜血……那个存在感……！”这声音虽然远没有你记忆中辛妮瓦在冰宫下发出的那种凄厉哀嚎，但却更加原始、更加令人毛骨悚然。看到局势正在恶化，瑞恩举起双手，向这个幽灵发出最后的恳求——但那个怪物已经扑到了她身上。那些被腐朽真菌覆盖的、仿佛由骨爪构成的拳头，如幽灵般伸向瑞恩的喉咙——这个只能被认定为大德鲁伊瓦瑞尔·萨达伦的怪物，正试图将她扼杀在空气中。“你竟敢来到这里，阿瑟德雷德？那片德鲁伊的领地中回荡着怒吼声，他的声音中充满了冬季风暴般的愤怒与悲伤。“你敢在你对辛妮瓦做了那些事之后，你还敢来到这里！你对我们所有人都做出了伤害！”这太荒谬了。瑞恩和她祖母长得太像了，这简直那个显而易见……不过，另一方面也可以看出，这位大德鲁伊的幽灵所依赖的感知手段显然不仅仅是视觉和触觉而已。当你冲过去想要帮助她时，伊瑟琳已经拔出了弓，搭上了一支箭，直接瞄准了那位德鲁伊那结满疤痕的胸膛。那支冰冷的箭呼啸着划过轨迹，从前方刺入瓦瑞尔的身体，然后从后方穿出，留下一滩散发着恶臭的异质物质。当那位大德鲁伊挥动布满树皮的手掌，试图扼住瑞恩的喉咙时，你一枪刺穿了他的身体。 rows.raw: " Her words are cut short by a gust of frigid wind, strong enough to buffet you all and send Ryn's cloak billowing. Clearly unnatural this far beneath the earth, it has you with your [pc.weapon] out and at the ready as Elthara's conjured light reveals a specter that wasn't there a moment ago. In life, he would've been a tall boreal elf, perhaps seven feet if he were standing at full height; his white linen shift rests loosely upon him in tatters, gold and silver adorning his wrists and ankles while a crown of leaves and twigs rests upon his brow, complete with carved wooden antlers. But there's little of him that remains pale to merit the name of pale elf. Clods of orange fungus infest the specter's skin like scabs from multiple wounds, spreading threads upon what parts of his body remain uncovered. The seething mass bursts with vileness and has claimed much of his twisted body; upon forcing yourself to gaze upon the specter directly, you realize that it's more than that. The druid's body is misshapen, giving the impression of so much flesh caught between forms; rampant growth unable to decide between the traditionally robust masculine or feminine figures of the boreal elves, or even the slighter figures of the half-sexed, resulting in something caught between all three. Then, of course, there's the massive, oversized dick that hangs between his legs and tents his tattered shift, and beneath that and a pair of oversized testicles, just a glimpse of a fat, gushing pussy that constantly dribbles pustulent fluids of arousal between his thighs. [etheryn.highConfidence |Ryn's eyes widen for a moment, and then her gaze hardens and she squares her shoulders. Still, she backs away warily from the revenant, holding up her hands with palms turned out. "We mean you no harm, whoever you are. Can you speak?" A terrible, hacking cough sounds from the druidic specter, spores spewing from his lips with each pained wheeze. "Pilgrims? You should not be here! Hurry, flee, flee before — " something snaps behind the spirit's gaze, a moment of cold, bitter realization before he refocuses his empty eyes on Ryn. "Synneva? No, it can't be. Synneva's... dead." "I'm not Synneva," Ryn says, continuing to back away from the ghostly druid's advance. "She rests peacefully now." "Peace? No. There was no peace for her up till the moment of her death. We know... we know what happens to those who are locked up in that... that place." The specter shudders, be it in agony of the body or the pain of remembrance. "If you can't be Synneva, then... that blood. That... that presence...!" It's not quite the banshee wail that you remember Synneva was capable of from below the palace of ice, but this is far more primal. Seeing things take a turn for the worse, Ryn raises her hands to make one final plea to the apparition, but he's already upon her. Ghostly, bark-encased fists dripping with corruptive fungus reach for Ryn's throat as the wight who can only be Archdruid Vaeril Xadaron seeks to throttle her out of existence. "You dare come here, Atheldred?" the druidic haunt roars, his voice howling over with the rage and sorrow of a winter storm. "You dare come here after what you did to Synneva! What you did to us all!" This is insane. Ryn's resemblance to her grandmother isn't that obvious... well, on the other hand, it's clear that the archdruid's specter is relying on senses other than mere sight and touch alone. As you rush to help her, Etheryn has already drawn her bow and nocked an arrow, aiming straight for the druid's scabbed-over chest. As the archdruid moves to close his bark-encrusted fists about Ryn's throat, you run him through with your [pc.weapon] — an act that takes a chunk of ectoplasm out of the haunt and leaves speckles of frost on your weapon. Having composed herself, Ryn nocks an arrow and aims it at the misshapen, hermaphroditic specter charging for her. "Oh, grandmother... please let this be the last piece you've left for me to pick up." It's a fight! "

The mere thought of being unable to avenge himself upon the var Ridell lineage is so damning for Vaeril that for a moment, you wonder if he's going to be able to resist your banishment through sheer force of will. He certainly isn't going to depart without a fight, but by and large, it looks to be a fight that the archdruid is oh-so-painfully losing. But at last, it happens all at once; the archdruid's mutated body — if it can even be called that — loses consistency under your banishment, and the tortured spirit forcibly shunted into whatever afterlife awaits him. Probably a better one than being kept here, at any rate. Seeing Vaeril's tortured departure, Elthara quickly mumbles a prayer to her goddess under her breath. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I- ]I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all." But there's no one to reply — even the foul-smelling ectoplasm that the specter's left behind is dissolving into chill mist, burned away by your spell while both Ryn and Elthara mouth prayers to their goddess. Several moments later, it was as if he were never there, the spirit finally granted rest by. |Unable to put up any more of a fight, Vaeril's revenant tumbles against the fountain's rim, sending several ancient bones — most likely his bones — clattering across the mold-carpeted floor. Even at this point, the smouldering hatred with which he regards Ryn as she steps forward with arrow nocked and bowstring drawn is palpable. "So this is how it ends," he chokes out. The outline of his translucent form is already beginning to waver, his dying emotions stubbornly keeping him tethered to the world for a few more words. "New gods kill off the old, one order replaces another and assumes its predecessor's mantle." "It ended long ago, ghost," Elthara spits, digging the point of her scythe into Vaeril's back. "To their credit, as frustrated as I can be with them sometimes, at least your descendants aren't half as stiff-necked as you." [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"I-I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all. No one wanted any of this, but... but as wonderful as it is, love can make us do terrible things." |"Was it not your order that once preached about the inevitability of death and rebirth," Ryn replies, visibly mustering the will to speak calmly to this spectral abomination who was once an elf. "The Godswar was unprecedented, and in times as strange as those, even gods may die..." |"The way your descendants tell it, you allowed your wealth and influence to turn you lax and forgetful of your basic duties," Ryn says, keeping herself tight-lipped. "A story that I'm intimately familiar with. It's time for this chapter of our history to be closed, and a better one opened. Ghosts should remain in the past, where they belong; let us move on from your mistakes." ] With that, Ryn looses an icy arrow straight into the archdruid's neck, driving its head down through the putrid fungus coating his skin and into what would have been his spine. Vaeril gathers his breath for a final wight's wail — but it never comes, his strength draining in a gurgle followed by a soft sigh as he crashes into the floor, his strength finally giving out. As all of you watch, the specter slowly starts dissolving into foul-smelling ectoplasm and mist, draining into the cracks between the stones. The grim task done, Ryn steps back while Elthara mumbles a quick prayer to Lumia. The priestess swings her scythe down at the remains, and the whitefire trailing from its point engulfs the remaining ectoplasm, engulfing the ghostly remains in the sun's radiance, evaporating into a chill mist that dissipates in the still air. ] "It is over?" Ryn asks quietly. "That's how it works, right? He was the archdruid, so surely any other spirits are now freed, aren't they?" Her words echo in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. You have to get out of here now, or you'll be crushed! Wasting no time, you direct your party back the way you came, eyes trained forward, legs pumping for the exit you hope will still be there. Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled, bark-encased root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions; the collapse grows increasingly worse as large blocks of stone come crashing down from the darkness above, smashing long-dead corpses to pieces and by some small providence of Tira's fortune not hitting any of you during their descent. Dust and spores fill the air as something groans deep within the earth, and then the floor gives out from under you. One moment you're double-timing it to the exit, the next you're tumbling head over heels as plant matter and ancient bricks plummet by your side; [pc.hasWings |you beat your wings in a bid to right yourself, but the sudden sharpness of the fall spikes a wrenching sensation in your joints as you realize you've sprained your wing trying to slow your fall |brief flashes of being dashed to pieces on the ground below invade your mind unbidden, but you force them away ]. It can't have been more than the blink of an eye, but it feels like forever; eventually, though, the impact comes, and it's much lighter than you feared. A large mushroom cushions your fall, stalk and cap crumbling under the weight of your impact and oozing foul liquid everywhere; as noisome as it is, the thing probably saved your life. Slowly, the quaking comes to a stop, and you carefully get back to your feet — just where are you, now?

] 就这样结束了？”瑞恩轻声问道，“事情就是这样的吧？他可是大德鲁伊，那么其他所有的灵魂应该也都得到了解放，对吧？”她的声音在黑暗中回荡，随后，地底下传来了阵阵呻吟声和嘎吱声，那些灰尘和碎石从天花板上掉落下来，纷纷落在他们身上。不，那种重型、压抑的气氛并没有消散，只是那种橙棕色的光线开始从灰浆的裂缝中渗出来，随着大理石砖块不断向内挤压，光线变得越来越明亮；片刻之后，地面开始震动某个东西岩石被穿透了，开始松动、脱落。你必须立刻离开这里，否则就会被压碎！你毫不浪费时间，带领团队沿着来时的路返回，目光紧紧盯着前方，双腿拼命地奔跑，希望能找到仍然存在的出口。当她附近的墙壁开始向内坍塌，一根被树皮包裹着的扭曲根茎突然破土而出，将碎裂的砖石抛向四面八方时，瑞恩发出了惊叫声。随着上方黑暗中巨石纷纷坠落，情况愈发糟糕——那些重型的石块将早已死去的尸体砸得粉碎，而幸运的是，在它们坠落的过程中，没有一块石头砸中在场的任何人。 尘土与孢子弥漫在空气中，地底深处传来某种沉闷的声响，紧接着地面开始在你足部下坍塌。前一刻你还在拼命往出口跑去，下一刻，植物残骸和古老的砖块就从你身边坠落下来，你整个人也被抛向了空中，开始滚来滚去 [pc.hasWings |你拼命拍打翅膀试图调整自己的姿势，但坠落的冲击力实在太大了，你的关节因此承受了巨大的压力，当你意识到自己在试图减缓坠落速度时扭伤了翅膀时，那种剧烈的疼痛让你感到无比难受。 |那些关于自己被摔得粉身碎骨的场景不由自主地浮现在你的脑海中，但你强行将它们赶走了。 ]那段时间短得仿佛只是眨眼之间，但却感觉像过了漫长的一世；不过最终，冲击力还是到来了，而它其实比你想象的要轻得多。一朵巨大的蘑菇缓冲了你坠落的冲击，它的菌柄和菌盖在你的重量作用下纷纷碎裂，同时渗出了难闻的液体；尽管这种液体非常刺鼻，但它很可能救了你的命。渐渐地，身体的颤抖停止了，你小心翼翼地站了起来——不过现在，你究竟身处何处呢？
rows.raw: " [var0 |"No... no...!" The mere thought of being unable to avenge himself upon the var Ridell lineage is so damning for Vaeril that for a moment, you wonder if he's going to be able to resist your banishment through sheer force of will. He certainly isn't going to depart without a fight, but by and large, it looks to be a fight that the archdruid is oh-so-painfully losing. But at last, it happens all at once; the archdruid's mutated body — if it can even be called that — loses consistency under your banishment, and the tortured spirit forcibly shunted into whatever afterlife awaits him. Probably a better one than being kept here, at any rate. Seeing Vaeril's tortured departure, Elthara quickly mumbles a prayer to her goddess under her breath. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I- ]I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all." But there's no one to reply — even the foul-smelling ectoplasm that the specter's left behind is dissolving into chill mist, burned away by your spell while both Ryn and Elthara mouth prayers to their goddess. Several moments later, it was as if he were never there, the spirit finally granted rest by. |Unable to put up any more of a fight, Vaeril's revenant tumbles against the fountain's rim, sending several ancient bones — most likely his bones — clattering across the mold-carpeted floor. Even at this point, the smouldering hatred with which he regards Ryn as she steps forward with arrow nocked and bowstring drawn is palpable. "So this is how it ends," he chokes out. The outline of his translucent form is already beginning to waver, his dying emotions stubbornly keeping him tethered to the world for a few more words. "New gods kill off the old, one order replaces another and assumes its predecessor's mantle." "It ended long ago, ghost," Elthara spits, digging the point of her scythe into Vaeril's back. "To their credit, as frustrated as I can be with them sometimes, at least your descendants aren't half as stiff-necked as you." [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"I-I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all. No one wanted any of this, but... but as wonderful as it is, love can make us do terrible things." |"Was it not your order that once preached about the inevitability of death and rebirth," Ryn replies, visibly mustering the will to speak calmly to this spectral abomination who was once an elf. "The Godswar was unprecedented, and in times as strange as those, even gods may die..." |"The way your descendants tell it, you allowed your wealth and influence to turn you lax and forgetful of your basic duties," Ryn says, keeping herself tight-lipped. "A story that I'm intimately familiar with. It's time for this chapter of our history to be closed, and a better one opened. Ghosts should remain in the past, where they belong; let us move on from your mistakes." ] With that, Ryn looses an icy arrow straight into the archdruid's neck, driving its head down through the putrid fungus coating his skin and into what would have been his spine. Vaeril gathers his breath for a final wight's wail — but it never comes, his strength draining in a gurgle followed by a soft sigh as he crashes into the floor, his strength finally giving out. As all of you watch, the specter slowly starts dissolving into foul-smelling ectoplasm and mist, draining into the cracks between the stones. The grim task done, Ryn steps back while Elthara mumbles a quick prayer to Lumia. The priestess swings her scythe down at the remains, and the whitefire trailing from its point engulfs the remaining ectoplasm, engulfing the ghostly remains in the sun's radiance, evaporating into a chill mist that dissipates in the still air. ] "It is over?" Ryn asks quietly. "That's how it works, right? He was the archdruid, so surely any other spirits are now freed, aren't they?" Her words echo in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. You have to get out of here now, or you'll be crushed! Wasting no time, you direct your party back the way you came, eyes trained forward, legs pumping for the exit you hope will still be there. Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled, bark-encased root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions; the collapse grows increasingly worse as large blocks of stone come crashing down from the darkness above, smashing long-dead corpses to pieces and by some small providence of Tira's fortune not hitting any of you during their descent. Dust and spores fill the air as something groans deep within the earth, and then the floor gives out from under you. One moment you're double-timing it to the exit, the next you're tumbling head over heels as plant matter and ancient bricks plummet by your side; [pc.hasWings |you beat your wings in a bid to right yourself, but the sudden sharpness of the fall spikes a wrenching sensation in your joints as you realize you've sprained your wing trying to slow your fall |brief flashes of being dashed to pieces on the ground below invade your mind unbidden, but you force them away ]. It can't have been more than the blink of an eye, but it feels like forever; eventually, though, the impact comes, and it's much lighter than you feared. A large mushroom cushions your fall, stalk and cap crumbling under the weight of your impact and oozing foul liquid everywhere; as noisome as it is, the thing probably saved your life. Slowly, the quaking comes to a stop, and you carefully get back to your feet — just where are you, now? "

rows.original: Things aren't going well — Elthara sends another bolt of whitefire straight for Vaeril but the archdruid bats it away, bark and fungus blackening upon the spell's impact. The maddened haunt only has eyes for Ryn, the successor of his hated bloodline, traitors of everything he believed in, and the rage of his dying moments fuels an inhuman strength. As he picks up a collapsed Ryn from the ground and holds her in contempt, the expression on his face is akin to that of a hound who, finally having caught his prey, has no idea what to do with it. You're not about to let that happen — [pc.isDK |no one fucks with Ryn except you |you weren't named Champion of Frost for nothing! If you can put down Alissa, you can put down a decrepit old man who doesn't know he's dead ]! Aiming for the archdruid's neck, you swing heavily with your [pc.weapon], just to have the bark skin harden in response and repel your weapon. Vaeril grunts from the impact of your blow, taking his attention away from Ryn just enough to pummel you with his fists and send you careening to the floor. "So much for your allies. You always so did love having dealings with the Belharans, and now you've begun worshipping their gods as well. Treachery by the queen against her own people and the Old Wyld — the boer'alvar will curse your name for generations for what you've led them into, Atheldred!" The archdruid's bitter laughter echoes in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. "You gave your entire people to your new god, so I'll give you to mine. A terrible exchange, to be sure, but I'll take what I can get." Dust and spores fill the air as the earth groans; Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions. It lashes this way and that like a tentacle, testing the air, and then the archdruid carefully, reverently passes the struggling Ryn into its grasp. "Where is your god now?" Vaeril roars. There's little rage in there now, mostly relief, catharsis, and bitter sorrow. One would've expected him to take more pleasure in the demise of one so hated, but... "surely if she cares so much for you, she'd personally arrive to pluck you from danger, isn't that right?" Finally, finally, the archdruid's specter begins to fade; one could consider his unfinished business in this world concluded, if nothing else. The last you see of Ryn is her struggling as the roots drag her into the earth amidst a collapsing chamber, and as the dust and spores overwhelm your lungs, you realize that orange-brown mold is creeping out of the fountain and off the elven remains that lie about the hallway, pushing and pulsing itself into shape. Mold and muck and rotting matter flow and gather in huge clumps, building themselves into... something...
rows.translation: 情况并不顺利——艾尔萨拉再次释放出一道白火攻击瓦雷尔，但这位大德鲁伊将其挡了回去，那道法术在击中目标后，使得树木的树皮和真菌都变成了黑色。这个被愤怒驱使的怪物，眼中只有瑞恩这个他憎恨的血脉继承人，这些背叛了他所有信念的人……在他生命即将终结的时刻，这份愤怒为他带来了超乎常人的力量。当他从地上捡起那个已经倒下的瑞恩，居高临下地注视着她时，他脸上的表情就像一只终于抓到了猎物，却不知道该如何处理它的猎犬。你绝对不能让这种事情发生—— [pc.isDK |除了你，没人敢招惹瑞恩。 |你被称作“冰霜冠军”绝非偶然！如果你能击败艾莉莎，那么你也能打败那个根本不知道自己已经死去的衰老老头。 ]你瞄准大德鲁伊的脖子，用力挥动你的武器 [pc.weapon]树皮会因此变硬，从而反弹你的武器。瓦雷尔被你的攻击击中，发出闷哼声，这一瞬间他的注意力从瑞恩身上转移开了，于是他用拳头猛击你，将你击倒在地。 你们的盟友也就这么回事吧。你们向来就喜欢与贝尔哈兰人打交道，现在甚至开始崇拜他们的神明。女王背叛自己的人民和古老的荒野——那些野兽会因为你们把他们引向这样的道路而诅咒你们的名字，阿瑟尔德雷德！大德鲁伊的苦涩笑声在黑暗中回荡，随后，地面传来阵阵呻吟与嘎吱声，灰尘和碎石从天花板上掉落下来。不，那重型压抑的气氛并未消散，只是那些橙棕色的光线开始从砖缝中渗出，越来越亮；片刻之后，地面开始震动某个东西岩石被穿透，开始松动、崩解。“你将你的全体子民献给了你的新神，那么我就把你献给我的神。这确实是一笔糟糕的交易，但我只能接受我所能得到的。”尘土与孢子弥漫在空气中，地面开始震动；瑞恩发出惊叫声——她附近的墙壁开始向内坍塌，一根扭曲的根茎破土而出，将碎裂的岩石抛向四面八方。那根根茎像触手一样四处伸展，试探着周围的空气，然后那位大德鲁伊小心翼翼地、充满敬畏地将挣扎中的瑞恩送入了它的怀抱。 你的神现在在哪里？”瓦雷尔怒吼道。他的话语中已经几乎没有愤怒了，更多的是解脱、宣泄，以及深深的悲痛。人们本以为他会为这样一个令人憎恨之人的灭亡而感到高兴，但是……“如果她真的那么关心你，她肯定会亲自来救你脱离危险，不是吗？ 终于，终于，那位大德鲁伊的幽灵开始消散了；至少可以认为，他在这个世界未完成的事业已经结束了。你最后看到的景象是，瑞恩在坍塌的房间中拼命挣扎，她的身体被那些根须拖向地面；而当尘埃和孢子充斥着你的肺部时，你会发现那种橙棕色的霉菌正从喷泉中渗出来，也从走廊里那些精灵的残骸上蔓延开来，它们不断蠕动、不断变形，逐渐形成完整的形态。霉菌、污垢以及腐烂的物质不断聚集，形成巨大的团块，逐渐构筑出…… 某个东西...

rows.original: You dust yourself off and look around, [pc.ass] still stinging from the long fall. The soft carpet of fleshy fungus might've cushioned your landing, but that was still quite the impact — you guess that you must be quite deep underground. Is everyone all right? [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"Owww," Cait moans, rubbing her butt. "I most certainly wasn't expecting that to happen." She's fine, right? "Yeah, I guess I am." Cait tries to dust herself off, and makes a face. "Eww, I thought it was bad up there, but the mold down here's everywhere. It's so... sticky and gross." Really? You hadn't noticed. Cait forces a smile at your byplay, but perks up as she looks about her. "Huh, wine. Dad once told Calla and I pale elven druids were once renowned vinters before the Godswar — much was lost not just in the fighting, but also because of the schism in their people. He may not have been intending to visit the Winter City itself, but you apparently can still get mirrorwine in Tychris — they have a thing going with the pale elves ever since one of their princes developed a taste for it. "We've seen a whole bunch of it in Njorhaalt — guess this is where it was made, huh?" |"Oof," Brint groans, pushing himself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've had two broken horns instead of one. That's one way in which I don't care to be balanced, thank you very much." Walking over, you dust off your minotaur friend while he rubs his head and takes in his surroundings, stamping on the spongy ground with his hooves. "Oh, wow. And I thought it was bad up there." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Once he's satisfied that his limbs are all working right, Brint gives you a thumbs-up and hefts his [brint.weapon] over his shoulder. "Come on, [pc.name]. I think this place's long overdue for a little pruning." |"Ohhh," Brienne moans, pushing herself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've broken the same horn. That's an experience I'd rather not live through again, thanks." Walking over, you dust off your cowgirl while she rubs her sore bits and takes in her surroundings. Everything all in one piece? "Yeah," Brienne replies with a weak smile and cups her huge tits in her hands. "I've got plenty of cushioning here to help break falls, don't worry about it." That, and some more padding down below. All right, if she's pulled herself together to make flirty jokes, you don't have to worry about her. "Just trying to cheer you up. You looked a bit down." Slowly, Brienne stamps on the spongy ground with her hooves, making a face. "Oh, eww. And I thought it was bad up there. This is just — eww." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Finally getting her uncooperative top back into shape, Brienne picks up her [brienne.weapon], reassured by its weight. "Nothing could've really prepared me for this." |"Aw, fuck," Arona groans, pushing herself off the ground and rubbing her jaw. "Fucking ghosts and their dirty tricks, even when you've beat the shit out of them. Fuck ghosts." That's three %"fucks" out of her — she's probably all right, then. "Sweet of you to notice. Yeah, I'm fine. The fall just shook me up a bit, that's all." Forcing a toothy smile, Arona scans the room for her [arona.weapon], and yanks it by the handle out of the moist fungal bed it'd fallen into. She strains a moment, there's a wet sucking sound, and it comes free with a pop. "Aw, shit. That stuff's disgusting. Thank the gods I didn't fall into that on the way down." Yeah, that stuff's just nasty. She could've suffocated — what a way to go. "If I'm going to snuff it, I'd like to have a better showing than that." Satisfied that everything's in order, your orcish companion claps you on the shoulder and looks around her at the rotting racks and presses, whistling. "Well, would you look at this. Sure, these elves may have been cocksleeves through and through, but at least they were cocksleeves who knew how to party; what I wouldn't give to have a stash like this would've been. I could drink every night for a year and not drain it all." Fine wines? You'd have pegged her for more of a mead kind of person. "This is the kind of stuff you bring back home when you've had a good raid, doesn't pay to be picky. And speaking of raiding, pushing that smug elf's face in has only left me wanting more. Come on, [pc.name], let's go find some more ghosts to beat the shit out of." |Azyrran doesn't reply immediately, instead struggling against the soft bed she's landed in — the hardness of her chitin's resulted in her sinking pretty deep into the soft mold. The vile mess clings to her like mud, and it's with your help that she extricates herself with a wet sucking sound. "Ugh," she says, cleaning herself off as best as she can. "Not that I'm not thankful for the soft landing, but maybe it might've been better to take a bruise or two." Doubt it. There isn't a single square inch of floor in this room that isn't covered in fungus of sorts, and the walls... "What about —" Azzy begins, then her eyes alight on the sap slowly oozing from the stone, and she blanches, instinctively taking a step back. After a moment, she swallows hard, squares her shoulders, and gives you a nod. "It's all right. I had to figure that it wasn't honey, not with that sweet stench." Remarkably like it, though. "Yes. Yes, very much so." She takes a deep breath, then as if mesmerized, reaches out to touch the nearest sap-slick wall with a finger; you slap her away, and she shivers and steps back as if woken from a walking dream. "Oh. I..." Is she fine? "I think I'll be. I just need a moment to get ahold of myself. The druidess said that this weapon was targeted at her kind and that we should be largely unaffected by it, but I'm not so sure that's fully the case, at least for me. It's like a whispering on my skin, if that makes sense. An itch that I know won't go away, no matter how much I scratch." |"I am... fine." There's an obvious expression of distaste on Kiyoko's face as your fox-wife pushes herself to her feet, her lip curled ever so slightly. "This place is noisome, to be blunt about it." You look at the carpet of spongy fungus and pinhead mushrooms that cover the floor, and find it hard to disagree. "No time to waste, beloved," she says. "The sooner we are done here, the sooner we can be gone from this place. I am sure that the four of us will be able to make short work of any obstacle in our way." |"Yeah," Atugia says, picking herself up from the ground and hurriedly dusting herself off. She looks for a spot to clean the worst of the moist, freshly crushed fungus off on, finds none, and settles for summoning up her halberd just to be able to scrape off the disgusting stuff. "Well, the arms and legs are working fine, at least. Can't say the fame for the rest o' this stuff — makes my skin crawl." Everything all in one piece? Nothing broken? "Nah. I tucked myself in when the floor gave way — that's a trick I learned back in the day, curl yourself up — then this stuff happened to break my fall. Not saying I ain't grateful to Tira for that bit of luck, but gods does it stink so bad. I just wanna get out of here so I can wash up." Oh, you can understand that sentiment. If her arms and legs are working just fine, then it's time to hit the road. Even if you can't go back the way you came, you get the feeling there's another way out of here. |"Ow, fuck." Quin twitches, groans, and then bounds back onto his feet in a short hop. "Wasn't expecting that kind of bullshit. Thought we'd deal with the head honcho and be done with it, short and sweet... but things are never that easy, are they?" Would they ever be. He looks just fine. "Yeah, could've been worse." Sniffing the air, Quin makes a face. "Ugh, this place stinks. That, and the air's making my fur itch." Hey, it could be worse.
