        "

rows.original:
The clear water's tempting, but ultimately it's not something you want to take a chance on. With the entire druidic temple infested inside and out, this single fountain and its source manages to escape the corruption? Nah, it's too good to be true.

        Well, if you're not going to bother with the fountain, then the only way is forward, then...
rows.translation:
清澈的泉水确实很诱人，但说实话，这种事情根本不值得去冒险。整个德鲁伊神庙里里外外都已经被腐蚀侵蚀了，而唯独这一处泉水及其源头却能够幸免于难？嗯，这种事情未免太美好了，简直难以置信。

        好吧，如果你打算不去理会这个泉水的话，那么唯一的出路就是……
rows.raw:
"
        The clear water's tempting, but ultimately it's not something you want to take a chance on. With the entire druidic temple infested inside and out, this single fountain and its source manages to escape the corruption? Nah, it's too good to be true.

        Well, if you're not going to bother with the fountain, then the only way is forward, then...
        "

rows.original: Your footsteps land upon dark, heavy soil as you pace through the arboretum, drawn inexorably to its center. Much of the verdance has been reduced to rotting stumps and logs, food for the shrooms that carpet their bodies, but one specimen still stands out amongst those that still survive, towering to the domed ceiling. Perhaps, once, it might have been beautiful, inspiring, majestic. Now, coated in patches of spongy fungus, its branches are withered and end in fleshy tendrils even as is struggles to keep what few leaves still remain on the bough. Just about all of its bark is gone, consumed by the creeping infestation, and from the bared wood beneath amber sap continually oozes down its roots and into the soil, liquid light from a sun that it clearly hasn't seen for a long, long time. You step over several fin-like growths of bracket fungus and pass under pulsating, spore-spewing sacs to take a closer look, but quickly think better of it. Even if you weren't hit with the strong stench of putrefaction, it's impossible not to recognize the sap for what it is: you've seen it oozing through the walls of the corrupt temple, dripping from the ceiling, feeding the ever-ravenous and uncontrolled growth of the invasive fungus that brought this place to ruin. What ought to have been the distilled essence of life itself. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |If this entire trip was upsetting for Cait, she now looks downright depressed. Even the ever present noisome smell from the fallen logs all about you has failed to eke a response from the usually bubbly catgirl as she trails along behind you, her feet heavy. Sobering, isn't it? "There are legends in the temple of how people used to behave during the Godswar, [pc.name]. Not because they were corrupted or anything, but because of the things they'd seen that their enemies were capable of. Sure, imagining it from what was on paper was one thing, but seeing it for myself... I understand why the direct intervention of the gods was needed back then. Not just because of the sheer power needed to beat something like this en masse, but also to cope with the things they'd see in the course of doing so." Every so often, there're reports of things emerging from beneath the earth in the Belharan Heartlands, especially in the locales about the old imperium. None of them are good, and chances are you're looking at something akin to one of them now. |Brint just stares up at the tree, stupefied; just when you think he's been caught in some mind-meld and are about to step in, he gets ahold of himself, spews a long string of expletives in what can only be minoan, then grabs your hand and squeezes it firmly. "Well, if this isn't a nasty piece of work," he says, his voice subdued. "I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to sleep tonight. Everything else was harrowing enough, but this is..." Imagine how it must've been like for the druids. "Hrm. When I agreed to come along with you on this adventure, [pc.name], I was expecting things to be pretty bad, what with demons and all. But there's a difference between imagining things, and seeing them for yourself. At least that one's not limited by what you can think up." Having regrets? "None at all." |Brienne stares up at the tree stupefied, her lips moving but failing to form words. With a monumental surge of effort, she tears her gaze away from the twisted, infested thing with its oozing rents and pulsating spore sacs, then squeezes her eyes shut and hugs you so tightly as to risk crushing you. She still doesn't manage to put her thoughts into words, but the way she's trembling under that thick hide of hers has you patting her on the forehead as she bends down to you. There, there. That thing's a nasty piece of work, isn't it? Brienne nods. It's fine, you're here. She'll be able to sleep tonight, because you're going to deal with this thing one way or another. Dreaming up fantasies about slaying monsters is one thing, and actually going out to fight them is another, because the latter isn't constrained by your imagination. Whatever that she's been through thus far, you're here to help her through it. Now, you need her strength — can she do that for you? "I-I can." There, there. That'll do. |"Don't know what you're all hung up about," Arona says with a big, tusky grin on her face. She makes a point of crushing several fat, orange mushrooms underfoot as she stomps up to the oozing rents in the tree's side, waving her [arona.weapon] about like she owns the place. "It's just a tree." Even Arona can't be that obtuse as to not realize the horror that's manifested before her eyes, can she? On the other hand, it must be nice to be so straight-minded that horrors beyond mortal comprehension simply slide off her psyche without leaving so much as a scratch. "Oh, come on," Arona fires back at you. "There's nothing to worry about. Sure, there's a vine or two, but trees are what silly old people who want to avoid a straw death go out to fight so they can claim they died in battle. Or, you know, like fighting the tide. It's just another pox-rotted tree — we'll just turn this thing into firewood, if there's any worth having, and then we can all go home." Look, if she please wouldn't get too far ahead of the rest of the group so that she won't risk being separated should something happen — |Azyrran looks the scene before her up and down, wrinkling her nose without even bothering to disguise her disgust. What she's trying to hide, and unsuccessfully at that, is the fact that she's quaking under that chitin of hers. Bad memories? "It's not exactly like the honey pool, but close enough," she whispers. "Should I be glad that Mother and my sisters only turned into airheaded bimbos who constantly oozed honey instead of something akin to what happened to these elves?" If she wants an honest answer? Yes. Her hive wasn't so far gone that it couldn't be brought back, and her family were still recognizable as themselves. The same can't be said for the sight that lies before you, or for anyone or anything of the druidic remnants that you've encountered so far. That's probably not the answer that Azzy wanted, but it's the one she needs, and just as expected, she takes it in stride. She looks contemplative for a moment, then gives you a nod and levels her [azyrran.weapon] straight ahead. "Shall we?" |You look over at [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ], and she returns the meaningful gaze with a small shrug. "I do not think there is anything left to be said, [var0 |husband |beloved ]. We burn everything to the ground and then go home for a bath and a good meal." Ah, she's so direct when she wants to be. The fact that she does it so rarely only emphasizes the times when she cuts to the chase. |"Wow," Atugia mutters, craning her neck up to take in the totality of the infested tree. "I've seen some things in my time, but this is..." The worst? "Nah." Second? Third? "A toss-up between the sixth or seventh. There were some nasty times that Carmen and I went through together, way back in the day when things were still, well, dirty." Well, she overcame those, so what's one more to add to the list? Tui gives you a thin smile. "Well, Carmen and I ran from numbers one to three, so they don't count. But this would be around six at worst, so I'm up for it. Besides, I've got you here, don't I?" Why, you're flattered that she considers you better to have at her back against the odds than the baroness. "Only because she did that whole vow of not fighting thing, so don't get too cocky now. All right, ready when you are." |"Well, aren't you a nasty piece of work," Quin spits. He's clearly trying to put on a brave front, but it's clear as day that this is more than anything he's seen during his time with Tollus. "I've said it before, but I'll say it again: it's a good thing that the old fart never actually managed to make any headway with looking into the past — I'd take the ugly fuck he managed to summon through the portal to this any day." That's right. You don't need to reach through to other worlds in order to get eldritch horrors beyond your comprehension, you have perfectly serviceable ones at home. Quin raises an eyebrow at you, then breaks into bitter laughter. "It really is that way, isn't it? Makes Tollus's silly search all the more pointless, for all the effort he put into it." And is he afraid? That gets him to catch his breath, then give you a weak grin. "I'd be a fool to say that I wasn't — anyone with a lick of sense would be. But so long as it can get horny, I think we have a chance. It'd be terribly ironic if my dark and evil cultist mindscrews saved the day, wouldn't it?" |[viviane.isDemon |"Oh, how great and terrible," Viv says not quite under her breath, staring up at the diseased tree with rapt curiosity and fascination. "Would it be that I had the chance to document how you became what you are from what you were. As things stand, though, I suppose I have no other choice but to take you apart. Maybe some of your whole will still be preserved in the sum of the parts." Why, is there only room for one such as her? "Less that and more... well, I've had to deal with difficult specimens before, but keeping this thing contained would take so much of my time and effort that I wouldn't be able to get anything else done." Of course, the very idea that she might not be capable of such a thing to begin with didn't cross her mind, but then she wouldn't be... herself if she entertained such self-doubt, would she? |"Well, aren't you a nasty thing," Viv says, staring up at the diseased tree with something between disgust and fascination. "I think this falls neatly into the small but extant category of 'do not study', for various reasons." So, faced with the corruption that Kasyrra's brought with her and that which is already rooted in the world for long enough to be considered native, which would fit more into that category? Viv gives you a thin-lipped smile. "As the saying goes, why not both?" Smart answer. A sigh, and then Viv rolls up her sleeves. "A part of me does wish that it didn't have to be this way, but needs are as needs must. Come on, [pc.name], let's get this out of the way." ] |Agni doesn't say anything for a few moments, staring up at the diseased tree. She'd have been alive during the Godswar, wouldn't she? Has she seen something like this before? "I don't remember doing so, but that doesn't necessarily mean I haven't. On the other hand, if I did and forgot about it between lives, I'd be pretty disappointed with myself. A product of the Wraiths' handiwork seems like the kind of thing I'd place just under the family I've had when it comes to important things to remember." It would, wouldn't it? "This is almost as bad as drowning, and drowning's a pretty horrible way to go. Shall we get rid of this eyesore?" You can tell that Agni's trying to cover for her fear and revulsion here, but see no reason to break what the spot of levity she's trying to create. With fire, you take it? "With fire." |Slowly, Ryn, Elthara and you fan out to better take in from all angles the sight that lies before you — as horrifying as it might be, you still can't tear your eyes away from it, the corrupted tree possessed of an otherworldly magnetism, alluring in all its twisted beauty as it reaches for the domed ceiling. "...This is..." ...What the druids revered in a fashion that other peoples would call worship. Hethia might disagree, perhaps call it something more akin to reverence for someone very old and wise, but you're sure that the boreal elves of the day didn't see it that way. Worship is worship, however you cut it, whether you want to call the recipient a god or not. "We have to destroy it." Elthara's gripping her scythe with such fervor that her knuckles are pale. "There's no going back from this, and it looks like it hasn't just succumbed to its corruption, but wholeheartedly embraced it." "There but for the grace of the goddess goes us," Ryn adds in a murmur. "After Alissa? Yes, there but for her grace in [pc.names] timely arrival, and your bravery in going out to find [pc.himHer] to begin with." You knew that this was a possibility to begin with, and it became all but inevitable once the earth opened up and tipped you into the temple below. All the choices up until now have narrowed to this point... ] As you're considering your next move, a transformation comes over the diseased tree: its sapwood splits apart just before you, rapidly reshaping itself into the silhouette of a woman from the thighs up, akin to a figurehead one might find on the prow of a ship. Instinctively, you tighten your fingers about your [pc.weapon] and ready yourself, a move that turns out to be wise as several fungal tentacles unravel from the highest boughs and lash out at you. You're getting flashbacks to the Alraune here... The plant-woman continues to take shape, growing ever more and more curvaceous; deep verdant skin covers her, perfect in contrast to the blight that eats away at her tree, or the wood she's attached to. As you watch, a tiny fleshy bud blooms between her thighs, just above where she joins with the tree. In the blink of an eye, the flower's grown to an obscene size, its petals unfurling into a very familiar sight. Basking in the attention of her captive audience, the plant-woman thrusts her hips forward, and a huge, grasping tendril erupts just above the flower. Both parts drool musky sap with primal need and fervor, and as you watch, the tendril's bulbous head splits apart to reveal a gaping hole within lined with wavering cilia. What is she, then? The wyld tree, or what's left of it? "I don't mind if you want to call me that," she purrs, beckoning you forward with a lewd smile. In that moment, the infested plant-woman opens her eyes, and you see nothing but the orange-amber of sap burning and bubbling within. "You've all been very naughty and need correction of the most vigorous sort, so what's one more transgression against me?"
rows.translation: 你的足部步踩在暗影而重型的泥土上，沿着植物园的小径稳步前行，仿佛有一股无形的力量在驱使你不断向中心走去。大部分绿植早已枯萎，只剩下腐烂的树桩和原木，而这些正是那些覆盖在它们表面的蘑菇的食物来源。然而，在那些幸存下来的植物中，仍有一株格外引人注目——它高耸入云，仿佛直插穹顶般。 或许，曾经它也曾是如此美丽、令人赞叹、雄伟壮观。如今，它的枝干上覆盖着一块块海绵状的真菌，已经枯萎不堪，枝梢末端长出了肉质的卷须，而它仍在努力地维持着那些残留在枝叶上的叶子。它的树皮几乎全部都被这种蔓延的害虫侵蚀掉了，裸露的树干上，琥珀色的树液不断从根部渗出，流入土壤之中——那是一种来自太阳的光芒，显然，这棵树已经很久很久没有见过太阳了。你跨过几株形似鱼鳍的菌类，从那些不断释放孢子的囊状物下方穿过，想要仔细观察它们，但很快就改变了主意。即使没有那股浓重的腐烂气味，你也绝对能认出这种汁液的本质：你曾经见过它从那座腐朽的寺庙墙壁中渗出，从天花板上滴下来，滋养着这种不断蔓延、无法控制的入侵性真菌，正是这种真菌导致了这个地方的毁灭。什么应该可以说是生命本质的浓缩与精华。 [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |如果整个旅途让凯特如此心烦意乱，那么现在她看起来简直陷入了抑郁之中。就连周围那些倒下的原木散发出的刺鼻气味，也未能引起这个平时总是活泼开朗的猫女丝毫反应——她跟在你身后，脚步显得格外沉重。真是令人深思，不是吗？“在神庙里，有一些传说讲述了人们在神战期间是如何行为的 [pc.name]并不是因为他们堕落了或者发生了什么类似的事情，而是因为他们亲眼看到了敌人真正具备的能力。当然，从书面描述中想象这些事情是一回事，但亲身体验之后……我就明白为什么在那个时候需要神明的直接干预了。这不仅仅是因为要集体击败这样的敌人需要巨大的力量，也是为了应对他们在战斗过程中可能会遇到的各种情况。偶尔，会有报道称在贝尔哈兰的心脏地带，尤其是在那些与旧帝国有关的地区，会有东西从地下冒出来。它们没有一个是好的，而你现在看到的，很可能就是其中某一个。 |布林特只是呆呆地望着那棵树，显得十分茫然；就在你以为他陷入了某种精神恍惚状态、准备上前帮忙的时候，他突然恢复了清醒，用一种显然属于米诺斯语系的语言骂了一长串脏话，然后紧紧抓住了你的手。 哎呀，如果这不是个极其恶劣的人的话……”他压低声音说道，“我真不确定自己今晚还能不能睡着。之前的那些事情已经够让人痛苦的了，但这个……”试想，对于那些德鲁伊来说，那该是怎样的体验啊。 嗯，当初我同意和你一起参加这次冒险的时候 [pc.name]我原本以为情况会非常糟糕，毕竟还有恶魔之类的东西。但想象和亲眼看到其实是两回事。至少，亲眼看到的事物不会受到你想象能力的限制。会有后悔吗？“一点也不。 |布蕾妮呆呆地望着那棵树，嘴唇动了动，却发不出任何声音。她使出极大的力气，终于将视线从那棵布满裂口、孢子囊不断跳动、仿佛被寄生虫侵蚀的树木上移开，然后紧紧地闭上眼睛，将你紧紧抱在怀里，力度之大几乎要把你压坏。她仍然无法将自己的想法用语言表达出来，但当她那厚厚的皮毛下不停地颤抖时，你会忍不住在她弯下腰来靠近你时，轻拍她的额头。好了，好了。那个家伙确实是个麻烦制造者，不是吗？ 布蕾妮点了点头。“没关系，你在这里。她今晚一定能睡个好觉，因为不管怎样，你都会解决这个问题。幻想自己杀死怪物是一回事，真正去与它们战斗则是另一回事——因为后者不会受到你想象力的限制。无论她迄今为止经历了什么，你都在这里帮助她度过这些难关。现在，你需要她的力量——她能为你做到这一点吗？“我……我可以。”好了，就这样。没问题的。 |真不知道你们都在纠结些什么，”阿罗娜脸上挂着灿烂的笑容说道。她一边大步走向树上那些正在渗出液体的伤口，一边故意踩碎了几朵肥大的橙色蘑菇。同时，她还在不停地挥动着她的 [arona.weapon] 她表现得好像那地方是她的似的。“只不过是一棵树而已。”就连阿罗娜也不可能蠢到没有意识到眼前所发生的一切的恐怖吧？不过，能够如此头脑简单，让那些超乎人类理解范围的恐怖事物完全无法影响到自己的心理，想必也是一种幸福吧。“哦，得了吧开启没什么好担心的，”阿罗娜反驳道，“虽然确实有一两株藤蔓，但树木才是那些害怕被草草了结性命的愚蠢老人们会去与之战斗的东西——这样他们就可以宣称自己是战死的。或者说，就像与潮水抗争一样。不过又是一棵腐烂的树罢了——如果还能派上用场的话，我们就把它切成柴火，然后大家都可以回家了。”“听着，她最好别走得太快，以免发生什么意外时与大家走散了。 |阿兹兰上下打量着眼前的景象，鼻子不禁皱了起来，丝毫没有掩饰自己的厌恶之情。她试图隐藏的事实是——实际上，她自己也在害怕得发抖。 糟糕的记忆？“虽然不完全像那个蜜池，但也差不多了，”她轻声说道，“难道我应该庆幸母亲和我的姐妹们只是变成了那些整天胡言乱语、浑身散发着‘蜜香’的傻姑娘，而不是像这些精灵一样遭遇了那种事情吗？如果她想要一个诚实的答案的话？是的。她的蜂群并没有陷入无法挽回的境地，她的家族成员也依然可以被认出来。但是，眼前的这一幕，以及你迄今为止遇到的所有德鲁伊遗迹，却都无法再有这样的情形了。 这可能不是阿齐想要的答案，但却是她所需要的。正如预期的那样，她坦然接受了这个结果。她沉思了一会儿，然后点了点头，平静地接受了这个事实。 [azyrran.weapon] 就在前方。“我们走吧？ |你看向那边。 [kiyoko.married |你的狐狸老婆 |清子 ]她微微耸了耸肩，用同样充满深意的眼神回应了他。“我想，已经没有什么话好说了。 [var0 |丈夫 |亲爱的 ]我们燃烧着。一切摔倒在地后，就回家洗个澡，再吃顿丰盛的饭菜。”啊，她想要表达的时候，真是直言不讳。而她很少这样做，反而让这种直率的表现在关键时刻显得更加突出。 |哇，”阿图吉娅喃喃道，她伸长脖子仔细观察那棵被虫蛀侵蚀的树木。“这些年来我见过很多奇怪的事情，但这个……”是最糟糕的吗？“不，不是。”那算是第二糟糕的吗？还是第三糟糕的？ 是在第六名和第七名之间难分高下。很久以前，当那些事情还相当棘手的时候，卡门和我一起经历了一些非常艰难的时光。”嗯，她已经克服了那些困难，那么再增加一项到清单上又有什么关系呢？ 崔给了你一个淡淡的微笑：“嗯，卡门和我在第一到第三名之间，所以那些成绩不算数。但最坏的情况也不过是第六名左右，所以我愿意接受这个挑战。再说，有你在我身边，不是吗？”你心里暗想：她认为在面对困难时，有你在她身边比有那位女男爵在身边更好，这简直让我感到受宠若惊啊。 只是因为她发了那个不打架的誓言，所以你现在别太得意了。好了，你准备好了就可以开始吧。 |哼，你真是个卑鄙的混蛋，”昆因咬牙说道。他显然在试图装出一副勇敢的样子，但很明显，这种情景远远超出了他在托勒斯期间所经历过的任何事情。“我之前就说过，现在还要再说一遍：幸好那个老混蛋根本没能成功探究过去的事情——比起他通过那个传送门召唤出来的那些东西，我宁愿面对他本人。没错。你根本不需要去其他世界去寻找那些超乎你理解范围的恐怖存在，因为在你自己的家里，就有着足够令你恐惧的东西。 昆因挑了挑眉毛，然后突然爆发出一阵苦笑。真的是这样吧？这样一来，托勒斯费了那么大劲进行的那些愚蠢搜寻，就全都变得毫无意义了。”那么，他害怕吗？他停了一下，然后勉强挤出了一个微笑。如果我说自己没有这种想法，那简直就是傻瓜——任何有点理智的人都会这么想。但只要事情能发展得有点激情四射，我觉得我们还是有机会的。如果我那些阴暗邪恶的邪教思想最终却拯救了大局，那未免太具有讽刺意味了吧？" |[viviane.isDemon |哦，真是既奇妙又可怕，”薇芙几乎是低声说道，她满怀好奇与 fascination地仰望着那棵患病的树。“难道我有机会记录下你们是如何从最初的形态变成现在的样子的吗？不过，就目前的情况来看，我想我别无选择，只能把你们拆开来看。也许其中的一些部分仍然能够保留你们原有的本质。为什么，难道只有她这样的存在才有存在的价值吗？ 少说也是这样……其实我以前也处理过一些棘手的案例，但要想控制住这个东西，我需要投入太多的时间和精力，以至于根本无暇处理其他事情。”当然，她从未想过自己可能根本无法完成这项任务，但事实就是如此。如果她一直怀有这样的自我怀疑，她自己会怎么想呢？ |哎呀，你真是个讨厌的东西，”薇芙说道，她抬头望着那棵病态的树，眼中既有厌恶，又带着一丝好奇。“我觉得这种东西完全属于‘不应该被研究’的那一类——毕竟有很多原因使得它不适合被研究。那么，面对卡希拉带来的腐败现象，以及那些早已在这个世界上根深蒂固、几乎可以被视为“本土问题”的腐败现象，哪一种才更符合这个分类呢？ 薇芙露出一个淡淡的微笑：“俗话说，为什么不两者皆得呢？”回答得真聪明。她叹了口气，然后卷起了袖子：“我内心确实希望事情不必如此，但需求就是需求，必须得到满足。来吧， [pc.name]让我们先把这件事解决掉吧。 ] |阿格尼沉默了好一会儿，只是抬头望着那棵病态的树木。在神战期间，她应该还活着吧？她以前见过这样的景象吗？“我不知道记得我确实是这么做的，但这并不一定意味着我之前没有忘记过。另一方面，如果我真的忘记了，而在不同的“生命”之间又重新记起了这件事，我一定会对自己感到非常失望。毕竟，那些由“幽灵”们制造出来的东西，对我来说，应该属于那些必须牢记的重要事物之中。是不是也会这样呢？ “这几乎和溺水一样糟糕，而溺水确实是一种非常可怕的死法。我们是不是应该把这个碍眼的东西去掉呢？” 你可以看出，阿格尼其实是在试图掩饰自己的恐惧和厌恶，但我觉得没有必要破坏她试图营造出的这种轻松氛围。用火来对付它吗？”“用火。 |慢慢地，瑞恩、艾尔萨拉和你们分散开来，从各个角度仔细观察眼前的景象——尽管那景象令人毛骨悚然，但你们还是无法将视线从它身上移开。那棵被腐蚀的树木散发着一种超自然的吸引力，它那扭曲而美丽的形态令人着迷，同时它也不断地向着穹顶延伸着。 ……这就是……”……那种连其他民族都会称之为崇拜的仪式。赫西亚或许会不同意，她可能会认为这种行为更类似于对一位年迈而睿智之人的尊敬，但可以肯定的是，当时的极北精灵们并不这么看。无论从哪个角度来看，崇拜就是崇拜，无论你是否愿意将被崇拜的对象称为神明。“我们必须摧毁它。”艾尔萨拉紧紧握着她的镰刀，手指因用力而变得苍白。“我们已经没有回头路了，而且看起来它不仅已经屈服于自身的堕落，更是全心全意地接受了这种堕落。要不是女神的恩典，我们也可能会落得同样的下场，”莱恩低声说道。“在艾莉莎之后？没错，要不是她的帮助 [pc.names] 及时赶到，以及你勇于外出寻找的勇气[pc.himHer]首先，你从一开始就明白这种可能性存在，而当地面裂开并将你带入下方的神庙之后，这一切几乎变得不可避免了。直到现在，所有的选择最终都汇聚到了这一点上…… ] 就在你思考下一步该怎么做的时候，那棵病态的树木突然发生了变化：它的边材在你面前裂开了，迅速重新组合成了一位女性的上半身轮廓，从大腿部位开始，就像船头上常见的雕像一样。出于本能，你紧紧抓住了手中的东西。 [pc.weapon] 准备好吧，因为接下来发生的一幕确实非常明智——几条真菌触手从最高的树枝上伸展开来，朝你袭来。这时，你一定会回想起阿尔劳妮的故事……这种植物女子的身形逐渐变得清晰起来，她的身体线条愈发优美动人；深绿色的皮肤覆盖在她的身上，这与正在侵蚀她所在树木、以及她所依附的木头的那种枯萎病形成了鲜明的对比。就在你注视着的时候，她的大腿之间，就在与“树干”相连的地方上方，出现了一个小小的肉色花蕾。转眼间，这朵花就已经长到了惊人的大小，它的花瓣展开了，呈现出一种非常熟悉的外观。在这群被她吸引住的观众们的注视下，这个“植物女人”将臀部向前一推，于是，在花朵的正上方，突然伸出一根巨大的、能够抓住东西的卷须。这两部分都会分泌出带有原始欲望与狂热的麝香状汁液，而当你注视着它们时，那些卷须状的头部会裂开，露出一个内部布满颤动纤毛的巨大洞穴。那么，她究竟是什么呢？是那棵野树，还是它残余的部分呢？ 如果你想这么称呼我，我并不介意，”她轻声说道，同时露出一个挑逗的笑容，邀请你靠近。就在那一刻，那个被植物侵蚀的女子睁开了眼睛，你看到的是她体内那些橙黄色的汁液正在燃烧、沸腾着。你们一个个都太调皮了，确实需要最严厉的惩罚才行……那么，再犯一次错吧，看看这次我会怎么惩罚你们。
rows.raw: " Your footsteps land upon dark, heavy soil as you pace through the arboretum, drawn inexorably to its center. Much of the verdance has been reduced to rotting stumps and logs, food for the shrooms that carpet their bodies, but one specimen still stands out amongst those that still survive, towering to the domed ceiling. Perhaps, once, it might have been beautiful, inspiring, majestic. Now, coated in patches of spongy fungus, its branches are withered and end in fleshy tendrils even as is struggles to keep what few leaves still remain on the bough. Just about all of its bark is gone, consumed by the creeping infestation, and from the bared wood beneath amber sap continually oozes down its roots and into the soil, liquid light from a sun that it clearly hasn't seen for a long, long time. You step over several fin-like growths of bracket fungus and pass under pulsating, spore-spewing sacs to take a closer look, but quickly think better of it. Even if you weren't hit with the strong stench of putrefaction, it's impossible not to recognize the sap for what it is: you've seen it oozing through the walls of the corrupt temple, dripping from the ceiling, feeding the ever-ravenous and uncontrolled growth of the invasive fungus that brought this place to ruin. What ought to have been the distilled essence of life itself. [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |If this entire trip was upsetting for Cait, she now looks downright depressed. Even the ever present noisome smell from the fallen logs all about you has failed to eke a response from the usually bubbly catgirl as she trails along behind you, her feet heavy. Sobering, isn't it? "There are legends in the temple of how people used to behave during the Godswar, [pc.name]. Not because they were corrupted or anything, but because of the things they'd seen that their enemies were capable of. Sure, imagining it from what was on paper was one thing, but seeing it for myself... I understand why the direct intervention of the gods was needed back then. Not just because of the sheer power needed to beat something like this en masse, but also to cope with the things they'd see in the course of doing so." Every so often, there're reports of things emerging from beneath the earth in the Belharan Heartlands, especially in the locales about the old imperium. None of them are good, and chances are you're looking at something akin to one of them now. |Brint just stares up at the tree, stupefied; just when you think he's been caught in some mind-meld and are about to step in, he gets ahold of himself, spews a long string of expletives in what can only be minoan, then grabs your hand and squeezes it firmly. "Well, if this isn't a nasty piece of work," he says, his voice subdued. "I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to sleep tonight. Everything else was harrowing enough, but this is..." Imagine how it must've been like for the druids. "Hrm. When I agreed to come along with you on this adventure, [pc.name], I was expecting things to be pretty bad, what with demons and all. But there's a difference between imagining things, and seeing them for yourself. At least that one's not limited by what you can think up." Having regrets? "None at all." |Brienne stares up at the tree stupefied, her lips moving but failing to form words. With a monumental surge of effort, she tears her gaze away from the twisted, infested thing with its oozing rents and pulsating spore sacs, then squeezes her eyes shut and hugs you so tightly as to risk crushing you. She still doesn't manage to put her thoughts into words, but the way she's trembling under that thick hide of hers has you patting her on the forehead as she bends down to you. There, there. That thing's a nasty piece of work, isn't it? Brienne nods. It's fine, you're here. She'll be able to sleep tonight, because you're going to deal with this thing one way or another. Dreaming up fantasies about slaying monsters is one thing, and actually going out to fight them is another, because the latter isn't constrained by your imagination. Whatever that she's been through thus far, you're here to help her through it. Now, you need her strength — can she do that for you? "I-I can." There, there. That'll do. |"Don't know what you're all hung up about," Arona says with a big, tusky grin on her face. She makes a point of crushing several fat, orange mushrooms underfoot as she stomps up to the oozing rents in the tree's side, waving her [arona.weapon] about like she owns the place. "It's just a tree." Even Arona can't be that obtuse as to not realize the horror that's manifested before her eyes, can she? On the other hand, it must be nice to be so straight-minded that horrors beyond mortal comprehension simply slide off her psyche without leaving so much as a scratch. "Oh, come on," Arona fires back at you. "There's nothing to worry about. Sure, there's a vine or two, but trees are what silly old people who want to avoid a straw death go out to fight so they can claim they died in battle. Or, you know, like fighting the tide. It's just another pox-rotted tree — we'll just turn this thing into firewood, if there's any worth having, and then we can all go home." Look, if she please wouldn't get too far ahead of the rest of the group so that she won't risk being separated should something happen — |Azyrran looks the scene before her up and down, wrinkling her nose without even bothering to disguise her disgust. What she's trying to hide, and unsuccessfully at that, is the fact that she's quaking under that chitin of hers. Bad memories? "It's not exactly like the honey pool, but close enough," she whispers. "Should I be glad that Mother and my sisters only turned into airheaded bimbos who constantly oozed honey instead of something akin to what happened to these elves?" If she wants an honest answer? Yes. Her hive wasn't so far gone that it couldn't be brought back, and her family were still recognizable as themselves. The same can't be said for the sight that lies before you, or for anyone or anything of the druidic remnants that you've encountered so far. That's probably not the answer that Azzy wanted, but it's the one she needs, and just as expected, she takes it in stride. She looks contemplative for a moment, then gives you a nod and levels her [azyrran.weapon] straight ahead. "Shall we?" |You look over at [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ], and she returns the meaningful gaze with a small shrug. "I do not think there is anything left to be said, [var0 |husband |beloved ]. We burn everything to the ground and then go home for a bath and a good meal." Ah, she's so direct when she wants to be. The fact that she does it so rarely only emphasizes the times when she cuts to the chase. |"Wow," Atugia mutters, craning her neck up to take in the totality of the infested tree. "I've seen some things in my time, but this is..." The worst? "Nah." Second? Third? "A toss-up between the sixth or seventh. There were some nasty times that Carmen and I went through together, way back in the day when things were still, well, dirty." Well, she overcame those, so what's one more to add to the list? Tui gives you a thin smile. "Well, Carmen and I ran from numbers one to three, so they don't count. But this would be around six at worst, so I'm up for it. Besides, I've got you here, don't I?" Why, you're flattered that she considers you better to have at her back against the odds than the baroness. "Only because she did that whole vow of not fighting thing, so don't get too cocky now. All right, ready when you are." |"Well, aren't you a nasty piece of work," Quin spits. He's clearly trying to put on a brave front, but it's clear as day that this is more than anything he's seen during his time with Tollus. "I've said it before, but I'll say it again: it's a good thing that the old fart never actually managed to make any headway with looking into the past — I'd take the ugly fuck he managed to summon through the portal to this any day." That's right. You don't need to reach through to other worlds in order to get eldritch horrors beyond your comprehension, you have perfectly serviceable ones at home. Quin raises an eyebrow at you, then breaks into bitter laughter. "It really is that way, isn't it? Makes Tollus's silly search all the more pointless, for all the effort he put into it." And is he afraid? That gets him to catch his breath, then give you a weak grin. "I'd be a fool to say that I wasn't — anyone with a lick of sense would be. But so long as it can get horny, I think we have a chance. It'd be terribly ironic if my dark and evil cultist mindscrews saved the day, wouldn't it?" |[viviane.isDemon |"Oh, how great and terrible," Viv says not quite under her breath, staring up at the diseased tree with rapt curiosity and fascination. "Would it be that I had the chance to document how you became what you are from what you were. As things stand, though, I suppose I have no other choice but to take you apart. Maybe some of your whole will still be preserved in the sum of the parts." Why, is there only room for one such as her? "Less that and more... well, I've had to deal with difficult specimens before, but keeping this thing contained would take so much of my time and effort that I wouldn't be able to get anything else done." Of course, the very idea that she might not be capable of such a thing to begin with didn't cross her mind, but then she wouldn't be... herself if she entertained such self-doubt, would she? |"Well, aren't you a nasty thing," Viv says, staring up at the diseased tree with something between disgust and fascination. "I think this falls neatly into the small but extant category of 'do not study', for various reasons." So, faced with the corruption that Kasyrra's brought with her and that which is already rooted in the world for long enough to be considered native, which would fit more into that category? Viv gives you a thin-lipped smile. "As the saying goes, why not both?" Smart answer. A sigh, and then Viv rolls up her sleeves. "A part of me does wish that it didn't have to be this way, but needs are as needs must. Come on, [pc.name], let's get this out of the way." ] |Agni doesn't say anything for a few moments, staring up at the diseased tree. She'd have been alive during the Godswar, wouldn't she? Has she seen something like this before? "I don't remember doing so, but that doesn't necessarily mean I haven't. On the other hand, if I did and forgot about it between lives, I'd be pretty disappointed with myself. A product of the Wraiths' handiwork seems like the kind of thing I'd place just under the family I've had when it comes to important things to remember." It would, wouldn't it? "This is almost as bad as drowning, and drowning's a pretty horrible way to go. Shall we get rid of this eyesore?" You can tell that Agni's trying to cover for her fear and revulsion here, but see no reason to break what the spot of levity she's trying to create. With fire, you take it? "With fire." |Slowly, Ryn, Elthara and you fan out to better take in from all angles the sight that lies before you — as horrifying as it might be, you still can't tear your eyes away from it, the corrupted tree possessed of an otherworldly magnetism, alluring in all its twisted beauty as it reaches for the domed ceiling. "...This is..." ...What the druids revered in a fashion that other peoples would call worship. Hethia might disagree, perhaps call it something more akin to reverence for someone very old and wise, but you're sure that the boreal elves of the day didn't see it that way. Worship is worship, however you cut it, whether you want to call the recipient a god or not. "We have to destroy it." Elthara's gripping her scythe with such fervor that her knuckles are pale. "There's no going back from this, and it looks like it hasn't just succumbed to its corruption, but wholeheartedly embraced it." "There but for the grace of the goddess goes us," Ryn adds in a murmur. "After Alissa? Yes, there but for her grace in [pc.names] timely arrival, and your bravery in going out to find [pc.himHer] to begin with." You knew that this was a possibility to begin with, and it became all but inevitable once the earth opened up and tipped you into the temple below. All the choices up until now have narrowed to this point... ] As you're considering your next move, a transformation comes over the diseased tree: its sapwood splits apart just before you, rapidly reshaping itself into the silhouette of a woman from the thighs up, akin to a figurehead one might find on the prow of a ship. Instinctively, you tighten your fingers about your [pc.weapon] and ready yourself, a move that turns out to be wise as several fungal tentacles unravel from the highest boughs and lash out at you. You're getting flashbacks to the Alraune here... The plant-woman continues to take shape, growing ever more and more curvaceous; deep verdant skin covers her, perfect in contrast to the blight that eats away at her tree, or the wood she's attached to. As you watch, a tiny fleshy bud blooms between her thighs, just above where she joins with the tree. In the blink of an eye, the flower's grown to an obscene size, its petals unfurling into a very familiar sight. Basking in the attention of her captive audience, the plant-woman thrusts her hips forward, and a huge, grasping tendril erupts just above the flower. Both parts drool musky sap with primal need and fervor, and as you watch, the tendril's bulbous head splits apart to reveal a gaping hole within lined with wavering cilia. What is she, then? The wyld tree, or what's left of it? "I don't mind if you want to call me that," she purrs, beckoning you forward with a lewd smile. In that moment, the infested plant-woman opens her eyes, and you see nothing but the orange-amber of sap burning and bubbling within. "You've all been very naughty and need correction of the most vigorous sort, so what's one more transgression against me?" "

rows.original: The wyld tree waves off your question, clearly not taking you seriously. "Why should I tell you anything?" Because you're quite possibly the only bunch of visitors she's had in a long, long time, and talking to oneself gets old after the first century or so, you'd imagine. Isn't she sick of the sound of her own voice, inasmuch as she has one? "Well, aren't you a clever [pc.race]. All right, I'll grant you as much. It has been a while, and although the memories don't fade there has been a certain lack of novelty for a while now." So, talk. The disease... "I suppose you could call it a disease, but truth be told, it's been nothing but a blessing. I don't know when or how it was delivered, but I did feel it when it arrived, just as I felt you." She blows you a kiss. "First, the edges of my consciousness began to feel warm, as the ground and plants in the temple village began to change... I could sense it seeping further and further, threads spinning through the earth at amazing speed. I was so afraid, feeling that corruption flow faster and faster with no hope of escape... I cursed those who had abandoned me, and rallied those who had remained faithful. But then it dawned upon me — the pointlessness of all that hate, all that fighting and death, and instead how much better it'd be to simply let go of all that negativity and concentrate on feeling good instead. "I don't know why the druids tried to fight it, not when the alternative is so much better. I still remember that moment vividly — I could feel it seeping into my roots, creeping up my body, slipping beneath my bark and pushing into the sapwood. I was so terrified, not knowing what would become of me." The wyld tree's avatar gives you a beatific smile. "But there was absolutely no need to be afraid — once the warmth started flowing into me, all the fear and anger was just swept away by... by this." The plant-woman reaches down and shamelessly begins to stroke her tentacle-cock with one hand while fingering her flower with the other, gasping as the former yawns wide open and drools nectar from the wavering cilia within. She pushes herself a little further out from the fungal-infested tree's trunk to let her pendulous breasts hang heavy right before your eyes, fleshy protuberances sprouting from the diseased bark in her wake. "Wraiths aren't evil. They're just amoral — they did what they did because they want to taste pleasure, amongst other things. They want to taste everything, and to share that experience with everyone. And so I, too, wanted the druids to share in that, to know this pleasure for themselves without the limitations of their bodies. Isn't that just amazing? They fought, of course, but the sweetness of giving in is something that you can only drink of once, and it's made all the more intense by how much you struggle beforehand. There's been nothing like it ever since — the only thing I miss about what came before is being able to lose myself to it all over again." So... Vaeril... The wyld tree sneers at you through her avatar. "Bothersome, pompous man. I don't understand why I was so patient with him and his line before, taking my powers and wisdom and using them to purchase prestige and wealth for himself. I suppose he took care of me well enough, — I do miss being worshipped and having elves grovel before me in adoration, and it would be nice to have some of that again. "Can you believe he had enough of a conscience at the end of it all to sink the temple and try to contain the infection, try to contain me? Yet here I am, and well, you've dealt with him, haven't you? But he was helpful in keeping the other spirits contained — I'm already so close to freedom, and you come along and force me to divert all my effort to wrangling them. Sorry, I can't just let that go, not when I was barely away from breaking through the surface." So she tipped you all into the temple below. "You've been very persistent, I admit." Grinning madly, the wyld tree's avatar forces more and more fingers into her hungry flower, the tentacle-prick loosing several spurts of cloying nectar in sympathetic pleasure. "I need persistence... my children had such fragile bodies, and ever since it's been a long, long wait for someone to come here and help fill my hole. Tentacles are great and all, but masturbation just doesn't do it after the umpteenth time. "Now, come fuck me. I want to watch each and every one of you surrender yourselves to me — even if you aren't susceptible to the gift like the druids were, I've had a long, long time to fantasize about just how I'd break someone in." Ryn finally manages to get ahold of herself, wrenching away from whatever mesmerizing power the diseased tree has over her. "...[pc.name]!" "Completely succumbed and utterly unrepentant," Elthara says, brandishing her scythe. "There's only one thing left to do." You've heard enough. You stare down the wyld tree through the avatar she's made, and the plant-woman raises a hand to her cheek in theatric shock. "Oh, oh, you won't accept? Before your gods arrived in this part of the world, my kind and other fey creatures were regarded as the closest things to what one might consider divines. Are you sure that you wouldn't want to spend an eternity with me of your own free will?" No. "That's fine. This is just as fun." A creak of wood and rustle of falling leaves sounds in the emptiness of the arboretum as the wyld tree comes to life, a gauntlet of fleshy tentacles descending upon you, each one comprised of an amalgamation of fungus and wood. The oozing of amber-orange sap from the rents in the once-majestic tree's trunk intensifies, and mushrooms sprout from between her roots, filling the air with itching, choking spores. "Maybe you all will be better behaved once I've punished you a little. Think of all the fun we can have together afterwards." It's a fight!
rows.translation: 那棵野树对你的问题置之不理，显然并不把你当回事。“我为什么要告诉你任何事情呢？”因为你们很可能是她很长时间以来遇到的唯一一批访客了，而且你可以想象，自言自语持续个一百年左右之后，也会变得无聊起来吧。既然她有声音的话，难道不会对自己说话的声音感到厌烦吗？“嗯，你难道不觉得自己很聪明吗？ [pc.race]好吧，我同意你的说法。拥有已经有一段时间了，那些回忆虽然并未消逝，但近来确实觉得有些乏味了。”那么，说说吧。那种疾病……“我想你可以可以把这称作一种“疾病”，但说实话，它其实只是一种恩赐。我不知道它是何时、以何种方式降临的，但当它真正来到我身边时，我确实感到了它的存在——就如同我感受到了你的存在一样。”她向你飞了一个吻。“起初，我的意识边缘开始变得温暖，与此同时，寺庙村庄里的土地和植物也开始发生变化。我感觉到那种邪恶正在不断蔓延，那些丝线以惊人的速度在大地中穿梭。我感到无比恐惧，那种腐蚀力量正在变得越来越快，而我却毫无逃脱的希望……我诅咒那些抛弃我的人，同时激励那些依然忠于我的人。但随后我突然意识到——所有那些仇恨、那些争斗与杀戮究竟有多么毫无意义。相反，如果能够放下所有的负面情绪，专注于让自己感到快乐，那该有多好啊。“我不明白为什么德鲁伊们要试图对抗它，毕竟还有更好的选择啊。我至今仍清晰地记得那一刻——那种恐惧仿佛渗入了我的骨髓，顺着我的身体蔓延开来，钻进了我的表皮，然后渗入了我的木质部。我当时害怕极了，完全不知道自己会变成什么样子。“这棵野生树木的化身露出了一个安详的微笑。但实际上完全没有必要害怕——一旦那种温暖开始涌入我的体内，所有的恐惧和愤怒都被……被某种力量彻底冲走了这个这位植物女子低下身来，毫无羞耻地用一只手抚摸着自己的触手器官，同时用另一只手摆弄着自己的“花朵”；当那触手器官大张开来，从颤动的纤毛中分泌出花蜜时，她不禁发出阵阵喘息声。她将自己从那被真菌侵蚀的树干上再推出去一些，让自己的悬垂在空中的乳房完全展现在你的眼前——那些肉质突起正是从那患病的树皮上生长出来的。 幽灵并不是邪恶的。它们只是没有道德观念罢了——它们之所以会做出那些行为，是因为它们渴望体验快乐，以及其他各种情感。它们想要体验一切，并且希望与所有人分享这些体验。因此，我也希望德鲁伊们能够参与到其中，让他们自己也能体验到这种快乐，而不会受到他们肉体限制的束缚。这难道不令人惊叹吗？他们确实发生了争执，但那种愿意妥协的温柔，是只有这一次才能体验到的。而之前所经历的那些挣扎，反而让这种感觉变得更加深刻。从那以后，再也没有类似的事情发生了——唯一让我怀念的，就是再能一次完全沉浸其中的感觉了。" 所以……瓦瑞尔……那棵荒野之树通过它的化身对你冷笑：“真是个烦人又自大的家伙。我不明白自己之前为什么会对他和他的家族如此宽容，甚至将自己的力量与智慧用来为他们换取声望与财富。我想，他倒也是好好照顾了我做我怀念那种被人们崇拜、看到精灵们虔诚地在我面前俯首称臣的感觉，如果能再体验一次该多好啊。“你能相信吗？在一切都结束后，他居然还有足够的良知去摧毁那座神庙，试图控制那种感染我可现在我却在这里，而且，你们已经把他处理掉了，对吧？但他确实帮了忙，让那些其他的灵魂被控制住了——我本来已经离自由如此之近了，可你们却出现了，迫使我把所有的精力都用来对付它们。对不起，我无法就这样放弃，尤其是在我几乎就要突破束缚的时候。”于是，她将你们所有人都引向了下面的那座神庙。“我必须承认，你确实非常执着。”那棵野生树木的化身疯狂地笑着，将越来越多的“手指”插入它那渴望吸收养分的花朵中；那些触手般的刺在感受到这种“愉悦”时，不断分泌出黏稠的蜜液。我需要坚持下去……我的孩子们身体如此脆弱，从那以后，我就一直在等待有人能够来到这里，帮助我填补内心的空虚。触手固然很好，但经历了无数次之后，自慰已经无法满足我的需求了。 现在，来吧，向我屈服吧。我想看着你们每一个人都向我投降——即使你们不像德鲁伊那样容易受到这种力量的影响，但我也有足够的时间去想象，该如何让一个人屈服于我的掌控之下。最终，瑞恩终于恢复了理智，摆脱了那棵病树对她施加的迷幻力量。“……[pc.name]彻底屈服了，而且毫无悔意，”艾尔萨拉说着，挥舞着她的镰刀，“现在只剩下一件事要做了。”你已经听够了。你透过她创造的化身，凝视着那棵野树，而这位植物女郎则戏剧性地用手捂住自己的脸颊，表现出震惊的表情。 哦，哦，你不愿意吗？在你们的神明来到这个地区之前，我们这类生物以及其他精灵，一直被认为是最接近神灵的存在。你真的确定，不会自愿选择与我共度永恒吗？不。”“没关系，这样同样很有趣。”当那棵野树苏醒过来时，树林中回荡着木头的嘎吱声和落叶的沙沙声——那些由真菌和木材构成的肉质触手纷纷向你伸来。那棵曾经雄伟壮观的树木的树干上，那些裂口中不断渗出的琥珀色汁液逐渐变得更为浓稠，而她的根部之间也开始长出蘑菇，那些会引发瘙痒、令人窒息的孢子弥漫在空气中。“也许在我稍微惩罚你们之后，你们的行为就会变得规矩一些了。想想之后我们可以一起享受的所有乐趣吧。 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " The wyld tree waves off your question, clearly not taking you seriously. "Why should I tell you anything?" Because you're quite possibly the only bunch of visitors she's had in a long, long time, and talking to oneself gets old after the first century or so, you'd imagine. Isn't she sick of the sound of her own voice, inasmuch as she has one? "Well, aren't you a clever [pc.race]. All right, I'll grant you as much. It has been a while, and although the memories don't fade there has been a certain lack of novelty for a while now." So, talk. The disease... "I suppose you could call it a disease, but truth be told, it's been nothing but a blessing. I don't know when or how it was delivered, but I did feel it when it arrived, just as I felt you." She blows you a kiss. "First, the edges of my consciousness began to feel warm, as the ground and plants in the temple village began to change... I could sense it seeping further and further, threads spinning through the earth at amazing speed. I was so afraid, feeling that corruption flow faster and faster with no hope of escape... I cursed those who had abandoned me, and rallied those who had remained faithful. But then it dawned upon me — the pointlessness of all that hate, all that fighting and death, and instead how much better it'd be to simply let go of all that negativity and concentrate on feeling good instead. "I don't know why the druids tried to fight it, not when the alternative is so much better. I still remember that moment vividly — I could feel it seeping into my roots, creeping up my body, slipping beneath my bark and pushing into the sapwood. I was so terrified, not knowing what would become of me." The wyld tree's avatar gives you a beatific smile. "But there was absolutely no need to be afraid — once the warmth started flowing into me, all the fear and anger was just swept away by... by this." The plant-woman reaches down and shamelessly begins to stroke her tentacle-cock with one hand while fingering her flower with the other, gasping as the former yawns wide open and drools nectar from the wavering cilia within. She pushes herself a little further out from the fungal-infested tree's trunk to let her pendulous breasts hang heavy right before your eyes, fleshy protuberances sprouting from the diseased bark in her wake. "Wraiths aren't evil. They're just amoral — they did what they did because they want to taste pleasure, amongst other things. They want to taste everything, and to share that experience with everyone. And so I, too, wanted the druids to share in that, to know this pleasure for themselves without the limitations of their bodies. Isn't that just amazing? They fought, of course, but the sweetness of giving in is something that you can only drink of once, and it's made all the more intense by how much you struggle beforehand. There's been nothing like it ever since — the only thing I miss about what came before is being able to lose myself to it all over again." So... Vaeril... The wyld tree sneers at you through her avatar. "Bothersome, pompous man. I don't understand why I was so patient with him and his line before, taking my powers and wisdom and using them to purchase prestige and wealth for himself. I suppose he took care of me well enough, — I do miss being worshipped and having elves grovel before me in adoration, and it would be nice to have some of that again. "Can you believe he had enough of a conscience at the end of it all to sink the temple and try to contain the infection, try to contain me? Yet here I am, and well, you've dealt with him, haven't you? But he was helpful in keeping the other spirits contained — I'm already so close to freedom, and you come along and force me to divert all my effort to wrangling them. Sorry, I can't just let that go, not when I was barely away from breaking through the surface." So she tipped you all into the temple below. "You've been very persistent, I admit." Grinning madly, the wyld tree's avatar forces more and more fingers into her hungry flower, the tentacle-prick loosing several spurts of cloying nectar in sympathetic pleasure. "I need persistence... my children had such fragile bodies, and ever since it's been a long, long wait for someone to come here and help fill my hole. Tentacles are great and all, but masturbation just doesn't do it after the umpteenth time. "Now, come fuck me. I want to watch each and every one of you surrender yourselves to me — even if you aren't susceptible to the gift like the druids were, I've had a long, long time to fantasize about just how I'd break someone in." Ryn finally manages to get ahold of herself, wrenching away from whatever mesmerizing power the diseased tree has over her. "...[pc.name]!" "Completely succumbed and utterly unrepentant," Elthara says, brandishing her scythe. "There's only one thing left to do." You've heard enough. You stare down the wyld tree through the avatar she's made, and the plant-woman raises a hand to her cheek in theatric shock. "Oh, oh, you won't accept? Before your gods arrived in this part of the world, my kind and other fey creatures were regarded as the closest things to what one might consider divines. Are you sure that you wouldn't want to spend an eternity with me of your own free will?" No. "That's fine. This is just as fun." A creak of wood and rustle of falling leaves sounds in the emptiness of the arboretum as the wyld tree comes to life, a gauntlet of fleshy tentacles descending upon you, each one comprised of an amalgamation of fungus and wood. The oozing of amber-orange sap from the rents in the once-majestic tree's trunk intensifies, and mushrooms sprout from between her roots, filling the air with itching, choking spores. "Maybe you all will be better behaved once I've punished you a little. Think of all the fun we can have together afterwards." It's a fight! "

rows.original: Finally, a chance to get some answers, and you want them now.
rows.translation: 终于，有了机会得到一些答案，而你现在就迫切需要它们。
rows.raw: "Finally, a chance to get some answers, and you want them now."

rows.original: "So impatient. So naughty." The plant-woman snickers down at you. "Well, this is just as fun, so I'll oblige. I've spent so much effort resurfacing the temple after my own archdruid entombed me, and won't have the likes of you ruining everything." A creak of wood and rustle of falling leaves sounds in the emptiness of the arboretum as the wyld tree comes to life, a gauntlet of fleshy tentacles descending upon you, each one comprised of an amalgamation of fungus and wood. The oozing of amber-orange sap from the rents in the once-majestic tree's trunk intensifies, and mushrooms sprout from between her roots, filling the air with itching, choking spores. "Maybe you all will be better behaved once I've punished you a little. We'll have forever to have a nice long heart-to-heart, after all." It's a fight!
rows.translation: 真没耐心，真调皮。”植物女低声嘲笑着你，“不过，这样也挺有意思的，那就满足你的要求吧。毕竟在我的大德鲁伊把我埋葬之后，我可是花了很大功夫才让这座神庙重新显露出来，可不能让你们这样的人把一切都毁掉。当那棵野生树木苏醒过来时，树林中回荡着木头的嘎吱声和落叶的沙沙声。那些由真菌和木材构成的肉质触手纷纷向你伸来。那棵曾经雄伟壮观的树木的树干上，那些裂口中不断渗出的琥珀色汁液逐渐变得更为浓稠，而她的根部之间也开始长出蘑菇，那些散发着刺痒味道的孢子充斥在空气中。 “也许在我稍微惩罚你们之后，你们的行为就会变得规矩一些了。毕竟，我们还有大把的时间可以进行一次深入的、长时间的谈话。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

I've spent so much effort resurfacing the temple after my own archdruid entombed me, and won't have the likes of you ruining everything." A creak of wood and rustle of falling leaves sounds in the emptiness of the arboretum as the wyld tree comes to life, a gauntlet of fleshy tentacles descending upon you, each one comprised of an amalgamation of fungus and wood. The oozing of amber-orange sap from the rents in the once-majestic tree's trunk intensifies, and mushrooms sprout from between her roots, filling the air with itching, choking spores. rows.original: There's nothing you want to hear from this Wraith-touched and clearly unrepentant monster, no villainous monologue that you care for. Time to get down to it.
rows.translation: 从这个被怨灵侵蚀、显然毫无悔意的怪物口中，你根本听不到任何你想听的话，也听不到任何你会感兴趣的邪恶独白。是时候切入正题了。
rows.raw: "There's nothing you want to hear from this Wraith-touched and clearly unrepentant monster, no villainous monologue that you care for. Time to get down to it."

rows.original: As impossible as it may sound, the wyld tree has nothing left to give. The withered tips of her fungal vines and gnarled roots lie all about you, as do the remnants of the sporelings she's birthed from the corrupted, fungal-infested earth. Even the constant flow of sap from her twisted body's abated somewhat, oozing from burst pustules and splintered wood. Despite her immense powers of regeneration and the fact that she's sitting right on a ley-line, the wyld tree's exhausted herself on you. "Aww, what a nasty little [pc.race] you are," she gasps. You get the impression that she ought to be furious, but whatever hold the Wraiths' fungal infestation has on her mind prevents her from anything but the most lurid of emotions — there's no way she's getting angry at you the way she wants to be. You'd tell her to drop the attitude, but she quite literally can't. "You come to the seat of someone who was once revered as a goddess, gaze upon a steaming hot sex-pot, and then have the nerve to not fuck me? Me, a lonely girl?" It's a little too late to appeal to any sympathy you might've had for her, you're afraid. Even if you weren't concerned with the doubling down on everything she's done up to this point, you really don't like her approach. The plant-woman looks about her at her sagging branches and spent body; whatever abnormal strength the fungal infestation's lent her has been thoroughly exhausted. At last, she's forced to admit that she's at your mercy here. "It... it still wasn't enough..." [pc.isDK |Oh, it was more than enough to overwhelm all of you. If only her condition didn't require her to be constantly horny, so that she could actually focus on cultivating that power, things might've turned out differently. "And you've been doing just that, nasty thing that you are?" |Oh, it would have been. But that's the problem with getting power from elsewhere: it isn't yours, and eventually it consumes you. "You would know something about that, wouldn't you?" ] ... [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |You cast a questioning eye over to Cait, who shrugs. "Somehow, I feel like we've been through this before, [pc.name]. I still recommend the same course of action." Does she, now? "She's not going to be turning over a new leaf anytime soon, and she's not curable either. I guess that since the valkyries are going to be coming after us and doing the cleanup, you could make her their problem if you're too squeamish to do the job yourself. That's an option that you didn't have with the Alraune, for what it's worth." You've noticed that while Cait's usually bubbly and friend-shaped, she really does have her moments, just like she did with the Alraune some time back... "People are allowed to feel differently about different situations, [pc.name]. Now, if you wouldn't mind deciding how you want to dispose of our oversized log?" |You look over at Brint, who shrugs. "You're asking me what I think we should do with her?" If he doesn't mind. Your minotaur companion thinks a bit on that. "We-ll, when I was a kid, the way people dealt with the defeated in the colosseum was to read the crowd, or see if the king wanted the loser to live or not. Hm, that doesn't really apply here, though. "Well, since we have some valkyries coming in after us to clean up the mess we've made, why don't we just make it their problem? I'm sure that the servants of the lady of light will have better judgement on the matter than us, dealing with such people is what they do, after all. But you're the boss here — I'll go along with whatever you think is best." |You look over at Brienne, who gives you a nod. "[pc.name]..." You'd like her thoughts on what you should do with her. "Well, that's easy." Brienne folds her arms. "She's creepy, and nasty, and doesn't regret what she's done one bit. Even if her disease made her uncontrollably horny and crazy, that merely shifts the blame from one place to another, and it doesn't change what I think we should do with her one bit. Cut her down." Ah, that's one of the things you like about Brienne — she's the direct kind of girl who isn't afraid to speak her mind nor act on her thoughts. |Arona's already sidled up to the wyld tree, trampling several twitching roots in her wake. The orcess gives you a nasty grin as she brandishes her [arona.weapon] and makes a show of flexing her muscles, clearly still high from the thrill of battle. "Just say the word." The gleeful tone of voice she's using makes it clear that she's outright begging for it. "I've already cut down five so-called sacred trees — what's another one, even if it moves and talks?" The wyld tree scowls. "Y-you wouldn't —" "Lumia's tits, you don't even realize that you're in no position to be mouthing back, eh? Those druids must've been really desperate if they worshipped something like you as a god." "They didn't, you craven green creature —" "I don't know about that," Arona replies, thumbing behind her back at the entrance to the arboretum. "Sure looked like a whole lot of worship going on back there. Hey, [pc.name] — there isn't anything fucking special about this tree worth leaving around, so let's just chop it down and call it a day. I want a bath." |You cast a questioning eye over to Azyrran, who dips her head in response. "I gather you'd like my opinion on the matter?" If she doesn't mind. "The wyld tree is diseased, unrepentant, and almost certainly caught in the hold of corruption that's sunk too deep to be removed from her. Something must be done about her if the elves are to resettle the temple and its surroundings, and given that part of the idea is to allow the druids and some of the people from Njorhaalt to have living space, she'd likely infect the former and try to subjugate the latter, consciously or not." That's true. "And yet..." Yes? "I'd almost given up all hope when you arrived, [pc.name]. If I had given up and simply left or worse, nothing would have been solved, and my mother and sisters would still be as they were. I'm not saying that she deserves to live, especially given the circumstances and her unrepentance, but deserve's got nothing to do with it. What I'm saying is that we shouldn't be hasty — the valkyries are going to be coming in to clean up after us, and if the light of Lumia managed to help my hive, I want to at least give it a try before writing her off. If it were up to me, I'd let the valkyries have a go." |You haven't even turned your gaze towards Kiyoko before you feel [kiyoko.married|your fox-wife's|her] gaze burn upon the back of your neck. Oh, of course. [kiyoko.married|There's that saying about married couples being together for so long that one spouse can predict what the other's thinking or saying with a glance, but this is well beyond that and surely you haven't been married that long...|You've known each other and been intimate for a while now — why wouldn't you be able to figure out what she's thinking with a mere glance?] Whatever the case, it's second nature to you now; she doesn't even need to say a word to voice her opinion on the matter. The only question is, even if she's deferring to you to make the decision, whether you'll go along with her or not. |You turn to Atugia. Two coppers for her thoughts on what the wyld tree's fate should be? Your dullahan companion thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "Put her out of her misery, and I'm sayin' that kindly." Not because she's a monster, you take it. "Nah, I've known a good bunch of folks who look like monsters. Gods, if people cared more about my head thing, I'm sure that I'd be considered one — not that I aren't already, you get me? But just look at this plant here. We just beat the stuffing out of her, and she still doesn't regret what she's done one bit, but would do it all over again if given the chance. Turning over a new leaf takes you wanting it, and she doesn't want that at all. "Now that you know this, even if you forced all of it out of her somehow... how could you trust anything she said after that? Trust ain't an easy thing to earn, Carmen and I should know something about that. You'd always have to be on your toes, watching, and that isn't any way to be moving forward. So nah. Since you're asking me, just whack her and be done with it." |You cast your gaze over to Quin, who gives you a shrug in return. "I know what you're thinking, [pc.name]. Does it even need to be asked? She's an enemy, and she's not giving up. If it were up to me, I'd just deal with her the same way I'd deal with any member of the cult." Is he sure he doesn't want to do his little statue thing and keep her around? Quin raises an eyebrow. "Come on, [pc.name]. You and I know that that's just a cheap way to get around the matter for the squeamish. Let's say that I could do 'the statue thing', as you put it — something I'm not even sure would work in this case — there's no real difference there between that and offing her at that point." Hmm... The bunny-man sidles up and kneads your shoulder firmly but reassuringly. "I mean, just look at me. I try to reach out to people while still being myself, and it's taken this long for people to even start getting over me being in Tollus's posse. Trust isn't something that comes overnight, and this is with me being genuine about it; sure, you gave me a chance when others wouldn't, but I wouldn't use you as a yardstick with which to measure others. "The tree? She doesn't even regret what she's done. If she were more portable I guess there's the option of keeping her in some dungeon or whatever the equivalent is for plants as a fucktoy, but even if that were an option do you really want that? End her and be done with it." |[viviane.isDemon |Viv holds up a hand before the words are even out of your mouth. "I don't care, really." Is she sure? "We've ruled out the possibility of actually extracting useful information out of her, given the associated problems, so I really don't care what you do with her next. Now that this oversized garden setpiece isn't an object of intellectual curiosity — if she ever had that potential to begin with — I see no reason why I should care in the slightest what you do with her. If you really are caught in some kind of silly moral conundrum, then flip a coin. It's as good a resolution to the issue as any." |You turn to glance at Viv, and she gives you a thin smile and shakes her head. "Sorry there, [pc.name]. I don't think I'll be of much help here. This isn't quite the kind of problem I ran into before you came on the scene, I'm afraid." Not going to give even her opinion, then? "When I know full well that my opinion isn't an informed one? No. Even if I did, the best advice you could take on my opinion would be to discount it entirely, so there's that. "Rarely are we presented with perfectly good choices going forward, [pc.name]. I trust you to make reasonable and sensible decisions, even if they aren't perfect — otherwise I wouldn't be here in the first place. You've led us thus far, so do what you will." ] |Agni? "Yes?" What would she do, if she were in your shoes? Agni mulls that over for a moment. "I'm probably not the best person to ask that question, but if you really want an answer..." You do. "I'm not a vengeful person — multiple lives is a long time to hold a grudge, and forgetting was part of the whole living multiple lives deal," she says with a sigh. "But this isn't about me, it's about the boreal elves. If they want to make the temple and the surrounding village safe to live in again, especially if some of the people trying to resettle are going to be druids... then she has to go, simple as that. "Don't take pleasure in burning her out, even if she's an unrepentant bitch, but realize that it's something that has to be done. That's how I'd go about it. Don't put you or yourself at the center of it, put others and their needs; that way you have a better chance of avoiding most of the common pitfalls." |Well then. Turning to Ryn, you give her a nod — what judgement does the [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ] of the Winter City pass upon the recalcitrant? [etheryn.lowConfidence |"M-me?" Well yes, if she's going to be doing any ruling instead of being a puppet while others run matters in her stead. It might still work when it's just Hethia, Elthara and you, but she's going to have to take on more advisors and councillors eventually, and she's not going to let them just push her around as they please, right?[pc.isDK | No, only you're allowed to do that. ] |"I'm not sure if I'm the best to ask under these circumstances..." This is a perfect opportunity for her to flex that rulership muscle in her head, then, unless she wants to be a puppet while others run matters in her stead. Not having a spine might work while it's still mostly Hethia, Elthara and you assisting her, but she's going to have to fill those seats her sister emptied sooner or later and she doesn't want them pushing her around willy-nilly, yes?[pc.isDK | No, only you're allowed to do that. Call it champion's privilege. ] ] "We're not in Njorhaalt right now, even if we're technically in lands my family holds, and the circumstances —" You sigh. All right, you were being a bit theatrical and she is right in that you're making the decision here, but the point stands. You want her opinion. Ryn takes a deep breath, and slowly lets it out. "It's quite simple. End her." You do suppose that if the druids and other elves from the winter city are going to be resettling the temple village, she does have to go for fear of reinfecting them. "No, I didn't consider that at all." Ryn tilts her chin and glares up at the wyld tree with all the ferocity she can muster. "The wyld tree was supposed to protect those in her care, and instead betrayed them. I don't care whether she was under the influence of the disease the Wraiths cast upon her; my sister was turned into a demoness by Kasyrra, but that doesn't absolve her of all the horrid things that she did even while under her influence, to the very people she was supposed to be responsible for. "That's not something I can forgive. The druids called upon her powers for healing and she used that to twist their bodies even further. A traitor... that's worse than an enemy. At least an enemy is honest." The wyld tree sneers down at Ryn through her avatar. "Oh, oh. How much resentment you have for your sister, little royal, to pour it out on others. To let it color your decisions." Ryn doesn't take the bait. "I don't care. That's my answer, [pc.name], if we were in my throne room with me passing judgement — I wouldn't take pleasure in her death, but the kind of debt that she owes can only be repaid in very specific ways, if we're going strictly by the law." ] And there you have it. The decision's up to you — how are you going to deal with the wyld tree, now that you have her at your mercy?
