Kiyoko's got a pretty solid head start on her, but if she's determined to see this through... it's hard to think of your daughter doing what he mother does. "Sure, trying to play with a lot of people at once tires me out really quickly. But I know where to go if I want a quick nap, the same way Mama sends us all out to play when she wants to be alone for a bit. It just requires you be an excellent manager and to learn how to properly entrust people with delegated authority." Those are some awfully big words for an eight-year old to use... "I'm not just any eight-year old kitsune, I'm Big Sis! I'm also [kinu.Dad]'s fusspet, but that's another thing. Since I'm doing good these days, do you think I deserve a reward?" Ah, some things never change. |"Since there're so many of us, we're all good at different things. Seems like there isn't a skill or job that one of my brothers or sisters isn't talented in. I, of course, am the super-duper best!" Oh, really? Kinu nods enthusiastically. "See, like it's great to be talented at things. But it's really great to be talented at learning things, because then you can be great at everything! So long as you put in the effort, that is. Some days, I'd rather nap." If she's got that much potential, she'd better not waste it. "Hee hee, how do you think so many of my brothers and sisters know what they do? I taught them, of course! Teaching is a great way to reinforce what you yourself have learnt, it's great! You should try it sometime, [kinu.Dad]!" |"One of my brothers came up this morning and asked really nicely if I could darn a hole in his sock for him. So I did! He was really thankful, and that made me happy as well!" It's nice to know that she's making herself useful to everyone, not just her mother. "I don't know why, especially since I'd have been pretty annoyed at anyone who asked before, but it's all good. Still, there's one thing that's bothering me..." And what would that be? "He's been following me around all day, hoping to repay the favor. I know we are commanded by Lord Keros to pay back any genuine kindness shown to us, but maybe that's taking it a little too far... if anything, he's doing the exact opposite by annoying me, but I still haven't the heart to tell him to go away." On one hand, patience is a virtue. On the other, she needs to stand up for herself. |"So, I heard Mama make a really odd joke..." Yes? "She said that she's had enough kids to field both sides of a sporting event, if not more. I'm not exactly sure why this is supposed to be funny, but it had her in stitches for a good while. Having this many siblings is a thing I take quite seriously." Perhaps, but it's also good to be able to see the funny side of things. A little levity goes a long way, especially on the longer days. "I don't get it..." |"When I look back on every day, it really strikes me as to how well I'm doing," Kinu tells you proudly. "I didn't really realize it until I put things down to paper, but there's sooooo much work involved in feeding, clothing, wrangling and instructing everyone. Mama calls it logistics, and says that it's good practice for what I'll be doing later in life." Is it? "Must be, because I don't really notice it anymore. I just gotta say a few words, and things kinda run by themselves now that everyone knows what they have to do." Your daughter reaches up and scratches a large, furry ear. "It's all one big mess, but it's an orderly mess, and I don't think I'd have it any other way. Did you know how much everyone eats every day? It surprised me when I sat down to do the numbers." ] ]"

rows.original: [rand|"Hey, don't tell Mama that I told you, but she used to be terrible at cooking." Did she? The way she's so proficient in the kitchen, you'd never have guessed. "Yep! When she was younger, Mama was so busy studying magic and divination that she didn't have time for anything else. Besides, as the den mother's firstborn daughter, she always had other people around to do the cooking for her, so she never quite needed it... all that changed, of course, and she suddenly had a lot of time on her hands and no one around to prepare meals." And what of little Kinu? Will she learn to cook, too? Kinu broadens her stance a little and gives you the most serious look her adorable round face can muster. "[kinu.Dad], I will learn all the things. It would be a shame to waste my inheritance, wouldn't it?" Haha. There's a clever girl. Kinu preens at the praise, looking very pleased with herself. |"There's an underground river that flows beneath the roots of the home tree; we have a basement so we can get to it. The water there's really cold and clear, so we use it for all sorts of things! Not bathing, though! Hot water is for bathing, cold water is for drinking! "Oh! Also, we put fresh-picked veggies from the fields in netted boxes, then put those into the stream to chill! Veggies taste so much better when they've been chilled with cold clean water!" |"Did you know that dried persimmons are really yummy? You wouldn't know it, especially since they're really sour when fresh. But then there's something about the drying process that takes out all that tartness and leaves only a delicious fruity flavor. It's amazing, hee hee!" |"Noon is the most awful time of day," your daughter declares. This ought to be good. You're all ears. "Mm-hm. My tummy gets growly and rumbly, then I feel tired and don't want to do anything but wait for lunch. But then after I've eaten, I feel all nice and full, and don't want to do anything but nap in the sun. Of course, there's always chores to be done around then, so I don't get to do any of that... and then by the time I can go out to play or nap, the feeling's passed." Very convincing, except for the fact that you know that eating's not much of a necessity on the astral plane, and that Kiyoko mostly does mealtimes to give structure to her day. Kinu huffs and folds her arms, sulking. "Maybe it is to you and Mama, but I get awfully hungry..." |"I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" Ha! You reach down and tousle Kinu's hair, ruffling her large ears, and the little kitsune squeals in delight. Closing her eyes and bowing her head towards you, Kinu luxuriates in the simple bliss of affectionate human contact. "See? See?" She's as sensitive as her mother is, that's for sure; you have no doubt she'll make some other kitsune very happy when she grows up. Kinu looks a little disappointed when you finish petting her, but settles back with a wiggle of her ears and swish of her three tails. "I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" She already said that. "I know!" |"Growing taller takes so long," Kinu grumps. Let's guess... she wants to be taller because then it'll be easier for her to reach the peaches on the higher branches? "I'm not saying anything..." She knows that there are other kinds of fruit which don't grow on trees, right? Maybe she could try planting a berry bush or two? Or how about some melons? Those are pretty good and grow close to the ground... "I'll think about it. Mama gets mad with me if I dig in the dirt too much." |"Are you going to play with Mama again today?" You're going to see her, yes. After all, you wouldn't come all this way onto the astral plane and leave without paying Kiyoko a visit, would you? "I didn't mean visit, I meant play." Now... what exactly does your foxy little darling daughter mean by play? "I'm not exactly sure, but I know you have a lot of fun because Mama only raises her voice like that when she's enjoying herself. It's okay, I like to play alone or just with someone else, too. Too many people at once tires me out quickly." Kinu thinks a moment. "Every time Mama is done playing with you, she becomes very happy for days on end... I'd like to see her happy more often. That's another way how I know you have lots of fun playing together." Uh, you most definitely do. "I like playing with you too, [kinu.Dad]." Okay, this conversation just got awkward. Time to change the subject. |"No one will play any board games with me," Kinu grumps, the little kitsune's ears drooping. Oh? Why's that? [kiyoko.numKits 0 2|A sigh. "Mama's always busy with... whatever it is she does. Half the time I see her, it's for lessons; the other half, it's for mealtimes and scolding me for getting myself all dirty. Well, if she doesn't want me to be dirty, maybe she should take a little while to play with me, right? Otherwise, I'm just going to dig in the dirt or find some peaches, because playing both sides of go gets really boring after a while..." |Kinu looks away, unwilling to meet your gaze. "My siblings won't play with me; they say I always win at go and shogi, and that it's not fun if they haven't even a chance at coming out ahead." You can understand where they're coming from, yes. Can't blame them for not wanting to throw themselves against an insurmountable wall like that. "Nor is it fun for me to walk all over them and win so easily. Mama's the only one who's capable of putting up any real opposition, and she can't play with me all the time, so I'm right back where I started." ] Well, now that you're here to visit, maybe you can entertain your fluffy daughter for a bit before going to be with her mother. It might not necessarily be a board game, but you definitely can spare a little time to play with her — after all, as you understand things, the passage of time in the astral plane doesn't quite completely map to that in the waking world. "I would really like that, [kinu.Dad]." [kiyoko.numKits 4|Although there is one thing... "What is it?" Why doesn't she coach her siblings in those games? Kinu blinks. Look, she herself admits that defeating an opponent who can barely fight back is boring, right? Clearly, the thing to do is to help her siblings get better, like a farmer fattening calves for the slaughter. That way her eventual triumph will be truly fulfilling, instead of the meaningless walkovers she's been having to date. As if on cue, Kinu's ears start wiggling. "Ooooooh. That's not a bad idea, [kinu.Dad]..." Of course, there's always the danger of the students surpassing the master, which is why she's got to improve as well. But she's a smart little thing; you're sure she can manage it. ] |"So the other day, I was sorting through where Mama keeps the spices..." That sounds interesting. Did she discover anything of note? "Yes! Yes! I discovered wasabi. Have you tasted the stuff, [kinu.Dad]? It's super-duper amazing!" No, not yet. Can she tell you what it tastes like? "Ehe. Kinda sorta..." Oh, from the furrowed brow on your little fusspet, this is going to be a good one. "See, [kinu.Dad], I was going to try, so I put a big whole dollop of it on my tongue, and then my tongue went numb. Then Mama noticed what I was doing, and made me wash out my mouth... my tongue's still numb, though. It feels kinda funny." Hah. Whatever this wasabi thing is, it's probably not something to be eaten directly, especially if it's a condiment of some sort. "I dunno about that, [kinu.Dad]. It's really great." ]
rows.translation: [rand|“嘿，别告诉妈妈是我说的——她以前做饭可难吃了。” 是吗？看她现在在厨房里那么熟练的样子，真想不到。 “可不是嘛！妈妈年轻的时候，光顾着研究魔法和占卜，根本没时间做别的。再说了，作为族长母亲的长女，她身边总有人替她做饭，所以她也一直没真正需要自己动手……不过后来当然就不一样了——她突然闲下来了，身边也没人给她做饭了。” 那咱们的小小娟呢？她也会学做饭吗？ 小娟调整了一下站姿，用那张圆嘟嘟的可爱脸蛋挤出了最认真的表情。“[kinu.Dad]，我要学所有东西。不好好继承这些本领，岂不是太可惜了？” 哈哈，真是个聪明的小丫头。 小娟听到夸奖，得意地挺了挺胸，满脸欢喜。 |“咱们家那棵大树根底下有一条地下河，我们有个地下室可以通到那儿。那水又凉又清，可以用来做很多事情！不过洗澡可不行——热水才是洗澡用的，冷水是用来喝的！” “哦对了！我们还会把田里新摘的蔬菜装进网袋里，放到溪水里冰镇！用清凉的干净水冰过的蔬菜，吃起来味道好多了！” |“你知道吗，柿子干特别好吃！你肯定想不到——新鲜的柿子明明酸得要命，可一晒成干，那股酸味就全没了，只剩下甜甜的果香。好神奇呢，嘿嘿！” |“中午是最讨厌的时候了。”你女儿宣布道。 这可得好好听听。你竖起耳朵。 “嗯嗯。我肚子会咕咕叫，然后整个人都懒洋洋的，什么都不想干，只想等着吃午饭。可吃完了吧，又觉得饱饱的，什么都不想干，只想在太阳底下打盹。但偏偏那时候总有一堆家务等着我，哪样都做不了……等终于有空出去玩或者打盹了，那股劲头又过去了。” 说得挺有道理，不过你知道在星界，吃东西其实不是必须的——清子安排一日三餐，更多是为了给生活找个节奏。 小娟哼了一声，双臂抱在胸前，赌气似的嘟着嘴。“也许对妈妈来说是这样，可我是真的会饿嘛……” |“我最喜欢[kinu.Dad]来了，因为你可以使劲摸我的头！” 哈！你伸手揉了揉小娟的头发，把那双大耳朵也弄得乱蓬蓬的，小狐妖开心地尖叫起来。她闭上眼睛，低着头，沉浸在亲昵抚摸带来的单纯幸福中。 “看吧？看吧？” 她果然和她妈妈一样敏感。等她长大了，肯定也会让别的狐族感到很幸福吧。你摸完她之后，小娟露出一丝失望的表情，不过很快又抖了抖耳朵、甩了甩三条尾巴，恢复了精神。 “我最喜欢[kinu.Dad]来了，因为你可以使劲摸我的头！” 她刚才已经说过了。 “我知道！” |“长高真的好慢啊。”小娟嘟囔着。 让我猜猜……她想长高，是不是因为这样就能摘到树枝上更高的桃子了？ “我可什么都没说……” 她知道有些水果不长在树上，对吧？要不要试着种几棵浆果灌木？或者种点瓜类？那些也很好吃，而且长在地上…… “我再想想吧。妈妈要是看到我玩泥巴玩得太厉害，会生气的。” |“你今天还要跟妈妈玩吗？” 你确实是要去见她的。毕竟大老远跑到星界来，总不能不见清子一面就走吧？ “我不是说‘见’，我是说‘玩’。” 嗯……你那只狡黠的小女儿说的玩到底是指什么呢？ “我也不太确定，但我知道你们玩得肯定很开心——因为妈妈只有在开心的时候才会那样大声说话。不过没关系，我也喜欢自己一个人玩，或者只跟一个人玩。人太多了，我会很快累的。”小娟想了想，又说：“每次妈妈跟你玩完之后，都会接连好几天心情特别好……我挺想她多开心一些的。所以我才知道，你们一起玩的时候一定特别有意思。” 呃，这个嘛……确实很有意思。 “我也很喜欢跟[kinu.Dad]玩呢。” 好吧，这对话怎么突然变尴尬了……换个话题。 |“没人愿意跟我下棋。”小娟嘟着嘴，那双狐耳朵也跟着耷拉下来。 哦？为什么呢？ [kiyoko.numKits 0 2|她叹了口气。“妈妈总是忙着……忙她那些事。我见到她的时候，一半时间在讲课，另一半在吃饭，或者是在骂我把自己弄脏了。哼，既然不想让我弄脏，那她倒是抽空陪我玩玩啊，对不对？不然我就只能去挖泥巴或者摘桃子了——自己跟自己下棋下久了真的很无聊……” |小娟移开目光，不愿与你对视。“弟弟妹妹们都不肯跟我玩，他们说下围棋和将棋我总是赢，他们根本没机会赢，所以一点也不好玩。” 你能理解他们的想法，这确实不能怪他们——谁愿意去撞一堵怎么也翻不过去的墙呢。 “对我来说，赢得太轻松也没什么意思。只有妈妈能跟我真正较量一番，可她不可能一直陪我下棋，所以我还是回到老样子。” ] 不过，既然你来了，不妨在去见她妈妈之前，先陪这只毛茸茸的小家伙玩一会儿。不一定非要是下棋，但你总可以抽出一点时间来陪陪她——毕竟据你所知，星界的时间流逝和现实世界并不是完全同步的。 “我真的好喜欢这样，[kinu.Dad]。” [kiyoko.numKits 4|不过有件事…… “什么事？” 她为什么不教她的兄弟姐妹下棋呢？ 小娟眨了眨眼睛。 你看，她自己都说了，打败一个根本打不过自己的对手很无聊，对吧？那不如帮她兄弟姐妹们提高水平——就像农夫养肥小牛一样。这样的话，她最终的胜利才真正有意义，而不是像现在这样，赢得毫无挑战性。 仿佛是听到了什么好主意，小娟的耳朵开始轻轻抖动。“噢——这主意不错啊，[kinu.Dad]……” 当然，也有学生超过老师的风险，所以她也得不断提升自己才行。不过她那么聪明，相信她能处理好的。 ] |“那天我在翻妈妈放香料的地方……” 听起来挺有意思的。她发现了什么特别的东西吗？ “有有有！我发现了一样好东西——芥末！[kinu.Dad]，你尝过那玩意儿吗？真的超级超级棒！” 还没有。那她能不能描述一下那是什么味道？ “呃……大概……算是吧……” 哦，从你那小家伙皱起的眉头来看，这一定是个好故事。 “是这样的，[kinu.Dad]，我本来想尝尝，就挖了一大块放在舌头上，结果舌头一下子就麻了。然后妈妈看到了，赶紧让我漱口……不过我的舌头到现在还是麻的，感觉还挺好笑的。” 哈哈。不管这芥末是什么东西，大概都不适合直接吃吧——尤其是如果它只是一种调味料的话。 “这我可说不好，[kinu.Dad]——它真的很好吃啊。” ]
rows.raw: " [rand|"Hey, don't tell Mama that I told you, but she used to be terrible at cooking." Did she? The way she's so proficient in the kitchen, you'd never have guessed. "Yep! When she was younger, Mama was so busy studying magic and divination that she didn't have time for anything else. Besides, as the den mother's firstborn daughter, she always had other people around to do the cooking for her, so she never quite needed it... all that changed, of course, and she suddenly had a lot of time on her hands and no one around to prepare meals." And what of little Kinu? Will she learn to cook, too? Kinu broadens her stance a little and gives you the most serious look her adorable round face can muster. "[kinu.Dad], I will learn all the things. It would be a shame to waste my inheritance, wouldn't it?" Haha. There's a clever girl. Kinu preens at the praise, looking very pleased with herself. |"There's an underground river that flows beneath the roots of the home tree; we have a basement so we can get to it. The water there's really cold and clear, so we use it for all sorts of things! Not bathing, though! Hot water is for bathing, cold water is for drinking! "Oh! Also, we put fresh-picked veggies from the fields in netted boxes, then put those into the stream to chill! Veggies taste so much better when they've been chilled with cold clean water!" |"Did you know that dried persimmons are really yummy? You wouldn't know it, especially since they're really sour when fresh. But then there's something about the drying process that takes out all that tartness and leaves only a delicious fruity flavor. It's amazing, hee hee!" |"Noon is the most awful time of day," your daughter declares. This ought to be good. You're all ears. "Mm-hm. My tummy gets growly and rumbly, then I feel tired and don't want to do anything but wait for lunch. But then after I've eaten, I feel all nice and full, and don't want to do anything but nap in the sun. Of course, there's always chores to be done around then, so I don't get to do any of that... and then by the time I can go out to play or nap, the feeling's passed." Very convincing, except for the fact that you know that eating's not much of a necessity on the astral plane, and that Kiyoko mostly does mealtimes to give structure to her day. Kinu huffs and folds her arms, sulking. "Maybe it is to you and Mama, but I get awfully hungry..." |"I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" Ha! You reach down and tousle Kinu's hair, ruffling her large ears, and the little kitsune squeals in delight. Closing her eyes and bowing her head towards you, Kinu luxuriates in the simple bliss of affectionate human contact. "See? See?" She's as sensitive as her mother is, that's for sure; you have no doubt she'll make some other kitsune very happy when she grows up. Kinu looks a little disappointed when you finish petting her, but settles back with a wiggle of her ears and swish of her three tails. "I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" She already said that. "I know!" |"Growing taller takes so long," Kinu grumps. Let's guess... she wants to be taller because then it'll be easier for her to reach the peaches on the higher branches? "I'm not saying anything..." She knows that there are other kinds of fruit which don't grow on trees, right? Maybe she could try planting a berry bush or two? Or how about some melons? Those are pretty good and grow close to the ground... "I'll think about it. Mama gets mad with me if I dig in the dirt too much." |"Are you going to play with Mama again today?" You're going to see her, yes. After all, you wouldn't come all this way onto the astral plane and leave without paying Kiyoko a visit, would you? "I didn't mean visit, I meant play." Now... what exactly does your foxy little darling daughter mean by play? "I'm not exactly sure, but I know you have a lot of fun because Mama only raises her voice like that when she's enjoying herself. It's okay, I like to play alone or just with someone else, too. Too many people at once tires me out quickly." Kinu thinks a moment. "Every time Mama is done playing with you, she becomes very happy for days on end... I'd like to see her happy more often. That's another way how I know you have lots of fun playing together." Uh, you most definitely do. "I like playing with you too, [kinu.Dad]." Okay, this conversation just got awkward. Time to change the subject. |"No one will play any board games with me," Kinu grumps, the little kitsune's ears drooping. Oh? Why's that? [kiyoko.numKits 0 2|A sigh. "Mama's always busy with... whatever it is she does. Half the time I see her, it's for lessons; the other half, it's for mealtimes and scolding me for getting myself all dirty. Well, if she doesn't want me to be dirty, maybe she should take a little while to play with me, right? Otherwise, I'm just going to dig in the dirt or find some peaches, because playing both sides of go gets really boring after a while..." |Kinu looks away, unwilling to meet your gaze. "My siblings won't play with me; they say I always win at go and shogi, and that it's not fun if they haven't even a chance at coming out ahead." You can understand where they're coming from, yes. Can't blame them for not wanting to throw themselves against an insurmountable wall like that. "Nor is it fun for me to walk all over them and win so easily. Mama's the only one who's capable of putting up any real opposition, and she can't play with me all the time, so I'm right back where I started." ] Well, now that you're here to visit, maybe you can entertain your fluffy daughter for a bit before going to be with her mother. It might not necessarily be a board game, but you definitely can spare a little time to play with her — after all, as you understand things, the passage of time in the astral plane doesn't quite completely map to that in the waking world. "I would really like that, [kinu.Dad]." [kiyoko.numKits 4|Although there is one thing... "What is it?" Why doesn't she coach her siblings in those games? Kinu blinks. Look, she herself admits that defeating an opponent who can barely fight back is boring, right? Clearly, the thing to do is to help her siblings get better, like a farmer fattening calves for the slaughter. That way her eventual triumph will be truly fulfilling, instead of the meaningless walkovers she's been having to date. As if on cue, Kinu's ears start wiggling. "Ooooooh. That's not a bad idea, [kinu.Dad]..." Of course, there's always the danger of the students surpassing the master, which is why she's got to improve as well. But she's a smart little thing; you're sure she can manage it. ] |"So the other day, I was sorting through where Mama keeps the spices..." That sounds interesting. Did she discover anything of note? "Yes! Yes! I discovered wasabi. Have you tasted the stuff, [kinu.Dad]? It's super-duper amazing!" No, not yet. Can she tell you what it tastes like? "Ehe. Kinda sorta..." Oh, from the furrowed brow on your little fusspet, this is going to be a good one. "See, [kinu.Dad], I was going to try, so I put a big whole dollop of it on my tongue, and then my tongue went numb. Then Mama noticed what I was doing, and made me wash out my mouth... my tongue's still numb, though. It feels kinda funny." Hah. Whatever this wasabi thing is, it's probably not something to be eaten directly, especially if it's a condiment of some sort. "I dunno about that, [kinu.Dad]. It's really great." ]"

rows.original: [rand|"Mama is teaching me her mother tongue. It's very different from the one that we usually speak in, [kinu.Dad]. Very different, but I'm managing." Now that's interesting. [pc.bg scholar noblescion courtesan|You did have the opportunity to learn some foreign languages in the past, but with Belharan being the general trade tongue of the continent you didn't really see the need. After all, anyone who didn't know Belharan wasn't worth talking to, as the saying went.|You didn't have the chance to learn any foreign languages, and even if you did they wouldn't have been much use in the life you led back then.] Still, you can see why Kiyoko would insist on her daughter learning her mother tongue, and not just for the purposes of spellcrafting. "Kitsune aside, I don't think there'll be anyone who speaks or writes it once we get out of here..." But it's nevertheless important for understanding where she came from. That, and it can be fun to have a conversation in front of others who can't understand the language. It makes you feel like you're in a secret club, doesn't it? Kinu brightens. "Yeah... when you put it that way, it kind of sounds fun, [kinu.Dad]. Now, if only there were people who didn't understand the kitsune tongue to try this on — you excepted, of course." You'll just have to work harder on that "getting everyone out of here" thing, won't you? "Yep! Although no need to rush, I suppose. After all, Mama tells me that time doesn't flow the same way here it does outside..." |"I hate swimming," your daughter declares with an unmistakable note of finality. Does that mean that she can't swim, she won't swim, she doesn't know how to swim, or some combination of the above? Kinu pouts and plants her hands on her hips. "Eh. I can swim, [kinu.Dad]. A bit. And then I don't want to any more." That's not very reassuring. What if she fell into a river someday and couldn't swim back out? "Hot springs are okay. Playing in the shallows is okay. What's not okay is cold water that goes in over my head. It gets in my ears and saps all my strength. Seriously, [kinu.Dad]. Less than a minute in that kind of water, and I might as well be a log." One way or the other, this is rather concerning. The danger posed to her from large bodies of water aside, this refusal to even try to overcome this weakness is rather uncharacteristic of Kinu. Maybe you should speak to her mother about this. A sniff. "Do whatever you want, [kinu.Dad]. It doesn't change the fact that it is what it is." Maybe, but you'd like to understand the situation better, if nothing else. |"Mama says that it's vital for me to develop a steady and organized mind that isn't prone to panic. Only then will I be ready to deal with large numbers of screaming, crying, mischievous kits, all of whom will do their best to drive me to my wits' end." Amusingly enough, the way Kiyoko's training her for that is to have her daughter deal with large numbers of screaming, crying, mischievous kits, all of whom will do their best to drive her to her wits' end. In a controlled setting, of course. When she has kits of her own, she won't be able to run crying to her mother whenever a problem that's too big for her to handle crops up. "Ehe. Or maybe I will, anyway. Mama does tell me stories from when she was a girl." Maybe you'll even get to hear them someday. But back to the point — Kinu is a level-headed little thing most of the time, which is more than what you can say for some of the other kits. There's nothing like having to deal with utter chaos on a daily basis to hone one's mental strength. "Ehe, it feels good to be praised. Although if I don't cry that often... when I do cry, people will think I'm faking it to earn sympathy, since it's so out character for me. Maybe I should do it a bit more, or at least fake it?" Oh dear. Whatever are you going to do with her? |"I don't think I'm too bad at cooking, [kinu.Dad]." Now, what brought this up? "Well, for some time now I've been helping Mama in the kitchen, and I can do some simple meals — nothing fancy like what Mama can cook up, yet. And while everything seems fine when I taste the end result myself, [kiyoko.numKits 3 |my brothers and sisters always balk whenever I serve up something I've prepared. Is there something I'm missing, or is my sense of taste just off?" Has she tried asking them exactly why they dislike her food? Kinu shrugs. "I've tried, but they're all just too polite to tell Big Sister when she asks. Either that, or they're afraid I'll take umbrage if they criticise me." |Mama always manages to find fault with the dish, and is able to tell me exactly why. Is there something I'm missing, or is my sense of taste just off?" ] Heh. There are drawbacks to being her mother's right hand, it seems. Well, if she's going to try preparing an actual dish for you — not just roasting chestnuts and mushrooms over a fire — you'd be more than willing to help. With the way things are, though, you suspect it's not about the taste or the presentation, but something else that's possibly unrelated to the food. This is a good exercise in discreetly gathering information if you ever saw one; best to start small with these things. |"I'm doing excellently in my spellcrafting studies." Oh? And who's the judge of that? "Mama, of course. That, and when I do fail at it, I tend to do so in rather spectacular and obvious ways that don't leave me any room to rationalise away my mistakes." That's... one way to put it. [pc.bg arcanist scholar|You've learned enough about these things to know that the most miniscule spell gone wrong can have the most... obvious effects.|While you haven't had much history with all things arcane, you'd like to think you know enough to figure out your daughter isn't exaggerating.] It's a good thing that her mother insists on all the proper precautions before giving lessons. "My calligraphy is perfect, if I may say so," Kinu continues, turning up her little nose in the air. "That, and the actual physical assembly of the scroll's components. What I'd really like to see, though..." Yes? "...Is some foreign magic. Mama tells me people in your part of the world use things like staves and totems as spell foci, [kinu.Dad]. The underlying principles may be the same, but I really want to see the forms in their proper context, take them apart to see what makes them work." Now that's an idea. Maybe you should drop in the next time they have a lesson... if you can time your arrival right, that is. |"Mama sure is teaching me a lot of things... she wants to impart all that she knows to me so that I can teach my brothers and sisters, too!" Is she okay with this? Kinu looks a little uncertain, but nods. "There's no better way to reinforce what you've learned than teaching it to someone else." In that case, she needs to be more confident in what she's learned. Book teaching will only go so far, after all; experience will take her the rest of the way. That being said, you're sure that she'll get better at it with time. "I hope so, [kinu.Dad]. But I'll do my best nevertheless!" Best is one thing. Whether it's sufficient is another. |"It seems like I inherited Mama's talent for magic." [pc.bg acolyte scholar|And yours as well, given your training and background. |Along with most of her other fetching qualities, you note. ] Kinu huffs. "I can only hope so. Mama says we'll only know for sure when I get older, although I'm not certain what she means by that. Either way, I seem to be really really good with magic." Why then, might she cast a spell for you, perhaps show you what she's learned? "Hee hee, of course!" Kinu balls her hands and waves them about in the air. "I cast fist!" Umm... "Sorry. That was a lot funnier when I went over it in my head." A lot of things are, you tell Kinu, tweaking the little kitsune's downcast ears. Maybe she ought to save that demonstration for when her mother's around. "Aww, boo. There is one thing I really want to learn, though, and Mama won't teach me..." Oh? "I wanna learn how to grasp things from afar." Uh, no. Both she and you know that she'll pick the peach grove clean the moment she learns that trick. Both you are Kiyoko are standing together on this point. "Awww..." Maybe when she's older and better able to control her appetites. |While you have little doubt that Kinu's mental faculties are being developed under her mother's careful supervision, does she get any physical training? "Hmm..." Kinu looks a little unsure at that. "Mama says I get enough exercise with all the running around and climbing trees I do..." It's not just the exercise. It's the way she handles herself. Kinu is quick to catch on. "Do you mean you want me to learn how to handle weapons like you do, [kinu.Dad]?" Hey, you didn't say anything about that — she brought that one up herself. You'll have to see the extent of her physical abilities, and it's not likely that she'll be able to do much while this young. But there's always room for working on her constitution and stamina even at a young age. You don't want a frail daughter by any means, after all. Kinu huffs. "Do I look frail to you, [kinu.Dad]? I'm not made out of porcelain, after all. Maybe I should dig around in the dirt more." Maybe she should do just that — after she learns a spell to clean herself up so Kiyoko doesn't have to bemoan a dirty daughter. |Does she ever forget anything she's learned? It's no good filling one's head with things if it's all going to flow right out again like trying to fill a sieve with water. Kinu considers the question deeply, her kitsune instincts no doubt warning her of a potential snare here. Eventually, she shakes her head and gives you a weak smile. "Um... no?" Is she sure? She never forgets anything? "Yes, [kinu.Dad]!" Good, good. Since she's got such an excellent memory, you'll take it that any misbehavior on her part is wholly deliberate, instead of her simply having forgotten to be good in the heat of the moment. Kinu's ears fold forward, and she pouts. "Aw, boo..." |"Mama is putting me on what she calls a 'classical education.' I'm not exactly sure what that means, but it's not for lack of trying, that's for sure." You'll trust Kiyoko with these things — she was trained from childhood to see to the raising of children, after all. But what does your daughter learn all day? "A whole bunch of things from where Mama came from, which is very far away!" And she's not bothered by the fact that she's learning subjects from a land she might never see? "Don't be silly, [kinu.Dad]. I have to know where I came from, if I'm going to figure out where I'm going. Besides, I'm going to live a decently long time. Who's to say I won't be able to make the trip?" Well, if she has that much confidence in herself, there's no reason she wouldn't be able to eventually do so. |"Mama has been trying to teach me the poetry of the place where she came from..." [pc.bg scholar noblescion|You nod. Much can be inferred about a people and their values from the literature they hold dear. You yourself had the opportunity to study some old Belharan poetry during your younger days, thanks to your position in society; regardless of the subject matter, it offered insights into the way people of that time went about their lives and what they thought important. |Literature's not really your thing, but you're not going to let your own lack of understanding get in the way of your daughter's education. ] "I keep on forgetting that haiku poetry is different from traditional waka poetry. Waka poetry has verses in five, seven, five, seven and seven syllables, and is always on the subject of people or scenery. Haiku poetry verses are in five, seven, and five syllables, and they always tout the beauty of the seasons with required seasonal words. Then Mama gets mad at me for not recalling the difference..." Wait, didn't she just remember — Kinu blinks, realization dawning upon your daughter's face. "Oh. Ehe. Maybe you should help me study sometime, [kinu.Dad]... I might do better if you're around." Or maybe she never forgot it at all, and just couldn't bring it to mind until given sufficient incentive. |[kinu.kinuWeapon| [rand| "Mama is so amazing when she goes through the forms with her naginata. Her steps and motions are so dignified and flowing, she looks like a fire dancing in the hearth. I know I was a bit reluctant when I first began learning it from her... but seriously, [kinu.Dad], after you've seen enough of that you really, really start to appreciate the naginata for what it is." After what happened, you're glad to see that she's having a more positive attitude about learning a martial art. Still, it's important not to overdo it, okay? She's still young and you don't want her to get sick again; her mother was worried enough the first time. Kinu bites her lip and shifts her eyes from side to side. "I don't want to be sick like that again, either. It wasn't nice." That's making an understatement of the grossest degree. "For the time being, Mama's keeping me on the practice one she made out of bamboo so I can do the forms easily. She says she'll graduate me to a proper naginata when I'm stronger in my arms." That's perfectly fine. It'll be some years before she'll actually need to put what she's learning here into practice anyways — she'll no longer be a child at that point. | "The more I learn about the history of the naginata and its meaning to the kitsune people, [kinu.Dad], the more I feel inspired to get better at wielding one. You were right that day — knowing the whys and wherefores has given me a greater appreciation for the weapon." That's great to hear. "Isn't it? Even when I'm holding the practice naginata Mama made for me, I can feel a connection to the den mothers and matrons of old who defended their homes with one of these. I may never visit the land where she came from, but I feel braver already just imagining myself as one of them. Even Mama who doesn't favor it as a weapon still knows the forms; they're something that's handed down from mother to daughter. "As they say, this is an art with history, and I'm enjoying it more and more." You pet Kinu on the head, and your daughter squeals in delight as you ruffle her fur. On your part, you're glad that she took your words so deeply to heart. She just has to remember to pace herself and not make her mother worry by falling sick again, okay? "Okay!" ] | [rand| "Mama says I may never be able to use another bow besides the hankyu. It's not just the draw strength of the bow, it's the sheer size..." Sure, Kinu might be a petite thing, but isn't it a little too early to say how tall she'll eventually be in the future? "Oh come on, [kinu.Dad]. By the looks of it, I'll be even tinier than Mama is when I'm grown-up. There's no need to not be realistic about things." Ah, such fatalism from one so young, and especially from one so usually cheerful at that. Kinu sniffs. "Back to the point, [kinu.Dad]. I think it fits me, anyway. It's small and compact, but there's a lot of energy in the bowstring. I can't quite imagine me doing any of that with a bigger one... with the hankyu, I feel pretty quick and nimble." Can she reliably hit things, though? "Yeeeah..." Kinu looks a little sheepish and grinds her toes against the dirt. "I'm working on that part." | Say... maybe it's just your imagination, but has Kinu gained a little more bulk in her arms? Maybe not since the last time you saw her, but she's definitely changed from how you remember her from a while back. "Eh, you're not wrong, [kinu.Dad]. Mama's had me working out my arms, giving me more physical chores from day to day. Nowadays, she shoos me out of the house if she catches me loafing about indoors. 'Go play outside!'." Hmm. It's probably not a good idea to bulk up too much when one's as young as she is, but she oughtn't worry; she'd have to actually work out pretty hard to raise any concern. Why this, though? "Well, after I took ill... both you and Mama were quite worried about me." Yes. It was rather upsetting. You take it Kiyoko's found a decent way to develop her daughter's arm strength; it certainly looks like she's been getting results, at any rate. "Ehe. At least I can draw the bowstring without my arms shaking all over the place. That's a good start, isn't it?" Indeed. Now, she has to try and actually hit something instead of all her arrows going wild... "Like I said, [kinu.Dad], I'm working on it..." ] ] |[kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0| [rand| "Learning how to keep my brothers and sisters in line is tiring, I don't know how Mama manages it so effortlessly. Sometimes I wonder if it's some mystical den mother power I'll only come into when I get older." Keeping them in line is tiring, huh? What's the problem, exactly? Maybe you can offer some advice, and if not, encouragement at least. "Well, you told me it was important to try and find out why people did bad things before passing judgement. So each time this kind of thing happens, I try to dig out the underlying problem...and once I unearth it, I just can't rest well until it's resolved. It just gnaws at me." Hmm, you don't know what to think about this, and it's not exactly what you envisioned happening when you said those words back then. Being affectionate isn't wrong in and of itself, but as with anything, there's always a risk of overdoing it. She doesn't want to develop a reputation for being a nosy meddler or smother her siblings, does she? Kinu looks a little worried at that. "I think I understand what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad], but it's very hard to step back and simply not do anything when someone's in trouble. It...it doesn't make me feel good at all." So is this about helping other people, or is it about making herself feel good? Your foxy daughter mumbles something not quite under her breath and turns askance, refusing to look you in the eye. "Can't it be both?" She just needs to remember not to spread herself too thinly. Can't help others if she herself is indisposed, or if people instinctively reject her approaches. "I need to think about this, [kinu.Dad]. I'm getting conflicting messages here." That would be a good idea, yes. | "I'm learning how to properly go about doing agriculture!" Oh, really? So she can have a never-ending supply of peaches on which to gorge herself on? And the way she put it — "doing agriculture" — it makes simple farming sound so... well, formal. "Heeey, unlike Mama, I'm taking this seriously. The peach grove is the only real thing she tried her hand at, and that was as a hobby. I, on the other hand —" she puffs out her chest at you — "am learning what crops flourish in what seasons, when to leave land fallow and how to keep it productive without wearing it out. That sort of thing. And I'm learning it myself out of books, instead of Mama teaching." Fascinating. Why the sudden interest in working the land, though? "Wellll... ehe... I'd say that pulling up veggies is lots of fun, but that's just a small part of it. I kinda like seeing things grow, and while I do enjoy them being pretty, there's also the practical aspect to consider. Flower arrangements are a soothing sight, but flowers get cut down first when hunger sets in." Putting her learning into practice is a lot of hard physical labor. Is she sure someone as slight as her is up to it? Kinu winks at you. "Oh, not to worry, [kinu.Dad]. That's what I have brothers and sisters for — and when I get old enough, kits of my own. In the meantime, I'm doing what I can on a smaller scale. You're not wrong in that it's a lot of sweaty work, but I think it's worth it." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, and she offered to teach me how to play the koto. It's not quite my style, though, so I turned her down. It's too cramped for me, for a lack of a better word to describe it." What has she taken up, then? You know your daughter well enough to know that she wouldn't stop there. "Ehe. I'm learning the shakuhachi!" The what? "Um, uh, it's kind of a flute?" Kinu scratches the back of her head, ears wiggling as she thinks. "I guess it is a flute, by the way you would understand the word, [kinu.Dad]. But the important thing is that it's got this nice, meditative tone, and I can carry it around when I go about my daily work. I feel it's more flexible that way." Hmm. Her mother's teaching her the ins and outs, you take it? "Nope, she doesn't know anything of it. Which means I have to make do with the manuals I have, try and figure things out on my own. If Mama could do it for so many other subjects, I don't see why I can't at least give it a go." She thinks a moment. "Progress is pretty slow, though. Everyone keeps on telling me that my playing is awful, so I don't think I'm going to be showing off anytime soon. Learning by yourself is a lot different from learning from a teacher." Naturally, and she doesn't have to worry about progress being slow — what's important here is that she's learning an additional skill in the bargain — that of autodidactism. When one learns to learn effectively, so many possibilities open up, and one can explore them at one's own pace. "Hmm... I like the sound of that, [kinu.Dad]. Exploring. That's a pretty exciting way to put it. I don't know if everyone else will find it that exciting, though. From their reactions so far, it's more annoyance than anything else; I keep on telling them it's only to be expected when one's trying to learn a new instrument but Mama makes me do my practice outside where I won't burst everyone's eardrums. Which, to be frank, suits me just fine." | "I wish I had more people to talk to." Oh? Is she feeling lonely? "No, I'd just like to talk to more kinds of people. For example, I notice that your manner of speech is different than Mama's, but it doesn't end there. It's the way you move when conversing with other people, [kinu.Dad]." The way you move, huh... "Yep. Most people don't even bother thinking about it, so you can tell a lot about what they're really thinking while they're speaking. The same goes for a bunch of animals I see in the forest, too, except they don't talk. I think Mama's the only person who's aware of this, but she doesn't bother trying to conceal it most of the time." So, can she read your mood right now? Your daughter frowns. "Not very well. Like I said, [kinu.Dad], you're different. It's kind of hard to make generalisations when all I have to practice on is Mama and my brothers and sisters. That's why I'd like to have the chance to converse with many different kinds of people and observe them while they're speaking. The more people I get to observe, the better I'll be at reading them in general. Makes sense, right?" It always boils down to that, doesn't it? You're working on it — finding a deity can be a little tricky at times. "Oh? I didn't say anything about that at all, [kinu.Dad]. You came up with that by your very own self." She sticks her tongue out at you. "I think I'm getting a better hold of you already." | You're seeing Kinu outside a lot these days. Does her mother not want her in the house? "There is that, but I don't mind it so much these days, [kinu.Dad]. I feel more comfortable outside and with fresh air, even when playing shogi or go. Besides, it gives me plenty of opportunities to practice my magic — I feel a lot more confident experimenting with spells when I'm in the peach grove or veggie garden. It's like the plants there are cheering me on." Hmm... is she showing druidic tendencies? "From the way you described them, [kinu.Dad], no. Druids worship nature, from what I'm told — agriculture is the most direct union of civilization and nature. The forest is nice, but I don't get the same feeling from it that I do from the growing veggies... we've been together with them for so long that the both of us have changed each other. They trust me enough to lend me power to be repaid later; the plants in the forest are either too mean or too scared of me to even want to talk." She certainly is growing apart from her mother's way of doing things... Kiyoko's bound to blame you for this. "Ehehe. Can't I just be my own person, [kinu.Dad]? Learning by experimentation is so much more fun than sitting down and listening to Mama lecture away." She eyes you shiftily, then leans in to stage-whisper. "You know what we need?" What? "We need a rice paddy. Like, just a wide expanse of golden rice..." Kinu claps her hands together and goes all starry-eyed. "Imagine how amazing I'd look framed against it. But Mama says no, a veggie garden's already enough trouble to tend as it is." If she's trying to play you off against Kiyoko, the answer is no. You're standing with her mother on this. "Boo..." ] | [rand| "Keeping my siblings in line is important, both for them and for Mama's sanity. It's been a lot of trial and error and understanding what makes them tick individually, but I think I'm getting the hang of making sure they behave." She sighs and gives you a little wry smile. "Being Big Sister is hard. They may not fully understand why it's important to behave beyond an I-said-so, but I'm sure they'll thank me in the days to come." [pc.isDK|Certainly. You hope that she's adequately impressing upon them the importance of following her leadership and authority. "Um, [kinu.Dad], that's not exactly what I meant... but you do have a point there. Why shouldn't they follow me when Mama's not around? I'm the smartest and oldest, after all — it naturally follows that they should listen to my direction whether they like it or not. I only have their best interests in mind, after all!" You smirk and tousle Kinu's hair. The little kitsune may look like her mother in body, but she's truly a fox after your own heart.|That might be true, but she shouldn't stop trying to explain the whys and wherefores to them. Even if her siblings can't comprehend the reason she's disciplining them, they ought to be able to realize there that she isn't doing it just on a whim. Kinu gives you a wry smile and plants her little hands on her hips. "Isn't it all the same, [kinu.Dad]? Train them up when they're young, and they'll be set in their ways when they're older?" That's one way to put it...] "Either way, this is a part of my education that Mama can't guide me the whole way through. Being a den mother isn't just about making kits, it's also about raising them to be decent and useful people who live in accordance with Keros' teachings. Hence, I really can't be easy on any of them, even if they cry and pout." And when her own mother reprimands her, does she take the lesson with grace? "I do my best to, [kinu.Dad]; I'd be a hypocrite otherwise. It's not that I don't get peeved — I do — but I realize what I'm doing is wrong, and try to get over myself to understand why Mama is ticked off at me. It's not perfect, but I think it's an important experience. After all, which is better — to be born as a perfectly good girl, or to have some flaws but carefully work to overcome them?" | "I'm learning to cultivate flowers!" Huh. You're not quite sure if flowers needed cultivating. "Weell... when I do flower arrangement with Mama, going out to the forest to get flowers is a pain. Not the going out part, but the finding part. It's so hard to get one that matches exactly what I need — and I'm not going to let Mama just tell the plane to conjure one. That would defeat the point..." Ah, you see where this is going. If she raises them from scratch, she'll get exactly what she needs. "That. Finding blossoms of a particular color, size, and shape is hair-tearing, but if I raise them myself I can influence them as they grow and mould them into something suitable for my arrangements. Although I'll say, [kinu.Dad], that I've discovered there's something pleasing about raising them in and of itself." Indeed. Raising something and seeing the effects of your care on it can be one of the most fulfilling or terrible things in the world, depending on how well of a job one does. You're glad that she's getting to experience this first-hand on a smaller scale in a controlled setting. Kinu pulls her brows together and looks thoughtful. "I get the feeling that you're trying to be deep and meaningful here, [kinu.Dad], but I can't place my finger on it..." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, so she's started teaching me the koto. It's what she's been playing since she was a girl, or so Mama says, so I have the benefit of a good teacher to draw experience from." The koto, huh? What sort of instrument is that? "It's..." Kinu pauses. "It has strings, and you pluck them to make music. I have very slender and nimble fingers, so Mama said it was a good choice for me." A string instrument, eh? Kind of like a lute? "What's a lute?" There's a moment's awkward silence, and then your daughter brushes off the faux pas and continues, ever the cheery fox kit. "I think Mama's kind of proud that I'm following in her footsteps. She's definitely putting more into these lessons than she usually does for other subjects." Well, you know what they say: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. | "I've decided it's important for a lady-to-be like me to be eloquent in both speech and writing. As a den mother, my children will be looking up to me the same way my brothers and sisters do for Mama, so I'll have to set a good example for them." That's nice, although deciding on a matter is easy; carrying it out to fruition takes a little more effort. What's she doing about it? "Well, Mama's busy enough already, so I've taken to reading some of the old classics she's got lying about in the upper branches of the tree. I don't think she's touched them for a long, looong time, [kinu.Dad]." No, ever since she and her siblings came on the scene, you don't imagine Kiyoko has had much in the way of spare time, especially when she's doing what she truly enjoys. "That's just the beginning, of course," Kinu continues. "Studying how the people of that time strung together words not just to convey meaning in no uncertain terms, but knowing which ones to use to evoke the proper impressions and emotions in whoever reads your words or listens to you speak — and of course, knowing when to use which." That's rather eloquent for something coming out of an eight-year-old's mouth. Kinu smiles. "See? It's working already! Sure, it's important to be outwardly pretty, but that image is going to be ruined if you embarrass yourself the moment you open your mouth. Mama is pretty great in that regard — she always knows the right thing to say in any situation. I know I've still got a looong way to go before I get anywhere approaching her level..." | "The arcane magic Mama uses for divination is fascinating. I can't help but imagine the things I could do if I could just get better... Mama is pacing my lessons so I don't get ahead of myself, but I really want to know more and it's bugging me to no end." Her mother must be pretty happy her daughter's chosen to follow in her footsteps so closely. "Ehe. I'm doing it because I want to, not because Mama's forcing me to do anything. The feel of old scrolls, tomes and manuals beneath my fingers... there's something that's lovely and exquisite about them that I can't put into words." Kinu folds her ears forward and smiles, going all starry-eyed. "I like to think they can speak to me with the voices of the people who wrote them. Isn't that amazing?" [pc.bg arcanist scholar|Well, with both sides of the family into this sort of thing, it's little surprise your daughter turned out this way. At least it's something you know Kiyoko and you can cope with...|Hmph. It's a small relief that your relative inexperience with these things hasn't dampened the enthusiasm your daughter's apparently inherited from her mother.] "Guess patience is one of those virtues Mama wants to cultivate in me," Kinu grumps. "Hmph. I'm smart enough to handle more than what she's willing to teach..." ] ] ]
rows.translation: [rand|妈妈正在教我她的母语。这种语言和我们平时说的那种语言非常不同 [kinu.Dad]非常不同，但我正在努力应对。 这可真有意思。 [pc.bg scholar noblescion courtesan|你过去确实有机会学习一些外语，但由于贝尔哈兰语是这片大陆上通用的语言，你觉得并没有必要去学习其他语言。毕竟，正如那句俗话所说，任何不懂贝尔哈兰语的人都不值得与你交谈。|你当时根本没有机会学习任何外语，即使学会了，那些语言在你当时的生活环境中也几乎派不上什么用场。] 不过，你也可以理解为什么清子会坚持让女儿学习她的母语——这不仅仅是为了魔法施放的需要。 除了狐妖，我想等我们离开这里之后，应该不会再有人会说或写这种语言了…… 但这对于了解她的背景来说仍然很重要。而且，在那些听不懂这种语言的人面前进行对话，也会是一件有趣的事情。这样会让你觉得自己仿佛属于一个秘密俱乐部，不是吗？ 小娟的笑容变得更加灿烂了。是啊……你这么一说，听起来还挺有趣的。 [kinu.Dad]现在，要是有那些不懂狐语的人来试试这个该多好啊——当然，你除外。 你只需要在“把所有人都弄出去”这件事上更加努力一些，对吧？ 没错！不过我想也没必要着急。毕竟妈妈告诉我，这里的时间流逝方式和外面是不一样的…… |我讨厌游泳。你的女儿用一种不容置疑的坚定语气说道。 那么，这是意味着她不会游泳、根本不会游泳、还是根本不知道如何游泳，又或者是以上几种情况的某种组合呢？ 小娟撅起嘴，双手叉腰站在那里。呃，我可以游泳吧。 [kinu.Dad]有点吧。然后我就不再想继续了。 这可不太让人放心。要是有一天她掉进了河里，又不会游泳，那该怎么办呢？ 温泉还好，在浅水区玩耍也没问题。但问题是那种冰冷的水——一旦淹过我的头，它就会进入我的耳朵，让我彻底失去力气。说真的，这真的太难受了。 [kinu.Dad]在那种水里待不到一分钟，我就跟根木头没两样了。 不管怎样，这确实令人担忧。除了大型水域对她构成的危险之外，她甚至都不愿意尝试克服这个弱点，这种态度实在不符合小娟的一贯性格。或许你应该和她母亲谈谈这件事。 嗯你想做什么就做什么吧， [kinu.Dad]但这并不能改变它本身的本质。 也许吧，但至少你也想更清楚地了解实际情况吧。 |妈妈说，对我来说，培养一种沉着冷静、有条理的思维方式是非常重要的。只有这样，我才有能力应对那些吵闹、哭泣、调皮捣蛋的小家伙们——他们肯定会想尽一切办法把我逼得抓狂的。 有趣的是，清子训练女儿的方式就是让女儿去应对那些大喊大叫、哭闹不休、调皮捣蛋的小动物们——这些小动物们总会想方设法把女儿逼得抓狂。当然，这一切都是在受控的环境中发生的。等到女儿自己也拥有了自己的小动物们，当遇到那些她无法独自解决的问题时，她就不会再哭着跑去找妈妈求助了。 呵呵，也许我最终还是会这么做的。妈妈总会给我讲她小时候的故事。 也许有一天你真的会听到它们的声音。不过回到正题——小娟大多数时候都是个冷静理智的小家伙，这一点可比其他一些角色要强多了。每天都要应对一片混乱，这样才能锻炼出坚强的意志力，没有什么比这更有效的了。 嘿嘿，被人表扬的感觉真好。不过要是我不经常哭的话……该多好啊做如果我哭了，人们会认为我在装哭以博取同情，因为这完全不符合我的性格。也许我应该再哭得夸张一点，或者至少装得更像一点才行。 哦天哪，你到底打算对她做什么呢？ |我觉得我并不太不擅长做饭。 [kinu.Dad]." 那么，是什么引发了这个话题呢？ 嗯，这些天我一直在帮妈妈做饭，也学会做一些简单的菜肴——当然还比不上妈妈做的那些美味佳肴。不过每次自己品尝成品的时候，感觉也都还不错。 [kiyoko.numKits 3 |每次我准备好食物端上来，我的兄弟姐妹们总是表示不喜欢。是不是我遗漏了什么，还是说我的口味确实不太对呢？ 她有没有试着直接问他们，为什么不喜欢她的食物？ 小娟耸了耸肩。我试过了，但每当大姐姐提问时，他们总是太客气了，不肯指出来。要么就是他们害怕如果批评我，我会生气。 |妈妈总是能找出这道菜的不足之处，而且还能准确地告诉我原因。是我想忽略了什么，还是我的口味真的有问题呢？ ] Or maybe she never forgot it at all, and just couldn't bring it to mind until given sufficient incentive. |[kinu.kinuWeapon| [rand| "Mama is so amazing when she goes through the forms with her naginata. Her steps and motions are so dignified and flowing, she looks like a fire dancing in the hearth. I know I was a bit reluctant when I first began learning it from her... but seriously, [kinu.Dad], after you've seen enough of that you really, really start to appreciate the naginata for what it is." After what happened, you're glad to see that she's having a more positive attitude about learning a martial art. Still, it's important not to overdo it, okay? She's still young and you don't want her to get sick again; her mother was worried enough the first time. Kinu bites her lip and shifts her eyes from side to side. "I don't want to be sick like that again, either. It wasn't nice." That's making an understatement of the grossest degree. "For the time being, Mama's keeping me on the practice one she made out of bamboo so I can do the forms easily. She says she'll graduate me to a proper naginata when I'm stronger in my arms." That's perfectly fine. It'll be some years before she'll actually need to put what she's learning here into practice anyways — she'll no longer be a child at that point. | "The more I learn about the history of the naginata and its meaning to the kitsune people, [kinu.Dad], the more I feel inspired to get better at wielding one. You were right that day — knowing the whys and wherefores has given me a greater appreciation for the weapon." That's great to hear. "Isn't it? Even when I'm holding the practice naginata Mama made for me, I can feel a connection to the den mothers and matrons of old who defended their homes with one of these. I may never visit the land where she came from, but I feel braver already just imagining myself as one of them. Even Mama who doesn't favor it as a weapon still knows the forms; they're something that's handed down from mother to daughter. "As they say, this is an art with history, and I'm enjoying it more and more." You pet Kinu on the head, and your daughter squeals in delight as you ruffle her fur. On your part, you're glad that she took your words so deeply to heart. She just has to remember to pace herself and not make her mother worry by falling sick again, okay? "Okay!" ] | [rand| "Mama says I may never be able to use another bow besides the hankyu. It's not just the draw strength of the bow, it's the sheer size..." Sure, Kinu might be a petite thing, but isn't it a little too early to say how tall she'll eventually be in the future? "Oh come on, [kinu.Dad]. By the looks of it, I'll be even tinier than Mama is when I'm grown-up. There's no need to not be realistic about things." Ah, such fatalism from one so young, and especially from one so usually cheerful at that. Kinu sniffs. "Back to the point, [kinu.Dad]. I think it fits me, anyway. It's small and compact, but there's a lot of energy in the bowstring. I can't quite imagine me doing any of that with a bigger one... with the hankyu, I feel pretty quick and nimble." Can she reliably hit things, though? "Yeeeah..." Kinu looks a little sheepish and grinds her toes against the dirt. "I'm working on that part." | Say... maybe it's just your imagination, but has Kinu gained a little more bulk in her arms? Maybe not since the last time you saw her, but she's definitely changed from how you remember her from a while back. "Eh, you're not wrong, [kinu.Dad]. Mama's had me working out my arms, giving me more physical chores from day to day. Nowadays, she shoos me out of the house if she catches me loafing about indoors. 'Go play outside!'." Hmm. It's probably not a good idea to bulk up too much when one's as young as she is, but she oughtn't worry; she'd have to actually work out pretty hard to raise any concern. Why this, though? "Well, after I took ill... both you and Mama were quite worried about me." Yes. It was rather upsetting. You take it Kiyoko's found a decent way to develop her daughter's arm strength; it certainly looks like she's been getting results, at any rate. "Ehe. At least I can draw the bowstring without my arms shaking all over the place. That's a good start, isn't it?" Indeed. Now, she has to try and actually hit something instead of all her arrows going wild... "Like I said, [kinu.Dad], I'm working on it..." ] ] |[kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0| [rand| "Learning how to keep my brothers and sisters in line is tiring, I don't know how Mama manages it so effortlessly. Sometimes I wonder if it's some mystical den mother power I'll only come into when I get older." Keeping them in line is tiring, huh? What's the problem, exactly? Maybe you can offer some advice, and if not, encouragement at least. "Well, you told me it was important to try and find out why people did bad things before passing judgement. So each time this kind of thing happens, I try to dig out the underlying problem...and once I unearth it, I just can't rest well until it's resolved. It just gnaws at me." Hmm, you don't know what to think about this, and it's not exactly what you envisioned happening when you said those words back then. Being affectionate isn't wrong in and of itself, but as with anything, there's always a risk of overdoing it. She doesn't want to develop a reputation for being a nosy meddler or smother her siblings, does she? Kinu looks a little worried at that. "I think I understand what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad], but it's very hard to step back and simply not do anything when someone's in trouble. It...it doesn't make me feel good at all." So is this about helping other people, or is it about making herself feel good? Your foxy daughter mumbles something not quite under her breath and turns askance, refusing to look you in the eye. "Can't it be both?" She just needs to remember not to spread herself too thinly. Can't help others if she herself is indisposed, or if people instinctively reject her approaches. "I need to think about this, [kinu.Dad]. I'm getting conflicting messages here." That would be a good idea, yes. | "I'm learning how to properly go about doing agriculture!" Oh, really? So she can have a never-ending supply of peaches on which to gorge herself on? And the way she put it — "doing agriculture" — it makes simple farming sound so... well, formal. "Heeey, unlike Mama, I'm taking this seriously. The peach grove is the only real thing she tried her hand at, and that was as a hobby. I, on the other hand —" she puffs out her chest at you — "am learning what crops flourish in what seasons, when to leave land fallow and how to keep it productive without wearing it out. That sort of thing. And I'm learning it myself out of books, instead of Mama teaching." Fascinating. Why the sudden interest in working the land, though? "Wellll... ehe... I'd say that pulling up veggies is lots of fun, but that's just a small part of it. I kinda like seeing things grow, and while I do enjoy them being pretty, there's also the practical aspect to consider. Flower arrangements are a soothing sight, but flowers get cut down first when hunger sets in." Putting her learning into practice is a lot of hard physical labor. Is she sure someone as slight as her is up to it? Kinu winks at you. "Oh, not to worry, [kinu.Dad]. That's what I have brothers and sisters for — and when I get old enough, kits of my own. In the meantime, I'm doing what I can on a smaller scale. You're not wrong in that it's a lot of sweaty work, but I think it's worth it." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, and she offered to teach me how to play the koto. It's not quite my style, though, so I turned her down. It's too cramped for me, for a lack of a better word to describe it." What has she taken up, then? You know your daughter well enough to know that she wouldn't stop there. "Ehe. I'm learning the shakuhachi!" The what? "Um, uh, it's kind of a flute?" Kinu scratches the back of her head, ears wiggling as she thinks. "I guess it is a flute, by the way you would understand the word, [kinu.Dad]. But the important thing is that it's got this nice, meditative tone, and I can carry it around when I go about my daily work. I feel it's more flexible that way." Hmm. Her mother's teaching her the ins and outs, you take it? "Nope, she doesn't know anything of it. Which means I have to make do with the manuals I have, try and figure things out on my own. If Mama could do it for so many other subjects, I don't see why I can't at least give it a go." She thinks a moment. "Progress is pretty slow, though. Everyone keeps on telling me that my playing is awful, so I don't think I'm going to be showing off anytime soon. Learning by yourself is a lot different from learning from a teacher." Naturally, and she doesn't have to worry about progress being slow — what's important here is that she's learning an additional skill in the bargain — that of autodidactism. When one learns to learn effectively, so many possibilities open up, and one can explore them at one's own pace. "Hmm... I like the sound of that, [kinu.Dad]. Exploring. That's a pretty exciting way to put it. I don't know if everyone else will find it that exciting, though. From their reactions so far, it's more annoyance than anything else; I keep on telling them it's only to be expected when one's trying to learn a new instrument but Mama makes me do my practice outside where I won't burst everyone's eardrums. Which, to be frank, suits me just fine." | "I wish I had more people to talk to." Oh? Is she feeling lonely? "No, I'd just like to talk to more kinds of people. For example, I notice that your manner of speech is different than Mama's, but it doesn't end there. It's the way you move when conversing with other people, [kinu.Dad]." The way you move, huh... "Yep. Most people don't even bother thinking about it, so you can tell a lot about what they're really thinking while they're speaking. The same goes for a bunch of animals I see in the forest, too, except they don't talk. I think Mama's the only person who's aware of this, but she doesn't bother trying to conceal it most of the time." So, can she read your mood right now? Your daughter frowns. "Not very well. Like I said, [kinu.Dad], you're different. It's kind of hard to make generalisations when all I have to practice on is Mama and my brothers and sisters. That's why I'd like to have the chance to converse with many different kinds of people and observe them while they're speaking. The more people I get to observe, the better I'll be at reading them in general. Makes sense, right?" It always boils down to that, doesn't it? You're working on it — finding a deity can be a little tricky at times. "Oh? I didn't say anything about that at all, [kinu.Dad]. You came up with that by your very own self." She sticks her tongue out at you. "I think I'm getting a better hold of you already." | You're seeing Kinu outside a lot these days. Does her mother not want her in the house? "There is that, but I don't mind it so much these days, [kinu.Dad]. I feel more comfortable outside and with fresh air, even when playing shogi or go. Besides, it gives me plenty of opportunities to practice my magic — I feel a lot more confident experimenting with spells when I'm in the peach grove or veggie garden. It's like the plants there are cheering me on." Hmm... is she showing druidic tendencies? "From the way you described them, [kinu.Dad], no. Druids worship nature, from what I'm told — agriculture is the most direct union of civilization and nature. The forest is nice, but I don't get the same feeling from it that I do from the growing veggies... we've been together with them for so long that the both of us have changed each other. They trust me enough to lend me power to be repaid later; the plants in the forest are either too mean or too scared of me to even want to talk." She certainly is growing apart from her mother's way of doing things... Kiyoko's bound to blame you for this. "Ehehe. Can't I just be my own person, [kinu.Dad]? Learning by experimentation is so much more fun than sitting down and listening to Mama lecture away." She eyes you shiftily, then leans in to stage-whisper. "You know what we need?" What? "We need a rice paddy. Like, just a wide expanse of golden rice..." Kinu claps her hands together and goes all starry-eyed. "Imagine how amazing I'd look framed against it. But Mama says no, a veggie garden's already enough trouble to tend as it is." If she's trying to play you off against Kiyoko, the answer is no. You're standing with her mother on this. "Boo..." ] | [rand| "Keeping my siblings in line is important, both for them and for Mama's sanity. It's been a lot of trial and error and understanding what makes them tick individually, but I think I'm getting the hang of making sure they behave." She sighs and gives you a little wry smile. "Being Big Sister is hard. They may not fully understand why it's important to behave beyond an I-said-so, but I'm sure they'll thank me in the days to come." [pc.isDK|Certainly. You hope that she's adequately impressing upon them the importance of following her leadership and authority. "Um, [kinu.Dad], that's not exactly what I meant... but you do have a point there. Why shouldn't they follow me when Mama's not around? I'm the smartest and oldest, after all — it naturally follows that they should listen to my direction whether they like it or not. I only have their best interests in mind, after all!" You smirk and tousle Kinu's hair. The little kitsune may look like her mother in body, but she's truly a fox after your own heart.|That might be true, but she shouldn't stop trying to explain the whys and wherefores to them. Even if her siblings can't comprehend the reason she's disciplining them, they ought to be able to realize there that she isn't doing it just on a whim. Kinu gives you a wry smile and plants her little hands on her hips. "Isn't it all the same, [kinu.Dad]? Train them up when they're young, and they'll be set in their ways when they're older?" That's one way to put it...] "Either way, this is a part of my education that Mama can't guide me the whole way through. Being a den mother isn't just about making kits, it's also about raising them to be decent and useful people who live in accordance with Keros' teachings. Hence, I really can't be easy on any of them, even if they cry and pout." And when her own mother reprimands her, does she take the lesson with grace? "I do my best to, [kinu.Dad]; I'd be a hypocrite otherwise. It's not that I don't get peeved — I do — but I realize what I'm doing is wrong, and try to get over myself to understand why Mama is ticked off at me. It's not perfect, but I think it's an important experience. After all, which is better — to be born as a perfectly good girl, or to have some flaws but carefully work to overcome them?" | "I'm learning to cultivate flowers!" Huh. You're not quite sure if flowers needed cultivating. "Weell... when I do flower arrangement with Mama, going out to the forest to get flowers is a pain. Not the going out part, but the finding part. It's so hard to get one that matches exactly what I need — and I'm not going to let Mama just tell the plane to conjure one. That would defeat the point..." Ah, you see where this is going. If she raises them from scratch, she'll get exactly what she needs. "That. Finding blossoms of a particular color, size, and shape is hair-tearing, but if I raise them myself I can influence them as they grow and mould them into something suitable for my arrangements. Although I'll say, [kinu.Dad], that I've discovered there's something pleasing about raising them in and of itself." Indeed. Raising something and seeing the effects of your care on it can be one of the most fulfilling or terrible things in the world, depending on how well of a job one does. You're glad that she's getting to experience this first-hand on a smaller scale in a controlled setting. Kinu pulls her brows together and looks thoughtful. "I get the feeling that you're trying to be deep and meaningful here, [kinu.Dad], but I can't place my finger on it..." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, so she's started teaching me the koto. It's what she's been playing since she was a girl, or so Mama says, so I have the benefit of a good teacher to draw experience from." The koto, huh? What sort of instrument is that? "It's..." Kinu pauses. "It has strings, and you pluck them to make music. I have very slender and nimble fingers, so Mama said it was a good choice for me." A string instrument, eh? Kind of like a lute? "What's a lute?" There's a moment's awkward silence, and then your daughter brushes off the faux pas and continues, ever the cheery fox kit. "I think Mama's kind of proud that I'm following in her footsteps. She's definitely putting more into these lessons than she usually does for other subjects." Well, you know what they say: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. | "I've decided it's important for a lady-to-be like me to be eloquent in both speech and writing. As a den mother, my children will be looking up to me the same way my brothers and sisters do for Mama, so I'll have to set a good example for them." That's nice, although deciding on a matter is easy; carrying it out to fruition takes a little more effort. What's she doing about it? "Well, Mama's busy enough already, so I've taken to reading some of the old classics she's got lying about in the upper branches of the tree. I don't think she's touched them for a long, looong time, [kinu.Dad]." No, ever since she and her siblings came on the scene, you don't imagine Kiyoko has had much in the way of spare time, especially when she's doing what she truly enjoys. "That's just the beginning, of course," Kinu continues. "Studying how the people of that time strung together words not just to convey meaning in no uncertain terms, but knowing which ones to use to evoke the proper impressions and emotions in whoever reads your words or listens to you speak — and of course, knowing when to use which." That's rather eloquent for something coming out of an eight-year-old's mouth. Kinu smiles. "See? It's working already! Sure, it's important to be outwardly pretty, but that image is going to be ruined if you embarrass yourself the moment you open your mouth. Mama is pretty great in that regard — she always knows the right thing to say in any situation. I know I've still got a looong way to go before I get anywhere approaching her level..." | "The arcane magic Mama uses for divination is fascinating. I can't help but imagine the things I could do if I could just get better... Mama is pacing my lessons so I don't get ahead of myself, but I really want to know more and it's bugging me to no end." Her mother must be pretty happy her daughter's chosen to follow in her footsteps so closely. "Ehe. I'm doing it because I want to, not because Mama's forcing me to do anything. The feel of old scrolls, tomes and manuals beneath my fingers... there's something that's lovely and exquisite about them that I can't put into words." Kinu folds her ears forward and smiles, going all starry-eyed. "I like to think they can speak to me with the voices of the people who wrote them. Isn't that amazing?" [pc.bg arcanist scholar|Well, with both sides of the family into this sort of thing, it's little surprise your daughter turned out this way. At least it's something you know Kiyoko and you can cope with...|Hmph. It's a small relief that your relative inexperience with these things hasn't dampened the enthusiasm your daughter's apparently inherited from her mother.] "Guess patience is one of those virtues Mama wants to cultivate in me," Kinu grumps. "Hmph. I'm smart enough to handle more than what she's willing to teach..." ] ] ]"

rows.original: Kinu squeals the moment you reach out and down, knowing what you're after. "I wanna be petted! I wanna be petted!" My, she sure is enthusiastic about it. "You should know, [kinu.Dad]. Someday when I'm older, I'll pet you back. It'll be repayment for all the times you petted me, so you should pet me more now!" Why not now? "I'm not tall enough..." All right, girl, hold your horses. Firmly planting the heel of your palm on Kinu's forehead, you give your daughter a noogie right between the eyes. The little white kitsune's ears perk up at your touch, then begin wiggling uncontrollably, as do her three tails. "Eheehee! It tickles!" Of course. You wouldn't do it if it didn't tickle. "Come on! Pet more! Pet more!" Grinning madly, Kinu pushes her head against your hand, nuzzling against you to and fro. Now, now. She can't rush these things. Just like with fruit, she's got to learn how to stop and savor the pleasantries of life instead of wolfing them down with wanton abandon. Now that your palm is secure, you lay your fingers down atop your daughter's head and dig them into the smooth, flowing hair and fur, then begin rubbing with a gentle back-and-forth motion. "Aaah..." Heh. Pushing back against you like this, Kinu looks more like a fox than a human, eyes closed and head nodding back and forth as you continue to pet away. The little kitsune's mouth opens and closes wordlessly as you lavish affection upon her; she's clearly luxuriating in the simple joy of being pampered, taking it in for everything it's worth. Now, if she wants to properly repay you for your petting, she has to be good and obey her mother when you're not around, okay? "Mmm..." Also, she mustn't stuff herself with fruit until she gets sick from overeating. "Aww..." That's a non-negotiable, and being cute isn't going to help her any. "Okay... if you'll pet me some more, [kinu.Dad]." It's a deal, then. You finish up the simple head-petting, and move on to Kinu's ears. They're less fluffy to the touch than her mother's, but far, far more sensitive; Kinu doesn't have fluffy tufts in her large fox ears, but makes little incoherent yips of delight as your fingertips brush against the hairs within. Little Kinu sighs, then slumps against you and gives you a big hug as you shower every exposed bit of your daughter's ears with plenty of affection. Meanwhile, you hook your fingertips around her ears, scratching at their sensitive backs in turn. Kinu's three tails wrap around her and curl about your feet, their silken fur siding back and forth as she embraces you with everything she has. There, there. When you finally pull away and push a clingy Kinu off you, your daughter has a big, dreamy smile on her face, eyes half-lidded and unfocused until she gathers her wits again. "That was fun." Wasn't it? You'll give her another petting if she continues being a good girl until the next time you visit. "Okay, I will, [kinu.Dad]! Bye bye now! Make Mama happy, okay!"
rows.translation: 当你伸手去拿的时候，小娟立刻发出了尖叫，因为它知道你在想要什么。我想让人抚摸我！我想让人抚摸我！ 哎呀，她对这件事真是充满热情啊。 你应该知道， [kinu.Dad]等我长大了，一定会反过来抚摸你。那将是对你一直以来抚摸我的回报，所以现在你应该多抚摸我一些哦！ 为什么不是现在呢？ 我的个子还不够高…… 好了，姑娘，先别急。你把手掌的根部紧紧按在小娟的额头上，然后用力敲了她的太阳穴一下。那只小白色的狐妖听到你的触碰后，耳朵立刻竖了起来，接着它的三条尾巴也开始不受控制地扭动起来。 嘿嘿嘿！真好玩啊！ 当然。如果这件事不能让你感到有趣、感到开心，你也不会去做它。 来吧！多摸摸它吧！多摸摸它吧！小娟疯狂地笑着，把头往你的手上蹭来蹭去，紧紧依偎在你身边。 现在，她不能急于求成。就像品尝水果一样，她必须学会停下来，细细品味生活中这些美好的时刻，而不是肆无忌惮地狼吞虎咽。现在你的手掌已经稳稳地放在她头上了，你用手指轻轻抚摸她那顺滑柔亮的头发和毛发，然后开始有节奏地轻轻按摩起来。 啊…… 呵呵，像这样对你撒娇的小娟，看起来更像只狐妖而不是人类——她闭着眼睛，不断地点头回应你的抚摸。当你给予她关爱时，她的小嘴无声地张开又闭上，显然她正在尽情享受这种被宠爱的快乐，把每一刻都珍视不已。 现在，如果她想好好报答你对自己的关爱，就必须在你不在的时候听妈妈的话，乖巧地表现出来，好吗？ 嗯…… 另外，她也不能吃太多水果，否则会因为吃得太多而生病。 哎呀…… 这是没有商量余地的，而且长得可爱对她来说也毫无帮助。 好吧……如果你再多摸摸我一会儿的话 [kinu.Dad]." 那就这么定了。你先完成那些简单的抚摸动作，然后再继续抚摸小娟的耳朵。她的耳朵摸起来没有她妈妈的耳朵那么柔软蓬松，但敏感度要高得多；小娟那对大大的狐妖耳朵上并没有柔软的绒毛，但当你的指尖轻轻触碰到里面的毛发时，她就会发出一些愉悦的、断断续续的叫声。小希努轻轻叹了口气，然后靠在你身上，给了你一个紧紧的拥抱。而你则用充满爱意的手抚摸着女儿耳朵的每一个部位。与此同时，你也用指尖轻轻挠了挠她耳朵后面那些敏感的地方。小娟的三条尾巴环绕着她的身躯，又盘绕在你的足部边，它们那柔软的毛皮不断地来回摆动，而她则用自己全部的力量紧紧拥抱着你。 好了，好了。 当你终于拉开距离，将这个黏人的小娟从自己身上推开时，你的女儿脸上露出了灿烂而梦幻般的笑容，她的眼睛半闭着，目光有些呆滞，直到她重新恢复了清醒。 那真是太有趣了。 不是吗？如果她下次你来访之前继续表现得好，你就会再抚摸她一次的。 好的，我会的。 [kinu.Dad]好了，现在要走了哦！要让妈妈开心，好吗？
