rows.raw: " Hmm. You're not one for sitting around today, so why don't the both of you go out into the woods that surround the hill? She can show you all the things in that enchanted forest that she's discovered while you're gone, perhaps get some exercise while you're about it. You spend so much time with Kiyoko when you do come and visit her in the astral plane; exploring the rest of this pocket dimension with a little guide at your side would be quite the treat. "Okay! Come with me, [kinu.Dad] — I'm going to show you something really cool!" Without waiting for a reply, Kinu takes hold of one of your hands and starts tugging insistently, making a beeline for the forest's edge. Your foxy daughter leads you down trails and over roots, practically bouncing along like she's had one too many peaches. Come to think of it, she probably has... [var3|The both of you end up by the bank of a rocky river, its channel wide and flat, the water clear and sluggish. Barefoot as always, Kinu wades out into middle without so much as a thought, the water coming up to her waist. "See, [kinu.Dad]? There are fish in here! Most of them aren't really big enough to be eaten on their own, but if you take them home and pound them whole into fish paste they go really well on rice! Especially when you mix them with onions and ginger! You don't even need to gut them!" Mm. You notice she's got nothing to fish with, though. Kinu beams. "You catch them by hand, that's what makes it so fun! C'mon, give it a try!" As you watch, your daughter rolls up her sleeves, stoops down into the water and turns into a predator, albeit a small and fuzzy one. Looking every part of the fox kit on the prowl, her big blue eyes watch the waters intently, her hands hidden beneath the surface. And then, lightning-quick, the waters foam, and — "Hee hee! Look! Look!" Wriggling about in Kinu's cupped hands is a small, silvery fish, no bigger than your thumb. "See? All you have to do is be faster than they are! C'mon, I'll show you!" You spend the next couple of hours wading about in the shallows with Kinu, your daughter trying to teach you the fine art of hand fishing. [var0|While you try your best under Kinu's patient guidance and even manage to land a few catches here and there, most of your attempts come up empty-handed. The fish are just too quick for you — you're just not trained for this kind of thing. "Don't worry, [kinu.Dad]," Kinu reassures you with a pat on your side. "I get that you don't do this often, and that's okay. Being with you is still lots of fun!" Aww, cripes. You think you just got something in your eye... |[var1|Even for someone who doesn't do this often, you make a fairly good showing, landing more than a dozen small fish over the course of those two hours. Kinu is a slow and patient teacher, pointing out your mistakes and giving you encouragement where warranted; every now and then, you step back to see her demonstrate how to flip one of the river fish out of the water. While it's true that you don't have the natural agility and reflexes she has, her tutelage makes you feel as if you're truly accomplishing something. "See? See? Nothing to it! I've got a cloth with me; we can wrap all this up and take it home to Mama! Then out comes the salt, the mortar and the pestle, and we'll have so much fun! Not immediately, though — I'm all wet and my fingers and toes are wrinkly." |Unsurprisingly, you take to this little exercise like a fox-girl to sweet peaches, and are flipping little fishies out of the water and into your hands in no time at all. Kinu hangs around you for a little while to make sure you've got the technique down right, but soon splashes off to do her own hand fishing when she's sure you've got things down pat. By the time the two hours are up, you've managed to gather quite the pile of freshwater anchovies between the two of you. Stepping out of the river shallows, Kinu shakes herself dry, then wraps the lot in a cloth. "Wow, you're really good at this, [kinu.Dad]!" Guess you're just a natural, eh? "I'm going to have to take this home to Mama. We'll pound them and put the lot on hot rice tomorrow, and it's going to taste great!" ]] |Eventually, the trees part into a wide forest clearing, sunlight pouring in from the clear blue sky; the scents of several different species of blossoms greets you as you step into the knee-high grasses with Kinu at your side. Indeed, a spread of color unfurls before your eyes as you take in the sight, a small pond in the middle of the clearing serving as its centerpiece. "Isn't this amazing? I need to get some flowers for my flower arrangement lessons with Mama tomorrow. Since it's for my education and all..." Should you help her? "Umm... not really. I don't know very much about flower arrangement yet, but Mama says it's important to carefully remove them so they stay alive for as long as possible when we put them in vases. I just want you to watch me and take in this place, [kinu.Dad] — for some reason, this is so much more fun when you're around!" If she says so, but you're not going to let your hands go idle, either. While Kinu scampers off into the flower field, you find a large mossy log and take a seat. Kiyoko may be teaching your daughter about blossoms from the perspective of her culture, but that doesn't mean you can't do the same. There, these'll serve as a pretty decent base... maybe a few of these... and a dash of color with these, too... Time passes, and you're just about done when Kinu returns, a large bunch of flowers in her hands. She's dirty, she's sweaty, there're grass stains on her knees and clothes, and you suspect she might have waded out into the pond at least once. But then again, she wouldn't be Kinu if she didn't do all these things. "Ta-daaaaah!" Your little fox-daughter shoves the impromptu bouquet in your face. "This looks great! I don't know their meaning, but they look great nevertheless!" Indeed, they do. And while she was gone, you made something for her. See? As Kinu tilts her head up, you plonk the flower crown you made straight on her brow, using her large fox ears to hold it firmly in place. She squirms a little, but discomfort soon gives way to hyperactive excitement as she scoots over to the pond to look at her reflection in the water. "Eeeee! This is really great, [kinu.Dad], and it smells sooo nice on my head! How do you get the flowers to hold together like that? All the flowers look really good against my fur!" Ha, you're just glad that she likes it well enough. It's not the best, since it's only what you could cook up on a moment's notice, but anything you put on your darling daughter is going to look great. "Hee hee, I love being praised! Now I gotta repay you! Gonna give you a great big hug, and there's nothing you can do about it!" Kinu is good to her word, the little kitsune flumphing against you and squeezing your legs with her little arms. Petals fall from the flowers she's picked and from the crown on her brow, but she holds on until she's finally satisfied. "Maybe we should be heading back now, [kinu.Dad]. You still have to visit Mama before the day is out, right?" Yeah... and she has to show off her flower crown to everyone while the blooms are at their best. "Hee hee!" |So, where are you going this time? "To find some bees! Wild honey is great, but I'm not tall enough to reach hives in trees... if I stood on your shoulders, though, I could totally get to them! I spotted a few good ones some days ago, and have been itching to get at the honey... and then you come along, [kinu.Dad]!" [pc.bg hunter barbarian|You nod; you've had to do this a couple of times yourself out in the wilds as [a] [pc.background]. While it's not without its dangers — getting stung by a swarm of angry bees being only one of them — wild honey's pretty great. Besides, Kinu's a smart girl, and you'll be here to supervise her every step of the way. Now this is the kind of education that your daughter won't be getting from Kiyoko. |You're not entirely sure about this. Isn't she worried about being stung? Kinu looks up at you incredulously. "Stung? Me? Don't be silly, [kinu.Dad]. Oh, I got stung the first dozen times I tried raiding beehives, but I'm pretty confident in my abilities now. Just help me, okay?" The first dozen times? "I think there's a saying, something along the lines of 'nothing worth doing was ever easy?' Anyways, wild honeycomb is totally worth it, and besides, you're here! You'll keep me safe, won't you [kinu.Dad]?" Well, your daughter seems to know what she's doing, and she's right in saying that she isn't just any old fox kit. Besides, this is the kind of education that she won't be getting from her mother... ...You're probably going to regret this, aren't you? ] "Here! Here we are! I saw this one yesterday, but I couldn't reach it!" You look up at where Kinu's pointing, and indeed, there's a hive on one of the lowest boughs of a nearby pine tree, sticking out like the gills of a fish or some kind of gigantic fungus. Sequestered in the crook between bough and trunk, the support both have afforded has allowed the hive to grow to considerable proportions, though still well out of Kinu's reach; the buzzing of bees is deafening even at this distance, and your daughter gives you a big, maddened, and above all, mischievous grin. "Isn't it great? It's really big, and there's so much exposed honeycomb!" And there're so many bees. At least they're bees, and she didn't mistake a wasp's nest for a hive... "Just gotta find some pine needles! Help me, [kinu.Dad]?" Looks like there's no backing out now. The two of you scrounge about in the forest underbrush for a while, collecting some dry deadwood and handfuls of pine needles. Kinu is quick on her feet and even quicker with her hands, taking the deadwood from you and lashing the needles to them with long blades of grass to fashion a long-handled smokestick. [pc.bg hunter barbarian|Looking at her work away, you can't help but feel your heart swell with pride. Your daughter might take after her mother in appearance, but she's [a] [pc.background] at heart; it's nice to see once more that Kinu inherited your spirit, if not your appearance. |Seeing her work with practiced ease, you relax a little. At least this clearly isn't the first time your daughter's done this, although it does raise some questions as to whether her mother knows she's been raiding beehives... ] A snap of your daughter's fingers, and a gout of pale blue foxfire washes over the smokestick's tip, setting it alight. A moment's concentration, another snap of her fingers, and a gentle breeze starts up in the direction of the beehive. "Okay, [kinu.Dad]! This is where teamwork is important — I need to stand on your shoulders so I can smoke out the hive and get us some honeycomb! You ready?" As ready as she'll ever be. You crouch down, and Kinu scrambles up your back and onto your shoulders. It's a bit of a balancing act, but she's a little fox and pretty light to boot; with your hands on her calves and her natural agility, she's able to keep upright while you start at a brisk walk towards the hive, all three of her tails looped under your arms for extra support. "Slowly does it, [kinu.Dad]. No need for any sudden moves. Just act natural." [pc.bg hunter barbarian|Oh, you know. This might not be her first time doing this, but neither is it yours. Although you do have to wonder if wild honey here tastes different from that of the waking world... |Act natural, she says. Easier said than done, especially when there're so many of the little terrors buzzing about you. ] "Oh-kay. We're almost there. Almost there..." You don't dare to look up, but ahead of you, Kinu lets the thick, roiling clouds of white smoke emanating from the end of her smoke stick to envelop most of the beehive, allowing the smoke to stew for about a minute before making her next move. Working deftly, she draws a small knife from the folds of her yukata, eyes the beehive through the smoke, then slices deeply and pries loose a section of honeycomb as long as her forearm. You're half-expecting either of you to be stung at any moment, but no sharp pinpricks of pain come to assail you or Kinu. As the smoke begins to clear, you see the bees clustered about their hive, still seemingly placated; a few buzz angrily in the air, but aren't up for pressing an attack. "See? That wasn't so bad." Kinu lets go of you, hops off your shoulders, and does a little somersault in the air before landing on her feet with a flourish. She stomps out the smokestick on the soft forest soil, then presents the filched honeycomb for your approval. "It's called teamwork!" My, that's a pretty big one. "And I couldn't have done it without you, [kinu.Dad]. Come on, let's go find someplace where we can wash this, then I'll open it up!" So it comes to pass that the two of you wind up by the shallows of a forest stream; Kinu washes off bits of wax from the comb, then splits it in half with her knife and cuts off the top. Ears wiggling, a big smile on her face, your kitsune daughter presents you with your share of the spoils. "Ta-daaaah! You've got to love this stuff. It's light and tasty without being cloyingly sweet like candies are! You can really taste the flowers in them — that's why I only cut off a bit of the comb each time, so that the bees don't move away and there's always more to be had!" Right, that's pretty forward-looking of her. [pc.bg hunter barbarian|Well, no time like the present, then. You've had wild honey before, but somehow this particular comb promises to be much better than most you've sampled in the past. Maybe it's because your daughter worked so hard to get it for you... Yeah, that's probably why it smells so great. "I want to do this again sometime, [kinu.Dad]. Standing on your shoulders makes me feel really tall! I can get to so many places I couldn't before... the possibilities are endless!" |One thing, though. It does smell pretty great, but is it okay to eat the honey straight from the comb? She did wash it in the stream, but... "Well... I could go home with it and put it through Mama's sieve, but then she'd notice and make me share. Also, it loses some of its flavor and becomes thicker, and I don't like that. I kinda prefer surprises in my honeycomb! "Don't worry about it, though, you won't get sick or anything. Did you know you can put honey on bandages, and they'll stop the wound from getting infected? I read that in one of Mama's books!" ] Mm-mm-mm. Without further ado, Kinu tears into the honeycomb with undisguised glee, her three tails curled about herself as she empties the beeswax cells of their precious contents. Sweet wild honey gets all over the little kitsune's face, chin and fingers as she polishes off the lot, getting everything all sticky. Despite all this, your daughter is deliriously happy as she savours her spoils, polishing off the last of the honey with her tongue and sucking on her fingers to get as much of it into her as possible. While you know she's not usually a fan of sweet things, the light, fruity aroma of the honey has clearly changed her mind. You have to admit it's good. There's a little bit of loose beeswax here and there and some of the honey has crystallised, but it's still pretty tasty. The point that no one really needs to eat here pipes up in the back of your mind, but that isn't the point — the point is spending a lovely time out here with your hyperactive rapscallion of a foxy daughter. "Did you want the rest of that, [kinu.Dad]?" Naaah, you'll be having it all. You worked as hard as she did for it. "Okie! Just give me the leftover comb so I can wash it out, there's plenty of stuff you can do with beeswax!" By the way she's looking, she ought to wash herself out as well. Kiyoko's going to be pretty mad if she turns up on the doorstep all sweet-smelling and sticky. "Hee hee!" |Where does she intend to take you this time? Any good sights of late? As far as you can understand it, the forest is practically infinite — yet whenever you want to return to the cherry blossom tree, it's never more than a few dozen paces away... "We're going to be picking mushrooms! A certain kind, in fact." Oh? What kind? "Do you know what a matsutake is, [kinu.Dad]?" [pc.bg hunter barbarian|As Kinu rattles off the description to you, realization slowly dawns: you do know this mushroom. The ones that grow in the Frost Marches have white caps instead of the brown ones your daughter is describing, but are edible enough, and they certainly don't have the aromatic scent that's got Kinu so excited. Either way, they should be pretty safe, you think — it's not as if anything you eat here counts as real, right? |As you listen to Kinu excitedly rattle off the description, a small worm of doubt finds its way into your mind: eating wild mushrooms isn't generally the best of ideas, or at least that's what you've always been told. Nevertheless, your daughter is a smart cookie, and seems to know what she's doing. Trusting her should be fine, right? Oh well, it's not as if anything you eat here is for real, isn't it? Could you even get sick from dream food? Every time you've had a meal with Kiyoko, that's never carried into the waking world... ] "...You find them about the roots of pines! I'll show you! They're supposed to be really seasonal, but Mama kinda controls things here, so they pop up every so often! Then we'll get lots and lots of them, cook up some for ourselves, then give the rest to Mama! Isn't that amazing?" You ruffle Kinu's hair and tickle her ears. She is really excited about some mushrooms, isn't she? "Ehehe. They're really good. Mama likes to slice them and cook them with rice, but I prefer them roasted over a fire. I think food tastes better when it's more natural, [kinu.Dad]." So long as that doesn't mean she's eating her food raw... or at least, that which isn't meant to be eaten raw. "Okay! We're here! We're here!" Indeed, here you are. Tall, thick-rooted pines tower above this section of the forest; judging by the looks of them, if they were real they'd have to be centuries old to get this big. Kinu hops excitedly from dirt mound to dirt mound, then drops to her hands and knees and starts crawling away from the trail and into the underbrush. Nose to the ground, tails swishing behind her, Kinu clambers over roots and across soft mats of old pine needles, scrounging in the dirt and getting stains all over her yukata. Pick up the trail yet? "Ssh! I'm concentrating!" This goes on for perhaps five more minutes, Kinu's face a mask of absolute seriousness as she crawls all over the forest floor in a winding, snaking pattern. Just when you start wondering if she's going to get anywhere, your daughter pounces on one particular spot that doesn't seem any different from any other, then starts digging through dirt and old pine needles with her bare hands. "It's here! It's here! Come and see, [kinu.Dad]!" Now you see it too — a rounded cap amidst the underbrush, poking its way out of the soft forest soil. With all the utmost care of a mother tending to her newborn, Kinu unearths the mushroom, digging away at the surrounding dirt with her fingers until she's exposed enough of the treat to wrench it free. "Hee hee, this is great! Look! Look!" Grinning madly, Kinu holds up the mushroom for you to see. Long and thin, a pale brown cap veined with white — even freshly dug from the earth, you can smell it[pc.ra lupine|, and what a scent it is to your lupine nose. Whatever else you might call it, it's strong; there's little doubt that you'd be able to track this kind of scent pretty well|]. "Now it's your turn to hunt for matsutake, [kinu.Dad]! I'll help you! I've got a good nose, after all!" [pc.bg hunter barbarian|Oh, you're game. If the brown-capped variety is anything like the white-capped one, then this shouldn't be too hard. Besides, you've got your floofy, squishy daughter at your side helping you, right? |All right, all right. This sort of thing isn't exactly what you were raised to do, but you're willing to give it a go for your floofy daughter. Besides, she loves showing off how much she knows about things, right? Perfect for her to flaunt her knowledge of mushroom hunting. ] Under Kinu's direction, you follow her lead, getting down on all fours to creep close to the forest floor like what she's doing. [pc.ra lupine|It feels a little silly to be doing this, but then again, it's for a good cause. Now that you've scented what that mushroom smells like, though, it's hard to miss it. Earthy, spicy, not altogether unlike cinnamon in some respects — lupines are great at catching scents, and you're no exception. Before long, you're ahead of Kinu, pushing aggressively through the underbrush in search of the source of the scent. "Where are you going, [kinu.Dad]?" Ssh! You're concentrating! Kinu gets the hint and falls silent, following along behind as you track down your quarry. It's getting closer and closer, and... yes, there, behind that fallen log! "Oh! Oh! I smell it too!" Kinu doesn't need any encouragement, scampering forward and pushing at the log with all her might. It shifts, it moves, and she scrounges about in the dirt until she's unearthed a pine mushroom as long as your hand. So, how'd you do? "Not bad, not bad! You have a really good nose, [kinu.Dad]!" Aw, shucks. So, who's got the better sense of smell, the fox or the hound? "We'll see! Since you clearly don't need me to teach you anything, we'll see who can get more, okay?" The two of you spend the next hour or so rooting about in the shadow of the pine trees, covering a pretty wide swathe as you uncover more mushrooms, large, firm, and with that heady aroma that Kinu promises is a harbinger of delectable things to come. Between your nose and hers, you manage to fill your daughter's pockets with all manner of sharp-smelling pine mushrooms. "'Eehee! Guess I can't beat you, [kinu.Dad]. Truth be told, I'm kinda jealous of your nose..." You smile and ruffle Kinu's hair. She's not half bad herself. "Guess we ought to be heading home now. You still have to visit Mama before you go, right? I have to put all of these matsutake down and wash them, too — watch out for me the next time you come visit, okay? We'll roast them up and have a feast!" Of course, of course. There's a good girl. |[pc.bg hunter barbarian|Your time as [a] [pc.background] meant that you'd have to live off the land in the past, and this isn't even amongst the top three awkward things you've done in order to bring home dinner. Although there is something to be said for food you don't have to clean the dirt off of before cooking... "Smell anything, [kinu.Dad]?" Not really — you don't have a nose like hers. Nevertheless, you can make an educated guess from what you know of forestry and wilderness survival; mushrooms and fungi all share some basic needs, and combined with what she's told you about these matsutake mushrooms and their habits, you can use your time and energy in the most efficient manner. At this point, Kinu has fallen largely silent, watching your movements intently as you go about your search. Now this is another way to get an education, instead of sitting around with books and scrolls all day. Aha. Now that spot in the shade of that tall pine... still on all fours, you shuffle over and brush away some rotting bark and old pine needles. Barely have you begun when that same spicy smell greets you, and Kinu rushes over to dig up your find while you stand and dust your hands off. "Ha-ha! You're really great, [kinu.Dad]! Of course, I knew it was there, but I wouldn't have if it weren't for my nose." Say, why don't the two of you work together? You can look out for likely spots and direct her to them, and she can check them out without needing to go to all the trouble of clearing or digging. Teamwork, it's called. "Teamwork!" Without skipping a beat, Kinu's face is down to the ground once more, sniffing away as she crawls forward through the underbrush. She really is like a little fox, isn't she? Between the two of you, though, you have a grand old time; with you surveying the surroundings and Kinu checking out particular locales, squeezing into cramped spots with her petite form, it's easy to cover a wide swathe of forest. Between your daughter's nose and energy and your own experience, it's not long before you've filled the pockets of her yukata to bulging with spicy-smelling pine mushrooms. "This is great!" Kinu says as she finally gets to her feet, stained and dirty all over. "We picked so many today!" Mm-hm. She should be sure to give them some time to recover on their own, or there probably won't be as many the next time she comes around. Then she'll have to ask her mother to do something about it, and that would be awkward, wouldn't it? "Ehe..." You smile and ruffle Kinu's hair. Come now, it's about time you started heading back — she has to put down her find, and you have to go see her mother. |[var2|While this isn't exactly what you thought you'd be doing with your life, it's always good to try new things, right? Kinu's excitement is palpable as she shepherds you between the tall pines, stopping every now and then to explain the intricacies of mushroom hunting to you. "You have to watch out for the squirrels, they're sneaky little thieves. They won't just eat the matsutake out of the ground, but leave your find alone for a bit and they'll come down from the trees and try to steal them. That's why I always know where the nearest pine cone is; that way I can shoo them off at a distance. I can hit them pretty often!" [pc.isDK|There's your girl — nailing those nasty, thieving squirrels! Little fuzzy bastards getting what's coming to them.|Well, when you look at it from the squirrels' point of view, she's the one stealing the mushrooms from their forest.] Really makes one think, doesn't it? Kinu sticks her tongue out at you. "We should have a throwing competition sometime, [kinu.Dad]. But for now..." Yes, but for now, what's that over there? Your daughter's gaze follows your pointed finger, and then she stops and sniffs the air. "Hey, you're right, [kinu.Dad]! C'mon, c'mon!" Without waiting for so much as a reply, Kinu breaks away from you, hops over a rotting log, and bounds over to the spot you pointed out. Her face a mask of furious concentration, Kinu grubs about in the dirt, digging with her fingers until she pulls out a long-stalked mushroom from the cool earth. "Ta-daaaah!" Hey, that one's pretty big. "So it is! You have pretty good eyes, [kinu.Dad]! Almost as good as mine!" Almost as good, she says? Why, whose side of the family does she think she got that amazing eyesight from? "Ehehe. C'mon, then — let's go find some more! With two pairs of amazing eyes and my nose, we'll be unstoppable!" The next hour or so is filled with all sorts of dirty, earthy fun with Kinu. You'd never thought mushroom hunting would be your sort of thing, but having a bouncy, noisy eight-year old kitsune child along with you makes it all worthwhile — Kinu is clearly the more experienced one at this, but your eyes are sharp enough for you to make a good number of finds on your own. Eventually, the two of you gather enough pine mushrooms to fill Kinu's pockets, and the both of you are quite thoroughly stained all over with what the forest has to offer. "This looks pretty good, [kinu.Dad]," Kinu says as she unloads her haul onto a mossy, flat-topped rock and counts the mushrooms one by one before packing them away. "I'll have to take them home and wash them, of course, but it shouldn't be more than a day or two before I can have them ready to be roasted. You'll be there too, right?" Uh... "I know you're busy out there trying to save everyone, so it doesn't matter if you're too busy," Kinu continues, her ears turning downwards. "But I would really, really like it if you'd drop by the next time you visit, okay? Will you keep that in mind, [kinu.Dad]?" Oh all right, you will. In the meantime, you should probably be taking her home. You still need to see her mother before your time here is up, after all. |You've little doubt that you look quite silly bumbling about like this, and that feeling soon turns to embarrassment at how well your daughter is doing in spite of you. Kinu practically bounds from spot to spot on the soft carpet of dirt and dry pine needles, pouncing on suspicious heaps, and when she does find one of those coveted mushrooms, running up to present it to you with pride. Untrained and with none of the natural advantages that Kinu has, mushroom hunting is more easily said than done. This is your daughter's world — and you're more aware than ever that it isn't yours. Yet being invited to play with her in it, if only for a little while... it makes it all worth it? "Look, [kinu.Dad]! I found another one!" Kinu races up to you with a long, thick brown-capped mushroom in her hands, fresh dirt still on it. "Aren't I amazing?" Mm-hm. She sure is a clever girl. Truth be told, you're not sure if you're just weighing her down. Your daughter preens at the praise, ears twitching all the while. "Ehe... I don't mind, [kinu.Dad]. Just having you watch me makes me want to do my best... so you're still helping, even if you don't manage to find any matsutake!" Gods, when did she learn to be so sweet and adorable? "I mean, it's fun to go out into the forest and play, but it's always more fun when you play together with someone else. Mama can't come out with me all the time since she's so busy, but you'll do just as well!" You sigh and ruffle Kinu's hair, eliciting a happy squeal from your daughter. Yeah... she's right. Out of the mouths of babes, as the saying goes. "Don't worry, [kinu.Dad]. Even if you're not very good at it, matsutake hunting is still fun, and I'll help you! I'm a good helper!" Your daughter is good to her word. Even though you're content to step back and leave the bulk of the work to her, Kinu urges you forward through the underbrush with all the eagerness of a bright-eyed puppy. She sniffs out each hidden mushroom, lets you dig out the firm, earthy prize, then the both of you take turns savouring the unique spicy, cinnamon-like aroma of these brown-capped pine mushrooms before she tucks them away into her yukata. "It's okay to not know things," Kinu explains as she sniffs about clumps of old pine cones and needles alike. "I wasn't born knowing very much, either. If you won't admit to yourself that you don't know things, then you won't learn anything, so there's nothing wrong with that. Watch and learn, [kinu.Dad]!" You get the feeling she's relishing the chance to show off as much as you are in watching her, but who's complaining? It's a nice walk in the woods with your kitsune daughter, having a leisurely chat with her, and feeling the cool dirt on your fingers as you dig up her next prize... Gods, how long has it been? An hour? Two? You still need to visit Kiyoko before your time's up, and Kinu is thoroughly dirty and scruffy at this point. Perhaps it's time to head back. "All right, [kinu.Dad]. I didn't get as many as I'd hoped to, but it's all right because I got to spend time with you! Look, once I get these matsutake all washed up and prepared you can come look for me, okay? Then we can roast them up and have a feast! It should only take a day or two, please tell me you can come! I know you're really busy, but..." Unf. It's hard not to say yes to Kinu and her big blue eyes... all right, you'll see what you can do, but she should go ahead if you don't manage to visit soon. No point in letting the mushrooms spoil. "Yaaaaaay!" ] ] ] ]"

rows.original: As the two of you make the trek back to the hilltop, Kinu suddenly brightens. "Oh, right! I had so much fun playing that I almost forgot! We gotta clean up before entering the house!" Before you can reply, Kinu snaps her fingers, and the dirt and damp of the forest falls away from the two of you, leaving you feeling refreshed, a faint scent of mint lingering on your [pc.skinFurScales]. Hey, that's a pretty neat trick. Your daughter beams. "Mama usually doesn't want me using magic to clean up, but I think this warrants an exception. You've got to look your best while playing with Mama, right? It's the least I can do to thank you for taking the time to play with me, [kinu.Dad]." No, no. You had fun too and even if you wouldn't have, seeing her happy makes you happy, too. "Aww, that's so sweet. I'm supposed to be the sweet one here!" Kinu makes a pouty face, but can't hold it as the little kitsune breaks into giggles. "Why don't you go ahead, [kinu.Dad]? I think I can see home from here — I know Mama would like some time alone to play with just you, okay? Don't let me get in your way! Byebye!" Leaning forward, your foxy daughter gives you a little kiss on the side, then turns tail — all three of them — and scampers up the hillside, soon disappearing from sight. For someone who's just spent hours playing in the forest, she sure has a lot of energy...
rows.translation: 当你们两人开始往山顶走去时，小娟突然亮了起来。哦，对了！玩得太开心了，差点忘了这件事！在进屋之前，我们得先把东西收拾干净才行！ 还没等你来得及回答，小娟打了个响指，森林中的尘土和湿气立刻从你们身上消失了，你们顿时感到神清气爽，身上还残留着一丝淡淡的薄荷香气。 [pc.skinFurScales]嘿，这个技巧真是太棒了。你的女儿开心极了。妈妈通常不让我用魔法来打扫，但我觉得这次应该是个例外。当你和妈妈一起玩的时候，你肯定想看起来最漂亮吧？能感谢你抽出时间陪我玩，这也是我至少能做的吧？ [kinu.Dad]." 不，不。你也很开心，而且即使你没有开心，看到她开心，你也会感到开心的。 哇，太贴心了。本来应该是我来表现贴心一面的才对啊！小娟做了个撅嘴的表情，但很快就忍不住笑了起来，因为那只小狐妖突然开始咯咯地笑起来。你为什么不继续呢？ [kinu.Dad]我想从这里应该就能看到家了……我知道妈妈肯定想有段时间能单独和你一起玩，好吗？别让我妨碍你们哦！再见！ 你那机灵的女儿向前倾了倾身子，在你的脸颊上轻轻一吻，然后三个人一起转身，快步跑上了山坡，很快就消失在了视线之外。对于一个刚刚在森林里玩了几个小时的人来说，她确实精力充沛得很……

rows.original: Well, you don't feel up to running around and getting yourself all winded and dirty — after all, you're intending to see her mother later on and ought to at least look decent. How about a nice board game out in the open? "Are you sure, [kinu.Dad]?" Kinu clasps her hands together and starts rubbing away, impish glee written all over her adorable face. "Are you absoluuuutely sure?" Yes, you know how strategy games are her forte. Yes, you know how even her mother has trouble beating her at times. But she's your darling daughter, and [pc.cunningRange 0 50 80 |even if you're not the best at these kinds of games, you still want to entertain her. Who knows, you might even improve with time. Kinu seems to have realized something, and stops her hand-rubbing. "Yeah, about that, [kinu.Dad]... the thought is really appreciated, but when I turn it over in my head some more it doesn't really seem appealing to me anymore. Don't take this the wrong way or anything, but there really isn't fun in walking all over an opponent." So, she doesn't want to play today? "Not like this. It would be unfair, and besides, I want you to have fun too, not suffer in silence for my sake over something so trivial. Why don't we play something else?" Sheesh, when she puts it that way... it's hard not to feel guilty, too. All right, then — maybe you'll find another game to play with her... |you think you can put up a good fight, even if you're likely to lose. Who knows, you might even get lucky and pull an unexpected move over on her. "There are some who say playing against beginners can be enlightening at times," Kinu replies matter-of-factly. "They may even attempt gambits more seasoned players would deem too risky or not worth one's time." Haha, that's one way to put it. You don't think you're that bad, though... "It's all — ahem — relative. At least you're not a walkover like some of my siblings are, [kinu.Dad]. Come on, let's get started!" |besides, you think you have a decent-to-good chance of winning, even if she's your opponent. Kinu whistles, her ears perky and ever so innocent. "If that's how you feel, [kinu.Dad]. If that's how you feel. Maybe I'll go easy on you and let you win." No, absolutely not. If you're going to come out on top, it's going to be in spite of her doing her best, and you absolutely forbid her from throwing the game just because she feels sorry for you. She's got to be honest and give it her all, okay? Kinu grins. "I had a feeling that you'd say that, [kinu.Dad]; I just wanted to hear it from you in no uncertain terms. Okay, I won't hold back!" ]
rows.translation: 嗯，你大概没精力到处跑来跑去，弄得自己气喘吁吁、满身脏兮兮的吧——毕竟你之后还打算去见她的母亲，至少应该看起来整洁一些。不如在户外玩一款不错的桌游怎么样？ 你确定吗？ [kinu.Dad]?"小娟双手交叠，开始搓来搓去，她那可爱的脸上洋溢着调皮的笑容。你真的确定吗？ 没错，你们都知道策略游戏才是她的强项。没错，就连她的母亲有时也很难战胜她。但她毕竟是你们的宝贝女儿啊 [pc.cunningRange 0 50 80 |即使你不是这类游戏的高手，你仍然想逗她开心。谁知道呢，随着时间的推移，你说不定还会进步呢。 小娟似乎意识到了什么，于是停止了揉手的行为。是的，关于那个 [kinu.Dad]……这个想法确实很值得考虑，但再仔细想一想，我觉得它并没有那么吸引人。别误会我的意思，但真的，一路追着对手跑来跑去并没有什么乐趣可言。 所以，她今天不想玩了吗？ 不是这样的。那样太不公平了，而且，我也希望你能开心地玩，而不是因为这么琐碎的事情而默默忍受。我们为什么不玩点别的吧？ 哎呀，她这么一说……确实会让人感到内疚啊。好吧，那你就再找别的游戏和她一起玩吧…… |你觉得自己就算很可能失败，也能好好抗争一番。谁知道呢，说不定你还会走运，使出某个意想不到的招数，反而战胜她呢。 有些人认为，与初学者对战有时也会让人有所收获。纪久回答得非常淡然。他们甚至可能会尝试那些经验更丰富的玩家认为风险太大或不值得花费时间的策略。 哈哈，这么说也有道理。你难道不觉得自己那个不过，这也挺糟糕的…… 这一切啊——咳——都是相对的。至少你不像我的一些兄弟姐妹那样，那么容易就被击败。 [kinu.Dad]来吧，我们开始吧！ |此外，你认为自己即使面对她这样的对手，也有相当大的胜算。 小娟吹着口哨，她的耳朵竖得高高的，显得格外天真无邪。如果你是这么想的， [kinu.Dad]如果你是这么想的的话，也许我会放你一马，让你赢吧。 不，绝对不行。如果你想取得胜利，那就必须是在她尽了最大努力的情况下依然取得胜利；你绝对不能因为她同情你而让她放弃比赛。她必须诚实面对，全力以赴，明白吗？ 小娟露出了微笑。我就觉得你会这么说 [kinu.Dad]我只是想从你口中明确听到这个答案。好吧，我不会再犹豫了！ ]

rows.original: With that, Kinu breaks off into a quick jog for her home, motioning for you to wait here. The little kitsune can be fast when she puts her mind to it — you don't think more than fifteen minutes have passed before she returns with the board and pieces in her arms, ears all perky and her three silky tails having taken a life of their own with her excitement. "All right, then! Let's find a nice place to sit down and play! There're few things better in life than enjoying a game out with a hilltop breeze caressing your skin; I hope you can share in this simple pleasure, [kinu.Dad]!" So it comes to pass that you and your kitsune daughter wind up in the shade of a parasol, facing each other down over a game of [rand|go|shogi]. You're not exactly sure where the tea and rice crackers came from — one moment they weren't there, the next moment they were — but it's not done to question things too deeply around here. At least the tea is hot and the crackers passable, if very bland and dry. To you, it's like eating paper, but Kinu doesn't seem to mind in the least. For the next hour or so — time is rather indeterminate in the astral plane — all that can be heard is the clacking of pieces against the board, broken every so often by the gentle tinkling of wind chimes. [var0|Kinu's usually cheerful and carefree expression has gathered into one of absolute concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing the board as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|Though you're not too familiar with the game itself, you've had plenty of chances to play chess and other strategy board games in the past, and the principles are eerily similar to what you're facing now. Some things truly are universal, one supposes. |Although you really haven't had the chance to play such board games in the past, you nevertheless manage to intuitively connect some of the strategies to your experiences growing up as [a] [pc.background], and a number of possibilities become open to you. Maybe you're just talented at this kind of stuff. ] The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand|"I believe I've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the looks of things it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more. "I'm not going to deny that; you gave me a run for my money. Ehehe, Mama is the only other person who can do that, and she doesn't have all the time in the world to play with me all day. "Either way, this was a good game. It was fun! I think I learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. |"I believe you've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. "Is it? I'm just good at this, I never quite said I was unbeatable." She looks down at the board again and wiggles in her seat. "Yeah, I see it now, [kinu.Dad]. I could've won if I'd done this —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may be talented, but experience is something that can't be rushed. That being said, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Ehe. This is kinda embarrassing... I'm not sure I deserve the praise if I still lost in the end. It was fun, though. I learned a lot!" So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |[rand|The picture of peaceful serenity doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your kitsune daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and has free rein of the board. It's not long after that you're forced to admit defeat, perhaps a little relieved that this wasn't dragged out any longer than it needed to be. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, chewing her lip as she looks over what pieces remain on the board. Eventually, she sighs and shakes her head, mumbling to herself. "Well, guess you had a bit of bad strategy back there, [kinu.Dad]. Unless I intentionally went easy on you, I don't think there was any way you could've salvaged the situation past the twelfth move back —" she jabs a finger on the board — "there." And you absolutely refuse to let her go easy on you, otherwise what would be the point? "Ehe. I like to think that I'm not the kind of person to enjoy cat-and-mouse games and drag out someone's loss when it's clear there's not much point to doing so. Those get boring fast." Still, did she have fun? "Not from the game itself, I'll admit to that. But spending time with you is always great, [kinu.Dad]." Now there's a honey-tongued little flatterer if you ever saw one. |As the game proceeds, your kitsune daughter gradually becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing as she studies the board. Almost unconsciously, Kinu's three tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. "...And there. Good show, [kinu.Dad], but seems like I win in the end. For a moment I thought that gambit wasn't going to work, but then that, more than anything else, was the time to take a risk." A desperation move, huh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|You've had some time to do things like chess and checkers in your youth, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "Weeeelll... that's one way of putting it, [kinu.Dad]. I'm very thankful for the time you've taken to play with me. I think I learned something from all this. Maybe I'd learn more if you played with me again some other time." Heh. Is that an invitation? Well, you'll see. "Well, I always enjoy the time I get to spend with you, [kinu.Dad], so you should definitely take me up on that offer!" |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of games in your youth, being able to back her into a corner like this must be some kind of achievement in and of itself. Kinu looks up at you, her expression inscrutable. "Well, if you got to play more, [kinu.Dad], who knows how you might improve? Perhaps you should play more strategy games with me in the future?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Well, Mama says that people are more likely to agree with you if you point out how your actions are going to benefit them." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, perhaps realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence. Still, she gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. Untouched, the tea grows cold and the rice crackers lie forlornly on their plate, but neither of you have time for such trivialities. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "Congratulations, [kinu.Dad]. It appears that you've won." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Oh, please. Don't undersell yourself, [kinu.Dad]. Now then, perhaps you ought to play with me more at another time to show that this wasn't a fluke." You grin. Is she really that starved for competent players to challenge? "It's more than that. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We don't get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special, you know? Absence, fondness, and all that good stuff." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thick. ] ] "Either way, thank you once more. I'll stay here, finish up the tea, and pick up the board later, okay? For now, I'd like to go over the game we just had, review our moves and see what could have been done better." You nod, stand and give her a pat on the head. She really takes these games seriously, doesn't she? Kinu squirms under the petting. "Ehe, you don't get good at anything by taking it lightly, [kinu.Dad]. Eee! Not there, it tickles! Um, maybe you should go and see Mama now, okay? I can't think straight with you petting my ears like this." Ha! You give Kinu's hair one final run-through, then say goodbye to your foxy daughter. She'll be here the next time you drop by to visit her mother.

rows.raw: " With that, Kinu breaks off into a quick jog for her home, motioning for you to wait here. The little kitsune can be fast when she puts her mind to it — you don't think more than fifteen minutes have passed before she returns with the board and pieces in her arms, ears all perky and her three silky tails having taken a life of their own with her excitement. "All right, then! Let's find a nice place to sit down and play! There're few things better in life than enjoying a game out with a hilltop breeze caressing your skin; I hope you can share in this simple pleasure, [kinu.Dad]!" So it comes to pass that you and your kitsune daughter wind up in the shade of a parasol, facing each other down over a game of [rand|go|shogi]. You're not exactly sure where the tea and rice crackers came from — one moment they weren't there, the next moment they were — but it's not done to question things too deeply around here. At least the tea is hot and the crackers passable, if very bland and dry. To you, it's like eating paper, but Kinu doesn't seem to mind in the least. For the next hour or so — time is rather indeterminate in the astral plane — all that can be heard is the clacking of pieces against the board, broken every so often by the gentle tinkling of wind chimes. [var0|Kinu's usually cheerful and carefree expression has gathered into one of absolute concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing the board as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|Though you're not too familiar with the game itself, you've had plenty of chances to play chess and other strategy board games in the past, and the principles are eerily similar to what you're facing now. Some things truly are universal, one supposes. |Although you really haven't had the chance to play such board games in the past, you nevertheless manage to intuitively connect some of the strategies to your experiences growing up as [a] [pc.background], and a number of possibilities become open to you. Maybe you're just talented at this kind of stuff. ] The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand|"I believe I've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the looks of things it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more. "I'm not going to deny that; you gave me a run for my money. Ehehe, Mama is the only other person who can do that, and she doesn't have all the time in the world to play with me all day. "Either way, this was a good game. It was fun! I think I learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. |"I believe you've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. "Is it? I'm just good at this, I never quite said I was unbeatable." She looks down at the board again and wiggles in her seat. "Yeah, I see it now, [kinu.Dad]. I could've won if I'd done this —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may be talented, but experience is something that can't be rushed. That being said, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Ehe. This is kinda embarrassing... I'm not sure I deserve the praise if I still lost in the end. It was fun, though. I learned a lot!" So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |[rand|The picture of peaceful serenity doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your kitsune daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and has free rein of the board. It's not long after that you're forced to admit defeat, perhaps a little relieved that this wasn't dragged out any longer than it needed to be. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, chewing her lip as she looks over what pieces remain on the board. Eventually, she sighs and shakes her head, mumbling to herself. "Well, guess you had a bit of bad strategy back there, [kinu.Dad]. Unless I intentionally went easy on you, I don't think there was any way you could've salvaged the situation past the twelfth move back —" she jabs a finger on the board — "there." And you absolutely refuse to let her go easy on you, otherwise what would be the point? "Ehe. I like to think that I'm not the kind of person to enjoy cat-and-mouse games and drag out someone's loss when it's clear there's not much point to doing so. Those get boring fast." Still, did she have fun? "Not from the game itself, I'll admit to that. But spending time with you is always great, [kinu.Dad]." Now there's a honey-tongued little flatterer if you ever saw one. |As the game proceeds, your kitsune daughter gradually becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing as she studies the board. Almost unconsciously, Kinu's three tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. "...And there. Good show, [kinu.Dad], but seems like I win in the end. For a moment I thought that gambit wasn't going to work, but then that, more than anything else, was the time to take a risk." A desperation move, huh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|You've had some time to do things like chess and checkers in your youth, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "Weeeelll... that's one way of putting it, [kinu.Dad]. I'm very thankful for the time you've taken to play with me. I think I learned something from all this. Maybe I'd learn more if you played with me again some other time." Heh. Is that an invitation? Well, you'll see. "Well, I always enjoy the time I get to spend with you, [kinu.Dad], so you should definitely take me up on that offer!" |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of games in your youth, being able to back her into a corner like this must be some kind of achievement in and of itself. Kinu looks up at you, her expression inscrutable. "Well, if you got to play more, [kinu.Dad], who knows how you might improve? Perhaps you should play more strategy games with me in the future?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Well, Mama says that people are more likely to agree with you if you point out how your actions are going to benefit them." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, perhaps realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence. Still, she gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. Untouched, the tea grows cold and the rice crackers lie forlornly on their plate, but neither of you have time for such trivialities. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "Congratulations, [kinu.Dad]. It appears that you've won." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Oh, please. Don't undersell yourself, [kinu.Dad]. Now then, perhaps you ought to play with me more at another time to show that this wasn't a fluke." You grin. Is she really that starved for competent players to challenge? "It's more than that. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We don't get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special, you know? Absence, fondness, and all that good stuff." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thick. ] ] "Either way, thank you once more. I'll stay here, finish up the tea, and pick up the board later, okay? For now, I'd like to go over the game we just had, review our moves and see what could have been done better." You nod, stand and give her a pat on the head. She really takes these games seriously, doesn't she? Kinu squirms under the petting. "Ehe, you don't get good at anything by taking it lightly, [kinu.Dad]. Eee! Not there, it tickles! Um, maybe you should go and see Mama now, okay? I can't think straight with you petting my ears like this." Ha! You give Kinu's hair one final run-through, then say goodbye to your foxy daughter. She'll be here the next time you drop by to visit her mother."

rows.original: the traditional brave adventures/knights in shining armor. Group arcanist/scholar/acolyte in another, stories about gods and spirits and magicians. Barbarian/hunter in another, focus on mysticism/animism/paganism-esque stories. Slum rat/courtesan for urban myths and tales focused around the cities and injustice. Dig around for various myths/fairy tales. "Hooray, a story! I love stories! Mama tells me stories from her homeland, but it's nice to hear tales from all kinds of places! Will you tell me a story from where you grew up?" From where you grew up, eh? Let's see if you can't recall anything good... but first, might as well get comfortable, since this is probably going to take a while. Kinu excitedly leads the both of you over to a mossy tree stump, and you take a seat on the grassy soil with your backs to it, your daughter snuggling up to you. Now, let's see... stories you remember from your youth...
rows.translation: 传统的勇敢冒险故事，以及那些身披闪亮铠甲的骑士们。还有另一类故事，讲述的是法师、学者和学徒们的传奇经历，其中充斥着关于神灵、精灵和魔法师的故事。再有就是以野蛮人或猎人为主角的故事，这类故事侧重于神秘主义、万物有灵论或异教风格的主题。而对于都市传说来说，则以贫民窟居民或妓女作为主角，讲述发生在城市里那些与不公相关的故事。当然，我们还可以挖掘各种不同的神话和童话故事。 太好了，有故事听了！我超爱听故事的！妈妈会给我讲她家乡的故事，不过听到来自各种各样地方的故事也真是太有趣了！你能给我讲讲你成长的地方的故事吗？ 在你成长的地方，对吧？让我们看看你是否还能想起一些美好的回忆……不过首先，还是先放松下来吧，因为这个过程可能会花一些时间。小娟兴奋地带着你们俩来到一棵长满苔藓的树桩旁，你靠在树桩旁的草地上坐下，你的女儿则依偎在你身边。 那么，现在让我们来想想……你年轻时记得的一些故事吧……
