rows.original: For a moment, silence falls over the birthing chamber as Kiyoko takes a moment to catch her breath, resting the newborn kit on her slightly smaller belly. Then, on the edge of your hearing, a shuffling noise as the screen door is drawn aside, and - "Mama?" Weakly, Kiyoko rolls her head over to take in the sight of little Kinu peering into the verdant birthing chamber, and her face becomes even paler. "Kinu! You're not —" But it's too late. Kinu's pale blue eyes are as wide as dinner plates as she takes in her mother's panting, naked form, the mess that's the afterbirth, and finally, the little fox kit in Kiyoko's arms. Swallowing hard, the little kitsune focuses furiously on the last, while studiously ignoring the first two. "I-I'm sorry, Mother. I just wanted..." Kiyoko sighs. "Well, you're here now. What did you want?" "I... I wanted to hold the baby. While they're still small. So when I heard that you were indisposed, I snuck in..." Kinu swallows hard again as she looks down at the mess of afterbirth. "Did... did all that come out of your tummy?" "It's what helps the kit grow while they're in my tummy, yes. But now they don't need it anymore." Kiyoko looks unsure for a moment, then beckons Kinu over. "I suppose since I'm teaching you how to care for your siblings, you should learn about this as well. After all, it was how you were born, and you'll have to go through it yourself someday. [pc.name], would you please help clean up?" "I... this looks yucky." "Of course it is," Kiyoko replies, giving you a nod as you move to pick up one of the damp towels and clean up the mess from the birth. "It's also exhausting, painful, and mind-numbing, at least for the first few times it happens. But it's worth it. You don't regret being born, do you?" Kinu says nothing and just looks down at her feet. She stays like that for half a minute or so, then looks up at her mother and sticks out her arms expectantly. Kiyoko considers her, then carefully hands over the newborn kitsune kit, making sure Kinu's grip is secure before letting go completely. The little kit mewls and snuffles about in Kinu's arms, a small, tightly-wrapped bundle of fluff. Kinu practically bounces in place, petting and stroking her newborn sibling all over. "Eeeeee! So cute! I want one of my own!" "Even knowing where they come from and how they come out?" "I can do it!" Kiyoko can't help but laugh weakly at that. "You'll have to be a lot older before you can get started on that, love. That, and babies don't grow up so quickly outside of the astral plane. You'll have to feed and care for a helpless little kit for more than just a few moments, you know. They'll cry, they'll need to be changed, they'll wake you up when you need sleep the most." "I know." Kiyoko smiles and ruffles her eldest daughter's ears. "You need the right temperament to be a den mother, if you want to be like me. Beauty fades, strength weakens, but a well-cultivated temperament and good-natured attitude will last you for the whole of your life." Kinu hugs the newborn close to her for a little while longer, then looks to her mother worriedly as the little kit begins to wail, a tiny, high-pitched screaming ringing in the air. Despite all the cradling and shushing that she's applying to her little sibling, the fox kit's screaming just gets louder. "Mama! Mama! What do I do?" "Improvise, of course. You'll be having to deal with this a lot when you grow up if you want to be like your mama." Kinu pouts. "That's not very useful..." "It's more an art than a science, which is why you're getting started while you're young. Both experience and instruction are important, but the former counts for more than the latter. Now, let me show you how it's done." Kinu looks a little uncertain, but hands back the newborn to her mother. Exhausted but relieved, Kiyoko cradles her child and shushes the little one's wailing with a few gentle earpets, then turns to Kinu. "You need to be a little more gentle. Babies are delicate." Kinu frowns, then looks up at her sibling snuffling at her mother's breast once more. Several moments of silence pass as Kiyoko slowly recovers a little while longer, then Kiyoko gives her daughter a nod. "You should be going." "But..." "If you want additional lessons on child-rearing, dear, I can make some time for that. At the very least, it'll keep your little hands away from the peach grove. But right now, your mother wants some time alone with your new sibling and your [pc.mf|father|mother]." That doesn't quite satisfy Kinu, but at least the little kitsune is wise enough to let it go. She stiffens up, gives Kiyoko a very formal bow, then slips out of the birthing chambers; the last you see of your daughter are her three silvery-white tails vanishing around the corner.
rows.translation: 一时间，产房里陷入了寂静。清子稍作休息，调整呼吸，将刚出生的小生命放在自己略显隆起的腹部上。随后，你几乎听不见的微弱声响传来——屏风门被轻轻拉开 妈妈？ 基代子无力地转过头，看到了小纪努正从那片翠绿的产房中探出头来，她的脸色变得更加苍白了。小娟！你不可能—— 但为时已晚。金色的淡蓝色眼睛瞪得像餐盘一样大，她看到了母亲那气喘吁吁、赤裸的身体，看到了那些产后的残骸，最后也看到了清子怀中的那只小狐妖幼崽。小狐妖艰难地咽了口唾沫，拼命地注视着最后那个，而刻意忽略了前两个。 对、对不起，妈妈。我只是想…… 清子叹了口气。好吧，你现在来了。你到底想要什么？ 我……我想在宝宝还小的时候抱抱他们。所以当我听说你身体不适时，我就偷偷溜进来了……金子再次艰难地咽了咽口水，低头看着那一团胎盘残渣。那些……那些都是从你肚子里出来的吗？ 没错，正是这种物质在它们还在我肚子里的时候帮助它们成长。但现在，它们已经不再需要它了。清子犹豫了片刻，然后招手让纪久过来。既然我在教你如何照顾你的兄弟姐妹，那你也应该了解一下这个。毕竟，这是你与生俱来的责任，总有一天你也必须亲自经历这个过程。 [pc.name]你能帮忙打扫一下吗？ 我……这个看起来真恶心。 当然是了。清子点了点头，你便拿起一条湿毛巾，开始清理分娩后留下的凌乱景象。至少在最初几次经历这种时候，这确实会让人感到精疲力竭、痛苦不堪，甚至会让人感到麻木。但这一切都是值得的。你不会后悔自己来到了这个世界上，对吧？ 小娟什么也没说，只是低头看着自己的足部。她这样保持了好半分钟左右，然后抬起头看着母亲，满怀期待地伸出双臂。清子仔细地看了看她，然后小心翼翼地将那只新生的狐妖幼崽递到她手中，确保小娟握得稳当之后才松开手。小狐妖在小娟的怀里喵喵叫着、抽抽鼻子，就像一个被紧紧包裹起来的小绒球。小娟高兴得在原地跳来跳去，不停地抚摸和轻拍她的新弟弟妹妹。 哇塞！太可爱了！我也想要一个！ 即使知道它们从哪里来，又是如何形成的？ 我能做到！ 清子听到这话，不禁弱弱地笑了起来。亲爱的，你得再长大一些才能开始做那些事。而且，在星界之外，婴儿的成长速度并不会那么快。你知道的，你得照顾这个无助的小生命，这个责任可不会持续短短几分钟而已。他们会哭闹，需要换尿布，还会在你最需要休息的时候把你吵醒。 我知道。 清子微笑着，轻轻挠了挠女儿的耳朵。如果你想成为像我这样的人，就必须具备合适的性格特质。外貌会消逝，力量也会减弱，但良好的性格修养和友善的态度会伴随你一生。 小娟又将新生儿紧紧抱在怀里片刻，然后忧心忡忡地看向她的母亲——那只小狐妖开始大声哭闹起来，那细小的、高亢的哭声在空气中回荡。尽管小娟不停地安抚着她的弟弟妹妹，但它的哭声却越来越大。 妈妈！妈妈！我该怎么办？ 当然，要即兴发挥。你得想办法解决这个问题。很多等你长大了，如果想成为像你妈妈那样的人的话。 小娟 makes a pout. 那没什么用处…… 这更像是一门艺术，而非科学，因此你需要在年轻的时候就开始学习。经验和指导都很重要，但经验的重要性要远远超过指导。现在，让我来告诉你具体该怎么做。 小娟看起来有些犹豫，但还是把新生儿交还给了她的母亲。基代子虽然疲惫，但心中却感到宽慰。她轻轻抱起自己的孩子，用几句温柔的话语安抚着婴儿的哭声，然后转向小娟。 你得再温柔一点，婴儿可是很脆弱的。 纪夫皱了皱眉头，然后抬头看着正在母亲怀里抽泣的女儿。几秒钟的沉默之后，清子终于慢慢恢复了平静，于是她点了点头，示意女儿可以停止哭泣了。你该走了。 但是…… 亲爱的，如果你想了解更多关于育儿的知识，我完全可以抽时间陪你学习。至少这样，你的小手就不会再去碰那些桃树了。不过现在，你的妈妈想要和一些时间单独和你的新弟弟/妹妹待在一起 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]." 这并没有让小娟完全满意，但至少这只小狐妖还算聪明，没有继续纠缠下去。她挺直身体，向清子行了一个非常正式的鞠躬，然后悄悄地离开了产房；当你最后一次看到你的女儿时，只见她那三条银白色的尾巴在转角处消失了。

rows.original: Hmm. You don't often get the chance to do things as a family, so you're actually considering asking her mother to come out and play as well. That should make it more fun, right? [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |For a moment, you see something flicker across your daughter's face that's not sweet, saccharine joy — hesitation, disappointment, unease, perhaps all of the above in varying amounts. It's gone as soon as you realize it's there, but there's no doubt as to its presence. Kinu's adorable smile returns with enthusiastic vigor, her little body wiggling from side to side as she makes a show of considering the matter. "Okay! Let's go and get her, [kinu.Dad]!" |Your daughter's face brightens up at the suggestion, her soft white ears twitching like mad. "Yeah, that sounds like a really good idea, [kinu.Dad]. Come on, then — let's go!" ] With that, Kinu takes off across the open hilltop, your fox-daughter's short little legs a blur as she makes a beeline for the cabin. Pausing barely long enough to wipe her feet at the threshold, she pushes open the door and hops in with you hot on her heels. "Mama! Mama! [kinu.Dad]'s come to visit today, and we want to play! Come on out, okay? It's such a nice day outside!" With your daughter zipping around at high speeds, it doesn't take long for the two of you to home in on Kiyoko; your fox-wife is [rand |out back behind the tree hanging up laundry from a big basket. As Kinu bursts onto the scene, she serenely secures the last garment onto the clothesline, then steps off the low stool and turns to you. |by the well, drawing a bucket of water. She startles a little when Kinu bursts in on the scene, but softens her expression as she sees you coming in hot on the heels of the little ball of fluff, setting down the empty bucket by the well's side. "Oh my, oh my. If you work her up like this all day, [pc.name], she won't be able to sleep at night." Well then, you'll just have to tire Kinu out so thoroughly that she'll drop like a rock the moment she's put to bed. Does she want to help? It could be fun. |on her hands and knees in one of the hallways, polishing the wooden floor to a shine. It's amazing how she can do such a thing with merely what looks to be a simple rag and water, but Kiyoko is always full of surprises. She sets aside the rag and looks up as Kinu approaches, annoyance creasing her features, but sighs and relents as she sees you hot on your daughter's heels. "It's good that I was just finishing up, because otherwise I'd have to worry about what mischief the both of you were up to while working." Mischief? Well then, it looks like you'll have to make her an accomplice as well and get her to partake in your dastardly deeds. That way she can have some much-needed fun while keeping an eye on the both of you. "Ehehe." Acquiescing resignation crosses your fox-wife's face as she puts aside the rag and bucket. "We do need to do more things together as a family, I suppose." ] "So! So! You'll play with us, Mama?" Little Kinu bounces up and down on the spot. "Oh, all right. [kiyoko.pregStage 3 |But don't expect me to chase you all over the place. You know I'll never be able to catch you when all I can do is waddle around." Kiyoko pats her big, round tummy for emphasis. "If you want to play, let's play something more... calm, shall we?" "Hee hee." "Don't you giggle at me like that, young lady. Soon enough you'll be in my shoes and you'll remember what your mother said when you were a girl. |It's not that often that your [pc.mf|father|mother] visits, after all, and we ought to tire you out nicely so you don't bother us when we're having our time alone. ]" "Eh, okay! So, [kinu.Dad], what do you want to play?" Well, that's up to her, isn't it? She's in charge of entertaining her parents and making sure everyone has a good time, and that's a pretty big responsibility. "Hmm... I know! I know! Follow me!" Kiyoko sighs a little as she [kiyoko.pregStage 3|waddles|starts] off after Kinu. "Well, here we go again." You just smile, take your fox-wife's hand in yours, and putter off to see where your daughter will lead you."

rows.original: [rand |With Kinu headed off, your lovely fox-wife turns and gives you a wide smile. "Ah, to be young again. I wish you were here more often to see our daughter grow..." Yeah, you agree. Still, days like this help make up for it. "Mm-hmm. But the day is still far from over, as you might imagine. Come now, I think that after all this exertion, you and I have earned a little time together, don't you think?"|As Kinu scampers off, your beautiful fox-wife slinks up to you, draping herself across your [pc.chest] and planting her hands on your shoulders. "Ah, our daughter is such a rapscallion. Children are always so cheeky and playful... up until you want an afternoon nap. "Now... how about we go in and get some alone time?"] Of course, of course. Tire out the daughter first, then you get the mother all to yourself. A perfect strategy. "Ehehe." Kiyoko leads you back into the cabin, down the hallway and to the familiar sight of the sitting room. You set up the cushions while she brews the tea and gets the candies, and it's not long before the two of you are relaxing in silence, just savouring the sweetness of each other's company. Keeping up with that energetic fluffy snowball sure has taken it out of the both of you... but that's part and parcel of being a parent, isn't it? "Now," Kiyoko says as she finishes her tea, [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|then moves her hands to rest on her increasingly pregnant tummy, having trouble fitting the fertile bump between her and the table.|the kitsune's immensely gravid tummy resting on her knees as she loosens her muscles and make herself comfortable.|then turns and gives you a warm smile.] "Shall we begin? If you play with our daughter but neglect to play with me, I might get jealous, you know..."
rows.translation: [rand |在小娟离开后，你那位可爱的狐狸妻子转过身来，对你露出了灿烂的笑容。啊，要能再年轻一次就好了。真希望你能多来看看我们的女儿，看看她是怎么成长的…… 是啊，你也是这么认为的。不过，这样的日子还是有助于弥补那些不足的。 嗯，不过正如你想象的那样，这一天还远未结束。来吧，我觉得经过这一切努力，你我确实应该好好享受一些属于我们的时光，不是吗？|当小娟飞快地跑开时，你那位美丽的狐狸妻子悄悄地走到你身边，然后依偎在你的怀里 [pc.chest] 然后将双手放在你的肩上。啊，我们家女儿真是个调皮鬼。孩子们总是这么调皮捣蛋、爱玩耍……直到你想要小睡一会儿的时候。 现在……我们进去单独待一会儿怎么样？] 当然，当然。先让女儿累坏了，然后再把母亲据为己有。这策略太完美了。 嘿嘿。 清子带你回到了小屋，穿过走廊，来到了那熟悉的客厅。你摆好靠垫，而她则去泡茶、拿糖果。不久之后，你们俩便静静地坐在一起，尽情享受彼此的陪伴所带来的温暖与愉悦。照顾那个精力充沛的小雪球确实让你们都累坏了……但这也是为人父母不可避免的一部分，不是吗？ 现在，清子一边喝完茶，一边说道： [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|然后，她将双手放在逐渐隆起的腹部上，发现自己的手已经很难再把那圆鼓鼓的腹部与桌子隔开来了。|那只狐狸将那颗明显已经怀孕的肚子搁在膝盖上，放松肌肉，让自己处于最舒适的位置。|然后转过身来，对你露出温暖的微笑。] 我们开始吧？如果你和我们女儿一起玩，却忽略和我玩，我可能会吃醋的，你知道的……

rows.original: As it turns out, Kinu leads the both of you around to the little garden by the back of the cabin, treading between rows of sprouts and dark, fresh-turned earth. "Ehe. There's been something I've been wanting to show the both of you!" Well, let's see it, then. What kind of surprise does she have for you? "Give me a moment, okay?" With those words, Kinu nips off and disappears behind a nearby open-air shed, reappearing in a minute with a cloth apron tied about her waist and a nice little kerchief on her head. Practically bouncing up and down with excitement, your daughter hands both you and Kiyoko a trowel each, keeping one for herself. There's a nice outfit she's got there. "Mama says to be properly dressed when I mess with the garden, because having to wash my clothes when I come in from the forest is already enough to give her conniptions." You chuckle and turn to Kiyoko, who sniffs. "Have you ever tried to remove grass stains from wool? It's an uphill task, even with good ash soap." Ah, how precocious. So now, what does little Kinu need you to do? "I need you and Mama to help me dig up a turnip, [kinu.Dad]. I've had one in the ground for a little while now, and while I don't know how big it exactly is, I'm not quite able to pull it out by myself. So, I need some help!" Three people to pull out a turnip? Just how big is this thing supposed to be, anyway? "Well, I probably don't need both you and Mama, but I want both you and Mama to be around." Sounds a lot like work... Kinu sticks her tongue out at you. "It's not work if you have fun doing it." Haha, that sounds like something her mother would have taught her. Did she? "It's a positive attitude for anyone to take," Kiyoko says very matter-of-factly, donning a pair of thin gloves. All right, then. Let's get down to work. "Yaaaaay!" So it comes to pass that you end up on your knees by a row of turnips, carefully digging away the dirt from one particularly hefty specimen. Kiyoko instructs you on how to properly handle the trowel, while Kinu digs away like a particularly enthusiastic dog. You can tell your daughter is trying not to get dirt everywhere, especially since she's got her mother's eyes on her, but it's probably kind to say that her efforts at remaining clean leave something to be desired. This goes double when you notice that unlike her mother, she isn't wearing gloves, plus she far prefers to dig with her fingers... This is normal for her, isn't it? The vegetable gardening and all? Your fox-wife folds her arms, her expression carefully neutral. "Hmm. Back in the Old Country, flower gardening is an acceptable pastime for a young woman like her, as is bonsai. Working with mere vegetables, though, is probably going to cause some consternation if her relatives on that side of the family were to ever discover it." Well, it's a good thing she's likely to never meet them, then, what with the whole two hundred and fifty years having passed in the waking world and all. "Perhaps. Just the other day, she was pestering me to get her a rice field. I had to carefully explain to her that not only would such a thing take up far too much space, but also it would involve more work than what a single child like her was capable of. I fear that I may have just put off the problem for some years, but at least I don't have to deal with such an impossible, childish request now." She seems so enthusiastic about it, though. "If only she would display that kind of energy during her archery practice, alas. She merely puts in barely enough effort to avoid being reprimanded." The more dirt you clean off the offending vegetable, the more imposing the task reveals itself to be. What looks like a simple turnip with a few greens sticking above ground turns out to be far more than that, more and more of the root vegetable's impressive girth revealed the more the three of you dig. At length, you've uncovered an enormous white turnip, crisp to the touch, its leaves still wet with the morning dew. It's the biggest that you've ever seen, and to think so much of it was hidden under the earth. Kinu does a little excited dance. "It's humongous! Ginormous! Look, [kinu.Dad], Mama! Isn't it amazing? And so crisp, too!" You turn the massive, head-sized turnip in your hands and smile. Sheer mass aside, it doesn't have a speck of rot or blemish on it — for someone who can judge these things, it really is a work of art. Nature must really love Kinu. Kiyoko dusts off her hands, crumbs of dirt falling from her gloves. "I will admit it is something, considering the effort that went into it. I have to tell our daughter here to wash up well before coming in everyday, because she always smells of compost by the time evening comes around." "Aren't I amazing? Praise me! Praise me!" Hahaha. That sounds really familiar — like mother, like daughter, as they say. For all they try to be different on the surface, Kiyoko and Kinu really are quite similar where it counts. "Hm. I don't know..." Now, there's no need to be grumpy. It'll be but a short decade or so before her daughter wakes up one morning and realizes she's turned into her mother — exactly like her mother before her. Until then, though... Kiyoko gives you a small smile and smacks you lightly on the back of your head. "Jokes are fine in moderation, dear, but that one cut just a little too close to home." Oh no, can she ever forgive you for your indiscretions? A chuckle. "You can make it up to me when we're alone later."
rows.translation: 原来，小娟带着你们俩来到了小屋后面的小花园，她穿梭在一排排幼苗和刚刚翻过的黑土之间。 嘿嘿，有样东西我一直想给你们俩看看！ 那我们就拭目以待吧。她究竟会为你准备什么惊喜呢？ 给我一点时间，好吗？说完这些话，小娟迅速跑进了附近的一间露天棚屋，不一会儿就回来了，她腰间系着一条布围裙，头上还戴着一块漂亮的小头巾。她兴奋得几乎跳了起来，然后递给了你和清子每人一把铲子，自己也留了一把。她穿的那身衣服可真漂亮啊。 妈妈说，我在花园里玩耍的时候一定要穿得整齐些，因为等我从森林里回来后还得洗衣服，这已经足以让她大发雷霆了。 你轻笑一声，然后转向清子，而清子则抽了抽鼻子。你有没有试过去除羊毛上的草渍？即使使用质量好的灰皂，这也是一件非常困难的事情。 啊，真是早熟啊。那么，现在，小小娟需要你做些什么呢？ 我需要你和妈妈帮我去挖一个萝卜。 [kinu.Dad]我在地里埋了一个东西，已经有一段时间了。虽然我不知道它到底有多大，但我一个人实在拔不出来，所以需要一些帮助！ 三个人才能拔出一颗萝卜？这东西到底得有多大才行啊？ 嗯，其实我大概并不需要你和妈妈两个人都陪在我身边，但是想要希望你和妈妈都能一直在我身边。 听起来像是在工作…… 小娟对着你吐了吐舌头。如果做这件事的过程中你能感到乐趣，那就根本不算工作。 哈哈，这听起来像是她妈妈会教她的东西。她真的这么做过吗？ 这种积极的态度，任何人都应该采纳。清子若无其事地戴上了一副薄手套，说道：“好吧，那我们开始工作吧。 耶耶耶！ 于是，你最终跪在了一排萝卜旁边，仔细地挖开其中一颗特别大的萝卜上的泥土。清子教你如何正确使用铁锹，而小娟则像一只异常热情的狗一样拼命地挖着。你可以看出，你的女儿正在努力不让自己弄得满身都是污垢，尤其是当她妈妈一直在注视着她的时候。不过，说实话，她保持清洁的努力还是有些不够到位。尤其是当你注意到，与她的母亲不同，她并没有戴手套，而且她更喜欢用手指来挖东西。这对她来说很正常吧？种菜这些事情……你的狐狸妻子双臂交叉抱在胸前，表情刻意保持中立。嗯，在老家，像她这样的年轻女性，从事花卉园艺或盆景制作确实是一种可以接受的消遣方式。不过，如果她那边的亲戚知道了她只是在种植蔬菜，恐怕会感到非常惊讶吧。 嗯，幸好她很可能永远都不会遇到他们，毕竟在现实世界里已经过去了250年啊。 也许吧。就在前几天，她还缠着我让她弄一块稻田。我不得不仔细地向她解释，这样的东西不仅会占用太多空间，而且所需的工作量也超出了她这样一个孩子的能力范围。虽然我可能只是把这个问题暂时推迟了几年，但至少现在我不用再处理这种不切实际、幼稚的要求了。 不过，她看起来对此确实非常热情。 要是在射箭练习时她也能拿出这样的劲头来该多好啊，可惜她只是稍微花点力气，只是为了不受到责备而已。 你清理掉这种蔬菜表面的污垢越多，就会发现这项任务其实越发艰巨。原本看起来只是个长着几片叶子、埋在土里的简单萝卜，实际上远比想象中复杂得多——你们三个人挖得越深，就越能看到这种根茎类蔬菜惊人的体积。终于，你发现了一个巨大的白色萝卜，触感脆嫩，叶子上还带着晨露。这是你见过的最大的萝卜，想想看，竟然有这么多东西隐藏在地下。 纪久兴奋地跳起了小舞。它大得离谱！大得惊人！看， [kinu.Dad]妈妈！太神奇了吧？而且口感还这么脆嫩！ 你手中拿着那个巨大的、有脑袋那么大的萝卜，脸上露出了笑容。除了体积庞大之外，它上面没有一点腐烂或瑕疵——对于一个能够辨别这些细节的人来说，这确实是一件艺术品。大自然一定非常喜爱小娟。清子拍掉手上的灰尘，手套上掉下了些许泥土碎屑。我得承认，考虑到为此付出的一切努力，这个成果确实不错。我得告诉我们的女儿，每天回来之前一定要好好洗澡，因为到了晚上，她身上总是会有一股堆肥的味道。 我不是很厉害吗？快赞美我吧！赞美我！ 哈哈哈，这听起来真是太熟悉了——就像人们说的，有其母必有其女。尽管表面上她们试图表现出不同，但在关键方面，清子和小雪其实非常相似。 嗯……我也不确定…… 现在，没必要再生气了。大概再过十年左右的时间，她的女儿某个早晨醒来时会发现自己已经变成了她母亲的样子——和她母亲一模一样。不过，在那之前…… 清子对你微微一笑，然后轻轻拍了拍你的后脑勺。亲爱的，适度的玩笑没什么问题，但那个玩笑确实有点太触到痛点了。 哦不，她能原谅你的那些轻率行为吗？一阵轻笑。等我们以后单独在一起的时候，你可以补偿我。

rows.original: It doesn't take long to realize where Kinu is leading you: back to the cabin and up atop the porch. You'd imagine an active little thing like her would want to play outside, but evidently your daughter has other ideas. Stopping at the door, the little fluffball waves at you to wait on the porch, then disappears inside. "Wait here, okay? I'll go bring it out!" Bring what out, you may ask? "I have an idea," your foxy wife purrs as she lowers herself into her rocking chair. "I've never been a fan of letting kits have very many toys... much as the way I was raised myself, I far prefer to let them use their imaginations when it comes to playthings. Although..." Although? The pattering of feet on floorboards returns, and Kinu bursts back out onto the porch with something in her hands. It looks vaguely like a wooden gavel or mallet, only there's a spike at the top and a ball tied to it with string. Your firstborn fox-daughter is practically hopping on the spot, vibrating with excitement as she waves the toy about. "Ah, kendama," Kiyoko says as she rocks back and forth in the rocking chair. A small smile plays upon her lips as she [kiyoko.pregStage 3|snuggles up with her big, pregnant belly|gathers her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails in her lap] and makes herself comfortable. "Roughly translated, 'sword and ball.' Our daughter's really taken to the toy." Haha, you can see that for yourself. Kinu's delight is scrawled messily all over her face — genuine, innocent, childish joy you'll probably never see again once she grows up. "I want to show you some tricks, [kinu.Dad]!" You lean down and pet your squirmy fox-daughter between the ears. Oh, really. And where did she learn those tricks from? "Well, Mama taught me some. But I came up with most of them myself!" Oh, really. You look back up to Kiyoko, who's blushing slightly as she looks away, refusing to meet your eyes. She's always so calm and serious — you didn't think she was the kind for children's toys. "Kendama... it didn't come from my homeland, you know. One of my juniors — a peppy maiden named Komari — came up with it after watching two wolf pups play with a similar toy, carved the first piece from a fallen log. She got so excited about having a new toy to play with, she practically forgot we were supposed to be at war... to be fair, we needed some kind of distraction to take our minds off what was going on not too far from where we'd holed up. "Komari was always so excitable, just like our daughter — she insisted that I learn all the little tricks she'd come up with watching the wolf pups play with their little ball-and-cup game. So I did... we turned it into a drinking game. If you made a mistake, you took another shot of sake — I ended up under the table most nights." Hm... Kiyoko clears her throat and continues. "I don't mind our daughter playing with the kendama, really. If nothing, it's really helped her wrists and hand-eye coordination, as well as flexibility in general. It's really noticeable when put her through the forms during weapons practice." "Are you two done talking already? I wanna show you what I can do, [kinu.Dad]!" Kiyoko just chuckles. All right, all right. You crouch down so you're level with Kinu, and look her in the eye. Since she's such hot stuff, she can flaunt what she's learned. "Eeheehee! Okay, then!" For an eight year-old kit, it really is fairly impressive. Kinu's hand and wrist are a blur as she runs the gamut of a array of tricks. She starts simple, catching the wooden ball in the handle and both ends of the hammer-like head, then moves to more and more elaborate displays of manual dexterity — balancing, catching, twisting her grip mid-trick so as to allow her wrist the range of motion it needs, even going as far as to swap hands while the wooden ball's in the air. Eventually, Kinu ends up juggling the ball between both ends of the head and the handle at a rapid pace, singing a little tune in Kiyoko's mother tongue to help keep her timing. When she's done, she catches the ball in the biggest cup and lets the clack of wood hitting wood ring out over the porch. The whole affair definitely looks like one of those %"easy to pick up, incredibly difficult to master" things. Kiyoko smiles, tuts a little, and slowly claps thrice. "Decently impressive, Kinu. Why don't you let your [pc.mf|father|mother] have a try?" You? "Yeah, [kinu.Dad]! It's fine, I'll teach you!" "Look at her, she's so fired up; you don't see our daughter like that every day," Kiyoko purrs, still rocking in the chair. "You wouldn't want to disappoint little Kinu, would you? Or do you think that you can't outdo our daughter when it comes to a child's game?" Ooh, that's some nasty verbal arm-twisting she's got right there. Mother and daughter ganging up on you like that... well, it looks like you've got no choice but to acquiesce and do your best, right? "Yaaaay!" Kinu happily hands over the kendama to you, and you test the wooden toy's weight in your hand, getting a feel for it. [pc.agilityRange 50 80|It's not that bad once you get a feel for it — but for a child's toy, the kendama is surprisingly complex to handle. Kinu walks you through a number of the basics, such as juggling the ball in the air and catching it with the cup on the bigger head; it takes you a little while but you do eventually get the hang of it. When she moves on to the more complex tricks and motions, though — that's when the difficulty begins. Increasingly, you find yourself messing up more and more, with the ball slipping out of the cup, the string catching on the spike or on your wrist, your wrist shaking, or any other number of small but ultimately fatal errors that mess up your momentum. Of course, this amuses Kiyoko to no end. Even though she's trying to hide the smile behind her hand, you're pretty damn sure it's just a fig leaf and she jolly well wants you to know her mirth at you making quite the silly fool of yourself in front of your daughter. "Ehehehe. Don't worry, [kinu.Dad]," Kinu says after you fail for the last time at a particularly complex motion. Standing on tiptoe in order to reach your shoulder, she gives you a series of reassuring pats before plucking the toy from your hands. "You're actually pretty good at this. Not as good as Mama or I am, but then again you haven't had much experience with the kendama. Don't worry about it too much." Yeah, she's right. Besides, it was fun having her trying to teach you something for once, and that's what really matters here.|It may not be an extension of your body, but you do as much as you can within the moment's notice that you have. Kinu walks you through some of the basics — catching the ball in each of the three cups, spearing the ball through its hole with the pointy end — then quickly moves on to more complex tricks when you quickly and easily master the basics. "Eeheehee. I know I'm supposed to be the one who picks things up quickly, [kinu.Dad], but this is pretty good. Let's see if you can do this..." And you do. You flip, twist and turn your wrist, moving through the tricks that Kinu demonstrates first, then has you copy after careful observation. The clack-clack-clack of wood against wood sounds in the air, and before long you're flipping the cup-and-ball toy with ease, catching the ball on the side of the head and following your daughter's lead. Kinu squeals in delight and claps her hands together. "Ehe, [kinu.Dad], you're great at this!" Are you, now? One supposes that when one possesses such finesse with weapons as you do, something as simple as a child's toy is, well, child's play. You improvise a couple more tricks, much to Kinu's delight, then flip the kendama's handle in your grip and offer it back to Kinu. "Wooooow..." Heh, that wasn't so bad. At times, Kinu is really easy to impress.|If it were anything like the hammer or mallet it so resembles, the kendama would be easy for you. Of course, it's nothing like such. Kinu is ever patient, but while you manage to the first few simplest tricks she shows you down, the rest has you struggling with increasing complexity — and the more annoyed you grow with your repeated failure in front of your foxy wife and daughter, the harder it is to keep your fingers from trembling and wrist from shaking. At length, you feel eyes on the back of your neck, and turn to find Kiyoko amused to no end. Even though she's trying to hide the smile behind her hand, you're pretty damn sure it's just a fig leaf and she jolly well wants you to know her mirth at you making quite the silly fool of yourself in front of your daughter. Catching your eye, she gives you a small wink, clearly telling you that there's no point trying to save face in front of Kinu here. Even so... you have to try, if it's only for your sweet daughter's sake. And so you do, for a few more tries until Kinu gives you a sheepish smile and plucks the kendama from your hand. "It's fine, [kinu.Dad]. I just need more practice in tutoring others — it's a skill I've got to cultivate." How sweet of her to offer you a way out without disgracing yourself further. Sighing, you pet Kinu between the ears, and offer her a few empty words of encouragement. She'll get better at this, you're sure of it. Or at least, you might... ] "I know, I know! You have a go too, Mama! Everyone else already has!" Kiyoko swivels her gaze towards her daughter and chortles. "Oh, you want me to join in?" Well, it's a family affair. Besides, since your lovely fox-wife is so adorable, it only makes sense for her to be young at heart, isn't it? After all, being sprightly inside and able to see the fun in things will only reflect well upon her complexion when it shines forth from her. "Please, Mama!" "Ah, well. Since I'm being ganged up upon, I suppose I have no choice. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|I'll go ahead and make a fool of myself, being as unwieldy as I am right now.|I'll entertain the two of you with a little of what I know.]" With that, Kiyoko reaches out for the kendama with one of her tails. Kinu is quick to pass it along to her mother, and your lovely kitsune wife turns the wooden toy over in her hand, a small, wistful look in her eyes. "Oh, Komari. You must be long dead by now..." Still reclining in the rocking chair, Kiyoko gives the kendama's handle a small kiss, then sets herself into motion. Like Kinu and you beforehand, she starts with a series of simple catches with all three cups on the toy, then starts juggling the ball with skilled expertise. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|Even with her huge pregnant belly in the way|Even leaning in the rocking chair as she is], Kiyoko is considerably adroit at fiddling with the children's toy, the red wooden ball a blur as it spins and clacks away. "Eh, Mama, you're great!" "Oh my, that's the first praise I've had from you in a while. Usually it's the other way round, as it should be, but I still feel all good and warm inside. Well then, watch this." Kiyoko still doesn't move from the spot, but that's no issue when one has tails as lovely as hers. Your kitsune wife tosses the kendama into the air, and the tip of one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails curls about the handle and catches the toy perfectly. Kinu squeals and claps, and you yourself can't help but smile, too — perhaps recalling all the other things these fluffy tails are capable of... Still, you have to admit it's rather impressive how prehensile these fox tails are. Your kitsune wife passes the toy from one tail to the other, tossing it up and down in the air behind her, then eventually flips it into her left hand and twirls it with a flourish, spearing the wooden ball right through on the spike. Wow, truly impressive. "Why, thank you. Both Komari and I got completely wasted when playing against each other back in the day. Those were good times, and long, long past. A dim memory..." With that, Kiyoko pushes herself out of the rocking chair, [kiyoko.pregStage 3|a small sigh of effort escaping her lips as she steadies herself with her tails|a small sigh of contentment rising from her as she limbers her joints]. "Ah, that was fun, and I needed a sit-down. Kinu?" "Mama?" "Go and play for the rest of the day[kiyoko.numKits 2|, and tell the others to stay out of the house until dinnertime]. You don't have to return until the sun starts coming down — I have some business to attend to with your [pc.mf|father|mother]. Understood?" "Good girl." Kiyoko hands the kendama back to Kinu, then shoos your daughter off with a gentle push to the back.

你俯下身，轻轻抚摸着你那调皮的女儿耳朵后面的部位。哦，真是太有趣了。她这些把戏是从哪里学来的呢？ 嗯，妈妈教了我一些。但其中大部分都是我自己想出来的！ 哦，真的吗？你再看看清子，她正微微脸红地低下头，拒绝与你对视。她向来都是那么冷静和严肃，你肯定没想过她会喜欢儿童玩具这类东西吧。 嗯，这毕竟是一家人的事情。而且，既然你那位可爱的狐妖妻子这么惹人喜欢，她保持年轻的心态也是理所当然的，不是吗？毕竟，如果她内心充满活力，能够看到事情中的乐趣，那么这种乐观的态度肯定会让她的容颜更加光彩照人。 求你了，妈妈！ 啊，好吧。既然大家都联合起来对付我，我想我也别无选择了。 [kiyoko.pregStage 3|就我现在的这个笨手笨脚的样子，我还是去出丑吧。|我就用我所知道的一些知识来陪你们俩消遣一下吧。]" 说着，清子用她的一条尾巴拿起了那个手鼓。纪久迅速将它递给了母亲，而你那位可爱的狐妻将这个木制玩具在手中翻来覆去，眼中流露出一丝淡淡的忧伤。 哦，麻里……你现在应该早就去世了吧……基约子依然躺在摇椅上，轻轻吻了吻肯达玛的把手，然后开始行动起来。和之前小娟以及你一样，她首先用玩具上的三个杯子进行了一系列简单的接球练习，随后便以娴熟的技巧开始玩杂技般地抛接球体。 [kiyoko.pregStage 3|尽管她那巨大的孕妇肚子挡住了去路……|即使她当时正倚坐在摇椅上。]清子玩弄那些儿童玩具时显得相当熟练，那个红色的木球在旋转时会发出咔嗒咔嗒的声音，看起来快要把视线弄模糊了。 哎，妈妈，你太棒了！ 哦，天哪，这是我很久以来第一次收到你的表扬。通常情况下应该是反过来才对，但即便如此，我内心还是感到非常温暖和愉悦。那么，接下来请看这个吧。 清子依然站在原地一动不动，但拥有像她这样漂亮的尾巴，这根本不是问题。你的九尾妻子将那个剑玉抛向空中，她的其中一根尾巴的尖端 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 尾巴在把手上盘绕着，将玩具牢牢地固定住。小娟发出欢快的叫声，还不停地拍手庆祝，而你自己也会不由得露出微笑——或许会回想起那些美好的时光其他这些毛茸茸的尾巴到底能做出什么事情来…… 不过，你不得不承认，这些狐妖尾巴的抓握能力确实相当惊人。你的九尾狐妻子把玩具从一根尾巴换到另一根尾巴上，在身后把玩具抛来抛去，最后终于把它抓到左手中，熟练地旋转着它，让木球准确地穿过了那根带刺的尾巴。 哇，真的太厉害了。 哦，谢谢。当年我和麻里互相对战的时候，确实都玩得非常尽兴。那些真是美好的时光，不过已经过去很久很久了，现在只剩下些模糊的记忆罢了…… 说完这句话，清子从摇椅中站了起来。 [kiyoko.pregStage 3|她用力调整身体平衡，尾巴也在此过程中微微一颤，发出一声轻微的叹息。|她活动着关节，心中涌出一丝满足的叹息。]. 啊，真是太有趣了，我现在需要坐下来休息一下。小娟，你觉得呢？ 妈妈？ 去玩吧，剩下的时间都用来玩吧。[kiyoko.numKits 2|并且告诉其他人，在晚餐时间之前都不要进屋。]你不必等到太阳开始下山才回来——我还有些事情需要和你处理。 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]明白了吗？ 好姑娘。清子将肯达玛递还给小娟，然后轻轻推了推你的女儿，让她走开。
rows.raw: " It doesn't take long to realize where Kinu is leading you: back to the cabin and up atop the porch. You'd imagine an active little thing like her would want to play outside, but evidently your daughter has other ideas. Stopping at the door, the little fluffball waves at you to wait on the porch, then disappears inside. "Wait here, okay? I'll go bring it out!" Bring what out, you may ask? "I have an idea," your foxy wife purrs as she lowers herself into her rocking chair. "I've never been a fan of letting kits have very many toys... much as the way I was raised myself, I far prefer to let them use their imaginations when it comes to playthings. Although..." Although? The pattering of feet on floorboards returns, and Kinu bursts back out onto the porch with something in her hands. It looks vaguely like a wooden gavel or mallet, only there's a spike at the top and a ball tied to it with string. Your firstborn fox-daughter is practically hopping on the spot, vibrating with excitement as she waves the toy about. "Ah, kendama," Kiyoko says as she rocks back and forth in the rocking chair. A small smile plays upon her lips as she [kiyoko.pregStage 3|snuggles up with her big, pregnant belly|gathers her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails in her lap] and makes herself comfortable. "Roughly translated, 'sword and ball.' Our daughter's really taken to the toy." Haha, you can see that for yourself. Kinu's delight is scrawled messily all over her face — genuine, innocent, childish joy you'll probably never see again once she grows up. "I want to show you some tricks, [kinu.Dad]!" You lean down and pet your squirmy fox-daughter between the ears. Oh, really. And where did she learn those tricks from? "Well, Mama taught me some. But I came up with most of them myself!" Oh, really. You look back up to Kiyoko, who's blushing slightly as she looks away, refusing to meet your eyes. She's always so calm and serious — you didn't think she was the kind for children's toys. "Kendama... it didn't come from my homeland, you know. One of my juniors — a peppy maiden named Komari — came up with it after watching two wolf pups play with a similar toy, carved the first piece from a fallen log. She got so excited about having a new toy to play with, she practically forgot we were supposed to be at war... to be fair, we needed some kind of distraction to take our minds off what was going on not too far from where we'd holed up. "Komari was always so excitable, just like our daughter — she insisted that I learn all the little tricks she'd come up with watching the wolf pups play with their little ball-and-cup game. So I did... we turned it into a drinking game. If you made a mistake, you took another shot of sake — I ended up under the table most nights." Hm... Kiyoko clears her throat and continues. "I don't mind our daughter playing with the kendama, really. If nothing, it's really helped her wrists and hand-eye coordination, as well as flexibility in general. It's really noticeable when put her through the forms during weapons practice." "Are you two done talking already? I wanna show you what I can do, [kinu.Dad]!" Kiyoko just chuckles. All right, all right. You crouch down so you're level with Kinu, and look her in the eye. Since she's such hot stuff, she can flaunt what she's learned. "Eeheehee! Okay, then!" For an eight year-old kit, it really is fairly impressive. Kinu's hand and wrist are a blur as she runs the gamut of a array of tricks. She starts simple, catching the wooden ball in the handle and both ends of the hammer-like head, then moves to more and more elaborate displays of manual dexterity — balancing, catching, twisting her grip mid-trick so as to allow her wrist the range of motion it needs, even going as far as to swap hands while the wooden ball's in the air. Eventually, Kinu ends up juggling the ball between both ends of the head and the handle at a rapid pace, singing a little tune in Kiyoko's mother tongue to help keep her timing. When she's done, she catches the ball in the biggest cup and lets the clack of wood hitting wood ring out over the porch. The whole affair definitely looks like one of those %"easy to pick up, incredibly difficult to master" things. Kiyoko smiles, tuts a little, and slowly claps thrice. "Decently impressive, Kinu. Why don't you let your [pc.mf|father|mother] have a try?" You? "Yeah, [kinu.Dad]! It's fine, I'll teach you!" "Look at her, she's so fired up; you don't see our daughter like that every day," Kiyoko purrs, still rocking in the chair. "You wouldn't want to disappoint little Kinu, would you? Or do you think that you can't outdo our daughter when it comes to a child's game?" Ooh, that's some nasty verbal arm-twisting she's got right there. Mother and daughter ganging up on you like that... well, it looks like you've got no choice but to acquiesce and do your best, right? "Yaaaay!" Kinu happily hands over the kendama to you, and you test the wooden toy's weight in your hand, getting a feel for it. [pc.agilityRange 50 80|It's not that bad once you get a feel for it — but for a child's toy, the kendama is surprisingly complex to handle. Kinu walks you through a number of the basics, such as juggling the ball in the air and catching it with the cup on the bigger head; it takes you a little while but you do eventually get the hang of it. When she moves on to the more complex tricks and motions, though — that's when the difficulty begins. Increasingly, you find yourself messing up more and more, with the ball slipping out of the cup, the string catching on the spike or on your wrist, your wrist shaking, or any other number of small but ultimately fatal errors that mess up your momentum. Of course, this amuses Kiyoko to no end. Even though she's trying to hide the smile behind her hand, you're pretty damn sure it's just a fig leaf and she jolly well wants you to know her mirth at you making quite the silly fool of yourself in front of your daughter. "Ehehehe. Don't worry, [kinu.Dad]," Kinu says after you fail for the last time at a particularly complex motion. Standing on tiptoe in order to reach your shoulder, she gives you a series of reassuring pats before plucking the toy from your hands. "You're actually pretty good at this. Not as good as Mama or I am, but then again you haven't had much experience with the kendama. Don't worry about it too much." Yeah, she's right. Besides, it was fun having her trying to teach you something for once, and that's what really matters here.|It may not be an extension of your body, but you do as much as you can within the moment's notice that you have. Kinu walks you through some of the basics — catching the ball in each of the three cups, spearing the ball through its hole with the pointy end — then quickly moves on to more complex tricks when you quickly and easily master the basics. "Eeheehee. I know I'm supposed to be the one who picks things up quickly, [kinu.Dad], but this is pretty good. Let's see if you can do this..." And you do. You flip, twist and turn your wrist, moving through the tricks that Kinu demonstrates first, then has you copy after careful observation. The clack-clack-clack of wood against wood sounds in the air, and before long you're flipping the cup-and-ball toy with ease, catching the ball on the side of the head and following your daughter's lead. Kinu squeals in delight and claps her hands together. "Ehe, [kinu.Dad], you're great at this!" Are you, now? One supposes that when one possesses such finesse with weapons as you do, something as simple as a child's toy is, well, child's play. You improvise a couple more tricks, much to Kinu's delight, then flip the kendama's handle in your grip and offer it back to Kinu. "Wooooow..." Heh, that wasn't so bad. At times, Kinu is really easy to impress.|If it were anything like the hammer or mallet it so resembles, the kendama would be easy for you. Of course, it's nothing like such. Kinu is ever patient, but while you manage to the first few simplest tricks she shows you down, the rest has you struggling with increasing complexity — and the more annoyed you grow with your repeated failure in front of your foxy wife and daughter, the harder it is to keep your fingers from trembling and wrist from shaking. At length, you feel eyes on the back of your neck, and turn to find Kiyoko amused to no end. Even though she's trying to hide the smile behind her hand, you're pretty damn sure it's just a fig leaf and she jolly well wants you to know her mirth at you making quite the silly fool of yourself in front of your daughter. Catching your eye, she gives you a small wink, clearly telling you that there's no point trying to save face in front of Kinu here. Even so... you have to try, if it's only for your sweet daughter's sake. And so you do, for a few more tries until Kinu gives you a sheepish smile and plucks the kendama from your hand. "It's fine, [kinu.Dad]. I just need more practice in tutoring others — it's a skill I've got to cultivate." How sweet of her to offer you a way out without disgracing yourself further. Sighing, you pet Kinu between the ears, and offer her a few empty words of encouragement. She'll get better at this, you're sure of it. Or at least, you might... ] "I know, I know! You have a go too, Mama! Everyone else already has!" Kiyoko swivels her gaze towards her daughter and chortles. "Oh, you want me to join in?" Well, it's a family affair. Besides, since your lovely fox-wife is so adorable, it only makes sense for her to be young at heart, isn't it? After all, being sprightly inside and able to see the fun in things will only reflect well upon her complexion when it shines forth from her. "Please, Mama!" "Ah, well. Since I'm being ganged up upon, I suppose I have no choice. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|I'll go ahead and make a fool of myself, being as unwieldy as I am right now.|I'll entertain the two of you with a little of what I know.]" With that, Kiyoko reaches out for the kendama with one of her tails. Kinu is quick to pass it along to her mother, and your lovely kitsune wife turns the wooden toy over in her hand, a small, wistful look in her eyes. "Oh, Komari. You must be long dead by now..." Still reclining in the rocking chair, Kiyoko gives the kendama's handle a small kiss, then sets herself into motion. Like Kinu and you beforehand, she starts with a series of simple catches with all three cups on the toy, then starts juggling the ball with skilled expertise. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|Even with her huge pregnant belly in the way|Even leaning in the rocking chair as she is], Kiyoko is considerably adroit at fiddling with the children's toy, the red wooden ball a blur as it spins and clacks away. "Eh, Mama, you're great!" "Oh my, that's the first praise I've had from you in a while. Usually it's the other way round, as it should be, but I still feel all good and warm inside. Well then, watch this." Kiyoko still doesn't move from the spot, but that's no issue when one has tails as lovely as hers. Your kitsune wife tosses the kendama into the air, and the tip of one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails curls about the handle and catches the toy perfectly. Kinu squeals and claps, and you yourself can't help but smile, too — perhaps recalling all the other things these fluffy tails are capable of... Still, you have to admit it's rather impressive how prehensile these fox tails are. Your kitsune wife passes the toy from one tail to the other, tossing it up and down in the air behind her, then eventually flips it into her left hand and twirls it with a flourish, spearing the wooden ball right through on the spike. Wow, truly impressive. "Why, thank you. Both Komari and I got completely wasted when playing against each other back in the day. Those were good times, and long, long past. A dim memory..." With that, Kiyoko pushes herself out of the rocking chair, [kiyoko.pregStage 3|a small sigh of effort escaping her lips as she steadies herself with her tails|a small sigh of contentment rising from her as she limbers her joints]. "Ah, that was fun, and I needed a sit-down. Kinu?" "Mama?" "Go and play for the rest of the day[kiyoko.numKits 2|, and tell the others to stay out of the house until dinnertime]. You don't have to return until the sun starts coming down — I have some business to attend to with your [pc.mf|father|mother]. Understood?" "Good girl." Kiyoko hands the kendama back to Kinu, then shoos your daughter off with a gentle push to the back."

rows.original: As it so happens, your daughter leads you back to the cabin, clambering up to the porch with the both of you on her heels. Throwing open the front door, she peeks inside, then darts in. "Wait here, okay?" "Kinu! Make sure your feet are clean! You're the one who's going to have to polish the floor later, you know!" "Okay!" comes Kinu's fading reply. Shaking her head and tutting, Kiyoko leans against you and wraps one of her tails about your leg, pressing the warmth of her body against you through her silken garments.[kiyoko.pregStage 3| Your lovely fox-wife snuggles the warm weight of her big pregnant belly against your side, bringing back memories of where Kinu came from to begin with.] "Ah, children." She's a handful? "She is indeed a handful." And as things turn out, Kinu returns with a handful of her own, a handful of small beanbags to be precise — five in total. Brightly colored and of the same make as Kiyoko and Kinu's clothes, the tightly sewn things gleam slightly in the warm sunlight as they sit in your daughter's cupped hands, the little floof herself looking up hopefully at the both of you. "Can we play otedama, Mama?" "Um, well." Kiyoko clears her throat. Is something the matter? Did Kinu make yet another breach of the convoluted web of kitsune etiquette? Kiyoko blushes, the bridge of her nose coloring as your foxy wife looks down and away. "No, nothing like that. I'm merely a little too old for otedama..." "And yet you taught me how to sew the beanbags and play the game, Mama." "Well... you're still young, my daughter. It fits you more... that, and the songs I taught you were passed down to me by my grandmother. Traditionally, you'd be taught all this by your own grandmother... but since you don't have one around, I filled in for her. It wouldn't do if you didn't learn them as the next den mother in line." "...That's still years off, though..." Kiyoko pets Kinu's ears, eliciting a happy squeal from your daughter. "All the better for you to learn everything I have to teach, then. Even with your talents, it'll take a long time." That's beyond the point, though. Here and now, you'd love it if she played a silly children's game with your daughter, no matter how juvenile it's supposed to be. A gentle sigh of mock exasperation. "But for now... I suppose I can play with the two of you." "Yaaaaay!" "Come along now, the both of you. Let's get started." Kiyoko dusts off one side of the porch by the rocking chair, then settles down on her knees[kiyoko.pregStage 3|, resting her full dome of her pregnancy in her lap]. Kinu settles in beside her mother, spilling the beanbags to the ground before her, leaving a conveniently empty spot in the circle for you to fill. It's a little awkward to sit on your knees like Kiyoko and Kinu are doing instead of on the floor like you're used to, but as the saying goes, when in Khor'minos... So, how is this played, anyway? "Watch closely, [kinu.Dad]. I'll show you!" With that, Kinu begins, bursting into a cheery children's song in her mother tongue. You don't know the words, but Kinu's definitely inherited her mother's voice... and her mother can make anything sound beautiful, let alone a language like this. With the upbeat simplicity of it all, you can't help but break into a smile as Kinu flips the beanbags up into the air one by one, catching each before it falls to the floorboards. When she reaches five, she lets them all fall to the floor, whereupon the process repeats itself. Ah, a simple children's juggling game, then. As the game progresses, the tune picks up pace, with Kinu's hands moving ever faster and faster in time with her singing — until she misses a catch, and the little beanbags come tumbling out of her hands. Your fox-daughter grins, rubs the side of her head, and sticks out her tongue at the both of you. "I messed up..." Oh, there's no need to be that serious. It's just a game, after all. "Still, when I wanted to impress [kinu.Dad] and Mama..." "Well then. I suppose it's my turn." Bending forward[kiyoko.pregStage 3| over her baby bump], your fox-wife scoops the beanbags towards her and picks one up to study it. "This brings back memories..." It's not often that you see her melancholy like this. "Just a moment's remembrance for times gone by." Kiyoko smiles a small, thin-lipped smile, and then starts the game, her beautiful, flute-like voice breaking into lively song as she starts tossing the beanbags into the air and catching them. It's not long before Kinu joins in the singing alongside her mother, and as the pace of game and melody alike pick up you can't help but start clapping along, too. Your fox-wife lasts a good while longer than your daughter does, her hands moving with easy alacrity as she tosses and catches the beanbags, her fingers a blur. After about eight rounds of this, though, she simply can't keep up with the music and fumbles, beanbags scattering all over the floor; bosom heaving from the exhilaration of it all, Kiyoko settles back and pushes the beanbags towards you. "Your turn, [pc.name]. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|That took a lot out of me... expectant mothers aren't supposed to move this quickly, ehehe.|I'm all tired out, but then again, this is a game for young girls...]" You look between your fox-wife and daughter, and the big smiles on their faces. Yep, there's no way you're squirming out of this one. "Come on, [kinu.Dad], give it a go!" It's rather embarrassing, since you don't know the language... "Oh, is that all?" Kiyoko snuggles up to you, chuckling. "We'll sing for you, if that's what you want." Well... "Well, [kinu.Dad]?" Well, you wouldn't mind. Far from it being you to deny your daughter when she asks so politely. "Ehehehe. Okay!" As one, mother and daughter break into song, the upbeat, lively music ringing in the porch as you start juggling the little beanbags in time with it. Sure, you may not know a word of the language, but the tune is enough to make your fingers feel light and set your heart skipping — there's a certain peace to the world like this, just tossing and catching little beanbags in front of your foxy family while they sing and clap along. [pc.agilityRange 40 80 |Strangely enough — or perhaps not — it's fun. The motions of juggling the brightly colored silk beanbags in the air is repetitive enough that you can really bask in this soothing atmosphere; mother and daughter make a great duet when they actually try to work together. [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0|If only they were comfortable with doing it more; their voices are truly heavenly. Truth be told, you ought to be honored; it's not that often that mother and daughter work together spontaneously like this — and all for you.|You'd ask them to sing for you more, especially in this native language of theirs, but requesting it specifically would... well, it wouldn't feel like it came from the heart, would it?] They're not picking up the pace of the tune as quickly as they ought to, you can tell. You may not be as familiar with this odetama game as they are, but that much is obvious to you; they want to drag it out as much as you do. It's both flattering and heartwarming at the same time. Up and down, up and down; each time all five beanbags find their way into your hand, you roll them out onto the floor again, and the game begins anew at a faster tempo. The movements of the silken beanbags through the air are strangely slow, the singing about you strangely hypnotic. You aren't the clumsiest of people around, but even so you're not wholly sure you expected to last this long in this little game. There always comes a moment, though, when the flesh fails the spirit, and that moment is now. You throw a beanbag up, it falls down, and you see the entire motion in painful detail as the silk slips off your fingers and falls to the floorboards with a very final hiss of dry beans. The three of you stare down at the beanbag for what can't be more than a moment or two, but achingly feels like forever; then, both your foxy wife and daughter are upon you. Giggling all the while, they swat at you with their fluffy tails good-naturedly, teasing you at Kinu gathers up the fallen beanbags. "That wasn't so bad, [kinu.Dad]. You might not be as good as Mama is, but I could see you putting in the effort and taking it seriously, and that's what matters here, right?" Hah, when it comes to your cute little daughter, you'll take even play seriously. Kiyoko just chuckles. "Oh, if you would only be as serious with some other things." |After the first few rounds of juggling the beagbags one by one, the game starts to pick up in earnest. You're pretty sure that your foxy family is turning up the rhythm of their song faster than they were doing for each other, but you can't help but smile at that. Let them play at their shenanigans all they want — you'll simply outpace them with sheer skill and determination. Kinu is the first one to give in, wheezing and panting as her little voice simply can't keep up with the fast-paced tempo. Your daughter doubles over, patting her little chest as she grins sheepishly, ears folded down against her head. "Wow, [kinu.Dad]..." Kiyoko lasts three more rounds of this, and despite you giving everything you have, you're starting to feel a little hard-pressed yourself, too. As it so happens, you and your fox-wife flub your tasks at the exact same moment, you with your fingers and she with her tongue. The little beanbags fall to the floorboards as Kiyoko's melody stumbles, and for a moment silence reigns on the porch as the both of you trade mischievous glances. Looks like it's a draw, if you were ever competing to begin with. "Well," Kiyoko says as she catches her breath, her [kiyoko.numKits 16|ample|pert] bosom heaving, "at least I know where our daughter's propensity to run all over the place comes from, and it's not from my side of the family." "Eeheehee." Kinu squirms on the spot and blushes, little rosy patches fading into existence on her cheeks. "That was amazing, [kinu.Dad]! I didn't think you would be so great at odetama!" Wasn't it? These hands of yours have to fight monsters and get you out of all kinds of trouble, so it's only natural that they're great at doing what they do. See, she can discover that for herself... reaching out, you pinch your fox-daughter's cheeks lightly. They're so soft and squishy, and Kinu giggles and squeals when you tease her, her three silky tails wagging back and forth in a blur. Kiyoko just laughs behind a hand. "Oh my. If you get her worked up like this, dear, I'll have so much trouble settling her down to sleep tonight. |Sure, you're not the best at this, but you give it your all for the sake of your foxy family. Eyes trained on the thumb-length beanbags, you start tossing and catching them, perhaps moving a little more stiffly than what you'd have liked to. Kiyoko and Kinu keep time with their singing and clapping as you throw and catch, throw and catch; every time you have all five beanbags in hand, you loose them back upon the floorboards, and the game repeats itself at a faster pace. To your surprise, you last longer than you'd expected to. Maybe it's the joyous faces of your fox-wife and daughter staring intently at you, maybe it's their beautiful singing, maybe it's the fact that your body feels lighter than the poor, normally clumsy thing has any right to be. Whatever's the case, you really want to do right by Kinu, and put in every iota of furious concentration you have into this children's game, trying desperately not to fumble your movements. It's on the fifth or sixth iteration that you finally slip up and make a mistake — the beanbags are small, and you were pretty tired before heading to bed, and you really need to stop making excuses for yourself. Whatever the case, the next thing you know there's silk sliding off your fingers, and both your fox-wife and child are giggling and giving you affectionate pats. "There, there," Kiyoko says, running fingertips across your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. "It's all right. You lasted longer than I did when I was a girl learning the game at my grandmother's knees." You chuckle and shake your head. Oh, that's a high bar to clear all right. "You really tried, [kinu.Dad]," Kinu adds. "I could see it." Oh, really? Kinu sticks out her tongue teasingly. "When you [kiyoko.numKits 4|have as many little siblings as I do|get a good eye for it], it's not that hard to tell. Figuring out when someone's not really trying isn't that hard, [kinu.Dad]" "It takes one to know one." Kiyoko chuckles and pats Kinu between the ears as your little three-tailed daughter pouts. "Jokes aside, that was entertaining. I haven't felt such genuine levity in a while now." "You should smile more, Mama," Kinu pipes up. "It'll be good for your beauty." "So young, and you're already learning how to flatter. Oh, what am I to do with you? ] "All right, then, young lady. Put back your toys, and you can have the rest of the day off outside. Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I would love to have some time alone to ourselves.[kiyoko.numKits 4| Tell your siblings that we're occupied, and not to be disturbed unless it's an absolute emergency.]" For a split second, Kinu looks as mischievous and calculating as can be, but that expression's quickly hidden by one of quiet deference as Kinu picks up the beanbags in both hands and scoot off back indoors.
rows.translation: 巧的是，你的女儿带着你们回到了小屋，她爬上门廊，你们跟在她的后面。她猛地推开门，往里面瞥了一眼，然后迅速跑了进去。 在这里等着，好吗？ 小娟！一定要把你的足部擦干净！以后可是要由你来擦地板的，知道吗？ 好的！小娟微弱的回应传了过来。 基代子摇着头，发出“啧”的一声，然后靠在你身上，将她的一条尾巴缠在你的腿上，透过她那丝滑的衣物，将她身体的温暖传递给你。[kiyoko.pregStage 3| 你那可爱的狐狸妻子将她那圆滚滚的、充满孕意的肚子紧贴在你的身侧，这一幕让人不禁回想起小娟的起源之地。] 啊，孩子们。 她真是个难对付的人？ 她确实是个难对付的人。 结果，小娟带回了几个这样的小东西，确切地说，是五个颜色鲜艳的小豆袋。这些豆袋与清子和小娟的衣服采用同样的材质制成，缝线非常结实。当它们被放在你女儿的掌心中时，在温暖的阳光下会微微闪烁着光芒，而那个小小的毛茸茸的生物也会满怀期待地抬头看着你们俩。 妈妈，我们能玩抓人游戏吗？ 嗯，好吧。清子清了清嗓子。 “是不是出了什么问题？难道小娟又违反了那些复杂的狐族礼仪规范吗？” 清子的脸颊顿时泛起了红晕，她低下头，将视线移开了。不，并非那样。只是我年纪有点大了，已经不适合玩‘おてだま’游戏了…… 可是妈妈，是你教会了我如何缝制这些豆袋，以及如何玩这个游戏的。 嗯……你还年轻，我的女儿。这些更适合你……而且那些歌曲也是我祖母传给我的。按照传统，这些都应该由你自己的祖母来教你……但既然你没有祖母在身边，我就来代替她吧。如果你不能作为下一任族长的女儿来学习这些，那可不行。 不过，那还是需要好几年的时间才行…… 清子轻轻抚摸着纪子的耳朵，这让你的女儿开心地发出了吱吱的叫声。那样的话，你学会我所有要教你的东西反而会更好。即便你有这样的天赋，也需要花费很长时间才能掌握。 不过，这已经超出了讨论的范围了。此刻，你肯定希望她能和你的女儿一起玩一些幼稚的儿童游戏，无论这些游戏看起来有多简单、多适合小孩子玩。 轻轻地叹了口气，假装显得有些无奈。不过目前来说……我想我可以和你们两个一起玩。 耶耶耶！ 快点吧，你们两个。我们开始吧。 清子将摇椅旁的门廊打扫干净，然后跪了下来。[kiyoko.pregStage 3|将她整个隆起的孕肚放在腿上休息]小娟坐在她母亲旁边，把豆袋子散落在她面前，这样圆圈里就留出了一个空位，让你可以坐上去。像清子和小小娟那样跪着坐，确实有点不太习惯，因为你们平时都是坐在地板上的……但俗话说，人在异乡…… 那么，这个游戏到底是怎么玩的呢？ 仔细看好了， [kinu.Dad]我这就给你看！ 就这样，小娟开始用她母亲的母语唱起了一首欢快的儿童歌曲。你可能听不懂那些歌词，但小娟无疑继承了她母亲的声音……而她母亲的声音，确实非常动听。任何东西听起来太美妙了，更何况这是一种如此优美的语言。它的简洁明快让人不禁会露出微笑——当小娟一个接一个地将豆袋抛向空中，然后在它们落回地板之前接住它们时，这种感觉更是如此。当她五岁的时候，她会让那些小物件全部掉到地上，然后这个过程就会重新开始。 啊，原来这只是一个简单的儿童杂耍游戏罢了。 随着游戏的进行，节奏会逐渐加快，小娟的手也会随着她的歌声变得越来越快——直到她有一次没能接住那些小物件，它们就会从她手中掉出来，四处滚落。你的狐妖女儿咧嘴一笑，揉了揉自己的脑袋，然后对着你们俩吐了吐舌头。 我搞砸了…… 哦，没必要那么严肃吧。毕竟这只是一场游戏而已。 不过，每当我想要给人留下深刻印象的时候 [kinu.Dad] 还有妈妈…… 那么，我想现在该轮到我了。弯下腰来[kiyoko.pregStage 3| 凸出的腹部]你的狐妖妻子把那些豆袋子捡起来，拿了一个仔细端详起来。这让人回忆起许多往事…… 你很少见到她如此忧郁。 只是为了纪念那些已经逝去的时光。清子微微一笑，嘴角带着一丝淡淡的笑意，然后开始玩游戏。她那优美如笛声般的嗓音随着将豆袋抛向空中又接住它们的动作而变得活泼动听起来。不久之后，小娟也加入了母亲的行列，一起唱起歌来。随着游戏节奏和旋律的加快，你也不由自主地开始跟着拍手起来。 你的狐妖妻子比你的女儿坚持得久多了——她灵活地抛接着豆袋，手指动作快得让人看不清。然而，经过大约八轮这样的游戏后，她终究跟不上节奏，动作变得笨拙起来，豆袋纷纷散落在地上。基约子兴奋得胸口剧烈起伏，随后她把那些豆袋推到了你的面前。 轮到你了， [pc.name]. [kiyoko.pregStage 3|那真的让我累坏了……孕妇本来就不应该这么快就做这些动作的，嘿嘿。|我累坏了，不过话说回来，这也挺正常的吧是一款专为年轻女孩设计的游戏……]" 你看着自己的狐妖妻子和女儿，她们脸上洋溢着灿烂的笑容。没错，这次你绝对无法逃避这个责任了。 来吧， [kinu.Dad]试试看吧！ 这确实有点尴尬，因为你并不懂这种语言…… 哦，就这些吗？清子依偎在你身边，轻声笑着。如果你们愿意，我们可以为你们唱歌。 嗯…… 嗯， [kinu.Dad]?" 嗯，你肯定不会介意的。女儿这么礼貌地提出请求，你当然不会拒绝她。 嘿嘿嘿，好的！ 母女俩一起唱起歌来，欢快明亮的旋律在门廊里回荡，而你也开始跟着节奏抛接那些小豆袋。当然，你可能完全不懂这种语言，但这段旋律足以让你手指变得灵活，让心跳加速——在这样的时刻，世界仿佛变得格外宁静，只需和你的家人一起唱歌、拍手，一边抛接那些小豆袋罢了。 [pc.agilityRange 40 80 小娟是第一个放弃的人，她喘着粗气，因为她的细小声音根本跟不上这种快节奏。你的女儿弯下腰，双手轻拍着自己的小胸脯，害羞地笑着，耳朵也紧紧贴在脑袋上。 哇， [kinu.Dad]..." 清子又坚持进行了三轮这样的游戏，而尽管你已经竭尽全力，自己也开始感到有些吃力了。巧合的是，你和你的狐妖妻子在同一时刻都搞砸了各自的任务——你是用手指，而她则是用舌头。当清子的旋律出现些许失误时，那些小豆袋纷纷掉落在地板上。刹那间，门廊里陷入一片寂静，而你们两人则互相交换着调皮的眼神。 看来如果真要比赛的话，结果应该是平局吧。 嗯，清子一边喘着气一边说道 [kiyoko.numKits 16|充足的|挺翘的] 心潮澎湃，至少我知道我们女儿喜欢到处乱跑的这个习惯是从哪里来的，而这并不是我这一家遗传下来的。 嘻嘻嘻。小娟在原地扭来扭去，脸上渐渐泛起了红晕，那些小小的粉红色斑点也渐渐消失了。太棒了， [kinu.Dad]我真没想到你居然这么擅长玩“Odetama”这个游戏！ 不是吗？你的双手就是用来与怪物战斗、帮你摆脱各种麻烦的，所以它们擅长这些事情也是理所当然的。看，她自己就能发现这一点……你伸出手，轻轻捏了捏女儿狐妖的脸颊，它们柔软得让人忍不住想继续逗弄。当你逗她的时候，小娟会咯咯笑着尖叫，她那三条丝滑的尾巴也会快速地来回摆动。 而清子则只是用手遮住嘴，轻声笑了起来。哦，天哪。亲爱的，如果你把她弄得这么兴奋，今晚我可就没法让她安静下来睡觉了。 |当然，你在这方面可能不是最出色的，但为了你的那些可爱的家人，你已经付出了全部的努力。你的目光紧紧盯着那些有拇指那么大的豆袋，开始尝试抛接它们，不过动作可能有些生硬，不如你期望的那么流畅。当你一次又一次地抛接豆袋时，清子和小娟会通过唱歌和拍手来为节奏伴奏；每当你手中握住全部五个豆袋时，你就需要把它们重新扔回到地板上，于是游戏会以更快的节奏重新开始。 令你惊讶的是，你的坚持时间比预想的要长。也许是因为你的狐妖妻子和女儿那充满喜悦的面孔正紧紧地注视着你，也许是因为她们美妙的歌声，又或许是因为你的身体感觉比平时轻了许多——这个原本笨拙不堪的身体，此刻竟仿佛拥有了不寻常的力量。无论发生什么，你都真心想把这件事做好，把所有精力都投入到这个儿童游戏中，竭力避免犯任何错误。
