哎哟，真是太精彩了。当你女儿的演奏达到高潮时，你的注意力又重新被小娟吸引了过来——房间里回荡着美妙的音乐，那种旋律仿佛渗透进了你的骨髓。小娟全神贯注地演奏着，她那大大的狐狸耳朵竖得高高的，手指在琴弦上飞快地移动，那种专注与投入令人印象深刻。太厉害了，她竟然没有漏掉一个音符…… [ pc.bg minstrel |你可能会认为，这些也是小娟从你那里得到的，但这么说未免有点自吹自擂了。其实你并不是什么了不起的吟游诗人然而 |或者也许她确实这么做了，但就算她真的这么做了，你也根本无从察觉。 ]终于，音乐声渐渐消失了，小娟不确定地抬头看着你们俩。这个可怜的小家伙显然在寻求你们的认可；你们微笑着走上前，轻抚着她耳边的毛发。她做得很好——你们那个毛茸茸的小女儿一直在努力保持镇定和优雅，但当你们抚摸她的耳朵时，她脸颊上浮现的红晕还是显而易见的。 谢谢， [kinu.Dad]我、我这就走了。 你还来不及抗议，小堇就已经把她的乐器夹在胳膊下，迅速跑掉了。清子只是笑了笑，继续喝着茶，双臂交叉抱在胸前。[kiyoko.pregStage 1| 因为怀孕而腹部隆起]. 哦天，看来你让她感到难堪了。我记得自己第一次在不是我妈妈的人面前表演时，也有同样的感觉。别担心，这种感觉会过去的。她示意你回到桌子旁坐下。那场面还挺有趣的，不是吗？ 确实如此。对于小娟来说，能够组织出这样的表演…… 一个微笑。就像我之前说的， [pc.name]她真的非常渴望得到你的认可。不过，先不说这个了，今天是个美好的日子，我们为什么不一起享受一些时光呢？ ]
rows.raw: " Knocking on the door, you're greeted by Kiyoko as usual. Your foxy wife is looking rather pleased with herself today, [kiyoko.pregStage 1|even more than the usual cheery demeanour that tends to accompany her when she's with child|but it's not the kind of sly smile that precedes events getting... uh, intense]. Rather, it's the kind of eager grin that bodes childish excitement, the kind that only looks good on someone as foxy as she is. "There you are, [pc.name]. I'd a feeling you'd turn up today; our firstborn daughter was quite excited at the prospect of your visit. She's been bouncing off the walls since yesterday." Not literally bouncing, you hope. A dry laugh. "I don't know about that, especially after she's gotten too much sweet fruit in her. But no, our daughter's just been rather enthusiastic about showing you what she's learned of late." You nod, close the door behind you, and follow Kiyoko into the cabin down familiar hallways. Oh? Why you? "Well, [pc.name]... call it a hunch, but I think Kinu looks up to you. She wants your approval more than she does mine — I'll admit I'm kind of jealous." And you'll admit you're somewhat flattered. One can only wonder why, though. "My guess is that you come by so infrequently that praise from you is a rare thing to behold," Kiyoko replies with a small sigh. "While I merely do the job of feeding and clothing our daughter, not to mention the small task of raising her to be a decent and useful person. You know, things that cause her to grow overfamiliar with me." Ha. As Kiyoko pushes aside the screen door to the sitting room, you're greeted by the sight of [ kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |Kinu sitting cross-legged on a cushion in a corner, right next to the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. She's got what looks like a long, thick flute nestled in both her hands like a prized possession, and stands to give the both of you a bow as you enter. "[kinu.Dad], Mama. Umm..." Kinu hesitates, your daughter's face coloring a little, then she puffs herself up as best as a petite eight year-old can, gathering confidence in the face of stage fright. "I'll be playing Call of the Swan for the both of you today. I hope you enjoy what I have to offer." "Hmph." Kiyoko tosses her head — she doesn't actually sniff derisively, but she conceivably could have any moment. "Come and sit at the table, [pc.name]. I'll serve us some tea while our daughter entertains us." While Kiyoko's back is turned getting the tea set, Kinu gives you a pleading look, her ice-blue eyes all big and wide. You... you're not exactly sure what's expected of you here. The best you manage is an encouraging nod, which appears to be enough; your daughter turns back to her preparations just as her mother saunters over and plonks the tea set down on the low table, serving up cups of bitter draught for you and herself. That's an interesting make of flute, you note as you sip the tea Kiyoko offers you. Something from Kiyoko's homeland, is it? "It's a shakuhachi. I don't really know much about them, save that one of my many brothers took it up as a hobby. I spent my years as a kit learning to play the koto from my mother, a properly elegant instrument." You're sensing a bit of conflict here. Did Kinu make it herself? "Ha, no. Those things take up to ten years to fashion from scratch. The astral plane must have conjured one for our daughter — but I didn't order it to do such..." Which means that it's starting to obey Kinu, too. Ah, you're starting to see the beginnings of why your daughter's progress is starting to get your foxy wife just the slightest bit worried. "I'm not resentful, just worried. It could cause problems if the astral plane started giving into her demands — can you imagine our daughter just conjuring up a never-ending supply of peaches to stuff her face with? I simply don't like unexpected developments sneaking in under my nose, you know? Especially when it concerns our daughter?" Hmm... Slowly, music begins to fill the room as Kinu starts playing, her fingers dancing over the flute's length as she closes her eyes in concentration. The tune is solemn with a deep and rich timbre — practically meditative and spiritual, when you focus a bit. It's calming, perhaps a little too much so, threatening to lull you to sleep if you don't keep your guard up... About the playing itself, though... not the best, to be honest. [ pc.bg minstrel |Listening to Kinu work the flute, you're pretty sure your daughter's missed a couple notes here and there, and ugh — that one was off-key, no doubt about it. The tune's still holding together, but there's little doubt in your mind there's plenty of room for improvement. If you knew the instrument yourself, you might've the mind to take her aside afterwards. |You may not know how to play music, but you've definitely heard enough in your time to tell if something's off, and the expression of disapproving distaste on Kiyoko's face is enough to suggest that it's indeed the case. Did Kinu just miss a note there? ] She's trying, gods knows she is, but perhaps she could've practiced a little bit more before choosing to perform for you... "Like I said, one of my many brothers used to play the shakuhachi back in the day," Kiyoko says with a sniff. "Our daughter has quite a ways to go yet, I'd say. Why, when I asked her the reason for choosing that over the koto where I'd be able to give her a proper education and guidance, she told me that I was too good at it and wanted to do something where she wouldn't be smothered." Hmm... is that animosity you're hearing from her? Kiyoko tightens her lips and sips her tea. "I don't know, I think I raised our daughter better than to pass over a perfectly good opportunity instead of stubbornly demanding to take the hard road." Eventually, the music dies down, Kinu lowers the bamboo flute, and she breaks the steady rhythm of her breathing with a small sigh. Turning your gaze from mother to daughter and back again, you clear your throat and tell Kinu you'll see her outside. "Yes, [kinu.Dad]." Wrapping her three tails about herself, Kinu shuffles out of the sitting room and into the hallway beyond. You follow suit, and it's only when the screen door's shut behind the two of you that your daughter looks askance and grinds her heels into the floor. So... "That wasn't very good, was it?" It could have been better, yes. If she knew she wasn't at a presentable level yet, why did she insist on performing in front of her mother and you? "I..." Kinu's lip trembles, but she catches herself and turns it into a pout. "I wanted you to recognize me." And so you are. She's catching flak for disobeying her mother, isn't she? "It's not disobeying. I... I just don't want to play the koto, [kinu.Dad]. It's not me, and I don't want to end up as a miniature copy of Mama, anyway. If two people are the same and agree on everything, one of them is unnecessary. Yes, I'm having a harder time learning the shakuhachi than I would the koto, but it's worth it. I want to find my way of expressing myself, not do it because it's what Mama does." ...So, at the end of the day, she wants to be more independent and her mother doesn't like it because she's interpreting it as disobedience. And yet the same argument she made for not wanting to learn the koto could arguably be applied to anything she was too lazy to bother with... "Are you on my side or not, [kinu.Dad]?" You're on no one's side. In fact, you'd like to see how this plays out — you'll tentatively support her efforts for now, but she should know you'll also be keeping a close eye on this situation. Hopefully, she'll conduct herself in a manner that'll reflect well on her and be able to perform again for you sometime down the road. "Boo." Kinu sniffs. "Well, I'm going to practice some more, then. Can't let you down, can I?" With that, she's off, eyes locked straight ahead and very definitely not eyeing you out of the corner of her vision. You watch your daughter disappear around a corner, her footsteps fading into the distance, then slip back into the sitting room where Kiyoko's waiting. "So? Were you able to coax anything out of our daughter?" Somewhat. There're some issues to be worked out with Kinu, but it was time you took a more active role in your daughter's life, anyway. You should also make some time to talk to Kiyoko about this, but not right now when tempers are running high. Maybe during another visit, when everyone's cooled down enough to be able to think more rationally about the issue. "You do that," Kiyoko says with a sigh as she pours herself another cup of tea. "It would really be nice if you helped with that handful of fluff from time to time. But enough about our daughter's misbehavior — let's have some alone time, [pc.name]. What's on your mind?" |Kinu kneeling on a cushion in one corner, right by the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. Set out in front of her is... well, it would look a little like a lute of the kind that little bard-boy in the Frost Hound plays, if a lute were flat, placed on the floor and raised on one end. All right, strings aside, it looks absolutely nothing like a lute. [ pc.bg minstrel |Now that you're thinking about it, you've vaguely heard of these kinds of instruments — a whole family of them, if you're not wrong. Zithers, were they? For some reason, they never seemed to catch on amongst any of your fellow minstrels. Probably a combination of them being less portable and local customs, if anything. ] "Hello, [kinu.Dad]," your firstborn fox-daughter pipes up. "And Mama, too." Indeed. What's this all about? "Well." Kinu looks a little uncertain for all of a moment, then puffs herself up as best as an eight year-old fox-child can. "I've been learning the koto from Mama, and um... I'd like to show you how far I've progressed. That, and I really want you to be able to enjoy some relaxing music, [kinu.Dad]. You always seem so stressed when you come. Think of it as thanks for always petting and playing with me." Kiyoko purrs and leans against you, one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] foxy tails caressing your leg. "Such a sweet little thing, isn't she? Come, sit down; I'll bring us some tea." Faced with such an invitation by both wife and daughter, it's hard to say no. You take your usual place at the low table, Kiyoko brings up the tea set before settling in beside you, and she pours you a steaming cup of fresh, bitter brew as Kinu begins to play. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [ pc.bg minstrel |as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use |but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though ]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, that's for sure. Beside you, Kiyoko has a big smile on her face as she sips at her tea, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails swishing back and forth as she savours the melody. Your foxy wife is looking immensely self-satisfied, and gives you a wink as you catch her eye. "It's very good, isn't it? She's better than I was when I was her age; it's almost frightening how quickly she picked it up. And she's playing one of my favorites, too." Mm-hm. But a clever child must have had an excellent teacher and mother to have gotten anywhere, right? "By Keros' name, you're such a flatterer," Kiyoko purrs. "In that case, your seed must have been exceptionally strong to produce such a precocious daughter, because that didn't come from my side of the family, I can tell as much." Oof, that was a good one. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. Amazing, she hasn't missed a single note — [ pc.bg minstrel |you'd like to think that this is something Kinu got from you as well, but that's probably patting yourself on the back a little too hard. You aren't that great of a minstrel — yet |or maybe she might have, but if she did you damn well couldn't tell ]. At last, though, the music dies down, and Kinu looks up uncertainly at the both of you. Poor thing's clearly seeking approval; smiling, you stand, step up to your daughter and pet her between the ears. She did good there. Your little floof daughter does her best to remain composed and elegant, but the color that creeps into her cheeks is obvious as you fluff her ear fur while she bows. "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. I-I'll be going now." Before you can protest, little Kinu's picked up her instrument under and arm and is high-tailing it out in a flash. Kiyoko just laughs, sips her tea and folds her arms[kiyoko.pregStage 1| on her kit-swollen belly]. "Oh dear, seems like you embarrassed her. I remember feeling much the same when performing for the first time in front of someone who wasn't my mother. Don't worry, it'll pass." She gestures for you to take up your seat back at the table. "That was entertaining, wasn't it?" Indeed, it was. For Kinu to throw together a performance like that... A smile. "Like I said, [pc.name], she really, really wants your approval. But enough about that, it's a lovely day. Why don't we enjoy some time together?" ]"

rows.original: Somewhere else and some time ago... Warm sunlight breaks through the forest canopy in bright rays, warm against your skin as you clamber over roots and fallen logs. The soft, crumbly soil is just as cool, sticking to your bare feet and toes and feeling very, very pleasant. Mother'll kick up a fuss when you get back into the house if you don't wash your feet first... ...Come to think of it, you've got to be further into the forest than you've ever been before. Sure, home's always but a short distance away if you put your mind to it, but there's the thrill of adventure at going so deep, past the familiar landmarks... Does it ever end? The sound of flowing water catches your ear, and you slink through the pines and maples to investigate its source. Gradually,the trees fall away to reveal a small forest pond, its clear surface sparkling with reflected warmth, its bottom clearly visible even from where you stand. That's not all that there is to the place, though: flowers of every shape and color cluster about the water's edge, butterflies and moths flitting about their many-hued petals. A small stream flows outwards from whatever underground spring feeds the pool, trickling over mossy rock as it vanishes into the forest. This is perfect. A place to sit and rest your feet, plus Mother said she wanted you to gather some choice specimens for tomorrow's flower arrangement lessons. You've been walking for what feels like hours in search of something like this, and just when you were about to give up, such a scene of natural beauty happens to present itself... Is this what Mother means when she speaks of fate? Either way, there's no rest for someone as responsible as you! Getting on your hands and knees so that your face is level with the multitudes of blossoms strewn about the clearing, you set to sniffing and searching, doing your best to find the flower that's the prettiest. Tall grass tickles your tails and pollen gets in your nose, making you sneeze and your eyes water, but that's fine. Good things come to those who persevere, after all. One by one, you spend the rest of the afternoon picking through the options available to you, sniffing scents and munching on petals as you make your way around the forest glade. No, that one's blemished and wilted. No, that one's off; each flower in the arrangement must harmonise with the others, Mother says. No, that kind won't stay fresh for very long once you break it from its roots; the point is to keep the flowers pristine for as long as possible. One bad choice could ruin the entire arrangement... Hmm... Eventually, you get tired enough that you stop for a moment and soak your smarting feet in the pond's cool waters. So much time spent searching, and nothing to show for it... it's then that you spy a bunch of lilies growing in the soft, wet dirt by the water's edge. Those large, showy blooms with their elegant white petals and gentle fragrance make your heart skip a beat — sweet enough to be alluring, yet not so much that you dislike them. Kind of like peaches, really. If you cut them properly, they'd make a great centerpiece for tomorrow's lesson. Yes, this will certainly do. As you start towards the lilies, though, a flash of yellow catches your eye. Not five paces from them stands a clump of dandelions, their bright yellow color advertising itself, begging for your attention. Sure, they look a little scraggly, but you're sure they'd stay fresh a long time and moreover, you can feel new ideas for arrangements worming their way into your mind just by looking at them. Such resilience, such vigor, it can only spark inspiration even as it warms your heart. The two won't work together, though. Their colors, their auras — they simply clash too much, refusing to work together. Each one demands to be its own centerpiece, setting the theme for which the rest of the arrangement should take shape around. Dignified, alluring, fragrant — by all rights, you should take the lilies home for your lesson tomorrow. Yet there's a quiet resilience to the dandelions' simple beauty, one that draws the eye and makes your ears twitch. Mother won't be happy you brought home a weed, but she's never seen the appeal in such things — and besides, you can eat the dandelion when you're done with it. Which flower will you pick for your flower arrangement lesson with Mother?
rows.translation: 在某个地方，某个时候…… 温暖的阳光穿透森林的树冠，洒下明亮的光芒，当你攀爬着树根和倒下的原木时，这些光线温暖地抚触着你的皮肤。而那柔软、松软的泥土也同样凉爽，粘在你的赤足部上，感觉非常舒适。如果你不先洗足部就回到家里，妈妈肯定会大发雷霆的…… 仔细想想，你这次进入森林的范围肯定比以往任何时候都要深。当然，只要你想回去，家其实永远都在不远处，但深入森林，越过那些熟悉的地标，那种冒险的刺激感确实是非同寻常的…… 这种状态究竟何时才会结束呢？ 潺潺的流水声传入你的耳中，你悄悄地穿过松树和枫树林，去探寻它的源头。渐渐地，树木消失了，出现了一个小森林池塘——它清澈的湖面反射着温暖的光芒，即使站在那里，也能清楚地看到湖底。不过，这个地方的可观赏之处还不止这些：各种形状和颜色的花朵簇拥在水边，蝴蝶和飞蛾在它们五彩斑斓的花瓣周围飞舞。有一条小溪从为这个水池提供水源的地下泉眼中流出，它蜿蜒流过长满苔藓的岩石，最终消失在森林之中。 这简直太完美了。这里既可以坐下来休息，而且妈妈还说让你采集一些优质的标本，用来准备明天的插花课。你似乎走了好几个小时才找到这样的地方，就在你准备放弃的时候，这样一片自然美景竟然出现在你面前…… 母亲所说的命运，难道就是这个意思吗？ 无论如何，对于你这样一个责任心强的人来说，根本不可能有休息的机会！你跪倒在地，让脸与空地上散落的那些花朵处于同一水平线上，开始仔细嗅闻、寻找，竭力找出最漂亮的那朵花。高高的草丛会挠你的尾巴，花粉也会进入你的鼻子，让你打喷嚏、眼睛流泪，但这些都没关系。毕竟，坚持到底的人总会得到好的回报。 一个下午的时间，你逐一挑选那些可供选择的鲜花，穿梭在森林的小径间，闻着花香，品尝着花瓣的芬芳。不，这一朵有瑕疵，已经枯萎了；不，这一朵也不行——母亲说过，插花时每一朵花都必须与其他花朵相协调。不，这种花一旦从花茎上摘下来，很快就不会新鲜了；关键是要让这些花朵保持最新鲜的状态。一个错误的选择，就可能会毁掉整个插花作品…… 嗯…… 最终，你累得实在受不了了，便停下来，将发痛的双足部浸入池塘清凉的水中。花了这么多时间寻找，却一无所获……就在这时，你注意到水边柔软潮湿的泥土中长着一丛丛莲花。那些大型、醒目的花朵，拥有优雅的白色花瓣和淡淡的香气，会让你的心跳加速——它们甜美诱人，却又不会让人感到反感。其实，它们和桃子有点相似。如果处理得当，它们完全可以成为明天课程中完美的装饰品。是的，这样肯定就可以了。 然而，当你朝着百合花的方向走去时，一道黄色的光芒吸引了你的目光。距离百合花仅有五步之遥的地方，有一丛蒲公英，它们那鲜艳的黄色色彩格外显眼，仿佛在吸引你的注意。虽然这些蒲公英看起来有点杂乱无章，但你相信它们一定能够保持很长时间的新鲜状态。更重要的是，仅仅是看着它们，你就会产生一些关于如何搭配花束的新想法。这种生命力、这种活力，不仅能激发你的灵感，还能温暖你的心。 然而，这两者是无法协同工作的。它们的颜色、它们所散发的气场——这些元素之间的冲突实在太过剧烈，根本无法协调一致。每一部分都坚持要成为整个组合的核心，都试图让自己成为整个布局的主题，而其他部分则必须围绕这个主题来展开。高贵、诱人、芳香——按常理来说，你应该把这些百合花带回家，作为明天的学习素材。然而，蒲公英那种朴素的美中蕴含着一种默默的力量，这种美能够吸引人们的目光，让人忍不住想要仔细欣赏。妈妈肯定不会高兴你带了一株野草回家，但她从来没见过这类东西的魅力所在……更何况，你总可以吃用完之后，就把蒲公英扔掉吧。 那么，在和妈妈一起做插花练习时，你会选择哪朵花呢？

Is this what Mother means when she speaks of fate? Either way, there's no rest for someone as responsible as you! Getting on your hands and knees so that your face is level with the multitudes of blossoms strewn about the clearing, you set to sniffing and searching, doing your best to find the flower that's the prettiest. Tall grass tickles your tails and pollen gets in your nose, making you sneeze and your eyes water, but that's fine. Good things come to those who persevere, after all. One by one, you spend the rest of the afternoon picking through the options available to you, sniffing scents and munching on petals as you make your way around the forest glade. No, that one's blemished and wilted. No, that one's off; each flower in the arrangement must harmonise with the others, Mother says. No, that kind won't stay fresh for very long once you break it from its roots; the point is to keep the flowers pristine for as long as possible. One bad choice could ruin the entire arrangement... Hmm... Eventually, you get tired enough that you stop for a moment and soak your smarting feet in the pond's cool waters. So much time spent searching, and nothing to show for it... it's then that you spy a bunch of lilies growing in the soft, wet dirt by the water's edge. Those large, showy blooms with their elegant white petals and gentle fragrance make your heart skip a beat — sweet enough to be alluring, yet not so much that you dislike them. Kind of like peaches, really. If you cut them properly, they'd make a great centerpiece for tomorrow's lesson. Yes, this will certainly do. As you start towards the lilies, though, a flash of yellow catches your eye. Not five paces from them stands a clump of dandelions, their bright yellow color advertising itself, begging for your attention. Sure, they look a little scraggly, but you're sure they'd stay fresh a long time and moreover, you can feel new ideas for arrangements worming their way into your mind just by looking at them. Such resilience, such vigor, it can only spark inspiration even as it warms your heart. The two won't work together, though. Their colors, their auras — they simply clash too much, refusing to work together. Each one demands to be its own centerpiece, setting the theme for which the rest of the arrangement should take shape around. Dignified, alluring, fragrant — by all rights, you should take the lilies home for your lesson tomorrow. Yet there's a quiet resilience to the dandelions' simple beauty, one that draws the eye and makes your ears twitch. Mother won't be happy you brought home a weed, but she's never seen the appeal in such things — and besides, you can eat the dandelion when you're done with it. Which flower will you pick for your flower arrangement lesson with Mother?"

rows.original: You give the dandelions one last look, then decide against them. As nice and energetic as they may be, they simply lack the propriety needed to go into a flower arrangement; plants like that belong out in the fields and woods where they ought to be. A flower arrangement is supposed to be something refined and carefully curated; weeds like these have no place in one. Now these lilies, though, that's another matter. Even just taking one of the petals and rubbing it between thumb and forefinger makes you feel serene and happy; you're sure that Mother will approve of your choice. Good thing you brought everything you needed out all this way — filling a small vase with water from the pond, you cut the lilies near the base of the stem and quickly transfer them to the porcelain vase. That should keep them fresh and perky for as long as possible. It's odd. The more you look at the lilies, the more you like them; before long, there's a big smile on your face as you trundle back home. It's obvious these blossoms have a unique magnetism of their own, and Mother's sure to like them as much as you do. No matter how deep you venture into the forest, home is always but a thought away. Within minutes, the trees part and fall away to open up into the familiar sight of the hilltop once more. Mother's on the porch as you approach the door, a broom in her hands as she sweeps away fallen leaves and cherry blossoms. "Kinu!" You stop and give Mother a small bow. "Mama." "Ah, you're back, and I see you brought something for tomorrow's lesson. Wash your feet before you step into the house, okay? I just finished cleaning, and don't want you tracking dirt all over the place." "Yes, Mama." "Now, shall we see what you brought home?" Happily, you bounce up to Mother and push your tiny, fluffy body against hers, then hold out the vase for inspection. "Now, where'd you find these?" "Oh, here and there." "Really." A sly smile spreading on her face, Mother sets aside her broom and kneels down so her face is level with yours.[kiyoko.pregStage 3| It's a bit of a stretch considering how big her pregnant belly is, but Mother is surprisingly flexible for her current gravid state.] Slowly, she cups her chin in her hands and turns the full force of her jade-green eyes on you. "Well then, this is quite the pleasant surprise. It'll make a pretty good centerpiece for what we're going to be doing in tomorrow's lesson. You have a good eye for these things, Kinu." "Ehehehe. I wanted to make you a present, Mama." "Oh?" You flush a little and start fingering your braid. "I just wanted to thank you for all the good things you've done for me, Mama, starting with being born and everything since that." Upon hearing this, Mother lets out a little dry laugh. "I'm glad you were born too, even if it was the most difficult birth I've had to date. You had a big head even as a newborn; just make sure it's not the only thing that gets bigger as you get older, okay? It's easy to be full of yourself, especially when you don't just think, but know you're smart. It would be a pity if nothing but your head grew." "Ehehe." You clasp your hands together, and contrive to look a little sheepish. "Always be my mother, and never change, okay?" "That much I can do. All right then, I'll take these off your hands until tomorrow's flower arrangement lesson. Hmm, I know exactly where to put this, too — we have a bit of wall that's looking a little bare. Maybe we'll have to do a little calligraphy and make a scroll to hang up behind the flowers; that would look good." Mother takes the lilies from you, gives them a sniff, and sighs happily. "They're good, aren't they?" "So adorable. Just don't be like your mother and turn all grouchy and moody when you get to a difficult age, okay? I know I caused my mother all sorts of grief back in the day. Come here, let Mother pet you." You obediently bow your head, ears tilted forward, and squeal aloud as Mother dispenses affectionate headpats. Her fingers slide through your silky hair, firm against your scalp; your three tails wag so fast they're practically a blur. "Ehehehehehe." "Now then, off with you. Wash your feet, then get ready to help with dinner."
rows.translation: 你最后再看了一眼那些蒲公英，但还是决定不选用它们。尽管它们看起来很漂亮、充满生机，但它们确实缺乏制作花束所需的品质；这样的植物应该被种在田野和树林里，它们属于那里。花束应该是精致而经过精心挑选的物品，而这类杂草根本不适合用来制作花束。 不过，这些百合花就另当别论了那就是另一件事是，哪怕只是摘下一片花瓣，用拇指和食指轻轻揉搓，也会让你感到宁静而愉悦；你肯定相信，母亲会认可你的选择。幸好你一路上都带上了所需的一切——从池塘里取水装满一个小花瓶，然后在莲花的茎部附近将花剪下，迅速将它们移栽到那个瓷花瓶里。这样就能让它们尽可能长时间地保持新鲜和活力。 奇怪的是，你越看这些百合花，就越喜欢它们；不久之后，当你欢快地走回家时，脸上一定会露出灿烂的笑容。显然，这些花朵本身就有一种独特的魅力，妈妈肯定也会和你一样喜欢它们的。 无论你走进森林多深，家始终就在咫尺之间。几分钟之内，树木就会让开道路，让你再次看到那熟悉的山顶景象。当你走近家门时，母亲会站在门廊上，手里拿着一把扫帚，正在清扫落下的树叶和樱花花瓣。 小娟！ 你停下来，向母亲微微鞠了一躬。妈妈。 啊，你回来了，我看你带了些东西准备明天的课程用。进屋之前先洗洗足部，好吗？我刚打扫完，可不想让你把脏东西带得到处都是。 是的，妈妈。 现在，让我们来看看你带回了什么吧？ 幸运的是，你立刻跑向妈妈，将自己那柔软、毛茸茸的小身体贴在她身上，然后把花瓶拿出来让她看。 那么，你是在哪里找到这些的？ 哦，到处都是吧。 真的吗。她脸上露出狡黠的笑容，放下扫帚，跪了下来，让自己的脸与你平视。[kiyoko.pregStage 3| 考虑到她怀孕后肚子已经变得那么大了，她还能保持这样的灵活性，确实有点不可思议。不过，以她目前的孕期状态来看，她的柔韧性确实相当不错。] 她缓缓地将下巴托在双手之间，然后用那双翠绿色的眼睛紧紧地注视着你。那么，这真是个令人愉快的惊喜。它将会成为我们明天课程中讨论内容的绝佳切入点。小娟，你在这些方面确实有独到的眼光。 嘿嘿嘿，妈妈，我想送你一份礼物。 哦？ 你稍微冲洗了一下，然后开始摆弄自己的辫子。妈妈，我只是想感谢你为我做过的所有好事，从你让我出生开始，到之后发生的每一件事。 听到这话，母亲发出了一声干涩的笑声。我很高兴你也能来到这个世界上，尽管那是我经历过的最艰难的分娩过程。你刚出生的时候脑袋就很大；不过要记住，随着年龄的增长，不要让只有脑袋变得越来越大哦，好吗？人很容易变得自高自大，尤其是当你不仅会思考知道你真聪明。要是你只有脑袋能长出来，那就太可惜了。 嘿嘿。你双手交叠在一起，努力做出一副有点害羞的样子。永远做我的妈妈，永远不要改变，好吗？ 这些我就能帮忙处理了。好吧，那这些就由我来帮您保管，等到明天的插花课再还给您。嗯，我也知道该把它们放在哪里——我们家里有段墙看起来有点空荡荡的，或许我们可以写些书法，制作一幅卷轴挂在花后面，那样会看起来很漂亮。 母亲从你手中接过百合花，闻了闻，然后开心地叹了口气。 它们很不错，对吧？ 太可爱了。只是别像你妈妈那样，到了青春期就变得脾气暴躁、情绪多变，好吗？我知道是我造成的我的过去，它总是惹来各种麻烦。过来吧，让妈妈抱抱你。 你乖乖地低下头，耳朵向前倾，当妈妈温柔地轻拍你的头时，你发出了欢快的叫声。她的手指穿过你柔软的头发，轻轻触碰着你的头皮；而你的三条尾巴则快速地摇动，几乎看不清它们的动作了。 嘿嘿嘿嘿。 好了，你现在可以走了。去洗洗足部，然后准备帮忙准备晚餐吧。

rows.original: Pick some of the lilies. Calm and elegant is your style.
rows.translation: 摘一些百合花吧。宁静而优雅，这才是你的风格。
rows.raw: "Pick some of the lilies. Calm and elegant is your style."

rows.original: You've made your decision — the dandelions it is. Rolling up your sleeves, you take a firm grip on the stems near the base of the choicest specimen, and pull. The weed is stubborn, but you're even more so; it fights you every step of the way, clinging to the ground with surprisingly strong roots. Little wonder Mother's so aghast when one of these happens to take root in the vegetable garden; it just refuses to give up when other, lesser weeds would've surrendered long ago. In a way, you can't help but feel a grudging respect for your foe even as it resists you to the very end, even though the outcome is clearly no longer in doubt. But you win — at long last, you win. Clods of dirt still clinging to its roots, the dandelion comes free of the earth and into your hands. Your fingers sting and the scent of sap is heavy in the air, but you've nevertheless won. Phew. Were you supposed to put it in water? Eh, you've forgotten to bring a bowl or vase or something to put it in; you simply can't move in the woods with something like that weighing you down anyway. Best to get it home as quickly as possible, then. Despite you having been rooting about in the forest for hours, finding your way back to the big tree is always a simple matter of minutes, and you practically bump into Mother on your way in. She's sweeping the porch of fallen leaves and cherry blossoms, and looks up at you sharply as you try to push past her. "Kinu!" "Can't talk, Mama. I need to put down this flower in some water before it starts to wilt!" "No, young lady, you're stopping right there. You're not going to track dirt into the house when I've just finished cleaning it." Mother stops, looks you up and down, then curls her lip. "You needed to get water, you said? Well then, march yourself over to the well and draw yourself a bath. You're filthy from head to toe, and there's pollen all over your hair and fur." Eeeeh... you never noticed. But now that Mother's pointed it out, there's no denying it. You are pretty dirty. Guess you were a little too into the spirit of things... "You did get something for tomorrow's flower arrangement lesson, didn't you?" "Like I said, Mama, I have to put this flower in some water!" Mother blinks at the brilliant yellow dandelion you have in your hands, its roots still attached to a clod of earth. What's with the disappointment? Surely she can see why you made your choice, can't she? "Why a dandelion?" she says at last. "I like it! It's very strong and vibrant!" "And... ?" "And you can use it for many things! The flower, the roots, the stem and leaves..." "I spend hours trying to teach you the language of flowers, and this is what you come up with?" You pout. "I know the language, Mama. Trust me, I do. But sometimes I find that it isn't able to speak the words I want to say. That's why... that's why I want this one!" This dandelion, it's yours. You found it. If Mother makes you throw it out and get another one from the forest, you'll... you'll... You'll what, exactly? A small sigh. Then, to your surprise, Mother's hand finds its way to your head and begins ruffling the scruffy hair between your ears. "Fine, do as you wish. Just go and wash that dirt off you now, understand? That, and check in on the daikon radishes while you're behind the house; we'll be having some for dinner." Strange. You'd expected Mother to put up more of a fight than that, but you're not going to question her change of heart. Dandelion still clasped in your cupped hands, you turn tail and head for the rear of the tree. Some things never change... but sometimes, they do.
rows.translation: 你已经做出了决定——要拔掉那些蒲公英。你卷起袖子，紧紧抓住那株最茂盛的蒲公英的茎部，开始用力拔拉。这种杂草非常顽固，但你也毫不退缩；它在每一个环节都在与你抗争，那些根系紧紧地抓住地面，让人感到十分难以拔除。难怪当这种杂草在菜园里扎根时，妈妈会如此惊慌失措——因为它会顽强地坚持下去，而那些比较普通的杂草早就放弃了抵抗。在某种程度上，你甚至会不由得对这种敌人产生一种莫名的敬意，尽管它一直在与你抗争到底，尽管结果早已显而易见。 但你赢了——终于，你赢了。那些粘在蒲公英根部的泥土还未完全脱落，但它已经从土里钻了出来，落在了你的手中。你的手指被刺痛了，空气中弥漫着浓重的汁液气味，但无论如何，你还是赢了。 呼…… 你是不是应该把它放在水里呢？呃，你忘了带碗或者花瓶之类的容器来装它吧；直接这样放是不对的。移动当有这样的东西压在身上时，待在树林里实在不是什么好事。所以，最好尽快把它带回家。尽管你在森林里找了几个小时，但找到回到那棵大树的路其实只需要几分钟而已。而当你往回走的时候，几乎一下子就碰到了妈妈。她正在打扫门廊上落下的树叶和樱花花瓣，当你试图从她身边经过时，她猛地抬头看了你一眼。 小娟！ 妈妈，我现在不能说话。我得把这朵花放在水里，否则它就会开始枯萎了！ 不行，小姐，您就停在这里吧。我刚把房子打扫干净，您可不能把灰尘带进屋里去。母亲停下来，上下打量了你一番，然后撇了撇嘴。你说你需要去取水，是吧？那就好好走到井边去打些水来洗个澡吧。你从头到脚都脏兮兮的，头发和毛皮上还沾满了花粉。 呃……你之前从来都没有注意到这一点。但既然妈妈指了出来，那就无可否认了。你是相当过分啊。看来你真是太投入其中了…… 你做了你为明天的插花课准备了一些东西，对吧？ 就像我说的，妈妈，我必须把这朵花放在水里才行！ 母亲看着你手中那朵亮黄色的蒲公英，它的根部还紧紧地粘着一块土。你为什么看起来这么失望呢？她肯定能够理解你做出这个选择的原因，对吧？ 为什么选蒲公英呢？她终于开口说道。 我喜欢！它非常有力，充满活力！ 然后……？ 而且它的用途非常多！花、根、茎、叶……都可以用来做各种事情。 我花了数小时的时间试图教你理解花语，而你给出的却是这样的结果？ 你撅起了嘴。妈妈，我会说这种语言。相信我，我真的会。但有时候，我发现这种语言无法表达我想说的话。所以……所以我才想要这个！ 这种蒲公英啊，真是你的你找到了它。如果妈妈让你把它扔掉，然后去森林里再找一个，你就会……你就会……” “你到底会怎么样呢？” 轻轻叹了口气。然后，令你惊讶的是，妈妈的手伸到了你的头上，开始拨弄你耳边那些乱糟糟的头发。 好吧，随你的便。现在就去把身上的脏东西洗干净，明白吗？另外，在你去屋后的时候顺便看看那些大根萝卜吧，我们晚饭要用它们。 奇怪。你本以为母亲会抵抗得更激烈一些，但你也不会质疑她态度的转变。手中依然紧握着那朵蒲公英，你转身朝树的后方走去。有些事情永远都不会改变……但有时候，它们也会改变的。

Surely she can see why you made your choice, can't she? "Why a dandelion?" she says at last. "I like it! It's very strong and vibrant!" "And... ?" "And you can use it for many things! The flower, the roots, the stem and leaves..." "I spend hours trying to teach you the language of flowers, and this is what you come up with?" You pout. "I know the language, Mama. Trust me, I do. But sometimes I find that it isn't able to speak the words I want to say. That's why... that's why I want this one!" This dandelion, it's yours. You found it. If Mother makes you throw it out and get another one from the forest, you'll... you'll... You'll what, exactly? A small sigh. Then, to your surprise, Mother's hand finds its way to your head and begins ruffling the scruffy hair between your ears. "Fine, do as you wish. Just go and wash that dirt off you now, understand? That, and check in on the daikon radishes while you're behind the house; we'll be having some for dinner." Strange. You'd expected Mother to put up more of a fight than that, but you're not going to question her change of heart. Dandelion still clasped in your cupped hands, you turn tail and head for the rear of the tree. Some things never change... but sometimes, they do."

rows.original: Pick some of the dandelions. Simple beauty and vibrance beats quick-wilting showiness.
rows.translation: 摘一些蒲公英吧。这种朴素的美与生机，远比那些昙花一现的华丽要值得珍惜。
rows.raw: "Pick some of the dandelions. Simple beauty and vibrance beats quick-wilting showiness."

rows.original: As you step up to the hilltop, a blur of color whizzes up and comes to a screeching halt just before it crashes into you. Standing before you is little Kinu, looking up at you with an expression of pure-hearted excitement. "Hello, [kinu.Dad]!" Why, hello there — it's always a good thing to see your favorite foxy daughter. "Hey, [kinu.Dad]. Did you say I was your favorite foxy daughter?" Oh dear, you must have. "Ehehe." Kinu clasps her hands together and giggles. "I knew it! I'm [kinu.Dad]'s favorite!" She shouldn't let it get to her head, though. But that brings up the question — to what do you owe the pleasure? She's not at her lessons at the moment, nor is she giving any to her siblings; she should be playing outside on such a fine day. Footsteps sound from behind Kinu, and you look up to meet Kiyoko's ever-genial face. "Greetings, [pc.name]. I asked our daughter to keep an eye out for you, since you do appear to have arrived at a most fortuitous time." Oh? And that would be? "We're celebrating the Festival of Longevity today, dear. While I'm afraid I won't be able to entertain you in the usual fashion, I still hope you'll come and join us for the occasion." Well, you're here already, and it sounds like fun. So, what is she going to do for this little event, anyway? Kiyoko bows and leads you to the cabin, Kinu trailing behind the both of you as her mother leads you indoors and into a part of the cabin you don't head into that often. Judging by the distance, though, you might be approaching the heart of the cherry blossom tree... "We're almost there, [pc.name]. To explain it, today we eat congee — rice porridge — made with seven different spring vegetables. It's supposed to insure that you live a long life, and stay healthy for the rest of the year." "There're other bits to this, too!" Kinu adds helpfully from behind the two of you. "Like how if you keep smiling for the whole day, you'll have good luck for the entire year!" Ha! "Why, [kinu.Dad], do you doubt my ability to hold a smile for one day?" It's less about the ability to do so, rather than the will. She's so excitable, it might just slip her mind when she's preoccupied with something else... "Any other day, I might sulk at that, but I'm not going to do it today, [kinu.Dad]! I'm going to keep this smile on my face until I go to bed, and you're not going to trick me out of it!" Kiyoko chuckles. "You have to admit, our daughter looks much better this way compared to when she's pouting. Let's head on in." With that, she pushes open the vine-covered door to reveal a large dining room, brightly lit by several warmly glowing orbs set in the ceiling. A number of long tables line the middle of the hall, at which are seated your foxy family. While you'd known the foxy family you've been growing with Kiyoko has been getting pretty large, seeing all the kits in one place... well, it really drives home the point. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3|If that wasn't enough, the little bulge of her belly will be getting bigger before too long, and then said foxy family will grow by the same amount... |Plus, with how hugely pregnant your kitsune slut-wife is, it won't be long before said family gets even bigger... |And knowing the proclivities your kitsune slut-wife has, it won't be long before she'll be wanting to add more kits to that number... ] As one, every single pair of slitted vulpine eyes in the room turns to look at you. "Look who came to visit today! It's your [pc.mf|father|mother]!" Various squeaky noises roughly recognisable as "hello, [kinu.Dad]," fill the room, each one blending into the other until it's a mess of noise. Kiyoko just smiles, rolls her eyes good-naturedly and takes hold of your arm. "Kinu, keep your brothers and sisters in line until we're ready to eat, okay? Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I will head into the kitchen to get out the porridge." "Yes, Mama." Leading you on by the crook of your arm, Kiyoko sweeps you through the dining hall, through a curtained doorway, and into the kitchen. The place is simply furnished, but definitely not sparse — cooking up enough at one go to feed so many kits is a heroic task in and of itself, even with the proper tools to do so. Several porcelain tureens stand on a sideboard, steam seeping from under the cover of each and bringing with it a crisp, slightly salty aroma. Kiyoko sighs wistfully and motions for you to pick one up before doing the same herself. "Before we had kits, when I was all alone in here — I didn't bother celebrating this festival. To me back then, there was little point in doing so; after all, I was doomed to be stuck in the Astral Plane until I eventually lost my grip on my sanity. Longevity was a curse, not a blessing. And now..." She's found a reason, you take it. Many reasons. "It's not just that feasts and festivals are meant to be shared with other people. It's also that it's important for the kits to know where they're coming from, so they know where they're going. Grounding in their home culture, no matter that it's the unfortunate, watered-down version I can give them." Kiyoko shakes her head. "There's no spring here nor seasons, or at least not that I don't command the Astral Plane to mimic. Health and longevity don't really mean much either, not in this gilded cage we're all stuck in. "Look at me, being all depressing when our children are so excited. I shouldn't be such a wet blanket — come on, let's get this out to the kits, they're hungry enough already." That you can do. Two tureens are hardly enough to fill the stomachs of all the hungry kits waiting at their tables, so it takes several trips between the both of you to carry out enough to make sure everyone's served. Even though Kinu is doing a fine job of keeping her siblings in check, you can tell the kits are getting quite antsy to start already. Still, everyone keeps in place until you're done, and Kiyoko ushers you to the head of the biggest table, taking the seat to your right while Kinu takes the one to your left. "All right then, we can begin. Today, we wish in Keros' name for the health of those near and dear to us. That's each and every one of you, my children, and it was worth it to stay up last night to prepare it for all of you and ensure it stayed warm." Smiling, Kiyoko turns to you, leans in, and gives you a quick peck on the cheek. "And to you, of course. May you have a happy and healthy year ahead, even if you can't be with us all the time." Kinu waves a ladle about in the air. "Will you do the honor of having the first taste, [kinu.Dad]?" But of course. Cheerily, your foxy firstborn daughter lifts the lid off the tureen closest to you, and serves up a large bowl of thick, gooey rice porridge. It's all chunky and gloppy with vegetables and herbs everywhere in a multicolored mess, and Kinu presents it to you with pride. "I think the Festival of Longevity is real neat. Porridge is porridge, but it tastes so different depending on who makes it. Me, I hope to be as good as Mama someday; she does a pretty amazing job at this kind of stuff. "So here! Eat up and stay healthy, okay? Take every last mouthful, because all of us here are counting on you!" Aww, that's so sweet — and so true, too. With all of the kits you've sired on Kiyoko assembled before you in the dining hall, it's hard not to see Kinu's point. You poke at the steaming mess in your bowl for a bit to let it cool down, then take a big mouthful. Like most of Kiyoko's cuisine, it tastes nothing like what you're used to in the waking world — to be frank, you're not sure if there's a word to describe what you're tasting right now. It's very... crisp. Vegetable-y. Seeing you give the go ahead, your foxy children follow suit, and soon the hall is filled with the clink of porcelain as they apply themselves to the food. "Here you go, Mama," Kinu says, ladling out another bowl for Kiyoko. "Here, Mama. This is from me — to a happy, healthy year without getting hurt or sick! I look forward to seeing your beautiful smile for a good long time to come!" "Whatever shall I do with you and your glib little tongue, daughter? Oh, whatever shall I do?" Kiyoko gives Kinu a pat on the head between the ears and takes the bowl, stopping for a moment to savour the aroma of her handiwork. "I really wonder where she gets that from, [pc.name] — you or me?" [pc.presenceRange 0 40 70| Her, of course. You're not the most eloquent person around, you've noticed. Kiyoko wiggles her ears. "Well, I suppose that's true. But you do have plenty of redeeming qualities, I'll say." See? There's no doubt Kinu inherited her honeyed tongue from her mother. | Hmm... definitely more of her mother, but you'd like to imagine that you contributed that certain something or the other that's making your daughter uncanny in that respect. A little more willingness to push the boundaries, perhaps? Kiyoko arches an eyebrow at that and flicks an ear at you. "Pushing boundaries is something she is doing more than I used to when I was her age. Tell me, Kinu, how many boundaries have you pushed this week?" "Twelmph." Your daughter swallows, and wipes some congee off her chin. "Make that thirteen, now." "If you want to ensure your mother stays healthy for the rest of the year and doesn't fall ill from sheer exasperation, I'd suggest you don't push any more boundaries." "Ehehe. I'll consider it deeply, Mama." | Why can't it be both, really? It's very possible that two disparate yet similar talents combined to produce something that's unique in and of itself. "I swear, you're almost as bad as she is." See? Almost, but not quite at Kinu's level. She's something else together, isn't she? Kinu stops munching on her porridge just long enough to speak. "Really, [kinu.Dad], now you're laying it on a little too thickly." ] Kiyoko sighs in mock exasperation and pinches the delicate bridge of her foxy nose. "Come on now, the both of you. Eat up before the congee gets cold, okay?" For a few moments, the three of you apply yourselves to the food, the clink of spoon against bowl echoing that made by your many foxy children. Kiyoko is a delicate, elegant eater; Kinu is none of the above. How such a small body can pack away that much food is eye-raising, but your daughter's already serving up her second bowl before her mother's even finished half of hers. Sure, the turnips don't taste half bad, and there're some finely chopped greens with an interesting flavor, but even so... It's interesting how so many festivals all around the world involve eating and drinking of some sort. "That's probably because everyone, everywhere does it at some point. That, and having meals together is a simple yet effective way to connect with other people. Would you please pass the soy sauce?" This? "Yes, that's it. Please." Kiyoko tips the sauce boat ever so lightly and sprinkles some of its contents onto her rice porridge. "As this congee is made with vegetables and seasoned with herbs that thrive in early spring, it's said to cleanse the body of undesirable influences." Desirable influences, on the other hand... "Ehe. Oh. Kinu, that's enough. You'll have two bowls, and no more." Is that right? She's a growing girl. "She's also a greedy girl. I don't want her getting chubby when young — it sets a bad precedent for her self-restraint when she grows older." You shan't question her, then. The rest of the meal passes in silence, but no words are needed for basking in each other's presence. Kinu greedily polishes off her second bowl of rice porridge, scraping every last morsel off the sides with her spoon and shovelling it into her mouth. Is it really that good? "It is!" "Flattery won't get you anywhere, daughter." "Well, that and I want to grow a bit taller. At this rate, I'm going to wind up even shorter than Mama when I'm done..." Well, if you got the gist of things, this is a day to wish good health upon those you love. For a kit like her, growing taller probably falls under that purview. "Eehee. Thanks, [kinu.Dad]. But even if the wish doesn't come true, I'm still glad you managed to show up today and join us. We... we don't really get to do many things together as a family, or at least, not as often as I'd like. Part of it is getting everyone together, of course..." Ah, right. "We all trust that you're doing your best, [pc.name]," Kiyoko says, quickly moving in to close the awkward silence with a kiss to your cheek and a curl of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails. "If you're going to get us out of here, then it makes perfect sense to wish good health for you, doesn't it? Stay safe out there, and visit us as often as you can." Little Kinu stands from her seat and gives you a small bow. "Please stay free from injury while you're out there, [kinu.Dad]. Goodbye for now!" It's not perfectly coordinated, but Kiyoko's many kits do make a concerted effort to mirror their big sister's actions, bowing together as they bid you farewell. "Goodbye, [kinu.Dad]. Thank you for joining us for the meal." Gee, that's a little embarrassing and more than a little heart-tugging. Her tails and yukata flowing behind her, Kiyoko gently takes you by the arm and starts leading you away from the dining hall and out of the cabin while Kinu starts commandeering her many siblings into cleaning up after the meal. "I hope you enjoyed yourself. It's the simple things in life that are the most meaningful, I imagine." Indeed. A thought, though... there were so many kits back there in the dining hall. You'd never really thought about it until you saw them all together at once, but... wow, have you really sired that many kits on Kiyoko? How does she manage? Any other family with this many energetic kits in one place would be in total chaos by now. "Practice, tenacity, Kinu's help, and an ordered, patient mind," comes the even-handed reply. "Once more, [pc.name]... thank you for coming and spending time with us. May you stay healthy and safe out there, and feel free to summon me should you need my assistance." Out of the cabin, and onto the hilltop; even as you walk, you can feel your time in the Astral Plane drawing to a close, your surroundings becoming misty and insubstantial as the waking world beckons. Kiyoko's at your side all this while, and the last thing you feel is your kitsune wife's hands upon your back, giving you a gentle push...
rows.translation: 当你走上山顶时，一道五彩斑斓的光芒急速飞来，在即将撞上你的瞬间突然停住了。站在你面前的是小小娟，她仰望着你，脸上洋溢着纯真而兴奋的表情。 你好， [kinu.Dad]!" 喂，你好啊——能见到你最喜欢的那个狡黠的女儿，总是件愉快的事。 嘿， [kinu.Dad]你刚才说，我是你最喜欢的狐妖女儿？ 哎呀，你肯定是不小心说出口了。 嘿嘿。小娟双手交叠，咯咯地笑了起来。我就知道！我果然 [kinu.Dad]他最喜欢的！ 不过，她不应该因此而骄傲自满。但这就引出了一个问题——这种快乐究竟是源于什么呢？现在她既没有去上课，也没有陪兄弟姐妹们一起玩耍；在这样一个美好的日子里，她本应该在外面玩耍才对。 突然，身后传来了脚步声，你抬头一看，看到了清子那总是面带微笑的脸。问候， [pc.name]我让我们的女儿留意你，因为你确实来得非常及时。 哦？那会是什么呢？ 亲爱的，今天我们正在庆祝重阳节。虽然恐怕不能像往常那样为你准备精彩的节目，但我还是希望你能来和我们一起共度这个节日。 嗯，既然你已经来了，而且听起来还挺有趣的。那么，她究竟会为这个小小的活动做些什么呢？ 清子鞠了一躬，然后带你走向小屋，小娟则跟在你们身后。她的母亲将你们领进了小屋的内部，进入了一个你们不常去的区域。不过，从距离来看，你们似乎正在接近那棵樱花的中心部位…… 我们快到了， [pc.name]为了说明这一点，今天我们吃的粥是用七种不同的春季蔬菜熬制而成的。人们相信，吃这种粥能够让人长寿，并在接下来的一年内保持健康。 这件事还有其他一些细节需要考虑！小娟从你们身后走了过来，热心地提供了帮助。就像这样，如果你一整天都保持微笑，那么一整年你都会好运连连的！ 哈！ 为什么， [kinu.Dad]你难道怀疑我有能力一天都保持微笑吗？ 关键不在于是否有这个能力，而在于是否愿意去做。她太容易分心了，当她专注于其他事情时，可能就会把这件事给忘掉…… 换作其他日子，我可能会因此生闷气，但今天我不会这样做的。 [kinu.Dad]我一定会保持这个笑容，直到上床睡觉，你绝对不可能让我把笑容从脸上抹掉！ 清子轻声笑了起来。你得承认，我们女儿这样看起来可比生闷气的样子好看多了。我们进去吧。 说着，她推开了那扇被藤蔓覆盖的门，里面是一间宽敞的餐厅，天花板上的几个散发着温暖光芒的球体为房间带来了明亮的光线。大厅中央排列着几张长桌，你的那些狐妖家族成员正坐在那里。虽然你早就知道和清子一起成长的这些狐妖家族成员已经变得相当多了，但当真正把他们全部聚集在一起来看的时候……嗯，这一幕确实让这个事实更加显而易见了。 [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3|如果这还不够的话，她肚子上的那小凸起很快就会变得更大，而那个“狡猾的小家伙”也会随之成长…… |而且，你的那个狐狸娘们现在怀孕都快把肚子撑破了，用不了多久，这个家庭就会变得更大了…… |考虑到你那个喜欢变身的狐狸老婆的那些癖好，用不了多久，她就会想要再增加一些“狐狸”来扩充那个数字了…… ] 瞬间，房间里的每一双狭长的狐妖般的眼睛都转向了你。 看看今天来拜访的是谁！是你的 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]!" 各种可以大致辨认出来的刺耳声响你好， [kinu.Dad],"这些声音充斥着整个房间，彼此交织在一起，形成一片嘈杂的混音。清子只是微笑着，善意地翻了个白眼，然后握住了你的手臂。 小娟，等我们准备吃饭的时候，一定要让你的兄弟姐妹们守规矩，听话，好吗？你的 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲] 然后我就会去厨房把粥拿出来。 是的，妈妈。 清子挽着你的手臂，带你穿过餐厅，经过一道帘子遮住的门，进入了厨房。这个地方陈设简单，但绝不显得拥挤——要想同时为这么多小动物准备食物，即使有合适的工具，这也是一项艰巨的任务。几个瓷制花瓶摆放在边柜上，每个花瓶的盖子下面都冒着热气，散发着一种清新的、略带咸味的香气。 清子满怀感慨地叹了口气，然后示意你先拿一个起来，自己也跟着拿了一个。在我们有这些装备之前，当我独自一人的时候——我根本不会费心去庆祝这个节日。在那个时候，我觉得这样做毫无意义；毕竟，我注定要被困在星界之中，直到最终失去理智。长寿对我来说是一种诅咒，而不是祝福。而现在…… 她找了个理由，信不信由你……其实是很多个理由呢。 举办宴席和节日，不仅仅是为了与他人共享欢乐；更重要的是，让这些孩子了解自己的根源，从而明白自己未来的方向。让他们扎根于自己的文化之中，哪怕这种文化只是我所能呈现给他们的、已经被削弱和稀释了的版本罢了。清子摇了摇头。这里没有春天，也没有季节的变化——至少，在我没有命令星界之力模仿这些自然现象的情况下，是不存在的。健康与长寿在这里也毫无意义，至少在我们所有人都被困在这座金光闪闪的牢笼里的时候是这样。 看看我，孩子们这么兴奋，我却搞得气氛这么沉闷。我真不应该当这样的扫兴者——来吧，我们把这些东西分发给孩子们吧，他们已经饿坏了。 你确实可以做到。仅仅两个罐头远远不够满足那些在桌旁等待的饥饿小动物的需求，因此你们需要往返几次才能带来足够的食物，确保每个人都能得到食物。虽然小娟在控制她的兄弟姐妹们方面做得很好，但你可以看出，那些小动物们已经开始变得焦躁不安了。不过，在你完成之前，所有人都保持着原来的位置。纪代子把你引到最大那张桌子的前面，自己坐在你的右边，而小娟则坐在你的左边。 那么，我们可以开始了。今天，我们以凯罗斯的名义，为所有在我们身边、对我们来说无比重要的人们祈求健康。这些人就是在场的每一位，我的孩子们。为了为大家准备这些仪式，我昨晚甚至熬了一整夜，确保一切都能顺利进行。基代子微笑着转向你，靠近你，然后在你的脸颊上轻吻了一下。当然，也祝你们所有人新年快乐、身体健康。即使不能一直和我们在一起，也愿你们拥有幸福美好的未来。 纪努将一把勺子在空中挥舞着。您能赐予我们这个荣幸，先品尝一下吗？ [kinu.Dad]?" 当然啦。 你那机灵的第一个女儿欢快地掀开了离你最近的那个汤锅盖，然后盛了一大碗浓稠粘稠的米粥递给你。粥里到处都是蔬菜和香草，颜色五彩斑斓，看起来非常诱人，小娟满怀自豪地将它递到你面前。我觉得长寿节真的挺有意思的。粥就是粥，但不同人做的味道却大不相同。我希望能有朝一日能像妈妈一样擅长做这类事情；她在这方面真的做得非常棒。 给你！吃光它，保持健康，好吗？把每一口都吃干净，因为在这里的每一个人都在期待着你！ 哎呀，真是太贴心了——同时也非常道理深刻。当看到基约科在餐厅里为你准备好了所有这些小点心时，就很难不理解小娟的想法了。你轻轻拨了拨碗里那热气腾腾的点心，等它们稍微凉一些后，便大口吃了起来。就像清子的多数菜肴一样，这种食物的味道完全不同于你在现实世界中习惯的那些味道——坦白说，你甚至不确定该用哪个词来形容你现在所品尝到的这种味道。它非常……清爽，带有蔬菜的清香。看到你允许他们动手，那些调皮的孩子也纷纷跟了上来，不久之后，大厅里就充满了瓷器碰撞发出的声响，因为他们都在专心致志地品尝这些食物。 给你，妈妈。纪夫给清子又盛了一碗饭。给，妈妈。这是我送给你的——愿你新的一年里幸福、健康，远离伤害和疾病！我期待着在未来很长一段时间里，都能看到你美丽的笑容！ 女儿啊，我该怎么处置你和你那巧舌如簧的嘴呢？哦，真不知道该怎么办才好……清子轻轻拍了拍犬的耳朵之间，然后拿起了那个碗，停了一会儿，细细品味着自己亲手做出来的食物的香气。我真想知道她是从哪里得到这种想法的 [pc.name] 是你还是我？ [pc.presenceRange 0 40 70| 当然是她了。你自己也注意到了，你并不是最擅长表达的人。 清子扭了扭耳朵。嗯，我想那是事实。不过我得说，你确实有很多值得肯定的优点。 看到了吧？毫无疑问，小娟是从她母亲那里继承了那副能说会道的本领的。 | 嗯……她确实更像她母亲，但你会忍不住想，自己肯定也在其中起到了一定的作用，才让女儿在这一点上显得如此与众不同。或许，是自己更愿意去挑战那些界限吧？ 清子听到这话，挑了挑眉毛，还朝你甩了甩耳朵。突破界限，正是她的风格。是现在我做的，比她那个年纪时做的还要多。告诉我，小娟，这周你究竟突破了多少界限呢？ 特沃尔姆夫。你的女儿把粥咽了下去，然后擦掉了下巴上残留的粥粒。现在总数已经是十三了。 如果你想确保你的母亲在今年的剩余时间里保持健康，不至于因为太过恼火而生病，我建议你不要再挑战她的底线了。 呵呵，妈妈，我会认真考虑的。 | 为什么不能两者兼而有之呢？完全有可能，两种看似不同却又有所相似的才能结合在一起，从而创造出某种独一无二的东西来。 我发誓，你简直和她一样糟糕。 看到吧？差不多了，但还差一点达到小娟的水平。她确实与众不同，不是吗？ 小娟暂时停下了吃粥的动作，开口说道。真的吗， [kinu.Dad]现在你有点夸张了吧太浓密地。 ] 清子假装恼怒地叹了口气，然后捏了捏自己那小巧精致的鼻子。快点吧，你们两个。趁粥还没凉掉，赶紧吃吧，好吗？ 有那么几分钟，你们三个人专心致志地吃饭，勺子敲击碗皿的声音，与你们那些调皮的孩子们发出的声音如出一辙。清子吃饭时动作娴静而优雅，而小娟则完全不是这样。这么小的身体竟能吃下这么多食物，实在让人惊叹——你的女儿甚至还在妈妈还没吃完自己那一半饭之前，就已经开始吃第二碗了。确实，这些芜菁的味道还算不错，里面还加了一些切得细碎的蔬菜，味道也挺有意思的，但即便如此…… 有趣的是，世界上有这么多节日，都会涉及到某种形式的饮食活动。 大概是因为在世界各地，每个人都会在某个时候这么做吧。而且，一起用餐是一种简单却有效的方式，可以帮助人们建立联系。请问能把酱油递给我吗？ 这个？ 是的，就是这个。请吧。清子轻轻地将酱料壶倾斜，然后把里面的一些酱料撒在她的米粥上。由于这种粥是用早春时节的蔬菜制成的，并且加入了那些在早春时节生长茂盛的香草来调味，因此据说它能够清除人体内那些不良的物质。 令人向往的另一方面，这些因素也会产生相应的影响…… 呵呵，哦，小娟，够了，你就吃两碗吧，不能再多了。 是吗？她还是个正在成长的女孩啊。 她也是个贪吃的女孩。我可不想让她在年纪小的时候就变胖——那样会给她将来养成自律的习惯带来负面影响。 那你就不该质疑她了。接下来的用餐时间在沉默中度过，但彼此的陪伴本身就已经足够了。小娟贪婪地吃完了第二碗米粥，用勺子把碗边上的每一粒米都刮干净，然后一口一口地吃下去。真的有那么好吃吗？ 就是这样！ 奉承是没有任何用处的，女儿。 嗯，还有我想再长高一点。照这个速度发展，等我长成大人后，可能会比妈妈还矮…… 嗯，如果你理解了其中的意思，今天就是一个应该为你所爱的人祈愿健康的好日子。对于像她这样的角色来说，长高应该也属于这些祈愿的范围之内吧。 嘻嘻，谢谢。 [kinu.Dad]但即使这个愿望没有实现，我依然很高兴你今天能够来到这里，与我们一起度过这段时光。我们……作为一家人，其实并没有太多机会一起做些什么，至少没有我期望的那么频繁。当然，让所有人聚在一起，也是其中的一个重要原因…… 啊，对了。 我们都相信你正在尽自己最大的努力。 [pc.name],"清子迅速凑过来，轻吻了你的脸颊，然后用一种俏皮的方式打破了那尴尬的沉默。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 尾巴。如果你真的要带我们离开这里，那么祝你身体健康当然是理所应当的，不是吗？在外面一定要注意安全，有空的时候经常来看看我们吧。 小日向从座位上站起来，向你轻轻鞠了一躬。在户外活动时，请一定要注意安全，避免受伤。 [kinu.Dad]暂时再见了！ 虽然动作并不完全协调一致，但清子的那些角色们确实都在努力模仿她们姐姐的动作——当它们一起向您道别时，也会一起鞠躬。再见了， [kinu.Dad]感谢您与我们共进这顿饭。 哎呀，这真是有点尴尬，同时也让人感到十分心疼。随着她的尾巴和和服在身后飘动，清子轻轻握住你的手臂，开始带你离开餐厅，走出小屋；而小娟则开始指挥她的那些兄弟姐妹们，让他们收拾残局。 希望你们玩得开心。我想，生活中最珍贵的就是那些简单的东西。 确实。不过有个想法……餐厅里有那么多小动物，直到你把它们全部看在一起时，才会真正想到这一点。但是……哇，你真的在清子身上生了这么多小动物吗？真是不可思议。做她是怎么做到的？如果其他家庭也有这么多精力充沛的孩子集中在一个地方，早就乱成一团了。 练习、毅力、小娟的帮助，再加上有条不紊的努力耐心注意。随之而来的是公正而中立的回应。再一次， [pc.name]……感谢您抽出时间与我们共度这段时光。愿您在外出时始终保持健康与安全，如果您需要我的帮助，请随时召唤我。 走出小屋，登上山顶；就在你行走的过程中，你会感觉到自己在星界中的时光即将结束，周围的环境逐渐变得朦胧、虚无缥缈，而现实世界正在召唤你。整个过程中，清子一直陪伴在你身边，而你感受到的最后一幕，就是你的狐妖妻子轻轻把手放在你的背上，推了你一下……
rows.raw: " As you step up to the hilltop, a blur of color whizzes up and comes to a screeching halt just before it crashes into you. Standing before you is little Kinu, looking up at you with an expression of pure-hearted excitement. "Hello, [kinu.Dad]!" Why, hello there — it's always a good thing to see your favorite foxy daughter. "Hey, [kinu.Dad]. Did you say I was your favorite foxy daughter?" Oh dear, you must have. "Ehehe." Kinu clasps her hands together and giggles. "I knew it! I'm [kinu.Dad]'s favorite!" She shouldn't let it get to her head, though. But that brings up the question — to what do you owe the pleasure? She's not at her lessons at the moment, nor is she giving any to her siblings; she should be playing outside on such a fine day. Footsteps sound from behind Kinu, and you look up to meet Kiyoko's ever-genial face. "Greetings, [pc.name]. I asked our daughter to keep an eye out for you, since you do appear to have arrived at a most fortuitous time." Oh? And that would be? "We're celebrating the Festival of Longevity today, dear. While I'm afraid I won't be able to entertain you in the usual fashion, I still hope you'll come and join us for the occasion." Well, you're here already, and it sounds like fun. So, what is she going to do for this little event, anyway? Kiyoko bows and leads you to the cabin, Kinu trailing behind the both of you as her mother leads you indoors and into a part of the cabin you don't head into that often. Judging by the distance, though, you might be approaching the heart of the cherry blossom tree... "We're almost there, [pc.name]. To explain it, today we eat congee — rice porridge — made with seven different spring vegetables. It's supposed to insure that you live a long life, and stay healthy for the rest of the year." "There're other bits to this, too!" Kinu adds helpfully from behind the two of you. "Like how if you keep smiling for the whole day, you'll have good luck for the entire year!" Ha! "Why, [kinu.Dad], do you doubt my ability to hold a smile for one day?" It's less about the ability to do so, rather than the will. She's so excitable, it might just slip her mind when she's preoccupied with something else... "Any other day, I might sulk at that, but I'm not going to do it today, [kinu.Dad]! I'm going to keep this smile on my face until I go to bed, and you're not going to trick me out of it!" Kiyoko chuckles. "You have to admit, our daughter looks much better this way compared to when she's pouting. Let's head on in." With that, she pushes open the vine-covered door to reveal a large dining room, brightly lit by several warmly glowing orbs set in the ceiling. A number of long tables line the middle of the hall, at which are seated your foxy family. While you'd known the foxy family you've been growing with Kiyoko has been getting pretty large, seeing all the kits in one place... well, it really drives home the point. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3|If that wasn't enough, the little bulge of her belly will be getting bigger before too long, and then said foxy family will grow by the same amount... |Plus, with how hugely pregnant your kitsune slut-wife is, it won't be long before said family gets even bigger... |And knowing the proclivities your kitsune slut-wife has, it won't be long before she'll be wanting to add more kits to that number... ] As one, every single pair of slitted vulpine eyes in the room turns to look at you. "Look who came to visit today! It's your [pc.mf|father|mother]!" Various squeaky noises roughly recognisable as "hello, [kinu.Dad]," fill the room, each one blending into the other until it's a mess of noise. Kiyoko just smiles, rolls her eyes good-naturedly and takes hold of your arm. "Kinu, keep your brothers and sisters in line until we're ready to eat, okay? Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I will head into the kitchen to get out the porridge." "Yes, Mama." Leading you on by the crook of your arm, Kiyoko sweeps you through the dining hall, through a curtained doorway, and into the kitchen. The place is simply furnished, but definitely not sparse — cooking up enough at one go to feed so many kits is a heroic task in and of itself, even with the proper tools to do so. Several porcelain tureens stand on a sideboard, steam seeping from under the cover of each and bringing with it a crisp, slightly salty aroma. Kiyoko sighs wistfully and motions for you to pick one up before doing the same herself. "Before we had kits, when I was all alone in here — I didn't bother celebrating this festival. To me back then, there was little point in doing so; after all, I was doomed to be stuck in the Astral Plane until I eventually lost my grip on my sanity. Longevity was a curse, not a blessing. And now..." She's found a reason, you take it. Many reasons. "It's not just that feasts and festivals are meant to be shared with other people. It's also that it's important for the kits to know where they're coming from, so they know where they're going. Grounding in their home culture, no matter that it's the unfortunate, watered-down version I can give them." Kiyoko shakes her head. "There's no spring here nor seasons, or at least not that I don't command the Astral Plane to mimic. Health and longevity don't really mean much either, not in this gilded cage we're all stuck in. "Look at me, being all depressing when our children are so excited. I shouldn't be such a wet blanket — come on, let's get this out to the kits, they're hungry enough already." That you can do. Two tureens are hardly enough to fill the stomachs of all the hungry kits waiting at their tables, so it takes several trips between the both of you to carry out enough to make sure everyone's served. Even though Kinu is doing a fine job of keeping her siblings in check, you can tell the kits are getting quite antsy to start already. Still, everyone keeps in place until you're done, and Kiyoko ushers you to the head of the biggest table, taking the seat to your right while Kinu takes the one to your left. "All right then, we can begin. Today, we wish in Keros' name for the health of those near and dear to us. That's each and every one of you, my children, and it was worth it to stay up last night to prepare it for all of you and ensure it stayed warm." Smiling, Kiyoko turns to you, leans in, and gives you a quick peck on the cheek. "And to you, of course. May you have a happy and healthy year ahead, even if you can't be with us all the time." Kinu waves a ladle about in the air. "Will you do the honor of having the first taste, [kinu.Dad]?" But of course. Cheerily, your foxy firstborn daughter lifts the lid off the tureen closest to you, and serves up a large bowl of thick, gooey rice porridge. It's all chunky and gloppy with vegetables and herbs everywhere in a multicolored mess, and Kinu presents it to you with pride. "I think the Festival of Longevity is real neat. Porridge is porridge, but it tastes so different depending on who makes it. Me, I hope to be as good as Mama someday; she does a pretty amazing job at this kind of stuff. "So here! Eat up and stay healthy, okay? Take every last mouthful, because all of us here are counting on you!" Aww, that's so sweet — and so true, too. With all of the kits you've sired on Kiyoko assembled before you in the dining hall, it's hard not to see Kinu's point. You poke at the steaming mess in your bowl for a bit to let it cool down, then take a big mouthful. Like most of Kiyoko's cuisine, it tastes nothing like what you're used to in the waking world — to be frank, you're not sure if there's a word to describe what you're tasting right now. It's very... crisp. Vegetable-y. Seeing you give the go ahead, your foxy children follow suit, and soon the hall is filled with the clink of porcelain as they apply themselves to the food. "Here you go, Mama," Kinu says, ladling out another bowl for Kiyoko. "Here, Mama. This is from me — to a happy, healthy year without getting hurt or sick! I look forward to seeing your beautiful smile for a good long time to come!" "Whatever shall I do with you and your glib little tongue, daughter? Oh, whatever shall I do?" Kiyoko gives Kinu a pat on the head between the ears and takes the bowl, stopping for a moment to savour the aroma of her handiwork. "I really wonder where she gets that from, [pc.name] — you or me?" [pc.presenceRange 0 40 70| Her, of course. You're not the most eloquent person around, you've noticed. Kiyoko wiggles her ears. "Well, I suppose that's true. But you do have plenty of redeeming qualities, I'll say." See? There's no doubt Kinu inherited her honeyed tongue from her mother. | Hmm... definitely more of her mother, but you'd like to imagine that you contributed that certain something or the other that's making your daughter uncanny in that respect. A little more willingness to push the boundaries, perhaps? Kiyoko arches an eyebrow at that and flicks an ear at you. "Pushing boundaries is something she is doing more than I used to when I was her age. Tell me, Kinu, how many boundaries have you pushed this week?" "Twelmph." Your daughter swallows, and wipes some congee off her chin. "Make that thirteen, now." "If you want to ensure your mother stays healthy for the rest of the year and doesn't fall ill from sheer exasperation, I'd suggest you don't push any more boundaries." "Ehehe. I'll consider it deeply, Mama." | Why can't it be both, really? It's very possible that two disparate yet similar talents combined to produce something that's unique in and of itself. "I swear, you're almost as bad as she is." See? Almost, but not quite at Kinu's level. She's something else together, isn't she? Kinu stops munching on her porridge just long enough to speak. "Really, [kinu.Dad], now you're laying it on a little too thickly." ] Kiyoko sighs in mock exasperation and pinches the delicate bridge of her foxy nose. "Come on now, the both of you. Eat up before the congee gets cold, okay?" For a few moments, the three of you apply yourselves to the food, the clink of spoon against bowl echoing that made by your many foxy children. Kiyoko is a delicate, elegant eater; Kinu is none of the above. How such a small body can pack away that much food is eye-raising, but your daughter's already serving up her second bowl before her mother's even finished half of hers. Sure, the turnips don't taste half bad, and there're some finely chopped greens with an interesting flavor, but even so... It's interesting how so many festivals all around the world involve eating and drinking of some sort. "That's probably because everyone, everywhere does it at some point. That, and having meals together is a simple yet effective way to connect with other people. Would you please pass the soy sauce?" This? "Yes, that's it. Please." Kiyoko tips the sauce boat ever so lightly and sprinkles some of its contents onto her rice porridge. "As this congee is made with vegetables and seasoned with herbs that thrive in early spring, it's said to cleanse the body of undesirable influences." Desirable influences, on the other hand... "Ehe. Oh. Kinu, that's enough. You'll have two bowls, and no more." Is that right? She's a growing girl. "She's also a greedy girl. I don't want her getting chubby when young — it sets a bad precedent for her self-restraint when she grows older." You shan't question her, then. The rest of the meal passes in silence, but no words are needed for basking in each other's presence. Kinu greedily polishes off her second bowl of rice porridge, scraping every last morsel off the sides with her spoon and shovelling it into her mouth. Is it really that good? "It is!" "Flattery won't get you anywhere, daughter." "Well, that and I want to grow a bit taller. At this rate, I'm going to wind up even shorter than Mama when I'm done..." Well, if you got the gist of things, this is a day to wish good health upon those you love. For a kit like her, growing taller probably falls under that purview. "Eehee. Thanks, [kinu.Dad]. But even if the wish doesn't come true, I'm still glad you managed to show up today and join us. We... we don't really get to do many things together as a family, or at least, not as often as I'd like. Part of it is getting everyone together, of course..." Ah, right. "We all trust that you're doing your best, [pc.name]," Kiyoko says, quickly moving in to close the awkward silence with a kiss to your cheek and a curl of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails. "If you're going to get us out of here, then it makes perfect sense to wish good health for you, doesn't it? Stay safe out there, and visit us as often as you can." Little Kinu stands from her seat and gives you a small bow. "Please stay free from injury while you're out there, [kinu.Dad]. Goodbye for now!" It's not perfectly coordinated, but Kiyoko's many kits do make a concerted effort to mirror their big sister's actions, bowing together as they bid you farewell. "Goodbye, [kinu.Dad]. Thank you for joining us for the meal." Gee, that's a little embarrassing and more than a little heart-tugging. Her tails and yukata flowing behind her, Kiyoko gently takes you by the arm and starts leading you away from the dining hall and out of the cabin while Kinu starts commandeering her many siblings into cleaning up after the meal. "I hope you enjoyed yourself. It's the simple things in life that are the most meaningful, I imagine." Indeed. A thought, though... there were so many kits back there in the dining hall. You'd never really thought about it until you saw them all together at once, but... wow, have you really sired that many kits on Kiyoko? How does she manage? Any other family with this many energetic kits in one place would be in total chaos by now. "Practice, tenacity, Kinu's help, and an ordered, patient mind," comes the even-handed reply. "Once more, [pc.name]... thank you for coming and spending time with us. May you stay healthy and safe out there, and feel free to summon me should you need my assistance." Out of the cabin, and onto the hilltop; even as you walk, you can feel your time in the Astral Plane drawing to a close, your surroundings becoming misty and insubstantial as the waking world beckons. Kiyoko's at your side all this while, and the last thing you feel is your kitsune wife's hands upon your back, giving you a gentle push... "

rows.original: [pc.isDK|Sure, your first instinct would have been to make her understand her defiance isn't appreciated, probably with a good slap|You could], but what would be the point of that? Without addressing the underlying issue here, she's just going to head on back once neither you nor Kiyoko are around to watch her. It's not hard to tell here that your daughter is behaving in a most uncharacteristic manner. Why doesn't she tell you what's on her mind, and perhaps you can work things out? The next peach stops halfway to Kinu's mouth. "What?" You said, why doesn't she tell you what's on her mind? "Nobody ever asks what's on my mind. Not in that fashion." Well, you're doing it right now. You can't promise that you'll be able to solve her problems for her, or that you will even if you could, but at the very least you can hear her out and provide guidance — it's better than the alternative, at any rate. Stressed or not, it's not a healthy response of any sort to stuff one's face like that. It doesn't solve the root of the problem, and she'll get fat if she does it all the time. There has to be a better way to work out her problems than temporary half-measures that'll only cause things to get worse in the long run. Filling her mouth the moment she gets stressed might be her first instinct ever since she was a very young kit, but proper behavior means tempering one's desires to suit one's ends. Kinu laughs, a short, sharp barking noise that's more fox than human, then her face collapses back into glumness once more. "You're ever so sensible, [kinu.Dad]. Stop being so sensible. I wanted you to get angry at me, to punish me, not try to be reasonable and talk me down! Fine, then! Tell me what I should do!" She's getting ahead of herself there. Didn't you say you had to hear her out first? And so it happens that for the next half-hour or so, your kitsune daughter pours out her woes to you. Like a river that's finally overflown its banks with snowmelt and is racing across the countryside, Kinu just keeps talking, the words coming so quickly that it's hard to tell where one concern ends and the other begins. Everything just seems to mesh into one another, from what seems to be the pettiest of troubles — feeling tired in the morning, being pestered by siblings — to the gravest of concerns, first and foremost being her suitability to be who she's being set up to be. "... And then I can hardly talk to Mama in that fashion, can I? She is, after all, the delegating authority here. I'm sure she'd be able to sit down and listen to my woes, but then... well, I don't think I'd get anything done. She knows what she's putting me through is necessary, and I know it, too, so I can't argue with her." Kinu sighs and starts fiddling with the peach in her hands. "As for my siblings... all they will ever say is that I should be happy instead that I'm heir to Mama's title of den mother, and that I'm getting so many good things showered on me that I've no cause to complain. Which, again, is also true." Gods, will she please take a breath before she passes out where she's sitting? Your kitsune daughter simply ignores you and keeps going on rapid fire. "And that's what makes it so hard — it would be so much easier if I could just say everyone was intent on being jerks and refuse to get out of bed until Mama drags me out by my tails. But I won't, or maybe it's because I can't. And —" All right, you've heard enough. It's a good thing you came across her today and stopped to talk, because she'd probably have burst had she continued like this for that much longer. Reaching out, you firmly plant a hand on Kinu's white hair and begin to rub back and forth, back and forth. Your kitsune daughter's ears start wiggling of their own accord, and her tails slow their agitated thrashing. Words die down to mumbling, and Kinu slumps her shoulders in defeat. "I'm... I'm not some kind of animal to be so easily placated... this isn't going to make the problems go away any more than stuffing myself with fruit until I'm sick will..." ...That was part of the plan, wasn't it? If she got sick from overeating, she'd have a reason she'd have felt was halfway legitimate for being out of commission. But then if she knew said sickness was self-inflicted... "...Bah... first you refuse to get mad at or punish me, then you point out that inconvenient fact. And I'd almost managed to make myself forget it too, until you came along. You really know how to ruin peoples' plans, don't you, [kinu.Dad]?" You say nothing and keep on patting Kinu's head, taking extra care to smooth down her large ears and finger the large fuzzy tufts sticking out from within. Still mumbling to herself, your kitsune daughter sighs and slumps against your side, the peaches rolling out of her lap and scattering on the grassy earth. "Guess I won't be needing those any more." Maybe not. What she should do is gather them up and offer them to her siblings. "...Maybe." A sigh. "I really like it that you're an outsider here, [kinu.Dad]. Apart from the structure, as it were. It puts you in a nice position to be able to listen without the entire conversation turning awkward..." You continue petting. At this point, Kinu's ears have taken on a life of their own, actively trying to escape your fingers as you chase them across her head. "...And you being a foreigner to kitsune culture means that you just mostly listen, and don't cut too deeply when you do comment. It's really nice." You'll tell Kiyoko to prepare more nutritious meals for her, maybe even stew up a tonic or two. If she's going to push ahead despite all this — and you know she's going to, her demeanour during the entire conversation said as much — she might as well fortify herself for what lies ahead. Although from the way things went today, maybe you should visit more often, too. Whatever else she may be, your daughter is still a child in both body and spirit. "I would like it if you visited more, [kinu.Dad]." You'll try. With a final tousle of Kinu's utterly disheveled hair, you finish up the headpats and let your kitsune daughter practically flow off the log and onto the grass. She lays there for a moment, all three of her tails wagging back and forth, then remembers something of her propriety and picks herself up to her knees, gathering the fallen peaches. "I guess I'll put these in the basket on the way out." One final question. What was her point anyway in attempting to provoke you into punishing her? What's she done — or more likely, what does she imagine she's done that warrants as much? "...Hmph." Your kitsune daughter's face instantly sours back to its old grumpy expression. "If I have to tell you, then doing so would be pointless." Before you can shout out a response, she's already turned tail and broken into a run straight for the trees, disappearing amongst them in the blink of an eye. Gods. Isn't this too early for her to be at a difficult age? You were under the impression that wasn't supposed to be until she had a handful more years on her. And more importantly, how much of Kinu's cheerful demeanour is just a facade she wears? Perhaps it would be worth it to talk to her mother some more, try and involve yourself a little more in your daughter's life and education. At the very least, it can't do any harm, can it?
rows.translation: [pc.isDK|当然，你的第一反应肯定是让她明白，她的反抗是没有人会喜欢的，或许还会给她一记响亮的耳光。|你可以。]但是，那样做又有什么意义呢？如果不解决根本问题，等你们或者清子都不在的时候，她还是会故态复萌的。很明显，你女儿现在的行为完全不符合她的性格。她为什么不把心里的想法告诉你呢？也许这样你们才能一起解决问题。 下一颗桃子，在到达堇的嘴边之前，突然停住了。什么？ 你说，她为什么不告诉你她心里在想什么呢？ 从来没有人会问我在想什么。至少不是以那种方式。 嗯，你现在做的就是正确的。你无法保证自己能够解决她的问题，甚至无法保证自己即便有能力也能帮到她，但至少你可以认真倾听她的倾诉并给予指导——无论如何，这总比什么都不做要好。无论有没有压力，那样暴饮暴食根本不是一种健康的应对方式。这种做法并不能解决根本问题，如果她一直这样下去，只会变胖。肯定有更好的方法来帮助她解决这些问题，而不是采取那些只会让情况越来越糟的临时性措施。每当她感到压力时，第一反应就是吃东西，这或许是从她还是个幼小的小动物时就养成的习惯。但作为一个有教养的人，就应该学会克制自己的欲望，以便更好地实现目标。 小娟发出一声短促而尖锐的叫声，那声音更像狐妖而不是人类，但很快她的脸色又恢复了阴沉。你真是太明智了， [kinu.Dad]别这么理智了。我本来希望你生我的气，惩罚我，而不是试图讲道理、劝我冷静下来！好吧，那你说我该怎么做？ 她未免太急功近利了。你不是说过要先听她把话说完吗？ 于是，在接下来的半个小时里，你的九尾狐女儿开始向你倾诉她的种种烦恼。就像一条被融雪冲破河堤、在乡间肆意奔流的河流一样，小娟喋喋不休，话语来得如此之快，以至于很难分辨一个烦恼究竟在什么时候结束，另一个烦恼又从什么时候开始。一切似乎都相互关联、紧密相连，从那些看似微不足道的小麻烦——比如早上感到疲倦、被兄弟姐妹打扰——到那些最为严重的担忧，其中最关键的问题就是她是否适合成为别人期望她成为的那个人。 ……那样的话，我几乎没法和妈妈好好谈话，对吧？毕竟她才是这里有最终决定权的人。我肯定她愿意坐下来听我倾诉，但那样的话……嗯，我觉得什么问题也解决不了。她知道让我经历这些是必要的，而且我也明白这一点，所以我也无法和她争论。纪久叹了口气，开始摆弄着手中的桃子。至于我的兄弟姐妹们……他们说的总是，我应该感到高兴才对，毕竟我是妈妈这个‘族群领袖’头衔的继承人，而且得到了这么多好东西，根本没有任何理由抱怨。嗯，说实话，他们说的也是对的。 天啊，她能不能先喘口气，免得在原地就晕过去啊？ 你的那只九尾狐女儿根本不理你，还在不停地快速攻击着。而这正是让事情变得如此困难的原因——如果我能声称所有人都是故意耍混蛋的，然后拒绝起床，直到妈妈拽着我才能起来，那一切就会简单多了。但我不会那么做，或许是因为我根本做不到。而且—— 好了，你们已经听够了。幸好你们今天遇到了她并停下来和她交谈，否则如果她继续这样下去，恐怕早就崩溃了。你伸出手，牢牢地握住小娟的白发，开始来回轻揉。你那只狐妖女儿的耳朵不由自主地动了起来，她的尾巴也不再那么慌乱地摆动。话语渐渐变成了低声呢喃，而小娟也无奈地低下了肩膀。 我……我可不是什么能轻易被安抚的动物……这样做根本无法解决这些问题，就像一直吃水果直到吃撑一样…… …这本来也是计划的一部分，对吧？如果她因为吃得太多而生病，那么她就有了一个看似合理的理由来解释自己为什么不能继续工作。但要是她知道这种“生病”其实是自己造成的…… ……哼……首先你拒绝生我的气或惩罚我，然后又指出那个让人尴尬的事实。我差点就真的把它忘掉了，直到你出现。你真的擅长破坏别人的计划，不是吗？ [kinu.Dad]?" 你一言不发，只是继续轻拍着小娟的脑袋，格外小心地抚平她那两只大耳朵，还用手指轻轻拨弄着从耳朵里伸出来的那些蓬松的毛簇。你还在喃喃自语着，而你的九尾狐女儿则叹了口气，软软地靠在你的身上，她怀里的桃子纷纷掉落，散落在那片长满草地的土地上。 看来我再也不需要那些东西了。 也许不行。她应该把它们收集起来，然后送给她的兄弟姐妹们。 ……也许吧。一声叹息。我真的很喜欢你是一个外来者这一点， [kinu.Dad]除了结构上的安排之外，这种设计确实能让你在聆听对话时保持一个舒适的立场，避免整个对话变得尴尬…… 你继续轻轻抚摸着她的耳朵。此时，小娟的耳朵仿佛有了自己的生命，当你试图在她的头顶上追逐它们时，它们会拼命试图逃脱你的手指。 ……而作为对狐妖文化并不熟悉的外人，你通常只需要倾听别人的意见，在发表评论时也不会过于深入地探讨某些问题。这样真的很好。 你应该让清子为她准备一些更有营养的食物，甚至可以炖一些滋补品。如果她无论如何都要坚持下去——而你也知道她一定会这样，她在整个谈话过程中的表现已经说明了一切——那么她最好为自己即将面对的事情做好充分的准备。不过，从今天发生的事情来看，也许你也应该更经常地去看看她。无论她已经长大到什么程度，你的女儿在身心上仍然还是个孩子。 如果你们能多来拜访几次，我会非常高兴的。 [kinu.Dad]." 你试一试吧。最后你把小娟那乱蓬蓬的头发整理了一下，然后继续轻拍她的头，直到你那只狐妖女儿从原木上跳到草地上。她躺在那里，三条尾巴不停地来回摆动，过了一会儿，她似乎想起了自己应该保持的体面，便跪了起来，把掉落的桃子捡了起来。 我想我出门的时候会把这些放进篮子里。 最后一个问题。她之所以试图激怒你，让你惩罚她，究竟是为了什么目的呢？她究竟做了什么——或者更确切地说，她自认为做了什么错事，才会招致这样的惩罚呢？ ……哼。你那只狐妖女儿的脸立刻又恢复了它那副脾气暴躁的表情。如果我非得告诉你的话，那么这样做也是毫无意义的。你还来不及喊出回应，她就已经转身拔腿朝树林跑去，转眼间就消失在了树丛之中。 天啊……对于她这个年纪来说，发生这种事未免也太早了吧？你原本以为，直到她再长大几岁，这种情况才会发生。更重要的是，小娟那种开朗的性格，有多少只是她伪装出来的外表呢？ 或许，再和她母亲多谈谈，试着更多地参与你女儿的生活和教育，会是一件很有意义的事情。至少，它不会造成任何伤害，对吧？
