rows.original: Stepping up onto the sunny hilltop, you find it largely devoid of activity, quiet save for the rustling of wind through the leaves. [kiyoko.numKits 4|Your kits must be off having fun somewhere else. ]Well, that and a certain unmistakable snuffling and munching — oh yes, there she is. Freshly picked off the bough, several huge, almost overripe specimens of fruit lie in the grass, and even more in your dearest daughter's skirts. Your firstborn kitsune daughter is lounging on a mossy fallen log, holding an enormous peach in both hands as she studies it like a housewife at a marketplace. Seeing you approach, Kinu stiffens, but her face sets into a resolute expression, her lips thinning into a barely visible line as she looks up at you. Holding your gaze every step of the way, your kitsune daughter yawns her mouth as wide as her tiny eight-year-old body will allow, and takes a comically large bite out of the peach, as if daring you to stop her. There's a lot being said here with absolutely no words, but as to what's exactly being said... ...One way or the other, what do you do now?
rows.translation: 当你登上阳光明媚的山顶，会发现那里几乎没有任何活动，只有风穿过树叶时发出的沙沙声，一片宁静。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|你的工具包肯定被拿去别的地方玩啦，肯定玩得很开心吧。 ]嗯，再加上那种清晰可闻的吸吮声和咀嚼声——哦，对了，它就在那儿。几颗新鲜摘下的、几乎已经熟透的巨大果实躺在草地上，而更多果实则粘在你最亲爱的女儿的裙子上。你的第一个孩子——那只狐妖女儿，正躺在一根长满苔藓的倒木上，双手捧着一个巨大的桃子，仔细端详着它，就像一位在市场上选购商品的家庭主妇一样。 看到你走过来，小娟的身体瞬间绷紧了，但她的脸上浮现出坚定的神情，嘴唇紧抿成一条几乎看不见的线，然后她抬头看着你。你的九尾狐女儿每走一步都会注视着你，她张大自己那八岁孩童般的小嘴巴，吃下了那颗桃子中一大口，仿佛在挑衅你阻止她。这里面蕴含着许多意味，尽管没有任何言语表达出来，但具体是什么呢存在 ……不管怎样，你现在打算怎么做呢？

rows.original: So, just what does she think she's doing here? Kinu stops just long enough to answer. "I'm eating a peach, of course." She takes another comically large bite out of the massive fruit, juices running down her chin in a most uncharacteristic fashion. "What did you think I was doing, [kinu.Dad]?" She does know what her mother thinks of stuffing her face between meals, doesn't she? "Of course I do, and I should know better." You don't know what's worse — if she were binge eating out of sheer gluttony, or this premeditated defiance. Kinu takes another big bite out of the peach, studies her handiwork, then tosses the stone over her shoulder. Her eyes shift, her ears swivel, and finally she folds her arms in front of her juice-stained yukata and continues to hold your gaze. "I know exactly what's going to happen here, [kinu.Dad], and I know I'm probably going to get into trouble for this. Thing is, I just want to eat something naturally sweet, now. If you're going to stop me by force, then please do it, because that's the only way you're going to stop me at this point."
rows.translation: 那么，她究竟认为自己在这里是在做什么呢？ 小娟停下来，稍作停留，然后回答道。我当然在吃桃子。她又大口咬下一口那个巨大的水果，果汁不由自主地从她的下巴流下来，这一幕显得格外滑稽。你以为我在干什么呢？ [kinu.Dad]?" 她心里很清楚，她妈妈对于她两餐之间不停地吃东西这种行为是怎么看的，对吧？ 我当然知道了，而且我本应该更明白这一点。 你根本不知道哪一点更糟糕——是她纯粹出于贪吃而暴饮暴食，还是这种蓄意为之的反抗。小娟又大口吃了一口桃子，仔细欣赏自己“创作”的成果，然后把桃核扔到了身后。她的目光四处游移，耳朵也微微转动，最后她双臂交叉在沾满果汁的和服前，继续凝视着你的眼睛。 我完全清楚这里将会发生什么。 [kinu.Dad]我知道这样做可能会给我带来麻烦。不过，我只是想吃一些天然甜味的东西而已。现在如果你想用武力阻止我，那就尽管动手吧，因为在这个时候，这就是阻止我的唯一办法。
rows.raw: " So, just what does she think she's doing here? Kinu stops just long enough to answer. "I'm eating a peach, of course." She takes another comically large bite out of the massive fruit, juices running down her chin in a most uncharacteristic fashion. "What did you think I was doing, [kinu.Dad]?" She does know what her mother thinks of stuffing her face between meals, doesn't she? "Of course I do, and I should know better." You don't know what's worse — if she were binge eating out of sheer gluttony, or this premeditated defiance. Kinu takes another big bite out of the peach, studies her handiwork, then tosses the stone over her shoulder. Her eyes shift, her ears swivel, and finally she folds her arms in front of her juice-stained yukata and continues to hold your gaze. "I know exactly what's going to happen here, [kinu.Dad], and I know I'm probably going to get into trouble for this. Thing is, I just want to eat something naturally sweet, now. If you're going to stop me by force, then please do it, because that's the only way you're going to stop me at this point.""

rows.original: Meet Kinu's defiance head-on and explain in no uncertain terms what you think of her stuffing her face.
rows.translation: 直接面对小娟的反抗，明确地告诉她，你对她那种暴饮暴食的行为有何看法。
rows.raw: "Meet Kinu's defiance head-on and explain in no uncertain terms what you think of her stuffing her face."

rows.original: Saying nothing, you sit down beside Kinu, close enough to be in her personal space but not too close. Your daughter eyes you warily, staring at you with the same precise pointedness with which you're not looking at her. Having failed to get a rise out of you, Kinu takes another large bite out of the peach, the fruit's crisp flesh audibly crunching as her teeth sink into it. Another bite, and another bite. Soon, all that's left of the humongous fruit is an equally oversized stone, which Kinu tosses over her shoulder. Oh, you felt the challenge all right — but letting her get a rise out of you would be exactly what she was trying to provoke, and you're not about to give her that satisfaction. At length, Kinu picks up another peach from her lap, makes to raise it to her mouth, then sighs and sets it down again. "Aren't you going to try and stop me, [kinu.Dad]? I'm doing a bad thing right now. It's your duty as a good parent to make sure that I don't go astray and become a delinquent."
rows.translation: 你什么也没说，只是坐在小娟的身边，距离足够近，已经进入了她的私人空间，但又不至于太过接近。太你关上了门。你的女儿警惕地注视着你，她的目光与你注视她的目光一样专注而锐利。不是看着她。既然没能引起你的注意，小娟又大口咬了一口桃子，牙齿咬在果肉上时，那清脆的声音清晰可闻。 又一口，再一口。很快，这个巨大的桃子就只剩下同样巨大的核了，小娟把核扔到了肩后。哦，你确实感受到了这个挑战——但让她得逞、惹怒你，正是她想要达到的目的，而你绝对不会让她如愿以偿。最终，小娟从自己腿上拿起了另一个桃子，刚要把它送到嘴边，却又叹了口气，把桃子放了回去。 你难道不打算阻止我吗？ [kinu.Dad]我现在正在做一件不好的事情。作为一位称职的父母，你的责任就是确保我不会误入歧途，不会变成一个犯错的人。

Your daughter eyes you warily, staring at you with the same precise pointedness with which you're not looking at her. Having failed to get a rise out of you, Kinu takes another large bite out of the peach, the fruit's crisp flesh audibly crunching as her teeth sink into it. Another bite, and another bite. Soon, all that's left of the humongous fruit is an equally oversized stone, which Kinu tosses over her shoulder. Oh, you felt the challenge all right — but letting her get a rise out of you would be exactly what she was trying to provoke, and you're not about to give her that satisfaction. At length, Kinu picks up another peach from her lap, makes to raise it to her mouth, then sighs and sets it down again. "Aren't you going to try and stop me, [kinu.Dad]? I'm doing a bad thing right now. It's your duty as a good parent to make sure that I don't go astray and become a delinquent.""

rows.original: Say nothing and take a seat beside Kinu for a bit. Let her simmer before seeing if words are needed.
rows.translation: 什么也别说，先坐在小娟旁边待一会儿。让她先冷静一下，然后再看看是否需要说些什么。
rows.raw: "Say nothing and take a seat beside Kinu for a bit. Let her simmer before seeing if words are needed."

rows.original: When you step into the hillside, you're greeted by the sight of Kinu sitting on one of the benches. Your hackles start to rise instinctively, but calm down soon enough when you realize there's not a single peach within reach of your daughter — instead, she's putting together what looks like a fox out of straw. A straw fox. It's somewhat crude, but then it is a straw sculpture. Ears bent forward, her tongue sticking out the corner of her mouth in concentration, Kinu weaves together her creation out of rice straw, completely oblivious to her surroundings. It isn't even until you're practically standing over her that she finally notices your presence, looking up with a sheepish grin on her face. "Hello, [kinu.Dad]." That's a cute fox she has there. Where'd she get the materials for it? In all your visits to Kiyoko's little pocket dimension, you haven't seen any grain fields about. "Ehe." Kinu pauses a moment to shape the fox's ears. They look a bit oversized, but then both she and her mother have pretty large ears... "I'm not entirely sure myself, to be honest. I was just thinking of trying my hand at making a straw fox, because I heard that kitsune used to make these in honor of Keros when the rice harvest came in. Then when I was looking around the back of the house, what do I find? A nice large bundle of rice straw. If only the same thing happened with peaches..." You sit down on the grass beside Kinu and watch her continue patting the fox into shape. Yes... there's a certain resemblance that can only be called familial. It's also too small to be a full-grown fox... but about just the right size to be a fox kit. "...Oh, and when you head on in to play with Mama, don't tell anyone I'm making this. I want it to be a surprise. I went out all the way here so that no one would see me putting the doll together." Hmm. Well, it couldn't hurt. Is she feeling better since the last time you spoke to her in this place, though? She looks cheerful enough, but by this point you know Kinu well enough to know that like her mother, your daughter is well-versed in all forms of emotional labor. "[kinu.Dad]..." Look, you know that she understands the responsibilities that come with her talents and station, and that she's doing her best to live up to them. Well, doing her best is a bit of an understatement. She's desperate to live up to them, isn't she? Kinu says nothing and continues putting together her creation. And not that this is a pass for her to misbehave or anything, but being a good girl all the time is tiring, isn't it? "It doesn't matter if it is, [kinu.Dad]." Kinu's voice is very carefully flat and neutral. "If we all only did things we wanted to do, no one would get anywhere. In my case, even if I did only do the things I wanted to, it wouldn't be enough for me to honestly call myself lazy. "That's a completely roundabout way of saying things, isn't it?" You don't know about that. All you know is you're concerned if she's going to explode. A long pause. Then, your daughter heaves a long sigh and pats the completed straw fox on the head right between the ears, just like how she herself loves to be petted. "I appreciate what you're trying to do here, [kinu.Dad], I really do. But I can't act like a baby myself if I'm going to be looking after babies. I have my own ways of pacing myself, and I'll do my best not to — well, if I wind up sick it won't be because of the daily grind, okay?" Hmm... "Trust me on this." Silence. ...Well. Who's the straw fox for? "Aya," Kinu replies without skipping a beat. "She loves playing with rag dolls. This... well, it's close enough." It's nice of her to think of her siblings like this. "I am responsible for them too, [kinu.Dad]." With that, she stands, picks up the now fairly lifelike fox and starts trundling away. "I'm going to give this to Aya, then I'm going to have a nap." Her jaw is set, her steps firm as all three-odd feet of little fox-child tugs away a fox almost two-thirds as big as she is. That's determination there all right, for better or for worse. You watch Kinu leave, her three tails swaying behind her, then sigh and prepare to head off yourself. That girl... it's as if she doesn't know if she wants to act like a child or an adult half the time. Well, time to go and see her mother...
rows.translation: 当你走进山坡时，首先映入眼帘的是坐在长椅上的小娟。你的直觉立刻令你感到有些不安，但很快你就放心下来，因为你发现女儿身边根本没有桃子——相反，她正在用稻草制作着什么。 一只稻草狐妖。虽然看起来有点粗糙，但是一个用稻草制成的雕塑。小娟专注地工作着，耳朵向前倾，舌头微微伸出嘴角，她用稻草一点一点地编织着自己的作品，完全没有注意到周围发生了什么。直到你几乎站在她的身边，她才终于注意到你的存在，抬起头，脸上带着一丝羞涩的微笑。 你好， [kinu.Dad]." 她养的那只狐妖真可爱啊。这些材料她是从哪里弄来的呢？你在每次访问清子的那个小异空间时，都没看到过有稻田之类的地方啊。 呵呵。小娟暂停了一下，仔细地塑造着狐妖的耳朵。它们看起来有点过大，不过她和她的母亲本来就都有比较大的耳朵…… 说实话，我自己也不太确定。我只是想试试看能不能制作一些稻草狐妖，因为听说在稻谷收获的季节，狐妖们会制作这些东西来纪念凯罗斯。然后当我去房子后面找东西的时候，你猜我发现了什么？一大捆稻草！要是桃子也能遇到同样的事情该多好…… 你坐在小娟旁边的草地上，看着她继续把那只狐妖抚养成形。没错……它们之间确实存在某种只能用“亲缘关系”来形容的相似之处。不过这只狐妖太小了，还无法被称为成年狐妖……但它的体型正好适合被称为一只幼狐妖。 ……哦，等你去和妈妈一起玩的时候，千万不要告诉别人是我做的这个。我想给妈妈一个惊喜。我专门跑到这里来，就是为了不让任何人看到我组装这个玩偶。 嗯，试试看也没坏处。不过，自从你上次在这个地方和她谈话之后，她的状况有没有好转呢？她看起来确实挺开心的，但你也应该很了解小娟——和她母亲一样，你的女儿也很擅长处理各种情感方面的问题。 "[kinu.Dad]..." 你看，她很清楚自己的才能和地位所带来的责任，也在竭尽全力去履行这些责任。不过，说她在“竭尽全力”其实有点轻描淡写了——她其实是迫切地想要做到最好，对吧？ 小娟什么也没说，继续忙着自己的创作。 当然，这并不是说她就可以因此行为不端或做什么不好的事情，但一直做一个“好女孩”也会让人感到疲惫吧？ 就算真是这样也没关系。 [kinu.Dad]."小娟的声音刻意保持着平淡而中立的语调。如果我们都只做自己想做的事情，那么谁也无法取得任何成就。就我而言，即使我做了只要能做我想做的事情，那么称自己为懒人也是理所应当的。 这么说其实有点绕弯子，不是吗？ 你并不了解内情。你只知道，你很担心她会发火。 长时间的沉默之后，你的女儿长叹一声，然后像自己喜欢被人抚摸一样，轻轻拍了拍那只已经完成制作的草编狐妖的脑袋。我很感谢你正在努力做的事情， [kinu.Dad]我真的这么认为。但如果我要照顾婴儿的话，我就不能自己还像个小孩子一样行事了。我有自己调节节奏的方法，我会尽力避免这种情况发生——嗯，如果我最终生病了，那肯定不是因为这些日常琐事导致的，好吗？ 嗯…… 相信我，这件事没骗你。 沉默。 ……那么，谁才是那个“稻草人狐妖”呢？ 阿雅，小娟毫不犹豫地回答道。她喜欢玩布偶。这个……嗯，也差不多吧。 她能这样关心自己的兄弟姐妹，真是太好了。 我是也要对它们负责。 [kinu.Dad]."说完，她站起身来，捡起那只已经变得栩栩如生的狐妖，然后开始慢悠悠地走开了。我要把这个送给Aya，然后去小睡一会儿。 她的下巴紧绷着，足部步坚定地拖着那只比她大差不多三分之二的小狐妖。那份决心确实令人印象深刻，无论结果是好是坏。你看着小娟离去，她那三条尾巴在身后摇摆，然后叹了口气，准备自己也动身前往。那个女孩……有时候她似乎自己都不清楚自己到底想表现得像个孩子，还是像个成年人。 好吧，是时候去看看她的母亲了……

rows.original: Indeed, Kiyoko returns from over the hill, looking carefully neutral instead of the frown she was wearing when she departed. Your fox-wife looks between you and Kinu for a few moments, then sighs and shakes her head. "Well, [pc.name]? Is our daughter fine?" Firstly, is she fine? "I'm very well, thank you. I had some tea, brushed out three of my tails, and meditated on several verses of poetry. Yes, I believe I am in a different frame of mind than when I left. Now, [pc.name]. Have you managed to talk some sense into our daughter?" More or less. You think that Kinu's gotten so used to picking up skills so effortlessly that it was quite a shock to her when she didn't advance as quickly as she'd hoped. That quickly led to frustration, and manifested in an obstinate nature and being too eager to give up. Seems like her natural talents worked against her this time around. Kiyoko considers this and narrows her eyes. "Very well, love. What do you suggest, then?" You know your daughter eventually will be learning both the bladed spear and shortbow, but perhaps starting with both at the same time is a bit too much for Kinu. Perhaps it would be best to start with what she favors — the [kinu.kinuWeapon|naginata|hankyu] — and teach her the other once she's developed a little more strength and a more robust constitution. Much of her education has been more on the intellectual and spiritual so far, after all, but most of all, what Kinu needs now is a hug and reassurance that her mother cares for her. A sigh. "I'll... I'll see what I can do about that. Some reworking of her lessons will probably be in order." With that, Kiyoko pads over to Kinu and scoops up the little kitsune in her arms. Kinu squirms unhappily. "Mama..." "Come on, then. Let's pick up all of this and head back for a bath. Maybe I did push you a bit too hard today." Clearing her throat, Kiyoko, turns to you. "I'm sorry, [pc.name], but I think I'll have to pass on entertaining you this time around. Our daughter needs me." Does she need any help? Should you stay a little longer? "No, no, that won't be necessary. Besides, you wouldn't be able to stay that long anyway. It's all right, [pc.name] — I'll simply see you another time. Goodbye, and please take care."
rows.translation: 的确，清子从山那边回来了，她的表情变得十分中性，再没有了离开时那种皱眉的神情。你的狐妖妻子在你们和小娟之间来回看了看，然后叹了口气，摇了摇头。 嗯， [pc.name]我们的女儿没事吧？ 首先，是她好吧？ 我很好，谢谢。我喝了一些茶，梳理了三条尾巴，还仔细思考了几首诗的意味。没错，我觉得现在的心境和离开时相比确实有所不同。现在， [pc.name]你有没有办法让我们的女儿听进去一些道理？ 差不多吧。你认为纪久已经习惯了如此轻松地掌握各种技能，因此当她没有像预期的那样快速取得进步时，她感到非常震惊。这种情绪很快导致了沮丧，进而使她变得固执己见，也更容易放弃努力。看来这一次，她的天赋反而成了她的障碍。 清子思考着这些，眯起了眼睛。好吧，亲爱的。那你有什么建议呢？ 你知道你的女儿最终会学习长矛和短弓这两种武器，但或许同时开始学习这两样东西对纪努来说有点太难了。也许最好先让她从她更喜欢的那一种开始学习—— [kinu.kinuWeapon|长刀|汉京] — 等她力气再大一些，体质也更强壮一些，再教她另外那件事吧。毕竟，到目前为止，她的教育主要集中在智力和精神层面，但最重要的是，现在小娟所需要的，只是一个拥抱和一句“妈妈关心你”的安慰。 叹了口气。我……我会想办法处理的。可能需要对她的教学内容进行一些调整。说着，清子走到犬身上，将那只小狐妖抱到了怀里。 犬不高兴地扭动着身体。妈妈…… 那好吧，我们把这些东西都收拾起来，然后回去洗澡吧。也许今天我确实逼你太紧了。清了清嗓子，清子转向了你。对不起， [pc.name]不过这次恐怕不能陪你们玩了，我们的女儿需要我。 她需要帮助吗？你应该再留一会儿吗？ 不，不，没必要那么做。而且，你也没办法待那么久。没关系 [pc.name] — 那我们就改天见吧。再见，一定要注意身体。

Perhaps it would be best to start with what she favors — the [kinu.kinuWeapon|naginata|hankyu] — and teach her the other once she's developed a little more strength and a more robust constitution. Much of her education has been more on the intellectual and spiritual so far, after all, but most of all, what Kinu needs now is a hug and reassurance that her mother cares for her. A sigh. "I'll... I'll see what I can do about that. Some reworking of her lessons will probably be in order." With that, Kiyoko pads over to Kinu and scoops up the little kitsune in her arms. Kinu squirms unhappily. "Mama..." "Come on, then. Let's pick up all of this and head back for a bath. Maybe I did push you a bit too hard today." Clearing her throat, Kiyoko, turns to you. "I'm sorry, [pc.name], but I think I'll have to pass on entertaining you this time around. Our daughter needs me." Does she need any help? Should you stay a little longer? "No, no, that won't be necessary. Besides, you wouldn't be able to stay that long anyway. It's all right, [pc.name] — I'll simply see you another time. Goodbye, and please take care."'

rows.original: As you approach the crest of the hill, a curious sight greets you: silhouetted against the sunlight are Kiyoko and Kinu, standing in an open area that's been cleared of the usual affectations. Instead, several archery butts have been set up where benches and parasols would usually be, a couple short arrows stick out of the closest one, but most have gone wild. Not that it's in use at the moment — Kiyoko is circling your daughter, barking out commands in a most uncharacteristic tone of voice while Kinu fumbles with the weapon, a bladed spear of odd design. "But Mama, this is so heavy," Kinu grumps, trying not to struggle with the bladed spear that looks to be a little more one and a half times as tall as she is. "The hankyu wasn't much better, either... my arms are aching already." Kiyoko watches Kinu flail about, her face impassive; looks like she's in full teacher mode right now. "These activities encourage reflection, mindfulness, and self-discipline, which is exactly why you need them. Of course it was hard when I began learning naginata forms under my own mother's tutelage; seeing you like this, my only regret is that I was too soft-hearted and didn't start you earlier." "Boo..." "Let's have none of this, now." Kiyoko folds her arms under her [kiyoko.numKits 1 8 32|slight|ample|generous] bust. "I've seen you trying to hit down the peaches from the branches with a bamboo pole for goodness knows how long, and not get the slightest bit tired. As hard as it can be to believe, I was once a child like you. I know how these things work." "B-b-but—" for a moment, it looks like little Kinu is about to turn on the waterworks, then that shuts off with considerable rapidity when she realizes it's not going to work on her mother. Your daughter's ears fold to the sides, and she resigns herself to her fate, wincing as her mother moves to correct her form once more. Seems like this is a good time to drop in, then. What's going on here? "Oh." Kiyoko finishes adjusting Kinu's posture, then turns to you. "My apologies, [pc.name]. How long have you been standing there?" [pc.isDK|About long enough, you'd say.|It's all right, what she was doing looked to be more important.] But as you said, what's going on here? The slightest of frowns appears on Kiyoko's usually genial expression. "I... I am attempting to get our daughter started on some basic martial skills. However, she is being the most recalcitrant little thing with her particular brand of passive-aggression, and frankly I am finding myself wishing that I could shove her back into where she came from." That's particularly strong language, coming from one such as Kiyoko. All right, why did she have to go make her mother all mad? The usually calm and serene Kiyoko all worked up like this? Kinu grumps and drops her stance, planting the base of her spear on the ground. "It's not my fault that everything about this is just so tiring. This isn't like history or math or magic, I actually have to move about so much, and stay still when I don't want to." "And yet you can play in the forest for hours on end without any issue whatsoever. Your problem isn't an issue with your limbs, it's an issue with your motivation and self-discipline. Of which, I note, you have none, and that brings us back to the point of why this is necessary..." Kinu says nothing, but looks up at you, her expression pleading. "...A naginata is not merely a noblewoman's weapon, it is a den mother's weapon. The symbolism is clear, a defensive weapon for the protection of home and hearth —" Dear? Kiyoko stops mid-lecture. "Yes?" Perhaps she should let up for a moment, go have a bit of tea, maybe straighten out her tails, all [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] of them. She's been working so hard at Kinu's education, and you've been lax — perhaps it's better that you try to catch up in your parental duties while she has a small break to calm her nerves. Yes? Yes? "I know when I'm being talked down to, [pc.name]." But it's still not a bad idea, isn't it? Otherwise this is just going to devolve into angry fox noises, and no one likes angry fox noises. Not to mention that nothing's going to get done when the angry fox noises are being made. Silence. And then, "Fine, suit yourself. Take her off my hands!" The two of you watch Kiyoko whisk herself away in the direction of the cherry blossom tree, leaving little Kinu there holding the bladed spear. "Thanks, [kinu.Dad]. I —" Now, this doesn't mean she's off the hook, either. Passive-aggression, eh? Yes, that would be most like her. Kinu beams, looking every part the perfect model of pure innocence. "Whatever do you mean, [kinu.Dad]?" If this isn't it right here before you, you don't know what is. Oh, and that she was considering crying earlier to try and manipulate her mother. If this is how things are going to be right now, just imagine when she's at that age where she's no longer a girl, but not quite a woman yet. There're going to be so many angry fox noises. "..." Are you right, or are you not? Your daughter looks appropriately apologetic and plops down on the grassy ground, leaning her spear against one of the archery butts. "I just thought this would be more fun, like learning usually is. It's not supposed to be fun, I get that, but it wouldn't hurt, would it?" Hmm... well. [pc.bg soldier hunter barbarian| You might be trained in the use of arms, but this bladed spear and the shortbow don't look like anything you've ever had the chance to wield before. Sure, the basic principles are probably similar to what you know, but then the problem's always in the details and then her mother would get upset at you for miseducating her. | You're not really trained in the use of arms, or at least not formally. While you might have picked up a thing or two ever since your adventure started, it's probably not up to the standard to which Kiyoko wants her daughter to be brought to. ] "So you're just as dumb as I am." That's kinda blunt, but yeah. You don't know... maybe this is because Kiyoko's trying to teach her both archery and the spear at the same time? She's so used to Kinu moving at the pace of her mind that she forgets to slow down when the body gets involved. "I don't know, either," Kinu grumps. "All I know is that I want to curl into a ball and go to sleep for a week." Look. You know that her mother eventually intends to have her do both archery and the spear. It couldn't hurt, though, for her to focus on one over the other for now until she feels more confident at these things. It's not as if she doesn't have time, right? "What do you suggest, [kinu.Dad]?" Well... You get the feeling what you say here may be rather important.
rows.translation: 当你即将爬上山顶时，一幅奇特的景象映入眼帘：在阳光的照耀下，清子与纪夫的身影清晰可见。他们站在一片被清理干净、没有杂物的空地上。通常摆放长椅和遮阳伞的地方，此刻却架起了几支弓；离得最近的那支弓上还插着几支短箭，但大多数弓都已经闲置不用了。目前它并没有被使用——清子正绕着你的女儿转圈，用一种极其不寻常的肌肉度发出命令，而小娟则手忙脚乱地摆弄着那件设计奇特的带刃长矛。 但是妈妈，这个太重了。纪努皱着眉头，努力操控着那根看起来比她高出一倍半的长矛。汉久这个游戏也好不到哪里去……我的胳膊都已经开始疼了。 清子冷眼旁观着犬子手忙脚乱地挣扎，脸上毫无表情；看样子她现在完全进入了“老师模式”。这些活动能够培养人们的反思能力、专注力以及自律精神，而这正是你所需要的。当然，在我最初在母亲的指导下学习薙刀技巧时，也确实遇到了很多困难；看到你现在的样子，我唯一感到遗憾的是自己当时太心软了，没有更早开始教你。 嘘…… 我们现在就不要再谈这些了。清子将双臂交叉在胸前。 [kiyoko.numKits 1 8 32|轻微的|充足的|慷慨的] 失败。我看你用竹竿试图把树枝上的桃子摘下来，这个动作已经持续了不知道多久，但你却一点也没有显得疲倦。虽然很难相信，但我也曾像你一样是个孩子，所以我明白这些事情该怎么做。 但是……有那么一瞬间，看起来小小娟马上就要哭出来了，但当她意识到这样做对妈妈没有用时，她的泪水又迅速止住了。你女儿的耳朵耷拉在身体两侧，她只能认命地忍受着，当妈妈再次要求她纠正姿势时，她不禁皱起了眉头。 看来现在正是插手的好时机……这里到底发生了什么？ 哦。清子调整完犬的姿势后，转向了你。非常抱歉， [pc.name]你在那里站了多久了？ [pc.isDK|可以说，这个时间已经够长了。|没关系，她当时正在做的事情似乎更为重要。] 但正如你所说，这里到底发生了什么？ 基约科原本和蔼的表情此刻浮现出一丝忧色。我……我正在尝试让我们的女儿学习一些基本的武术技能。然而，她表现得极其顽固，总是用那种消极抵抗的方式来对抗我，说实话，我真的希望自己能把她扔回她来的地方去。 这话可真够严厉的，尤其是出自像清子这样的人之口。好吧，她究竟为什么要惹妈妈生气呢？平时总是那么冷静、沉着的清子，这次怎么会变得这么激动呢？ 纪久嘟囔着，放下了手中的长矛，将其矛柄插在地上。这一切都变成这样，确实不是我的错累人这和历史、数学或魔法不一样，实际上我经常需要四处移动，而当我不想动的时候，也必须保持静止。 然而，你却可以在森林里连续玩上几个小时，而且完全不会遇到任何问题。你的问题并不出在四肢上，而在于你的动力和自律性。事实上，你这两样东西都完全没有。那个这就引出了为什么这样做是必要的这个话题…… 纪久什么也没说，只是抬头看着你，她的表情充满了恳求。 ……薙刀不仅仅是一位贵族女性使用的武器，它更是母亲用来保护家庭的武器。这种象征意义非常明显——它是一种用于守护家园的防御性武器。 亲爱的？ 清子突然在讲课过程中停了下来。是吗？ 或许她应该暂时停下来，去喝点茶，或者整理一下自己的头发，怎么样？ [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 他们中的一个人。她在孩子的教育上付出了那么多努力，而你却一直疏于履行自己的责任——或许，在她暂时休息、调整一下状态的时候，你应该抓紧时间弥补自己的过失，好好履行你的父母职责。这样不是更好吗？ 我知道当别人用居高临下的态度和我说话的时候 [pc.name]." 但这仍然是个不错的主意，不是吗？否则的话，这一切最终只会变成愤怒的狐狸叫声，而没人喜欢这种声音。更不用说，在这些愤怒的狐狸叫声响起的时候，根本什么事情都做不成。 沉默。然后，好吧，随你便。把她从我手里带走吧！ 你们两个看着清子朝樱花树的方向快步离去，只留下小娟站在那里，手里还握着那支带刃的长矛。谢谢， [kinu.Dad]我—— 不过，这并不意味着她就可以摆脱责任了。这种消极对抗的态度，嗯？没错，这确实很符合她的性格。 小娟笑得灿烂，看上去完全就是纯真无邪的典范。你到底是什么意思？ [kinu.Dad]?" 如果眼前所看到的就是事实，那你根本就不知道什么才叫真正的真相。哦，还有，她之前甚至考虑过通过哭泣来影响她母亲的决定。如果现在就是这种状况，那么试想一下，等她到了那个年纪——既不再是小女孩，又还没有完全成为女人时，情况会变成什么样吧……肯定会有很多麻烦出现的。很多愤怒的狐狸发出的声音。 "..." 你是对的，还是错的呢？ 你的女儿看起来确实很抱歉，然后就坐到了草地上，把她的长矛靠在其中一个射箭架上。我只是觉得这样会更有意思，就像平常学习一样。虽然学习本来就不应该是一件有趣的事情，但我认为这样做也不会有什么坏处，对吧？ 嗯……好吧。 [pc.bg soldier hunter barbarian| 你可能接受过使用武器的训练，但这种带刃的长矛和短弓，看起来与你以前使用过的任何武器都不一样。当然，它们的基本使用原理可能与你所熟悉的那些武器相似，但问题总是出在细节上——而如果你的使用方法让她母亲不满意，她肯定会责怪你没有教好她。 | 你其实并没有接受过正式的武器使用训练。虽然自从开始这次冒险后，你可能也学到了一些东西，但这些技能恐怕还达不到纪代子希望她女儿达到的标准。 ] 这么说来，你和我一样笨。 这么说有点直白了，但确实是这样。你可能不知道……也许这是因为清子同时试图教她射箭和使用长矛吧？她已经太习惯小娟按照她的节奏行动了，以至于当真正需要让身体参与这些动作时，她反而忘记了放慢速度。 我也不知道。小娟嘟起了嘴。我只想把自己蜷成一团，然后睡上一整周。 你看，她母亲最终还是希望她同时学习射箭和长矛技巧。不过，在她对这些技能还没有足够信心之前，先专注于其中一项也没什么坏处，对吧？她又不是没有时间学习，不是吗？ 你有什么建议吗？ [kinu.Dad]?" 嗯…… 你会觉得，自己在这里说的话可能相当重要。

rows.original: "[kinu.Dad]?" The naginata, then. That's what it's called, yes? The bladed spear? Her mother made it out to have quite the bit of cultural significance — you didn't catch all of the lecture she was giving back there, but it sounded pretty involved. Perhaps instead of worrying too much about her little arms aching, maybe she should try and find out more about its place in kitsune history and what it means to her people, and to her in particular. Or more correctly, the person she wants to be. You're not sure if it's too early for her to get started on this, though... "Mama said she started learning the way of the naginata just after she turned seven. I'm eight." Really. Come to think of it, you've never actually seen her hold one — or any common weapon, for that matter. "Mama doesn't go through the forms that much anymore because she has so many things to do," your daughter replies with a sigh. "Unlike me. I sure have too much free time on my hands." Well, your point stands. If she discovers more about the roots of what she's learning, instead of going through the motions for their own sake, she'll be more inspired to take these martial lessons more seriously. As they say in Tychris, you can't see where you're going if you don't know where you came from; being rooted firmly means that one can reach further ahead. "Where's Tychris, [kinu.Dad]?" Um, a city pretty far away. Come to think of it, can you see her naginata? "Mm-hm." Kinu stands, gets her spear from the three where she left it, and holds it out to you. You lean down and test the blade's edge with a finger — though it looks sharp, it feels pretty dull. [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|Yeah, you see it now — there's a spell on it that prevents it from doing any actual harm.|Maybe there's a spell on it to dull the edge so Kinu doesn't hurt herself? That would be like Kiyoko.] You have to admit, it's quite the exquisite piece, from the detachable blade all the way to how light the shaft is. Did Kiyoko dabble in weapons crafting in her long time trapped alone in the astral plane? "Dunno. Mama just handed it to me this morning." Perhaps she should ask her mother about it, then. "I get it, I get it." Kinu squirms on the spot, looking most resigned as she flicks her ears at you. "If nothing else, it'll be the kind of learning that I prefer. Maybe I might even be interested." Guess that'll have to do. A little more enthusiasm would be nice, but this is already an improvement given how hostile she was to the whole thing a few moments ago. And oh look, here comes her mother.
rows.translation: "[kinu.Dad]?" 那么，这就是所谓的“薙刀”吧？那种带刃的长矛？她的母亲说过，这种武器具有相当重要的文化意义——你可能没有听完整她当时讲的那些内容，但听起来确实很复杂。或许，她不应该过分担心自己的小胳膊会疼，而应该试着去了解这个特征在狐族历史中的意义，以及它对她们的族人，尤其是对她自己来说，代表着什么。或者更准确地说，应该是去了解这个特征与她想要成为的那个人之间的关联。不过，你不确定现在让她开始做这件事是否还为时过早…… 妈妈说，她七岁刚满就开始学习使用薙刀了。而我现在八岁。 真的。仔细想想，你其实从来没见过她拿过任何武器——或者说，任何常见的武器。 妈妈现在没那么多时间去处理那些繁琐的手续了，因为她有太多事情要忙。你的女儿叹了口气作为回应。不像我，我可有的是空闲时间。 嗯，你的观点很有道理。如果她能更深入地了解自己所学知识的根源，而不仅仅是为了完成任务而机械地学习，那么她就会更有动力认真对待这些武术训练。正如在提克里斯所说，如果你不知道自己从哪里来，你就无法知道自己将要去往何处；只有根基扎实，才能走得更远。 提克里斯在哪里？ [kinu.Dad]?" 嗯，那是一座距离这里相当远的城市。仔细想想，你能看到她手中的那把长柄刀吗？ 嗯。纪努站了起来，从她之前放置它的那个地方取出了她的长矛，然后递给了你。你弯下身子，用手指试了试矛刃的锋利程度——虽然看起来很锋利，但实际上摸起来却相当钝。 [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|是的，你现在看到了——它被施加了某种魔法，因此无法造成任何实际的伤害。|也许它被施加了某种魔法，使得边缘变得不那么锋利，这样小娟就不会受伤了。这和清子的情况一样吧。] 你不得不承认，这件武器确实制作精良，从可拆卸的刀刃到刀柄的轻便程度，都体现出了高超的工艺。难道在星界中独自被困的那些年里，清子也涉足过武器制造吗？ 不知道。妈妈今天早上刚把它交给我。 或许她应该去问问她母亲的意见。 我明白了，我明白了。小娟在原地扭来扭去，看起来显得非常无奈，同时她还用耳朵轻轻碰了你一下。至少，这种学习方式正是我喜欢的。也许我甚至会对它感兴趣。 看来也只能这样了。要是她能再热情一点当然更好，但考虑到她刚才对这件事还表现得那么反对，能做到这样已经算是进步了。哦，看，她的母亲来了。
rows.raw: " "[kinu.Dad]?" The naginata, then. That's what it's called, yes? The bladed spear? Her mother made it out to have quite the bit of cultural significance — you didn't catch all of the lecture she was giving back there, but it sounded pretty involved. Perhaps instead of worrying too much about her little arms aching, maybe she should try and find out more about its place in kitsune history and what it means to her people, and to her in particular. Or more correctly, the person she wants to be. You're not sure if it's too early for her to get started on this, though... "Mama said she started learning the way of the naginata just after she turned seven. I'm eight." Really. Come to think of it, you've never actually seen her hold one — or any common weapon, for that matter. "Mama doesn't go through the forms that much anymore because she has so many things to do," your daughter replies with a sigh. "Unlike me. I sure have too much free time on my hands." Well, your point stands. If she discovers more about the roots of what she's learning, instead of going through the motions for their own sake, she'll be more inspired to take these martial lessons more seriously. As they say in Tychris, you can't see where you're going if you don't know where you came from; being rooted firmly means that one can reach further ahead. "Where's Tychris, [kinu.Dad]?" Um, a city pretty far away. Come to think of it, can you see her naginata? "Mm-hm." Kinu stands, gets her spear from the three where she left it, and holds it out to you. You lean down and test the blade's edge with a finger — though it looks sharp, it feels pretty dull. [pc.cl blackmage whitemage|Yeah, you see it now — there's a spell on it that prevents it from doing any actual harm.|Maybe there's a spell on it to dull the edge so Kinu doesn't hurt herself? That would be like Kiyoko.] You have to admit, it's quite the exquisite piece, from the detachable blade all the way to how light the shaft is. Did Kiyoko dabble in weapons crafting in her long time trapped alone in the astral plane? "Dunno. Mama just handed it to me this morning." Perhaps she should ask her mother about it, then. "I get it, I get it." Kinu squirms on the spot, looking most resigned as she flicks her ears at you. "If nothing else, it'll be the kind of learning that I prefer. Maybe I might even be interested." Guess that'll have to do. A little more enthusiasm would be nice, but this is already an improvement given how hostile she was to the whole thing a few moments ago. And oh look, here comes her mother."

rows.original: "[kinu.Dad]?" Hmm, maybe she's a little too short to use that bladed spear effectively. Kiyoko's not the tallest, sure, but Kinu looks to be shaping up to be even more petite than her mother. Would she do better with a shortbow in the meantime, until she gets a little taller? "It's called a hankyu, [kinu.Dad]." That, then. You turn to look at the archery butts. Yeah, Kinu was definitely practicing earlier — seems like most of her arrows flew wide, with only a few hitting the targets. Hmm... seems like she's been angling up too much consistently... ...Oh. So that's why she's been missing. Really, Kiyoko should have known better to place the archery butts directly in line of sight of the peach grove. Perhaps the distraction might have been useful later on in training Kinu's concentration, but now the constant misses are just discouraging her. Hey, that gives you an idea... "Where are you going, [kinu.Dad]?" Just one moment — you'll be right back. It isn't too much work to find and pick a peach from one of the low boughs in the grove, then return to Kinu with it in hand. Your daughter eyes you with half-lidded eyes, then looks away, completely nonplussed. "[kinu.Dad]... do you seriously mean to bribe me with food to listen to Mama? Even if it is peaches..." No, no, not that way. Why doesn't she go get her bow and meet you? "...If you say so, [kinu.Dad]. My arms still ache." Hah, she'll change her tune once she sees what you've got in store. Moving an archery butt away from the peach grove is a little harder, but you manage it without too much hassle, and check that there's no one downrange. Excellent. Meanwhile, Kinu has retrieved her shortbow and a couple of arrows, moving like a little fuzzy slug towards the beginning of the makeshift range. "What now?' You grin and make a little indentation in the hay of the archery butt, then put the peach right smack in the center. Once that's done with, you make sure the coast is clear, return to Kinu's side, then point straight at the target. Why doesn't she give it a go now? As Kinu nocks an arrow and prepares to loose it, it's clear that she knows how to go about handling the shortbow, it's just that her body is insufficient for the task and she doesn't have the arm strength to properly handle the thing. Her hands shake as she draws the bowstring, even with the shortbow being what it is — what was Kiyoko thinking, trying to teach her archery? Nevertheless, Kinu does her best. She narrows her eyes, holds herself as steady as possible, and looses the arrow, her breathing controlled. At the last possible moment, her fingers jerk involuntarily, and the bowstring twangs. When it's all over, the arrow is sticking in the edge of the hay butt, still wobbling slightly from the impact. "Oops..." You give Kinu a pat on the head, smoothing down her fluffy ears. Look, the peach is helping — at least she's not missing the target completely any more. This isn't going to be something she can fix overnight — she'll need to work on her draw strength to be able to hold the bow steady like she knows she needs to. Now, try again. What she needs is to know that she's capable of improving, even if she doesn't pick it up with her usual ease. "Gods, [kinu.Dad]. Is this what everyone has to go through when they learn something new? I can't imagine being so slow about it. It'd be like... like if I didn't have my tails at all." To varying degrees, yes. Now exhale... and loose. Kinu looses the arrow, and this time it hurtles towards the target... and explodes into flame, streaks of pale blue fire wreathing the arrow's head and shaft as it flies towards the peach. The poor fruit doesn't stand a chance — it pops, splattering juice everywhere and dousing the now-charred arrow. And what was that supposed to be? "Oops... I... I just hated that peach so much, like I hated everything... pity, though. Such a waste of food..." Now, where was that earlier disdain when she thought you intended to bribe her with food? Kinu just looks defeated at this point, more sad than sulky; there's probably not much use in trying to talk sense into her right now. You get the feeling that maybe a hot bath and a bit of pampering is in order for your little floof, even if her mother isn't in the best of moods now. "Oh. I think Mama's coming back now."
rows.translation: "[kinu.Dad]?" 嗯，也许她的身高太矮了，无法有效地使用那种带刃的长矛。虽然清子的身高也不是特别高，但小娟看起来会比她母亲更加娇小。那么，在她长高一些之前，使用短弓会不会更适合她呢？ 它被称为‘半袖’。 [kinu.Dad]." 那么，你转头看向那些射箭的靶子。没错，小娟之前肯定在练习——看起来她射出的大多数箭都偏离了目标，只有少数几支击中了靶心。嗯……看来她总是过度地调整瞄准角度吧…… ……哦，原来如此。那就是这就是她一直失踪的原因。说真的，清子本应该更聪明一些，不要把那些射箭用的靶子放在桃树林的正视范围内。也许这种干扰在后来训练纪久的注意力时还会有用，但现在这种情况只会让她越来越失去信心。嘿，这个想法也许可以帮你理解…… 你要去哪里？ [kinu.Dad]?" 稍等片刻，马上就回来。从果园里那些低矮的树枝上摘一个桃子，然后再带着它回到小娟，其实并不费什么力气。你的女儿半睁着眼睛看着你，然后又把目光移开了，显然完全搞不清楚发生了什么。 "[kinu.Dad]……你真的是想用食物来收买我，让我听妈妈的话吗？哪怕是桃子也好…… 不，不是那样的。她为什么不去拿她的弓，然后来见你呢？ ……如果你这么说的话 [kinu.Dad]我的胳膊还是疼。 哈，等她看到你准备好了什么，她的态度肯定会改变的。把那个射箭的人从桃树林里弄走确实有点麻烦，但你还是顺利地解决了这个问题，而且还确认了目标区域里没有其他人。干得不错。与此同时，小娟也已经拿回了她的短弓和几支箭，像一只毛茸茸的小蛞蝓一样爬向了那个临时设置的射击场入口。 现在该怎么办？ 你微笑着在弓把上的干草上压出一个小凹痕，然后将箭头准确地放在那个凹痕的正中央。完成这些步骤后，你会确保周围没有障碍物，然后回到小娟的身边，直接瞄准目标。她为什么现在还不试试呢？ 当小娟搭上箭准备射出时，显然她知道该如何使用那把短弓呢？问题在于她的身体条件并不适合使用这种武器，也没有足够的手臂力量来正确地操作它。每当她拉弓时，双手都会颤抖——基约子究竟是出于什么考虑，才试图教她射箭的呢？ 尽管如此，小娟还是尽了最大努力。她眯起眼睛，尽可能保持身体稳定，然后松开了箭，同时控制着自己的呼吸。在最后的那一刻，她的手指不自觉地抽搐了一下，弓弦也随之绷紧了。当一切结束时，那支箭仍然插在干草堆的边缘上，由于撞击的力量，它还在微微摇晃。 哎呀…… 你轻轻拍了拍小娟的脑袋，整理她那蓬松的耳朵。看，那个桃子确实有帮助——至少她现在不再完全偏离目标了。这件事不可能让她一夜之间就解决，她需要不断练习控制拉弓的力量，才能像自己期望的那样稳稳地握住弓。再来试一次吧。她需要相信自己是有进步能力的，即使这次练习并不像往常那样轻松顺利。 天啊， [kinu.Dad]难道每个人在学习新东西时都得经历这样的过程吗？我简直无法想象自己会变得这么迟钝。那感觉就像是……就像完全没有尾巴一样。 在不同程度上，是的。现在呼气……然后放松。 小娟射出了那支箭，这一次，箭矢直冲目标而去……在飞向桃子的过程中，箭头和箭身突然燃烧起来，淡蓝色的火焰缠绕在箭身上。那只可怜的桃子根本没有任何机会——它瞬间被炸裂开来，果汁四溅，同时也把已经燃烧起来的箭也给浸湿了。 那么，原来发生了什么呢？那个应该是这样吧？ 哎呀……我……我就是特别讨厌那个桃子，简直讨厌所有东西……不过也真可惜，这么浪费食物啊…… 现在，当初她以为你打算用食物来贿赂她的时候，那种轻蔑的态度哪里去了？ 此时，小娟看起来简直就像被彻底打败了一样，更多的是悲伤而不是生闷气；现在试图跟她讲道理恐怕也没什么用。你感觉，或许应该给你的小家伙泡个热水澡，好好宠溺她一下，哪怕她的妈妈现在心情并不是很好。 哦，我想妈妈现在应该要回来了。

rows.original: Once more, your dreams coalesce into the familiar surroundings of the sunlit hilltop and the gigantic cherry blossom tree perched atop it. Odd, though, that there's no one around. [kiyoko.numKits 4|Even if Kiyoko herself isn't out and about, some of your kitsune children should be running around and creating some kind of ruckus somewhere. Peace is fine, but it's a little too peaceful around here. |There's usually at least some kind of life out and about, even if it's not Kiyoko herself.] A little worried, you check the hilltop and peach grove for any sign of Kinu, but neither is your daughter anywhere to be found. Nothing left for it but to check the cabin; a few minutes' walk has you up to the door, and you let yourself in. [pc.isDK|They left it unlocked, after all, so that's an invitation if you ever saw one.|It's a little awkward entering uninvited like this, but the circumstances do warrant it.] Hello? Anyone? There's no answer, and the entry hallway is bare. There's a certain sense of deja vu here, much like the day Kiyoko gave birth to Kinu... Oh. Down the hallway and up to the cabin's second floor, taking the steps two at a time. The verdant balcony has definitely changed since the first time you were up here — as you push aside the shoji screen door, you note that morning glories and other flowering vines have grown around the beams and along the walls, adding their fragrance to that of the potted plants and miniature trees. That observation, though, is quickly washed away by the sight of Kinu lying on the ground in a futon, a blanket pulled up all the way to her slight nose. Eyes closed and face flushed, your daughter is lying still, more still than you've ever seen her before — if not for the flush of her face and her slight breathing under the thin blanket, it might be possible to imagine her dead - — No, what are you thinking? Perched on a stool and bent over your daughter is Kiyoko, dipping her fingers into a small bowl of water and drizzling it gently on Kinu's face. As you step through the door and approach, the little kitsune's screws up, and she begins to rock her head from side to side on the pillow, mewling — the sight manages to be even more miserable than her lying deathly still. "Kinu, what's the matter? Does it hurt?" Kiyoko fusses over Kinu for a bit, then looks up and notices you. "Oh, [pc.name], Keros be praised! I was hoping you'd come, and there you are!" What's going on here? "Our daughter is quite ill. She's running a terrible fever, and all her energy's left her." And... um... Kiyoko looks away. "So long as it doesn't get worse, she won't be in any danger. I'm not too experienced at these things, but I do know something. Nevertheless, she's still absolutely enervated and miserable." Does she know what caused this? While Kinu's not exactly the hardiest of kits, neither is she prone to falling ill for no good reason. Kiyoko shakes her head. "Truth be told, I have none. It started three days ago; so far I've just been trying to treat the symptoms and let the sickness run its course without worsening any further.[kiyoko.numKits 4| At least the other kits have promised to be good while their big sister is ill, so I don't have to worry about them running amok without supervision. Maybe I should know better than to take them at their word, but I can't really do anything about it anyway.]" You see. Is there anything you can do to help? "I've got some herbal medicine brewing over a low fire for some hours now. Could you watch our daughter for a moment while I go bring it up?" Oh, you can do as much. In fact, that's probably the least you can do. "Nevertheless, it's appreciated. I'll be right back; please keep a close eye on Kinu." With that, Kiyoko stands, stretches her limbs, and heads out the door, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] trailing behind her. If your daughter looks miserable, then her mother is just as harried, her hair and fur unbrushed and all in tangles. The door slides shut, leaving you alone with Kinu and the calm atmosphere of the open balcony and all its verdance. Cautiously, you reach out with a hand and stroke Kinu on the forehead just below her hairline. As expected, it's pretty hot. Your daughter's eyelids flutter, but don't open as you dip your palm into the water bowl and daub her cheeks. "[kinu.Dad]..." Kinu's voice is barely above a whisper, so soft that you have to lean in her hear her speak. "Am I going to die?" What?! No, of course not! Her mother said she's going to be fine. "I feel like I'm going to die." Nonsense. No one who has died has returned to tell the tale, so she can't possibly say that for sure. Besides, those are words one shouldn't bandy about lightly. "I know. I'm not permitted to die. People would be sad if I'm not around anymore." Silly kit. She doesn't just exist for the sake of other people. Considering the needs of those around her is important, yes, but doesn't she herself have a reason to go on regardless? Silence. And then, "I'm not sure anymore. I'm such a failure." Failure at what? "At both archery and the naginata." Wait, what? Oh. Oh. It's then that realization dawns. Her mother's — and subsequently your own — attempts at giving Kinu martial training must have been the first time in your daughter's life that she's been unable to pick up a skill with that trademark instinctive ease of hers. For someone who's never really experienced actual, meaningful failure before, it must cut deep — sure, it's not as if her mother has never chastised or corrected her in the past, but for Kinu to be self-aware of it is on another level altogether. For someone who practically defined herself by this very talent, the experience must have struck at the core of her identity. In a strange way, it's a reason to be proud of your daughter. Another kit — no, even an adult — might have lied to oneself, said it was just a fluke, that things didn't matter, that the goal wasn't worth it and was never wanted anyway. Kinu faced the full reality of her situation head-on — and was utterly crushed by it. No matter how intelligent she is... she's still a child with the wisdom of such; little wonder she couldn't cope to the point where she actually fell ill because of it. And with the expectations placed on her, both by Kiyoko and more importantly, herself, it makes complete sense that she wouldn't have told her mother anything. Oh, what a child. What a stupid, stupid child. Both in a good way, and a bad way. "What if I've lost my touch? What if I can't do anything any more? Or I have to learn something I absolutely must, and don't get it done in time? So many people will be depending on me." You sigh, pat Kinu on the head, and tell your daughter that she's going to make it. She just needs to apply herself — not necessarily harder, but more efficiently. She'll get it in the end, and it's not just her mother who'll help her in any way she can, but you as well. "..." Now, she should save her strength and not talk so much, okay? You'll be here for as long as you can, until you have to return to the waking world. "...I feel like I can tell you things I can't really speak to Mama about, [kinu.Dad]." It's then that the shoji screen slides open once more, Kiyoko stepping in with a large clay cup of bitter-smelling brown-green liquid. She sets the cup down on the stool she was sitting on, then gives you a nod. "Help me sit her up so I can administer her medicine." Your foxy wife sighs and wipes her brow. "All the ways I can bend this realm to my liking, and yet I can't wish for my daughter to be healthy again." You unroll the blanket from Kinu's body, and grimace at how sweat-soaked her nightgown and fur are. Kinu's limp body feels like a rag doll in your hands as Kiyoko and you ease her into a sitting position against the wall, her three tails wrapped about herself; Kiyoko kneels down by the futon, cup in hand, and raises it to Kinu's lips. "There, there... drink up and get better soon, okay?" Another child might have balked, but Kinu either doesn't have the strength or doesn't care enough to resist her mother tipping the thin, bitter liquid down her throat. Once she's done, you lie her back down in the futon, and Kiyoko covers her with the blanket once more. With that out of the way, that seems to be the extent of things for the moment; Kinu's ears are hot to the touch, but you stroke them softly until your daughter is sound asleep. "That's all that I can do for her at the moment," Kiyoko says, watching Kinu's thin blanket rise and fall gently with her breathing. "Medicine wasn't something I really devoted my time to — I'd never imagined people could even get ill in the Astral Plane." Perhaps not in the normal way, but your guess is that Kinu's illness is a reflection of whatever trouble has gripped her heart. That's all that can be done... or is it? Is there something you could do to help Kinu recover faster?
rows.translation: 再一次，你的梦境将你带到了那个熟悉的场景：阳光洒满的山顶，以及矗立在山顶上的那棵巨大的樱花树。不过，奇怪的是，周围竟然没有人。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|即使清子本人并没有外出活动，你们的那些狐族后裔应该会到处跑来跑去，闹出一些动静来吧。某个地方和平固然很好，但有点太这里很宁静。 |通常至少会有一些那种四处游历的生活方式，即使不是清子本人也在经历着。] 你有些担心，便在山顶和桃树林里寻找小娟的踪迹，但女儿依然不见踪影。这时，你只能去检查小屋了。步行几分钟后，你来到了小屋门前，推门走了进去。 [pc.isDK|他们毕竟没有锁上它，所以，如果这可以算作一种邀请的话……那简直就是再明确不过的邀请了。|这样不请自来的确有点尴尬，但目前的情形确实有必要这样做。] 喂？有人在吗？ 没有回应，入口处的走廊空荡荡的。这里给人一种似曾相识的感觉，就像清子生下堇的那天一样…… 哦。 沿着走廊向上走，来到小屋的二楼，一步跨上两级台阶。自从你第一次来到这个绿意盎然的阳台以来，这里确实发生了变化——当你推开障子门时，你会注意到牵牛花和其他开花藤蔓已经爬满了横梁和墙壁，它们的芬芳与那些盆栽植物和小型树木的气息交织在了一起。然而，这一观察很快就被眼前的景象冲淡了：小娟躺在榻子上，毯子一直拉到了她微微凸起的鼻子上。她闭着眼睛，脸庞通红，一动不动地躺着，这种安静程度是你从未见过的——要不是她脸上那抹红晕，以及被薄毯子遮住的微弱呼吸声，你甚至可能会以为她已经去世了。 不，你在想什么啊？”坐在凳子上、弯下腰照顾女儿的清子，正用手指蘸取一小碗水，轻轻洒在小娟的脸上。当你走进门走近时，那只小狐妖立刻紧张起来，开始在枕头上左右摇晃着头，发出呜咽声——这一幕看起来，甚至比它之前一动不动地躺着还要可怜。 纪夫，怎么了？疼吗？清子忙了一会儿照顾犬，然后抬头看到了你。哦， [pc.name]凯罗斯，真是太感谢你了！我本来就希望你能来，而你果然出现了！ 这里发生了什么？ 我们的女儿病得很重，她发高烧，而且已经完全没有力气了。 然后……嗯…… 清子把目光移开了。只要情况不恶化，她就不会有危险。我在这些事情上经验不多，但总归还是懂一些的。不过，她现在确实非常焦虑和痛苦。 她知道这是由什么引起的吗？虽然小娟并不是最强壮的角色，但她也不会无缘无故地生病。 清子摇了摇头。说实话，我没有任何有效的办法。这种情况开始于三天前，到目前为止，我只是在尝试缓解症状，让这种病自然发展，以免病情进一步恶化。[kiyoko.numKits 4| 至少其他那些小工具在它们“大姐”生病的时候承诺会表现得很好，这样我就不用担心它们会在无人监管的情况下乱来。也许我本应该更谨慎一些，不该轻信它们的承诺，但实际上我也无能为力啊。]" 你看，有没有什么办法可以帮助我呢？ 我已经在小火上熬制这些草药好几个小时了。你能帮忙照看一下我们的女儿吗？我马上就去把药取出来。 哦，你完全可以这么做。事实上，这恐怕是最起码该做的。 尽管如此，我还是非常感激。我马上回来，请大家密切关注小娟的情况。 说完之后，清子站了起来，活动了一下四肢，然后走出了门去。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 跟在她身后。如果你的女儿看起来很痛苦，那么她的母亲肯定也同样疲惫不堪，她的头发和毛发都乱糟糟的，没有梳理过。门缓缓关上了，将你和小娟留在了开阔的阳台上，那里空气宁静，绿意盎然。 你小心翼翼地伸出手，轻轻抚摸着小娟发际线以下的额头。正如你所预料的，那里的温度相当高。你女儿的眼皮微微颤动，但并没有睁开眼睛。你将手掌浸入水碗中，然后轻轻抹在她的脸颊上。 "[kinu.Dad]..."小娟的声音几乎低得只能算是在耳语，如此轻柔，以至于你必须凑近她的耳边才能听清她在说什么。我会死吗？ 什么？！不，当然不会！她妈妈说她不会有事的。 我觉得自己快要死了。 胡说八道。没有人会拥有已经死去的人回来了，亲自讲述了这段故事，所以她不可能确定地说出那种话。更何况，这些话可不是可以轻易说出口的。 我知道。我不能死。如果我不在了，大家会很难过的。 愚蠢的想法。她存在的意义并不仅仅是为了别人。考虑周围人的需求固然重要，但难道她自己就没有继续前行的理由吗？ 沉默。然后， 我现在也不确定了。我真是个失败者。 在什么事情上失败了？ 在射箭和薙刀使用方面都是如此。 等等，什么？ 哦。 哦。 就在这时，我突然明白了：她母亲——以及后来你也尝试过的——让小娟接受武术训练，想必是你女儿有生以来第一次无法以她那种与生俱来的轻松自如的方式掌握一项技能。对于一个从未真正经历过真正意义上的失败的人来说，这种打击肯定非常沉重。当然，她的母亲过去也曾经批评过她、纠正过她的错误，但小娟能够意识到这一点，确实说明她的自我认知能力已经达到了一个全新的水平。对于一个几乎将自己的人生价值完全建立在这一天赋之上的人来说，这样的经历无疑触动了她身份认同的核心。 从某种角度来看，这正是值得为女儿感到骄傲的理由。换作其他普通人，甚至是一个成年人，也可能会欺骗自己，认为自己只是运气好而已，认为这些事情并不重要，认为这个目标并不值得追求，甚至从来就没有真正想要过它。小娟不得不直面自己处境的全部现实——而这一现实令她彻底崩溃了。无论她多么聪明……她终究还是个孩子，拥有着孩子应有的认知水平；难怪她会因此而无法应对，甚至因此生病了。考虑到基代子对她的期望，更重要的是，她自己所设定的期望，她没有告诉母亲任何事情，这一点完全是可以理解的。 哦，多么孩子气啊……多么愚蠢、多么天真烂漫的孩子啊。都是以积极的方式。以及一种糟糕的方式。 要是我已经失去了那份能力怎么办？要是我再什么也做不了怎么办？又或者，我有必须要学习的东西，但却没能及时完成，那该怎么办？会有那么多人依赖着我啊。 你叹了口气，轻拍着小娟的脑袋，对女儿说她一定能够成功。她只需要更加努力一些——不一定非得更加拼命，而是要更加高效地付出努力。最终她一定会成功的，而且不仅她的母亲会尽一切可能帮助她，你也会伸出援手。 "..." 现在，她应该节省体力，少说点话，好吗？你会在这里待尽可能长的时间，直到不得不回到现实世界为止。 ……我觉得我可以跟你说一些我实在无法跟妈妈倾诉的事情。 [kinu.Dad]." 就在这时，障子门再次被拉开，清子走进来，手里拿着一个装着散发着苦味的棕绿色液体的大陶杯。她把杯子放在自己坐着的凳子上，然后向你点了点头。 帮我把她扶坐起来，这样我就能给她服药了。你那位狡黠的妻子叹了口气，然后擦了擦额头。我可以用各种方法让这个世界按照我的意愿运转，但却无法让我的女儿恢复健康。 你将毯子从小娟的身体上掀开，看到她的睡衣和毛皮都浸满了汗水，不禁皱起了眉头。小娟的身体软弱无力，就像一个布偶一样，你在清子的帮助下，把她扶着靠在墙上坐好，她的三条尾巴紧紧地缠在身上；清子则跪在榻榻米旁，用手捧起水杯，将水送到小娟的嘴边。 来，来……把药喝完，很快就会好起来的，好吗？ 另一个孩子可能会反抗，但小娟要么没有力气，要么根本不在乎，所以她没有抗拒母亲将那种稀薄而苦涩的液体灌进她喉咙里。等这一切完成后，你把她重新放回蒲团上，清子又用毯子把她盖好。就这样，目前看来事情似乎就到此为止了；小娟的耳朵摸起来很烫，但你轻轻抚摸着她，直到她熟睡为止。 目前，我能为她做的就只有这些了。清子看着纪久的薄毯子随着她的呼吸轻轻起伏，说道。医学其实并不是我真正投入过多精力的领域——我从未想过在星界中人们也会生病。 或许不是以常规的方式，但你可以猜测，小娟的病情其实反映了她内心所面临的那些困扰。目前我们能做的也就只有这些了……真的吗？难道就没有什么办法可以帮助小娟更快地康复吗？
rows.raw: " Once more, your dreams coalesce into the familiar surroundings of the sunlit hilltop and the gigantic cherry blossom tree perched atop it. Odd, though, that there's no one around. [kiyoko.numKits 4|Even if Kiyoko herself isn't out and about, some of your kitsune children should be running around and creating some kind of ruckus somewhere. Peace is fine, but it's a little too peaceful around here. |There's usually at least some kind of life out and about, even if it's not Kiyoko herself.] A little worried, you check the hilltop and peach grove for any sign of Kinu, but neither is your daughter anywhere to be found. Nothing left for it but to check the cabin; a few minutes' walk has you up to the door, and you let yourself in. [pc.isDK|They left it unlocked, after all, so that's an invitation if you ever saw one.|It's a little awkward entering uninvited like this, but the circumstances do warrant it.] Hello? Anyone? There's no answer, and the entry hallway is bare. There's a certain sense of deja vu here, much like the day Kiyoko gave birth to Kinu... Oh. Down the hallway and up to the cabin's second floor, taking the steps two at a time. The verdant balcony has definitely changed since the first time you were up here — as you push aside the shoji screen door, you note that morning glories and other flowering vines have grown around the beams and along the walls, adding their fragrance to that of the potted plants and miniature trees. That observation, though, is quickly washed away by the sight of Kinu lying on the ground in a futon, a blanket pulled up all the way to her slight nose. Eyes closed and face flushed, your daughter is lying still, more still than you've ever seen her before — if not for the flush of her face and her slight breathing under the thin blanket, it might be possible to imagine her dead - — No, what are you thinking? Perched on a stool and bent over your daughter is Kiyoko, dipping her fingers into a small bowl of water and drizzling it gently on Kinu's face. As you step through the door and approach, the little kitsune's screws up, and she begins to rock her head from side to side on the pillow, mewling — the sight manages to be even more miserable than her lying deathly still. "Kinu, what's the matter? Does it hurt?" Kiyoko fusses over Kinu for a bit, then looks up and notices you. "Oh, [pc.name], Keros be praised! I was hoping you'd come, and there you are!" What's going on here? "Our daughter is quite ill. She's running a terrible fever, and all her energy's left her." And... um... Kiyoko looks away. "So long as it doesn't get worse, she won't be in any danger. I'm not too experienced at these things, but I do know something. Nevertheless, she's still absolutely enervated and miserable." Does she know what caused this? While Kinu's not exactly the hardiest of kits, neither is she prone to falling ill for no good reason. Kiyoko shakes her head. "Truth be told, I have none. It started three days ago; so far I've just been trying to treat the symptoms and let the sickness run its course without worsening any further.[kiyoko.numKits 4| At least the other kits have promised to be good while their big sister is ill, so I don't have to worry about them running amok without supervision. Maybe I should know better than to take them at their word, but I can't really do anything about it anyway.]" You see. Is there anything you can do to help? "I've got some herbal medicine brewing over a low fire for some hours now. Could you watch our daughter for a moment while I go bring it up?" Oh, you can do as much. In fact, that's probably the least you can do. "Nevertheless, it's appreciated. I'll be right back; please keep a close eye on Kinu." With that, Kiyoko stands, stretches her limbs, and heads out the door, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] trailing behind her. If your daughter looks miserable, then her mother is just as harried, her hair and fur unbrushed and all in tangles. The door slides shut, leaving you alone with Kinu and the calm atmosphere of the open balcony and all its verdance. Cautiously, you reach out with a hand and stroke Kinu on the forehead just below her hairline. As expected, it's pretty hot. Your daughter's eyelids flutter, but don't open as you dip your palm into the water bowl and daub her cheeks. "[kinu.Dad]..." Kinu's voice is barely above a whisper, so soft that you have to lean in her hear her speak. "Am I going to die?" What?! No, of course not! Her mother said she's going to be fine. "I feel like I'm going to die." Nonsense. No one who has died has returned to tell the tale, so she can't possibly say that for sure. Besides, those are words one shouldn't bandy about lightly. "I know. I'm not permitted to die. People would be sad if I'm not around anymore." Silly kit. She doesn't just exist for the sake of other people. Considering the needs of those around her is important, yes, but doesn't she herself have a reason to go on regardless? Silence. And then, "I'm not sure anymore. I'm such a failure." Failure at what? "At both archery and the naginata." Wait, what? Oh. Oh. It's then that realization dawns. Her mother's — and subsequently your own — attempts at giving Kinu martial training must have been the first time in your daughter's life that she's been unable to pick up a skill with that trademark instinctive ease of hers. For someone who's never really experienced actual, meaningful failure before, it must cut deep — sure, it's not as if her mother has never chastised or corrected her in the past, but for Kinu to be self-aware of it is on another level altogether. For someone who practically defined herself by this very talent, the experience must have struck at the core of her identity. In a strange way, it's a reason to be proud of your daughter. Another kit — no, even an adult — might have lied to oneself, said it was just a fluke, that things didn't matter, that the goal wasn't worth it and was never wanted anyway. Kinu faced the full reality of her situation head-on — and was utterly crushed by it. No matter how intelligent she is... she's still a child with the wisdom of such; little wonder she couldn't cope to the point where she actually fell ill because of it. And with the expectations placed on her, both by Kiyoko and more importantly, herself, it makes complete sense that she wouldn't have told her mother anything. Oh, what a child. What a stupid, stupid child. Both in a good way, and a bad way. "What if I've lost my touch? What if I can't do anything any more? Or I have to learn something I absolutely must, and don't get it done in time? So many people will be depending on me." You sigh, pat Kinu on the head, and tell your daughter that she's going to make it. She just needs to apply herself — not necessarily harder, but more efficiently. She'll get it in the end, and it's not just her mother who'll help her in any way she can, but you as well. "..." Now, she should save her strength and not talk so much, okay? You'll be here for as long as you can, until you have to return to the waking world. "...I feel like I can tell you things I can't really speak to Mama about, [kinu.Dad]." It's then that the shoji screen slides open once more, Kiyoko stepping in with a large clay cup of bitter-smelling brown-green liquid. She sets the cup down on the stool she was sitting on, then gives you a nod. "Help me sit her up so I can administer her medicine." Your foxy wife sighs and wipes her brow. "All the ways I can bend this realm to my liking, and yet I can't wish for my daughter to be healthy again." You unroll the blanket from Kinu's body, and grimace at how sweat-soaked her nightgown and fur are. Kinu's limp body feels like a rag doll in your hands as Kiyoko and you ease her into a sitting position against the wall, her three tails wrapped about herself; Kiyoko kneels down by the futon, cup in hand, and raises it to Kinu's lips. "There, there... drink up and get better soon, okay?" Another child might have balked, but Kinu either doesn't have the strength or doesn't care enough to resist her mother tipping the thin, bitter liquid down her throat. Once she's done, you lie her back down in the futon, and Kiyoko covers her with the blanket once more. With that out of the way, that seems to be the extent of things for the moment; Kinu's ears are hot to the touch, but you stroke them softly until your daughter is sound asleep. "That's all that I can do for her at the moment," Kiyoko says, watching Kinu's thin blanket rise and fall gently with her breathing. "Medicine wasn't something I really devoted my time to — I'd never imagined people could even get ill in the Astral Plane." Perhaps not in the normal way, but your guess is that Kinu's illness is a reflection of whatever trouble has gripped her heart. That's all that can be done... or is it? Is there something you could do to help Kinu recover faster?"

rows.original: You draw the wyldsap from your possessions, palming the small vial in your hand. A flash of hesitation passes over you, but you shake it off — this stuff might be precious and hard to come by, but it's your daughter's health that's in the balance here. Kiyoko looks pensive as she studies the vial of wyldsap. "I know what this is, yes — some of Velun's creatures used it back when — when I was out in the world. A powerful restorative, to say the least." She's not wrong. This is too strong for a child as-is; she'll have to dilute it before letting Kinu have any. Kiyoko nods. "I concur. I'll mix a drop or two in when I next give her something to drink." Looking down at Kinu, that shouldn't be long by the way your daughter is sweating. "Don't worry about it, I'll keep her hydrated. No harm'll come to her on my watch."
rows.translation: 你从自己的物品中取出了那种名为“野性之液”的物质，将小瓶子握在手中。心中闪过一丝犹豫，但你很快将其抛到脑后——这种东西或许十分珍贵且难以获得，但此刻，你女儿的健康才是最重要的。 清子凝视着那小瓶子，神情显得十分深思。我知道这是什么，没错——在我还在外面的时候，维伦的一些生物就用过它。至少可以说，这是一种非常有效的恢复剂。 她说得没错。对于一个孩子来说，这种浓度实在太高了；在让纪久服用之前，必须先稀释它。 清子点了点头。我同意。下次给她喝东西的时候，我会加上一两滴。 看着小娟，以你女儿现在出汗的程度来看，应该不会太久了。 别担心，我会确保她保持水分补充。在我照看她的期间，她绝对不会受到任何伤害。

I'll mix a drop or two in when I next give her something to drink." Looking down at Kinu, that shouldn't be long by the way your daughter is sweating. "Don't worry about it, I'll keep her hydrated. rows.original: Kiyoko looks a little uncertain when you hold out the small bundle of winterstem to her. "And this is..." A local relaxant and minor restorative. You're not sure how much it'll actually help with the illness itself, but at the least Kinu will be able to rest well. Kiyoko pauses, perhaps pondering whether mixing treatments would be wise, but worry and desperation clearly win over caution and she accepts the herb from you. Under your direction, your foxy wife brings in a small censer to burn the winterstem in, and before long pale white smoke rises into the room, bringing with it a sensation of calm soothing. Can she feel it? "Mhm. It's not altogether unpleasant." As one, the both of you turn to Kinu. No, there's no miraculous recovery — not that you were expecting one anyway — but at least your kitsune daughter is breathing easier with winterstem smoke suffusing the room. The balcony is well-ventilated, so there shouldn't be any issue with leaving the censer in a corner and letting it burn out; the winterstem you have there should be good for a few hours or so. "It certainly seems effective enough," Kiyoko says after checking over Kinu. "To be frank, it's making me sleepy too..."
rows.translation: 当你把那小包冬茎递给清子时，她看起来有些犹豫不决。而这就是…… 这是一种具有舒缓作用且能帮助恢复体力的草药。你不确定它对治疗疾病本身能起到多大的作用，但至少能让小娟得到充分的休息。 清子停顿了一下，可能在考虑是否应该将多种治疗方法结合使用，但忧虑与绝望最终战胜了她的谨慎，她还是接受了你递给她的这种草药。在您的指示下，您那位机智的妻子拿来一个小香炉，用来焚烧冬草。不久之后，淡白色的烟雾便弥漫在整个房间里，带来一种宁静而舒缓的感觉。 她能感受到这种气息吗？ 嗯，也不算太糟糕。 你们俩一起转向小娟。不，并没有什么奇迹般的康复——反正你们也没指望会有这样的结果——但至少，当房间里弥漫着冬茎的烟雾时，你们的狐妖女儿呼吸似乎变得顺畅了一些。阳台的通风条件很好，所以把香炉放在角落里让它慢慢燃烧应该不会有任何问题；你们准备的冬茎应该可以燃烧好几个小时吧。 这确实看起来非常有效。清子检查完纪久之后说道。说实话，这也让我觉得有点困……

rows.original: Yes. If magic works here, then perhaps you could help your daughter with your powers. Given the nature of her malady, it probably won't be possible to outright cure her, but at least some of the symptoms can be alleviated while she makes a recovery. Kiyoko frowns. "The nature of her malady? Is there something you know that I don't, [pc.name]?" You'll explain later. For now, you ought to tend to your daughter. "Yes. Yes, of course. If you would, please — healing magic was never my forte, it'll be interesting to see you at work." You nod, roll up your sleeves, then uncover the blanket from Kinu. She lets out a quiet whimper as you place your hands on her chest but is otherwise still, not having much energy to do anything else. The moment you begin channelling power into her, your suspicions are proven right; there's no way you can simply wish this illness of hers away, and even if you did she'd just relapse if the underlying root cause isn't addressed. Furthermore, applying your healing magics on Kinu makes you feel most odd — whether it's because of the nature of this place, Kinu herself or some other reason, you're not completely sure. Nevertheless, the spell appears to work as intended. You move your hands over Kinu's tiny form, soothing aches and alleviating some of your daughter's misery; she struggles and squirms for a bit, trying to get away from you, but eventually seems to realize that the foreign magic isn't a threat and her instincts settle down. At the end of it all, Kinu looks more comfortable, sweat no longer beading on her forehead as she breathes easier. You haven't cured your daughter, but at least she'll be able to rest easier and get some undisturbed sleep, which should help a lot.
rows.translation: 是的。如果魔法在这里真的有效的话，或许你可以用你的力量帮助你的女儿。考虑到她所患疾病的性质，或许无法彻底治愈她，但至少可以在她康复的过程中缓解一些症状。 清子皱起了眉头。她所患疾病的性质究竟如何？是否有什么你知道而我不知道的事情？ [pc.name]?" 你稍后再解释吧。现在，你应该去照顾你的女儿。 是的，当然可以。如果您愿意的话，请便——治疗魔法从来都不是我的强项，看看您是如何运用的，一定会很有意思。 你点了点头，卷起袖子，然后掀开了覆盖在小娟身上的毯子。当你将手放在她的胸前时，她轻轻地发出了一声呜咽，但除此之外，她依然一动不动，几乎没有力气做任何事情。当你开始将力量输送到她体内时，你的怀疑得到了证实——你不可能仅仅通过许愿就能让她摆脱这种疾病，而且，如果根本原因没有得到解决，即使你暂时让她恢复了健康，她也会再次发病。此外，对小娟使用治愈魔法会让你感到非常奇怪——无论是因为这个地方的特殊性质、小娟本身的原因，还是其他什么原因，你都无法完全确定。 不过，这个魔法似乎确实起到了预期的效果。你将双手放在小娟娇小的身上，轻轻抚摸，缓解她身上的疼痛，减轻她的一些不适；她起初挣扎着想要逃离你的怀抱，但最终似乎意识到这种陌生的魔法并不会对她造成威胁，她的紧张情绪也逐渐平息下来。 最终，小娟看起来舒服多了，额头上不再有汗珠，呼吸也变得顺畅了。你虽然没能治愈你的女儿，但至少她现在可以安心休息，获得一些不受打扰的睡眠，这应该会对她有所帮助。

rows.original: You think about it for a moment, then shake your head. Kiyoko knows what she's doing here, and besides, you've heard all kinds of stories about potions mixing and creating all kinds of interesting effects, to say the least. If she asks you for anything, you'd be glad to help, but not meddling with your daughter's treatment unnecessarily would be the best thing for her right now.
rows.translation: 你想了想，然后摇了摇头。清子知道自己在这里要做什么，而且，你也听说过很多关于药剂混合后会产生各种有趣效果的故事。如果她需要你的帮助，你当然会乐意帮忙，但此刻，最重要的是不要不必要的干扰你女儿的治疗过程。
rows.raw: "\n    You think about it for a moment, then shake your head. Kiyoko knows what she's doing here, and besides, you've heard all kinds of stories about potions mixing and creating all kinds of interesting effects, to say the least. If she asks you for anything, you'd be glad to help, but not meddling with your daughter's treatment unnecessarily would be the best thing for her right now."

rows.original: There is one more thing you'd like to bring up, though. "Yes? What is it?" Look, you understand that Kiyoko's the one spending the bulk of the time with Kinu here, that she's the one feeding, clothing and educating your daughter when all you're able to do is come in, play with her and spoil her rotten. But even so... between her education and duties as the firstborn daughter, couldn't a little more time be made for her to be a child? Kiyoko looks a little guilty, but also unsure at the same time, chewing on her lip as she thinks. "It really ebbs and flows, to be honest. That day you caught us having that tiff over her martial education, she was being a difficult little thing; in the days that ensued, she took herself more seriously than ever. I keep on having to adjust to the push-pull of her demands; but I'd wager that she's just as hard on herself than I am, if not more — when she's in the mood for such, at any rate." But will she at least make sure that Kinu gets some play and rest in? "Play isn't any good if it isn't heartfelt," Kiyoko replies with a sigh. "But I can enforce more rest upon her if necessary." And more importantly... she needs to know that just because she doesn't immediately pick something up, it doesn't mean her worth as a person or the station she holds is diminished in any way. Kiyoko stops and stares at you. "Now what makes you think that?" You briefly outline the conversation you had with Kinu when she was downstairs preparing Kinu's medicine. Kiyoko's consternation only grows as you recount Kinu's words, and then she finally sighs and rubs her temples with the heel of her palms. "Oh, my child. My stupid, stupid, adorable child. Whatever am I going to do with you?" She sighs again and daubs more water on her daughter's forehead, making the little kitsune kit mewl and roll over on the futon. You have no doubt that she's had plenty of lectures from her mother, but this is the first time she's ever faced any true adversity from the world itself, isn't it? As beautiful as it is and despite Kiyoko's best efforts, a paradise like what the Astral Plane is isn't the ideal place to raise resilient kits. At the very least, the experience will be good for Kinu when she pulls through; hopefully she'll take this lesson to heart. She needs not to only encounter true setbacks — as hard as that might be for someone as talented as she is — but also overcome them on her own. "It's a fine line we're walking as parents here," Kiyoko says with another small sigh. She snaps her fingers, and a gentle breeze begins to waft through the balcony, cool and refreshing. "But—" Your foxy wife's words cut off as she yawns and stretches, catches herself, then looks apologetically at you. Gods, how much sleep has she had lately? "Enough." No, no, this won't do at all. At least you know which side of the family Kinu gets her workaholic streak from. She's going to take one of those pillows from the racks and have a lie-down, even if it's on the floor. You'll keep an eye on Kinu for as long as you can, until you're forced to leave. If she's going to be nursing Kinu for the foreseeable future, she's going to need some proper rest of her own. Kiyoko opens her mouth as if to protest, then thinks better of it and pulls down a pillow like you said. She certainly has no problems dozing off on the floor, curling into a ball about the pillow, [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails tucked about her. Finally. All's good and well, or at least, as well as they can be. [kiyoko.numKits 4|Hopefully the other kits will be able to not create a terrible mess or get into trouble when both their mother and big sister are out of commission, but if Kiyoko went on for much longer like this she might have very well fallen ill herself, and then where would everyone be?] Mother and daughter alike asleep before you — come to think of it, you've never actually seen them sleeping, have you? They look so adorable as a pair, and the resemblance is there. Ha... You're not sure how long you keep vigil for — hours seem to pass like minutes while you sit by Kinu's side, or perhaps it's minutes that seem to pass like hours. But by and large the world around you begins to fade, and you feel drowsier and drowsier... ... Until you come to once more, this time in the waking world. Hopefully they'll be all right until you can visit them once more...
rows.translation: 不过，你还有一件事想要提一下。 嗯？什么事？ 你看，你明明知道在这里，大部分时间都是清子在陪着小娟，是她在照顾你的女儿，给她提供食物、衣物，还教育她；而你所能做的，只是偶尔过来陪她玩玩，宠溺她而已。但即便如此……考虑到她要接受教育，还要承担作为长女的责任，难道就不能为她留出一点时间，让她好好享受一下童年的快乐吗？ 清子看起来有些内疚，同时又显得很不确定，她咬着嘴唇思考着。说实话，这种情况确实时好时坏。那天你看到我们因为她的武术训练问题发生了争执，当时她确实表现得非常固执；而在之后的几天里，她却比以往任何时候都更加严格要求自己。我一直在努力适应她这些反复无常的要求；但可以肯定的是，至少在她有这种想法的时候，她对自己要求的严格程度丝毫不亚于我，甚至可能更甚。 但至少，她会不会确保小娟有足够的时间去玩耍和休息呢？ 如果游戏缺乏真诚的态度，那就毫无意义了。清子叹了口气作为回应。但如果有必要，我完全可以要求她多休息一些。 更重要的是……她需要明白，即使她不能立刻理解某些事情，也不意味着她的个人价值或她所担任的职位会因此而降低。 清子停了下来，直视着你的眼睛。那么，是什么让你这么认为的呢？那个?" 你简要描述了当小娟在楼下准备她的药物时，你们之间的对话。当你复述小娟说过的话时，清子的担忧只会越来越深，最后她终于叹了口气，用手掌的背面揉了揉太阳穴。 哦，我的孩子。我这个愚蠢又可爱的孩子……我到底该拿你怎么办呢？她又叹了口气，又在女儿的额头上抹了些水，这让小狐妖发出呜咽声，然后在榻子上翻了个身。 毫无疑问，她肯定已经听过了母亲无数次的训斥，但这一次，她却是第一次真正面对来自外界的困境，不是吗？尽管它如此美丽，也尽管清子付出了种种努力，但像星界这样的天堂并不适合培养坚韧不拔的孩子。至少，当小娟最终挺过这一关时，这段经历会对她有所帮助；希望她能认真吸取这个教训。她不仅需要面对真正的挫折——对于她这样才华横溢的人来说，这无疑是非常艰难的——而且还要独自战胜这些挫折。 作为父母，我们此刻正走在一条非常微妙的道路上。清子又轻轻叹了口气，然后打了个响指，一阵轻柔的微风便开始在阳台上拂动，清凉而宜人。但是—— 你那位狡黠的妻子突然打了个哈欠，伸了个懒腰，随即意识到自己的行为，便歉意地望着你。天啊，她最近到底睡了多少觉啊？ 够了。 不行，这样绝对不行。至少你应该知道，小娟的这种工作狂习性是从家族的哪一方遗传来的。她肯定会从架子上拿一个枕头来躺下休息，哪怕只是躺在地板上也好。你尽量多留一会儿，直到不得不离开为止，一定要照看好小娟。如果她在可预见的未来都要继续给小娟喂奶，那么她自己也需要好好休息才行。 清子张了张嘴，似乎想提出反对，但转念一想，还是照你说的那样拿了一个枕头过来。她完全可以在地板上蜷缩成一团，轻松地睡着。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 她的尾巴紧紧地贴在身体两侧。 终于，一切都好了，或者至少已经达到了最好的状态。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|希望其他角色在他们的“母亲”和“姐姐”都无法正常发挥作用时，也不会弄得一团糟或惹上麻烦。但如果纪代子继续这样下去，她自己也很可能会生病，到那时大家又会陷入怎样的困境呢？] 在你之前，母女俩都已经睡着了——仔细想想，你其实从来都没有真正见过她们。睡眠状态你有没有注意到？它们成对在一起看起来真是太可爱了，而且确实有那么几分相似之处呢……哈…… 你也不清楚自己究竟守了多久——当你坐在小娟身边时，几个小时仿佛就像几分钟一样飞快地过去了；而反过来，几分钟也可能感觉像几个小时那么漫长。不过，总的来说，你周围的世界开始逐渐变得模糊不清，你也变得越来越困倦…… ……直到你再次醒来，这一次是在清醒的世界里。希望等到你再次去看它们时，它们一切都还好吧……

rows.original: The dark fog of dreamless sleep slowly recedes from your mind, and once more the warm sunlight of the Astral Plane meets your [pc.skinFurScales]. You open your eyes, finding yourself at the edge of the clearing where hilltop meets forest, pick yourself up, and start at a brisk walk towards Kiyoko's cabin. Given how ill Kinu was the last time you visited, nothing's getting done here until you check in on her. You don't have to look for long, though. As you draw close to the hilltop, the shadow of the cherry blossom tree coming into view, Kinu's voice carries over the air to you. Wait, she's already well enough to be up and about? But she looked so sickly - "Good morning, [kinu.Dad]." You stop, sigh, and look down at your daughter. [kinu.kinuWeapon|Instead of a bladed spear — a naginata, that's what she called it the last time — in hand, Kinu has an imitation of such in the form of a bamboo pole, right down to the blade. A look of straight-faced determination etched on her features, she's imitating Kiyoko step by step as the two of them go through various forms with the polearm. |Your kitsune daughter is struggling under the weight of a large basket of white radishes, the wicker handles spread apart just so that she has to flex her little elbows in order to keep it off the ground as she trundles along. It would be comical, if not for the fact that the basket is half her size and filled to the brim.] All in all, while she's not vibrating on the spot and could stand to have better posture, at least she's not bedridden anymore. Slowly — perhaps almost bashfully — Kinu stops what she's doing and turns to face you, grinding the toes of one foot into the dirt. And how is she doing today? "I'm still a little sleepy... not to mention tired." Sleepy and tired will do just fine. She had both you and her mother worried for her life back there; it's good enough that she's standing and speaking to you. Time doesn't flow at the same rate inside the orb than it does on the outside, you know as much — how long has it been since you last visited? "About a week," Kiyoko replies with a nod. "It's not good for children to lie in bed for too long, but I've been careful to give her only light duties while she recovers. [kiyoko.numKits 4|No handling screaming kits, for one.]" Kinu folds her ears down against her head and looks at her feet. "I'm sorry to make you worry, [kinu.Dad]..." That doesn't matter — what does matter is that she's on the road to getting better. You note that she's getting to move around, at the very least. Fresh air should do her a world of good. Kinu still won't meet your gaze. [kinu.kinuWeapon|"Mama says that if I'm not strong enough yet to handle a full naginata, then I might as well use a bamboo one to go through the forms and practice while I get stronger in the arms. She spent all that time while I was ill putting one together from scratch..." Oh, that's just adorable. Kiyoko shrugs, a hint of a tired smile on her face. "I needed something to do while keeping vigil over our daughter. [kiyoko.numKits 4|The other children helped too, so you've got to give them credit for that.] Anything to take my mind off the fact that there wasn't much I could do about our daughter's state." Kinu squirms and looks extremely guilty. |"Mama says that if my arms aren't strong enough to handle the draw of a hankyu, I'm not going to be making any meaningful progress in archery. That's why she's got me carrying in the daikon from the vegetable patch..." "I'm planning to set her gradually heavier loads, when she's fully recovered. There's always need for someone to haul water up from the basement." "Mmmrrhh..." Kinu looks more resigned than resentful, but it's clear she's not particularly enthused about the prospect, even if she does appear to acknowledge its necessity.] Smiling, you kneel so that you're on eye level with your daughter, and embrace her in a big hug. That catches Kinu off-guard — the little kitsune squeaks and wriggles for a second or so, then snuggles up against you in a cuddle, all three of her tails wagging back and forth. There, that's much better, isn't it? Kinu says nothing, but buries her face against your body. You give her a few pats on the head, smoothing out the backs of her large, foxy ears, then finish up with a few brushes of her tails. Now, did she learn anything from this entire episode? "Um... I shouldn't get ill, because that will make people sad?" Well, that's true, but it's not the point that you wanted to press home here. There's no point beating up herself like this over her mistakes, because if she literally worries herself sick she's going to waste time that could be better spent on improving. Being aware of one's expectations is one thing and laudable in any child, but there's also being too hard on herself. For all that she may be assuming the responsibilities of an adult this early in life, she's still a kit, and her experience with the [kinu.kinuWeapon|spear|bow] proves as much. ...Well, and also that you and her mother would still love her even if she wasn't as talented as she was. So... while Kiyoko may be hard on her, simply failing doesn't mean she's diminished in any way because of that, it's what happens after that's important. Right? Kiyoko nods. "Quite so." For a whole handful of seconds, Kinu just absorbs this. Then, the sniffles begin, followed by the entire waterworks, as your daughter starts to blubber and wail, getting your [pc.armor] all wet and soppy with foxy tears. "I couldn't help it, [kinu.Dad]. If-if I wasn't the smart one, then who was I?" Why, she's Kinu. Her parents love her, [kiyoko.numKits 4|her brothers and sisters too, ]and experiences like these are how she discovers other facets of her personality and who she is. A sigh from Kiyoko. "While neither you nor I enjoyed this experience in the least, daughter, it's better that this happened early on, where we could watch over you, rather than at some critical juncture later in your life. Your [pc.mf|father|mother] was right in that your talents left you ill-equipped to deal with actual adversity of this nature." "Waaaaaaaah! I really thought I was going to die!" There, there. She's fine now. Gods, what a large emotional outburst coming from such a petite kit. You pet Kinu's silken fur for a little longer, only stopping when the little kitsune's sniffling ceases. Her eyes are all red and her face is wet, but she's still hugging you as ferociously as ever. Smiling, Kiyoko reaches down and pries the clingy little kit from you. "It seems like we're not going to be getting much done today, now that our daughter's emotions are all over the place. I think I've got some melons chilling in the basement river; why don't we all have some? That should settle her down enough so she'll actually be able to sleep by bedtime." That sounds like a magnificent idea. You'll go set up one of the parasols while they prepare the fruit. And so it happens that the rest of the day — or what passes for such here, anyway — is spent with your foxy wife and daughter, slicing apart melons and savouring them while making small talk. [kiyoko.numKits 4|Every now and then, one of Kinu's siblings will come up and beg for a slice of melon, which your daughter is more than happy to share. ]Just sitting and talking like this makes time seem to pass in the blink of an eye... Indeed, when you do leave, it's not a conscious thing. One moment you're debating mother and daughter alike on the merits of sweet over sour in one's choice of melons, and then the next you're blinking blearily in the light of the morning sun. Despite the abrupt departure, at least you're safe in the knowledge that Kinu is recovering her characteristic energy and spirit, even if she's not wholly there yet. But at least here and now, you've more of a reason to go out and face an increasingly corrupt world.

|你的九尾狐女儿正费力地拖着一大篮白萝卜前进，篮子的柳条把手已经完全张开，因此她不得不弯曲小小的肘部才能让篮子不至于触地。如果这不是因为这个篮子的大小只有她身体的一半，而且还是装得满满当当的，的话，这一幕反而会显得很滑稽。] 她困倦不堪、疲惫不堪也完全没关系。在那边，她让你们母子俩都为她的安危忧心忡忡；她现在能够站在这里跟你们说话，就已经很好了。你知道的，在那个球体内部，时间的流逝速度与外部是不同的——你上次去那里已经过去多久了？ 大约一周的时间。清子点了点头作为回应。孩子们长时间躺在床上对身体并不好，但在她恢复期间，我确实注意让她只做一些轻松的工作。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|首先，不需要处理那些会发出尖叫的装备。]" 小娟将耳朵贴在头上，低头看着自己的足部。很抱歉让你们担心了， [kinu.Dad]..." 那没关系——什么？做关键在于，她的身体状况正在好转。至少，她已经能够活动了。新鲜空气对她的健康肯定大有帮助。 不过，小娟仍然不愿意与你对视。
