rows.original: You see them; they're trying to hide in the shadows of walls, wagons and haystacks. Not that it matters; even if you couldn't see them, you can smell them anyway. You stand in the middle of the road, ready your [pc.weapon], and growl. "Come on out, then. I've walked straight into your trap, aren't you going to press the advantage?" One of them calls out from the darkness. "The master — " "Yeah well, fuck him. Are you going to try and kill me while I'm surrounded, or not? Gotta throw you a bone, or else it'll be a complete walkover." That gets them out of hiding, emerging one by one from their inept attempts to conceal themselves. Some of them, you might have once recognised as kids you knew, perhaps even liked. Now, though... You eye the approaching figures as kitchen knives and reshaped ploughshares glint in the dim light. "Now that we can see each other, I'm going to tell you once, and once only. If there's anything left of the pups that I once served drinks to at the Hound within your thick skulls, you're going to drop those toys you call weapons and run; I'll pretend I never saw you here. "Move one inch closer and I'll take pleasure in gutting you all." "For the master! The night of the ritual must not be interrupted!" They never learn.
rows.translation: 你能看到它们；它们正试图躲在墙壁、马车和干草堆的阴影里。不过其实也没关系；即使你看不见它们，你也依然能察觉到它们的存在。气味无论如何，你都站在马路中间，准备好了 [pc.weapon]那你就出来吧。我明明是走进了你的陷阱，你们难道不打算利用这个优势吗？”其中一个人从黑暗中喊道：“主人——”“去他的吧。既然我已经被包围了，你们到底要不要动手杀我？总得给你点好处，否则这场战斗简直就是一边倒。”这句话让他们不再躲藏，一个个从那些拙劣的藏身之处走了出来。其中有些人，你或许曾经在小时候认识他们，甚至可能喜欢过他们。现在，不过……那些逐渐靠近的身影，在昏暗的光线下，看起来就像厨房刀具或是被重新锻造的犁头。“既然我们现在能够看清彼此了，我就只说这一次。如果你们那些厚厚的脑袋里还有一丝良心，还记得我曾经在‘猎犬酒吧’里为那些小狗们倒过酒的话，就赶紧放下你们那些所谓的‘武器’，赶紧跑开吧；我会装作根本没在这里见过你们。 再靠近一寸，我就很乐意把你们全都杀得片甲不留。”“为了大师！仪式的夜晚绝不能被打扰！”他们永远都不会吸取教训。

rows.original: The last of the dark-robed so-called cultists falls to the dirt road, and doesn't get up again. You look at the mess you've made — kitchen knives and ploughshares hastily beaten into crude ritualistic implements, robes cut and sewn together from their old clothes and sackcloth. Blood soaking the dirt, on your gambeson and fur, melting the lightly falling snow.
rows.translation: 最后一个穿着黑袍的所谓邪教徒倒在了土路上，再也没能站起来。你看着自己造成的这一片混乱——厨房刀具和犁头被匆忙改造成简陋的祭祀工具，旧衣服和麻布被剪裁缝制在一起制成袍子。鲜血浸透了泥土，也浸湿了你的铠甲和毛皮，使得轻轻飘落的雪花都融化了。

Blood soaking the dirt, on your gambeson and fur, melting the lightly falling snow.\n    "

rows.original:
When the next of the dark-robed so-called cultists falls to the dirt road, the rest lose their nerve and run — not back into town, as you might've hoped, but towards the eastern gate.
    
    "Flee!" one of the kids screeches — or at least, attempts to with that stupid high, squeaky voice of hers — grabbing the closest one still standing other by the shoulder and turning to run. "We must warn the master!"
    
    You're tempted to run them down, to chase them into the alleys and make sure they never get to their destination, but there's no warning they can give that Sanders already hasn't by his clomping around.
rows.translation:
当下一个那些身穿黑袍的所谓“邪教徒”倒在那条土路上时，其余的人顿时失去了勇气，开始逃跑——但他们并没有往城镇方向跑，而是朝着东门跑去。
    
    “快跑！”其中一个女孩尖叫道——至少，她是用自己那尖细得让人难受的声音试图喊出这句话的——然后抓住旁边还站着的一个人，一起开始奔跑。我们必须警告主人！”
    
    你很想追上他们，把他们逼进小巷里，确保他们永远无法到达目的地，但他们发出的任何警告，桑德斯那笨重的脚步声早就已经把消息传达到了。

rows.original:
Children playing at being in the cool club... except it wasn't playing, it was never playing, and the bastard who'd lured them into his fold by means of his words and promises. The faces are the same, but the people are different; they'd died sometime in between then and now. Ghouls wearing bodies as skin suits and demanding respect... 
    
    It's all fun and games until someone dies.
rows.translation:
孩子们假装自己属于那个酷炫的俱乐部……但实际上他们从来都没有真正属于过那里，只是被那个用言语和承诺将他们吸引过来的混蛋所欺骗罢了。那些面孔依然相同，但这些人已经变了——在从那时到现在这段时间里，他们已经死了。那些披着人类外皮、却要求别人尊重的怪物……
    
    直到有人死去，这一切才真正变成了一场残酷的游戏。

rows.original: [pc.Weapon] at the ready, you step up besides Sanders. He acknowledges your arrival with a grunt, not daring take his eyes off the village lads and lasses — or at least, that's how he thinks of them. That's Sanders for you, always believing that people deep down just really want to be good, that anyone can be saved if you really just try long and hard enough and that the fact that he actually sometimes kills people is just incidental to said saving. It's an attitude that you don't deny is necessary, especially in the village's early days, but here and now... "I'm here. Hope I didn't keep you waiting." "It's okay." "I'd have come earlier, but things happened, people tried to kill me. You know." Sanders has no reply for that, so you look back and forth over this stand-off — they're stalling you, you know that. The longer you're kept here, the further these assholes take Rianna off to whatever fate that awaits her in that pale elf ruin; you haven't seen much of that girl, being from one of the newer families to arrive in town, but she hadn't fallen in with this lot yet. A good girl who doesn't deserve any of this... ...But deserve's got nothing to do with it, as you know full well. Taking a deep breath, you summon up your old commanding voice and let your growls echo into the night. "All right, so here's the deal, same one which I gave the others: I'm going to tell you once, and once only. I know all your faces. I know most of your names. If you even give a shit about the folks who're waiting for you lot to come home, who wonder what went wrong with their sons and daughters who would let a bald fucker sway them with promises of — I don't know, mountains of electrum in the baroness's vaults — you drop the act right here and slink on back home. I don't know what could ever possess you lot to still believe you're doing the right thing after your dumbass master and his thugs kidnapped a girl to be sacrificed, but I don't care; I'll pretend I never saw you here, not even when I'm serving you drinks at the Hound. "On the other hand, choose to get in my way, and I'll sign each and every one of your death warrants with my own two hands." There's that moment, that singular blink of an eye where things could go either way; for the sake of these dumb kids, you hope that they'll make the right choice — not just for their sake, but for everyone's sake. You flex your fingers upon the grip of your [pc.weapon], waiting. "I know you're stalling for time, so I'm going to count to three. One." Silence. "Two." "She's bluffing. She wouldn't kill us!" You can hear Sanders' breath whistle through his teeth, the man's gaze flicking between the thirty or so warm bodies massed by the gate and you. "What do we do, Gweyr? They're barely more than kids — I can't kill children!" "No, but I can." Your [pc.weapon] is already wet with blood, what's a little more? "Here's what I think of people who use human shields, Sanders." "Gweyr! No!" He reaches for you, but you're already ahead of him, and as the poor bastards come to meet you you're walking and swinging and walking and swinging and —
rows.translation: [pc.Weapon] 随时准备行动，你走到桑德斯的身边。他只是哼了一声表示注意到你的到来，却不敢将目光从那些村里的男孩女孩们身上移开——至少他是这么认为的。这就是桑德斯，他始终相信人们内心深处其实是渴望成为善良之人的，只要付出足够的努力，任何人都是可以被拯救的；而事实上，他有时会杀人，这些也只是实现拯救这一目标过程中的偶然现象罢了。这种态度确实必不可少，尤其是在村庄发展的初期阶段。但如今…… 我到了。希望没有让你等待太久。”“没关系。”“我本来想早点来的，但发生了一些事情，有人试图杀我，你懂的。”桑德斯对此无言以对，于是你们就这样僵持着——他们其实是在拖延时间，你心里明白的。你们把她关在这里的时间越长，这些混蛋就会把瑞安娜带到那个苍白精灵的废墟里，让她遭遇更糟糕的命运。你们其实不太了解那个女孩——她只是最近才来到这个小镇的家族之一，不过她还没有跟这些人混到一起。一个如此善良的女孩，根本不应该遭受这些…… 但是，如你们所知，‘应得’与这件事毫无关系。深吸一口气，你重新用出了那副威严的声音，让你的怒吼在夜色中回荡。“好吧，事情是这样的：我和之前对其他人说的一样，我现在只会告诉你们一次，仅此一次。我认识你们所有人，也知道你们大多数人的名字。如果你们真的在乎那些正在等待你们回家的人，那些担心自己的儿子女儿出了什么问题的人，那些会被某个秃头混蛋用各种承诺所迷惑的人——比如什么女男爵的保险库里藏着堆积如山的电银之类的鬼话——那么就别再装模作样了，赶紧滚回家去吧。我不知道你们这些人究竟是怎么想的，明明你们的那个蠢货老板和他的手下绑架了一个女孩来作为祭品，你们却还坚信自己在做正确的事情。但我不在乎，我就当从来没在这里见过你们，哪怕我在“猎犬酒吧”为你们服务时也是如此。 另一方面，如果你们执意要阻挠我，那么我会亲自动手签署每一个人的死亡判决书。”就有那么一刻，那么短暂的一瞬间，事情可能会朝着任何方向发展；为了这些愚蠢的孩子们，你真心希望他们能做出正确的选择——不仅仅是为了他们自己，也是为了所有人。 你活动着手掌上的手指。 [pc.weapon]我在等着。我知道你是在拖延时间，所以我数到三。一。”沉默。“二。”“她在虚张声势。她不会杀我们的！”你可以听到桑德斯的气息从牙缝中呼出，他的目光在聚集在大门旁的三十来个年轻人和你之间来回扫视。“我们该怎么办，格维尔？他们不过是一些孩子而已——我不可能杀害孩子！”“不，但是我可以。”你的 [pc.weapon] 已经沾满鲜血了，再多一点又有什么关系呢？‘对于那些利用人类当盾牌的人，我这样看……’，桑德斯。”“格维尔！不行！他试图追上你，但你早已走在了他前面。当那些可怜的家伙们试图与你相遇时，你却继续一边走一边挥动手臂，就这样不停地走，不停地挥动手臂——
rows.raw: " [pc.Weapon] at the ready, you step up besides Sanders. He acknowledges your arrival with a grunt, not daring take his eyes off the village lads and lasses — or at least, that's how he thinks of them. That's Sanders for you, always believing that people deep down just really want to be good, that anyone can be saved if you really just try long and hard enough and that the fact that he actually sometimes kills people is just incidental to said saving. It's an attitude that you don't deny is necessary, especially in the village's early days, but here and now... "I'm here. Hope I didn't keep you waiting." "It's okay." "I'd have come earlier, but things happened, people tried to kill me. You know." Sanders has no reply for that, so you look back and forth over this stand-off — they're stalling you, you know that. The longer you're kept here, the further these assholes take Rianna off to whatever fate that awaits her in that pale elf ruin; you haven't seen much of that girl, being from one of the newer families to arrive in town, but she hadn't fallen in with this lot yet. A good girl who doesn't deserve any of this... ...But deserve's got nothing to do with it, as you know full well. Taking a deep breath, you summon up your old commanding voice and let your growls echo into the night. "All right, so here's the deal, same one which I gave the others: I'm going to tell you once, and once only. I know all your faces. I know most of your names. If you even give a shit about the folks who're waiting for you lot to come home, who wonder what went wrong with their sons and daughters who would let a bald fucker sway them with promises of — I don't know, mountains of electrum in the baroness's vaults — you drop the act right here and slink on back home. I don't know what could ever possess you lot to still believe you're doing the right thing after your dumbass master and his thugs kidnapped a girl to be sacrificed, but I don't care; I'll pretend I never saw you here, not even when I'm serving you drinks at the Hound. "On the other hand, choose to get in my way, and I'll sign each and every one of your death warrants with my own two hands." There's that moment, that singular blink of an eye where things could go either way; for the sake of these dumb kids, you hope that they'll make the right choice — not just for their sake, but for everyone's sake. You flex your fingers upon the grip of your [pc.weapon], waiting. "I know you're stalling for time, so I'm going to count to three. One." Silence. "Two." "She's bluffing. She wouldn't kill us!" You can hear Sanders' breath whistle through his teeth, the man's gaze flicking between the thirty or so warm bodies massed by the gate and you. "What do we do, Gweyr? They're barely more than kids — I can't kill children!" "No, but I can." Your [pc.weapon] is already wet with blood, what's a little more? "Here's what I think of people who use human shields, Sanders." "Gweyr! No!" He reaches for you, but you're already ahead of him, and as the poor bastards come to meet you you're walking and swinging and walking and swinging and — "

rows.original:
You've seen this before, been here before in some of the battles the Crossed Swords were hired to fight. Peasant conscripts, unskilled, undisciplined, sometimes full of bravado that more often than not happened to be absolutely false. Grist for the mill, that's all they turned out to be, meat for the grinder. Still, it's true that they're more fanatical than you'd have given them credit for, and you can't help but wonder if the bald bastard — Tollus, that was his name — has them in some kind of mind-meld... but does it matter? At this point, it's all the same.
    
    You just keep on crunching and smashing and crunching and smashing — names, faces, limbs blurring into a bloody mess, screams as you press twitching bodies underfoot. The deep ochre of fresh blood wets your fur as you press into milling bodies even as they swarm you, making it stick to your skin. You crush another skull, sink your jaws into a neck — did they think you were bluffing when you said you'd kill them all if it came to that?
    
    But the thing is, one of the things you learned at your father's knee was to never make threats you didn't intend to follow up on, and it's good advice that's served you well for years.
    
    The last warm body falls into a twitching mess upon the blood-soaked earth, and you whirl around, expecting more. But there aren't any — they're dead, they're all dead. You kick away the nearest bodies, making some space for yourself; it doesn't feel like it's over yet.
rows.translation:
你以前见过这样的场景，在那些Crossed Swords被雇佣参与的战斗中，你也曾经来到过这里。那些农民征召来的士兵，没有技能，缺乏纪律，有时虽然满口豪言壮语，但实际上那些勇气往往完全是虚张声势。只不过是一些可供利用的材料罢了，不过是用来喂机器的肉而已。不过，确实可以说，他们的狂热程度超出了你的预期；你不禁会想，那个光头混蛋——他的名字是托勒斯——是否对他们进行了某种精神控制。…但这真的重要吗？在这个阶段，一切都已经无所谓了。
    
    你不断地碾压、粉碎，名字、面孔、四肢全都混成了一团血肉模糊的烂泥；当你将那些还在抽搐的身体踩在脚下时，尖叫声此起彼伏。新鲜的血液呈现出深赭色，浸湿了你的毛皮；即使它们成群地围上来攻击你，你依然继续碾压那些挣扎的身体，使得血液粘在你的皮肤上。又一颗头骨被你碾碎了，你的下颌紧紧咬住了一条脖子——当你说如果必要的话，会把他们全部杀死时，他们难道以为你在虚张声势吗？
    
    但问题是，你在父亲身边学到的最重要的一点就是：永远不要发出那些你并不打算真正付诸行动的威胁。这个建议非常有用，这些年来它一直帮助你度过了许多难关。
    
    最后一个还活着的人倒在血迹斑斑的地上，身体不断抽搐着。你迅速转过身去，期待着还会有更多人出现。然而，已经没有人了——他们全都死了。你踢开那些最近的尸体，为自己腾出一些空间；你感觉，这场战斗还没有结束。

rows.original: You just keep on crunching and smashing and crunching and smashing — names, faces, limbs blurring into a bloody mess, screams as you press twitching bodies underfoot. There're just so many of them, maybe too many of them as you start running out of breath; maybe life as a tavernkeeper and mother has made you soft, maybe you're just out of practice. They're more fanatical than you'd have given them credit for, and you can't help but wonder if the bald bastard — Tollus, that was his name — has them in some kind of mind-meld... but does it matter? At this point, it's all the same. Then, just when you think it might be best to take a step back and put a little breathing distance between you and this seething mass of flesh and cloth, they break. Enough of the cultists, the village lads and lasses, whatever Sanders wants to call them this fine day, have died for the rest of them to finally lose their nerve and break ranks. They go scattering in all directions, screaming, panting — they obviously thought you were bluffing to begin with, and weren't really prepared for you to really wade in and cause some carnage. But the thing is, one of the things you learned at your father's knee was to never make threats you didn't intend to follow up on, and it's good advice that's served you well for years. Run, that's right, run. Stay alive. You tighten your grip on your [pc.weapon], wondering if this is a feint and they're going to circle around and come back at you, but it looks like they've truly lost their nerve and are gone.
rows.translation: 你不断地砍杀、碾压，名字、面孔、四肢全都混成了一片血肉模糊的景象，当你踩在那些还在抽搐的身体上时，尖叫声此起彼伏。他们的数量实在太多了，或许太当你的呼吸开始变得急促时，你会发现他们中的许多人其实都比你想象中要坚强；也许是因为长期担任酒馆老板和母亲的角色，让你变得有些软弱了，又或许只是因为你已经很久没有进行过这样的训练罢了。 他们的狂热程度超出了你的预期，你不禁会怀疑，那个光头混蛋——他的名字是托勒斯——是否通过某种方式控制了他们的思想。.. 但这真的重要吗？在这个时候，一切都已经无所谓了。 然后，就在你认为最好退一步，与这个由肉体和布料构成的混乱局面保持一些距离的时候，它们突然崩溃了。够了，那些狂热信徒们——无论桑德斯今天想怎么称呼他们——已经有很多人因此丧命，剩下的那些人终于失去了勇气，开始四散逃窜，边跑边尖叫，边喘息边逃跑。显然，他们一开始就认为你在虚张声势，并没有真正准备好面对你真的采取行动、造成一场屠杀。 但问题是，你在父亲身边学到的最重要的一点就是：永远不要发出那些你没有打算真正付诸行动的威胁。这个建议非常有用，这些年来它一直帮助你度过了许多难关。 快跑，没错，赶紧跑。活下来才是最重要的。你紧紧握住了它。 [pc.weapon]你不禁怀疑这是否只是个佯攻，他们会不会绕道回来再次攻击你，但看起来他们确实失去了勇气，已经离开了。

rows.original: "Worthless. Worthless, the lot of you! More than twenty, and you can't even kill one woman?" Your ears perk up. You know that voice. "Leold, you fucking asshole." "Why yes, I've been doing a lot of fucking of late, and yes, some of them were assholes. Kind of you to notice." You narrow your eyes. Like all of the others who'd thrown their lot in with this Tollus man, Leold looks... different. He was always a bit of a troublemaker, the 'mander, but he wasn't a bad man and did good work when he could stay sober... ...But something's changed, and it's not just the single black gauntlet he now wears on his right hand. You eye Leold's lithe frame up and down, but he doesn't have any obvious weapons on him — not unless you count the massive spiked gauntlet, of course. "Are you here to stall for your so-called master too, or did you come to be gutted like all the others?" He snorts. "Judging by the way things are, you led them into this, Leold. You set up this fucking human shield, knowing Sanders wouldn't dare to kill the lads and lasses of the village. For that, I'm going to feed you your own sorry ass, piece by piece; don't worry, though, I won't make you eat it raw. "Come on, then. I'm here." "Having trouble, Leold?" "Master. I just..." "No matter, their souls will further empower the ritual. Their sacrifices will not be in vain." This must be Tollus, then. You eye the man, sizing him up, the way he moves, carries himself — clearly some kind of wizard or the like. This is the first time you've seen the man up close, and he's no prettier at this distance than he was from afar, not with that tattooed face of his. Then again, you can hardly say that you're easy on the eyes as you are right now... "The sacrifice is secured; the others have the girl. Once the Conjunction of Worlds is done and the promised power is granted us, we'll march upon the baroness's vault and help ourselves to the riches within, riches that she's been withholding from you despite the hard times your little village has fallen upon." Tollus gestures at the gauntlet bound to Leold's hand. "You'd like more of where that came from, wouldn't you?" "Y... yes, master." "Now then, the local tavernkeeper. Welcome, welco — " Tollus's voice is cut off in a shriek as you rampage forward, interrupting his little monologue. He raises a hand, clearly intending to form some spell, but you grab the smug little fuckwit by the fingers and bend backwards until you hear the satisfying pop of his fingers breaking. A good old standby for dealing with wizards — Tollus's bladed staff falls to the ground with a clatter as he screams and babbles, and you're pretty sure he's pissing himself at the moment. Too bad you have to let go of him, though, for Leold's gauntlet comes smashing into the space where your head was a moment ago. "Kill her!" Tollus shrieks, scrambling away from the two of you and down the road, clutching both his broken fingers and bladed staff alike. "Kill her!" You whirl back upon Leold, the 'mander drawing his fist back for another blow at you, and show him your teeth. If you smiled at him, there's no humor in it. "You know, you should've been more diligent about paying your tab. Still, I guess I'll be taking what you owe me for those two rye beers you had a couple months ago off your dead body."
rows.translation: 一文不值。你们这些人全都一文不值！二十多人了，却连一个女人都杀不死？” 你们的耳朵立刻竖了起来。你们知道那个声音。 “利奥尔德，你这个该死的混蛋。” “没错，最近我确实干了不少该死的事，而且其中确实有些行为很混蛋。你能注意到这点，还真是挺不错的。” 你眯起了眼睛。就像所有那些支持这个托勒斯人的人一样，利奥尔德看起来…… 不同他一直都是个爱惹麻烦的人，那个“捣蛋鬼”，但他其实并不是那种糟糕那个人在能够保持清醒的状态下，确实做了一些不错的工作…… ……但是，有些事情改变了而且，他右手戴的那只黑色护手也并非唯一的武器。你仔细观察莱奥德的体型，会发现他身上并没有任何明显的武器——当然，除非你把那只巨大的带刺护手也算进去。 “你是来为你的所谓主人拖延时间的，还是像其他人一样，来送命的？ 他哼了一声。 “看现在的情形，这都是你造成的，莱奥德。你故意设置了这个人类盾牌，明知桑德斯不敢杀害村里的那些年轻人。为此，我会把你自己那可怜的屁股一块一块地喂到你嘴里；不过别担心，我不会让你生吃它的。 那好吧，我在这里等着你。” “遇到麻烦了吗，莱奥德？” “大师，我只是……” “没关系，他们的牺牲会让仪式更加圆满。他们的付出绝对不会白费。” 那么，这里一定是托勒斯了。你仔细观察着这个男人，注意他的动作和举止——显然他是个巫师之类的角色。这是你第一次近距离看到他，从这个距离来看，他的样子并不比远处看时更漂亮，尤其是他那脸上那些纹身。 话说回来，以你现在的样子，也很难说自己是个“赏心悦目”的人吧…… “牺牲品已经到手了，其他人也已经得到了那个女孩。等‘世界交汇仪式’完成，我们得到了承诺中的力量之后，就会攻打女男爵的藏宝库，把里面那些财富据为己有——那些财富，尽管你们这个小村庄经历了那么多艰难困苦，但她却一直瞒着你们不把它们分给你们。”托勒斯指了指莱奥德手上的护手。“你肯定还想知道，那些财富到底是从哪里来的，对吧？ 是……是的，主人。” “那么，现在来谈谈那个当地的酒馆老板吧。欢迎啊——”托勒斯的话还没说完，你就猛地冲了上去，打断了他的讲话。他抬手似乎想要施展什么法术，但你一把抓住了那个自鸣得意的混蛋的手指，用力一扭，直到听到他的手指啪地一声断裂，你才松手。对付巫师们，有一个非常有效的手段——托勒斯的带刃法杖会“哐当”一声掉在地上，而与此同时，他也会发出尖叫和胡言乱语，你完全可以肯定，他此刻肯定吓得尿裤子了。不过，可惜你还是不得不放开他，因为莱奥德的护手已经狠狠地砸在了你刚才还在的位置上。 杀了她！”托勒斯尖叫着，一边抓着自己的断指和那根带刃的法杖，一边从你们两人身边逃开，沿着道路奔去。击杀哼！” 你迅速转向莱奥德，只见他正准备再次挥拳攻击你，于是你露出了牙齿。如果你对他笑了，那绝对不是出于幽默。“你知道，你本应该更认真地支付你的账单才对。不过，我想我还是会从你的尸体上拿走你几个月前欠我的那两杯黑啤酒的钱。

"Are you here to stall for your so-called master too, or did you come to be gutted like all the others?" He snorts. "Judging by the way things are, you led them into this, Leold. You set up this fucking human shield, knowing Sanders wouldn't dare to kill the lads and lasses of the village. For that, I'm going to feed you your own sorry ass, piece by piece; don't worry, though, I won't make you eat it raw. "Come on, then. I'm here." "Having trouble, Leold?" "Master. I just..." "No matter, their souls will further empower the ritual. Their sacrifices will not be in vain." This must be Tollus, then. You eye the man, sizing him up, the way he moves, carries himself — clearly some kind of wizard or the like. This is the first time you've seen the man up close, and he's no prettier at this distance than he was from afar, not with that tattooed face of his. Then again, you can hardly say that you're easy on the eyes as you are right now... "The sacrifice is secured; the others have the girl. Once the Conjunction of Worlds is done and the promised power is granted us, we'll march upon the baroness's vault and help ourselves to the riches within, riches that she's been withholding from you despite the hard times your little village has fallen upon." Tollus gestures at the gauntlet bound to Leold's hand. "You'd like more of where that came from, wouldn't you?" "Y... yes, master." "Now then, the local tavernkeeper. Welcome, welco — " Tollus's voice is cut off in a shriek as you rampage forward, interrupting his little monologue. He raises a hand, clearly intending to form some spell, but you grab the smug little fuckwit by the fingers and bend backwards until you hear the satisfying pop of his fingers breaking. A good old standby for dealing with wizards — Tollus's bladed staff falls to the ground with a clatter as he screams and babbles, and you're pretty sure he's pissing himself at the moment. Too bad you have to let go of him, though, for Leold's gauntlet comes smashing into the space where your head was a moment ago. "Kill her!" Tollus shrieks, scrambling away from the two of you and down the road, clutching both his broken fingers and bladed staff alike. "Kill her!" You whirl back upon Leold, the 'mander drawing his fist back for another blow at you, and show him your teeth. If you smiled at him, there's no humor in it. "You know, you should've been more diligent about paying your tab. Still, I guess I'll be taking what you owe me for those two rye beers you had a couple months ago off your dead body." "

rows.original: You smack the blunt end of your [pc.weapon] straight into Leold's jaw, sending him staggering back. He glowers at you again, rubbing his chin with his hand, then moves to send in a swift right hook with the cruelly spiked gauntlet. "So, the boy has a toy," you snarl, sidestepping the blow. "But does he know how to use it? Doesn't look like he does." "Shut up! How the fuck aren't you out of breath already?" "All the magic shit a wizard can give you won't make up for the fact that you're outmatched, Leold. Just surrender already and throw yourself on Sanders' mercy, because I certainly don't have any of the like." Leold roars and the swing goes wide; it's not much of an opening, but it's enough for you to step in into his reach and deliver upon him a good blow to the shoulder, blood spurting out into the cold night air. He groans, takes a staggering step towards you, and falls to the ground with all the other cultists. Is it over? You kneel down and check if Leold's breathing; he isn't. But just to make sure, you run him through with your sword anyway, sheathing the blade in crimson. Can't be too certain when it comes to these things. All right... now it's over.
rows.translation: 你用棍子的粗端敲打了 [pc.weapon] 这一拳直接击中了莱奥德的下巴，使他踉跄后退。他再次怒视着你，用手揉着下巴，然后迅速挥出了戴着带刺护手的那记右勾拳。 “原来这小子还有个‘玩具’啊……”你咬牙说道，同时巧妙地躲过了这一击。但他知道怎么使用它吗？看起来他并不知道。” “闭嘴！你他妈怎么还没喘上气来？” “无论巫师能给你什么魔法，都弥补不了你实力不如对手这个事实，莱奥德。干脆投降吧，任由桑德斯处置你吧，因为我可没有那样的耐心。” 莱奥德怒吼着，挥动棍棒的力量也变得更大；这个攻击虽然不算特别有力，但已经足够让你进入他的攻击范围，给他肩膀上一记重击，鲜血顿时喷溅到寒冷的夜空中。他发出一声呻吟，踉跄着朝你走来，最终和其他那些邪教徒一起倒在了地上。 就这样结束了吗？ 你跪下来检查莱奥德的呼吸情况——他已经没有气了。但为了确认无误，你还是用剑刺了他一下，然后将剑收回鞘中，剑身被染成了猩红色。在这些事情上，确实很难做到百分百确定。 好吧…… 现在一切都结束了。

rows.original:
Snarling, Leold steps up and delivers a swift uppercut to your jaw; you see it coming, but he corrects the blow and the spiked gauntlet comes crashing into your skull nonetheless. You may not have lost a tooth there, but a handful have definitely been loosened from that — not to mention the spikes driving into your flesh.
    
    "Not so tough are you now, bitch? That's for all the times you've hounded me for my tab!"
    
    You spit, and it's tinged with blood. "Maybe if you could actually handle money worth a shit, you wouldn't drink to the point where you end up owing other people money for it."
    
    "That mouth of yours is real pretty, bitch — guess I need to rearrange it some more."
    
    Grimacing, you raise your [pc.weapon] to parry the blow, but it never comes. Leold looks surprised, then gazes down towards the glowing point of the lance that's entered his back and is now protruding from his chest. The 'mander tries to say something, but it only comes out as a blood-frothed gurgle before Sanders withdraws his lance with a flick of his wrist.
    
    You gasp. "About time you decided he was evil enough to warrant killing."
    
    "We're taught not to take lives hastily."
    
    "Yeah, okay."
rows.translation:
莱奥德咆哮着上前，迅速一记上勾拳击中了你的下颌；你虽然预感到了这一击，但他巧妙地调整了出拳的角度，那些带刺的手套还是狠狠地砸在了你的头骨上。虽然你可能没有掉掉任何牙齿，但肯定有几颗牙齿被震得松动了好几颗——更不用说那些刺入你肉中的尖刺了。
    
    现在你倒厉害起来了，贱人？这都是因为你以前一直缠着我讨要我的零花钱！”你吐出来的口水里带着血丝。“要是你真能好好理财，就不会喝得烂醉如泥，最后还欠别人钱了。你的嘴真漂亮啊，贱人——看来我还得再调整一下它才行。”你皱着眉头，抬起了你的 [pc.weapon] 试图格挡这一击，但它始终没有到来。莱奥德露出惊讶的表情，随后低头看向那支刺入他背部、如今正从他的胸前伸出来的长矛。那个“指挥官”试图说些什么，但最终只发出了一阵含血的咕噜声，随后桑德斯便手腕一抖，将长矛拔了出来。你倒吸了一口凉气：“你终于认定他坏到足以被杀死的地步了，真是迟到了。”“我们被教导过，不要轻易夺走别人的生命。”“是啊，好吧。

rows.original: Breath ragged, lungs heaving, you stand in place a moment more, half-expecting Tollus to emerge from the darkness; little backstabbing shits like that are prone to trying tricks. But no sneak attack comes, no bolt from the blue; as your eyes rove over the slaked earth and numerous bodies that litter your surroundings, you see no sign of the so-called master. He must've fled up the mountain, towards the old ruin, and that's where you're going as well — up until you see a willowy wyld elf girl by the side of the road and River kneeling down at her side, undoing her bonds. Once the ropes are loosened, he lets her lean on him despite the elf having more than a head of height on the little catboy. The poor thing is sobbing as the pair approach the gate — you can still see the rope marks on her wrists and ankles — but when she takes in the sight of the blood-soaked earth, the bodies littering the ground and you in the middle of it all, she screams and shrinks back from you. River looks down at the carnage, then up at you with a grimace on his face. You stare him down unapologetically for several moments, then step forward, your feet making wet noises upon the earth. "I see you got the girl." "I did. Leold and the Tollus creep were watching her, but since you drew them away I was able to sneak around and get her." "And of that Tollus asshole?" "He went up the mountainside, towards the foothills. I loosed a few shots at him, but he got away. I don't think he'll return to the temple, but we'll need to make a sweep of the old ruin just to make sure." "Maybe he's gone for good." "I doubt it. I've fought enough of his kind in my time — creatures like that don't have the grace to die on their own." Sanders makes a frustrated noise as he steps up. "I wish he could reconsider his ways, but the sad truth is that someone so steeped in evil is likely to rationalise away his misdeeds. If only we'd been able to capture him..." "... Hmph." "But that's not important now." Sanders' face creases in anger, true anger from such a man twinged with disappointment. "In the gods' names, Gweyr, what have you just done?!" "I did what I said I would, Sanders. I showed them exactly what I thought of human shields. Tollus and Leold, they clearly knew of your oaths as a Warrior of White, and that you wouldn't lift a finger against people you still thought of as poor misguided kids. You were just going to stand right there like an idiot until they sacrificed the girl to whatever horrible abominations they worship, and once they learned you could be cockblocked like that they'd just keep on doing it over and over again." "I don't think you get my point, Gweyr. In one night, you have killed more than half the youth in Hawkethorne!" Sanders roars, grabbing you by the shoulders and shaking you — and he does have the strength for that. "Does that mean absolutely nothing to you?" "And whose fucking fault is that that things have gotten to this point? If we'd kicked them straight out of town like I wanted to begin with over any protests their folks might've had, shit wouldn't have gotten to this point. I get it, you want to believe that people are basically good and that everyone deserves a second chance, Sanders. And sure, all those people, no one wants to see their kin run out of town. So things just stewed until they grew from bad to worse and half the fuckers thought they'd join the winning team, while the others hid in their homes while Tollus and his ass had the run of the village. That sure isn't what you and those kids' folks wanted, Sanders, but it sure as fuck is what happened! "You're just too nice for your own good, Sanders. It's not a failing for someone who used to be a holy warrior like you, but it does mean I've got to do the jobs you won't." Sanders grits his teeth and points down to the heaped bodies about your feet. "You. Call. This. A. Job." "You've known Garth and me for a decade now, Sanders; your order's hired the Crossed Swords more than once, they still do. So then, the question remains: what were you going to do while those assholes went and dragged off the girl up the mountain?" "I'd have thought of something that didn't involve such blatant butchery." "Really, now." The townsfolk are emerging from their homes now, peering out cautiously to see what the commotion is all about. One family's weeping tears of joy as River returns Rianna to her family, but so many, many more are weeping for another reason. Some of them have their eyes on you, red-hot needles of hate and resentment; though they dare say nothing to you, the monster with blood smeared over her fur and tail and with [pc.weapon] in hand, you know what's going on in their minds. "So, this is what it's come to, huh. Too afraid to act and hiding in your own homes while Tollus and his fuckers have the run of the town and openly talk of overthrowing the baroness, yet so swift to turn on the woman who gave enough of a shit to do something about it despite none of her own kin being personally involved in this mess. "At least Sanders has principles and is a good man. You lot are just chickenshits. Want to lynch me? Who's going to be first? For months, years, I served you lot drinks, played midwife for you, held Gwyn and Garret while you told me they were cute, and today — " "Gweyr. Please don't make this any worse." River's returned from handing off the elf girl to her folks and is tugging on your gambeson. "Please." Gods, your bones ache. With the heat and rush of battle finally beginning to fade, your recent exertions are starting to catch up to you, and yet everything feels far heavier than it should be. "So, that's it," Sanders spits. "You did the job that none of us were willing to do." "Yes." "I know why you did this, Gweyr. That, and it's my fault for thinking you could help the situation in the first place. It's why I'm not running you through this very moment, and why I'm not going to let these people try and hang you. "You have three hours, which is more than what your own customs dictate. Get your things and get out of here, because if you stay one night in this town someone is going to try and kill you in your sleep for what you've done tonight." "You're sending me to walk the ice." Sanders nods. "I am. There are no more jarls and the baroness isn't here, so I'll have to do."
rows.translation: 你气喘吁吁地站在原地，心中还在期待着托勒斯会从黑暗中现身——这种背信弃义的家伙总是喜欢使出诡计。然而，并没有任何突然的袭击发生，周围散落的泥土和众多尸体中，也没有任何关于那个所谓的“大师”的踪迹。他肯定已经逃上了那座山，朝着那片古老的废墟去了，而你也要去那里——直到你在路边看到一个柳枝般柔美的野精灵女孩，以及跪在她身边的瑞弗，正在为她解开束缚。当绳子被松开后，瑞弗让她依靠在自己身上，尽管这个精灵女孩的身高比那个小猫男孩要高出一大截。当那两人走近大门时，那个可怜的女孩正在哭泣——你仍然能看到她手腕和足部踝上留下的绳索痕迹——但当她看到那片被鲜血浸透的土地、地上散落的尸体，以及站在这一切中央的你时，她突然尖叫起来，然后吓得退缩了回去。 瑞弗低头看着那一片惨状，然后抬起头，脸上带着一丝苦涩的表情看着你。你毫不愧疚地与他对视了片刻，接着向前迈了一步，你的足部步在湿漉漉的地上发出声响。“看来你把那个女孩带走了。”“是的。莱奥德和那些托卢斯怪物一直在监视她，但因为你把他们引开了，我才能够悄悄地把她带走。 那个叫托卢斯的混蛋呢？”“他往山腰那边跑了，朝着山足部的方向。我朝他开了几枪，但他逃掉了。我觉得他应该不会再回到神庙里去了，不过我们还是得把那些古老的废墟仔细搜查一遍，以确保万无一失。”“也许他已经永远离开了。 我可不这么认为。这些年来，我遇到过太多他这种人了——这种生物根本没有尊严，连自杀的勇气都没有。”桑德斯沮丧地说道，一边向前走去。“我真希望他能改过自新，但事实就是，一个如此沉溺于邪恶之中的人，很可能会为自己的恶行找各种借口。要是我们当时能抓住他的话…… ……哼。”“但现在这已经不重要了。”桑德斯脸上布满了愤怒，这样一个男人真正的愤怒中还夹杂着失望。“看在诸神的份上，格韦尔，你刚才到底做了什么？完成我确实做到了我说过的话，桑德斯。我向他们清楚地表明了我对‘人肉盾牌’这种行为的看法。托卢斯和利奥尔德显然知道你作为‘白色战士’所立下的誓言，也知道你不会对那些你仍然认为只是些被误导的孩子们动一根手指头。你只会像个白痴一样站在那里，直到他们把那个女孩献给他们所崇拜的那些可怕的东西；而一旦他们发现你可以被那样轻易地阻止，他们就会一再重复这种行为。我认为你并没有理解我的意思，格维尔。就在一个晚上里，你已经杀害了鹰棘镇地区超过一半的年轻人！桑德斯怒吼着，抓住你的肩膀摇晃你——然后他做有足够的实力去做那件事。“这是否意味着绝对没什么这是谁的错，事情才会发展到这种地步？如果当初我按照自己的想法把他们赶出小镇，不管他们的家人会怎么抗议，事情也不会变成现在这个样子。我明白，你愿意相信人们本质上是善良的，每个人都应该得到第二次机会，桑德斯。当然，没有人愿意看到自己的亲人被迫离开这个小镇。于是，事情逐渐恶化，越来越糟。有一半的人以为自己会加入胜利的一方，而另外一半人则躲在家里，任由托卢斯和他的那些同伙掌控整个村庄。桑德斯，这肯定不是你和那些孩子们的家长所希望看到的，但事实就是如此！ 桑德斯，你太善良了，这种性格反而会给你带来麻烦。对于你这样曾经是个正义战士的人来说，这或许不是什么缺点，但这也意味着有些工作必须由我来完成——那些你不愿意去做的工作。”桑德斯咬紧牙关，指着你足部边那些倒下的敌人说道：“就你，来把这份工作做完吧。 桑德斯，你和加斯已经认识十年了；你的团队不止一次雇佣过‘十字剑’组织，现在依然在雇佣他们。那么问题来了：当那些混蛋把那个女孩拖上山去的时候，你到底打算做什么？”“我本应该想出一些不会导致如此残忍暴行的办法来。 真的，就是现在。”镇上的居民们纷纷从家中走出，小心翼翼地张望，想要弄清楚这场骚动究竟是怎么回事。当瑞弗将里安娜带回她的家人身边时，有一家人正喜极而泣；但还有许多人，他们流泪的原因却截然不同。其中一些人正用充满仇恨与怨恨的目光注视着你——虽然他们不敢对你说出口，但那个身上沾满鲜血、毛发和尾巴上都带着血迹的怪物 [pc.weapon] 现在你终于明白他们心里在想什么了。“所以，事情就是发展到这一步了，哈。他们太害怕采取行动，只能躲在自己的家里，而托勒斯和他的那些手下却在整个镇子上为非作歹，公然宣称要推翻女男爵的统治。然而，当有一个人不顾自己家族与这场混乱毫无关联，仍然挺身而出试图改变现状时，他们却立刻转而攻击她。 至少桑德斯有原则，是个好人。而你们这些人简直就是一群懦夫。想 lynch 我吗？谁会第一个动手？这些个月来，这些年来，我一直为你们准备酒水，帮你们解决各种麻烦，还帮你们照顾格温和加雷特，你们还总说他们很可爱……可今天—— 格韦尔，求你别让事情变得更糟了。”瑞弗在把那个精灵女孩交给她的家人后回来了，她拉了拉你的护肩，恳求道：“求你。”天啊，你的骨头都快疼死了。随着战斗的激烈与紧张逐渐消退，你最近付出的努力开始让你感到疲惫不堪，然而一切却似乎比预想的要沉重得多。 所以，就是这样，”桑德斯咬牙说道，“你做了我们所有人都不愿意去做的事情。”“是的。”“我知道你为什么这么做，格韦尔。这也是我的错——当初我竟然以为你能帮助改变这种局面。正因如此，我现在才没有严厉责备你，也不会让这些人试图把你陷害。 你有三个小时的时间，这个时间比你们自己的习俗所规定的还要长。收拾好你的东西，立刻离开这里，因为如果你再在这个小镇多待一个晚上有人他们肯定会趁你睡觉的时候杀了你，就因为你今晚所做的那些事。”“你是在逼我去送死。”桑德斯点了点头：“没错，我确实是在逼你去送死。现在再也没有酋长了，女男爵也不在这里，所以这个任务就只能由我来做。

I don't think he'll return to the temple, but we'll need to make a sweep of the old ruin just to make sure." "Maybe he's gone for good." "I doubt it. I've fought enough of his kind in my time — creatures like that don't have the grace to die on their own." Sanders makes a frustrated noise as he steps up. "I wish he could reconsider his ways, but the sad truth is that someone so steeped in evil is likely to rationalise away his misdeeds. If only we'd been able to capture him..." "... Hmph." "But that's not important now." Sanders' face creases in anger, true anger from such a man twinged with disappointment. "In the gods' names, Gweyr, what have you just done?!" "I did what I said I would, Sanders. I showed them exactly what I thought of human shields. Tollus and Leold, they clearly knew of your oaths as a Warrior of White, and that you wouldn't lift a finger against people you still thought of as poor misguided kids. You were just going to stand right there like an idiot until they sacrificed the girl to whatever horrible abominations they worship, and once they learned you could be cockblocked like that they'd just keep on doing it over and over again." "I don't think you get my point, Gweyr. In one night, you have killed more than half the youth in Hawkethorne!" Sanders roars, grabbing you by the shoulders and shaking you — and he does have the strength for that. "Does that mean absolutely nothing to you?" "And whose fucking fault is that that things have gotten to this point? If we'd kicked them straight out of town like I wanted to begin with over any protests their folks might've had, shit wouldn't have gotten to this point. I get it, you want to believe that people are basically good and that everyone deserves a second chance, Sanders. And sure, all those people, no one wants to see their kin run out of town. So things just stewed until they grew from bad to worse and half the fuckers thought they'd join the winning team, while the others hid in their homes while Tollus and his ass had the run of the village. That sure isn't what you and those kids' folks wanted, Sanders, but it sure as fuck is what happened! "You're just too nice for your own good, Sanders. It's not a failing for someone who used to be a holy warrior like you, but it does mean I've got to do the jobs you won't." Sanders grits his teeth and points down to the heaped bodies about your feet. "You. Call. This. A. Job." "You've known Garth and me for a decade now, Sanders; your order's hired the Crossed Swords more than once, they still do. So then, the question remains: what were you going to do while those assholes went and dragged off the girl up the mountain?" "I'd have thought of something that didn't involve such blatant butchery." "Really, now." The townsfolk are emerging from their homes now, peering out cautiously to see what the commotion is all about. One family's weeping tears of joy as River returns Rianna to her family, but so many, many more are weeping for another reason. Some of them have their eyes on you, red-hot needles of hate and resentment; though they dare say nothing to you, the monster with blood smeared over her fur and tail and with [pc.weapon] in hand, you know what's going on in their minds. "So, this is what it's come to, huh. Too afraid to act and hiding in your own homes while Tollus and his fuckers have the run of the town and openly talk of overthrowing the baroness, yet so swift to turn on the woman who gave enough of a shit to do something about it despite none of her own kin being personally involved in this mess. "At least Sanders has principles and is a good man. You lot are just chickenshits. Want to lynch me? Who's going to be first? For months, years, I served you lot drinks, played midwife for you, held Gwyn and Garret while you told me they were cute, and today — " "Gweyr. Please don't make this any worse." River's returned from handing off the elf girl to her folks and is tugging on your gambeson. "Please." Gods, your bones ache. With the heat and rush of battle finally beginning to fade, your recent exertions are starting to catch up to you, and yet everything feels far heavier than it should be. "So, that's it," Sanders spits. "You did the job that none of us were willing to do." "Yes." "I know why you did this, Gweyr. That, and it's my fault for thinking you could help the situation in the first place. It's why I'm not running you through this very moment, and why I'm not going to let these people try and hang you. "You have three hours, which is more than what your own customs dictate. Get your things and get out of here, because if you stay one night in this town someone is going to try and kill you in your sleep for what you've done tonight." "You're sending me to walk the ice." Sanders nods. "I am. There are no more jarls and the baroness isn't here, so I'll have to do." '

rows.original:
"You're not taking any weapons?"
        
        You shake your head. "I won't need them where I'm going. Give them to the pups as a reminder of their mother, although I won't blame them if they don't want to have anything to do with me. If that happens... I don't know, just pass them off them to someone who needs them more or something, I don't care."
        
        Garth sighs. "They turned on you so quickly..."
        
        "I understand why they did it. It's cowardly and chickenshit, but that doesn't stop me from understanding as much. Take care of the kids, okay? Make sure they grow up right." 
        
        "Gweyr, you're being sent away to walk the ice! How can you be so — so calm about it?"
        
        "I..." It's truly hard to find words that can encompass everything you're feeling right now. You knew something like this was going to happen once the townsfolk elected to simply do nothing and hope for the best, but... oh, Garth, poor dear that he is... how can you ever explain as much to him? "I'll be going. My time's almost up."
        
        "What will you do?"
        
        "I've got unfinished business with that Tollus asshole. And then after that... well, we'll see."
        
        "Gweyr...!"
        
        You have no reply for your husband as you turn your back on him and stride out of the home you built together. Snow's still falling and the streets are empty, although you can feel many eyes on you; as you pass through the eastern gate, you note that some of the bodies are gone, Leold's included. Their families must have claimed them... either that, or Sanders is busy filling graves. Barely have you gone three steps beyond the arch, though, that you hear a voice.
        
        "Mom?"
        
        Oh no, oh no... you crouch down so that you're on eye level with Garret and give your son a rub on the back; he likes that. The boy's still soft and fuzzy, but he's already starting to look like your father about the face and ears. "What are you doing out here, kid? You should be in bed."
        
        "I heard you and Dad talking, and couldn't sleep. Mom, you smell of blood."
        
        Ha, just like him to say it outright as if it were the most natural thing in the world. "...Yeah. I didn't have time to wash."
        
        "I heard you're going on a journey."
        
        "Yeah, kid."
        
        "Will you be coming home soon?"
        
        "...I'll be home as soon as I can, kid; I just have some business to take care of. Look after your sister, and your dad, too — he may not look like it, but he's actually a big [silly|simp|softy]. You can do that, yes?"
        
        Ever eager to please, your boy nods so fast his head's a blur. He's so young, you wonder if he'll ever remember this conversation when he gets older... "Are you going to bring back something good, mom?"
        
        "I'll see if I can't find something, kid. All right, back to bed with you; your dad is going to worry if he discovers you've slipped out of the house just to send me off." You smile and place your hands on Garret's head, rolling your palms down to his face and squeezing his cheeks lightly; he squirms on your grasp, clearly liking it but just a bit too full of himself to admit as much. His grandfather was the same way... the blood's strong in this one. "Go on then, shoo."
        
        There's an obvious reluctance in Garret to peel away from you, but you give him a firm swat on the back and that sends him on his way. Time for you to get moving, too — if you linger any longer, you'll be tempted to stay, one way or another...
rows.translation:
你不带任何武器吗？”你摇了摇头：“我去的地方并不需要它们。把它们交给那些小狗吧，让它们能记住它们的母亲……不过，如果它们不愿意和我有任何瓜葛，我也不会责怪它们。如果真的发生了那种情况……我也不确定，就把它们交给更需要它们的人吧，我并不在意。
        
        加斯叹了口气：“他们这么快就背叛了你……”“我明白他们为什么这么做。这种行为很懦弱，也很卑鄙，但这并不妨碍我理解他们的动机。一定要照顾好孩子们，好吗？一定要确保他们能够健康成长。”“格维尔，你被派去冰原上执行任务了！你怎么能表现得这么……如此冷静呢？
        
        我……”真的很难找到合适的词语来表达你此刻的所有感受。当你看到镇上的居民们选择什么都不做，只是寄希望于最好的结果时，你就知道这种事情会发生……但是，哦，加斯，可怜的加斯……你要怎么向他解释这一切呢？“我得走了。我的时间差不多快用完了。
        
        你打算怎么做？”“我还有些事情没跟那个叫托勒斯的混蛋算清。等办完那些事之后……嗯，到时候再看看吧。”“格维尔……！”你没有回答丈夫的话，只是转身走出了你们共同建造的家园。雪仍在飘落，街道上空无一人，但你能感觉到有许多目光在注视着你；当你穿过东门时，你注意到有些尸体已经不见了，包括利奥尔德的。他们的家人肯定已经来领走了这些尸体。要么就是那样，要么就是桑德斯正在忙着填坟墓。然而，你刚走过拱门三步远，就听到了一个声音。
        
        妈妈？”哦不，哦不……你蹲下来，让自己的视线与加雷特处于同一水平线上，然后轻轻拍拍儿子的背，他很喜欢这样。这个男孩的皮肤还是柔软而绒毛茸的，但他的脸型和耳朵已经开始有点像你父亲了。“孩子，你在这里干什么呢？你应该去睡觉的。
        
        我听到你和爸爸在说话，就睡不着了。妈妈，你身上有血腥味。”哈，他就这么直截了当地说出来，好像这是世界上最正常的事情一样。“……是啊，我没时间洗澡。”“我听说你要去旅行了。
        
        嗯，孩子。”“你很快就会回家吗？”“……我会尽快回家的，孩子；我只是有些事情需要处理。你要照顾好你的妹妹，还有你的爸爸——他看起来可能不太像，但实际上他是个很坚强的人。 [silly|简单易懂的东西。|软弱的人]你能做到，对吧？”你这个总是急于讨好别人的孩子，连头都忙得不停地点头，简直快把脑袋点晕了。他还这么小，你不禁会想，等他长大后，是否还能记得这次谈话……“妈妈，你一定会带回来一些好东西吧？我看看能不能找点东西给你，孩子。好了，你回去睡觉吧；要是你爸爸发现你只是为了送我走才偷偷溜出家的，他肯定会担心的。”你微笑着把双手放在加雷特的头上，然后轻轻地将手掌向下移动到他的脸上，轻轻捏了捏他的脸颊；他在你的怀里扭来扭去，显然很喜欢这个举动，但又因为太自负而不好意思承认这一点。他的祖父也是这样的……这种血脉确实很有力量。“那你就快去吧，快走。”加雷特显然很不情愿离开你，但你轻轻拍了他一下后背，他就只好走了。你也该动身了——如果你再拖延下去，迟早会忍不住想要留下来的……

rows.original: "So," Gweyr eventually says after a moment's pause to let the story sink in. "That's what happened. Am I a monster, [pc.name]?"
rows.translation: 所以，”格维尔在稍作停顿，让听众有时间消化这个故事之后，终于开口说道，“事情就是这样的。我是不是一个怪物 [pc.name]?"
rows.raw: '\n            "So," Gweyr eventually says after a moment\'s pause to let the story sink in. "That\'s what happened. Am I a monster, [pc.name]?"'

rows.original:
You can't deny that she did some monstrous things, that's true. Killing more than half of fledgeling Hawkethorne's youth in one night — that's a monstrous deed, to be sure. But whether it makes her a monster or not... she may be a necessary monster if you're going to dismantle Tollus's cult. She hasn't crossed that line.
            
                "I guess that's about as good as an answer I'm getting," Gweyr says with a sigh. "Well then, [pc.name]... if you're still in despite knowing everything I've done, talk to me about the matter again in an hour or two. For now, I think I just want to have a little time to myself."
rows.translation:
你不得不承认，她确实做了一些极其残忍的事情，这是事实。在一个晚上就杀害了鹰棘镇家族中超过一半的年轻成员——这无疑是一桩残忍至极的罪行。但究竟这是否意味着她本身就是一个怪物……如果你想摧毁托勒斯的邪教组织，那么她或许就是那个必须被利用的“怪物”。她并没有越过那条界限。
            
                “我想，这应该算是我得到的最合理的答案了吧，”格维尔叹了口气说道，“那么，就这样吧。 [pc.name]……如果你在知道我做过的一切之后仍然愿意继续和我在一起，那么一两个小时后再和我谈谈这件事吧。现在，我想我只是需要一些属于自己的时间。

rows.original: As you step through the old jotun halls, a chill runs down your spine. Something is very, very wrong here... "Look alive!" Gweyr says, a scowl on her face. "They're coming." The cultists are coming at you from behind pillars and from the shadows, eyes set with fanatical fury, legs pumping tirelessly as they dash towards you. No rest for the [pc.isDK|wicked|brave], alas — you have barely enough time to recover and hold your [pc.weapon] at the ready before battle is joined. The hows and whys can wait — here and now, you've got business to deal with. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 当你穿过那些古老的巨人之厅时，一阵寒意顺着脊椎传了下来。这里肯定出了什么大问题…… “快躲起来！”格维尔面带怒容说道，“他们来了。” 那些邪教徒们正从柱子后面以及阴影中朝你冲来，他们眼中燃烧着狂热的怒火，双腿不停地奔跑着，朝着你猛扑过来。这些人根本不会休息 [pc.isDK|邪恶的|勇敢的]唉——你几乎根本没有足够的时间来恢复体力，也没有足够的时间来保持 [pc.weapon] 在战斗开始之前，必须做好充分的准备。各种原因和细节可以稍后再考虑——此刻，你首要的任务就是完成手头的工作。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: Carefully, you make your way across the ancient stone bridge, following Gweyr's lead. The tiles underfoot are wet and slick with water and moss, and every now and then you find yourself stepping into a puddle you didn't know was there, kicking up water and sending small creatures scurrying out of your way. There doesn't seem to be any sign of Tollus's cultists yet, though... Thing is, you've put so much of yourself into looking around that you've neglected to pay attention to what's going on underfoot. Even though Gweyr makes a slow yet steady pace, tapping her path with the haft of her spear all the time, she must've weakened the bridge or something when she first passed over it. When you follow in her footsteps, splashing into one of the small pools where water dripping from the ceiling has gathered, an ominous crunching and grinding sounds from underfoot, muffled by the damp and wet all about you. Still, it's enough for Gweyr to whirl around[party.hasCompanions | and for [party.som||[comp1.name]|[comp1.name] and [comp2.name]] to leap back ], the old wolfess' hand outstretched as the ancient bricks crumble beneath your feet. Jagged chunks of masonry break free from the underside of the bridge, falling away into the dark water beneath with large splashes; you only barely manage to close your fingers about Gweyr's before the ground below you gives way. [pc.hasWings |You flap your wings desperately for all the good they're going to do you from a sudden standing start, but better something that nothing... | ] Even with Gweyr holding onto you, gravity still drags you forward against the rough, jagged edges in the newly-made hole in the bridge, scraping at your chin and arms. It's a second or two of heart-pounding and gut-wrenching terror before you've realized that everything's stabilized... even if it's with your legs dangling out over a perilous drop into open water. Slowly, Gweyr pulls you up[party.hasCompanions | with [party.compNames true]'s aid ], grunting with effort as she hauls you up and over the edge onto firm ground once more. "You all right there, [pc.mf |kid |girl ]?" You wipe the blood off your stinging forearms and grimace[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] looking on in concern ]. Nothing too bad, some scrapes on your chin, arms and knees... you've suffered worse. Was that a trap set by the cult? "Don't think so. I've run through my share of these places in my youth... old places get unstable. That, and with all this water around..." She waves a hand. "I've saved my share of friends from these, and lost more. Should've realized it before you stepped there... I'm getting old. You sure you're fine?" Does it change anything? You're not about to backtrack now. "It does. Trust me on that." Yeah, you can go on. All that noise no doubt has alerted every demon in this place to your presence, and you've got to move fast. Once you've [party.hasCompanions |carefully edged [party.compNames true] around the gaping hole in the bridge |checked yourself over and are ready ], you press on, taking care to circle around any more pools of stagnant water on the masonry.
rows.raw: " Carefully, you make your way across the ancient stone bridge, following Gweyr's lead. The tiles underfoot are wet and slick with water and moss, and every now and then you find yourself stepping into a puddle you didn't know was there, kicking up water and sending small creatures scurrying out of your way. There doesn't seem to be any sign of Tollus's cultists yet, though... Thing is, you've put so much of yourself into looking around that you've neglected to pay attention to what's going on underfoot. Even though Gweyr makes a slow yet steady pace, tapping her path with the haft of her spear all the time, she must've weakened the bridge or something when she first passed over it. When you follow in her footsteps, splashing into one of the small pools where water dripping from the ceiling has gathered, an ominous crunching and grinding sounds from underfoot, muffled by the damp and wet all about you. Still, it's enough for Gweyr to whirl around[party.hasCompanions | and for [party.som||[comp1.name]|[comp1.name] and [comp2.name]] to leap back ], the old wolfess' hand outstretched as the ancient bricks crumble beneath your feet. Jagged chunks of masonry break free from the underside of the bridge, falling away into the dark water beneath with large splashes; you only barely manage to close your fingers about Gweyr's before the ground below you gives way. [pc.hasWings |You flap your wings desperately for all the good they're going to do you from a sudden standing start, but better something that nothing... | ] Even with Gweyr holding onto you, gravity still drags you forward against the rough, jagged edges in the newly-made hole in the bridge, scraping at your chin and arms. It's a second or two of heart-pounding and gut-wrenching terror before you've realized that everything's stabilized... even if it's with your legs dangling out over a perilous drop into open water. Slowly, Gweyr pulls you up[party.hasCompanions | with [party.compNames true]'s aid ], grunting with effort as she hauls you up and over the edge onto firm ground once more. "You all right there, [pc.mf |kid |girl ]?" You wipe the blood off your stinging forearms and grimace[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] looking on in concern ]. Nothing too bad, some scrapes on your chin, arms and knees... you've suffered worse. Was that a trap set by the cult? "Don't think so. I've run through my share of these places in my youth... old places get unstable. That, and with all this water around..." She waves a hand. "I've saved my share of friends from these, and lost more. Should've realized it before you stepped there... I'm getting old. You sure you're fine?" Does it change anything? You're not about to backtrack now. "It does. Trust me on that." Yeah, you can go on. All that noise no doubt has alerted every demon in this place to your presence, and you've got to move fast. Once you've [party.hasCompanions |carefully edged [party.compNames true] around the gaping hole in the bridge |checked yourself over and are ready ], you press on, taking care to circle around any more pools of stagnant water on the masonry. "

rows.original:
Now that you've crossed the bridges, the actual entrance to the ancient jotun keep draws into view — and it's been heavily fortified. Would it be that it were a mere palisade, but alas, stone and mortar barricades have been built into the wide, jotun-sized gates, a properly entrenched position with a narrow killzone in front of it. Tollus's cultists have had a good long while to prepare for any kind of intrusion, and your arrival in particular has not gone unnoticed.
    
    "It's [pc.himHer]!"
    
    That's all the warning you get before arrows and firebolts alike sail through the air in arcs, raining down on your position and forcing you out of the gateway. Gweyr drops onto the ground instinctively, then takes cover behind a chunk of fallen rubble while [party.combatNames true] duck around a corner. Someone's designed this killbox very well... and it's your only way in as far as you can tell, unless you're willing to dig through gods know how much rock there is without accidentally breaking out into the open sea and flooding the whole place.
    
    You swallow hard, and consider your options...
rows.translation: 现在你已经穿过了那些障碍，那座古老的巨人之堡的真正入口终于出现在眼前了——而且它被加固得极为严密。本来以为那可能只是一道简单的栅栏，但实际上，那些宽大的、足以容纳巨人的大门上竟然筑起了石墙和砖垒，形成了一个防御工事严密的据点，其前方还设有狭窄的防御区域。托勒斯的信徒们已经有足够的时间来准备应对任何形式的入侵，而你的到来更是没有被他们忽视。“就是这里了[pc.himHer]就在这时，你只收到了这一声警告，紧接着，箭矢与火球便划着弧线飞向空中，如倾盆大雨般落在了你的所在位置，迫使你不得不离开那个通道。格维尔本能地跌落在地上，然后迅速躲到了一块倒塌的碎石后面 [party.combatNames true] 拐过那个角落。有人把这个陷阱设计得非常精妙……就你目前所知，这是你进入这里的唯一途径，除非你愿意挖开那些堆积如山的岩石，而不用担心会不小心挖到外面的大海，导致整个地方被水淹没。你艰难地咽了口唾沫，开始思考自己的选择……

"Gonna be a bit of a squeeze, but better than nothing." As if proving her point, a bolt of magical fire whistles down and lands smack in Arona's shield, the runes carved into hide and wood flaring up but still leaving an ugly scorch mark upon its face. She snarls and roars a curse [pc.ora orc |that would have made your mother blush |in suitably ferocious orcish ], then breaks into a broad-shouldered charge straight for the fortifications, dragging the rest of you in her wake to avoid being exposed to the missile fire coming from the cultists. She doesn't even bother to duck and weave, instead taking the straightest and most direct route into the defenses; a last desperate salvo of arrows and flame manages to singe Arona's arms and legs, painting her green skin with blood and soot. That only enrages her more as she bowls straight into the barricade and shoulders the nearest demon, snarling toothily in genuine orcish battle-rage. "Demons? "I'll lead." With him in his suit of ice armor, you have to admit he's best suited for the task of facing down arrows and fireballs. As Brint takes point, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind him, using the column of safety that his massive ice shield creates to advance upon the cultists' position. It's a bit of a squeeze, especially with both Brint and Gweyr having to take cover behind his shield, but maybe being squeezed between two slabs of meat isn't all that bad... Slow but resolute and utterly inexorable, Brint advances upon the fortifications like a mighty glacier, keeping an even pace and his shield raised; barbed arrows and bolts of flame rain down upon his shield and armor with vitriolic hissing aplenty, but it doesn't shatter or melt. His sheer size means that one or two firebolts clip his shoulders from an angle, but ice armor is arguably the best defense against such missiles, and nothing manages to stop his advance despite him not even bothering to take any kind of evasive action and simply absorbing everything with his shield. "You know, you shouldn't overrely on that thing," Gweyr mutters as an arrow clips her shin, whistling through her fur and narrowly avoiding drawing blood. "It's strong, but not infinitely so." "It's strong enough," Brint replies through gritted teeth. Seeing their defense being breached, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. It's a fight! |You don't have time to waste. [party.hasCompanions |Looking around, you shout for [party.compNames true] to get in under the cover of your shield. Seeing you come at them, the cultists loose another salvo, and another — some fall wide, others slam into your shield, and one or two nick your skin, stinging as the barbed heads manage to draw blood. Whatever, better a scrape or two's than being turned into a pincushion[pc.isDK | — but you'll be sure to make them pay dearly for this ]. Breaking into a sprint as the fortifications draw near, you soon close the distance[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] hot in your wake ], and the cultists drop their bows and pull out blades and daggers to meet you in the melee. "Now this is something that's more my style," Gweyr snarls as she slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Up close and personal." It's a fight! |"Shit," Gweyr snarls.
