]那些魔法屏障的碎片如同破碎的窗玻璃般纷纷坠落，随后便消失得无影无踪，导致你在瞬间视线模糊。看到自己的防御被突破了，那些邪教徒们立刻放下了弓，拔出了刀刃和匕首，准备进入近战状态。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ |你没有时间可以浪费。趁着针对你方向的攻击暂时停止，你采取防御性半蹲姿势，同时举起了武器。 [pc.offhand] 以一定角度迎接着下一波即将袭来的攻击。你还没来得及稳住身体，一支箭就已经精准地射中了你 [pc.offhand]当带刺的头部刺入盾牌表面时，你会因为那剧烈的冲击而不由自主地抽动前臂。哎哟，如果那刺真的击中了目标，那后果肯定非常严重。 [party.hasCompanions |环顾四周，你大声呼喊着。 [party.compNames true] 躲在你的保护伞下，确保在当前情况下，所有人都处于尽可能安全的状态。 |没什么别的办法了，只能快步走起来，让自己保持清醒。 ]你毅然举盾向前冲去。必须在那些混蛋再次射出箭矢，或者更糟的是用火箭直接击中你之前，缩短与他们的距离！当然，那些恶魔可丝毫没有放松攻势。看到你向他们冲去，那些邪教徒又发射了一阵子弹——有些子弹落空了，有些则击中了你的盾牌，还有一两颗划破了你的皮肤，那些带刺的弹头确实让你的皮肤感到剧痛。不过，被划几道伤总比被彻底撕成碎片要好得多吧。[pc.isDK | — 但你必须让他们为此付出沉重的代价。 ]随着防御工事逐渐靠近，你突然加速奔跑，很快便缩短了与它们的距离。[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] 紧随其后 ]那些邪教徒立刻放下弓箭，拔出刀刃和匕首，准备与你进行近战。“这才是我喜欢的战斗方式，”格维尔低吼着，将长矛的矛柄猛地刺向其中一个恶魔的侧身。“近身战斗，才够过瘾。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ |该死，”格维尔低吼道，“前路无路，后路也被堵住了，而且他们的射程比我们远。我以前经历过更糟糕的情况……但我也不再像年轻时那样精力充沛了，运气在过去确实帮了我很多，这次我真的不能再依赖它了。”那也只能这样了。“尽量贴近地面行动！ [pc.agilityRange 70 |你迅速蹲倒在那些古老的石板上，滚成一团，然后迅速爬起来，尽量保持低矮的姿势。你知道，在这个开阔的走廊里，每一刻都至关重要，于是你拼命地向路障跑去，尽可能地曲折前进，同时仍要尽快到达目标。幸运的是 [party.compNames]那些狂热信徒已经认定你是这里最大的威胁，因此他们把所有的攻击都集中在你身上，企图将你消灭。这种说法或许有点奉承的意味，不过你确实没有必要过于担心其他人，除了你自己之外。但另一方面，你也面临着巨大的压力，必须坚持下去。虽然那些时刻只有短短几秒钟，但那确实是一段极其煎熬的时光。不止一次，箭矢在距离你的身体只有几英寸的地方飞过，那些带刺的箭头随时都有可能刺中你 [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]不过，你的动作足够敏捷，反应速度也快得足以在最后一刻及时调整方向，躲开攻击。火箭灼烧着你的头发，烫伤了你的皮肤，但幸运的是，这些攻击并没有造成实质性的伤害——尽管你会觉得自己的皮肤仿佛正在被烧焦一样。有几颗带刺的箭头还是刺在了你的 [pc.armor] 虽然会流些血，但至少你受的伤不会比一些轻微的擦伤更严重。那些狂信徒在试图击败你的过程中，显然过于依赖数量而非质量，现在他们正在为此付出代价。最终，你终于距离那道路障只有一步之遥了，但战斗还没有结束。拔出你的 [pc.weapon] 与[party.compNames]一起那些敌人紧追不舍，你用肩膀撞开最近的恶魔，凭借出色的敏捷性跳过了它。时间仿佛在这一刻变得缓慢起来——你稳稳地踩在另一个邪教弓手的胸膛上，将他重重撞倒在地，让他摔在城堡古老的石墙上，发出“咚”的一声；可惜，这些恶魔的体质异常顽强，它们很快就又站了起来，继续追击你。尽管你的华丽登场并未让他们感到惊慌，剩下的那些邪教徒还是放下了弓，抽出了那些外形凶险的刀刃和匕首，纷纷逼近你，准备与你进行近战。 |你迅速蹲倒在那些古老的石板上，滚成一团，然后迅速站起身来，尽量保持低矮的姿势。那些邪教徒们已经很聪明地清理掉了通往这里的障碍物和任何可能提供掩护的物体，但现在退路已经被切断了——要么继续前进，要么等着被烤成肉饼。而你绝对不会让这些混蛋得逞，让他们享受到后一种结果。 尽管你试图以最混乱的方式移动，尽可能地来回曲折穿行，但你的速度和反应能力仍然远远达不到那种能够通过简单的闪避来避开所有针对你的魔法攻击和导弹攻击的人所应具备的水平。幸运的是， [party.compNames] ——而对你们来说不幸的是——那些狂热信徒已经意识到你们才是这里最大的威胁，因此他们正在集中力量试图将你们消灭。这或许有点夸张，不过你们确实没有必要过于担心其他人，除了自己之外。但另一方面，你们也面临着巨大的压力，必须坚持下去。毕竟 [pc.armor] 这虽然让你免于死亡，但当你终于冲破最后一段距离，抵达路障前时，你也已经伤痕累累了。 [party.compNames] 迅速落在了队伍的最后。“今天不行，”格维尔怒吼着，将长矛狠狠刺向其中一个恶魔的侧身。“今天绝对不行，你们这些混蛋。”那些邪教徒早已预料到了这一招，他们放下弓箭，拔出带锯齿的刀刃和匕首，准备近身搏斗。他们的动作迅速而井然有序，显然他们接受过专门的训练。但在战斗真正开始之后，谁为他们提供了这种训练，这个问题便立刻被抛到了脑后。 ] 这是一场激烈的战斗！ ]
rows.raw: " Motioning to [party.som |Gweyr |Gweyr and [party.compNames true] |Gweyr, [party.compNames true] ] to spring at a moment's notice, you wait for a lull in the barrage headed your way before giving the signal. [var0 |Arona snaps into action, the burly orcess pulling her shield out and holding the massive thing up at an angle as she takes point ahead of the party. She's clearly more than eager to get into the action but not so much as to arrive there a pincushion, your thoughts are cut short as she grabs you by the scruff of your neck and pulls you into the cover of her pavise. "Stop fucking around and get in close with me!" Once you're safely pressed against her, Arona [party.som | |angles her shield to cover both Gweyr and you as you advance. It's a tight fit, sandwiched between two burly women, but if you weren't in imminent danger maybe it wouldn't be so bad after all |reaches for [companion2.name] and helps [companion2.himHer] into the cover her shield affords, Gweyr bringing up the back. Wide as it is and with you all in single file, her shield is still barely enough to afford you as much cover as it does, and you hear Gweyr grunt as a barbed arrow nicks her pelt ]. "Gonna be a bit of a squeeze, but better than nothing." As if proving her point, a bolt of magical fire whistles down and lands smack in Arona's shield, the runes carved into hide and wood flaring up but still leaving an ugly scorch mark upon its face. She snarls and roars a curse [pc.ora orc |that would have made your mother blush |in suitably ferocious orcish ], then breaks into a broad-shouldered charge straight for the fortifications, dragging the rest of you in her wake to avoid being exposed to the missile fire coming from the cultists. She doesn't even bother to duck and weave, instead taking the straightest and most direct route into the defenses; a last desperate salvo of arrows and flame manages to singe Arona's arms and legs, painting her green skin with blood and soot. That only enrages her more as she bowls straight into the barricade and shoulders the nearest demon, snarling toothily in genuine orcish battle-rage. "Demons? You aren't worth the fucking after I'm done with you!" Looks like Arona's got her blood up. Bringing up the rear, the lot of you move to back up the orcess as the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike. It's a fight! |"Come on!" Brint says, hefting his shield of ice. "I'll lead." With him in his suit of ice armor, you have to admit he's best suited for the task of facing down arrows and fireballs. As Brint takes point, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind him, using the column of safety that his massive ice shield creates to advance upon the cultists' position. It's a bit of a squeeze, especially with both Brint and Gweyr having to take cover behind his shield, but maybe being squeezed between two slabs of meat isn't all that bad... Slow but resolute and utterly inexorable, Brint advances upon the fortifications like a mighty glacier, keeping an even pace and his shield raised; barbed arrows and bolts of flame rain down upon his shield and armor with vitriolic hissing aplenty, but it doesn't shatter or melt. His sheer size means that one or two firebolts clip his shoulders from an angle, but ice armor is arguably the best defense against such missiles, and nothing manages to stop his advance despite him not even bothering to take any kind of evasive action and simply absorbing everything with his shield. "You know, you shouldn't overrely on that thing," Gweyr mutters as an arrow clips her shin, whistling through her fur and narrowly avoiding drawing blood. "It's strong, but not infinitely so." "It's strong enough," Brint replies through gritted teeth. With the last handful of steps upon the fortifications, Brint breaks into a sudden sprint, dragging the rest of you along with him lest you be exposed to the cultists' fire. Barrelling straight for the nearest demon who's fumbling to draw a jagged-edged sword, he tackles the cultist, sending the line into disarray while the lot of you back him up, spreading out to take advantage of the chaos. Seeing their defense fail, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. It's a fight! |"It's okay," Atugia says, stepping out from the corner. "Behind me!" You briefly wonder what she's doing, then realize her intentions as the next salvo of missiles hurtle through the air at her — and are stopped cold by a crackling bubble of runic energy. With her making down the hallway, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind Atugia, entering the glimmering blue bubble before it seals entirely. It's a bit of a squeeze given what your dullahan companion can manage, but better some cover than nothing at all. How long can she keep this up for? "Not too long now!" "Then we'd better move fast." Without another word, Gweyr grabs Atugia by about the waist, lifting her clean off the ground and starting off into a brisk jog. Atugia yelps, then settles down when she realizes what Gweyr is about and concentrates on maintaining the runic barrier while Gweyr brings up the fore. Seeing your advance speed towards their position, the demon cultists redouble their efforts; flame and arrowhead alike slam into the shield of runic light, hairline cracks starting to run across its surface as you close the distance. It's just your good fortune, but the exact moment Atugia's shield gives out is the exact moment [silly |Gweyr throws her like a caber into the nearest demon cultist, bowling over their ranks as your dullahan companion lands squarely in his chest |you close the distance, weapons drawn ]; splinters of the magical barrier fall away like a broken window pane before dissolving into nothingness, blinding you for a moment. Seeing their defense being breached, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. It's a fight! |You don't have time to waste. Taking advantage of the lull in the barrage headed your direction, you take a defensive half-crouch and raise your [pc.offhand] at an angle to meet the next impending salvo. Barely have you steadied yourself before an arrow lands smack into your [pc.offhand], making your forearm jerk from the sharp impact as the barbed head digs into the shield's surface. Yeowch, that looks like it'd have been nasty had it actually managed to find its mark. [party.hasCompanions |Looking around, you shout for [party.compNames true] to get in under the cover of your shield. Once you're sure everyone's as safe as can be given the circumstances |There's nothing for it. Breaking into a brisk, braced walk ], you press ahead resolutely with your shield raised. You've got to close the distance before those bastards can loose more arrows at you, or even worse, strike you dead-on with a firebolt! Not that the demons are slacking any. Seeing you come at them, the cultists loose another salvo, and another — some fall wide, others slam into your shield, and one or two nick your skin, stinging as the barbed heads manage to draw blood. Whatever, better a scrape or two's than being turned into a pincushion[pc.isDK | — but you'll be sure to make them pay dearly for this ]. Breaking into a sprint as the fortifications draw near, you soon close the distance[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] hot in your wake ], and the cultists drop their bows and pull out blades and daggers to meet you in the melee. "Now this is something that's more my style," Gweyr snarls as she slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Up close and personal." It's a fight! |"Shit," Gweyr snarls. "No easy way forward, no easy way back, and they outrange us. I've survived worse... but I'm not as young as I used to be, and luck's carried me enough through my younger years that I don't want push her." Nothing for it, then. "Keep close to the ground!" [pc.agilityRange 70 |You drop to the old flagstones and turn into a roll, scrambling to your feet in short order, keeping yourself as low as possible. Knowing every moment out in the open hallway counts, you make a mad dash for the barricade, zigzagging as erratically as you can while still making expedient progress towards your goal. Fortunately for [party.compNames], the cultists have figured that you're the biggest threat here and are focusing their fire on you in an attempt to bring you down. Flattering, perhaps, and you definitely don't need to worry that much about anyone besides yourself, but on the other hand there's a lot of pressure on you to stay standing. It's but a few seconds, but those are harrowing seconds indeed. More than once, an arrow comes within inches of burying its cruel, barbed head into your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun], but you're light enough on your feet and blessed with quick enough reflexes to catch yourself in the nick of time and hurl yourself the other way. A firebolt singes your hair and chars your skin, but fortunately doesn't do any real damage even if you feel like your flesh is being seared alive. Several of the barbed heads catch in your [pc.armor] and draw blood, but at least you don't suffer wounds any more serious than a couple of stinging grazes. The cultists were clearly depending too much on quantity instead of quality in their attempt to bring you down, and are paying the price for it. Eventually, you're finally within arm's reach of the barricade, but the fight's not over yet. Drawing your [pc.weapon] with [party.compNames] hot on your heels, you shoulder-check the nearest demon and leap over him with your superior agility. Time slows as you plant your feet squarely on another of the cultist bowmen's chests, sending him sprawling off his post and to the castle's ancient stones with an %"oomph"; alas, neither stay down for long, their demonic constitutions having them up and on their feet in no time. Unperturbed by your flamboyant entrance, the remaining cultists drop their bows and draw wicked-looking blades and daggers, closing in to engage you in melee. |You drop to the old flagstones and turn into a roll, scrambling to your feet in short order, keeping yourself as low as possible. The cultists have been smart enough to clear the approach of debris and any other potential cover, but with retreat being out of the question, it's either move in or wait to be turned into a roasted pincushion, and you're not giving these bastards the satisfaction of the latter. Though you move in as erratic a fashion as possible and zigzag as much as you can, you've simply nowhere near the impressive speed and reflexes someone would need in order to evade the hail of magic and missile alike aimed at you simply by dodging. Fortunately for [party.compNames] — and unfortunately for you — the cultists have figured that you're the biggest threat here and are focusing their fire in an attempt to bring you down. Flattering, perhaps, and you definitely don't need to worry that much about anyone besides yourself, but on the other hand there's a lot of pressure on you to stay standing. While your [pc.armor] saves you from certain death, you're far from unscathed as you finally close the last of the distance to the barricades, [party.compNames] quickly bringing up the rear. "Not today," Gweyr snarls as slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Not today, you bastards." The cultists are prepared for this move, and drop their bows to brandish serrated blades and daggers, moving in to meet you in melee. Their actions are quick and disciplined, and it's clear they've been trained for this. Who supplied the training is a question that's dashed from your mind as the battle begins in earnest. ] It's a fight! ] "

rows.original: There's nothing for it, evaluate your options and charge the fortification.
rows.translation: 别无选择，仔细权衡各种方案，然后全力攻占那座堡垒吧。
rows.raw: "There's nothing for it, evaluate your options and charge the fortification."

rows.original: [var0 |If there's one thing you've learned about Tollus's demons from your experiences with them, it's that they're all incorrigibly horny. Grabbing a vial of wyvern venom from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the tinkle of shattering glass to echo down to you, followed by coughing and a bit of grunting and moaning. While these demons are actually a bit more disciplined than the others you've come across and haven't been outright sent into an orgy by the scent of the aphrodisiac cloud, the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the venom cloud's lingering effects. |If there's one thing you've learned about dug-in foes, it's that smoking them out tends to work. Grabbing a jug of naphtha from your possessions, you stuff a rag into the neck and light it as a wick, then find a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the crash of shattering ceramic to echo down to you, followed by shouts and the sounds of people attempting to beat out a fire. While the effect's bound to be limited in a place this incorrigibly damp, the lull in the demons' offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they step away from the flames. |Sure, Tollus's goons may have entrenched themselves pretty well, but you have ideas of your own. Grabbing a leananstone from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss into the air, timing it so it'll discharge above the barricade. Even with your eyes averted and ears covered, the flash of light and deafening boom that echoes down from the corridor shakes you to the bone. While these demons have resilience that surpasses that of ordinary people and probably aren't going to be outright disabled by the charged magical trinket, shockwave of storm energies creates a lull in the offense that you waste no time in making good use of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. Rubbing watering eyes and struggling to stand on unsteady legs, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the leananstone's lingering effects. |It's an expenditure of a precious resource, but if not now, then when? Grabbing the ley-crystal grenade from your possessions, you twist the two halves of the orb, feeling something within snap and give way. From there, it's just a matter of finding a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. Your breath catches in your throat, then the roar of heat and light comes down the corridor to you, punctuated by a scream or two. While the defenses have absorbed most of the blast and now lie in ruins, the demons' firing line has been thrown into disarray by the blast and the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they struggle to stand and form a defensive line. ] It's a fight!
rows.translation: [var0 |如果说从与托勒斯恶魔们的交手中你学到了什么的话，那就是它们全都无可救药地好色。你从自己的物品中拿出一小瓶双足飞龙毒液，在压制性火力的间隙，将它狠狠扔向那些邪教徒的据点。 不一会儿，玻璃碎裂的声音便传到了你的耳边，紧接着是咳嗽声以及一些哼哼声和呻吟声。虽然这些恶魔实际上比你之前遇到的那些要守纪律一些，没有因为那股催情云的气味而陷入疯狂，但这种进攻的暂时停歇正是你可以利用的机会。集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格维尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格维尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在据点的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，他们在试图摆脱毒云的持续影响的同时，也与你们展开了激战。 |如果说关于那些顽固的敌人，你有什么体会的话，那就是把他们引出来通常是个有效的办法。从你的物品中拿出一壶石脑油，把一块布塞进瓶口并点燃它作为导火索，然后趁敌方压制性火力有所减弱的时候，把这个燃烧的容器扔向那些邪教徒的据点。 不一会儿，破碎陶瓷撞击地面发出的声响便传到了你的耳边，紧接着是人们的呼喊声以及试图扑灭大火的声音。虽然在这种潮湿的环境中，这些措施的效果必然会大打折扣，但恶魔的攻击暂时停止了，这正是你可以利用的机会。集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格维尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格维尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在阵地上的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，即使他们刚刚才从火焰中逃出来，也立刻加入了战斗。 |当然，托勒斯的手下们可能已经把守得非常严密，但你自己也有办法。你从随身携带的物品中拿出一块长石，在压制性火力暂时停歇的瞬间，将它高高抛向空中，确保它能够落在路障的上方。 即使你闭着眼睛、捂着耳朵，从走廊里传来的闪光与震耳欲聋的爆炸声依然会让你浑身发抖。这些恶魔的恢复力远超常人，那些带电的魔法饰品很可能无法彻底击败它们，但风暴能量的冲击波确实为你的反击创造了机会，你毫不犹豫地抓住了这个机会。集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格维尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格维尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们冲向那些占据有利位置的邪教徒，拔出了武器。那些恶魔眼中含泪，脚步不稳，但他们还是放下了弓，匆忙加入近战，试图在摆脱那些石块带来的影响的同时与你们展开战斗。 |这是一种对珍贵资源的消耗，但如果不现在行动，那还要等到什么时候呢？从自己的物品中取出那颗能量水晶手雷，你扭动球体的两半，感觉到里面的某个部件突然断裂、松开了。接下来，只需要在敌方密集的火力间隙中，将手雷狠狠扔向那些邪教徒的据点即可。 你的呼吸瞬间变得急促起来，紧接着，一阵由热浪与光芒构成的巨响沿着走廊朝你袭来，其间还不时传来一两声尖叫。虽然防御设施已经吸收了大部分冲击力，如今早已沦为废墟，但那些恶魔的攻击线也因为这次爆炸而陷入混乱，这种进攻上的停滞正是你可以利用的机会。集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格维尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格维尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在据点中的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，他们在努力站稳脚跟、组成防御阵型的同时，也与你们展开了激战。 ] 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " [var0 |If there's one thing you've learned about Tollus's demons from your experiences with them, it's that they're all incorrigibly horny. Grabbing a vial of wyvern venom from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the tinkle of shattering glass to echo down to you, followed by coughing and a bit of grunting and moaning. While these demons are actually a bit more disciplined than the others you've come across and haven't been outright sent into an orgy by the scent of the aphrodisiac cloud, the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the venom cloud's lingering effects. |If there's one thing you've learned about dug-in foes, it's that smoking them out tends to work. Grabbing a jug of naphtha from your possessions, you stuff a rag into the neck and light it as a wick, then find a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the crash of shattering ceramic to echo down to you, followed by shouts and the sounds of people attempting to beat out a fire. While the effect's bound to be limited in a place this incorrigibly damp, the lull in the demons' offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they step away from the flames. |Sure, Tollus's goons may have entrenched themselves pretty well, but you have ideas of your own. Grabbing a leananstone from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss into the air, timing it so it'll discharge above the barricade. Even with your eyes averted and ears covered, the flash of light and deafening boom that echoes down from the corridor shakes you to the bone. While these demons have resilience that surpasses that of ordinary people and probably aren't going to be outright disabled by the charged magical trinket, shockwave of storm energies creates a lull in the offense that you waste no time in making good use of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. Rubbing watering eyes and struggling to stand on unsteady legs, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the leananstone's lingering effects. |It's an expenditure of a precious resource, but if not now, then when? Grabbing the ley-crystal grenade from your possessions, you twist the two halves of the orb, feeling something within snap and give way. From there, it's just a matter of finding a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. Your breath catches in your throat, then the roar of heat and light comes down the corridor to you, punctuated by a scream or two. While the defenses have absorbed most of the blast and now lie in ruins, the demons' firing line has been thrown into disarray by the blast and the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they struggle to stand and form a defensive line. ] It's a fight! "

rows.original: You whirl around, expecting more foes to emerge from the shadows and blind corners of the fortifications, but there aren't any more cultists for your [pc.weapon] to meet. Looking at the battlefield laid out before you with broken arrow shafts and scorch marks peppering the masonry walls and floor, you heave a sigh of relief and finally let your guard drop for just a moment to catch your breath. "Impressive," Gweyr mumbles, the old wolfess crouching down to examine the barricade and other defenses. "The entire hallway funnelled us into a killzone that we had no way to avoid taking. If it weren't for the grace of the gods and our own strength... hm. I'm not sure that I could've done much better in my heyday given the circumstances." Is that implying that Tollus has had mercenary training for his goons? "I can't say it was mercenary training for sure, but you saw what they did. The moment they realized that they couldn't win, they disengaged instead of fleeing. A retreat instead of a rout. That doesn't happen with greenhorns you pull in off the street, and it's not something you'd expect from members of a crazy cult. It's professional. Whether this means Tollus has acquired the backing of some kind of state or he's managed to charm someone with actual skill into his ranks, I don't know. What I do know is that it's bad." Well, damn. The demons who fled... they're going to tell their fellows that you're here. "We'd best not give them time to prepare. I'll sweep this position, but we should be ready to move shortly." [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona atugia quintillus kiyoko einin azyrran etheryn |You note a distracted look on Viviane's face, and approach the witch. Is something wrong? "[viv.isDemon|Ah, just quieting some thoughts. During the fight, I started to ask questions of myself that I hadn't in a long time. Years, even. I'm just attempting to figure out what caused them.|I... I'm not sure. During that fight and since, I've just been... thinking, I suppose. Asking questions whose answers I thought I'd found years ago. Questions of purpose, and the like.]" What does she mean? "[viv.isDemon|Well, I spent a lot of time alone over the years. During that, I sometimes found myself wondering if I was making the right choice, doing the right thing with my life, things like that. But I eventually overcame those and other metaphorical demons that plagued me. But something brought those to the surface again. Be on your guard. I may have learned not to listen to the voices in my head years ago, but something tells me the others may not be so fortunate.|I spent a lot of time on my own, just traveling the woods. Time would pass and pass, and I'd find myself asking if I was really doing what I wanted. If I was a researcher and enchantress and the like because I wanted to be or because it's all I'd known. When you go so long in silence that the first time you talk to someone to trade, you feel for those opening moments as if they'd invented speech for the first time, those sorts of questions start to really dig at you. Over the years, I found my answers to them in the joy of discovery and experimentation. But something about this place makes me question again. Despite... what it is. How excited I should be. We're in ancient ruins, and I can't help but ask myself what I'm doing here. Something is wrong with this place.]" |Stepping over to Cait, you give her a light punch on the shoulder. Is she fine? She looks a little downcast. "I-I'm fine. I only took scratches back there." You can see that she doesn't have any real injuries from that scrap. What you're worried about is up there — she looks morose all of a sudden. What's up? Cait squirms a bit, then folds her ears against her head and curls her tail about a leg. "I — I just had a thought. What if all of this was pointless?" What does she mean? "I just... What if we go through all this and don't find anything that'll help me get my sister back? What if I never get Calla back? What if all of this is pointless, and there's really no way to save her? S-she could already be dead, wherever she was sent to, or worse! Oh, Mallach, seeing those twisted people... what they've become. Is that what'll happen to Calla, too? It's been so many days, weeks, since she was dragged through that portal. What if time doesn't work the same way wherever she's gone, and when we do get her back she's a withered old woman? I — " Cait screams, clutching her head and ears; it's not a pretty sound. You grab her by the shoulders and shake her until she stops, but even then tears are still pouring down her cheeks, flowing from her big blue eyes. What's gotten into her all of a sudden? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr in her search, Brint steps over to you, placing a gentle hand on your shoulder. "[pc.name]. C-could I ask you a question?" What's up? He's not the kind to be hesitant. "Y-you're okay with me, aren't you?" What kind of question is that? Of course you're okay with him, you're more than okay with him. You've placed your life in his hands more than once, and are doing so right now. Why... why this question all of a sudden? It's most unlike him. "I left home because wanted to see the world, and now that I've seen the world I've only come to understand what it was I threw away. I know my mom and sis would always take me back if I wanted to go home and stay home... but they'd also take back my dad if he showed up on the doorstep one day. Because they want to... or because they're obligated to?" You study Brint's face; he's clearly not himself, his eyes wide, his expression terrified. And yet, the fear is very, very real. "Remember when we first met, [pc.name]? I didn't know if I'd fit into Hawkethorne, even with you backing me up; all the other places I'd been to outside of the undermountain weren't the same way. Garth smiles at me every morning — but is that because I'm just a paying customer and he has to do it? How do I know he's genuine, [pc.name]? "How do I know?" |Just as you're about to join Gweyr in her search, Brienne steps over to you, placing a gentle hand on your shoulder. "[pc.name]. C-could I ask you a question?" What's up? She's not the kind to be coy about what she wants. "Do you love me?" What's gotten into her all of a sudden? Why this question, here and now? "A-answer me! Do you love me? Sure, you'll fuck all kinds of people, but you won't ever throw me away, will you?" The words are on your lips, but she's not listening. Fingers trembling, her eyes wide and darting from side to side as she [pc.heightRange 80 |clutches |looms over ] you, Brienne shivers from head to toe, and it's not from the cold. "It's okay if I'm not your first, [pc.name]. Or your second. Or your third. But I'll — I'll even be your last, if it means I can be with you forever. Say it, [pc.name]. Say you'll be with me forever!" Brienne! This isn't — "Say it!" Her scream echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle, ringing in your ears; the breath rushes from your lungs as she grabs you by the shoulders with sweaty palms and slams you into the wall. Then finally realizing what she's done, Brienne recoils from you in horror, tears welling up in her eyes as she clutches her head. |You look around, checking your surroundings for any traces of Tollus's goons, and find none. What you do discover, though, is Arona staring off down the corridor, her eyes looking as if they're fit to pop free of their sockets, her mouth slightly agape. This isn't Arona. Definitely not when she should be flush with the heat of battle, cooling off after a bout of exhilaration — stepping up, you're just about to ask if she's okay when Arona snaps to you and grabs you by the shoulders. "[pc.name]. I just realized." W-what? Maybe she should calm down a bit. What's gotten into her? "I'm going to grow old someday. I'm going to get old and weak and stupid like my brother did, and... and I won't be able to do anything any more. I won't be able to fight. I won't be able to drink. I won't even be able to get it up — all that I'll be able to do is sit or lie around all day and have some slave feed me gruel water or something while I waste away." She just beat a whole bunch of demons! What's she talking about?! "No, no, you don't see." Her breath whistles through her tusks. "I — I even if I conquer everything. If I beat everything. That means that one day, there won't be anything left to do. I'll have beaten everyone. And that'll be me. Sitting miserable and alone on my throne, an ancient piece of shit who's just waiting for someone with the balls to kick me off. Just like my brother. Oh no, oh no, oh fuck. "I've got to find something worth dying to. Or better yet, dying for before that happens! I can't just sit around waiting for Tira's crows to peck my old bones. I want to go out like an orc! A Kervus!" You watch in horror as Arona raises her [arona.weapon] and turns towards the darkness, ready to charge off alone howling into the void. There's a brief struggle between the both of you, and it's for the best that she's off-kilter — your orcish companion's weapon clatters to the ground she staggers forward, breathing heavily. Before Arona can try to go get herself killed in glorious battle, you kick it out of her reach and thump her hard on the head. |You move to help Gweyr in securing the area, but gradually become aware of a gentle tugging at your [pc.armor]. Half-turning, you find Atugia gazing [pc.heightRange 65 |up |over ] at you, biting her lip. "Hey. You got a second??" Sure. What's gotten into her all of a sudden? "I just... never mind. Gods, this feels just like back then. I just need you to tell me that I'm not a monster, okay?" Sure, she's not a monster. Why should she be? The dogged dullahan looks uncertainly at the walls, the ceiling, anywhere but directly at you. She looks as if she wants to talk, but every time she starts she stops to look around again. Finally she manages to lock eyes with you, but instead of her usual determination you see a shadow of something unlike her. It's personal. But thanks. I needed to hear that." Tui lets out the breath she's been holding, and you notice for the first time that she's been balling her fists all this while. Her knuckles have turned white by the time she relaxes and lets you go. "I mean it when I say thank you. More than you know." |As Gweyr moves to secure the area, you spy Quin staring down the hallway, eyes trained in the direction the cultists fled in; he's breathing heavily and raggedly, gaze not leaving the darkness that lurks in the eaves of the ancient jotun castle. What's up? Worried that they might circle around for a counterattack? "No, no. I just — " given the confident demeanor that Quin tends to project, or at least tries to, seeing him openly rattled is a rare moment of open weakness indeed. "I was just thinking." [pc.isDK |Thinking, huh? Well, he does a lot of that, to be sure, but it's never at the opportune moments where it would be useful. It's at this moment where you'd have expected a cocky or dirty glare from Quin, but none's forthcoming |Penny for his thoughts? Quin demurs ]. "I... shit, [pc.name]. Looking at those dumbasses who ran off... sure, Tollus is an asshole, most of the big shots are assholes... but those were probably just decent people minding their own business until Tollus and his posse came along and swept them up. And even though I'm supposed to have turned my back on them, I still played along with Tollus and his shit for too long, far too long. "I helped him get to where he is today, [pc.name]! Sure, I told myself I was just in it for the sex and the fun, but when it came down to it he's only here because me, and people like me thought the same way for all these years!" Quin makes to grab for your collar, but his hands are so shaky, his movements so uncoordinated that you see it coming a mile away and slap his hands to the side. He looks as if he might make another pass at you, then slumps his shoulders and hangs his head. "It's my fault. I made all this possible. He mightn't have reached the tipping point if not for me and the people and other stuff I helped bring in. We're down here because of me, and I get the feeling that no matter what I do to try and make things right people won't ever forgive me. That damnable pink kitten of yours won't, for one. How many people out there are like her?" Yes, but he himself acknowledged it — you gave him a chance when no one else in Hawkethorne would. Even if no one else believes in his intentions, you do enough in order to actually entrust your life into his hands and to have his back against yours. He's demonstrated as much to your satisfaction. "But that's not the point!" Quin's voice rises to a hysterical, rabbit-like whining scream that echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle. "I — if all this shit spreads beyond the Marches, who knows who and what — " You've had enough of this. Drawing back a hand, you give Quin a good hard slap on the cheek, enough to sting but hopefully not enough to cause any actual hurt. Quin just stares at you blankly, dumbfounded in the throes of his hysterics, then shivers and settles down a little. "Fuck." You won't have him putting himself down like this, and more than that, you won't have him dragging not just you, but everyone else who gave him enough credit to try a do-over through the mud. If he wants to stop the thing he helped to set into motion, if he doesn't want Tollus influence to spread to those he actually cares about, then Tollus's ass still needs kicking and he's going to pull himself together in order to do just that. "Fuck," Quin says again, this time a little less morosely. He clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then rubs his cheeks, lingering on the spot where you slapped him. "Shit. I guess... I guess you're right. We still should talk about this once we've dealt with the skinny bastard, though." |You're just about to join Gweyr in looking over the remainder of the fortifications when you hear a choked sob from Kiyoko. Your fox-wife is trying hard to hide it in the usual polite fashion of her people, but either she's getting lax, or the emotion roiling within her is too much for her to keep a lid on. ...What's the matter? "Beloved, have you ever wondered if we're doing [kiyoko.numKits 2 |our kits |Kinu ] justice by being away for so long? I do know what we are doing is necessary to give [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ] a world that's worth growing up in, but... I know you have your qualms and regrets about missing so much of our daughter's early life. One one hand, we want to protect those we love, but at the same time, we know they need to experience life on their own... ah, it is so hard to let go, for a mother who defines herself so much by her children..." ... "Ah, it is so hard to not give in to selfish desires." Look, she raised [kiyoko.numKits 2 |your kits |Kinu ] for ten years in your absence. Whatever she may think of herself or the circumstances surrounding that absence, that's an accomplishment in its own right. If something happens while you're out... Kinu is a grown woman now. She'll be able to handle it on her own. The two of you put what you had and did what you could to raise her in the proper way that you believed she should go, and that's that. Sure, you wish you could be with your family more, but if you don't go through with this there won't be a future for them. And that's what's important — it hurts, of course, oh how it hurts, but someone's got to do it and it may as well be the both of you. Does she understand? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr on her search, you find Einin curled up into a little mousy ball in a corner, hugging her knees and mumbling to herself. She doesn't look too scuffed up from the fight, but there's clearly something up with her. Something the matter? "[pc.name], have I been in the wrong all my life?" What? You understand that she's a thief, that she relishes the joy of the job, the itch of fiddling with things that she shouldn't. So long as she uses her talents for good like she's doing now, it shouldn't be a problem, should it? "But... but all the things I did, I told myself it was because I was in the right, that I needed to support Dad and the others, that they were rich and wouldn't miss it or... or... but then they'd take out their anger at being robbed on those under them, or raise their rents, or... when it comes down to it, [pc.name], how many people have I actually harmed unknowingly?" She can't possibly know that. Why worry about it? And she really needs to take a breath before she passes out from that last run-on sentence. Despite your attempt at humor, Einin isn't buying it. She claps her hands to her cheeks, shaking her head furiously, desperately. "I won't ever be forgiven for it... will I? E-Even if Dad says so... if Mom says so... it won't matter, will it?" Look. You don't know the full tale of what she did before she tried to cut your purse, nor do you ever expect her to tell you every last detail. In the same way, she'll go mad if every single possible smidge of genuine harm she might have done in her past thieving ways tries to haunt her. What she needs to do is to trust in you going forward to do the right thing. You'll make sure of that. |As you go about the cleanup, helping Gweyr search the remnants of the fortifications for anything nasty the demons might have left, you spy Azzy sitting on a sack of sand, chin cupped in her hands. If she doesn't mind, would she help you and Gweyr secure the place? "I..." Azyrran blinks her dark eyes, and her gaze snaps into focus. "Of course." Is something the matter? She looks like she's on the verge of tears right now — this isn't her. "You won't ever leave me, right?" What kind of question is that to be asking, here and now? "Just answer me! You won't ever leave me, won't you?" You've no intention of doing so, especially not here and now. What brought this on? "I... I don't know why. I just started thinking back to before we met, when I was all alone in that garden just south of the bridge. All my life, I'd had Mother, my sisters, even my brothers by my side. And then in a blink of an eye, they weren't themselves anymore. I couldn't save them... "All my life I'd taken their company, their presence for granted; it was only when they weren't around, when I felt alone, that I realized what it was. I didn't even know what it was I was missing because I didn't have any idea that it could be such a thing! I might've, should've given up after all those days, wondering, not knowing, terrified of the faces of my own family — " But she didn't. She pushed on and conquered that fear and came out on the other side stronger for it. "Thanks, [pc.name], but I'm not going to lie to myself. I didn't do it all on my lonesome — I tried, and failed. If not for you coming along, Mother wouldn't have had any chance of being saved. And as much as I was afraid of losing them back then, now I have to worry about losing you, too. There's just so much — so much — " she raises chitin-plated hands to her cheeks and shudders — "I can't help but wonder if it'd been better if I'd never known anyone, that way I don't have to fear being alone because I'd be used to it — " As sternly as you can, you grab the stooped-over Azyrran by the shoulders and shake some sense into her. Does she even know what she's saying? That she was seriously considering giving up the companionship of her mother, sisters and brothers just so that she didn't have to fear their loss? |Feeling the heat of battle leave your blood, you decide to let Gweyr get on with the search and check your surroundings. While you don't find any of Tollus's goons lurking in the shadows, ready to spring out at a moment's notice, what you do find is Ryn looking at her own hands morosely. Ryn? Is something the matter? "[pc.name]... am I fit to rule?" Where did that come from... and what kind of question is that, anyway? Of course she's fit to rule. She stood up to her sister, went all the way down alone to look for help, and finally returned to set things right in the Winter City. Of course she's fit to rule! "But... that's got nothing with actual ruling. In just the short time since Alissa's deposal, I've realized just how little I actually know — you know what Alissa was really keeping me for, as so-called Duchess of the Rim. If I didn't have Elthara to do everything for me, I'd have expended the goodwill of the people long ago." Ryn stares down at her own feet. "I-I don't know, [pc.name]. My grandmother messed up even while she tried to fix things. My parents followed in their footsteps, and Alissa... well, you know. There's so much bad blood in the var Ridells that maybe... maybe it would be better for everyone if I just abdicated and let everything start on a new leaf! Elthara does most of the work, anyway! Look at me, I'm down under the ocean gallivanting away when I should be actually trying to steward what precious little is left of the pale elves! How can I rule when I'm not even in the place to do it? All the peoples of the rift hate us! I-I — " Etheryn's flailing about now in a fit of abject panic that's most unlike her, and doesn't stop until you catch your elven companion and give her a good shake. Look, she's not abdicating anything, either her throne or her responsibilities by being down here with you. Only she can actually face down this threat to her lands and people, so she needs to be here for the Winter City. Does she understand you? Those words coming from her mouth — that's not her, that's the madness talking, and you won't have any of it. |You're about to answer Gweyr when a sudden sensation of cold clamminess comes over you, a feeling like an eel, frog or fish wet against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. Without warning, you find it hard to breathe, doubling over and wheezing, coughing as you splutter and paw at your throat. The air's just so thick that it feels like molasses, that the mere act of drawing breath is an effort; Gweyr immediately notices this and drops what she's doing to rush over and thump you hard on the back and sides. "Breathe, damn it!" In that moment, your throat burns and you feel like your eye are going to pop clean of their sockets, but with a final splutter whatever that was constricting your airway loosens and you heave a tremendous sigh of relief. Air, sweet air... as cold and miserable as it is, it's still welcome. ] "It's this place," Gweyr growls as she grabs you by the arm. "When I was young digging around in the heartlands with Garth, they called it ruin sickness. When people go far down below the earth, away from the sun for hours, days, weeks... their minds start going crazy. No one really knows what causes it. This, though, it's more than that. We haven't been down here for that long, and already..." The demons looked and acted perfectly fine. "Those bastards were already insane, and you know it." You... you can feel it. A whisper on the edge of your hearing, yet you can swear you haven't heard a word. There's something about this place that's getting to you, probing your mind for weaknesses, trying to find a fracture, a fault to wrench open. "We should get a move on. If we stay here too long, who knows what might happen to us even if we win. I've got precious few of my years remaining to me, and I don't intend to spend them cippled with the shakes." You have no idea what the shakes are, but they don't sound like anything you'd want to contract. Yes, time to get a move on before your thoughts can start straying again...
rows.translation: 你迅速转身，期待着会有更多的敌人从防御工事的阴影处或隐蔽角落里出现，但实际上已经没有更多的邪教徒了 [pc.weapon] 看着眼前这片布满折断的箭杆和烧焦痕迹的战场，砖石墙壁和地面上都留下了这些痕迹，你终于松了一口气，暂时放下了警惕，喘了口气。 真是令人印象深刻，”格维尔低声说道。那头老母狼蹲下来仔细检查那些路障和其他防御设施。“整个走廊的设计简直把我们逼入了一个必死的区域，我们根本没有任何办法可以避开它。多亏了诸神的恩典，以及我们自身的力量，才能成功逃脱。嗯……在那种情况下，我不确定自己在巅峰时期能否做得更好。”这是不是意味着托勒斯让他的手下接受了雇佣兵训练？“我不能肯定地说确实如此。雇佣兵当然需要进行训练，但你们已经看到了他们的表现。当他们意识到自己无法获胜时，他们选择退出战斗而不是逃跑——这是一种有组织的撤退，而不是溃败。这种行为绝不会出现在那些从街头招来的新手身上，也更不符合那些极端狂热组织的成员应有的作风。这太专业了。我不知道这是意味着托勒斯获得了某个国家的支持，还是说他真的用自己的能力说服了某些人加入他的阵营，但我可以肯定的是，这绝对不是什么好事。唉，真糟糕。那些逃走的恶魔……他们会把你的存在告诉他们的同伙的。“我们最好不要给他们准备的时间。我会清理这个区域，但我们也应该尽快准备行动。 [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona atugia quintillus kiyoko einin azyrran etheryn |你注意到薇薇安的脸上带着心不在焉的神情，于是走过去询问那位女巫：“是不是出了什么问题？[viv.isDemon|啊，只是在整理一些思绪。在战斗的过程中，我开始问自己一些很久以来都没有问过的问题——甚至是好几年的时间都没有问过的问题。我只是在试图弄清楚，究竟是什么导致了这些疑问的产生。|我……我不太确定。在那场战斗之后，我一直都在……思考，大概可以这么说吧。我在追问一些问题，而那些答案，我原以为自己早在多年前就已经找到了。关于人生目标之类的问题。]她这话是什么意思？[viv.isDemon|这些年来，我确实花了很多时间独自一人。在那些日子里，我有时会怀疑自己是否做出了正确的选择，是否在正确地度过自己的人生，诸如此类的问题。但最终，我战胜了那些困扰我的念头以及其他各种心理障碍。然而，现在有些事情让它们再次浮上了表面。你们要提高警惕——虽然多年前我就学会了不再听那些内心中的声音，但我有预感，其他人可能就没有那么幸运了。|我花了很多时间独自在森林里漫游。时间一点点流逝，我开始质疑自己是否真的在做自己想做的事情。我是真的想成为一名研究者或一位女巫呢，还是仅仅因为我想成为那样的人，又或者因为那是我一直以来所熟悉的生活方式呢？当你长时间保持沉默，直到第一次与他人交谈进行交易时，你会感受到那些最初的对话时刻，仿佛人们是第一次发明了语言一样。这类问题会开始不断地萦绕在你的脑海中。这些年来，我是在探索与尝试的乐趣中找到了这些问题的答案。但这个地方有些地方让我再次产生了疑问。尽管……原因是什么。究竟为什么呢？兴奋不已我确实是这么想的。我们现在身处古老的废墟之中，我不禁会问自己，自己究竟为什么会来到这里。肯定有什么原因错误与这个地方相关。]" |你走到凯特身边，轻轻拍了拍她的肩膀。她没事吧？她看起来有点沮丧。“我、我没事的。只是在那场争执中受了些擦伤而已。”你可以看出，那场争执并没有给她造成任何严重的伤害。你担心的事情就在上面——她突然看起来很沮丧，怎么了？凯特扭动了一下身体，然后把耳朵贴在头上，把尾巴绕在腿上。“我……我只是突然想到一个问题：如果这一切都是毫无意义的，那该怎么办呢？她这话是什么意思？“我只是……如果我们费了这么大劲，却什么都没找到，无法帮我找回妹妹，那该怎么办？如果我从不把卡拉救回来？但如果这一切都是徒劳的，真的没有任何办法救她的话怎么办？她可能已经死了，无论被送到了哪里，甚至可能会遭遇更糟的事情！哦，马拉克，看到那些被扭曲的人们……他们已经变成了那样。卡拉也会变成那样吗？自从她被送进那个传送门之后，已经过去了好多天、好多周了。如果在她去到的那个地方，时间的流逝方式与我们这里不同，那么当我们做把她弄回来，她不过是个枯萎的老女人罢了……我——”凯特尖叫着，双手抱住头和耳朵；那声音实在很难听。你抓住她的肩膀摇晃她，直到她停止尖叫，但即便如此，泪水依然从她那双蓝色的大眼睛里涌出，顺着脸颊流下来。她突然间怎么了？ |就在你准备加入格维尔的搜寻行动时，布林特走了过来，轻轻地将手放在你的肩上。[pc.name]可以问你一个问题吗？”怎么了？他可不是会犹豫的人啊。“你……你没意见吧？”这算什么问题啊？你当然没意见啊，你更多你对他应该没有意见才对。你不止一次将自己的生命交到他手中，现在也是如此。为什么……为什么突然会提出这样的问题？这完全不符合他的性格。“我离开家是因为想看看这个世界，而现在当我真正看到了这个世界之后，我才意识到自己究竟放弃了什么。我知道，如果我想回家的话，妈妈和姐姐一定会接我回去……但要是爸爸有一天出现在家门口，她们也会接他回去。是因为她们愿意这么做，还是因为觉得有这个责任呢？ 你仔细观察布林特的表情，他显然已经不是原来的自己了，他的眼睛瞪得大大的，脸上充满了恐惧。然而，这种恐惧却是真实存在的。“还记得我们第一次见面的时候吗 [pc.name]我不知道，即使有你的支持，我是否真的能够适应鹰棘镇的生活；在山腹深域之外，我去过的其他地方都与这里截然不同。加思每天早上都会对我微笑——但那是因为我只是一个付费顾客，他不得不这样做吗？我怎么才能确定他的微笑是真心的呢？ [pc.name]我该怎么做呢？知道?" |就在你即将加入格薇尔一起开始寻找的时候，布蕾妮走了过来，轻轻地将手放在你的肩上。[pc.name]能请你回答一个问题吗？”怎么了？她可不是那种会对自己想要的东西遮遮掩掩的人。“你爱我吗？”她突然怎么了？为什么偏偏在这个时候问这个问题？“回答我！你爱我吗？当然，你可以和各种各样的人上床，但你永远不会抛弃我，对吧？”这些话已经到了你的嘴边，但她根本没有在听。她的手指在颤抖，眼睛睁得大大的，不停地在四处张望 [pc.heightRange 80 |握住 |如影随形 ] 你，布蕾妮从头到足部都在发抖，但这并不是因为寒冷。“如果我不是你的第一个……那也没关系。 [pc.name]或者你的第二个选择。又或者你的第三个选择。但我愿意——即使成为你的最后一个选择，只要这意味着我能永远与你在一起。说出来吧。 [pc.name]告诉我，你会永远和我在一起！”布蕾妮！这不是 说出来！ 她的尖叫声在古老的巨魔城堡的走廊里回荡，久久不能消散，仿佛仍萦绕在你的耳边；当她用汗湿的双手抓住你的肩膀，将你猛地撞向墙壁时，你的呼吸几乎被堵在喉咙里。直到这时，布蕾妮才终于意识到自己做了什么，她惊恐地后退了几步，泪水在眼中打转，双手紧紧抱住自己的头。 |你环顾四周，仔细检查周围环境，试图寻找托勒斯的打手们的任何踪迹，但一无所获。你做然而，你发现阿罗娜正站在走廊的尽头，她的双眼仿佛要从眼眶里瞪出来一样，嘴巴也微微张开。这根本不是阿罗娜。当她应该因为战斗的激情而面红耳赤、在兴奋之后逐渐平静下来的时候，她现在却完全不是这个样子——你刚要上前去问她是否没事，阿罗娜突然转过身来，抓住你的肩膀。[pc.name]我刚刚才意识到。”“什、什么？也许她应该先冷静一下。她到底发生了什么？”“总有一天我会变老的。我会变得像我哥哥那样老弱无力、愚笨不堪，然后……我就再也不能做任何事情了。我将无法战斗，也无法饮酒，甚至连站立都做不到——我所能做的，就是整天坐着或躺着，让别人把稀粥之类的东西喂到我嘴里，就这样慢慢消瘦下去。 她刚刚打败了一群恶魔！她在说什么呢？！“不，不，你没有明白。”她的呼吸从獠牙间呼出，“即使我征服了一切，即使我战胜了所有敌人，那也意味着总有一天，我会遇到 something 我无法战胜的东西做到那时，我将会打败所有人。而最终，我会独自一人、凄惨地坐在王座上——成为一个被所有人抛弃的废物，只是等待着有勇气的人来把我赶下王座。就像我的兄弟一样……哦不，哦不，该死。“我必须找到值得为之赴死的东西。或者，更确切地说，找到让我愿意为之献出生命的理由。为了在那之前！我可不能坐以待毙，等着提拉的乌鸦来啄食我的骨头。我想要像一个兽人一样壮烈地死去……像一个凯尔维斯一样！你惊恐地看着阿罗娜举起了她的 [arona.weapon] 它转身朝着暗影冲去，准备独自冲进虚无之中，发出凄厉的嚎叫。你们之间发生了一场短暂的挣扎，而她此刻处于混乱状态，反倒是一件好事——你的兽人同伴手中的武器掉落在地上，她踉跄着向前走去，呼吸变得急促而沉重。在阿罗娜试图去赴那场壮烈的死亡之战之前，你一足部将武器踢出了她的触及范围，然后狠狠地敲在了她的头上。 |你前往协助格维尔控制该区域，但渐渐察觉到有人正在轻轻拉扯你 [pc.armor]你微微转身，发现阿图吉娅正凝视着什么 [pc.heightRange 65 |向上 |超过 ] 喂，有空吗？”“当然有空。她突然怎么了？”“我只是……算了。天啊，这种感觉简直和那时候一模一样。我只是需要你告诉我，我并不是个怪物，好吗？当然，她并不是什么怪物。她为什么要成为怪物呢？ 那只固执的动物不安地望着墙壁、天花板，就是不敢直视你的眼睛。它看起来好像想说话，但每次刚开口，又会停下来环顾四周。终于，她成功地与你的目光对上了，但与你平时所见她的坚定神情不同，你从中看到了一丝与她以往性格不符的阴郁。“这是私人的事情。不过还是谢谢你，我确实需要听到这些话。”崔终于松开了她一直紧握的拳头，你这才注意到，她整个过程中都在紧握着双拳。直到她放松下来，放开你的手时，她的指关节都已经变白了。“我说谢谢，是真心的。这份感激之情，远超你的想象。 |当格维尔前去控制该区域时，你注意到昆因正盯着走廊的尽头，他的目光紧紧追随着那些邪教徒逃跑的方向；他呼吸急促而艰难，视线始终没有离开那座古老巨魔城堡屋檐下潜伏的暗影之处。 怎么了？是在担心他们会绕过来发动反击吗？“不，不是的。我只是……”考虑到昆因通常表现出的自信姿态，或者至少他是试图这样表现的，因此看到他如此慌乱，确实是一个难得的、暴露了他脆弱一面的时刻。我只是在思考而已。 [pc.isDK |在思考吗？嗯，他确实经常这样做，但从来都不会在那些真正需要思考的关键时刻。就在这个时候，你本应该期待看到昆因露出那种傲慢或者不屑的眼神，但实际上什么也没有发生。 |他在想什么？ ]我……该死， [pc.name]看着那些跑掉的蠢货……没错，托勒斯确实是个混蛋，大多数大人物也都是混蛋……但那些人本来可能只是些安分守己的普通人，直到托勒斯和他的那群人出现，把他们卷了进去。尽管我本应该抛弃他们，但我还是跟托勒斯和他的那些恶行一起混了太久，实在太久了。“我帮助他走到了今天这一步。 [pc.name]当然，我告诉自己，参与这些只是为了享受性爱和乐趣而已，但实际上，他之所以会在这里，完全是因为我；而这些年来，像我这样的人也一直都这么认为！”昆因试图抓住你的衣领，但他的手太颤抖了，动作也不协调，以至于你早就看出了他的意图，于是你一把拍开了他的手。他看起来好像还想再尝试接近你，但随后却耸了耸肩，低下了头。“都是我的错。这一切都是我造成的。如果没有我，以及我帮助引进的那些人和那些事情，他可能就不会走到那一步了。我们之所以会在这里，是因为我觉得，无论我做些什么来试图弥补过错，人们永远都不会原谅我。尤其是你那只该死的粉色小猫，它肯定也不会原谅我的。到底还有多少人和它一样呢？是的，但他自己也承认了这一点——在鹰棘镇，没有人愿意给他机会，而你却给了他这样的机会。即使没有人相信他的诚意，但他所做的已经足以让你放心地将自己的生命托付给他，让他成为你的后盾。他确实已经证明了这一点，让你感到满意。“但是，那并不是要点啊！”昆因的声音突然升高，变成了那种类似兔子的尖叫声，这种声音在古老的约顿城堡的走廊里回荡。“如果这一切都被传到边境以外的地方，谁知道还会招来什么后果……”你受够了这一切。你收回手，狠狠地打了昆因一记耳光，力度刚好能让他的脸发疼，但希望不会造成真正的伤害。昆因只是呆呆地望着你，正处于歇斯底里的状态中，浑身发抖，过了一会儿才稍微平静下来。 该死。”你绝不能让他继续这样自贬自己，更不能让他不仅拖累你，还连那些信任他、支持他重新尝试的人也一起陷入困境。如果他真的想阻止自己曾经推动的事情继续发展，如果他不想让托勒斯的影响波及到那些他在乎的人，那么他就必须振作起来，采取行动。 该死，”昆因又说道，这次的语气没那么沮丧了。他反复握紧又松开拳头，然后揉了揉脸颊，尤其是被你打到的地方。“靠……我想……你说的没错。不过，在解决了那个瘦子之后，我们还是应该再好好谈谈这件事。" rows.raw: " You whirl around, expecting more foes to emerge from the shadows and blind corners of the fortifications, but there aren't any more cultists for your [pc.weapon] to meet. Looking at the battlefield laid out before you with broken arrow shafts and scorch marks peppering the masonry walls and floor, you heave a sigh of relief and finally let your guard drop for just a moment to catch your breath. "Impressive," Gweyr mumbles, the old wolfess crouching down to examine the barricade and other defenses. "The entire hallway funnelled us into a killzone that we had no way to avoid taking. If it weren't for the grace of the gods and our own strength... hm. I'm not sure that I could've done much better in my heyday given the circumstances." Is that implying that Tollus has had mercenary training for his goons? "I can't say it was mercenary training for sure, but you saw what they did. The moment they realized that they couldn't win, they disengaged instead of fleeing. A retreat instead of a rout. That doesn't happen with greenhorns you pull in off the street, and it's not something you'd expect from members of a crazy cult. It's professional. Whether this means Tollus has acquired the backing of some kind of state or he's managed to charm someone with actual skill into his ranks, I don't know. What I do know is that it's bad." Well, damn. The demons who fled... they're going to tell their fellows that you're here. "We'd best not give them time to prepare. I'll sweep this position, but we should be ready to move shortly." "[viv.isDemon|Ah, just quieting some thoughts. During the fight, I started to ask questions of myself that I hadn't in a long time. Years, even. I'm just attempting to figure out what caused them.|I... I'm not sure. During that fight and since, I've just been... thinking, I suppose. Asking questions whose answers I thought I'd found years ago. Questions of purpose, and the like.]" What does she mean? "[viv.isDemon|Well, I spent a lot of time alone over the years. How many people out there are like her?" Yes, but he himself acknowledged it — you gave him a chance when no one else in Hawkethorne would. Even if no one else believes in his intentions, you do enough in order to actually entrust your life into his hands and to have his back against yours. He's demonstrated as much to your satisfaction. "But that's not the point!" Quin's voice rises to a hysterical, rabbit-like whining scream that echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle. "I — if all this shit spreads beyond the Marches, who knows who and what — " You've had enough of this. Drawing back a hand, you give Quin a good hard slap on the cheek, enough to sting but hopefully not enough to cause any actual hurt. Quin just stares at you blankly, dumbfounded in the throes of his hysterics, then shivers and settles down a little. "Fuck." You won't have him putting himself down like this, and more than that, you won't have him dragging not just you, but everyone else who gave him enough credit to try a do-over through the mud. If he wants to stop the thing he helped to set into motion, if he doesn't want Tollus influence to spread to those he actually cares about, then Tollus's ass still needs kicking and he's going to pull himself together in order to do just that. "Fuck," Quin says again, this time a little less morosely. He clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then rubs his cheeks, lingering on the spot where you slapped him. "Shit. I guess... I guess you're right. We still should talk about this once we've dealt with the skinny bastard, though." |You're just about to join Gweyr in looking over the remainder of the fortifications when you hear a choked sob from Kiyoko. Your fox-wife is trying hard to hide it in the usual polite fashion of her people, but either she's getting lax, or the emotion roiling within her is too much for her to keep a lid on. ...What's the matter? "Beloved, have you ever wondered if we're doing [kiyoko.numKits 2 |our kits |Kinu ] justice by being away for so long? I do know what we are doing is necessary to give [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ] a world that's worth growing up in, but... I know you have your qualms and regrets about missing so much of our daughter's early life. One one hand, we want to protect those we love, but at the same time, we know they need to experience life on their own... ah, it is so hard to let go, for a mother who defines herself so much by her children..." ... "Ah, it is so hard to not give in to selfish desires." Look, she raised [kiyoko.numKits 2 |your kits |Kinu ] for ten years in your absence. Whatever she may think of herself or the circumstances surrounding that absence, that's an accomplishment in its own right. If something happens while you're out... Kinu is a grown woman now. She'll be able to handle it on her own. The two of you put what you had and did what you could to raise her in the proper way that you believed she should go, and that's that. Sure, you wish you could be with your family more, but if you don't go through with this there won't be a future for them. And that's what's important — it hurts, of course, oh how it hurts, but someone's got to do it and it may as well be the both of you. Does she understand? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr on her search, you find Einin curled up into a little mousy ball in a corner, hugging her knees and mumbling to herself. She doesn't look too scuffed up from the fight, but there's clearly something up with her. Something the matter? "[pc.name], have I been in the wrong all my life?" What? You understand that she's a thief, that she relishes the joy of the job, the itch of fiddling with things that she shouldn't. So long as she uses her talents for good like she's doing now, it shouldn't be a problem, should it? "But... but all the things I did, I told myself it was because I was in the right, that I needed to support Dad and the others, that they were rich and wouldn't miss it or... or... but then they'd take out their anger at being robbed on those under them, or raise their rents, or... when it comes down to it, [pc.name], how many people have I actually harmed unknowingly?" She can't possibly know that. Why worry about it? And she really needs to take a breath before she passes out from that last run-on sentence. Despite your attempt at humor, Einin isn't buying it. She claps her hands to her cheeks, shaking her head furiously, desperately. "I won't ever be forgiven for it... will I? E-Even if Dad says so... if Mom says so... it won't matter, will it?" Look. You don't know the full tale of what she did before she tried to cut your purse, nor do you ever expect her to tell you every last detail. In the same way, she'll go mad if every single possible smidge of genuine harm she might have done in her past thieving ways tries to haunt her. What she needs to do is to trust in you going forward to do the right thing. You'll make sure of that. |As you go about the cleanup, helping Gweyr search the remnants of the fortifications for anything nasty the demons might have left, you spy Azzy sitting on a sack of sand, chin cupped in her hands. If she doesn't mind, would she help you and Gweyr secure the place? "I..." Azyrran blinks her dark eyes, and her gaze snaps into focus. "Of course." Is something the matter? She looks like she's on the verge of tears right now — this isn't her. "You won't ever leave me, right?" What kind of question is that to be asking, here and now? "Just answer me! You won't ever leave me, won't you?" You've no intention of doing so, especially not here and now. What brought this on? "I... I don't know why. I just started thinking back to before we met, when I was all alone in that garden just south of the bridge. All my life, I'd had Mother, my sisters, even my brothers by my side. And then in a blink of an eye, they weren't themselves anymore. I couldn't save them... "All my life I'd taken their company, their presence for granted; it was only when they weren't around, when I felt alone, that I realized what it was. I didn't even know what it was I was missing because I didn't have any idea that it could be such a thing! I might've, should've given up after all those days, wondering, not knowing, terrified of the faces of my own family — " But she didn't. She pushed on and conquered that fear and came out on the other side stronger for it. "Thanks, [pc.name], but I'm not going to lie to myself. I didn't do it all on my lonesome — I tried, and failed. If not for you coming along, Mother wouldn't have had any chance of being saved. And as much as I was afraid of losing them back then, now I have to worry about losing you, too. There's just so much — so much — " she raises chitin-plated hands to her cheeks and shudders — "I can't help but wonder if it'd been better if I'd never known anyone, that way I don't have to fear being alone because I'd be used to it — " As sternly as you can, you grab the stooped-over Azyrran by the shoulders and shake some sense into her. Does she even know what she's saying? That she was seriously considering giving up the companionship of her mother, sisters and brothers just so that she didn't have to fear their loss? |Feeling the heat of battle leave your blood, you decide to let Gweyr get on with the search and check your surroundings. While you don't find any of Tollus's goons lurking in the shadows, ready to spring out at a moment's notice, what you do find is Ryn looking at her own hands morosely. Ryn? Is something the matter? "[pc.name]... am I fit to rule?" Where did that come from... and what kind of question is that, anyway? Of course she's fit to rule. She stood up to her sister, went all the way down alone to look for help, and finally returned to set things right in the Winter City. Of course she's fit to rule! "But... that's got nothing with actual ruling. In just the short time since Alissa's deposal, I've realized just how little I actually know — you know what Alissa was really keeping me for, as so-called Duchess of the Rim. If I didn't have Elthara to do everything for me, I'd have expended the goodwill of the people long ago." Ryn stares down at her own feet. "I-I don't know, [pc.name]. My grandmother messed up even while she tried to fix things. My parents followed in their footsteps, and Alissa... well, you know. There's so much bad blood in the var Ridells that maybe... maybe it would be better for everyone if I just abdicated and let everything start on a new leaf! Elthara does most of the work, anyway! Look at me, I'm down under the ocean gallivanting away when I should be actually trying to steward what precious little is left of the pale elves! How can I rule when I'm not even in the place to do it? All the peoples of the rift hate us! I-I — " Etheryn's flailing about now in a fit of abject panic that's most unlike her, and doesn't stop until you catch your elven companion and give her a good shake. Look, she's not abdicating anything, either her throne or her responsibilities by being down here with you. Only she can actually face down this threat to her lands and people, so she needs to be here for the Winter City. Does she understand you? Those words coming from her mouth — that's not her, that's the madness talking, and you won't have any of it. |You're about to answer Gweyr when a sudden sensation of cold clamminess comes over you, a feeling like an eel, frog or fish wet against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. Without warning, you find it hard to breathe, doubling over and wheezing, coughing as you splutter and paw at your throat. The air's just so thick that it feels like molasses, that the mere act of drawing breath is an effort; Gweyr immediately notices this and drops what she's doing to rush over and thump you hard on the back and sides. "Breathe, damn it!" In that moment, your throat burns and you feel like your eye are going to pop clean of their sockets, but with a final splutter whatever that was constricting your airway loosens and you heave a tremendous sigh of relief. Air, sweet air... as cold and miserable as it is, it's still welcome. ] "It's this place," Gweyr growls as she grabs you by the arm. "When I was young digging around in the heartlands with Garth, they called it ruin sickness. When people go far down below the earth, away from the sun for hours, days, weeks... their minds start going crazy. No one really knows what causes it. This, though, it's more than that. We haven't been down here for that long, and already..." The demons looked and acted perfectly fine. "Those bastards were already insane, and you know it." You... you can feel it. A whisper on the edge of your hearing, yet you can swear you haven't heard a word. There's something about this place that's getting to you, probing your mind for weaknesses, trying to find a fracture, a fault to wrench open. "We should get a move on. If we stay here too long, who knows what might happen to us even if we win. I've got precious few of my years remaining to me, and I don't intend to spend them cippled with the shakes." You have no idea what the shakes are, but they don't sound like anything you'd want to contract. Yes, time to get a move on before your thoughts can start straying again... "

rows.original:
A sharp jolt of magic knocks your [pc.weapon] from your hand, and as you scramble to retrieve it more and more of the demon cultists pile onto you, stabbing away as they drag you down to the cold stone floor. Gweyr manages to hold out a little longer, but without you to back her up the sheer number of cultists soon manages to overwhelm her in much the same fashion.
    
    "We'll be taking you to see the master now," one of them hisses before delivering a sharp blow to the back of your head.
    
    The world goes dark...
rows.translation:
一阵强烈的魔法冲击力将你 [pc.weapon] 它从你手中掉落，而当你拼命试图抢回它时，越来越多的恶魔教徒扑了上来，他们一边刺你，一边将你拖向冰冷的石地面。格维尔勉强坚持了一会儿，但没有了你的支援，庞大的崇拜者人数最终还是让她陷入了同样的困境。
    
    “我们现在要带你去见大师了，”其中一个人嘶声道，随后猛地一击打在了你的后脑勺上。
    
    世界陷入了暗影……

rows.original:
You take step forward and take a gander at the mushrooms growing out of the exposed masonry flooring. They're certainly not natural — someone had to bring the things all the way to the bottom of the ocean — so presumably they're important to the cult in some way. For all you rack your brains, though, [pc.bgMulti arcanist scholar acolyte hunter barbarian
        |you don't remember these particular specimens being mentioned in any of the potions, reagents or components you'd had to study and handle as an arcanist. As far as you know, these fungi are perfectly mundane
        |you don't recall ever coming across any of these in all the texts you've ever read. Not that your scholarly inclinations were ever tilted towards natural philosophy, as it was called, but even so
        |you don't recall ever coming across any of these in all the texts you've ever read. Not that your education was ever tilted towards natural philosophy, as it was called in the seminary, but even so
        |these particular specimens are completely unfamiliar to you. It shouldn't be that surprising, given that you're far out of your depth with this one and away from lands you know as a hunter, but there was a chance
        |these particular specimens are completely unfamiliar to you. It shouldn't be that surprising, given that you're far out of your depth with this one and away from lands you know as a barbarian, but there was a chance
        |you come up with nothing — not that you ever had much reason to mess with mushrooms in your past
    ].
    
    [party.oneComp brint brienne
        |"Oh hey," Brint says, stooping down to investigate one of the mushrooms. "A plump helmet. What's this doing all the way here?"
        
        He knows what these are?
        
        "Oh, of course! Plump helmets grow all over the place in the Undermountain — Khor'minos itself has mostly moved to better food now save for the people still living in the slums, but the kobolds, batfolk and other critters make a feast out of them on the regular. You can also brew them into alcohol, but it tastes kind of disgusting, to be honest."
        
        Do they regularly pop up in places like these?
        
        Brint scratches his head at that. "Actually, no. Only place I've ever head of plump helmets growing is in and about Khor'minos itself. I don't suppose it's impossible for them to have taken root elsewhere... but it is a bit surprising. Still, if they were trying to farm in this miserable place, I couldn't have chosen a better crop than these mushrooms. They'll grow on anything, are pretty hardy, and you can subsist on them alone to boot. Only problem is... they taste of nothing."
        
        They taste awful?
        
        "No, no, not awful." Brint gesticulates with his hands. "Regardless of how much salt, how many spices you put on a plump helmet, how you prepare the cap and stalk... it always tastes like old, dead wood. There's a reason it's a poor man's meal; you don't think twice about eating literally anything else the second you can afford to."
        |"Oh hey," Brienne says, stooping down to investigate one of the mushrooms. "A plump helmet. What's this doing all the way here?"
        
        She knows what these are?
        
        "Oh, of course! Plump helmets grow all over the place in the Undermountain — Khor'minos itself has mostly moved past them to better food save for the people still living in the slums, but the kobolds, batfolk and other critters make a feast out of them on the regular. You can also brew them into alcohol, but it tastes kind of disgusting, to be honest."
        
        Do they regularly pop up in places like these?
        
        Brienne scratches her head at that. "Actually, no. Only place I've ever head of plump helmets growing is in and about Khor'minos itself. I don't suppose it's impossible for them to have taken root elsewhere... but it is a bit of a surprise. Still, if they were trying to farm in this miserable place, I couldn't have chosen a better crop than these mushrooms. They'll grow on anything, are pretty hardy, and you can subsist on them alone to boot. Only problem is... they taste of nothing."
        
        They taste awful?
        
        "No, no, not awful." Brienne gesticulates with her hands. "Regardless of how much salt, how many spices you put on a plump helmet, how you prepare the cap and stalk... it always tastes like old, dead wood. There's a reason it's a poor man's meal; you don't think twice about eating literally anything else the second you can afford to."
        |Still, they're kind of interesting. With their purple caps and squat features, they look like helmets growing out of the ground. [silly
            |Plump helmets, in fact. 
        ]Whoever would manage to stomach these kinds of things... you'd have to be mad to do so. Right? Right?
    ]
    
    Food, huh... they've been down here long enough that they've had to farm even with rations being brought down to them by ship, and by the looks of it, with some success. Demons being organized enough for farming... now that's a frightening thought. You'd never have guessed they'd be capable of focusing on something so mundane, going off the two queens among their kind you've seen.
    
    Doesn't seem to be anything you can actually learn from all this, though. Tollus's posse has been down here for some time now, but you've already figured that out given that they've had the time to build fortification and fix up the old jotun castle somewhat. Time to move on.
rows.translation:
你向前迈了一步，仔细观察那些从裸露的砖石地面中生长出来的蘑菇。这些蘑菇显然不是自然形成的——肯定有人把它们带到了海洋的最深处——所以，它们很可能对那个邪教组织有着某种重要的意义。然而，尽管你绞尽脑汁去思考，还是想不出个所以然来。 [pc.bgMulti arcanist scholar acolyte hunter barbarian
        |你并不记得作为一位奥术师，你在研究或处理过的任何药剂、试剂或成分中提到过这些特定的真菌。据你所知，这些真菌其实完全属于普通的、常见的种类。
        |你肯定不记得在自己读过的所有文本中曾经遇到过这些内容。虽然你并没有特别倾向于研究所谓的“自然哲学”，但即便如此，你也应该不记得了吧。
        |你回想起来，在自己读过的所有文本中，从未见过这些内容。当然，你的教育背景也并非偏向于神学院里所称的“自然哲学”领域，但即便如此……
        |这些特定的样本对你来说完全陌生。考虑到你在这个领域远远超出了自己的能力范围，同时也远离了你作为猎人所熟悉的地域，这种情况其实并不奇怪……不过，还是存在那么一点可能性。
        |这些特定的物种对你来说完全陌生。考虑到你在这个领域根本不懂行，而且这些地方也超出了你作为“野蛮人”所了解的范围，这种情况其实并不奇怪……不过，还是存在那么一点可能性。
        |你什么主意都没有——其实你以前也从来没有什么理由去研究蘑菇这类东西。
    ].
    
    [party.oneComp brint brienne
        |哦，嘿，”布林特说着，弯下腰去仔细观察其中一朵蘑菇。“一个胖乎乎的‘头盔’……它怎么会出现在这里呢？”
        
        他知道这些是什么吗？
        
        “哦，当然知道！在地下山脉的各个地方都能看到这种蘑菇——除了那些仍然生活在贫民区的人之外，科尔米诺斯的大多数居民现在都吃上了更好的食物，不过地精、蝙蝠人和其他一些生物还是经常把它们当作美餐来享用呢。你也可以把它们酿成酒，但说实话，味道挺难喝的。
        
        它们会经常出现在这样的地方吗？
        
        布林特听到这个问题，挠了挠头。“其实不会。我只在科尔米诺斯周边地区见过这种圆胖的头盔。不过，我也不能排除它们在其他地方也可能生长繁殖的可能性。不过，这确实有点令人惊讶。不过，如果他们真的想在这个环境恶劣的地方种植作物，的话，我实在想不出还有比这种蘑菇更好的选择了。这种蘑菇几乎可以在任何地方生长，生命力也非常顽强，而且仅仅依靠它们就能维持生计了。唯一的问题是……它们毫无味道。
        
        它们的味道很糟糕吗？”
        
        “不，不，并不糟糕。”布林特用手比划着解释道，“无论你在这些食物上加多少盐、多少香料，无论你用什么样的方法来烹饪它们……它们的味道总是像陈旧的木头一样。这就是为什么它们被称为‘穷人的食物’；一旦你有能力选择其他食物，你根本不会考虑再吃这些东西。
        |哦，嘿，”布蕾妮说着，蹲下来仔细观察其中一朵蘑菇。“一个胖乎乎的‘头盔’啊……它怎么会出现在这里呢？”
        
        她知道这些是什么吗？
        
        “哦，当然知道！在山腹深域的各个地方都能看到这种蘑菇——虽然科尔米诺斯的大多数居民早就不再吃它们了，因为他们能找到更好的食物，只有那些还住在贫民区的人还会吃它们；不过地精、蝙蝠人和其他一些生物可经常把它们当美味佳肴来享用呢。你也可以把它们酿成酒，但说实话，味道有点难喝。
        
        它们会经常出现在这样的地方吗？
        
        布蕾妮挠了挠头，说道：“其实不会。我只在科尔米诺斯附近见过这种圆胖的头盔。不过，我也不能排除它们在其他地方也可能生长繁殖的可能性。不过，这确实有点出乎我的意料。不过，如果他们真的想在这个环境恶劣的地方种植作物，那么没有什么比这些蘑菇更合适的了。这些蘑菇几乎可以在任何地方生长，生命力也非常顽强，而且仅靠它们就能维持生计。唯一的问题是……它们毫无味道。
        
        它们的味道很糟糕吗？”
        
        “不，不，并不糟糕。”布蕾妮用手比划着解释道，“无论你在那些‘胖帽子’里加多少盐、多少香料，无论你用什么样的方法来制作它们……它们的味道总是像陈旧的木头一样。这就是为什么它们只是穷人的食物；一旦你有能力选择其他食物，你根本不会考虑再吃这些东西。
        |不过，它们还挺有意思的。那些紫色的帽子和矮胖的外形，让它们看起来就像是从地里长出来的头盔。 [silly
            |其实就是那些圆胖的头盔。 
        ]谁要是能忍受这类事情……那肯定是疯了才会这么做，对吧？对吧？
    ]
    
    食物啊……他们在下面待了这么久，即使有船只向他们运送口粮，他们也不得不自己进行耕作，而且看起来还取得了一定的成效。恶魔竟然能够组织起来进行耕作……这个想法真是令人不寒而栗。你绝对想不到，它们竟然能够专注于如此平凡的事情——毕竟从你见过的它们那两位女王来看，它们似乎更应该关注一些更重要的事情。
    
    不过，这些事情似乎并没有什么值得学习的意义。托勒斯的那些家伙已经在这里待了很长时间了，但你也早就注意到了这一点：它们有足够的时间来建造防御工事，甚至对那座古老的约顿城堡进行了一些修缮。是时候继续前进了。
