rows.original: The trip back to Gweyr's cave has been a long, roundabout one — you left the Ways Between via the Winter City, enduring the curious stares of elves as [party.has etheryn |both you and Ryn |you ] drag a wet-furred and very ruffled Gweyr through the streets and up into the lift leading up onto the glacier. [party.has etheryn |Ryn offers |It doesn't take long for Ryn to personally make an appearance and offer ] to let you rest in the palace for a bit until everyone feels better, but Gweyr politely but firmly declines your elven companion's hospitality. It's a trip that takes a few hours, especially when you're all this tired, but eventually you all turn up at Gweyr's old cave, where you find Imora waiting for you by the unlit firepit, sitting cross-legged with her tail on her lap. The siorc's eyes light as as she sees you, then breaks into a sharp-toothed smile. "You made it back, old woman." Leaning her spear against the nearest wall, Gweyr struggles to light a fire, gives up, and slumps onto a pelt next to Imora. You've still got a little strength in you, so you take care of igniting the firepit with [pc.isMage |a snap of your fingers |the flint and tinder she's got nearby ]. "For a moment there, I wasn't sure I made it. But why are you here?" Imora motions for you to sit down next to her, and [party.combatNames] take up position around the fire. "The trench... it collapsed in on itself. There's still a trench, but it's quite a bit shallower and wider now, by all appearances. Seastone figured you were dead, so she called off the cordon, but I had a feeling you'd make it out nevertheless and went out here to wait for you. I have — uh, what's the word for it — premonitions every now and then. Not very often, but when I do they're often worth following up upon." "Oh. Well, I'm pretty hard to kill, but I think this is going to be my last adventure. After all this... it's starting to dawn on me that I'm too old to keep on like an adventurous pup." Gweyr groans. "My heart still feels like it's going to explode." Imora chuckles and gives Gweyr a pat on the head between the ears, then turns to you. "And you, [pc.name] — I'm glad you made it out alive. Everything's settled, then?" More or less. Tollus and Leold... Whisper... they got away. But at least the lureling is no longer in their hands, which means no more goo polluting the rift. Technically, Gweyr's business isn't finished... but by her own admission, she is. Imora waves you off. "Let's not dwell on that — tell me everything that happened so I can report back to Seastone on the matter." So you do. Imora listens attentively as you recount the entire tale from the moment you set foot in the ancient jotun castle to fleeing through the cracking waystone crystal, presumably the same way Tollus did. Gweyr adds in a few points here and there, but leaves you to tell the bulk of the story, content to just lie back and listen. "Huh. Now that you say it, we'd noticed a couple herds of selkies disappearing. We'd just assumed they'd migrated away as they do, even if it was a little early in the year for it. But a lureling, you say?" That's the name the cultists used for it, yes. Does she or the siorcs in general know anything about such a beast? "Just the name of 'Lureling,' but beyond that, little more. Just legends." Imora shakes her head. "Seastone might know something, but it's not my place to ask her. I'm just glad all of you are safe... and if you don't mind now, I've got to go and head back to Starhome. There are people waiting for me, after all. Just as there are for you, old woman." "..." "I'll see you around, then." Imora leaves, and it's just [party.combatNames] in the cave. The old wolfess is clearly tuckered out, having fallen asleep while you were finishing your tale, and to be honest the warmth you've got coming from the firepit is mighty relaxing... [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona kiyoko atugia quintillus azyrran einin etheryn |[viv.isDemon|Viviane cracks her neck and rolls her shoulders, relieving some of the tightness left from the Lureling's influence. Noticing your gaze, she gives you a wink and struts over. "Caught your eye, did I?" She did. She certainly seemed less... affected by everything than many of your fellows. "Of course. As I said: I knew my answers, and besides, it was mostly trying to tug on emotions that left with my soul. Instead, it just made me hungry for answers and research. Unfortunately for it, it happened to be both. Still, having something in your mind like that can still take a toll. So, stretching."|"Hey, [pc.name]," you hear Viviane's distinct voice call out. You turn to face her as she approaches, a relieved-yet-exhausted smile on her face. "Thank you. That place was... dangerous. I wasn't quite expecting to feel so empty again. To peer into an abyss like that—the metaphorical one, I mean. Still, you got us through it. So, thank you." Of course. What exactly did it even show her? "It made me think I'd burned out. That I just didn't feel anything anymore except that need to discover something or to experiment. As I told you earlier, I answered a lot of my personal struggles with my work, and the joy found within. The excitement of the little victories. All of that. So instead I found myself without that. Without, well, anything, really. Just a void, unable to be filled."] |Cait leans her head on your shoulder and yawns, stretching effusively in a stereotypical feline fashion. Your hand just to happens to find its way to her head, and after a few moments starts rubbing the edge of her ear, moving back and forth, back and forth... it just feels like the right thing to do. Cait? Your pink kitten purrs and opens an eye. "[pc.name]...?" All the things she said when down there... you know she really loves Calla and would do anything to get her back. That's the weakness the lureling exploited to get at her. "I wouldn't call it a weakness." Cait sighs and sinks in further against you. "But I know what you're trying to say, [pc.name]." You won't lie; it may be true that like her deepest fears foretold, that she might never get Calla back, or even worse, get her back in an unrecognizable state. But if you fail, it won't be for lack of trying. "...Thanks. And... I'm sorry, for the way I acted. I know that monster was in my mind, but even still, that's only a shallow excuse to act the part myself. Still friends?" Always. |Brint splays himself out on one of Gweyr's pelts — despite his immense constitution, this adventure would've taken it out of anyone, and not all the exertion is physical. He rolls his eyes over to you; your gazes meet, and he smiles. "We beat them, didn't we?" You did. Yeah, you did. Brint half-raises a fist, trying to decide if the fistbump is worth it, then gives in to exhaustion and melts into the fur. Look, about the things he said down there... "T-that wasn't me. I was crazy, it was that gods-damned fish thing speaking with my mouth." He doesn't need to deny it. There was more than a sliver of truth in there, aren't you right? "Well... I feel kinda ashamed for even thinking it. Even if I weren't accepted at home any more — which is silly in itself — I've still got you, and Garth, and frankly all the people we've met up to this point. They all care about me and would give me a place to fit in, even if I don't necessarily match up with their looks." He thumps his chest. "It's kind of embarrassing, having these doubts even in the face of proof otherwise." ...In a way, you're glad you finally know his deepest fears. It feels like it's brought the both of you closer together. "Well then, I'm glad too." |Brienne splays herself out on one of Gweyr's pelts — it barely fits her, really — and sighs up at the ceiling. despite her immense constitution, this adventure would've taken it out of anyone, and not all the exertion is physical. She rolls her eyes over to you; your gazes meet, and she smiles. "Well, we're all alone now." She still has the strength for that after — "Haha, no. What I meant was, it's over. We're done. For now, anyway, until Tollus decides to show his face again." ...Yeah. But at what cost? Brienne's silent for a little bit, melting into the furs and staring up at the cavern ceiling. Her voice drops to a whisper, and she sighs. "I was so terrified of losing you. No, not just that, of you rejecting me." After having her with you through all these adventures, why would you do that? "I don't know. It was just the fish-thing, I suppose, but at the same time... it's gone now, and I'm still feeling these things. And then I think back, and realize that it's not new, either. Just wondering if you would suddenly vanish one day, sort of like what I did myself..." Her story has the ring of truth to it, and in spite — no, because — of this you don't know what to say, really. Well, you can tell Brienne that you're not going to be vanishing on her anytime soon. In a way, you're glad you finally know her deepest fears; it shows how much she cares for you, and how much you mean to her. It feels like it's brought the both of you closer together. "Well then, I'm glad too." |It's rare that Arona's actually openly tired — given the Kervus, it's natural that she would be instinctively leery about openly showing weakness — but her exhaustion's driven her to the point where she doesn't quite care anymore. Your orcish companion hasn't even bothered to remove her [arona.armor], dealing with the discomfort as she melts further and further into the warm embrace of the furs. Just when it looks like she's about to start snoring, Arona rolls one eye open and glances over at you. "Hey, [pc.name]." Yes? "What happened down there stays down there, okay? The things I said..." Were perfectly understandable. It's the fate of every orcish leader to be replaced with someone younger, stronger, more vital; she doesn't have the kind of security in her position that Hretha has. "I don't want to think about that day." Arona jabs a thumb weakly over at the sleeping form of Gweyr. "But looking at her... we're the ones to replace that old bitch. And in time, someone's going to replace us. But at least she has someone to go home to, even if she refused to do so for the last twenty years. What do I have?" This sort of self-reflection is quite unlike her. Maybe having a big ugly fish-thing in her head really did make her smarter. "Psssh." Arona flops an arm in your direction, clearly intending to smack you, but she's too out of it to do anything meaningful. "I-I'm all right with you knowing all this, and I can trust that old bitch to be quiet about it, too. But not a word to anyone else, okay?" If that's what she wants. "Hmph.[arona.isDom | Don't gimme that... I'm just trying to say I... fuck. Words are hard. | Don't be an asshole. You know I'd keep your secrets, cuz... cuz you're more than just the strongest mainlander around, you know. ]" The big amazon reaches a thewy arm around you and pulls you in, giving you a hug so tight you're half afraid your neck's going to crack. Well, if you're going to die after all that, it might as well be buried in Arona's cleavage... |Kiyoko's curled up in a corner, trying to look as quietly dignified as possible while wearing salt-stained clothes and brushing her tails. The both of you are silent for a moment as something unspoken passes between you, then you take up position behind her, take the brush in hand, and begin the laborious process of smoothing out all the tangles from her fur. "..." ... It's calming, the simple, repetitive motions. Foxes are not people to talk about their emotions and desires, you've learned as much in your time with Kiyoko, but that's fine. Talk is cheap, action is what matters. Isn't that right? "..." ... You finish one tail, then another, and would have gone on to the third but your body really can't take it any more. Sensing this, your fox-wife leans in and gives you a kiss on the cheek, followed by curling a tail about you. For everything that's happened... you think it's worth it just for this moment, this feeling, this closeness after having gone through such a harrowing experience together. "Thank you, beloved." |Off on the other side of the fire, Atugia's bundled herself up in a bunch of furs, pulling several of the heavy pelts about her, snug as a bug in a rug. Sleeping in salt-stained clothes like this can't be great... but everyone's too tired to care right now. Is she fine? She waves you off and turns away. "Yeah, don't worry about me." The things she said down there... let's just say that you don't mind any of it. Rolling an eye open, Tui turns back towards you, although she doesn't let go of the furs. "You don't, huh." Being a monster doesn't necessarily mean anything about her... and given what happened below, you think it actually helped in beating another monster. It's fine, really. "That may be the kindest thing anyone besides Carmen and Severin's said to me for a while now." Oh really? Guess you'll have to start buttering her up even more now. She doesn't turn away as you cuddle up closer to her fur roll, and rubs her face against your chest when you wrap your arms around her shoulders. "That sounds lovely. Mmm. The salt reminds me of my trip," she says. As she nods off you hear one last thought leave her lips. "I'm glad I got to meet you." |Sighing heavily, Quin lays himself out spread-eagled upon the thickest of Gweyr's sleeping furs, rolling about and making himself absolutely comfortable — or at least, as much as one can be when wearing salt-stained clothes. Your taleer companion stares up at the ceiling for several moments, then turns his gaze to you. [silly |"Mission failed, huh?" It's all right, you'll get them next time. Him and you both. |"Well, if that wasn't an adventure." It was, even if you didn't accomplish everything you set out to do. ] "Mmmmh. I feel... I feel kinda awkward about everything I said down there. I ought to have had a stronger mind than that — to put it bluntly, I was trained as a spy, after all. For me to crack that easily..." Hey, it was a massive monster fish-thing. Everyone cracked except the cultists, but as he said, they were already nuts to begin with. Look, he doesn't need to worry about it. He said he was trained to be a spy... that sort of thing can hurt one's ability to trust others, you've heard — or in his case, to believe that others can trust in him. You gave him a chance back there on the day you found him chased by Tollus's goons, and unless he does something to prove otherwise — and the likelihood of that dwindles every day you know him — there's no reason to not continue giving him that chance. Quin sighs and sinks back into the furs. "Still, it doesn't stop me from feeling what I do. It's stupid, I know... but thanks." |Finally allowing herself to relax, Azyrran slumps against the nearest wall in a sitting position, huddling a bunch of the sleeping furs about her. You watch the cuddlebug as she stares into the fire for several more moments, her eyes growing heavier and heavier by the second... ...And then snap back open. "Hey, [pc.name]." Hm? "Thanks for being around for me back there." Of course you were. You were there for her when you needed help with her hive and mother, and since then it's never been called into question, has it? "...The things I said down there, though." Were for the better. You get it that she's a big, strong, tough girl and that she's got to keep up appearances. At the same time, it's better for the both of you that you know just how afraid she is of being alone. When it comes down to it, Vesperans are social people — she has her mother, her siblings, and of course, you; what she didn't manage to overcome alone, she managed with the help of others. What you're getting at is... everything you've gone through, no matter how painful it is, may have been for the better, this last adventure included. You don't mind that she said what she did, because at the end of the day she ought to understand that she doesn't need to go it alone. "...Tch. Oh, you. I guess that makes me feel a little better." |Utterly exhausted, Einin bundles herself up by the fire, throwing the heaviest of the sleeping pelts over her shoulders and wrapping her arms about her knees. Guess she's determined to keep watch until she finally nods off... not that such is really needed in the safety of Gweyr's home, but old habits die hard. "Hey..." Something the matter? "How much of what I said do you remember? Everything's still foggy in my head..." You sidle up to Einin and cuddle against your little mecian friend. She makes to shy away instinctively, then sighs and leans in against you as you tease the edges of her ears. "Come on, say something. Don't just tease me like that." Most of it, to be honest. Look, you know she's got a reputation to fix, past deeds to make amends for. And yes, the belief that she did what she was doing for a good cause doesn't eliminate the crimes she committed. But you're here to show her that there can be a better way to save the people she cares about, that doesn't necessarily involve harming innocent people — or at least, people who are as innocent as they get. There's no escaping that her past deeds are going to be sticky — miracles may happen, but you don't think Whisper will ever forgive her for what it was she did to him, or what he thinks she did to him, anyway. That being said, she shouldn't focus on what she can't repair, but what she can. Einin's far too world-weary to buy high-minded words, so you won't offer her any, but that doesn't mean she can't hope. "..." In that sense, you're glad that she went through all this with you, and you're just as glad that you got to know her better because of it. Einin's more than adept at dealing with outside dangers, but facing her own inner demons is another thing, and even though the journey isn't over just yet, you still think that the both of you are stronger for it. Einin mumbles and mutters as you trace a finger along the edge of her ear, and eventually sighs, wrapping her arms about you. "Yeah, okay. I think it's time to sleep." |Muttering to herself, Ryn sits on one of Gweyr's pelts, staring into the fire. Harrick's formed a large puffball on her lap, and she's stroking his head with a finger — back and forth, back and forth — the simple repetitive motion seemingly giving her some measure of solace for the harrowing experience you've been through. How's it going? Ryn looks up at you with bleary eyes. [etheryn.lowConfidence |"I-I'm fine. Just need to take care of Harrick before turning in." She doesn't look fine. Ryn sags her shoulders. "I'm a little afraid of what kinds of n-nightmares I may have, if I just drift off..." |"I'm fine. I just need to take care of Harrick before we head to sleep. Being carried all that way down into the sea really ruffled his feathers a lot, and I need to make it up to him." He looks comfy enough, if in need of a good preening. "He's been my most loyal subject all these years." ] Silence hangs between the both of you for an awkward moment, then Ryn sighs and glances sidelong at you. [etheryn.lowConfidence |"Y-you saw everything, didn't you?" You didn't see what Ryn thought she was seeing, but you could figure it out from how she was behaving. The lureling may have manipulated her, but her fears and doubts had to be there to begin with. "Then you k-know." Her doubts and fears? Yes, but they're very natural ones for what she's gone through in her life. "I-if I didn't exist, Mother would still be alive, Alissa would never have taken the throne, the demoness wouldn't have b-been able to worm her way into the palace... none of this would have happened. A-and don't tell me I wouldn't h-have gotten to rule if it all didn't happen... i-if it could all have been prevented, I'd have been f-fine with never existing to begin with." She can't change what happened, but she can change what's going to happen going forward. There's no point in dwelling on what-ifs, because for every world she can think of that might be better, you can think of another one where lacking her would have been worse. Work with what you have, not what could be. "..." |"You saw everything, didn't you?" You didn't see what Ryn thought she was seeing, but you could figure it out from how she was behaving. The lureling may have manipulated her, but it couldn't have used what wasn't there to begin with. "Then you know." Her doubts and fears? Yes, but they're very natural ones for what she's gone through in her life. While someone with her station may have to put on a strong front, to expect her to be ironclad isn't realistic. Besides, that just makes her foolhardy... and you'd take a monarch who knows things like guilt and concern for her subjects over one who doesn't. The lureling may have caused her inner demons to surface, but that doesn't mean it was a bad thing in the long run, nor for all the confidence she's gained since leaving her home for the first time do you expect her to be impervious to self-doubt. And for everything that's happened, you think going through this nightmare in order to know her better was worth it in the end. Ryn hesitates a bit, so you reach out and hook your fingers about hers, then smile as she grasps your hand and gives it a little squeeze. "Still... when I do get to meet Mother again in whatever afterlife the lady of light has in store for us..." You're sure that if she stays this course, the old elvenqueen will have no regrets about giving up her life for Ryn's. "...Thanks, [pc.name]." ] ] Glad you could help. And now, to get some rest...
rows.translation: 返回格维尔的洞穴的旅途可谓漫长而曲折——你是通过冬城离开那些通道的，一路上还忍受着精灵们那些好奇的目光 [party.has etheryn |你和瑞恩都 |你 ] 把一只湿漉漉、毛发凌乱的格维尔拖着，穿过街道，然后进入通往冰川的电梯。 [party.has etheryn |瑞恩提供 |没过多久，瑞恩就亲自出现了，并提出了帮助。 ] 他们本想让你在宫殿里休息一会儿，等大家都恢复一些体力后再继续出发，但格维尔礼貌而坚决地拒绝了你的精灵同伴的好意。这段旅程需要花费几个小时的时间，尤其是当你们都如此疲惫的时候，但最终你们还是来到了格维尔的旧洞穴。在那里，你们看到伊莫拉正盘腿坐在未点燃的火堆旁等待着你们，她的尾巴搭在腿上。当那位女巫看到你时，她的眼睛亮了起来，随即露出了一丝带着尖锐牙齿的微笑。“你终于回来了，老妇人。”格维尔将长矛靠在最近的墙上，试图生火，但失败了，于是便瘫倒在伊莫拉旁边的皮毛上。你身上还残存着一丝力量，所以就靠这点力量去点燃火堆吧。 [pc.isMage |弹指之间 |她手边那些可以用来生火的打火石和引火物。 ]有那么一刻，我甚至不确定自己是否成功了。但你怎么会在这里呢？”伊莫拉示意你坐在她旁边，然后 [party.combatNames] 大家围绕着火堆站位。“那条沟渠……它自己塌陷了。现在确实还有一条沟渠，但看起来它的深度和宽度都变浅了很多。西斯通以为你已经死了，所以她撤掉了警戒线，但我总觉得你一定能活下来，所以我来到这里等你。我偶尔会有一种……该怎么说呢，就是预感。虽然并不经常发生，但每当这种预感出现时，通常都值得去探究一番。“哦。嗯，我这个人可是很难被击败的，但我觉得这次应该会是我最后一次冒险了。经历了这一切之后……我开始意识到，自己已经太老了，不能再像那只热爱冒险的小狗一样活下去了。”格维尔呻吟道，“我的心脏还是感觉快要爆炸一样。”伊莫拉轻笑了一声，拍了拍格维尔耳朵中间的位置，然后转向了你。还有你， [pc.name] 我很高兴你能够活着逃出来。那么，一切都解决了吧？”差不多吧。托勒斯、莱奥德还有Whisper……他们都逃走了。但至少，那个诱饵已经不在他们手里了，这意味着不会再有那种黏稠的物质污染那个裂隙了。从技术上来说，格维尔的任务还没有完成……但按照她自己的说法，任务已经结束了。 伊莫拉摆了摆手：“我们不要纠结这个了——把发生的一切都告诉我，这样我就可以向海石城汇报这件事了。”于是你开始讲述。伊莫拉聚精会神地听着，你从踏入那座古老的巨魔城堡的那一刻开始，一直讲到通过那块裂开的路石水晶逃走的经过，想必托勒斯也是通过同样的方式逃走的。格维尔偶尔也会补充一些细节，但大部分时间都让你自己继续讲述，他只是静静地坐着聆听而已。 嗯，你说得对，我们确实注意到有几群人鱼消失了。我们原本以为它们像往常一样迁徙去了，虽然现在这个季节有点早。但你说的是‘ 诱妖’？”没错，那些狂热信徒就是用这个名字来称呼这种生物的。她，或者那些希奥克人，是否了解关于这种生物的任何信息呢？ 仅仅是一个叫做‘诱妖’的名字而已，除此之外，没什么特别的。都只是些传说罢了。”伊莫拉摇了摇头，“海石或许知道些什么，但这个问题不该由我来问她。我只是很高兴你们所有人都平安无事……如果现在不介意的话，我得回去星之家园了。是毕竟，还有人在等着我。就像也有人在等着你一样，老妇人。“……”“那我们以后见吧。”伊莫拉离开了，现场只剩下 [party.combatNames] 在山洞里。那只老母狼显然已经累坏了，就在你讲故事的时候它就睡着了。说实话，火堆散发出的温暖确实让人感到非常放松…… [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona kiyoko atugia quintillus azyrran einin etheryn |[viv.isDemon|薇薇安活动了一下脖子，扭了扭肩膀，缓解了被“诱惑之力”影响后留下的些许僵硬感。注意到你的目光，她朝你眨了眨眼，然后大步走了过来。“我吸引你的注意了，是吗？ 她确实如此。与你们中的许多人相比，她似乎确实没有那么……受到这些事情的影响。“当然。正如我所说：我知道自己的答案，而且，那些试图触动我内心情感的言论，其实并没有真正影响到我。相反，这反而让我更加渴望找到答案并进行深入研究。不幸的是，这两者恰好都成为了我的追求目标。不过，这样的想法始终会让人感到压力重重。所以，还是需要适当放松一下吧。|嘿， [pc.name]谢谢你，”你听到薇薇安那独特的声音在耳边响起。当你转身面向她时，她正朝你走来，脸上带着如释重负却又显得疲惫的笑容。“真的谢谢。那个地方……太危险了。我完全没预料到自己会再次感到如此空虚。那种仿佛坠入无底深渊的感觉——我是说比喻意义上的深渊。不过，你还是帮助我们度过了那段难关。所以，真的非常感谢你。”当然……那段经历究竟让她明白了什么呢？“它让我觉得自己已经精疲力竭了。我真的感觉自己已经任何东西只不过现在，我不再有那些东西了——再也没有需要去探索或去尝试的事情了。正如我之前所说，我曾经用工作来应对自己面临的许多个人困境，也在工作中找到了乐趣，体验到了那些小小的胜利带来的兴奋感。但现在，这一切都不见了。我真正拥有的，只是一片空虚，一片无法被填满的空白。] |凯特把头靠在你的肩膀上，打了个哈欠，然后以那种典型的猫科动物方式尽情地伸了个懒腰。你的手不由自主地摸到了她的头，过了一会儿，你开始轻轻揉她的耳尖，来回地抚摸着……这种感觉真是太舒服了正确有事情要做了。凯特？你的粉色小猫发出呼噜声，然后睁开了眼睛。[pc.name]……？”她当时在下面说的那些话……你知道，她其实是真的很爱卡拉，愿意不惜一切代价把她夺回来。而这个诱饵正是利用了她的这个弱点来接近她的。“我不认为那算是一个弱点。”凯特叹了口气，更加靠在你身上说道，“但我明白你的意思。 [pc.name]你不会骗我吧；事实上，正如她内心最深的恐惧所预料的那样，她可能永远无法让卡拉回到她身边，或者更糟的是，当卡拉回到她身边时，她已经变得面目全非。但是，如果你失败了，那也不是因为你没有努力过。 “……谢谢。还有……对于我之前的行为，我真的很抱歉。我知道当时我的脑海里充满了那些负面的想法，但即便如此，这也只是个站不住脚的借口罢了。我们还是朋友吧？” 永远都是。 |布林特躺在格维尔的皮毛上休息——尽管他体格强健，但这样的冒险对任何人来说都是一次巨大的考验，而其中的劳累并不仅仅体现在体力消耗上。他转过头看着你，你们的目光相遇了，然后他笑了。 我们打败他们了，对吧？”是的，你们做到了。布林特半举起拳头，正在考虑是否应该跟他们击掌庆祝，但最终还是因为疲惫而放弃了这个想法，重新躺回了毛茸茸的毯子里。听着，关于他下面说的那些话……那……那不是我干的。我当时疯了，是那该死的鱼在用我的嘴说话。”他其实没必要否认，其中确实有一部分是真的，对吧？ 嗯……想到这种事，我其实觉得有点惭愧。即使我在家里不再被接纳了——这本身就已经很可笑了——但我还有你、加斯，以及到目前为止我们遇到的所有朋友们。他们都在关心我，会给我一个属于我的地方，即使我的外貌可能与他们的期望不太相符。他捶了捶胸：“即便有足够的证据，还是会产生这样的怀疑，这确实有点尴尬。”……从某种角度来看，你反而庆幸自己终于了解了他最深处的恐惧。这种了解似乎让你们之间的距离变得更近了。 那好吧，我也很高兴。 |布蕾妮躺在格维尔的皮毛上——实际上，那皮毛几乎根本装不下她——然后她仰望着天花板叹了口气。尽管她体格强健，但这次冒险对任何人来说都是一件极其耗费体力的事情，而其中的劳累并不仅仅体现在体力消耗上。她转过头看着你，你们的目光相遇了，她笑了。“好吧，现在我们只有彼此了。”她仍然有足够的力气那个哈哈，不是的。我的意思是，一切都结束了。我们现在完了。至少目前是这样，直到托勒斯再次出现为止。”……是啊。但这是以什么代价换来的呢？布蕾妮沉默了一会儿，她蜷缩在毛皮中，抬头凝视着洞穴的天花板。她的声音低了下来，变成了轻声细语，同时叹了口气。“我真是害怕会失去你……不，不仅仅是害怕失去你，更害怕你会拒绝我。”在经历了这么多冒险之后，你为什么还要这样做呢？ 我不知道。我想，大概就是和那些鱼有关的事情吧，但同时……那些感觉现在依然存在。后来我回想起来，才意识到这些感觉其实并不新鲜。只是在想，如果有一天你自己也会突然消失，会不会也是这样的感觉。她的故事听起来很真实，正因如此——不，正是因为如此，你真的不知道该说些什么好。不过，你可以告诉布蕾妮，你短期内不会离开她。在某种程度上，你甚至为终于了解了她最深的恐惧而感到欣慰；这说明她有多么在乎你，你也对她来说有多重要。感觉这让你们俩的关系更加亲密了。“那么，我也很高兴。 |阿罗娜真正表现出疲惫的样子实属罕见——考虑到凯尔维斯的存在，她本能地会避免公开显露自己的弱点，因此这种表现实在不合常理。但她的疲惫已经到了让她不再在意这些的程度。你的兽人同伴甚至都懒得帮她脱掉 [arona.armor]她努力忍受着这种不适，渐渐融入那柔软的毛皮所带来的温暖怀抱之中。就在她似乎快要开始打鼾的时候，阿罗娜睁开了眼睛，瞥了你一眼：“嘿 [pc.name]嗯？”“下面发生的事情就让它留在下面吧，好吗？我之前说过的话……”那些话完全是可以理解的。对于每一位兽人领袖来说，被更年轻、更强壮、更有活力的人取代，都是不可避免的命运；她的地位并没有赫蕾莎那么稳固。 我不想去想那天。”阿罗娜无力地用拇指指向正在熟睡的格维尔。“但看着她……我们才是那个要取代那个老女人的人。而迟早，也会有人来取代我们。不过至少她还有家可以回去，尽管在过去的二十年里她一直拒绝回去。这是什么意思？我这是怎么回事？”这种自我反思确实与她平时的性格不太一样。也许是因为她脑子里总是想着那些奇怪的东西，才让她变得聪明了一些吧。“嘘。”阿罗娜朝你的方向挥了挥手臂，显然是想打你一巴掌，但她现在完全处于混乱状态，根本无法做出什么有力的动作。“我……我没事的。你知道了这一切，而且我也相信那个老女人会对此守口如瓶。但绝对不能告诉其他人，明白吗？”“如果那是她想要的的话。”“哼。[arona.isDom rows.raw: " The trip back to Gweyr's cave has been a long, roundabout one — you left the Ways Between via the Winter City, enduring the curious stares of elves as [party.has etheryn |both you and Ryn |you ] drag a wet-furred and very ruffled Gweyr through the streets and up into the lift leading up onto the glacier. [party.has etheryn |Ryn offers |It doesn't take long for Ryn to personally make an appearance and offer ] to let you rest in the palace for a bit until everyone feels better, but Gweyr politely but firmly declines your elven companion's hospitality. It's a trip that takes a few hours, especially when you're all this tired, but eventually you all turn up at Gweyr's old cave, where you find Imora waiting for you by the unlit firepit, sitting cross-legged with her tail on her lap. The siorc's eyes light as as she sees you, then breaks into a sharp-toothed smile. "You made it back, old woman." Leaning her spear against the nearest wall, Gweyr struggles to light a fire, gives up, and slumps onto a pelt next to Imora. You've still got a little strength in you, so you take care of igniting the firepit with [pc.isMage |a snap of your fingers |the flint and tinder she's got nearby ]. "For a moment there, I wasn't sure I made it. But why are you here?" Imora motions for you to sit down next to her, and [party.combatNames] take up position around the fire. "The trench... it collapsed in on itself. There's still a trench, but it's quite a bit shallower and wider now, by all appearances. Seastone figured you were dead, so she called off the cordon, but I had a feeling you'd make it out nevertheless and went out here to wait for you. I have — uh, what's the word for it — premonitions every now and then. Not very often, but when I do they're often worth following up upon." "Oh. Well, I'm pretty hard to kill, but I think this is going to be my last adventure. After all this... it's starting to dawn on me that I'm too old to keep on like an adventurous pup." Gweyr groans. "My heart still feels like it's going to explode." Imora chuckles and gives Gweyr a pat on the head between the ears, then turns to you. "And you, [pc.name] — I'm glad you made it out alive. Everything's settled, then?" More or less. Tollus and Leold... Whisper... they got away. But at least the lureling is no longer in their hands, which means no more goo polluting the rift. Technically, Gweyr's business isn't finished... but by her own admission, she is. Imora waves you off. "Let's not dwell on that — tell me everything that happened so I can report back to Seastone on the matter." So you do. Imora listens attentively as you recount the entire tale from the moment you set foot in the ancient jotun castle to fleeing through the cracking waystone crystal, presumably the same way Tollus did. Gweyr adds in a few points here and there, but leaves you to tell the bulk of the story, content to just lie back and listen. "Huh. Now that you say it, we'd noticed a couple herds of selkies disappearing. We'd just assumed they'd migrated away as they do, even if it was a little early in the year for it. But a lureling, you say?" That's the name the cultists used for it, yes. Does she or the siorcs in general know anything about such a beast? "Just the name of 'Lureling,' but beyond that, little more. Just legends." Imora shakes her head. "Seastone might know something, but it's not my place to ask her. I'm just glad all of you are safe... and if you don't mind now, I've got to go and head back to Starhome. There are people waiting for me, after all. Just as there are for you, old woman." "..." "I'll see you around, then." Imora leaves, and it's just [party.combatNames] in the cave. The old wolfess is clearly tuckered out, having fallen asleep while you were finishing your tale, and to be honest the warmth you've got coming from the firepit is mighty relaxing... [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona kiyoko atugia quintillus azyrran einin etheryn |[viv.isDemon|Viviane cracks her neck and rolls her shoulders, relieving some of the tightness left from the Lureling's influence. Noticing your gaze, she gives you a wink and struts over. "Caught your eye, did I?" She did. She certainly seemed less... affected by everything than many of your fellows. "Of course. As I said: I knew my answers, and besides, it was mostly trying to tug on emotions that left with my soul. Instead, it just made me hungry for answers and research. Unfortunately for it, it happened to be both. Still, having something in your mind like that can still take a toll. So, stretching."|"Hey, [pc.name]," you hear Viviane's distinct voice call out. You turn to face her as she approaches, a relieved-yet-exhausted smile on her face. "Thank you. That place was... dangerous. I wasn't quite expecting to feel so empty again. To peer into an abyss like that—the metaphorical one, I mean. Still, you got us through it. So, thank you." Of course. What exactly did it even show her? "It made me think I'd burned out. That I just didn't feel anything anymore except that need to discover something or to experiment. As I told you earlier, I answered a lot of my personal struggles with my work, and the joy found within. The excitement of the little victories. All of that. So instead I found myself without that. Without, well, anything, really. Just a void, unable to be filled."] |Cait leans her head on your shoulder and yawns, stretching effusively in a stereotypical feline fashion. Your hand just to happens to find its way to her head, and after a few moments starts rubbing the edge of her ear, moving back and forth, back and forth... it just feels like the right thing to do. Cait? Your pink kitten purrs and opens an eye. "[pc.name]...?" All the things she said when down there... you know she really loves Calla and would do anything to get her back. That's the weakness the lureling exploited to get at her. "I wouldn't call it a weakness." Cait sighs and sinks in further against you. "But I know what you're trying to say, [pc.name]." You won't lie; it may be true that like her deepest fears foretold, that she might never get Calla back, or even worse, get her back in an unrecognizable state. But if you fail, it won't be for lack of trying. "...Thanks. And... I'm sorry, for the way I acted. I know that monster was in my mind, but even still, that's only a shallow excuse to act the part myself. Still friends?" Always. |Brint splays himself out on one of Gweyr's pelts — despite his immense constitution, this adventure would've taken it out of anyone, and not all the exertion is physical. He rolls his eyes over to you; your gazes meet, and he smiles. "We beat them, didn't we?" You did. Yeah, you did. Brint half-raises a fist, trying to decide if the fistbump is worth it, then gives in to exhaustion and melts into the fur. Look, about the things he said down there... "T-that wasn't me. I was crazy, it was that gods-damned fish thing speaking with my mouth." He doesn't need to deny it. There was more than a sliver of truth in there, aren't you right? "Well... I feel kinda ashamed for even thinking it. Even if I weren't accepted at home any more — which is silly in itself — I've still got you, and Garth, and frankly all the people we've met up to this point. They all care about me and would give me a place to fit in, even if I don't necessarily match up with their looks." He thumps his chest. "It's kind of embarrassing, having these doubts even in the face of proof otherwise." ...In a way, you're glad you finally know his deepest fears. It feels like it's brought the both of you closer together. "Well then, I'm glad too." |Brienne splays herself out on one of Gweyr's pelts — it barely fits her, really — and sighs up at the ceiling. despite her immense constitution, this adventure would've taken it out of anyone, and not all the exertion is physical. She rolls her eyes over to you; your gazes meet, and she smiles. "Well, we're all alone now." She still has the strength for that after — "Haha, no. What I meant was, it's over. We're done. For now, anyway, until Tollus decides to show his face again." ...Yeah. But at what cost? Brienne's silent for a little bit, melting into the furs and staring up at the cavern ceiling. Her voice drops to a whisper, and she sighs. "I was so terrified of losing you. No, not just that, of you rejecting me." After having her with you through all these adventures, why would you do that? "I don't know. It was just the fish-thing, I suppose, but at the same time... it's gone now, and I'm still feeling these things. And then I think back, and realize that it's not new, either. Just wondering if you would suddenly vanish one day, sort of like what I did myself..." Her story has the ring of truth to it, and in spite — no, because — of this you don't know what to say, really. Well, you can tell Brienne that you're not going to be vanishing on her anytime soon. In a way, you're glad you finally know her deepest fears; it shows how much she cares for you, and how much you mean to her. It feels like it's brought the both of you closer together. "Well then, I'm glad too." |It's rare that Arona's actually openly tired — given the Kervus, it's natural that she would be instinctively leery about openly showing weakness — but her exhaustion's driven her to the point where she doesn't quite care anymore. Your orcish companion hasn't even bothered to remove her [arona.armor], dealing with the discomfort as she melts further and further into the warm embrace of the furs. Just when it looks like she's about to start snoring, Arona rolls one eye open and glances over at you. "Hey, [pc.name]." Yes? "What happened down there stays down there, okay? The things I said..." Were perfectly understandable. It's the fate of every orcish leader to be replaced with someone younger, stronger, more vital; she doesn't have the kind of security in her position that Hretha has. "I don't want to think about that day." Arona jabs a thumb weakly over at the sleeping form of Gweyr. "But looking at her... we're the ones to replace that old bitch. And in time, someone's going to replace us. But at least she has someone to go home to, even if she refused to do so for the last twenty years. What do I have?" This sort of self-reflection is quite unlike her. Maybe having a big ugly fish-thing in her head really did make her smarter. "Psssh." Arona flops an arm in your direction, clearly intending to smack you, but she's too out of it to do anything meaningful. "I-I'm all right with you knowing all this, and I can trust that old bitch to be quiet about it, too. But not a word to anyone else, okay?" If that's what she wants. "Hmph.[arona.isDom | Don't gimme that... I'm just trying to say I... fuck. Words are hard. | Don't be an asshole. You know I'd keep your secrets, cuz... cuz you're more than just the strongest mainlander around, you know. ]" The big amazon reaches a thewy arm around you and pulls you in, giving you a hug so tight you're half afraid your neck's going to crack. rows.original:
The next day dawns in the Rift as always — cold, bleak and miserable. It's begun to snow lightly outside Gweyr's home, and the old wolfess wakes you up to a quick breakfast of roasted liver and some kind of saltwater eel.
        
        "Thanks, [party.som
            |[pc.name]
            |the both of you
            |the lot of you
        ]. I couldn't have done it alone."
        
        So, what's she going to do now? She said something along the lines of being too old for this.
        
        Gweyr's eyes flicker. "I guess I'm not as young as I used to be, and this adventure was probably my last. It's time... it's time for old folks like me to pass the torch to you kids. Unlike Leold, I don't have potions to keep me young forever, and given how he and Tollus were getting them I wouldn't want the things anyway."
        
        ... 
        
        "Being banished to walk the ice is a death sentence in all but name. I guess now that I've done all I can about Tollus, after nipping at his heels all over for twenty years now... maybe it's time for me to lay down and — "
        
        All right, that's enough. The sun is shining out there, it's a new day, and the other denizens of the rift need her. Doesn't she have to go find the siorcs and speak with Seastone herself, corroborate Imora's report?
        
        "...Hmph. Fine, no rest for the wicked. I guess I'll be seeing you around, then. Finish up, I'll put out the embers and you can be on your way; despite the setback, Tollus is still out there and he's not going to stop until someone drives a stake through that rotten heart of his. Don't forget to visit every so often when you're out saving the world."
        
        ...Yeah.

第二天，在裂谷地带，一如既往地，天色降临了——寒冷、阴沉，令人感到凄凉。在格维尔的家中，外面已经开始下起小雪来，而那位年老的母狼将你唤醒，让你享用一顿由烤肝和某种咸水鳗鱼制成的简单早餐。“谢谢 [party.som
            |[pc.name]
            |你们两个
            |你们这些人
        ]我一个人是无法完成这个任务的。”那么，她现在打算怎么做呢？她说过自己已经太老了，不适合再参与这样的冒险了。格维尔的眼睛微微闪了闪：“我想，我确实不再像以前那样年轻了，而这次冒险，或许也是我最后一次了。是时候了……像我这样的老人，应该把接力棒交给你们这些年轻人了。与莱奥德不同，我没有那些能让我永远保持年轻的药剂，而且考虑到他和托勒斯获取那些药剂的方式，我其实也不想要那些东西。
        
        被流放到冰原上生活，其实等同于死刑。我想，既然这些年来我为托勒斯做了我所能做的一切，追了他二十年的时间……也许现在是我该放弃的时候了……
        
        好了，够了。外面阳光明媚，是新的一天，裂隙中的其他生物也需要她。她难道不应该自己去寻找那些西奥克人，亲自与海石谈谈，核实伊莫拉的报告吗？
        
        ……哼，好吧，恶人果然没有好下场。看来以后还会经常见到你吧。快结束吧，我等会把余火熄灭，你们就可以走了；尽管遇到了挫折，但托勒斯仍然还在那里，除非有人能彻底摧毁他那颗腐朽的心，否则他不会罢休的。在外面拯救世界的时候，记得偶尔回来看看哦。”……嗯，好的。

rows.original:
You take a few moments to rustle through the piles of pillows and blankets still scattered around the room. There's no question as to what this chamber was used for in the past: even after centuries of being left unused, the statuary circling the room — dozens of fertile figures cradling heavy bellies — makes it clear this was where the valleyfolk once came to ensure it wasn't only their farms that had a good plowing. 
    
    Something catches your eye as you lift some of the pillows aside — a hint of veridian patina clinging to time-weathered metal. You carefully extract the source: a slim ring, adorned with a verdant and blooming flower rather than a gem. Looks to be made of copper, but it's warm to the touch and, coloration aside, seems unharmed by the passage of time. 
    
    You pocket the ring, though you can't help but notice that heat's starting to spread from your fingers a bit...

rows.original:
The garden must once have been a marvel, an underground oasis of verdant bounty overflowing with fruit to feed the congregation. The latter might still be true — there's no shortage of fruit to eat down here — but the beauty of the place has been marred by long decades of neglect. It's overgrown so badly that it's hard to walk through the chamber, each step sinking into the foliage. 
    
    And then your foot crunches something brittle, hidden under the green. 
    
    Your first concern is that you've just found a skeleton, but thankfully a brief glance under the brush reveals a thin tablet of fired clay. You pick it up, dusting off the dirt and grass... and finding nothing but strange, triangular wedges pressed into it. 
    
    "What is this..." you murmur. [pc.bg scholar
        |"Nobody's written like this since before Belhar rose."
    ]
    
    [party.has brint
        |Brint shrugs. "Don't look at me."
    ]
    
    [party.has brienne
        |Brienne shrugs. "No idea, sorry."
    ]
    
    [party.has cait
        |"I think I recognize those symbols," Cait says. "I've seen them in the archives back home. No clue what any of it means, or where it's really from, though."
    ]
    
    [party.has viv
        |Viv taps her chin. "I recognize some of those shapes as primitive runes. Perhaps this is a spell of some sort?"
    ]
    
    As you lift it up, though, the ancient clay starts to feel... wet... in your hand. Earthy again. The writing, indeed the whole thing, begins to turn into a soft, wet sludge. Now it's completely indecipherable! 
    
    You sigh. What magic could have caused that to happen...

        ... But it's still wet, and the effect doesn't last more than a few seconds. Just as soon as the effect began, you're holding wet clay once more.
    ]
rows.translation:
[flags.ELOSA_TABLET_FIRE
        |这块平板仍然很热，还没有完全变硬，还没有达到可以让你舒适地将其举到眼前金光之下的程度。它的表面原本因为某种魔法而变得柔软，现在那种效果已经消失了，它的表面开始扭曲、蠕动起来。曾经那些难以理解的楔形图案，如今已逐渐变成了贝拉兰字符和可辨认的符文——整个系统正在自我进行翻译。
        
        ……但是烧制过程尚未完成，黏土仍然处于柔软状态。你需要尽快再次进行烧制，否则黏土会再次融化。不过，你至少还有一些时间。
        |你将那块湿润、沾满泥土的石板举到金色的光芒下。原本因某种魔法作用而变得柔软的石板表面，此刻重新恢复了原本的状态，那些原本无法辨认的符号开始扭曲、变形，渐渐变成了贝尔哈兰文字和可识别的符文——这块石板正在自我翻译。
        
        ……但它仍然湿润着，这种效果持续的时间不超过几秒钟。就在效果刚刚开始的时候，你手中握着的又变回了那块湿漉漉的黏土。
    ]
rows.raw:
"
    [flags.ELOSA_TABLET_FIRE
        |The tablet is still hot, and not yet hard, firm enough that you can comfortably hold it up to the golden light in front of you. The face of it, now blank from whatever magic had caused it to become soft again, begins to twist and writhe. Where once there were incomprehensible wedges, now you begin to see Belharan characters, recognizable runes — it's translating itself.
        
        ... But the firing isn't done, and the clay is still soft. You'll need to fire it again quickly before it melts again. You have some time at least, though.
        |You hold up the wet, earthy tablet to the golden light. The face of it, now blank from whatever magic had caused it to become soft again, begins to twist and writhe. Where once there were incomprehensible wedges, now you begin to see Belharan characters, recognizable runes — it's translating itself.
        
        ... But it's still wet, and the effect doesn't last more than a few seconds. Just as soon as the effect began, you're holding wet clay once more.
    ]
    "

rows.original: [flags.ELOSA_TABLET_ORB_FIRE |The fire's still hot, and you have a tablet with letters still legible on it, still forming words and phrases you can read — but you're pressed for time, watching them start to melt again. You throw more fuel into the fire after you lay the tablet back out onto the cook plate. It takes a few minutes, but the fire does its work, baking the words onto the clay permanently this time. When it's finally hard again, you gingerly remove the tablet from the flames and take a look at what you have: At first blush, it appears to be concerned with gardening — no surprise, you suppose, given where you found it. Half the tablet is given to extolling the benefits of fertile earth and pure water, coming together to form the basis for life both plant and animal. But the second half is pure magic, runes and invocations you don't recognize: forgotten magic, unique to this sect, though it doesn't look exactly like any spell you've seen before. It's almost more like dance moves. And at the bottom, a number of runes corresponding to gemstones, mixed with text. Some kind of riddle? Agate: Amethyst is to my right. Amethyst: Amber is beneath me. Jade: Lapis is to my left. Lapis: Pearl is beneath me. Pearl: Amber is above me. You glance at the door to your side. Oh... |You set the tablet in the fireplace's cooking plate, then quickly go and gather some sticks from the garden and outside, enough fuel to get a nice hearthfire going. Once done, you get a bit of flint from your pack and light 'er up. The flames are burning warmly soon enough, transferring heat into the copper plate, and from there into the old clay tablet. You watch intently as it begins to dry out, slowly hardening... but the writing is still gone. Vanished, lost to the sands of time. [party.has arona |"Welp," Arona says, poking at it with the tip of a small knife. "Least you can still bash somebody over the head with it. That'll get the point across." [party.has ryn |Etheryn groans. ] ] You scoop the ruined tablet out. It's not completely dried yet, still a little soft, but there's nothing visible on the face of it now. ]
rows.translation: [flags.ELOSA_TABLET_ORB_FIRE |火焰依然炽热，那块刻有文字的石板上的字迹依然清晰可读，那些文字和短语依然能够被你辨认出来——但时间紧迫，你看到那些字迹又开始慢慢融化了。于是你在把石板重新放回烤盘上之后，又往火里添加了更多的燃料。 这个过程需要几分钟时间，但火会完成它的使命——这一次，这些文字会被永久地烧制在陶土上。当陶土最终再次变硬时，你就要小心翼翼地将陶片从火焰中取出来，看看自己最终得到了什么： 乍一看，这个内容似乎与园艺有关——考虑到你是在哪里找到它的，这一点也不奇怪。文本的一半都在赞美肥沃的土壤和纯净的水源，正是这两种要素共同作用，才为植物和动物的生存奠定了基础。但后半部分简直就是魔法的世界——那些你根本不认识的符文与咒语：那些被遗忘的魔法，只有这个宗派才掌握，虽然它们看起来与你以前见过的任何法术都不一样。它们更像是一些舞蹈动作。 在底部，有一些与宝石相对应的符文，这些符文与文字混合在一起。这是某种谜语吗？ 玛瑙：紫水晶在我右边。 紫水晶：琥珀在我下方。 翡翠：青金石在我左边。 青金石：珍珠在我下方。 珍珠：琥珀在我上方。 你瞥了一眼身旁的门。哦…… |你将石板放在壁炉的烤架上，然后迅速去花园和外面捡了一些树枝，收集足够的燃料来生起一堆温暖的火焰。准备就绪后，你从背包里取出一块打火石，点燃了火焰。 不久，火焰开始温暖地燃烧起来，热量逐渐传递到铜板上，再从铜板传到那块古老的陶土石板上。你仔细观察着，看着石板逐渐变干、慢慢变硬……但那些文字却依然不见了。它们已经消失无踪，被时间的沙尘所掩埋了。 [party.has arona |好吧，”阿罗娜说着，用小刀的刀尖轻轻拨了拨那个东西，“至少你还可以用它敲打别人的头部。这样总能让别人明白你的意思吧。 [party.has ryn |伊瑟琳发出了呻吟声。 ] ] 你把那块已经损坏的石板取了出来。它还没有完全干透，仍然有些柔软，但现在它的表面已经没有任何可见的痕迹了。 ]

It's almost more like dance moves. And at the bottom, a number of runes corresponding to gemstones, mixed with text. Some kind of riddle? Agate: Amethyst is to my right. Amethyst: Amber is beneath me. Jade: Lapis is to my left. Lapis: Pearl is beneath me. Pearl: Amber is above me. You glance at the door to your side. Once done, you get a bit of flint from your pack and light 'er up. The flames are burning warmly soon enough, transferring heat into the copper plate, and from there into the old clay tablet. You watch intently as it begins to dry out, slowly hardening... but the writing is still gone. Vanished, lost to the sands of time. [party.has arona |"Welp," Arona says, poking at it with the tip of a small knife. "Least you can still bash somebody over the head with it. That'll get the point across." [party.has ryn |Etheryn groans. ] ] You scoop the ruined tablet out. It's not completely dried yet, still a little soft, but there's nothing visible on the face of it now. ] "

rows.original: You approach the door, glittering as it is with a myriad of gemstones. There is no handle here, no apparent means of opening it... but the gems appear able to be moved around, switched between their sockets.
rows.translation: 你走近那扇门，它上面镶嵌着无数宝石，闪闪发光。这里没有门把手，也没有任何明显的开门方式……但那些宝石似乎可以移动，可以在不同的插槽之间更换位置。
rows.raw: "\n    You approach the door, glittering as it is with a myriad of gemstones. There is no handle here, no apparent means of opening it... but the gems appear able to be moved around, switched between their sockets.\n    "

rows.translation: 珍珠在我下方（Pearl is beneath me）。

rows.original: Amethyst is far to my right.
rows.translation: 紫水晶在我右边较远处（Amethyst is far to my right）。

rows.original: Lapis is far to my left.
rows.translation: 青金石在我左边较远处（Lapis is far to my left）。
琥珀在我正上方（Amber is directly above me）。
琥珀在我下方（Amber is beneath me）。

rows.original: There is a deep rumble from inside the door, and then an audible hiss as it begins to open — just an inch, but that's enough for you to get your fingers in and pull it the rest of the way yourself. The stone proves almost feather-light now, yielding effortlessly to your touch. Before you lies the deepest depths of this temple.
rows.translation: 门内传来一阵低沉的轰鸣声，随后还有其他可以听清的声音嘶嘶声当它开始打开的时候——虽然只有一英寸宽，但这已经足够让你将手指伸进去，然后自己把它完全拉开。此刻，这块石头轻得仿佛像羽毛一般，你的触碰就能让它轻易地移动。 在你面前，便是这座寺庙最深处的入口。
rows.raw: " There is a deep rumble from inside the door, and then an audible hiss as it begins to open — just an inch, but that's enough for you to get your fingers in and pull it the rest of the way yourself. The stone proves almost feather-light now, yielding effortlessly to your touch. Before you lies the deepest depths of this temple. "

rows.original: You step back and sigh, hands on your hips and regarding the gem-studded door with a mix of confusion and contempt. You can't quite figure this out, at least not yet. [var0 |You just need to clear your mind for a minute and try again. |Maybe if you look around, you can find some clues to help you put this together somewhere in the temple. ] For now, though, you shake your head and try to think of something else.
rows.translation: 你后退一步，双手叉腰，望着那扇镶嵌着宝石的门，心中充满了困惑与轻蔑。你实在想不通这一切，至少现在还无法理解。 [var0 |你只需要稍微放松一下，再试一次就可以了。 |也许如果你环顾四周，就会发现你可以找到一些线索，帮助你把这一切弄清楚。在寺庙的某个地方。 ] 不过，此刻你只是摇了摇头，试图去想些别的事情。
rows.raw: " You step back and sigh, hands on your hips and regarding the gem-studded door with a mix of confusion and contempt. You can't quite figure this out, at least not yet. [var0 |You just need to clear your mind for a minute and try again. |Maybe if you look around, you can find some clues to help you put this together somewhere in the temple. ] For now, though, you shake your head and try to think of something else. "

rows.original:
You reach out and grab the haft of the axe. The way the statue's holding it reminds you of a dancer's pole, but her grip is loose enough that, with a little effort, you're able to slide the weapon up through her hands and off the plinth.

    There's a deeply fragrant scent to the weapon, a mix of rosey sweetness and deep, lustful musk. Just touching it makes you feel an unbidden, but not unpleasant, warmth spreading through your nethers. It feels like a warm hug from an expecting mother.
    
    You shake off the sensation with a shiver and claim the weapon, slinging it onto your shoulder.
rows.translation:
你伸手抓住了斧头的柄。那雕像握斧的方式让你联想到舞者的平衡杆，但她的握力相当松，因此稍加用力，你就能将武器从她的手中拔出来，从而让它脱离基座。

    这种武器散发着一种浓郁的香气，其中融合了玫瑰般的甜香与深沉、诱人的麝香气息。仅仅触碰它，就会让你感受到一种不由自主的、但却并不令人不快的温暖感，这种温暖仿佛从你体内蔓延开来。这种感觉，就像是一位即将分娩的母亲给予你的温暖拥抱一样。
    
    你打了个寒颤，驱散了那种感觉，然后抓起那件武器，将其甩到肩上。
rows.raw:
"
    You reach out and grab the haft of the axe. The way the statue's holding it reminds you of a dancer's pole, but her grip is loose enough that, with a little effort, you're able to slide the weapon up through her hands and off the plinth.

    There's a deeply fragrant scent to the weapon, a mix of rosey sweetness and deep, lustful musk. Just touching it makes you feel an unbidden, but not unpleasant, warmth spreading through your nethers. It feels like a warm hug from an expecting mother.
    
    You shake off the sensation with a shiver and claim the weapon, slinging it onto your shoulder.
    "

rows.original:
A pained noise startles you awake. You sit in bed for a moment, straining to listen before you hear it again. Standing and stretching out some of the grogginess from your limbs, you shuffle out into the hall and narrow down the source of the noise. It's coming from Atugia's room. When you quietly make your way up to the door, you can see her gently tossing and turning in her sleep. It would appear she's in the midst of a nightmare.
    
    It looks more like discomfort than actual pain at this point, but she occasionally lets out mewling cries as her head tosses back and forth. She appears to be having a rough time of things in whatever dream she's going through. Sleep is still calling you, but you could stay a while and maybe help her relax if you wanted.
rows.translation:
一阵痛苦的叫声将你惊醒。你在床上坐了一会儿，努力倾听，直到那声音再次响起。你站起身来，活动一下四肢，驱散身上的困意，然后摇摇晃晃地走到走廊，试图找出声音的来源。声音来自阿图吉娅的房间。当你悄悄地走到门口时，你会看到她在睡梦中不停地翻来覆去，显然她正在做噩梦。
    
    此刻，她的表现更像是感到不适，而不是真正的疼痛，但每当她的头部剧烈地前后晃动时，她还是会发出呜咽声。在她正在经历的那个梦境中，她似乎遇到了不少麻烦。睡眠仍在召唤着你，但如果你愿意的话，可以留下来帮她放松一下。
rows.raw:
"
    A pained noise startles you awake. You sit in bed for a moment, straining to listen before you hear it again. Standing and stretching out some of the grogginess from your limbs, you shuffle out into the hall and narrow down the source of the noise. It's coming from Atugia's room. When you quietly make your way up to the door, you can see her gently tossing and turning in her sleep. It would appear she's in the midst of a nightmare.
    
    It looks more like discomfort than actual pain at this point, but she occasionally lets out mewling cries as her head tosses back and forth. She appears to be having a rough time of things in whatever dream she's going through. Sleep is still calling you, but you could stay a while and maybe help her relax if you wanted.
    "

rows.original: Try to get back to sleep. You can check in with her some other time to make sure she's sleeping ok.
rows.translation: 试着再睡一会儿吧。你可以改天再和她联系，确认她是否睡得很好。
rows.raw: "Try to get back to sleep. You can check in with her some other time to make sure she's sleeping ok."

rows.original: You probably don't need to wake her up, but you can try to comfort her a little. This will start something further.
rows.translation: 你可能不需要叫醒她，但可以试着安慰她一下。这将会引发一系列进一步的行动或事件。
rows.raw: "You probably don't need to wake her up, but you can try to comfort her a little. This will start something further."

rows.original: You wander back to your own room and fall into bed, pulling the covers up over your head. You need some rest to deal with your day-to-day struggles, and you don't get enough as it is. You're sure the resourceful dullahan will be fine for now, and if this continues you can find time for it later.
rows.translation: 你回到自己的房间，躺倒在床上，把被子拉到头上。你需要休息一下，才能应对日常生活中那些种种困扰，而你现在的休息时间本来就不够。你相信，那个足智多谋的达拉汉应该暂时不会有问题，如果这种情况持续下去，以后再找时间处理它也不迟。
rows.raw: "\n    You wander back to your own room and fall into bed, pulling the covers up over your head. You need some rest to deal with your day-to-day struggles, and you don't get enough as it is. You're sure the resourceful dullahan will be fine for now, and if this continues you can find time for it later.\n    "

rows.original:
The least you can do is rub her shoulder and try to assuage the night terrors a little. You shuffle over to her bedside and reach out to do just that. She's still fretting something fierce as you start massaging, but then you're forced to pull back as a bright blue jolt of static interference jumps to your fingers as they approach her neck. Startling back, you rub your hand as tingling numbness flashes and then slowly recedes. What the hell was that?
    
    Whatever it was, Tui has returned to some semblance of normal sleep after discharging whatever magic jumped into you. Her brow is still furrowed a little, but there are no more pained noises issuing from her. That's enough for you for now, though you'll have to bring up the zapping business in the morning. It can't be good for her if she's storing up magical energy enough to do something like that in her sleep. For now, though, you return to your bed and plop down under the covers.
rows.translation:
你至少可以轻轻拍拍她的肩膀，试着缓解她夜间的恐惧。你走到她的床边，伸出手去这么做。当你开始按摩时，她仍在不停地焦虑着什么，但就在你的手指靠近她脖子的时候，一股明亮的蓝色静电干扰突然传到了你的手指上，迫使你立刻停止动作。你猛地一惊，揉了揉手，那种刺痛感渐渐消退。到底发生了什么？
    
    不管那是什么，在那些奇怪的力量离开你的身体后，涂终于恢复了还算正常的睡眠状态。她的眉头仍然微微皱着，但再也没有发出任何痛苦的声音了。不过，目前这样已经足够了，不过你还是得在早上再跟她谈谈那个“瞬间移动”的事情。如果她一直在睡眠中积聚足够的魔法能量来做出那样的事情，这对她肯定没有好处。不过，现在你还是回到床上，钻进被窝里吧。
rows.raw:
"
    The least you can do is rub her shoulder and try to assuage the night terrors a little. You shuffle over to her bedside and reach out to do just that. She's still fretting something fierce as you start massaging, but then you're forced to pull back as a bright blue jolt of static interference jumps to your fingers as they approach her neck. Startling back, you rub your hand as tingling numbness flashes and then slowly recedes. What the hell was that?
    
    Whatever it was, Tui has returned to some semblance of normal sleep after discharging whatever magic jumped into you. Her brow is still furrowed a little, but there are no more pained noises issuing from her. That's enough for you for now, though you'll have to bring up the zapping business in the morning. It can't be good for her if she's storing up magical energy enough to do something like that in her sleep. For now, though, you return to your bed and plop down under the covers.
    "

rows.original: You're startled awake for a second time by the sound of birds outside. It takes you a moment to dedicate enough wakefulness to flop out of bed and over to close the window, but in doing so you notice the distinctly sunny look the world has taken on. How late did you sleep in? And since when have the Frost Marches been this warm? Hmm? That's a funny thing to get wrong... What are the Frost Marches? You must have been having a really detailed dream to have been living somewhere other than Teiglache. Anyway, there are more important things to worry about! You hastily apply your markings, needing to start over three times because the nerves set your hands to shaking. Blast it all, you can ask your mother for help! You wouldn't live it down if anything you messed up caused the ritual to fail, and a mis-applied rune network is exactly the way to do that. Come on, Atugia, get your head in the game!
rows.translation: 外面的鸟叫声再次将你惊醒。你花了好一会儿才彻底清醒过来，然后从床上爬起来去关窗户，这时你才发现，外面的世界已经变得如此明媚晴朗。你今天睡到多晚了呢？而且，从什么时候开始，弗罗斯特边境地区的天气也会变成这样的呢？温暖嗯？这种事情居然会搞错……什么是“冰霜边境”？你肯定做了一个非常详细的梦，才会想象自己会在泰格拉赫以外的地方生活。无论如何，现在有更重要的事情需要担心！你慌忙地开始进行标记，但由于紧张，手一直在颤抖，结果不得不重新来过三次。算了，你完全可以向妈妈求助啊！如果因为自己的失误导致仪式失败，你肯定无法承受后果的，而错误地绘制符文网络，恰恰就会导致这种结果。 快点，阿图吉娅，专心玩游戏吧！
rows.raw: " You're startled awake for a second time by the sound of birds outside. It takes you a moment to dedicate enough wakefulness to flop out of bed and over to close the window, but in doing so you notice the distinctly sunny look the world has taken on. How late did you sleep in? And since when have the Frost Marches been this warm? Hmm? That's a funny thing to get wrong... What are the Frost Marches? You must have been having a really detailed dream to have been living somewhere other than Teiglache. Anyway, there are more important things to worry about! You hastily apply your markings, needing to start over three times because the nerves set your hands to shaking. Blast it all, you can ask your mother for help! You wouldn't live it down if anything you messed up caused the ritual to fail, and a mis-applied rune network is exactly the way to do that. Come on, Atugia, get your head in the game! "

rows.original: You rush through the door, hoping you didn't sleep in too late. Your mother is just finishing her own markings, drawing an intricate curl around one of her nipples before trailing it all the way down her side to end just above the crimson mess of fuzz between her legs. She's beautiful, resplendent in nudity except for a small satchel that holds her marking tools. Besides that, she's smiling gently to herself as she works, and looks up to greet you with that same smile. "Good mornin', little firelight. I was just about to come wake you," she says, eyeing your half finished markings in the next second and ushering you to sit. "I was gonna get up! I was just tired," you say, flustering slightly at the nickname as you cross the distance to sit next to her. "I don't doubt it! Still, I wanted to walk with you. This is the first time the elders have felt the need for these kinds of precautions in your lifetime! All of us are spooked, so if anythin' I'm glad you've been able to sleep so soundly," she says as she applies your markings with flawless expertise. When she's finished, yours are just as beautiful as hers. You yourself can't hold a candle, though. You took after your dad, more fit than curvy. Still, you're more than proud of some of your parts. "Are you thinkin' somethin' weird? You've got that kind of look on your face that says 'at least it's not all bad,'" she laughs. How does she do that? "N-no, that's silly. I was just hopin' these precautions don't end up bein' needed," you say. "I hope so too, we all do. With luck, this mess won't stretch this far south." "It wasn't supposed to, with the mountain ranges and the low population, the tribal grounds were almost entirely bypassed. We just got unlucky," you say, and your stomach drops. There it is again, that same feeling from when you woke up. It's as if you've done this before, and know what happens, but can't quite consciously remember it. Your mother continues speaking, replying to another line of conversation entirely. After all, you wouldn't have done that the first time. That line of thought slips away from you before you can grasp it, leaving you in the dark once more. "Are you alright, little firelight? You don't look well," she says, touching a hand to your cheek. "Yeah, It must just be nerves. I'm ready," you reply as the unease from before finishes its retreat. After a brief pause, you wrap her in a sudden hug. "My my, did you have a nightmare last night?" "I think so, but I can't remember." "Well. Whatever it is can't get to you now," she says, gently brushing your hair. "I think I'm good now. Just, it made me anxious. I'll be fine." "Good. Let's not make them wait any longer, then," she says with a smile, heading out through the door and waiting for you to follow.

rows.original:
You step over the lip of the final rise leading to the village's primary circle, filled with an unshakable apprehension that you can't pin to a single cause. You're relieved to see the gathered crowd is still working to get into place, and the elders are patiently guiding people to their designated places. No such help is needed in your case, as your father is waiting in the same spot you and your mother will use.
    
    He waves, and the two of you hurry to join him.
    
    "I'm glad you made it, and with time to spare!" he laughs, clapping you on the back as you settle in beside him. "It's been so long that people don't remember their own places."
    
    "Sleepyhead here just needed some help gettin' ready," your mother says, ruffling your hair.
    
    "Mooom. I just didn't want to get it wrong, that's all," you say.
    
    Your father gives you a sympathetic smile, shrugging as your mother laughs loud.
    
    "You won't get it wrong. Just follow our lead," he says, rubbing your shoulder and circling his other arm around your mother. 
    
    The elders signal that everything is ready, and your ritual begins. With enough spiritual power, provided by the whole village so as not to burn anyone out, you can channel all the powers of your ancestors to create a construct capable of stopping just about any threat. Sure there might be armies big enough to get around it out there, but it would give the village time to flee to Bel Carn.
    
    Brilliant light suffuses the rune-marked ground beneath you as every gathered person begins channeling the runic magic at once. The markings on all your bodies glow with muted shades of blue, green, and violet. You don't stagger, but you can feel the drain kick in as your power joins the coalescing energy and gathers into a pillar of flowing magic that flickers into the sky behind the elders.
    
    "Great ancestors! Protect us in our time of need! Return to join in our power and protect us from the enemy we hear of to the north! Come, COME!" the great elder shouts, directing the energies in a calculated dance that ties each family's ancestor spirits into the pillar of conjuration. 
    
    Then, almost imperceptibly at first, wisps of black smoke trail down from the clouds. They tickle at the light, teasing and twisting around it as more and more blackness descends. At first whatever it is recoils with curious hesitance, but then as the darkness thickens it plugs a tendril into the top half of the pillar. Immediately, you feel another gut-wrenching tug as more magic is drained from you.
    
    It's not like the first time. That was willingly given, while this is sucked out of you by force. Your vision dims, and this time you do stagger. The circle breaks, but your light doesn't go out. If anything it flares brighter as whatever this is sucks more and more from you. Managing to raise your head, you let out a horrified gasp as you watch the great elder strain and struggle before his magic is drained completely. He drops to the ground as a dried husk as his remaining animus is drawn into the pillar in a flash of light.
    
    The truth of the situation strikes you as all hell breaks loose. You've been here before, several times in fact, and you can't stop what's about to happen.
rows.translation:
你踏上了通往村庄中心区域的最后一段坡道，心中充满了一种难以名状的焦虑，这种感觉似乎并没有具体的原因。看到聚集在那里的人们仍在忙碌着安排自己的位置，而长者们也在耐心地引导大家到指定的地方，你感到一丝宽慰。至于你，根本不需要这样的帮助——因为你的父亲已经在你们母子将要使用的那个地方等着你了。
    
    他招了招手，你们俩立刻赶过去和他会合。
    
    “真高兴你们能及时赶到，而且还还有空闲时间！”他笑着，一边拍着你的背，一边让你在他旁边坐下。“这么久过去了，人们都已经记不起自己的家乡了。”
    
    “这个笨蛋只是需要一些帮助来准备而已，”你妈妈说着，轻轻揉了揉你的头发。
    
    妈妈，我只是不想犯错而已，真的没有别的原因，”你说道。
    
    你的父亲向你投来一个理解的目光，微微耸了耸肩，而你的母亲则哈哈大笑起来。
    
    “你不会犯错的。只要跟着我们的做法来做就行了，”他一边说，一边轻拍着你的肩膀，同时另一只手也搂住了你的母亲。 
    
    长者们示意一切准备就绪，你的仪式现在开始。在全村人的共同努力下，你获得了足够的精神力量，因此不会让任何人因此而精疲力竭。你可以运用祖先们赋予你的所有力量，创造出一种能够抵御几乎任何威胁的防御装置。当然，世上或许存在规模庞大的军队能够突破这种防御，但这样一来，村庄至少会有时间逃往贝尔卡恩。
    
    灿烂的光芒笼罩着你脚下那些刻有符文的地面，此时在场的所有人都开始同时释放符文魔法。你们每个人身上的符文都散发着淡蓝色的光芒，有些则是绿色或紫色。你们并没有踉跄，但却能感受到体力正在逐渐消耗——你们的力量与那些汇聚起来的能量融合在一起，形成了一道流动的魔法柱，直冲云霄，消失在长老们的身后。
    
    伟大的祖先们！在我们需要的时候，请保护我们吧！请回来，与我们共同的力量一起，保护我们免受北方那些敌人的侵害吧！快来吧，快来吧！”那位年长的长者大声呼喊着，以一种精心设计的仪式将每个家族的祖先灵力汇聚到那根祈求之柱中。 
    
    随后，起初几乎难以察觉，一些黑烟从云层中缓缓飘落。这些黑烟在光亮中嬉戏、缠绕，随着越来越多的黑暗降临，景象愈发诡异。起初，那些被黑烟触碰的东西似乎会出于好奇而犹豫退缩，但当黑暗逐渐浓密时，它们终于将触手伸向了那根柱子的上半部分。刹那间，你再次感受到那种令人心悸的拉力——更多的魔力正从你体内被吸走。
    
    这已经不是第一次了。上一次你是自愿给予的，而这一次却是被强行夺走的。你的视线开始模糊，这次你确实踉跄了一下。那个圈被打破了，但你的光芒并没有熄灭。相反，当这个东西不断地从你身上吸取能量时，你的光芒反而变得更加明亮了。你费力地抬起头，惊恐地倒吸一口凉气——只见那位伟大的长者正在拼命挣扎，直到他的魔力被完全吸干。他像一具干枯的壳一样倒在地上，而他残余的生命力则在一道闪光中被吸入那根柱子之中。
    
    当真相大白时，一切仿佛都陷入了混乱之中。其实你以前已经经历过这种情况，而且不止一次，但这一次，你根本无法阻止即将发生的事情。
